### R0.20 tilde-limits of adic spaces

### R0.20.1 tilde-limits of adic spaces

**Tilde-limits and the affinoid criterion.** (*tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion*) Huber's relation
`X ∼ lim X_i` — `|X| → lim |X_i|` a homeomorphism, and `X` covered by open affinoids `Spa(A, A⁺)`
in which the colimit of the rings of the affinoid opens of the `X_i` through which they factor is
dense — the affinoid criterion for it (a compatible direct system of complete Huber pairs
with sheafy levels and sheafy separated completion gives an adic tilde-limit, under the
definition-ring hypotheses below), and its stability under open immersions and under fibre products with a
fixed space over the system are the contracts of this section: the relation `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit`,
its affinoid criterion `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.affinoid`, the completed-direct-limit criterion
below, and base change `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.baseChange` (*tilde-limit-base-change*, stated in
R0.20.2). The spaces are quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and transition morphisms are adic; analyticity is not
required. The affinoid proof uses compatible rings of definition and their
finitely generated ideals, with density in the completed direct limit
(Scholze–Weinstein 2013 Definition 2.4.1 and Proposition 2.4.2; Huber96 §2.4,
Definition 2.4.2). PerfectoidSpaces P7 specializes this relation to analytic
towers and is not an input. *Needs:* *affinoid-fibre-product*, *fibre-products-existence*,
*base-change-stability* (R0.7). Lean: `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit`,
`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.affinoid` (which keeps the point-space homeomorphism as a hypothesis); the
completed-direct-limit criterion is specified in this README only.

For the completed-direct-limit criterion, take a filtered direct system of complete Huber
pairs `(A_i, A_i⁺)` with rings of definition `A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i⁺` preserved by transition maps
and finitely generated ideals of definition `I_i` with `I_j = I_i A_{j,0}` for `j ≥ i`.
Fix finite generators at one stage and restrict to its cofinal tail. Put `A = colim_i A_i`,
`A_0 = im(colim_i A_{i,0} → A)` and `I = I_i A_0`, and require finite-stage detection:
if the image of `a ∈ A_{i,0}` lies in `I^n`, it lies in `I_j^n` at some `j ≥ i`.
Give `A` the ring topology with open subring `A_0` and neighbourhoods `I^n`; put
`A⁺ = integral closure in A of im(colim_i A_i⁺ → A)`. Form the separated completion
`Â` and let `Â⁺` be the closure of the image of `A⁺` in `Â`.
Prove that this is a complete Huber pair, that restriction of valuations gives a
homeomorphism `Spa(Â, Â⁺) ≅ lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)`, and that the stage-ring images have
dense union in `Â`. These conclusions concern valuation spectra without assuming sheafiness.
If every level pair and `(Â, Â⁺)` are sheafy, conclude that the corresponding adic spaces
form a tilde-limit. Perfectoidness of `Â` supplies the latter hypothesis in perfectoid
applications (PerfectoidSpaces P3.10, *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*).
The construction and valuation argument are Scholze–Weinstein 2013 Proposition 2.4.2,
p. 20; its adic conclusion here uses the sheafy-pair convention of AdicSpacesPartII.

**Checks.**

- A constant complete sheafy pair gives its own completion and the identity tilde-limit.
- A constant zero pair gives empty valuation spectra and an empty adic tilde-limit.
- Sheafiness of the levels alone does not suffice: in HK Example 6.28, pp. 24–25,
  truncate the displayed generators of the definition ring at `n ≤ N`, complete
  `X₂`-adically and invert `X₂`. Each stage is noetherian and sheafy, but their
  completed colimit is the nonsheafy Huber–Rost ring. Its nonzero `X₃` vanishes
  on both rational domains `|X₁| ≤ 1` and `|X₁| ≥ 1`, so the adic conclusion fails.

### R0.20.2 base change of tilde-limits

**Tilde-limits are stable under base change along morphisms locally of weakly finite type.** (*tilde-limit-base-change*) Let `I` be a cofiltered category with a final object `j`, `(X_i)_{i∈I}`
a system of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces with adic transition morphisms, and `X` a
quasi-compact quasi-separated adic space with compatible adic morphisms `φ_i : X → X_i` such that
`X ∼ lim_i X_i` (Huber Definition 2.4.2; `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` in R0.20.1). Let `f : Y → X_j` be
an adic morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type, and
assume that the fibre products `Y ×_{X_j} X` and `Y ×_{X_j} X_i` exist in adic spaces and are
affinoid-locally `Spa` of completed tensor products (*affinoid-fibre-product*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); the
existence of the fibre products is a hypothesis, supplied by *fibre-products-existence* (R0.7)
in the stably sheafy case. AdicSpacesPartIV R5.5 develops the

## Layer R1: analytification and algebraic correspondences

This layer builds on layer R0. It takes affinoid subdomains of `Max A` for a `K`-affinoid algebra
`A`, the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem, Tate's acyclicity theorem, Tate's rigid-analytic spaces
`Rig_K` and their rigid analytification `X ↦ X^an` from RigidAnalyticGeometry (R1.1). It
constructs Huber's fibre product `X ×_Y S` of a scheme locally
of finite type with an adic space covered by stably sheafy affinoid charts (in particular, a
locally noetherian adic space), specialises it to the adic
analytification functor `X ↦ X^ad = X ×_{Spec K} Spa(K, K°)` over a complete rank-one field `K`
with its universal property, and proves its compatibilities with fibre products, open and closed
immersions, finite and finite locally free morphisms, flatness of `q_X`, analytified modules and
ideal sheaves, continuous differentials, and étale, smooth and unramified morphisms. Local rings at
classical points, constructible sets and connectedness are compared on `X` and `X^ad`;
separatedness, properness, finiteness, closed immersions, étaleness and smoothness of `f` are shown
to be detected on `f^ad`. Huber's functor `r_K` from rigid spaces to adic spaces locally of finite
type over `Spa(K, K°)`, supplied with its full faithfulness, essential image and equivalence on
quasi-separated objects by RigidAnalyticGeometry, is given its universal property, equivalence of
ringed topoi, the comparison `r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad`, and the
agreement of the rigid and adic notions of separated, partially proper, proper, étale, unramified
and smooth morphisms. Group schemes, finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties and
isogenies are analytified to analytic groups with their quotients and invariant differentials. The
layer closes with the ring-level and point-level lemmas (weight families from open ideals, valuation
extension in the divisible hull, fibre products of locally ringed spaces, flatness of restricted
power series over polynomials, and topological finite type of affinoid opens over a noetherian-type
base) that the comparisons use; the dimension of affinoid domains, the identity principle, standard
rational refinements, Conrad's `Γ`–`Spec` lemma, constructible density of classical points, and
connectedness, reducedness and normality of the rigid analytification are RigidAnalyticGeometry's.

### R1.1 affinoid subdomains and rigid-analytic spaces

**The plus ring of a `K`-affinoid algebra is its power-bounded subring.**
(*tft-plus-ring-power-bounded*) Let `K` be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field and `A` a Tate
ring topologically of finite type over `K` (a `K`-affinoid algebra: a quotient of some
`K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩` by a continuous open surjection, Wedhorn Definition 5.57). Among the rings of integral
elements `A⁺` of `A` containing the image of `K°`, exactly one makes the morphism of affinoid rings
`(K, K°) → (A, A⁺)` topologically of finite type, namely `A⁺ = A°` (Huber94 §4, Lem. 4.4, p. 543;
Wedhorn §7.7, Def. 7.56, p. 71, where the conclusion `A⁺ = A°` is built into the definition of a
tft affinoid algebra). The description of `A°` as the integral closure of `g(K°⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩)` for a
continuous open surjection `g : K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ → A` is *affinoid-power-bounded-integral*
(RigidAnalyticGeometry §2.3) and
is used here, not restated. The pair `(A, A°)` is Tau Ceti's `Huber.Pair.powerBounded A`, the pair
with the largest ring of integral elements, which the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap, layer 2.4,
attaches to every Huber ring; the content of this target is that no smaller `A⁺` makes the
structure morphism topologically of finite type. The ring-level assertion
`Huber.Pair.eq_powerBounded_iff_of_isTopologicallyFiniteType`
quantifies over continuous open quotient ring presentations; the equality `A⁺ = A°` does not
depend on the choice of the resulting `K`-algebra structure. For `A = K⟨T⟩` one gets `A° = K°⟨T⟩`, the plus
ring of the closed polydisc of the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap (Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc`). *Needs:* *affinoid-power-bounded-integral*
(RigidAnalyticGeometry §2.3);
Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.powerBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`.
Lean: `Pair.eq_powerBounded_iff_of_isTopologicallyFiniteType`.

**Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a `K`-affinoid algebra.** (*affinoid-subdomain*) A
subset `U ⊆ Max A` of a `K`-affinoid algebra is an affinoid subdomain when a homomorphism of
`K`-affinoid algebras `A → A_U` with `Max A_U` landing in `U` is universal for this property; the
coordinate ring `A_U` is unique up to unique isomorphism, `Max A_U → U` is a bijection, affinoid
subdomains are stable under transitivity, preimages and finite intersections, with the affinoid
tensor products as coordinate rings, and for `f₁,…,f_m, g` generating the unit ideal the rational
subdomain `X(f/g) = {x : |f_j(x)| ≤ |g(x)| for all j}` is an affinoid subdomain with coordinate ring
`A⟨f/g⟩ = A⟨T⟩/(gT_j − f_j)`, Tau Ceti's completed rational localisation. Supplied by
RigidAnalyticGeometry §1.4 and Layers 3–4. The supplier's carrier is `IsAffinoidAlgebra K A`
and its affinoid subdomain bundles the representing algebra as data; this roadmap applies it through
the carrier bridge of R0.9.

**Coordinate rings of affinoid subdomains are flat.** (*affinoid-subdomain-flat*) For an affinoid
subdomain `U ⊆ Max A` the restriction `A → A_U` is flat, and for a finite covering of `Max A` by
affinoid subdomains `A → ∏_i A_{U_i}` is faithfully flat. Supplied by RigidAnalyticGeometry Layers 3–4. The supplier's carrier
is `IsAffinoidAlgebra K A`; this roadmap applies it through the carrier bridge of R0.9.

**The Gerritzen–Grauert theorem.** (*gerritzen-grauert*) For an affinoid subdomain `U ⊆ Max A` there
is a finite covering of `Max A` by rational subdomains `V_i` with each `U ∩ V_i` a rational
subdomain of `V_i`; in particular `U` is a finite union of rational subdomains. Supplied by
RigidAnalyticGeometry Layers 3–4. The ambient-cover refinement is applied on the supplier’s carrier
`IsAffinoidAlgebra K A` through the carrier bridge of R0.9, reading `{V_i}` as a rational covering
of `Spa(A, A°)` by RigidAnalyticGeometry §8.2.

**Tate's acyclicity theorem for finite coverings by affinoid subdomains.**
(*affinoid-covering-tate-acyclicity*) For a finite covering of `Max A` by affinoid subdomains `U_i`
and any `A`-module `M`, the augmented Čech complex
`0 → M → ∏_i M ⊗_A A_{U_i} → ∏_{i<j} M ⊗_A A_{U_i ∩ U_j} → ⋯` is exact; in particular `U ↦ A_U` is a
sheaf for finite affinoid coverings, with vanishing higher Čech cohomology. Supplied by
RigidAnalyticGeometry Layer 5. The supplier's carrier is `IsAffinoidAlgebra K A` and its Čech
complex is Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor`; this roadmap applies it through the carrier bridge of
R0.9.

**Local rings of affinoid spaces at points are noetherian with the algebraic completion.**
(*rigid-local-ring-completion*) For `x ∈ Max A` with maximal ideal `m`, the stalk
`O_x = colim_{U ∋ x} A_U` over the affinoid subdomains containing `x` is a noetherian local ring
with maximal ideal `m·O_x`, and `A_m → O_x` is injective and induces an isomorphism of `m`-adic
completions. Supplied by RigidAnalyticGeometry Layers 3–4. The supplier's carrier is `IsAffinoidAlgebra K A`;
this roadmap applies it through the carrier bridge of R0.9.

The bridge `RigidSpace.stalk_completion_equiv` is RigidAnalyticGeometry Layers 3–4:
for a `K`-affinoid `A` and `x ∈ Max A`, completion of the rigid local ring at its maximal
ideal is canonically the completion of `A_x`, compatibly with the maps from `A`.

`Huber.chartIntegralSeries` is the subring given by this coefficient condition, expressed
with the pinned `weightMul`; `chartSeriesPair` takes the integral closure of its image in
`chartSeries`. These definitions assume a complete Hausdorff Huber ring `A`, its compatible additive
uniformity and nonarchimedean ring topology, a Huber pair `P`, and the finite weight family.
Boundedness of `A°` is not assumed. Prove that the coefficient subring is open and
consists of power-bounded elements, and that its integral closure is a ring of integral
elements in this generality
(Huber94 §3, definition before Lemma 3.5, p. 534).
`chartPair P λ n k E hE I` applies `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient` to this pair and the ideal
`I.map (chartSeries.baseMap λ n k E hE)`. Thus its plus ring is exactly the integral closure
of the image, including all nilpotent elements (Huber94 §3, p. 534, definition before
Lemma 3.5; Proposition 3.8, proof p. 537). The coefficient and quotient constructions do not
require the noetherian hypothesis. Under (i) the quotient itself is complete Hausdorff;
over a merely stably sheafy base its separated completion supplies the complete affinoid
carrier in *scheme-fibre-product-analytification*.

`Huber.chartTransition` is a morphism of these specified Huber pairs for `k ≤ h`, assuming
each element of `E` is topologically nilpotent. `chartTransition_polynomial` fixes every
polynomial in the unnormalised variables, including base coefficients;
`chartTransition_comp` gives restriction from index `j` to `h` to `k` as restriction from
`j` to `k`. The pair morphism includes continuity and preservation of the specified plus rings.

The zero-variable identity mixed chart over `A = ℚ_p[ε]/(ε²)` with
`P = (A, ℤ_p + ℚ_p ε)`, `λ = id` and relation ideal zero recovers `(A,P.plus)` at every
index. In particular `ε ≠ 0` survives. This base is strongly noetherian and stably sheafy,
but not uniform: all `cε` are power-bounded and their set is unbounded.

**Checks for plus rings, transitions and gluing.** `relativePlus_test_field` gives `A_k⁺ = K°`

**Huber's fibre product `X ×_Y S` of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space over a
scheme.** (*scheme-fibre-product-analytification*) Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of schemes locally
of finite type, `S` an adic space covered by open affinoid charts `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `A` complete
and stably sheafy (`HasStablySheafyCharts S`; Wedhorn §8.7, Proposition and Definition 8.61,
p. 91). This includes the locally noetherian case: every point has such a chart with `A` of
noetherian type (*locally-noetherian-adic-space*), in particular Huber's case, where `A` is
finite type over a noetherian ring of definition, strongly noetherian Tate, or discrete
(*huber-standing-class*); `IsLocallyNoetherian.isStablySheafy` supplies the required
chart hypothesis. Let `g : S_ → Y` be a morphism of
locally ringed spaces, where `S_ = (|S|, O_S)` is the underlying locally ringed space of `S`
(forgetting the topology of `O_S` and the valuations; no topology on `O_Y` enters). Then there are
an adic space `R = X ×_Y S`, a morphism of adic spaces `p : R → S` and a morphism of locally ringed
spaces `q : R_ → X` with `g ∘ p_ = f ∘ q`, such that for every adic space `U`, every morphism of
adic spaces `u : U → S` and every morphism of locally ringed spaces `v : U_ → X` with
`g ∘ u_ = f ∘ v` there is a unique morphism of adic spaces `w : U → R` with `p ∘ w = u` and
`q ∘ w_ = v`. The morphism `p` is locally of finite type (*finite-type-morphism-classes*) and `R`
has stably sheafy charts; it also satisfies Huber's noetherian-type condition when `S` does.
Over an affine open `Spec B ⊆ Y`, an affine open
`Spec C ⊆ f⁻¹(Spec B)` with `C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I` and an open affinoid `Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(Spec B)`,
the open subspace `p⁻¹(Spa(A,A⁺)) ∩ q⁻¹(Spec C)` of `R` is the increasing union
of the completed quotient charts below; when `A` is of noetherian type these are
`⋃_k Spa(A_k, A_k⁺)` of *affine-chart-analytification*. A `Y`-morphism `h : X₁ → X₂` of
`Y`-schemes locally of finite type induces `h_S : X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S`; this is functorial, and the

universal property, `p` locally of finite type, and the name and notation of the construction;
Huber96 §1.2, (1.2.7), p. 50, where the book restates the construction and imports it from

by transitivity of topological finite type (Wedhorn, Proposition 6.33, pp. 53–54,

normalization by sending the germ of every constant `a : K` to `a`; its existence

after Def. 1.2.1, p. 47, the book's restatement). For
`U = Spa(K⟨T⟩⟨1/T⟩, K°⟨T, 1/T⟩) ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩)` over `Spa(K, K°)`, the global ring
`K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩` is `K`-affinoid (a quotient of `K⟨T, S⟩` by `(TS − 1)`) with plus ring its
power-bounded subring. The chart case — a rational localisation of a strongly noetherian Tate ring
is strictly topologically of finite type over it, with plus ring the integral closure of the
adjoined fractions — is Tau Ceti's `isStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType_toCompletionLoc` and
`isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure_adjoin_plus`; the target is the statement for arbitrary
affinoid opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ Y` of a morphism locally of finite type, which are not rational
localisations of one another. *Needs:* *finite-type-morphism-classes* (layer R0);
*tft-plus-ring-power-bounded*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`,

`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType_toCompletionLoc`,

Lean: README target.

**Rigid analytification preserves and reflects reducedness and normality.**
(*rigid-analytification-normal-reduced*) For a `K`-scheme `X` locally of finite type with rigid
analytification `i_X : X^an → X`, `x ∈ X^an` and `x₀ = i_X(x)`, (i) the stalk map
`O_{X,x₀} → O_{X^an,x}` is a local homomorphism of noetherian local rings inducing an isomorphism of
completions, hence faithfully flat, (ii) `O_{X,x₀}` is reduced (resp. a normal domain) iff
`O_{X^an,x}` is, and (iii) `X` is reduced (resp. normal) iff every local ring of `X^an` is reduced
(resp. a normal domain). Supplied by RigidAnalyticGeometry §8.1. The supplier states (ii)–(iii) for
its analytification `X^{rig}`, which this roadmap writes `X^an` (*rigid-analytification*).

**A `K`-scheme locally of finite type is connected iff its rigid analytification is connected.**
(*rigid-analytification-connected*) A `K`-scheme `X` locally of finite type is connected iff `X^an`
is connected, and `Z ↦ i_X⁻¹(Z)` is a bijection from the irreducible components of `X` to the
analytic irreducible components of `X^an`, identifying each analytified reduced component with the
corresponding reduced analytic component. Supplied by RigidAnalyticGeometry §8.1. The supplier states it on its rigid varieties, which this roadmap
writes `RigidSpace K` (*rigid-analytic-space*).

### Examples

**Checks on the analytified projective line.** These apply the R0 properness and
specialization predicates to the R1 object
`analytification (fieldAffinoid K) (fieldAffinoid_stablySheafy K)
(projectiveSpace.over (fieldAffinoid K) 1)`.

- *Computation.* Over a complete nontrivially normed
  nonarchimedean field `K`, `P¹ → Spa(K,K°)` is proper and its two closed-disc charts
  cover. In either chart, the inverse image of the other is exactly `|T| = 1`,
  with chart coordinate rings continuously isomorphic to `K⟨T⟩`
  (Conrad-AWS, Example 2.4.4, p. 20). The valuative criterion gives the unique centre;
  the two discs account for the alternatives that a coordinate or its inverse is integral.
- *Non-example.* The open embedding `D₀ → P¹` is not
  specializing at the Gauss point `x`: the type-5 point of `D_∞` at the Gauss point in the direction
  `|T| > 1` is a specialization of `x` in `P¹` with no preimage specializing `x` in `D₀`. Being an
  open embedding therefore does not imply being universally specializing.
- *Computation.* Over a complete nontrivially normed
  nonarchimedean field `K`, the structure map of `P^{1,ad}_K` is proper, partially proper
  and quasi-compact, and the canonical scalar map `K → O(P^{1,ad}_K)` is bijective.
  The section calculation uses the two closed discs glued by reciprocal coordinates:
  a series in `T` agreeing with a series in `T⁻¹` on the unit annulus is constant
  (Conrad-AWS, Example 2.4.4, p. 20). The general properness target over a complete
  stably sheafy Tate affinoid is `projectiveSpace.analytic_proper`;
  Huber96 §1.3, Lemma 1.3.4, p. 51 relates the three properness predicates.


The following Checks give the algebraic computations used in these examples. Unless a row specifies an arbitrary field, K is a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field with its compatible nonarchimedean ring structure.

- Every power series in zero variables over K is a polynomial.
- For a pseudouniformiser ϖ and every k, the image of T is a non-zero-divisor in the weighted chart ring K⟨ϖᵏT⟩.
- Over any nontrivially normed field with 0 < ‖ϖ‖ < 1, the natural numbers m satisfying ‖ϖᵏϖ⁻ᵐ‖ ≤ 1 are exactly those with m ≤ k.
- Over any field K, the zero K-module is finite and projective but not faithfully flat; there are exactly two K-algebra maps K × K → K.
- For any field K and x in K[ε]/(ε²), equality x ⊗ 1 = 1 ⊗ x over K forces x to be a scalar.
- For a separable polynomial P over any field K, the image of P′ in K[X]/(P) is a unit.
- Over any field of prime characteristic p, the polynomial derivative of Tᵖ is zero.
- The quotient K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T⟩/(T) has zero relative Kähler differentials and is not flat.

**Relative analytification and its carriers.** The R0 constructions
`AdicSpace.toLocallyRingedSpace` and `AdicSpace.forgetToLocallyRingedSpace`
retain the actual structure sheaf and stalk maps.
`SchemePullback f S g` contains an adic space, its two projections, their commutative
square, and the unique factorization for every compatible adic test space.
`schemePullback` constructs this object when f is locally of finite type and S has stably
sheafy charts (Huber94, Prop. 3.8, p. 536; Wedhorn §8.7, Prop. and Def. 8.61, p. 91), including the locally
noetherian case via `IsLocallyNoetherian.isStablySheafy`. `Affinoid.toSpec` is classified by the canonical
coefficient map, and its point map is the support of the valuation.
`SchemeOver A` is the full subcategory of schemes locally of finite type over Spec A.
`analytification A X` is the mixed pullback along `Affinoid.toSpec`; the equation
`analytificationFunctor.map_snd`, together with the structure map to Spa A, specifies
its action on morphisms (Huber94, Proposition 3.8).

`projectiveSpace R n` is Mathlib's Proj of the standard grading on R[X₀,…,Xₙ].
`projectiveSpace.coeff_value` identifies a coefficient with its degree-zero homogeneous
fraction at every point. `projectiveSpace.toSpec` is the map classified by these sections,
and `projectiveSpace.over` is the resulting object of `SchemeOver`.
`projectiveSpace.locallyOfFiniteType` states that this structure morphism is locally
of finite type for every commutative coefficient ring R and n ≥ 0
(the standard affine charts in [Stacks, Lemma 27.13.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ND)).
The properness statement supplies n+1 analytic affinoid charts, with coordinate rings
the n-variable Tate algebras and plus rings the integral closures of the bounded
coordinate subrings (Conrad-AWS, §3.2, Example 3.2.5; Conrad-RA, §2.3, Example 2.3.11).

`ringCatSheaf` forgets commutativity of the supplied ring sheaf; `ringCatSheafMap` is its
actual morphism over inverse image on opens. `pullbackModules` uses Mathlib's sheafified
extension of scalars, and `analytification.modules` applies it to the scheme projection.
`moduleStalk` is the colimit of the underlying additive presheaf, with scalar multiplication
specified by `moduleStalk.germ_smul`. `analytification.modules_stalk` proves bijectivity of
`analytification.stalkComparison`, whose value `a ⊗ germ(m) ↦ a · germ(η_F(m))` is fixed by
`analytification.stalkComparison_germ`. Its scalar extension uses the actual local-ring
homomorphism ([Stacks, Lemma 6.26.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0094)).
For a strongly noetherian Tate base the projection is flat, hence this module functor
is exact and preserves monomorphisms of ideal sheaves (Zavyalov24 §6, Lemma 6.7, p. 14).

`AdicOver K` is the full subcategory of spaces locally of finite type over Spa K.
`analytificationLftFunctor` is the relative functor into this category, with its finite-product
comparison; `analytificationGrp` is the induced functor on group objects. Its equations
for multiplication, identity and inverse specify the group structure, with multiplication
transported through the product comparison (Huber94 §3, Proposition 3.8, p. 536;
Wedhorn Remark 8.62, p. 92).

`rigidToAdic` is the functor of RigidAnalyticGeometry §8.3 read on the R0 affinoid
carriers; it is specified on affinoids by `rigidToAdic_Sp` and on affinoid maps by
`rigidToAdic_Sp_map`.
`rigidToAdic.rho U` is the range of the image of the rigid open immersion U → X;
`rigidToAdic.sections` is the natural section comparison along this functor on opens.
`rigidToAdic.sections_coeff` identifies this comparison on every coefficient of a whole
affinoid. The cover equivalence and the section equations determine the gluing to arbitrary
rigid spaces (Huber94, Proposition 4.5(i)–(ii)).

**Checks for these carriers and constructions.** Names below are in `AdicSpace`;
K has the standing complete rank-one nonarchimedean hypotheses.

- Base change of the identity scheme map has an isomorphic projection to the adic space.
- An empty scheme source gives an empty mixed fibre product.
- Base change of a scheme open immersion is an adic open immersion whose image is the inverse image of the original open.
- For the zero ring, both the affinoid and its scheme spectrum are empty.
- For a field, every valuation point maps to the zero prime ideal.
- The map to Spec commutes with every continuous pair homomorphism, including quotient maps.
- The analytification of the base scheme has an isomorphic projection to the base affinoid.
- An empty scheme has empty adic analytification.
- The image of an analytified open immersion is the inverse image of the scheme open under the canonical projection.
- Relative projective zero-space has an isomorphic structure map in the category of schemes locally of finite type over the coefficient ring.
- Over the zero ring, every relative projective space is empty.
- Over a field, relative projective one-space has two distinct points.
- Projective zero-space is Spec R, and its constant-section map is bijective.
- Over the zero ring, projective space is empty and its structure map is an isomorphism.
- Over a field, projective one-space has distinct points with the same image in Spec R, while its global coefficient map remains bijective.
- Pullback sends the zero module sheaf to the zero module sheaf.
- Pullback of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf.
- Pullback preserves a free sheaf with n generators, including n = 0.
- The ring-sheaf map of the identity fixes every section.
- Sections over the empty open form the zero ring, and every induced map on these sections is bijective.
- The section homomorphism commutes with restriction along V ⊆ U.
- The stalk of a zero module sheaf is zero.
- The stalk of the unit module sheaf is the actual local ring, linearly over that ring.
- The stalk of a free sheaf on n generators is free of rank n.
- The transported unit satisfies `a·1 = a` for any analytic group.
- On `G_a`, the actual coordinate satisfies `i* T = −T`, `e* T = 0`, and `T ≠ 0`.
- On `G_m`, the actual coordinate satisfies `m* T = T₁T₂`, `e* T = 1`, and `T ≠ 1`.
- The rigid affinoid point becomes a one-point adic space, and its scalar homomorphism is bijective.
- The rigid spectrum of the zero affinoid algebra becomes empty, with zero coefficient ring.
- An identity rigid affinoid map becomes the identity adic map.
- The identity of Spa K is an object of the relative locally finite-type category.
- The relative category contains an empty object.
- The relative category contains the closed unit disc, whose structure map is not finite.
- An empty admissible open maps to the empty adic open and has the zero section ring.
- The whole rigid affinoid maps to the whole adic affinoid, and the section comparison there is bijective.
- The section comparison commutes with restriction to a smaller admissible open.

**AdicSpacesPartIII R3.6: invariant differential sheaves over a scheme base.**
For `K` as in R1's unit-fibre target, let `Y` be a `K`-scheme locally of finite
type and `f : G → Y` a group scheme
locally of finite type with unit `e`. Using R3.6's `AdicSpace.relativeDifferentials`
and `relativeDifferentials.analytificationIso`, construct
`ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} := (e^ad)^*Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad}` and prove a natural isomorphism
`ω_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (e^*Ω¹_{G/Y})^ad` of `O_{Y^ad}`-modules, by pulling back along `e^ad` the
identification `Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω_{G/Y})^ad` of the analytified algebraic differential sheaf
(*analytic-kahler-differentials*) and using `(e^ad)^*(F^ad) ≅ (e^*F)^ad`
(*analytification-of-modules*). It must commute with
pullback along group homomorphisms and with base change `Y' → Y` between
`K`-schemes locally of finite type. Prove also
`Ω¹_{G^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (f^ad)^*ω_{G^ad/Y^ad}` and local freeness of `ω` of rank `g`
when `f` is smooth of relative dimension `g`. At `Y = Spec K`, its unit fibre
must identify with `AdicSpace.continuousDifferentialFibre` and the four
`analytificationGrp.invariantDifferentials` theorems of R1. The algebraic
translation isomorphism is [Stacks, Tag 047I](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/047I);
its analytic comparison and base change use Huber96, (1.6.2)(i) and
Proposition 1.6.3(iii)–(iv), pp. 76–78.

The trivial group gives the zero sheaf. For `G_m`, the resulting sheaf is
`O·dT/T`, free of rank one. For an elliptic curve
`E : y² + a₁xy + a₃y = x³ + …`, the analytification of
`dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃)` spans `ω`, using Tau Ceti's
`WeierstrassCurve.Affine.invariantDifferential`, and `[n]^*` acts by `n`.
For commutative groups, require the global invariant-form identities
`μ*ω = pr₁*ω + pr₂*ω` and `[n]*ω = n·ω`. For the universal elliptic curve
over a modular curve, the comparison identifies `ω` with the analytified Hodge
line bundle, whose `(p−1)`-st power carries R2's Hasse invariant. This is the
consumer in BHW, §3.3, p. 12 of arXiv:1902.03985v4. These sheaf targets use
R3.6's gluing of the R1 *analytic-kahler-differentials* chart comparison.

# Roadmap: foundations of adic spaces, part III — formal geometry, formal models and coherent sheaves

**Summary.** Part III supplies the formal and coherent side of the adic-space programme. Layer F0
builds noetherian formal geometry after EGA I §10 and EGA III §§4–5 over Part II's adic rings: the formal
spectrum and formal schemes, completion of schemes and coherent sheaves along closed subsets,
coherent formal modules, the theorem on formal functions, Grothendieck's existence theorem and
formal GAGA. Layer R2 develops formal models over a complete rank-one valuation ring `O_K`, not
assumed discretely valued: algebras topologically of finite presentation, admissible formal
schemes and their generic fibres, specialisation and tubes, admissible blow-ups and Raynaud's
theorem, flattening after Bosch–Lütkebohmert and Raynaud–Gruson, formal completions and good
reduction, smooth formal schemes and Frobenius lifts, and fractional valuation bounds, section
domains and Hasse domains. Layer R3 develops coherent sheaves on adic spaces: Huber's and Tate's
acyclicity for finite modules, the affinoid section comparison for analytified modules,
Kiehl's glueing theorem, vector bundles and uniform rings, the sheaf
of continuous differentials, relative compactness and Kiehl-properness, the GAGA comparison maps,
traces of finite locally free morphisms with the pull–identify–trace operators used for Hecke
correspondences, and the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring; it cites Kiehl's theorems on
quasi-Stein spaces, his proper mapping theorem and proper GAGA. These
are the inputs for families and dagger geometry, étale and `p`-adic Hodge theory, and the integral
models and Hasse domains of modular curves and Shimura varieties.

This roadmap develops noetherian formal geometry, formal schemes over `O_K`, generic fibres
and Hasse domains, coherent sheaves, vector bundles, proper direct images, GAGA and traces.
Part III uses the morphisms and module pullback of [part II](../AdicSpacesPartII/README.md)
and identifies sections of analytified modules on affinoid charts in R3.1a.
[Part IV](../AdicSpacesPartIV/README.md) consumes its formal models and coherent sheaves.

| Layer | Title | What it builds |
|---|---|---|
| F0 | Formal geometry | `Spf` and formal schemes, completion, coherent formal modules, formal functions, existence and algebraisation |
| R2 | Formal schemes, generic fibres and Hasse domains | admissible formal schemes, blow-ups, Raynaud's theorem, generic fibres, good reduction, Hasse domains |
| R3 | Coherent sheaves and finite traces | `M̃`, affinoid sections of analytified modules, Tate and Kiehl, vector bundles, Kiehl-properness, GAGA, analytic elliptic classification and Hasse loci, traces |

## Conventions

1. **Huber pairs** are Tau Ceti's `Huber.Pair A`: the plus ring is explicit data. Morphisms are
   `Huber.Pair.Hom` (continuous, carrying `A⁺` into `B⁺`). Pairs of definition are
   `Huber.PairOfDefinition`.
2. **Complete includes Hausdorff**, as in AdicSpaces; every statement about complete rings, modules
   or pairs carries both.
3. **Adic spaces** are the objects of AdicSpaces' category (`TauCeti.AdicSpace`): locally
   `Spa(A, A⁺)` for sheafy complete Huber pairs. A point is *analytic* if it has an open
   neighbourhood whose ring of sections has a topologically nilpotent unit. A Huber ring is *of
   noetherian type* if it has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring;
   an adic space is *locally noetherian* if it is locally `Spa` of such a ring.
4. **The base field.** `K` is complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value,
   `O_K = K°`, `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser, `Spa K = Spa(K, K°)`. `O_K` is noetherian exactly when `K` is
   discretely valued; no statement assumes this unless it says so.
5. **Completed tensor products** `B ⊗̂_A C` are formed only along adic structure maps, with the
   topology from rings and ideals of definition, plus ring the integral closure of the image of
   `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺`, then completion. They are neither uniform nor sheafy in general; every fibre
   product carries its own existence and sheafiness hypotheses.
6. **Fibre products** are taken in AdicSpaces' category and exist under Huber's hypotheses (AdicSpacesPartII R0); the
   map from `|X ×_Z Y|` to the fibre product of the underlying sets is surjective when one of the two maps
   is adic (Part II *fibre-product-points*, `AdicSpace.exists_pullback_point` with `hg : IsAdic g`), and is
   not injective in general.
7. **Formal schemes** (F0) are locally `Spf A` for `A` complete and separated for an adic topology
   with a finitely generated ideal of definition. Admissible formal `O_K`-schemes (R2) are
   topologically finitely presented and `ϖ`-torsion-free, and are not noetherian unless `K` is
   discretely valued.
8. **Rigid spaces** are Tate's (AdicSpacesPartII R1). `X^an` is the rigid and `X^ad` the adic analytification; they
   are identified only through Huber's functor `r_K`.
9. **Valuation bounds.** `|f| ≤ |g|^{a/b}` means `v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)`; no root of `g` in the base field is
   assumed. Tubes and strict Hasse loci are interiors of preimages under specialisation (R2).
10. **Coherent and locally free.** Coherent sheaves are defined on locally noetherian adic spaces
    only; vector bundles on every adic space, corresponding to finite projective modules on sheafy
    Tate affinoids.
11. **Traces.** The scalar trace of a finite projective module is contraction through
    `dualTensorHomEquiv`. Its standard API follows Mathlib's finite-projective refactor
    [#44636](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/44636): `LinearMap.trace`,
    `Algebra.trace` and `Algebra.traceForm`. The local `projectiveTrace` spellings in R3 are
    compatibility material for the pinned library, whose standard traces require a finite basis
    to give this value. The basic linear trace is over commutative semirings and additive
    commutative monoids; the categorical realization and geometric applications are over rings.
    A trace is never defined as a sum over geometric points.
12. **Names.** Declarations live directly under `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartIII` or in its
    namespaces `IsAdicRing`, `AdicRing`, `FormalScheme`, `FormalModuleGluing`,
    `Module`, `IsCoherentRing`, `Huber`, `AlgebraicGeometry`, `ValuationSpectrum`, `AdicSpace`,
    `CountableType`, `LinearMap`, `Algebra`, `SheafOfModules`, `SheafCohomology`, `RigidSpace`,
    `EllipticModuli`, `GeneralisedEllipticCurve` and their subnamespaces, including
    `Module.IsCoherent`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`.
    The class `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing`, its chosen ideal and its completion
    criteria are imported from AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a–R0.1b in its `Suggested.lean`.
    Its field `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing.exists_isAdic` records a finite
    ideal defining the topology and algebraic adic completeness. The `IsAdicRing` namespace
    under Part III adds only the restricted-series and finite-module targets of F0.1.
    The projective trace declarations use `LinearMap` and `Algebra`; relative differential data
    use `AlgebraicGeometry`. `RigidSpace.fibreRank` and `RigidSpace.isFinite_iff_of_flat` use the
    rigid-space carriers imported from `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII`. Tau Ceti declarations
    are written with their `TauCeti.` prefix, and Mathlib declarations in the `Algebra` and
    `LinearMap` namespaces, which this roadmap shares, with `_root_.` where they could be read
    as this roadmap's.
13. **Targets.** Each target below is a definition, construction, theorem or comparison, written
    with its hypotheses in the sentence, its source locator in parentheses (short keys are resolved
    in the References), its API as named lemmas and its unit tests as `Checks`. The API names and
    Check labels are the names the declarations and tests take when the target is formalised.
    `Suggested.lean` states only the declarations listed under *How to read the build*; a target
    with a carrier there says so in a `Lean:` sentence, and every other target, with all its API
    names and Checks, is specified in this README only. A target's label `(*slug*)` is the name by
    which later targets, sibling roadmaps and the section headings of `Suggested.lean` refer to it.
14. **Thickenings as quotients.** The thickening `Xₙ = V(I^{n+1} 𝒪_X)` of a scheme over `Spec A`
    is encoded by the universal quotient `F ⧸ I^{n+1} F` of an `𝒪_X`-module (`IsPowQuotient`);
    cohomology on `Xₙ` is cohomology on `X` of the quotient. Such quotient systems are SchemeAndStackFoundations'
    coherent formal modules on `Formal.Scheme.formalCompletion X (I𝒪_X)` pushed forward to `X`
    (*pow-quotient-formal-module-comparison*).
15. **Towers.** SchemeAndStackFoundations' `Formal.AdicThickeningSystem` (§4.7) imposes no finiteness on the first-order ideal
    `ker(O_{X_1} → O_{X_0})`. F0 compares formal schemes only with its full subcategory of towers
    whose first-order ideal is of finite type (*formal-scheme-carrier-comparison*); Part III has no
    tower carrier of its own.

### Trace contracts

Follow the design of [Mathlib #44636](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/44636)
(head `655ffd91a9416821deede0476a01e773c70532f7`): the standard finite-projective scalar API is
`LinearMap.trace`, with `trace_comp_comm'` and `trace_baseChange`, and `Algebra.trace`,
`traceForm` and `trace_trace`. Build the required material in Tau Ceti against that design.
The local `projectiveTrace`, `projectiveTraceForm`, `projectiveTrace_cyclic`,
`projectiveTrace_baseChange` and `projectiveTrace_trans` declarations express compatibility with
the current pin; replace them by standard imports when the generalized API is available.
The categorical/scalar comparison, local-rank identities, étale pairing criterion and geometric
trace comparisons remain targets here.

### From Mathlib and Tau Ceti

Schemes, locally ringed spaces, adic completion, finite modules, flatness, sheaves of modules,
cohomology and homological algebra use the existing library APIs named in the targets.
Tau Ceti supplies Huber pairs, rational localization, sheafiness of strongly noetherian
Tate rings, the adic-space carrier, Fitting ideals, blow-ups, and the sheaf and completion
APIs specified above. R3's projective trace uses `dualTensorHomEquiv`; the free-module
specializations use Mathlib's trace.

### From DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.T.1 and 1.1

[DerivedModuleAlgebra](../DerivedModuleAlgebra/README.md#11-derived-limits-of-towers),
§1.1, with its ordinary tower foundation in §1.T.1, supplies the generic tower
calculus used by F0. Its native carrier is `ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat R`; the
integral-module/abelian-group adapter preserves projections and connecting maps.
For a levelwise short exact sequence of countable towers
`0 → A → B → C → 0`, use its six-term sequence
`0 → lim A → lim B → lim C → lim¹ A → lim¹ B → lim¹ C → 0`.
If `A` is Mittag-Leffler, the supplier's vanishing of `lim¹ A` gives
`0 → lim A → lim B → lim C → 0`, with the maps induced by the original tower maps
(Stacks Tags [07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW) and
[0598](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0598); EGA III₁ Ch. 0,

**Mittag-Leffler criteria for quotient, extension and Artinian towers.**
(*mittag-leffler-criteria*) Part III proves the following short consequences of the supplied
tower calculus, for countable towers of modules over a fixed ring with linear transitions:
in a levelwise short exact sequence, `B` Mittag-Leffler implies `C`
Mittag-Leffler, and `A` and `C` Mittag-Leffler imply `B` Mittag-Leffler
(EGA III₁ Ch. 0, 13.2.1, pp. 65–66). Quotient stability follows by applying the
levelwise surjections to stable transition images. For extension stability,
first stabilize the images in `A_n`, then the images in `C_m` at the resulting
intermediate level `m`; lifts of equal quotient images differ by an element
of `A_m`, whose image in `A_n` already lifts from every sufficiently high level.
For towers of modules over a fixed ring with linear transitions, Artinian
terms imply Mittag-Leffler by stabilization of descending transition-image
submodules (EGA III₁ Ch. 0, 13.1.2, p. 65).
Use Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler` in
`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean`, its
`isMittagLeffler_iff_eventualRange` and `isMittagLeffler_of_surjective`, and the
descending-chain stabilization theorem `IsArtinian.monotone_stabilizes` in
`Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean`. These three consequences are README-only targets here;
DerivedModuleAlgebra supplies the native towers, six-term sequence and ML vanishing.
Part III applies the consequences to its quotient-module and coherent-cohomology towers.
The dense Banach inverse-sequence theorem in R3.4 uses its own topological
hypotheses; density alone does not imply the algebraic Mittag-Leffler condition.

**Checks.**

- For constant towers from a short exact sequence of abelian groups, the supplied
  limit maps recover that sequence and all `lim¹` terms vanish.
- For a prime `p`, the sequence `0 → p^nℤ → ℤ → ℤ/p^n → 0`, with inclusion,
  identity and reduction transitions, gives the quotient boundary
  `ℤ_p → ℤ_p/ℤ`. The kernel tower fails Mittag-Leffler and `ℤ → ℤ_p` is not
  surjective.
- The constant `ℤ/p` tower with zero transitions is Artinian and
  Mittag-Leffler with stable image zero, despite nonsurjective transitions;
  the shift is the identity, so both `lim` and `lim¹` vanish.
- In the constant exact sequence `0 → pℤ → ℤ → ℤ/p → 0`, quotient stability gives
  the constant quotient tower its full stable image `ℤ/p`.
- In `0 → A → A ⊕ C → C → 0` with `A` constant and `C_n = ℤ/p` with zero
  transitions, extension stability gives stable image `A ⊕ 0` in every middle term.

### From DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1

[DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1](../DerivedModuleAlgebra/README.md#s1-the-spectral-sequence-of-a-first-quadrant-double-complex)
supplies `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows`, the canonical edges
`DoubleComplex.edgeBottom` and `DoubleComplex.edgeLeft`, and their naturality
`DoubleComplex.spectralSequence_map`, for first-quadrant double complexes of abelian groups
or modules. Exactness of rows in positive degrees identifies total cohomology with the
cohomology of the left kernel complex; transposition gives the bottom kernel complex for
exact columns. Exact augmentations identify the edge complexes with these kernels.
Use these identifications and the supplier's canonical edge maps in the Čech applications,
including their compatibility with refinement and the sheaf-cohomology augmentation.
The sign transport from the supplier's anticommuting convention to Mathlib's commuting
convention is the one in §S.1: the total differential here is `d′ + (−1)^p d″`.
The abstract comparison is also Stacks Tag [00M1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M1),
Lemma 10.75.3, in homological indexing; the cohomological exact-row form is NSW II,
Lemma 2.2.4, printed p. 105, as specified by the supplier.

**Checks.**

- On the singleton rational cover of `U`, the Čech augmentation is the identity on
  `F(U)` and the supplied edge comparison induces the identity in degree zero.
- For a double complex concentrated in bidegree `(0,0)` with value `ℤ`, the
  identity augmentation identifies `ℤ` with the kernel; the zero augmentation fails
  exactness, even though the unaugmented tails agree.
- For the sign transport, put `ℤ` in bidegrees `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(0,1)`, `(1,1)`
  with identity horizontal and vertical maps and zero elsewhere. On total degrees
  zero and one, in the order `(1,0),(0,1)`, the differentials are
  `x ↦ (x,x)` and `(a,b) ↦ −a+b`; their composite is zero. Thus the sign transport
  agrees with Mathlib's vertical signs `1` and `−1` in columns zero and one.

## How to read the build

F0 develops `Spf`, formal schemes, coherent formal modules, formal functions,
existence and algebraization over the adic rings supplied by AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a–R0.1b. R2 uses these with part II's morphism theory for formal models,
Raynaud's theorem, flattening and Hasse domains. R3 develops coherent sheaves, vector bundles,
Kiehl's glueing theorem, Kiehl-properness, the GAGA comparison maps and traces.
R3.7a develops analytic local algebraicity and elliptic classification after GAGA,
then applies them to the Hasse loci of generalised curves.
R2.3's generic fibres and fibre-product compatibility precede AdicEtaleGeometry A0/A1.
R2.9's formal étale equivalence uses SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.23a and F0's
finite-type adic systems. AdicEtaleGeometry A2.9a consumes R2.3/R2.9's site-free generic-fibre
facts to construct the continuous functor to the adic étale site.
The references to R2 in A0/A1 mean the R2.3 generic-fibre contracts.
A target's `*Needs:*` clause names its prerequisites. Within a layer the subsections follow
the mathematics; supporting results shared by several targets may occur in that layer's
last subsections. This README is definitive. `Suggested.lean` carries the parts of this roadmap
that are a few lines over the pinned carriers: completed localisations and tensor
products of Part II's adic rings, finite modules as adic systems, the first-order ideal of a square-zero tower, the
quotient-system forms of SchemeAndStackFoundations' formal functions and Grothendieck existence (§4.9,
§4.10) on schemes proper over
an adic noetherian ring, algebras topologically of finite presentation, Frobenius lifts,
fractional valuation bounds, glueing squares and Kiehl's theorem, exactness of dense Banach inverse sequences, finite-module acyclicity on
Laurent covers, uniform Banach rings, the Gel'fand spectrum and projective traces, including
the categorical realization, algebraic base change and geometric-point formula. Formal schemes,
coherent sheaves on adic spaces and everything built on them are stated in this README only. A target with a Lean carrier ends its
statement with a `Lean:` sentence naming the declarations; a target without one is specified in
this README only, and the API names and Check labels it gives (Convention 13) are the names to use
when it is formalised, not declarations of the current file. A supplier contract used
as a hypothesis in an adapter still requires the supplier theorem; that hypothesis
does not discharge the target. Library definitions from the supplier replace the
corresponding suggested carriers when available. Characterisation checks may directly
apply the named comparison theorem, retaining all its hypotheses.

## Layer F0: formal geometry

This layer builds noetherian formal geometry in the sense of EGA I §10 and EGA III §§4–5 on top
of Mathlib's schemes and adic completion, AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a–R0.1b's adic rings of finite ideal
type, and the Tau Ceti coherent-cohomology roadmaps named in the supplier contracts. It defines
completed localisations, restricted power series and
completed tensor products; the formal spectrum `Spf A` as a locally ringed space; formal schemes,
their ideals of definition and thickenings `X_n`, gluing, the formal scheme attached to an adic
system of thickenings and the colimit description of a locally noetherian formal scheme and of its
morphisms; fibre products; adic, finite-type and proper morphisms and closed formal subschemes;
the completion of a locally noetherian scheme and of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset;
coherent modules on formal schemes, the modules `M^Δ` on `Spf A` and the equivalence with finite
`A`-modules; the theorem on formal functions and the comparison of algebraic and formal higher
direct images; Grothendieck's existence theorem; and full faithfulness of completion on proper
schemes together with the algebraisation theorem (formal GAGA). Standing conventions: completeness
always includes separatedness; the topology of an adic ring is part of its data; 'scheme' means
Mathlib's `Scheme` (EGA's préschéma, no separatedness); `Spf A` and every formal scheme is a
locally ringed space, and the adic topology on rings of sections is recovered from the structure
sheaf rather than stored; every scheme is a formal scheme with discrete affine rings.

The Fujiwara–Kato locators below use the printed pagination of
[*Foundations of Rigid Geometry I*, arXiv:1308.4734v5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.4734v5).
The existence and algebraization locators use
[EGA III₁, §5, pp. 149–158](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1961__11__5_0/).

The formal-functions and existence theorems for proper schemes have one owner, SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4. Its
§4.9 (`Scheme.Modules.Cohomology.formalFunctionsIso`) owns *theorem-on-formal-functions*,
*formal-functions-affine* and *formal-functions-at-point*; its §4.10
(`Formal.grothendieck_existence` with full faithfulness, `Formal.algebraize_hom`) owns the
proper-`X` cases of *existence-fully-faithful* and *grothendieck-existence*, and
*existence-projective-case*, *existence-modification*, *existence-devissage*,
*closed-subscheme-algebraization* and *formal-morphism-full-faithfulness*. These targets, and the
Lean `formalFunctions`, `grothendieckExistence`, `grothendieckExistence_hom`, are adapters: Layer 4's
statement read through *pow-quotient-formal-module-comparison* and, where formal schemes appear,
*formal-scheme-carrier-comparison*. F0 owns both comparisons, the formal-scheme-level results
(coherent formal modules, formal direct images, formal Serre vanishing), the proper-support forms of
*existence-fully-faithful* and *grothendieck-existence* for `X` of finite type, and formal GAGA.

### F0.1 constructions on adic rings

AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a supplies *adic-ring*, the class
`TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing`, its chosen ideal of definition and its Huber-ring
instance. AdicSpacesPartII R0.1b supplies *adic-completion-noetherian*, including
`TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.isNoetherianRing_of_isAdicComplete` and
`TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing.adicCompletion`. The constructions below use these
supplied adic rings and completion criteria.

**The completed localisation `A_{f}` of an adic ring.** (*completed-localization*) Let `A` be an
adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition `I` and let `f ∈ A` be arbitrary. The
completed localisation is `A_{f} := AdicCompletion (I·A_f) A_f`, where `A_f = Localization.Away f`,
with the `I·A_{f}`-adic topology; equivalently `A_{f} = lim_n (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f` (EGA I Ch. 0,
7.6.1–7.6.2, 7.6.15). It does not depend on the choice of `I`, and `A_{f} = 0` exactly when `f` is
nilpotent modulo `I`. The canonical map `A → A_{f}` is continuous and sends `f` to a unit, and it
has the universal property that every continuous ring homomorphism `u : A → B` into a complete
separated linearly topologised ring `B` with `u(f)` a unit factors uniquely through a continuous
homomorphism `A_{f} → B` (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.6.6, p. 73). `A_{f}` is an adic ring of finite ideal
type with ideal of definition `I·A_{f}`, and `A_{f} ⧸ I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f`; if `A` is
noetherian then `A_{f}` is noetherian (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.6.11 Proposition, p. 74) and flat over `A`
(EGA I Ch. 0, 7.6.13 Proposition, p. 74). For `g ∈ A` with `g ∈ √(fA + I)`, i.e. `f` divides a
power of `g` modulo `I`, i.e. `D(g) ⊆ D(f)` in `Spf A` (in particular for `g` a multiple of `f`),
there is a unique continuous `A`-algebra map `A_{f} → A_{g}`: `A_{g}` is `I`-adically complete, so
`f` is a unit in `A_{g}` iff it is one in `A_{g}/IA_{g} = (A/I)_g`, iff `g^n ∈ fA + I` for some
`n`; and only then, since `f` must become a unit in the target. Direction witness: for `A = ℤ_p`,
`f = 1`, `g = p`, `p ∈ √(ℤ_p) = ℤ_p` and the map is `A_{1} = ℤ_p → A_{p} = 0`; for `f = p`,
`g = 1`, `1 ∉ √(pℤ_p + pℤ_p) = (p)`, and indeed no ring map `A_{p} = 0 → A_{1} = ℤ_p` exists. Tau
Ceti's completed rational localisation `A⟨T/s⟩` (the topology `locTopology`, the map
`toCompletionLoc`, the universal property `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_locTopology` and, for
`T = {1}`, the identification `toCompletionLocEquivDenomOne`) gives this ring for every Huber
ring, in particular for `A` with the pair of definition `PairOfDefinition.adic I`, `T = {1}` and
`s = f`, on the carrier `UniformSpace.Completion`; this target is that case on the carrier
`AdicCompletion`, and its content is the adic-ring structure, the noetherianity, flatness and
quotient clauses and the comparison with that construction. Define `AdicRing.CompletedAway` (the ring
`A_{f} = AdicCompletion (I·A_f) (Localization.Away f)` with its adic topology, for the chosen ideal
of definition `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing.ideal A`), with `CompletedAway.isAdicRing` and, when `A` is noetherian,
`CompletedAway.isNoetherianRing_flat` (`A_{f}` is noetherian and `A`-flat); prove that the
canonical map `A → A_{f}` is a continuous ring homomorphism and sends `f` to a unit;
`CompletedAway.existsUnique_lift` (for `B` complete separated linearly topologised and
`u : A →+* B` continuous with `IsUnit (u f)`, there is a unique continuous `A_{f} →+* B`
extending `u`), which carries the lift, its factorisation through `algebraMap` and its uniqueness:
two continuous ring maps `A_{f} → B` into a Hausdorff ring `B` agreeing on the image of `A` are
equal, for although the image of `A` is not dense in general — for `A = k[X]⟦T⟧`, `f = X` it is
`k[X]⟦T⟧ ⊂ k[X, X⁻¹]⟦T⟧` — ring maps preserve the inverse of `f`, so the two maps agree on the
dense image of `A_f`; that `A_{f} ⧸ I^(n+1)A_{f} ≃ₐ[A] Localization.Away` of the image of `f` in
`A ⧸ I^(n+1)`; that for `g ∈ A` with `g ∈ √(fA + I)`, that is `f` dividing a power of `g` modulo

**Restricted power series over an adic noetherian ring.** (*restricted-power-series-adic*) Let `A`
be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition `I`, and let `A{T₁,…,T_r}` be the
ring of restricted power series (Tau Ceti `restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring r A`: power series whose
coefficients tend to `0` along the cofinite filter; the statements use its completion
`restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion r A`, which coincides with the subring because `A` is complete),
with the topology in which the ideals
`I^n·A{T}` form a basis of neighbourhoods of `0` (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.5.1, pp. 69–70). Prove that (i)
`A{T}` is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition `I·A{T}`, and
`A{T} ⧸ I^{n+1}A{T} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})[T₁,…,T_r]`; (ii) if `A` is noetherian, `A{T}` is noetherian
(EGA I Ch. 0, 7.5.4 Proposition (ii), p. 71); (iii) for every complete separated linearly
topologised `A`-algebra `B` (continuous structure map `u`) and elements `b₁,…,b_r ∈ B` there is a
unique continuous `A`-algebra homomorphism `A{T} → B` with `T_i ↦ b_i` (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.5.3, p. 70;
7.5.2). No condition is placed on the `b_i`: in contrast with Huber-ring restricted series, where
the `b_i` must be power-bounded, every element of a linearly topologised ring is power-bounded.
For `A = ℤ_p`, `A{T} = ℤ_p⟨T⟩` is the ring of power series `Σ a_n T^n` with `a_n → 0`
`p`-adically and `ℤ_p⟨T⟩/p^{n+1} = (ℤ/p^{n+1})[T]`; for `A` discrete (`I = 0`), `A{T} = A[T]`.
The object is Tau Ceti's; the library proves its noetherianity only for one variable over a
complete nonarchimedean field and for discrete rings (`IsStronglyNoetherian.of_discreteTopology`),
and Mathlib's `MvPowerSeries.isNoetherianRing` concerns the full power-series ring, so (ii) in
general and (i), (iii) on the existing completed-series carrier are the content of this target.

For the lift of `CompletedAway.existsUnique_lift`, the target has a complete Hausdorff uniform ring

- (lift, identity) — at `f = 1`, lifting the identity sends the image of `a` to `a`.
- (lift, unit) — at a unit `u`, lifting the identity sends the inverse

- (lift, zero target) — at `f = 0` and a zero target ring, every element maps to zero.
- (quotient, level zero) — at `f = 1`, the quotient comparison modulo the chosen

composition with `inl` and `inr`; that `(B ⊗̂[A] C) ⧸ J^(n+1) ≃ₐ[A] (B ⊗[A] C) ⧸ J^(n+1)`; that

**Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems.**
(*finite-module-inverse-limit*) Let `A` be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition `I`
and `A_n = A/I^{n+1}`. That every finite `A`-module `M` is `I`-adically separated and complete is
Tau Ceti's `IsAdicComplete.of_finite` (`[IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
[Module.Finite A M] : IsAdicComplete I M`), used here and not restated. Prove that (i) for a
finite `A`-module `M` the `I`-adic topology is the quotient topology from any surjection
`A^n → M`, so every `A`-linear map between finite `A`-modules is continuous and strict for these
topologies (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.3.6 Corollaire, p. 68; 7.2.10; AdicSpacesPartII layer R0's
*noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict* and *noetherian-rod-module-complete* use this and
`IsAdicComplete.of_finite` at the ring of definition `A₀ = A`); (ii) if `(M_n)` is an inverse system
indexed by `ℕ` with `M_n` a finite `A_n`-module and surjective transitions `M_{n+1} → M_n` with
kernel `I^{n+1}M_{n+1}` (equivalently `M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n`), then `M := lim M_n` is a finite
`A`-module and `M/I^{n+1}M ≅ M_n` (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.2.9 Proposition, p. 65); (iii) morphisms of such
systems correspond bijectively to `A`-linear maps of the limits (EGA I Ch. 0, 7.2.10 Corollaire, p.
65). Hence `M ↦ (M/I^{n+1}M)_n` is an equivalence from finite `A`-modules to such compatible
systems (Lean: (ii) is `IsAdicRing.finite_limit`, for the chosen ideal of definition, with the
limit realised as the submodule of compatible families in `∏ M_n`; (i) and (iii) are specified in
this README only); the affine case `Coh(X, I) ≃` finite `Â`-modules of Stacks is proved by the same limit
argument (Stacks Tag 087W, Lem. 30.23.1). For `A = ℤ_p` and `M_n = ℤ/p^{n+1} ⊕ ℤ/p`,
`lim M_n = ℤ_p ⊕ ℤ/p`; for `M_n = ℤ/p^{n+1}·e_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ ℤ/p^{n+1}·e_n` with rank growing with `n` the
kernel condition fails and `lim M_n` is not finite. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a *adic-ring*;
DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.T.1 and 1.1; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.of_finite`; Mathlib
`AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian`,
`Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson`, `Module.Finite`, `AdicCompletion.map_exact`.

**Checks for the completed-tensor maps.**

All completed tensor products below have adic structure maps from the base. The chosen
factor ideals are used in `tensorIdeal`; their individual exponents are not canonical.

- (tensor ideal, discrete) — for a discrete field `k`, `tensorIdeal k k k = 0`.
- (tensor ideal, radical) — under `ℤ_p ⊗[ℤ_p] ℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p`, the tensor ideal has radical `(p)`.
- (tensor ideal, zero factor) — when the left factor is zero, the tensor ideal is the unit ideal
  of the zero tensor ring.
- `completedTensor_inl_self` — the left inclusion into `B ⊗̂_A A` is bijective.
- `completedTensor_inl_zero_factor` — when the right factor is zero, the left inclusion is zero.
- `completedTensor_inr_self` — the right inclusion into `A ⊗̂_A C` is bijective.
- `completedTensor_inr_zero_factor` — when the left factor is zero, the right inclusion is zero.
- `completedTensor_inclusions_distinct` — over a discrete field, the two polynomial
  generators in `k[X] ⊗̂_k k[X]` have distinct images under `inl` and `inr`.
- `completedTensor_lift_self` — the lift of two identity maps sends `inl(a)·inr(b)` to `ab`.
- `completedTensor_lift_zero_target` — a lift to a zero ring sends every element to zero.
- `completedTensor_lift_two_evaluations` — over a discrete field, lifting evaluation at `0`
  on the left and at `1` on the right sends the two polynomial generators to `0` and `1`.
- `completedTensor_quotient_level_zero` — the quotient comparison modulo `J` kills `x ∈ J`,
  where `J = tensorIdeal A B C` in the ordinary tensor algebra.
- `completedTensor_quotient_level_one` — modulo `J²`, `x ∈ J ∖ J²` has nonzero square-zero image.
- `completedTensor_quotient_zero_factor` — with zero right factor, every quotient comparison is zero.
- `completedTensor_map_identity` — the compatible triple of identity maps fixes every tensor.
- `completedTensor_map_evaluation` — the triple consisting of `id_k`, evaluation at `0`, and
  evaluation at `1` sends the two generators to `0` and `1` respectively.
- `completedTensor_map_zero_ring` — over the zero ring the induced identity map has only zero values.
- `restrictedEquiv_no_variables` — with no variables, the comparison sends the right coefficient
  `c` to the constant series `c`.
- `restrictedEquiv_one_variable` — with one variable, the left variable maps to the target variable.
- `restrictedEquiv_two_variables` — over a nonzero right factor, the images of the two left
  variables are distinct.

The induced maps of completed tensor products are continuous, functorial (identity and
composition) and restrict on the factors to the given maps. The comparison of the completions
formed with any two choices of ideals of definition is bicontinuous and fixes every ordinary
tensor. The restricted-series comparison is pinned on coefficients and variables (EGA I Ch. 0,
7.7.1, 7.7.6).

The category `IsAdicRing.FiniteAdicModuleSystem A I` is the full subcategory of
`ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ FGModuleCat A` with the annihilator, surjectivity and power-kernel conditions above.
`finiteModuleReduction` uses the actual quotients `M/I^{n+1}M` and their quotient maps;
`finiteModuleReductionFunctor` also reduces each linear map. The named theorem
`finiteModuleReduction_equivalence` identifies this functor as an equivalence when `A`
is complete noetherian adic and `I` is an ideal of definition; `finiteModuleReduction_limit`
identifies reconstruction with the submodule of compatible families.

**Checks for finite adic module systems.**

- `finiteSystem_zero_module` — reduction of a zero module is zero at every level and satisfies
  the adic-system axioms.
- `finiteSystem_discrete` — for `I = 0`, reduction is the constant diagram on the original module.
- `finiteSystem_unit_ideal` — reduction for `I = A` is zero at every level; the constant system
  on a nonzero `A` fails the annihilator condition.
- `finiteSystem_square_zero_level` — if `a ∈ I` but `a ∉ I²`, the image of `a` modulo `I²`
  is nonzero and has square zero; level `1` uses `I²`.
- `finiteSystem_map_zero` — the zero linear map induces zero on every quotient.
- `finiteSystem_map_scalar` — multiplication by `a` sends the class of `x` to the class of `ax`.
- `finiteSystem_map_identity` — the identity fixes each quotient class.

### F0.2 the formal spectrum

The finite-module topology interfaces of *finite-module-inverse-limit* (i) are: for every
surjection `A^r → M`, the adic topology on `M` makes this map an open quotient map; and every
linear map between finite modules is continuous and strict for their adic topologies (EGA I Ch. 0,
7.3.6). Here strict means that the quotient by the kernel has the subspace topology of the image.


**The formal spectrum `Spf A` of an adic ring.** (*formal-spectrum*) Let `A` be an adic ring of
finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a *adic-ring*) with ideal of definition `I`; noetherianity of `A` is assumed only
for the noetherian statements. The formal spectrum `Spf A` is the locally ringed space defined as
follows. Its underlying space is the closed subspace of `Spec A` consisting of the open prime
ideals, which is `V(I) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I` and is homeomorphic to `Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1})`
for every `n` via the quotient maps (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.1–10.1.2, pp. 180–181; Stacks Tag 0AHY,
§87.2 states the same definition). For each `n` let `O_n` be the structure sheaf of
`Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1})` transported to `V(I)`; the structure sheaf is `O_{Spf A} := lim_n O_n`, the
limit in sheaves of commutative rings along the reduction maps (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.2 Définition,
p. 181). Then `Γ(Spf A, O) ≅ A` (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.3 Proposition, p. 181); for `f ∈ A` and
`D(f)` (written also for the open `D(f) ∩ V(I)` of `Spf A`), `Γ(D(f), O) ≅ A_{f}` (the completed
localisation,
*completed-localization*) and `(D(f), O|_{D(f)}) ≅ Spf A_{f}` (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.4 Proposition,
p. 181); the stalk at an open prime `p` is `colim_{f ∉ p} A_{f}`, a local ring with residue field
`Frac(A ⧸ p)`, noetherian when `A` is noetherian (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.6 Proposition, p. 182). A
continuous homomorphism `φ : B → A` induces a morphism of locally ringed spaces
`Spf φ : Spf A → Spf B`, `q ↦ φ⁻¹(q)` (EGA I Ch. I, 10.2.1). Convention: `Spf A` is a locally
ringed space (Mathlib `LocallyRingedSpace`); the topology of the rings of sections is not part of
the data (see *locally-noetherian-formal-scheme*), and for quasi-compact open `U` the ring
`Γ(U, O)` carries the limit topology of the discrete rings `Γ(U, O_n)`, recorded in
`Spf.sectionsTopology`; for an arbitrary open `U` it carries the initial topology for the
restrictions to the quasi-compact opens contained in `U` (`quotientSectionsTopology` below),
which is not discrete in general (EGA I Ch. 0, 3.8.1, p. 35). Define `FormalScheme.Spf`
(`Spf A : LocallyRingedSpace` for `A` with `IsAdicRing A`); prove `FormalScheme.Spf.mem_iff` (`p ∈ Spf A ↔ IsOpen (p : Set A)` for a prime `p` of `A`, and `IsOpen (p : Set A) ↔ I ≤ p` for any ideal of definition `I`),
`FormalScheme.Spf.homeomorphSpecQuotient` (`Spf A ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum (A ⧸ I^(n+1))` for every `n` and
every ideal of definition `I`), `FormalScheme.Spf.globalSectionsIso`
(`Γ(Spf A, ⊤) ≅ CommRingCat.of A`, a homeomorphism for the limit topology on sections),
`FormalScheme.Spf.basicOpen` (the open subset `D(f) ∩ Spf A` for `f ∈ A`, with `basicOpen_mul`,
`basicOpen_one` and `Spf.isBasis_basicOpen`), `FormalScheme.Spf.basicOpenSectionsIso`
(`Γ(D(f), O) ≅ AdicRing.CompletedAway A f`, compatibly with restriction `D(f) ⊇ D(g)` and
the restriction maps of *completed-localization*), `FormalScheme.Spf.restrictBasicOpenIso`
(`(D(f), O|) ≅ Spf (AdicRing.CompletedAway A f)` as locally ringed spaces),
`FormalScheme.Spf.stalk_isLocalRing` (every stalk is a local ring, part of the
`LocallyRingedSpace` structure, and `residueField (stalk p) ≅ FractionRing (A ⧸ p)`),
`FormalScheme.Spf.stalk_isNoetherianRing` (if `A` is noetherian, every stalk of `Spf A` is
noetherian), `FormalScheme.Spf.map` (for a continuous ring homomorphism `φ : B →+* A`,
`Spf.map φ : Spf A ⟶ Spf B` with base `q ↦ q.comap φ`, with `Spf.map_id` and `Spf.map_comp`),
`FormalScheme.Spf.fromSpecQuotient` (for an ideal of definition `J`, the canonical morphism
`Spec (A ⧸ J) ⟶ Spf A`, a homeomorphism on spaces, whose sheaf map `O_{Spf A} → O_{Spec(A/J)}` is
surjective; write `J^Δ` for its kernel sheaf. When `A` is noetherian this is the
finite-module construction of *associated-formal-module*, F0.6)
(EGA I Ch. I, 10.3.2) and `FormalScheme.Spf.sectionsTopology` (for
quasi-compact open `U`, the topology on `Γ(U, O)` as limit of the discrete rings `Γ(U, O_n)`;
restriction maps are continuous and for `U = Spf A` it is the `I`-adic topology). `Spf ℤ_p`
(`p`-adic) is a single point with `Γ = ℤ_p` and stalk `ℤ_p`, whereas `Spec ℤ_p` has two points;
`Spf k[x]⟦t⟧` (`t`-adic) has underlying space `Spec k[x]` and `Γ(D(x), O) = k[x, x⁻¹]⟦t⟧`; for
`A` discrete, `Spf A = Spec A` as locally ringed spaces. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a *adic-ring*;
*completed-localization*; Mathlib `PrimeSpectrum`, `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus`,
`PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_zeroLocus`, `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.locallyRingedSpaceObj`,
`TopCat.Sheaf`, `IsAdicComplete`, `Ideal.Quotient.mk`, `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.createsLimits`,
`PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens`, `TopCat.Presheaf.stalk`,
`TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward`.

**Checks.**

- `Spf_padicInt_points` (computation) — the underlying space of `Spf ℤ_[p]` (`p`-adic topology) is
  a single point, the prime `(p)`, and the global sections are `ℤ_[p]`.
- `Spf_discrete_eq_Spec` (compatibility) — for a ring `R` with the discrete topology,
  `Spf R ≅ Spec.locallyRingedSpaceObj R` as locally ringed spaces (Mathlib `Spec`).
- `Spf_globalSections` (characterisation) — for every adic ring of finite ideal type `A`,
  `Γ(Spf A, ⊤) ≅ A` as rings, compatibly with `Spf.map`.
- `Spf_padicInt_ne_Spec` (non-example) — `Spf ℤ_[p]` (`p`-adic) is not isomorphic to `Spec ℤ_[p]`:
  the latter has two points. A wrong definition taking all primes of `A` (not only open ones) fails
  this test.
- `Spf_basicOpen_eq_empty` (degenerate) — for `A = ℤ_[p]` and `f = p`, the basic open `D(p)` of
  `Spf A` is empty and `CompletedAway A p = 0`.
- `Spf_powerSeries_polynomial_sections` (computation) — for `A = k[X]⟦T⟧` with the `T`-adic
  topology, `Γ(D(X), O_{Spf A}) ≅ (Localization.Away X)⟦T⟧` and the underlying space is
  homeomorphic to `Spec k[X]`.
- `Spf_zero_isEmpty` (degenerate, zero ring) — `Spf 0 = ∅` (no primes), and `Spf A = ∅` iff
  `A = 0`: a nonzero adic ring has an open prime, since `V(I) = Spec (A ⧸ I) ≠ ∅` because `I ≠ A`
  for nonzero `A` (separatedness). `Γ(∅, O) = 0` agrees with `A = 0`.
- `Spf_field` (degenerate, field) — a field `k` carries only the discrete adic topology, so
  `Spf k = Spec k` is one point with `Γ = k`; `Spf ℚ_[p]` does not exist, `ℚ_[p]` with its valuation
  topology not being an adic ring.

- `Spf_basicOpen_zero` (degenerate) — `D(0) ∩ V(I) = ∅`.
- `Spf_basicOpen_one` (compatibility) — `D(1) ∩ V(I) = V(I)`.
- `Spf_basicOpen_mul` (convention) — `D(fg) ∩ V(I) = (D(f) ∩ V(I)) ∩ (D(g) ∩ V(I))`.

**`Spf A` depends only on the topology of `A`.** (*spf-ideal-independence*) Let `A` be an adic
ring of finite ideal type and `I`, `J` two ideals of definition of `A` (the same topology).
`FormalScheme.Spf.ideal_independence` and `FormalScheme.Spf.ideal_independence_compat` assert that the locally
ringed spaces `Spf_I A` and `Spf_J A` constructed from the systems
`(Spec A ⧸ I^{n+1})_n` and `(Spec A ⧸ J^{n+1})_n` are canonically isomorphic: the isomorphism is
the identity on the common underlying space `V(I) = V(J) ⊆ Spec A`, is compatible with the
identifications of global sections with `A`, and commutes with the canonical morphisms
`Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) → Spf A` and `Spec(A ⧸ J^{m+1}) → Spf A`; both agree with EGA's limit over the
filtered set of all ideals of definition (EGA I Ch. I, 10.1.1, pp. 180–181; EGA I Ch. 0, 7.1.8–7.1.9,
p. 62: the adic topologies defined by the ideals of definition coincide). Consequently `Spf A` is
a functor of the topological ring `A` alone. For `A = k[x]⟦t⟧`, `I = (t)` and `J = (t², xt)` are
ideals of definition and both constructions give underlying space `Spec k[x]` and the same
sheaf; for `A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧` with `I = (p, T)` and `J = (p², T)`, `Spf` is a single point in both
constructions. *Needs:* *formal-spectrum*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a *adic-ring*; Mathlib `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_radical`,
`IsAdicComplete`.

The locally ringed-space carrier is `FormalScheme.AffineSpectrumData A I`: its points are
`V(I)`, its basic opens have membership `f ∉ 𝔭`, and its section ring on `D(f)` is
`AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f))) (Localization.Away f)`.
Thus the displayed ideal determines the completion, including its quotient system.
The restriction from `D(f)` to `D(g)` for `g ∈ √(fA + I)` preserves the canonical
images of every coefficient of `A`; this specifies the maps of completed localizations.
`affineSpectrumData A I hI` constructs these data for an ideal of definition, and `Spf A`
uses the chosen ideal. For that choice the section rings are definitionally `CompletedAway A f`;
`FormalScheme.affineSpectrumData_restriction_chosen` identifies the conjugated restrictions
with the restriction maps of *completed-localization*. The comparison of two ideals therefore compares their respective
completed-localization sheaves, using cofinality of the powers of the ideals
(EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.4, pp. 180–181).

**Checks for the ideal-dependent affine spectrum.**

- `affineSpectrumData_zero_ideal` — if zero defines the topology, sections on `D(f)`
  recover the uncompleted `Localization.Away f`.
- `affineSpectrumData_nilpotent_open` — if `f ∈ √I`, then `D(f)` is empty and its
  section ring is zero, even when the ordinary localization is nonzero.
- `affineSpectrumData_chosen_sections` — specializing to `TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpacesPartII.IsAdicRing.ideal A` gives
  the existing `CompletedAway A f` section comparison without an additional isomorphism.

**Checks for the affine formal spectrum and its quotient homeomorphism.**

- `Spf_discrete_eq_Spec` — for a discrete adic ring, the constructed locally ringed space
  is isomorphic to Mathlib's `Spec.locallyRingedSpaceObj A`.
- `Spf_zero_ringedSpace` — the zero ring gives the empty locally ringed space with zero global sections.
- `Spf_padicInt_sections` — `Spf ℤ_p` has exactly one point and global-section ring `ℤ_p`.
- `Spf_basicOpen_zero_ringedSpace`, `Spf_basicOpen_one_ringedSpace`,
  `Spf_basicOpen_mul_ringedSpace` — the constructed sheaf's opens satisfy `D(0) = ∅`,
  `D(1) = Spf A`, and `D(fg) = D(f) ∩ D(g)`.
- `Spf_globalSections_empty` — the global-section comparison for a zero ring sends every section to zero.
- `Spf_globalSections_nonzero` — for a nonzero ring it sends the unit section to a nonzero element.
- `Spf_globalSections_padic_square` — the section corresponding to `2 ∈ ℤ₂` has square
  corresponding to `4`, which is nonzero.
- `Spf_globalSections_local_unit` — on the discrete polynomial spectrum, the global section
  corresponding to `X` becomes a unit when restricted to `D(X)`.
- `Spf_globalSections_id` — conjugating the section map of the identity formal-spectrum morphism
  by the global-section comparisons gives the identity of `A`.
- `Spf_map_identity` — the continuous identity induces the identity locally ringed-space map.
- `Spf_map_zero_source` — a formal-spectrum map from the zero ring's spectrum has empty range.
- `Spf_map_evaluations` — over a discrete field, evaluation at `0` and at `1` induce distinct
  maps from `Spec k` to `Spec k[X]`.

`FormalScheme.Spf.globalSections_restrict` identifies restriction of the global section
associated with `a ∈ A` with the canonical image of `a` in every `CompletedAway A f`.
- `Spf_quotient_homeomorph_zero` — with ideal zero and `n = 0`, pulling back the image prime
  along `A → A/0` recovers the original prime.
- `Spf_quotient_homeomorph_unit` — with the unit ideal and `n = 1`, the homeomorphism has empty range.
- `Spf_quotient_homeomorph_square` — for `A = k⟦X⟧` with the `X`-adic topology and
  `I = (X)`, at `n = 1` the unique open prime maps to `(X)/(X²)` in `k[X]/(X²)`;
  the quotient retains the square-zero coordinate.


**Morphisms into `Spf A` and automatic continuity.** (*spf-morphism-correspondence*) Let `X` be a
formal scheme (*locally-noetherian-formal-scheme*) and `A` an adic ring of finite ideal type with
ideal of definition `I`; that `I` is finitely generated is used for automatic continuity. Prove

`X → Spf A` and ring homomorphisms `φ : A → Γ(X, O_X)` that are continuous on affine formal opens,
i.e. such that for every affine formal open `U ≅ Spf B` of `X` the composite
`A → Γ(U, O_X) ≅ B` is continuous; equivalently `φ(a)` vanishes in the residue field `κ(x)` for
all `a ∈ I` and `x ∈ X` (EGA I Ch. I, 10.2.2; 10.4.6 Proposition, p. 186). In particular, for
adic rings `A`, `B` of finite ideal type, `Hom_LRS(Spf B, Spf A) ≃ {continuous ring homomorphisms
A → B}` (EGA I Ch. I, after 10.2.2, p. 183; Stacks Tag 0AHY, §87.2, equation 87.2.0.1), so
`Spf` is a fully faithful contravariant functor from adic rings of finite ideal type (with
continuous homomorphisms) to locally ringed spaces, and every morphism of locally ringed spaces
between formal schemes is continuous on rings of sections (it is a morphism of topologically
ringed spaces in the sense of EGA I Ch. I, 10.4.5). Here `Γ(U, O_X)` for an arbitrary open `U`
carries the initial topology for the restrictions to the affine formal opens contained in `U`;
this is the sheaf topology of EGA I Ch. 0, 3.8.1, p. 35, and on `Spf A` it is

ideal `(p, T)` of `ℤ_p⟦T⟧`, via `S ↦` image of `S` (continuity forces the image of `S` to be
topologically nilpotent); `Hom(Spec F_p, Spf ℤ_p)` is a single point (`p ↦ 0`), whereas
`Hom(Spec ℚ_p, Spf ℤ_p)` is empty, the ring map `ℤ_p → ℚ_p` not being continuous for the discrete
topology on `ℚ_p` since `p` is not nilpotent. *Needs:* *formal-spectrum*;
*completed-localization*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.1a *adic-ring*; *locally-noetherian-formal-scheme*; *lrs-morphism-gluing*;

The sheaf in *formal-spectrum* is specified by `Spf.quotientSheaf`, the pushforward of
`O_Spec(A/J)` along `fromSpecQuotient`, and `quotientProjection`, its actual structure map.
`fromSpecQuotient_globalSections`, `fromSpecQuotient_points`,

map, space, quotient and transition directions. `quotientDiagram` uses the powers
`J^(n+1)` and `quotientConeIsLimit` identifies its canonical cone with `O_Spf A`.
`quotientSectionsTopology` is the topology on sections of the limit of the pseudo-discrete
quotient sheaves. On a quasi-compact open `U` it is the initial topology for the quotient-section
maps `Γ(U, O) → Γ(U, O_n)` into discrete rings. On an arbitrary open `U` it is the initial
