`AlgebraicGeometry.tildeHomIso` uses Mathlib's `tilde` on `ModuleCat A`,
with finite presentation required only of the source module; the target module
is arbitrary. `SheafOfModules.internalHom_isCoherent` uses finite presentation
of both sheaves on a locally noetherian scheme (EGA I 1.3.12(ii), pp. 88–89;
6.1.1, pp. 140–141).

**Closure properties of coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme.**
(*coherent-formal-module-properties*) Let `X` be locally noetherian. Prove `FormalScheme.isCoherentRing_structureSheaf` (`O_X` is a coherent sheaf of
rings; hence `IsFinitePresentation ↔` finite type with kernels of `O^n → F` of finite type),
`FormalScheme.Coh.ker_mem` (`Coh X` is closed under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions in
`O_X`-modules), `FormalScheme.Coh.tensor` (`F ⊗ G` and `Hom(F, G)` are coherent for coherent
`F`, `G`), `FormalScheme.cohPullback` (`f^* : Coh Y ⥤ Coh X` for a morphism of locally
noetherian formal schemes, with `(g ∘ f)^* ≅ f^* ∘ g^*`), `FormalScheme.coherentSystemFunctor`
(`F ↦ F_n := F ⊗ O_X/𝒥^(n+1)`, a coherent `O_{X_n}`-module; the content is
*coherent-as-inverse-system*), `FormalScheme.Coh.sectionsTopology` (for quasi-compact open `U`,
the limit topology on `Γ(U, F) = lim Γ(U, F_n)`; maps of coherent modules are continuous and
coherent submodules have closed sections) and `FormalScheme.Coh.isIdealOfDefinition_coherent`
(every ideal of definition of `X` is a coherent `O_X`-module). The abelian instance and these statements
follow from *affine-coherent-equivalence* (iii), pullback of associated finite modules
(EGA I Ch. I, 10.10.8, p. 203), and *coherent-as-inverse-system*
(EGA I Ch. I, 10.11.1, p. 204; 10.11.6, pp. 204–205). *Needs:*
*coherent-formal-module*; *affine-coherent-equivalence*; *associated-formal-module*;
*coherent-as-inverse-system*; *internal-hom-sheaf-of-modules*.

`FormalScheme.isCoherentRing_structureSheaf` states the local kernel criterion:
on every open formal subscheme, the kernel of every map from a finite free
module to the structure module is of finite type (EGA I 10.10.3, p. 202;
10.11.1, p. 204). `Coh.sectionsTopology_limit` identifies `Coh.sectionsTopology`
with the topology induced by all projections to the discrete sections of the
coherent thickening system, for any finite-type ideal of definition.
`Coh.sectionsTopology_continuous` and `Coh.sectionsTopology_closed` state
continuity of coherent morphisms and closedness of the sections of coherent
submodules (EGA I 10.11.3–6, pp. 204–205).

**Checks for coherent section topologies.**

- `Coh.sectionsTopology_discrete` — over an ordinary locally noetherian scheme, sections on a quasi-compact open have the discrete topology.
- `Coh.sectionsTopology_empty` — sections on the empty open have their unique, discrete topology.
- `Coh.sectionsTopology_affine` — global sections of `M^Δ` have exactly the `I`-adic module topology transported along `completedTildeGlobalIso`, for any ideal of definition `I`.

For locally noetherian `X`, `FormalScheme.Coh.coker_mem` isolates the cokernel
conclusion of `Coh.ker_mem`. `Coh.closedUnderKernels` and
`Coh.closedUnderCokernels` express closure for every limiting kernel fork and
colimiting cokernel cofork, using invariance of finite presentation under
isomorphism. `Coh.containsZero` uses the free sheaf of rank zero, and
`Coh.closedUnderFiniteProducts` uses finite direct sums. These yield
`FormalScheme.cohAbelian` through Mathlib's full-subcategory construction;
its preadditive structure is definitionally `Preadditive.fullSubcategory`.
The geometric input is coherence of the structure sheaf (EGA I Ch. I,
10.10.3, p. 202; 10.11.1, p. 204); kernels, cokernels and finite products
are formed in `SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf` before restricting to `Coh X`.

**Checks.** `cohAbelian_preadditive` compares the preadditive structure with
Mathlib's explicit full-subcategory instance by reflexivity;
`cohAbelian_add` computes `(f + g).hom = f.hom + g.hom`;
`cohAbelian_zero` computes the underlying zero morphism; and
`cohAbelian_comp` computes the underlying composite. All four are reflexivity
checks for every locally noetherian formal scheme, including the empty one.

**Formal glueing of modules along a flat map that is an isomorphism modulo `I`.**
(*formal-glueing-of-modules*) Let `φ₀ : R → S` be a flat ring map and `I ⊆ R` a finitely
generated ideal such that `R/I → S/IS` is an isomorphism (e.g. `S = AdicCompletion I R` for `R`
noetherian). Prove that, given an `R`-module `N`, an `S`-module `M′` and an `S`-linear map
`φ : M′ → N ⊗_R S` whose kernel and cokernel are `I`-power torsion, there are an `R`-module `M`,
an `R`-linear map `ψ : M → N` and an isomorphism `M ⊗_R S ≅ M′` compatible with `φ` and `ψ`, with
`Ker ψ ≅ Ker φ` and `Coker ψ ≅ Coker φ` (Stacks Tag 0ALK, More on Algebra Lem. 15.91.17 (1),
whose proof reduces to the glueing equivalence Prop. 15.91.16); the dual statement for
`φ : M ⊗_R S → N′` holds likewise (Stacks Tag 0ALK (2)). For `R = ℤ_(p)`, `S = ℤ_p`, `I = (p)`,
`N = R`, `M′ = pℤ_p ⊂ ℤ_p = N ⊗ S` (cokernel `F_p`): `M = pℤ_(p)`, `ψ` the inclusion; for
`N = 0`, `M′ = ℤ/p` (`φ = 0`, kernel `ℤ/p`): `M = ℤ/p`, whose base change to `ℤ_p` is `M′`.
*Needs:* Mathlib `Module.Flat`, `Ideal.FG`, `Localization.Away`,
`AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian`.

`FormalModuleGluing.into_baseChange` and `out_of_baseChange` state both directions
using actual modules, kernels, quotient cokernels and tensor products. The
scalar map is flat, the given ideal is finitely generated, and its induced
quotient ring map is bijective. A characteristic equation on every pure tensor
fixes each descended map and the comparison isomorphism. Power torsion is
quantified element by element; no uniform annihilating exponent is assumed
([Stacks, Tag 0ALK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ALK)).

**Checks for the power-torsion hypotheses of module gluing.**

- `formalGluing_torsion_zero_ideal` — every module is power torsion for the zero ideal.
- `formalGluing_torsion_unit_ideal` — for the unit ideal, only the zero module is power torsion.
- `formalGluing_torsion_wrong_prime` — `ℚ/ℤ` is not `(2)`-power torsion: the class of `1/3` survives every power of `2`.

**Coherent formal modules with proper support form Serre subcategories.**
(*proper-support-serre-subcategory*) Let `S` be a noetherian scheme, `f : X → S` of finite type,
`𝓘 ⊆ O_X` a quasi-coherent ideal and `Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) ≃ Coh(X, 𝓘)` (*coherent-as-inverse-system*).
Prove that the following full subcategories are Serre subcategories (Mathlib
`ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`: closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions): (1) the objects `G = (G_n)` such that `Supp G_0` (`= Supp G_n` for
all `n`) is proper over `S`; (2) the objects annihilated by the ideal sheaf of some closed
subscheme `Z ⊆ X` proper over `S` (Stacks Tag 0CYV, Lem. 30.26.11). For `X = A¹_{ℤ_p}` over
`S = Spec ℤ_p` and `𝓘 = (p)`: `Ô_{V(x)}` lies in both subcategories, `Ô_X` in neither (its
support `A¹_{F_p}` is not proper). *Needs:* *coherent-as-inverse-system*; Mathlib
`ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`.

`properCohProperty_isSerreClass` states closure under subobjects, quotients and
extensions for the proper-support property on the actual coherent category.
The distinct condition of being annihilated by the completed ideal of an
algebraic proper closed subscheme is the second property in the target above
(Stacks Tag 0CYV); it is not identified with proper support by definition.

### F0.9 projective geometry over a noetherian base, stated for this roadmap's use

The two results of this subsection are standard projective geometry over a noetherian base. The
Serre finiteness and vanishing statements are SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2
(§2.6, `ample_serre_vanishing`) and Chow's lemma is SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (§4.12, `chow_lemma`);
StableReduction Layer 2 is the sole owner of ordinary projective bundles, tensor powers,
nonvanishing opens and ampleness. F0 imports this package, including its universal quotient
and arbitrary base-change isomorphism; the displayed names below are imported interfaces or
compatibility abbreviations. The remaining clauses (compatibility with the chosen formal
thickenings, the eventual bijectivity of `M_n → Γ(X, M̃(n))` and the dévissage) are F0
targets because the existence and algebraisation theorems above need them in exactly this form.

**Projective bundles, ample sheaves and Serre finiteness and vanishing over a noetherian
base.** (*projective-bundles-ample-serre*) For a noetherian ring `A` and a finite `A`-module
`E`, use StableReduction Layer 2's projective bundle `P(E) = Proj(Sym E)` with its universal property
(morphisms `S → P(E)` over `Spec A` correspond to invertible quotients of `E ⊗ 𝒪_S`) (EGA II
4.2.3). Identify its base-change isomorphism along `Spec A/I^{n+1} → Spec A`
with the projective bundle on the formal thickening (EGA II 3.5.3).
For `X` proper over `A` with an ample invertible sheaf `L` and a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the
facts that some power of `L` is very ample (EGA II 4.6.11), that the `A`-modules `Hⁱ(X, F)` are
finitely generated (EGA III₁ 3.2.1, finiteness for proper morphisms; Stacks Tag 02O5), and that
`Hⁱ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗n}) = 0` for every `i > 0` and all `n ≫ 0` (EGA III₁ 2.2.1, 2.2.2, Serre's
theorem; Stacks Tag 0B5U) are SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.6, `ample_serre_vanishing`,
Stacks Tag 01XO) and are used here with `A` noetherian and `X` proper over `A`, not restated.
For a graded algebra `S` of finite type over `A` generated in degree
`1`, `X = Proj S` and a finitely generated graded `S`-module `M`, prove that the maps
`M_n → Γ(X, M̃(n))` are bijective for `n ≫ 0` (EGA III₁ 2.3.1–2.3.2). *Needs:*
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.6, `ample_serre_vanishing`); StableReduction layer 2; Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

In this imported interface, `AlgebraicGeometry.LineQuotient` retains a locally rank-one sheaf
and an epimorphism from the pulled-back module. `ProjectiveBundleData` represents these quotients with
the equation identifying the pulled-back universal quotient map.
`nonempty_projectiveBundleData`, `ProjectiveBundleData.baseChange` and
`ProjectiveBundleData.isProper` state existence, arbitrary base change and properness.

`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedTwistSections G ℳ n U` consists of functions on `U`
with values in the localizations of `M` at the underlying primes, locally given
by a homogeneous fraction `m/f` with `deg(m) = deg(f) + n`. The algebra has an
`ℕ`-grading `G`, the module has a `ℤ`-grading `ℳ`, and multiplication respects
these gradings. `gradedTwist G ℳ n` is the corresponding module sheaf on
Mathlib's `Proj G`, with pointwise scalar multiplication;
`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedTwist_restrict` identifies restriction with restriction
of these functions of primes. Thus the convention is `M(n)_d = M_{d+n}`. `gradedSections G ℳ n` is the
canonical additive map to its global sections, sending `m` to `m/1`.
For `A` noetherian, `S` a finite-type `A`-algebra generated by `G 1`, and
`M` a finite `S`-module with the stated direct-sum grading,
`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedSections_bijective` asserts that there exists
`n₀ : ℕ` such that this map is bijective for every `n ≥ n₀`.
No ampleness hypothesis is needed (EGA III₁, 2.3.1, pp. 102–103;
the related finite-type corollary is 2.3.2, p. 104).

**Checks for twisted graded modules and their sections.**

- `gradedTwistSections_empty` — the empty open has only the zero section.
- `gradedTwistSections_zeroModule` — every open has only the zero section for the zero module.
- `gradedTwistSections_fraction` — for `f ∈ S_d` and `m ∈ M_{d+n}`, the fraction `m/f` is a section on `D₊(f)`, including the empty open when `f = 0`.
- `gradedTwist_zeroModule` — the sheaf associated to every twist of the zero module is zero.
- `gradedTwist_structure` — the regular graded module at twist zero gives the structure sheaf.
- `gradedTwist_projectiveLine` — over a field, `O(-1)` on `P¹` has zero global sections and `O(1)` has nonzero global sections; this fixes the sign of the shift.
- `gradedSections_zeroModule` — for the zero module the canonical map is bijective in every degree.
- `gradedSections_polynomial` — for `S = k[X₀,…,Xᵣ]` with its regular graded module, the canonical map is bijective in every nonnegative degree, including `r = 0` and `n = 0`.
- `gradedSections_torsion` — if `S` is generated in degree one and a nonzero homogeneous `m` is killed by `S₁`, then its section is zero and that degree's map is not injective. This applies to `M = k[X₀,X₁]/(X₀,X₁)` in degree zero and prevents replacing eventual bijectivity by bijectivity in every degree.

**Checks for projective bundles.**

- `LineQuotient_zero` — a line quotient of zero forces the test scheme to be empty.
- `LineQuotient_rankOne` — a quotient of the unit line is an isomorphism.
- `LineQuotient_rankTwo` — the two coordinate quotients over a field are inequivalent.
- `ProjectiveBundleData_zero` — the projective bundle of zero is empty.
- `ProjectiveBundleData_rankOne` — the projective bundle of the unit line is the base.
- `ProjectiveBundleData_unique` — two representing objects are isomorphic over the base,
  compatibly with their universal lines.

**Chow's lemma and dévissage over a noetherian base.** (*chow-lemma-devissage*) Chow's lemma —
for a separated morphism of finite type `X → S` with `S` noetherian there is a projective (in
particular proper, surjective) morphism `X′ → X` which is an isomorphism over a dense open of
`X` and such that `X′ → S` is quasi-projective, projective when `X → S` is proper (EGA II 5.6.1,
5.6.2; [Stacks, 30.18.1, Tag 0200](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0200)) —
is the SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (§4.12, `chow_lemma`) contract used here.
`AlgebraicGeometry.chowModification` states it on scheme carriers: finite type is
`LocallyOfFiniteType f` together with `QuasiCompact f`; the dense open `U` has
`IsIso (pullback.snd π U.ι)`. The conclusion includes a closed immersion
`X′ → Pᵐ_X` over `X`, an immersion `i : X′ → Pⁿ_S` over `S`, and closedness of
`i` when `f` is proper. Thus both projectivity conclusions are explicit.
The proper case is the one used in EGA III₁, proof of 3.2.1, p. 117.

`AlgebraicGeometry.relativeProjectiveSpace S n` is `S × Pⁿ_ℤ`, formed over the
terminal scheme using Part II's imported `AdicSpace.projectiveSpace`; the map
to `S` is `pullback.fst` ([Stacks, Section 27.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ND)).
For `S = Spec R`, the affine comparison identifies the immersion with the
existing `AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective` condition.

**Checks for `relativeProjectiveSpace`.**

- `relativeProjectiveSpace_zero` — the projection `P⁰_S → S` is an isomorphism.
- `relativeProjectiveSpace_empty` — every dimension over an empty base is empty.
- `relativeProjectiveSpace_affine` — over `Spec R`, the comparison with Part II's
  `projectiveSpace R n` commutes with the structural maps, including for the zero ring.

Dévissage: let `X` be noetherian and `P` a property of coherent
`O_X`-modules such that `0` has `P` and, in every short exact sequence of coherent modules, if
two terms have `P` then so does the third. Prove that if for every integral closed subscheme
`Z ⊆ X` with generic point `ξ` there is a coherent module `G` with `P`, with support exactly `Z`,
whose stalk at `ξ` is a one-dimensional `κ(ξ)`-vector space, then every coherent `O_X`-module has
`P`;
and that if `P` is moreover stable under direct summands, a test module with nonzero stalk at
`ξ` annihilated by the maximal ideal of `O_{X,ξ}` suffices (EGA III₁ 3.1.2, 3.1.3; Stacks Tag 01YI). *Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations
Layer 4 (§4.12, `chow_lemma`); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`.

**Check `coherent_devissage_genericAnnihilation`.** Over `Spec(ℤ/4)`, the structure
module is projective but its residue field is not. Merely requiring a nonzero generic
stalk would therefore be insufficient: the positive-rank variant retains annihilation
by the maximal ideal, as in [Stacks, Lemma 30.12.7, Tag 01YL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YL).

## Layer R2: formal schemes, generic fibres and Hasse domains

This layer builds on layers F0, AdicSpacesPartII R0 and AdicSpacesPartII R1. It develops the formal-scheme side of rigid and adic
geometry over an arbitrary complete rank-one valuation ring `O_K`, not assumed discretely valued:
algebras topologically of finite type and of finite presentation over `O_K` and the admissible ones
among them; admissible formal `O_K`-schemes, Huber's formal schemes of type (S) and Conrad's
category `FS_C`; Huber's functor `t` on locally noetherian formal schemes and the generic-fibre
functor `d` to analytic adic spaces, its comparison with Raynaud's rigid generic fibre and its
invariance under admissible blow-ups; the specialisation map, tubes of locally closed subsets of the
special fibre and rig-points; admissible formal blow-ups with their strict transforms, and Raynaud's
theorem identifying quasi-compact admissible formal schemes localised at admissible blow-ups with
quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid (equivalently adic) spaces; separatedness and properness of a
formal model against its generic fibre, and the dimension, reducedness and pure dimension of
their fibres; flattening by admissible blow-up after Bosch–Lütkebohmert
and Raynaud–Gruson with its proof broken into its lemmas, quasi-finite and bounded-fibre-dimension
formal models, and Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion and topological invariance of affinoidness;
formal completions of schemes and the good-reduction locus; smooth formal schemes, Frobenius lifts
and residue discs; and fractional valuation bounds, section domains and Hasse domains with their
transition maps. Throughout, `K` is a field complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean
absolute value, `O_K` its valuation ring, `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser and `k` the residue field; where a
statement needs `K` discretely valued this is said in the statement.

### R2.1 algebras topologically of finite presentation

**Algebras topologically of finite type and of finite presentation over a complete rank-one
valuation ring; admissible algebras.** (*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*) Standing data:
`K` is a field complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value `|·|`, not assumed
discretely valued; `O_K = K° = {|x| ≤ 1}` is its valuation ring (so `O_K` is noetherian if and only
if `K` is discretely valued); `ϖ ∈ O_K` is a pseudouniformiser, `0 < |ϖ| < 1`; `k = O_K/m_K` is the
residue field. The `ϖ`-adic topology on `O_K` is its valuation topology and does not depend on `ϖ`.
For variables `ξ = (ξ_1, …, ξ_n)`, `O_K⟨ξ⟩` is the ring of restricted power series `Σ c_ν ξ^ν` with
`c_ν ∈ O_K` and `c_ν → 0`, equivalently the `ϖ`-adic completion of `O_K[ξ]`. An `O_K`-algebra `A` is
topologically of finite type (tft) if `A ≅ O_K⟨ξ⟩/a` for some `n` and some ideal `a`; it is
topologically of finite presentation (tfp) if moreover `a` is finitely generated (this does not
depend on the chosen presentation); it is admissible if it is tfp and has no `ϖ`-torsion,
equivalently (`O_K` being a valuation ring) if it is tfp and flat over `O_K`. Such `A` carries the
`ϖ`-adic topology, never the `m_K`-adic one (the two differ when `m_K = m_K²`, e.g. for `K = ℂ_p`);
presentations use finitely many variables; every `O_K`-algebra homomorphism between tft algebras is
continuous. The word "admissible" is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's and must not be confused with EGA's
admissible topological rings. The predicate `IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation` makes sense over any nonarchimedean
base ring; the results here assume the complete rank-one valuation base above. Bosch–Lütkebohmert's
noetherian-base case (II) is outside these statements. The topologically-finite-type half is Tau Ceti's `IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType`,
whose carrier is `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n O` (Tau Ceti's `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`
is the weighted notion, with weighted restricted power series as carrier); this target adds finite
presentation and admissibility. The standing data on the base — a valuation ring of rank one
(Mathlib `Valuation.RankOne`), `ϖ`-adically complete and separated, with `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser
(Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer`) — is bundled as the class `IsCompleteRankOneBase O ϖ`, which
records `ringKrullDim O = 1`, `ϖ ≠ 0`, `¬ IsUnit ϖ`, `IsAdic (ϖ)` and `IsAdicComplete (ϖ) O`; `ValuationRing O` and the domain structure are separate standing hypotheses. In `Huber`, define

**Saturated submodules of finite free modules over tft algebras are finitely generated.**
(*saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*) Let `O_K` be a complete valuation ring of rank one
(Fujiwara–Kato: any height) with `ϖ ∈ m_K` nonzero, `A` a tft `O_K`-algebra
(*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*), `F` a finite free `A`-module and `M ⊆ F` an
`A`-submodule that is `ϖ`-saturated: if `f ∈ F` and `ϖ^m f ∈ M` for some `m ≥ 1`, then `f ∈ M`.
Prove that `M` is finitely generated (BL I §1, Lem. 1.2(c), p. 293). Equivalently, for every
finitely generated `A`-module `N` the `ϖ`-power torsion `N[ϖ^∞]` is finitely generated and
`N/N[ϖ^∞]` is finitely presented; together with noetherianity of `A[1/ϖ]`, this gives adhesiveness of the pair `(A, ϖA)` in the sense of Fujiwara–Kato
(FK Ch. 0, §8.5, Prop. 8.5.3, p. 191, the adhesive reformulation; FK Ch. 0, §9.2(a), Thm 9.2.1, p.
221, adhesiveness of restricted power series over an `a`-adically complete valuation ring of any
height; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Lem. 3.3.2, p. 31, the `M_K ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩^r` form of the lemma for ideals).
Prove moreover (BL I §1, Lem. 1.2(a),(b); Bosch 2014 §7.3, Lem. 7(ii), p. 165, for every submodule
of a finite module over a tft algebra, and Prop. 8, pp. 165–166, completeness and separatedness of
finite modules) that the `ϖ`-adic topology of `F` induces the `ϖ`-adic topology on any submodule
`M`, saturated or not, that a finitely generated `M` is complete, and that it is closed in `F`
provided `A` is `ϖ`-adically separated — for instance when `A` is tfp
(*flat-tft-is-tfp*). Saturation cannot be dropped: for non-discrete `K`, say `K = ℂ_p`, the
`O_K`-submodule `m_K ⊂ O_K` (`A = O_K`, `F = O_K`) is not finitely generated and is not saturated
(`ϖ·1 ∈ m_K`, `1 ∉ m_K`). For `A = O_K⟨T⟩` and `M = (T − c)` with `c ∈ O_K`, `M` is saturated and
generated by one element. *Needs:* *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*.

**A flat algebra topologically of finite type over `O_K` is topologically finitely presented.**
(*flat-tft-is-tfp*) Let `O_K` be complete of rank one (Fujiwara–Kato: any height; `K` need not be
discretely valued) and `A = O_K⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩/a` tft over `O_K`. Prove: (a) `A` is `ϖ`-adically
precomplete (`IsPrecomplete`: every compatible residue system lifts); separatedness is not
part of (a). (b) If `a` is finitely generated, `a` is closed in `O_K⟨ξ⟩`, so `A` is `ϖ`-adically
complete and separated; (c) if `A` has no `ϖ`-torsion (equivalently `A` is `O_K`-flat), then `a` is
finitely generated, hence `A` is admissible (BL I §1, Prop. 1.1(c), p. 293). Prove the global form

flat and `A → ∏_i B_i` is faithfully flat (BL I §1, Prop. 1.7 and the globalisation after it, pp.
296–297; the locality is what makes the global definition of *admissible-formal-scheme* meaningful).
The first form to state is the case of a cover
by basic opens `Spf A⟨f_i⁻¹⟩` with `f_1, …, f_k` generating the unit ideal of `A` (equivalent to

reduces to it since every formal affine open is a finite union of basic opens. Prove the flatness

**Flatness of completed localisation over a tfp valuation-ring algebra.**
(*formal-localization-flatness*) Let `A` be a tfp `O_K`-algebra with its `ϖ`-adic topology
and let `f ∈ A`. On the carrier of *completed-localization*, put

`B/ϖ^m B ≅ (A/ϖ^m A)[1/f]`. This is an isomorphism of `A`-algebras: the class of the image
of `a ∈ A` is sent to the localized class of `a`; the reduction maps as `m` varies commute
with it. Ordinary localisation is flat, so the criterion `flat_iff_forall_flat_quotient`
in *tfp-locality*, applied to the coherent `B`-module `B`, proves `Module.Flat A B`
(BL I §1, Lemma 1.6, pp. 295–296, and the completed-localisation description preceding
Proposition 1.7, p. 296). This supplies the basic-open flatness used in *tfp-locality*;
the quotient criterion itself uses *adic-local-flatness-criterion*, independently of this
corollary. Nondiscrete rank-one valuation bases and tfp algebras with `ϖ`-torsion are allowed.
Tau Ceti's `PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc` applies instead to complete separated
strongly noetherian Tate rings, as used in R3. *Needs:* *completed-localization*;

**Checks.**

- For `A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩` and `f = T`, reduction is

- For `f = 1`, `B = A` and the quotient comparison is the identity. For `f = 0` or

- For `A = O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)` and `f = T`, `B = (O_K/ϖ)[T,T⁻¹]` and the comparison is

### R2.2 admissible formal schemes, type (S) and `FS_C`

**Admissible formal `O_K`-schemes (formal schemes locally topologically of finite presentation without
`ϖ`-torsion).** (*admissible-formal-scheme*) Let `K` be complete with nontrivial rank-one valuation,
`O_K` possibly non-noetherian. A formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf presentation is a formal scheme
`X` of finite ideal type in the sense of layer F0 (*locally-noetherian-formal-scheme*: locally `Spf
A` with `A` an adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition) with a morphism to `Spf O_K`,
that is covered by open formal subschemes isomorphic to `Spf A` with `A` a tfp `O_K`-algebra
carrying the `ϖ`-adic topology; then `ϖO_X` is an ideal of definition and each `X_m = X ⊗_{O_K} O_K/ϖ^{m+1}` is a scheme locally of finite presentation over `O_K/ϖ^{m+1}`. `X` is
admissible if moreover `O_X` has no `ϖ`-torsion; by *tfp-locality* this holds iff every
(equivalently: some covering family of) formal affine open `Spf A` has `A` admissible, iff every
local ring `O_{X,x}` is `O_K`-flat. Admissible is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's notion (tfp +
`ϖ`-torsion-free), distinct from EGA's "admissible ring"; the formal schemes are F0's formal schemes
of finite ideal type, and being locally tfp or admissible is a condition on them, not a new category
of spaces. Morphisms are morphisms of formal `O_K`-schemes; they are automatically adic. The special
fibre is `X_s = X ⊗_{O_K} k`; the underlying topological spaces of `X`, `X_0` and `X_s` coincide and
are locally noetherian (noetherian when `X` is quasi-compact) although `O_X` need not be noetherian.
The category of admissible formal `O_K`-schemes has fibre products: the formal fibre product `X ×_Z
Y` divided by its `ϖ`-power torsion ideal (which is zero if `X` or `Y` is flat over `Z`). A coherent
open ideal on `X` is a coherent ideal sheaf `𝒜 ⊆ O_X` which locally on `X` contains `ϖ^m O_X` for
some `m` (a single `m` works when `X` is quasi-compact). When `K` is discretely valued, admissible
formal `O_K`-schemes are exactly the locally noetherian formal schemes flat and adic locally of
finite type over `Spf O_K` (F0's notions). In `FormalScheme`, define `IsLocallyTFP` (`X` over `Spf
O_K` has an open cover by `Spf A` with `A` `IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation` over `O_K`, `ϖ`-adic
topology), `IsAdmissible` (`X` is `IsLocallyTFP` and `O_X` has no `ϖ`-torsion), `specialFibre` (`X_s := X ×_{Spf O_K} Spec k`, a `k`-scheme locally of finite type, with a homeomorphism of underlying
spaces `X_s → X`), `admissiblePullback` (for admissible `X → Z ← Y`, the closed formal subscheme of
`X ×_Z Y` cut out by its `ϖ`-power torsion ideal; it is admissible, is the fibre product in the
category of admissible formal `O_K`-schemes, and equals `X ×_Z Y` when `X` or `Y` is flat over `Z`),
`torsionFreeQuotient` (for `X` locally tfp the `ϖ`-power torsion ideal `O_X[ϖ^∞]` is coherent
(`torsionQuotient` of *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*) and `X^{tf} := V(O_X[ϖ^∞])` is
admissible — dividing by the `ϖ`-torsion `O_X[ϖ]` alone does not suffice, see
`admissible_test_powerTorsion`; every morphism from an admissible formal scheme to `X` factors
uniquely through `X^{tf}`), `CoherentOpenIdeal` (a coherent ideal `𝒜 ⊆ O_X` that is open: locally `𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r)O_{Spf A}` with `ϖ^m ∈ (f_0, …, f_r)` for some `m`; on quasi-compact `X` a single `m`
with `ϖ^m O_X ⊆ 𝒜`) and `CoherentModule` (a coherent `O_X`-module on `X` locally of tf presentation:
on every formal affine open `Spf A` it is the sheaf attached to a coherent — equivalently finitely
presented, by *tfp-algebra-coherent* — `A`-module (BL I §1, p. 298); coherence itself is
*coherent-modules*). Prove `isAdmissible_spf_iff` (`Spf A` is admissible iff `A` is
`IsAdmissibleAlgebra`), `isAdmissible_iff_affineOpens` (`X` is admissible iff `Γ(U, O_X)` is
admissible for every formal affine open `U`, iff this holds for the members of one affine open
cover, by *tfp-locality*), `isAdmissible_iff_flat_stalks` (for `X` locally tfp: `X` is admissible
iff every stalk `O_{X,x}` is a flat `O_K`-module), `IsAdmissible.ofIsOpenImmersion` (a theorem: an
open formal subscheme of an admissible formal scheme is admissible), `IsAdmissible.completion` (the
`ϖ`-adic completion `X̂` of an `O_K`-scheme `X` locally of finite presentation is `IsLocallyTFP`,
and is admissible when `X` is `O_K`-flat) and `IsAdmissible.iff_of_discreteValuation` (if `K` is
discretely valued, `X` is admissible iff `X` is a locally noetherian formal scheme (layer F0), flat
over `Spf O_K` and adic locally of finite type over `Spf O_K`) (BL I §1, after Prop. 1.7, p. 297,

The constructions use the structural map `s : X ⟶ ofSpf O` and the explicit
pseudouniformizer `ϖ`. `specialFibre ϖ s hX` is a scheme over `Spec k` for
`hX : IsLocallyTFP ϖ s`; `specialFibre_spec` supplies its locally finite type structure map,
the homeomorphic inclusion into `X`, and surjective affine section maps with kernel
`m_O Γ(U,O_X)`. Its scalar equation identifies the `k`-structure with the residue of `s`.
The maximal ideal is used even when it is not principal (Conrad-AWS §3.3,
Ex. 3.3.4 and Def. 3.3.5, p. 31; EGA I, 10.1.2–4, p. 181).

`torsionFreeQuotient ϖ s hX` is an object over `X`. The theorem
`torsionFreeQuotient_spec` asserts `IsAdmissible ϖ (q ≫ s)`, a closed embedding, and a
coherent kernel whose sections on each affine open are exactly the kernel of localization
at `ϖ`. The theorem `torsionFreeQuotient_universal` gives unique factorization for each
`f : T ⟶ X` with `IsAdmissible ϖ (f ≫ s)`. These statements globalize the power-torsion
calculation of Conrad-AWS §3.3, Lem. 3.3.2 and Ex. 3.3.3, p. 31.

For `f : X ⟶ Z`, `g : Y ⟶ Z`, and `s : Z ⟶ ofSpf O`,
`admissiblePullback ϖ s f g` assumes admissibility of `s`, `f ≫ s` and `g ≫ s`.
`admissiblePullback_spec` identifies its cone with the power-torsion quotient of the ordinary
formal fibre product and states unique lifting of compatible maps from an admissible source.
`admissiblePullback_eq_of_flat` says this cone is a limit in formal schemes if either `f` or
`g` is flat on stalks. This is the affine completed-tensor construction followed by the
quotient of Conrad-AWS §3.3, Lem. 3.3.2 and Ex. 3.3.3–4, p. 31; gluing uses Ex. 3.3.6, p. 32.

`CoherentOpenIdeal ϖ s hX`, for `hX : IsAdmissible ϖ s`, uses the existing ideal-sheaf
carrier and its finite-presentation predicate. `CoherentOpenIdeal.uniform_power` assumes
`X` quasi-compact and produces one exponent valid on every affine open.
`coherentOpenIdeal_iff_centre` identifies these ideals with `IsAdmissibleCentre O ϖ s`.
The finite-generation condition and containment of a power of `ϖ` are those of
Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.11, p. 33; the uniform exponent follows from a finite subcover.
`CoherentModule ϖ s hX`, with `hX : IsLocallyTFP ϖ s`, uses Mathlib's full subcategory
of locally finitely presented module sheaves. `CoherentModule.affine_finitePresentation`
asserts finite presentation of sections on each affine formal open, including over
nonnoetherian `O` (Conrad-AWS §3.3, p. 32, following Ex. 3.3.6).

`isAdmissible_iff_affineOpens` includes the intrinsic `ϖ`-adic topology as well as the
admissible-algebra predicate; `isAdmissible_iff_affineCover` tests the same conditions on
one affine open cover. `IsAdmissible.ofIsOpenImmersion` applies to every open immersion
into an admissible source, and `IsAdmissible.iff_of_discreteValuation` assumes
`IsDiscreteValuationRing O` and identifies admissibility with local noetherianity, F0's
adic local finite type, and flat structural stalks (Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.1,
Def. 3.3.5 and Ex. 3.3.6, pp. 30–32).

`IsAdmissible.completion` uses `idealCompletion Y I hI` for a scheme map
`b : Y ⟶ Spec O` locally of finite presentation, where `I` is locally generated by the
image of `ϖ`. It produces the structural map `s`, pins it on sections to `b`, asserts
`IsLocallyTFP ϖ s`, and asserts `IsAdmissible ϖ s` when `b` is flat. Its special fibre
is the scheme pullback along `Spec k ⟶ Spec O`. This uses no noetherianity hypothesis
(Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.9, pp. 32–33).

**Formal schemes of type (S): the class on which Huber's generic-fibre functor is defined, and its
relation to admissible formal schemes and to Conrad's `FS_C`.** (*formal-schemes-of-type-S*) A formal
scheme `X = (X, O_X)` is of type (S) if every point has an open affine neighbourhood `U` such that
the topology of `A := O_X(U)` is adic and either (a) `A` is noetherian, or (b) there is `s ∈ A` such
that `sA` is an ideal of definition and the Tate ring `A(1/s)` — the localisation `A_s` topologised
by the images of `s^m A` — is strongly noetherian. Condition (S) is local on `X` and is stated for
the rings of affine opens with adic topologies; the strongly noetherian hypothesis in (b) is on the
Tate ring `A(1/s)`, not on `A`. For `X` of type (S) every formal affine open has an adic topology
with a finitely generated ideal of definition. Morphisms of type-(S) formal schemes are adic (resp.
locally of finite type) when locally the ring maps are adic (resp. topologically of finite type) in
Huber's sense. Relations to admissible formal schemes and to Conrad's category `FS_C` (`C` an adic
noetherian ring: `FS_C` requires `C` noetherian, type (S) does not), all proved as part of this
target's API: (i) every locally noetherian formal scheme (layer F0) is of type (S) via (a); (ii)
every formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf type (covered by `Spf A` with `A` tft over `O_K` with the
`ϖ`-adic topology, `A` separated as `Spf` requires), in particular every locally tfp and every
admissible one, is of type (S) via (b) with `s = ϖ`, since `A[1/ϖ]` is a quotient of `K⟨ξ⟩` by an
ideal `aK⟨ξ⟩`, closed because `K⟨ξ⟩` is noetherian, hence a `K`-affinoid algebra, complete and
strongly noetherian, with ring of definition the image `A/A[ϖ^∞]` of `A`; (iii) every object of
Conrad's category `FS_C` is locally noetherian, hence of type (S) via (a); (iv) when `K` is not
discretely valued, admissible formal `O_K`-schemes such as `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` satisfy (b) but not (a) and
are not objects of any `FS_C`, whereas `Spf R_0[[T]]` for a complete discrete valuation ring `R_0 ⊆ O_K` lies in `FS_{R_0}` and satisfies (a) but not (b); (v) for non-discrete `K`, `Spf O_K[[T]]` with
the `(ϖ, T)`-adic topology is not of type (S) at all. Completion keeps (S) relative to a base of
type (S), as in R2.8 (*formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison*): for `f : X → Y` a morphism of
schemes locally of finite type and `Y' ⊆ Y` closed with quasi-coherent ideal of finite type, if the
completion `Ŷ` along `Y'` is of type (S), so is `X̂` along `X ×_Y Y'`, and `f̂` is adic (Huber96
§1.9, (1.9.5), p. 98). The hypothesis is on the completion actually formed, not on a coarser one:
`A¹_{O_K}` completed along `V(ϖ)` is the type-(S) `Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, but completed along `V(ϖ, T)` it is
`Spf O_K[[T]]` with the `(ϖ, T)`-adic topology, which for `K` not discretely valued is not of
type (S) by (v): its only point has the whole ring as its only affine neighbourhood, which is not
noetherian (its quotient by `T` is `O_K`) and has no principal ideal of definition (a generator `s`
would divide a power of `ϖ`, so `T ∤ s` as `(T)` is prime, and a power `T^N = s·u`; reducing mod
`T` and cancelling `T` repeatedly makes `s` a unit). In
`FormalScheme`, define `IsTypeS` as the structure: every point has a formal affine neighbourhood
`Spf A`, `A` adic, with `A` noetherian or with some `s ∈ A` generating an ideal of definition and
`A(1/s)` strongly noetherian. Prove `IsTypeS.of_isLocallyNoetherian` (an instance: locally

These examples use an arbitrary complete rank-one base: non-finite generation of its
maximal ideal expresses the nondiscrete case, and `IsDiscreteValuationRing` selects the
DVR case. `typeS_test_microbial` also identifies `O[1/ϖ]` with `FractionRing O`;
`typeS_test_dvr_powerSeries` retains the `(ϖ,T)`-adic topology and the object of `FSC O`.
The locators are Huber96 §1.9, condition (S), p. 96, and Example 1.9.2(i), p. 97.

The affine predicate `HasStronglyNoetherianPrincipalLocalization A` specifies clause (b)
by an element `s`, the `s`-adic topology of `A`, and a nonarchimedean topology on `A[1/s]`
whose zero-neighbourhood basis is the images of `s^n A`. It requires both `IsTateRing` and
`IsStronglyNoetherian` for that topology. The class `IsTypeS X` applies the disjunction
of (a) and (b) to intrinsic section topologies on an affine neighbourhood of each point.
The named implications `IsTypeS.of_isLocallyNoetherian`, `IsTypeS.of_isLocallyTFP` and
`IsTypeS.restrict` use these predicates (Huber96 §1.9, p. 96).

### R2.3 generic fibres

**Huber's functor `t` from locally noetherian formal schemes to adic spaces.**
(*noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space*) Let `X` be a locally noetherian formal scheme (layer F0);
for non-noetherian formal models the functor `d` of *generic-fibre-functor-d* is used instead. There
are an adic space `t(X)` and a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces `π_X: (t(X), O⁺_{t(X)}) → (X, O_X)` such that every morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces `(Z,
O⁺_Z) → (X, O_X)` from an adic space `Z` factors uniquely through a morphism of adic spaces `Z →
t(X)`. On affines `t(Spf A) = Spa(A, A)`, and `π_X(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}`, the open prime at
which the valuation ring `k(x)⁺` of `x` is centred on `Spec A` — centres are those of
*adic-valuation-rings-and-centres* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0), not redefined here; that `Spa(A, A)` is an adic
space rests on the structure presheaf of `Spa(A, A)` being a sheaf for a
noetherian adic ring `A` (Huber94 §2, Thm 2.2; *noetherian-type-stably-sheafy* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0)). The
universal property makes `t` a functor; `t` is fully faithful; a morphism `f` of locally noetherian
formal schemes is adic (EGA I 10.12) resp. locally of finite type (EGA I 10.13) if and only if
`t(f)` is adic resp. locally of finite type (Huber94 §4, Prop. 4.2(i), p. 540; Hübner §8, Thm 8.1,
p. 37, the modern statement with the affine formula). The trivial valuations form a subspace `t(X)_t
⊆ t(X)` and `π_X` restricts to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces `(t(X)_t, O⁺|) ≅ (X, O_X)`;
in particular `π_X` has a section `ι_X` by trivial valuations. The smallest saturated subcategory of
adic spaces containing the image of `t` consists of the adic spaces locally of the form `Spa(A, A⁺)`
with `A` finitely generated over a noetherian ring of definition `A_0` and `A⁺` the integral closure
of `A_0` in `A` (Huber94 §4, Prop. 4.2(ii)). In `FormalScheme`, define `toAdicSpace` (the functor
`t` from locally noetherian formal schemes to adic spaces), `centerMap` (`π_X: (t(X), O⁺) → (X,
O_X)`, a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces) and `trivialValuationSection` (`ι_X: X
→ t(X)`, sending an open prime `p` to the trivial valuation of `κ(p)`, with `π_X ∘ ι_X = id` and
image the trivial-valuation locus). Prove `toAdicSpace_spf` (a simp lemma: `t(Spf A) ≅ Spa(A, A)`
for a noetherian adic ring `A`), `centerMap_spf_apply` (a simp lemma: on `Spf A`, `π(x) = {a ∈ A :
|a(x)| < 1}`, the image of the closed point of `Spec κ(x)⁺`), `toAdicSpace.lift` (a morphism of
locally and topologically ringed spaces `(Z, O⁺_Z) → (X, O_X)` from an adic space factors as `π_X ∘
g` for a unique morphism of adic spaces `g: Z → t(X)`), `toAdicSpace.lift_comp_centerMap` (`π_X ∘
lift λ = λ`, and `lift` is unique with this property), `toAdicSpace.map_id` (`t(id_X) = id` and `t(g
∘ f) = t(g) ∘ t(f)`), `toAdicSpace.fullyFaithful` (`t` is fully faithful), `toAdicSpace_isAdic_iff`
(`f` is adic (EGA I 10.12) iff `t(f)` is an adic morphism in the sense of *adic-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0)) and `toAdicSpace_locallyOfFiniteType_iff` (`f` is locally of finite type (EGA I 10.13) iff
`t(f)` is locally of finite type in the sense of *finite-type-morphism-classes* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0)) (Huber94
§4, Prop. 4.1, p. 539, existence of `t(X)` and `π_X` with the universal property; Huber94 §4, proof
of Prop. 4.1, point (1), p. 539, the centre map on points; Huber94 §4, Prop. 4.2(i), p. 540).
*Needs:* *locally-noetherian-formal-scheme*, *formal-spectrum*, *adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes*,
*formal-morphism-finite-type* (layer F0); *locally-noetherian-adic-space*, *adic-morphism*,

The representing pair is `FormalScheme.TData X`: its `space` is a
`TauCeti.AdicSpace`, its `center` is an `IntegralSpecialisation space X`, and its
`universal` field asserts unique factorisation for every adic source and every integral
specialisation. Here `IntegralSpecialisation` retains the ring-sheaf morphism, continuity
on intrinsically topologised affine sections, the pointwise bound `|a| ≤ 1`, and the
stalk locality equation `|a| < 1 ↔ a` has nonunit germ on the formal scheme. Thus its
section maps land in `O⁺`, with the subspace topology. `nonempty_tData` assumes
`IsLocallyNoetherian X`; `tData` chooses this pair, `toAdicSpace` takes its space, and
`centerMap` takes its integral specialisation (Huber94, Prop. 4.1, pp. 539–540).

`IntegralSpecialisation.precomp` uses the underlying sheaf map of an adic morphism;
`IntegralSpecialisation.postcomp` uses a morphism between locally noetherian formal
schemes. `toAdicSpace.lift` is the chosen unique factor, with its equation in
`toAdicSpace.lift_comp_centerMap` and uniqueness in `toAdicSpace.lift_unique`.
`toAdicSpace.map` applies this lift to the postcomposed centre. Its functor laws are
`toAdicSpace.map_id` and `toAdicSpace.map_comp`; `toAdicSpace.fullyFaithful` states

are F0's `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic` and `FormalScheme.Hom.LocallyOfFiniteType`, and the
adic predicates are imported from Part II (Huber94, Props. 4.1–4.2(i), pp. 539–540).

For an imported `AdicSpace.Affinoid A` with noetherian adic coordinate ring and
`A.pair.plus = ⊤`, `toAdicSpace_spf` gives the affine isomorphism. The stronger
`centerMap_spf_apply` chooses it compatibly with `A.coeff`, then identifies the open
prime of every point with `{a | |a| < 1}`; `centerMap_spf_apply_affine` supplies the
open-prime assertion for any Huber ring (Huber94, proof of Prop. 4.1(1), pp. 539–540).
`trivialValuationSection_centerMap` states the retraction equation,
`trivialValuationSection_range` identifies its embedded image with the trivial valuations,
and `trivialValuationSection_stalk` says the centre induces stalk isomorphisms there.
At a trivial valuation the integral and ordinary stalks agree, so these statements
identify the restricted locally ringed space with `X` (Huber94, proof of Prop. 4.2(i),
p. 540; Hübner, Thm 8.1 and its following construction, pp. 37–38).
`toAdicSpace_saturated_iff` states the assertion about the smallest saturated
subcategory by quantifying over object properties closed under open subspaces, open
covers and isomorphisms and containing every `toAdicSpace X`; its right side uses
Part II's charts and a noetherian ring of definition over which the chart ring is
finitely generated (Huber94, Prop. 4.2(ii), p. 540).

The carrier `FormalScheme.AnalyticSpecialisation Z X` retains the continuous map and
its map of ring sheaves. On formal affine opens this map is continuous for the intrinsic
adic topology. Its image has valuation at most one; a section has valuation less than one
precisely when its germ at the centre is a nonunit. At every source point some
topologically nilpotent formal section has nonzero value. Thus it records the integral
locality and analytic conditions of Huber96, Proposition 1.9.1, without asserting that
the map into the full analytic structure sheaf is local. `GenericFibreData` represents
these maps, and `genericFibreData`, `genericFibre`, `specialisation` and
`genericFibre.lift` are its chosen data, space, point map and unique lift.

### R2.4 specialisation, tubes and rig-points

**The specialisation map `λ_X = sp: d(X) → X`.** (*specialisation-map*) For `X` of type (S) the
specialisation map is the continuous map `λ_X: d(X) → X` underlying Huber's Proposition 1.9.1
(*generic-fibre-functor-d*). For `X = Spf A` and `x ∈ d(X)`, `λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}`, an open
prime of `A`; equivalently `λ(x)` is the image of the closed point of `Spec κ(x)⁺` under the map
`Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A` induced by `A → κ(x)⁺` (`|A(x)| ≤ 1`), i.e. the centre on `Spec A` of the
valuation ring `(x, k(x)⁺)` in the sense of *adic-valuation-rings-and-centres* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0), which
owns the notion of centre. Properties, (i)
and (ii) for `X` of type (S) and (iii)–(v) for `X` admissible over `O_K`: (i) `λ` is continuous: for
`s ∈ A`, `λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {|s| = 1} = {|s| ≥ 1}` is open and `λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1}` is closed; (ii) `λ`
is natural: `λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X`; (iii) for `X` admissible over `O_K`, `λ` maps each classical
point (residue field finite over `K`) to a closed point of `X_s`, and every closed point of `X_s` is
the image of a classical point (BL I §3, 3.4, 3.5), `λ` of the classical point attached to a
rig-point being its special point; the restriction `sp: X_rig → X` to classical points is
Berthelot's specialisation map of rigid geometry, which is anticontinuous: preimages of closed
subsets are admissible opens (the tubes of *tube*); (iv) `λ` is compatible with admissible blow-ups
`φ: X' → X`, i.e. `φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ)` with `d(φ)` an isomorphism
(*generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*); (v) for `X` quasi-compact admissible, the maps
`λ_{X'}` over all admissible blow-ups `X' → X` induce a homeomorphism `d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'|` and an
isomorphism `(d(X), O⁺) ≅ lim (X', O_{X'})` (the Zariski–Riemann description; Hübner Thm 8.9, and Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35). Care: in the adic space,
`λ⁻¹` of a closed set is closed, not open; the rigid "anticontinuity" concerns classical points and
corresponds to the interior (*tube*). In `FormalScheme`, define `specialisation` (`λ_X: d(X) → X`,
the continuous map of Proposition 1.9.1) and `rigidSpecialisation` (on classical points, `λ` agrees
with Berthelot's `sp: X_rig → X` under *raynaud-generic-fibre* and AdicSpacesPartII layer R1's identification of
classical points). Prove `specialisation_spf_apply` (a simp theorem: for `X = Spf A`, `λ(x) = {a ∈ A :
v_x(a) < 1}`), `specialisation_eq_center` (`λ(x)` is the image of the closed point of `Spec κ(x)⁺`
under `Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A`),
`specialisation_preimage_basicOpen` (`λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {x : |s(x)| ≥ 1} = rationalSubset {1} s`, open;
`λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1}`, closed), `specialisation_naturality` (`λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X` for every adic
morphism `f: X → Y` of type-(S) formal schemes), `specialisation_classical_isClosed` (for `X`
admissible and `x` classical, `λ(x)` is a closed point of `X_s`),
`exists_classical_specialisation_eq` (for `X` admissible, every closed point of `X_s` equals `λ(x)`
for some classical `x`), `specialisation_blowUp` (for an admissible blow-up `φ: X' → X`, `φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ)`), `specialisationLimitHomeomorph` (for `X` quasi-compact admissible, `d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'|` over admissible blow-ups is a homeomorphism) and `RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation`
(for `X` admissible and a rig-point `u: Spf B → X` with classical point `x ∈ d(X)` under
`RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` of *rig-point*, `λ(x)` is the special point of `u`; this is stated
here rather than in *rig-point* because it refers to `λ`) (Huber94 §4, proof of Prop. 4.1, point

the specialisation is the centre map; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34, rigid-analytic
anticontinuity on classical points; Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35, the Zariski–Riemann description over all
formal models). *Needs:* *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; *rig-point*;

Continuity is carried by the `TopCat` morphism `specialisation`. The affine targets `specialisation_spf_apply`, `specialisation_eq_center` and
`specialisation_preimage_basicOpen` use `Spf.prime` and the pullback valuation

(Huber96 Prop. 1.9.1, pp. 96–97). The algebraic statement

with `φ(A) ⊆ B⁺` and `v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺)`; `specialisation_preimage_basicOpen_affine`
identifies the locus `1 ≤ |s|` in `Spa(B, B⁺)` with `R(1/s)`. These two statements
concern valuations on rings; the three formal-scheme statements above identify the
actual specialisation map. The two classical-point theorems use
`genericFibre.classicalPoints O K β s hs`: finiteness of the residue-field map induced by

Here `O` is a complete rank-one valuation ring, `s` is adic, and `X` is admissible;
no discreteness or quasi-compactness is required (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34;
[FK] II, Cor. 8.2.13, p. 555, and Cor. 8.2.18, p. 558, applied on affine
neighbourhoods to the tube of a closed point). Closed points are expressed by closed singletons on `X`,
whose topological space is also that of the special fibre.

`RigPoint` records a sheaf ideal, its special point, and the existence of an admissible
closed immersion from `Spf B` for a finite flat `O_K`-algebra `B` that is a
one-dimensional local domain. The algebra structure induces the composite map to
`Spf O_K`. Isomorphic
presentations therefore give the same rig-point. The closed immersion is expressed
by its closed embedding and surjective stalk maps, with an adic formal morphism,
including over nonnoetherian valuation rings. `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` is fixed
by `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints_kernel`: on every open containing the specialisation,
a section belongs to the rig-point ideal exactly when its analytic value is zero.
`RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation` then identifies the distinguished closed
point with `λ(x)` ([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.6, pp. 552–553, Prop. 8.2.10 and Cor. 8.2.11, p. 554,
the finite local domain obtained by schematic closure; Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34).

`specialisation_blowUp` includes both the commuting square and invertibility of the
actual generic-fibre morphism, for a finitely generated open centre on an admissible
formal scheme (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.11 and Exer. 3.3.12, pp. 33–34).
`specialisationLimitHomeomorph` states existence of a homeomorphism for quasi-compact
admissible `X` to the compatible families of centres on all admissible blow-ups.
The target has the subspace topology of the product; compatibility is with every
formal morphism over `X`. Its projection at each blow-up sends a lifted analytic point
to its specialisation, fixing the homeomorphism rather than just its isomorphism class
(Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35).

`rigidSpecialisation` is the restriction of `specialisation` to this classical subset,
identified with rigid points through Part II's `rigidToAdic.classicalPointsEquiv`.
It therefore uses the same centre formula (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34).

**Rig-points of admissible formal schemes.** (*rig-point*) Let `X` be an admissible formal
`O_K`-scheme over a complete rank-one `O_K`. A rig-point of `X` is a morphism `u: T → X` of
admissible formal `O_K`-schemes that is a closed immersion, with `T = Spf B` affine and `B` a local
integral domain of dimension `1`; its residue field is `Frac(B)`. (Bosch–Lütkebohmert allow locally
closed immersions; over a complete rank-one valuation ring locally closed rig-points are closed.)
Properties: (BL I 3.2) `B` is finite over `O_K` and the integral closure of `B` in `Frac(B)` is the
valuation ring `O_{K'}` of the finite extension `K' = Frac(B)` of `K`; (BL I 3.3) for an admissible
blow-up `X' → X` the induced map on rig-points is bijective and preserves residue fields; (BL I 3.4)
for `X = Spf A` the rig-points correspond bijectively to primes `p ⊂ A` with `ϖ ∉ p` and `dim A/p =
1`, and to closed points of `Spec A[1/ϖ]`, i.e. to maximal ideals of the `K`-affinoid algebra `A_K`;
(BL I 3.5) every closed point of `X_s` is the special point of some rig-point — in the rank-one case
the existence applies [BGR 7.1.5/4], the lifting of closed points of the reduction to points of `Sp

`X` correspond bijectively to the classical points of `d(X)` (residue field finite over `K`); the
compatibility with the specialisation map `λ` (the special point of `u` is `λ` of the corresponding
classical point) is `RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation` of *specialisation-map*, which depends

subspace of the given fibre product: its ideal is exactly the sections locally
annihilated by powers of the centre. It also identifies this space, over `Y`, with
`admissiblePullback`; when `f` is flat on stalks, the closed inclusion is an
isomorphism onto the ordinary formal fibre product.
`AdmissibleBlowup.isProper_surjective_specialFibre`
states surjectivity on formal points and properness of every reduction for any
compatible finite ideals of definition with source ideal equal to the extended target
ideal. This expresses adic properness without a noetherian assumption; formal points
and special-fibre points have the same underlying space ([FK] II, Prop. 1.1.4(1),
p. 435, Prop. 1.1.8, p. 437, and Prop. 1.2.9, p. 442; BL I, Rem. 2.4(c), p. 301).

`IdealSheafData.mul` is the sheaf ideal generated by products of local sections.
`AdmissibleBlowup.mul` gives an isomorphism over `X` for the two successive centres
`J` and the extension of `L`. `AdmissibleBlowup.dominate` supplies maps from the
product-centre blow-up to both given blow-ups, commuting with the projections.
For quasi-compact, quasi-separated `X`, `AdmissibleBlowup.comp` also supplies an
integer `n > 0` and an admissible ideal `K` downstairs whose extension is
`L · (J O_{X'})^n`; the composite is the blow-up of `J · K`.
`AdmissibleBlowup.comp_of_disjoint` retains a specified open on which both centres
are unit ideals. `AdmissibleBlowup.extend` gives one global blow-up dominating a
finite family on quasi-compact opens of such an `X`, including the empty family
([FK] II, Props. 1.1.8–1.1.10, pp. 437–439, and Prop. 1.3.1, p. 443;
RG I, Lem. 5.1.4, p. 36; [FK] II, Exercise 1.1, p. 444, for the product formula).

`strictTransform` and `strictTransformBaseChange` return `IdealTorsionQuotient`
data, including the quotient map and its local kernel, on the blow-up and on a
specified formal fibre product respectively. For a finitely presented input on an
admissible base, `strictTransform_coherent` gives finite presentation when the
quotient is `ϖ`-torsion-free on every open. `strictTransformBaseChange_coherent`
gives the relative version when the formal fibre product is locally topologically
finitely presented over `O`. `strictTransformBaseChange_comp` compares
the iterated and composite quotients of a finitely presented module on a locally
topologically finitely presented source, using a pair of Cartesian squares over an
admissible base and three admissible centres. Its composite blow-up is identified over the original base, and positive powers of the extended
composite centre and the product of the successive centres are required to contain
one another. These conditions express equality of their radicals and fix the common
scheme-theoretic open used for the strict transforms. In particular they apply to
the centre supplied by `AdmissibleBlowup.comp`; arbitrary choices of a centre
presenting the same morphism are not interchangeable for module strict transforms
([FK] II, Def. 1.2.1 and Props. 1.2.7, 1.2.11, pp. 440–443;
RG I, Rem. 5.3.2, p. 38).

### R2.6 separatedness, flattening, quasi-finite models and finiteness criteria

The formal blow-up carrier `FormalScheme.AdmissibleBlowup O ϖ s J` represents maps
from admissible formal schemes over `Spf O` on which `J` becomes invertible. Its
projection is adic and its source admissible. `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible` means
locally principal with a regular generator. `IsAdmissibleCentre` means locally
finitely generated and containing a power of the structural `ϖ`.
`nonempty_admissibleBlowup` supplies the representing object; the generic-fibre
map is an isomorphism by `AdmissibleBlowup.genericFibre_isIso` (BL I, §§2 and 4).
`exists_formalOpen_of_genericOpen` realizes each quasi-compact generic open as
the inverse image under specialization of an open on a blow-up (BL I, 4.4).

**Checks for the centre and blow-up.**

- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_unit`: the unit ideal is invertible.
- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_zero`: the zero ideal on a nonempty formal scheme is not invertible.
- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_product`: every power of an invertible ideal is invertible.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_unit`: the unit ideal is an admissible centre.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_zero`: the zero ideal on a nonempty admissible model is not a centre.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_power`: positive powers remain admissible centres.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_unit`: on an admissible source, blowing up the unit ideal is an isomorphism.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_specialFibre`: on a nonempty source killed by the pseudouniformizer, an admissible blow-up cannot have an invertible projection.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_invertible`: an already invertible centre has an isomorphic blow-up.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_power`: positive powers of the centre give uniquely isomorphic blow-ups over the base.

`FormalScheme.TorsionQuotient` is the quotient of a module sheaf by its locally
`ϖ`-power-torsion sections. The epimorphism and its kernel on every open specify
the quotient; the exponent may vary locally. This locality is needed on opens
that are not quasi-compact. The construction is the torsion quotient used for
strict transforms in BL II, §4.

**Checks for the torsion quotient.**

- `TorsionQuotient_zero`: the quotient of zero is zero.
- `TorsionQuotient_admissible`: the structure sheaf of an admissible model is unchanged.
- `TorsionQuotient_killed`: a module all of whose sections are power torsion has zero quotient.

`FormalScheme.IdealTorsionQuotient J M` specifies the quotient of `M` by sections
locally killed by a power of `J`. Its epimorphism and sectionwise kernel equation determine
the quotient. Applying it to the pulled-back centre and coefficient module gives the
strict transform in `exists_flattening`, `exists_flattening_lowerDimension`,
`exists_flattening_smooth` and `exists_flattening_largerOpen`.

**Checks for centre torsion.**

- `IdealTorsionQuotient_unit`: the unit ideal kills no nonzero section, so the quotient map is invertible.
- `IdealTorsionQuotient_zero`: the zero ideal makes the quotient zero.
- `IdealTorsionQuotient_annihilated`: if a fixed power of the ideal annihilates the module, its quotient is zero.

**The fibres of a formal model bound the fibres of its generic fibre (Conrad-MR Theorem A.2.1).**
(*formal-model-fibre-comparison*) Let `K` be complete of rank one, discreteness not assumed, and
`m_K` the maximal ideal of `O_K`. For an `O_K`-algebra `A` topologically of finite presentation
(*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*), write `A_K = A[1/ϖ] = A ⊗_{O_K} K` for the ring of its
generic affinoid (*raynaud-generic-fibre*) and `A_k = A/m_K A`, a finitely generated `k`-algebra,
for its special fibre. Prove: (i) `dim A_K ≤ dim A_k` for Krull dimensions, without flatness;
(ii) if `A` is `O_K`-flat then `dim A_K = dim A_k`; (iii) if `A` is `O_K`-flat, `A_k` is reduced
and `Spec A_k` has pure dimension `d`, then `A_K` is reduced and `Spec A_K` has pure dimension
`d`. For (i), lift a Noether normalisation `k[x_1, …, x_n] → A_k` to `O_K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩ → A`; this
lift is finite because its reduction is finite and `A` is `ϖ`-adically complete and separated. For
(ii), Noether normalisation for affinoid algebras applied to a presentation of `A` gives a finite
injective map `O_K⟨t_1, …, t_e⟩ → A` with `e = dim A_K`; flatness makes `A → A_K` injective. For
(iii), every nonzero element of `A_K` has a `K^×`-multiple in `A ∖ m_K A`, because ideals of Tate
algebras are closed and the residue norm is attained. This makes `A`, hence `A_K`, reduced.
Flatness makes every minimal prime `p` of `A` meet `O_K` only in `0`, and (ii) applied to the
quotients `A/p`, together with the same lemma, gives the pure dimension (Conrad-MR Appendix A.2,
Thm A.2.1, p. 39, statement; proof of Thm A.2.1, pp. 39–41, the finiteness criterion, equation
(A.2.2) and the pure-dimension argument; Lem. A.2.2, pp. 40–41).

Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, and
`f_0 : X_0 → Y_0` its reduction modulo `ϖ`. Let `K'/K` be a complete extension of rank-one valued
fields with residue field `k'`, not necessarily finite over `K`, and `y : Spa(K', O_{K'}) → d(Y)`
a morphism over `Spa(K, O_K)`. Prove: (iv) `y = d(ỹ)` for a unique morphism
`ỹ : Spf O_{K'} → Y` over `Spf O_K`. The fibre `X_ỹ = X ×_Y Spf O_{K'}` is locally of tf
presentation over `O_{K'}`, and `O_{K'}`-flat when `f` is flat. Its generic fibre is
`d(X_ỹ) ≅ d(X) ×_{d(Y)} Spa(K', O_{K'})` over `Spa(K', O_{K'})`. Its special fibre is
`f_0⁻¹(s) ⊗_{κ(s)} k'`, where `s ∈ Y_0` is the image of `ỹ`, the specialisation of `y`.
(v) The analytic fibre `d(X) ×_{d(Y)} Spa(K', O_{K'})` is covered by the charts
`d(Spf A_i) = Spa(A_{i,K'}, A_{i,K'}°)` for the formal affine opens `Spf A_i` of `X_ỹ`. If every
fibre of `f_0` has dimension `≤ d`, then `dim A_{i,K'} ≤ d` for every `i`. If `f` is flat and
every fibre of `f_0` is geometrically reduced of pure dimension `d`, then every `A_{i,K'}` is
reduced and `Spec A_{i,K'}` has pure dimension `d`. For (iv), `Spa(K', O_{K'})` is a single point,
so `y` lands in some `d(Spf B) = Spa(B_K, B_K°)`. There `y` is a continuous map of pairs
`(B_K, B_K°) → (K', O_{K'})` (Huber94 §2, Prop. 2.1(i), p. 522), and its restriction to `B`
defines `ỹ`; uniqueness holds because `O_{K'}` is `ϖ`-torsion free. The generic fibre of `X_ỹ` is
*generic-fibre-fibre-products* (b) followed by (a) over `O_{K'}`. Clause (v) is (i) and (iii) over
`O_{K'}` applied to the `A_i`. Here `Spec A_{i,k'}` is an open subscheme of
`f_0⁻¹(s) ⊗_{κ(s)} k'`, and the local dimension of a scheme of finite type over a field, hence its
pure dimension, does not change under field extension (Stacks Tag 00P4). Conrad proves the same
comparison at points with `K'/K` finite through *rig-point* (Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Lem. A.1.5,
p. 38; proof of Thm A.2.1, p. 39). Since (v) allows every complete `K'`, it also covers the field
extensions needed for geometric reducedness. *Needs:* *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;

- `Huber.formalModelFibre_torsion` (non-example, flatness) — `A = O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)` is topologically of

- `formalModelFibre_zero` (degenerate) — for `A = 0` both fibres are zero rings of dimension `⊥`

**Flattening by admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 5.2).** (*flattening-by-blow-up*)
For a morphism `f: X → Y` of quasi-compact admissible formal `O_K`-schemes with `f_rig` flat
(resp. flat in dimension `≥ n`), there is an admissible blow-up `Y' → Y` of the target such that
the strict transform `X'` of `X` — the closed formal subscheme of `X ×_Y Y'` cut out by the
sections supported over the centre, not the total transform — is flat (resp. flat in dimension
`≥ n`) over `Y'`: this is the case `T = Y`, `ℳ = O_X` of *module-flattening-by-blow-up* (BL II §5,
Thm 5.2, p. 426, deduced there from Thm 4.1; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Thm A.1.2, p. 38, its
use in the fibral finiteness criterion), and is a corollary, not a separate statement. For `X = ∅`
the statement is empty; with `Y = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` and `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ)`, `f_rig` is the
open immersion of the annulus `{|ϖ| ≤ |ζ| ≤ 1}` into the disc, `f` is not flat (`ζ` is a
zero-divisor on `k[ζ, ξ]/(ζξ)`), and after blowing up `(ζ, ϖ)` on `Y` the strict transform maps
isomorphically onto the chart `{ζ generates}` of `Y'`. *Needs:* *module-flattening-by-blow-up*;
*admissible-blow-up*.

`FormalScheme.locallyQuasiFinite_reduction_iff` identifies locally quasi-finite

**The finite part over a henselian local base.** (*henselian-quasi-finite-finite-part*)
Let `A` be a henselian local ring and `f : X → Spec A` separated and locally quasi-finite,
with finite closed fibre. Construct an open-and-closed decomposition `X = X_fin ⊔ X_miss`
with `X_fin → Spec A` finite and `X_miss` having empty closed fibre. The finite part is the
union of the finitely many open-and-closed neighbourhoods `Spec O_{X,x}` of the points
in that fibre; its closed fibre equals that of `X` (EGA IV₄ 18.5.11(c), pp. 130–131;
Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Lemma A.1.4, p. 38).
*Needs:* Mathlib `HenselianLocalRing`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`, open-and-closed restrictions.

- For a finite `A`-scheme, take `X_fin = X` and `X_miss = ∅`.
- Over `A = k⟦t⟧`, `Spec A ⊔ Spec A[1/t]` has finite part `Spec A` and missing part `Spec A[1/t]`.

constant on the base, it exhausts every fibre, so the complementary part is empty.

### R2.7 the proof of flattening

This subsection proves the flattening theorem of Bosch–Lütkebohmert II by breaking it into the
lemmas of their §§1–4: lifting generators, bases and smooth morphisms from the reduction modulo `ϖ`;
the étale-local structure theorem of Raynaud–Gruson and its formal counterpart (finite over smooth
with geometrically irreducible fibres); ideals of coefficients and contents along smooth morphisms
with geometrically irreducible fibres; dévissages of coherent modules and the flatness criteria they
give; rig-flatness, flatness in dimension `≥ n` and Fitting ideals; and the induction that lowers
the dimension of the non-flat locus by one admissible blow-up at a time. Throughout, `K` is complete
for a nontrivial rank-one valuation, `O_K` is its valuation ring and `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser; formal
schemes are formal `O_K`-schemes locally of topologically finite presentation
(*admissible-formal-scheme*), `X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}`, `X_0` has the underlying space of `X`, and
for `t ∈ T_0` the fibre `X ⊗ k(t)` is `X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t)`. The classical rigid case (base `Spf
O_K`) is the one proved; Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case uses parallel arguments that are
not decomposed here. Smooth and étale formal morphisms, elementary étale neighbourhoods and the
étale-site invariance used throughout are *smooth-formal-scheme* and *formal-etale-site-invariance*
of R2.9.

**Generators modulo `ϖ` generate topologically.** (*topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal*) Let
`f : X → Y` be an affine morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `ℳ` a coherent
`O_X`-module and `E ⊆ Γ(X, ℳ)` a family of sections, possibly infinite. Prove that if the images of
`E` generate `f_*(ℳ/ϖℳ)` as an `O_{Y_0}`-module, then `E` generates `f_*ℳ` topologically over `O_Y`:
over every formal affine open `Spf A ⊆ Y`, with `f⁻¹(Spf A) = Spf B` and `ℳ` corresponding to the
finite `B`-module `M`, every `m ∈ M` is a `ϖ`-adically convergent sum `Σ_{e∈E} a_e e` with `a_e ∈ A`
and `a_e → 0` (for each `λ` only finitely many `a_e` lie outside `ϖ^λ A`); equivalently the
`A`-linear map `Â^{(E)} → M` from the `ϖ`-adic completion of the free `A`-module on `E` is
surjective (BL II §1, Lem. 1.3(a) and its proof, p. 405: Nakayama on the powers of the ideal of
definition, reduction to the affine case and the approximation argument of BL I 1.5). Generation is
required modulo `ϖ`, the ideal of definition, not modulo `m_K`, and the conclusion is topological
generation, not generation: for `Y = Spf O_K`, `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`, `ℳ = O_X` and `E = {ζ^i : i ≥ 0}`,
`E` generates `(O_K/ϖ)[ζ]` modulo `ϖ` and every `g ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩` is `Σ c_i ζ^i` with `c_i → 0`, while
`Σ_i ϖ^i ζ^i ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩` is not a finite `O_K`-linear combination of the `ζ^i`. The affine core —
a map into a `ϖ`-adically complete module that is surjective modulo `ϖ` is surjective after
completing the source — is Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.map_surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective`; this
target adds the sheaf form on `Y` and the convergent-sum description over `Spf A`. *Needs:*
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
*saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`,
`AdicCompletion.map_surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective`.

**A basis modulo `ϖ` of a flat module lifts to a topological basis.** (*topological-basis-lifting*) In
the situation of *topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal* (`f : X → Y` affine, `ℳ` coherent on
`X`, `E ⊆ Γ(X, ℳ)`), assume that the images of `E` form a basis of `f_*(ℳ/ϖℳ)` over `O_{Y_0}` — a
basis, not only a generating family — and that `ℳ` is flat over `O_Y` (`ℳ_x` flat over `O_{Y,f(x)}`
for all `x`; over `Spf B → Spf A`: `M` flat over `A`). Prove that `E` is a topological basis of
`f_*ℳ` over `O_Y`: over `Spf A` the map `φ : Â^{(E)} → M` is bijective, so every `m ∈ M` has a
unique expansion `m = Σ_{e∈E} a_e e` with `a_e → 0` (BL II §1, Lem. 1.3(b) and its proof, p. 405:
the kernel lies in every power of the ideal of definition and the completed free module is
separated). For `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` over `Y = Spf O_K`, `{ζ^i : i ≥ 0}` is a topological basis of
`O_K⟨ζ⟩`, restricted power series having unique coefficients. Flatness is needed: for `Y = X = Spf
O_K`, `ℳ = O_K/ϖ` and `E = {1}`, `E` is a basis modulo `ϖ` but `φ : O_K → O_K/ϖ` is not injective.
*Needs:* *topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal*; *tfp-locality*; Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`IsAdicComplete`.

The affine carrier `TopologicalBasis I E M` is a linear equivalence between `M` and the
`I`-adic completion of the free module `E →₀ A`. Its `vector` and `coord` maps send standard
unit vectors to basis vectors and recover coefficients. For complete `A`, `coord_vector`
gives the Kronecker coefficients and `coord_decay` gives finite support outside each `I^n`;
`ext` gives uniqueness. For finitely generated `I`, `existsUnique_of_decay` gives existence
for every decaying coefficient family. `ofModBasis` and `ofModBasis_vector` lift the specified
vectors, with flatness and completeness as hypotheses (BL II Lem. 1.3(b), p. 405).

- `topologicalBasis_test_empty` — an empty basis exists exactly for the zero module.
- `topologicalBasis_test_rankOne` — the complete base ring has basis `{1}` and its coordinate
  map is the identity.
- `topologicalBasis_test_twoTerm` — the coordinates of `a e₀ + c e₁` are `(a,c)`, in that order.
- `topologicalBasis_test_infinite` — over `ℤ_p`, the coefficients `p^i` determine an element
  outside the algebraic span of a countably infinite topological basis.
- `topologicalBasis_test_torsion` — `ℤ_p/p` has no rank-one topological basis over `ℤ_p`.

The constructor itself has three computed Checks: `liftedBasis_test_rankOne` lifts the
residue basis `1` and recovers the identity coordinate map; `liftedBasis_test_twoTerm` lifts
the standard two vectors and sends `(a,c)` to coordinates `(a,c)`; `liftedBasis_test_empty`
lifts the empty basis of the zero module and its representation is zero.

`TopologicalBasis.coefficientIdeal b N` is the ideal generated by all coordinates of all
members of the submodule `N`. It does not assert finite generation. Its Checks are:

- `coefficientIdeal_test_zero` — the zero submodule has coefficient ideal zero.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_vector` — the submodule generated by `a e_i` has ideal `(a)`.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_twoTerm` — the submodule generated by `a e₀ + c e₁` has ideal `(a,c)`.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_unit` — the whole module has unit coefficient ideal when the basis

`TopologicalBasis.coefficientIdeal_span_isPrincipal` states the additional valuation-base
conclusion: for a complete rank-one base `O_K` and a topological basis over `O_K`, the
coefficients of one element generate a principal ideal. Zero gives the zero ideal; for a
nonzero element, decay and the rank-one topology give a coefficient of largest absolute
value (BL II Prop. 2.3(b), p. 408).

The pointwise predicates use `FormalScheme.RigPoint`, including its defining ideal;
its special point alone does not determine a rig-point. `IsRigFlatAt` tests the localized
coefficient module on every affine neighbourhood of that special point. `rigRelDim`
takes the infimum of the local fibre dimensions over those neighbourhoods: for the
structural map `A → B` and rig-point prime `q`, the ring is
`B_q / (q ∩ A)B_q`. This is the local ring of the fibre, and the value is independent
of the charts under the stated tfp hypotheses. The supremum over no rig-points is
`−∞`. The affine/classical dimension comparison is Fujiwara–Kato II,
Theorem 10.1.8 and Proposition 10.1.9, pp. 585–586; the polydisc calculation is
Propositions 10.1.12–10.1.13, p. 587.

`isRigFlatAt_iff_localization` assumes a tfp source, admissible base and a finitely
presented coefficient sheaf; the chosen affine chart contains the special point and
its specified prime equals the rig-point ideal on that chart.
`isRigFlatAt_iff_genericFibre_flat` assumes the source and base admit generic fibres,
the morphism is adic, the source is tfp and the base admissible. Its analytic point
has the given specialisation and valuation kernel on every formal affine neighbourhood.
It identifies rig-flatness of the structure sheaf with flatness of the actual stalk
map of `d(f)`. Fujiwara–Kato II, Proposition 8.3.1 and Corollary 8.3.2, p. 559,
supply the completed local-ring and affine restriction comparisons.

`IsRigFlatAt.admissibleBlowUp` assumes admissible source and base, open finite type
centres, their admissible blow-ups, a commuting lifted morphism and corresponding
rig-point ideals. It compares a finitely presented sheaf with its pullback along
the source projection; the generic fibres of both projections are isomorphisms
(Conrad AWS, Example 3.3.11 and Exercise 3.3.12, pp. 33–34).
`isRigFlatInDim_of_rigRelDim_le` assumes quasi-compact source and base, a tfp source
and admissible base. Its bound is `∀ r, rigRelDim f r < n`, so the zero-dimensional
threshold never uses truncated natural subtraction. The exceptional closed subscheme
is the whole source, including when the generic fibre is empty.
`IsRigFlatInDim.pushforward_finite` has quasi-compact tfp source and intermediate
space, admissible quasi-compact base, a finitely presented sheaf, and a map preserving
the specified ideals of definition whose every reduction is finite. Its equivalence
uses finite direct image and preservation of dimensions of closed supports in each
fibre (BL II, Definition 3.9, p. 416, and the definition after Theorem 4.1, p. 419).

**Checks for `IsRigFlatAt` and `rigRelDim`.**

- `IsRigFlatAt_zero`: the zero sheaf is rig-flat at every rig-point.
- `IsRigFlatAt_identity`: the structure sheaf is rig-flat over the identity.
- `IsRigFlatAt_torsion`: sections killed by powers of the structural pseudouniformizer
  localize to zero at every rig-point.
- `IsRigFlatAt_closedPoint`: the quotient by the disc coordinate fails rig-flatness
  at its zero rig-point, as in `rigFlat_test_closedPoint`.
- `rigRelDim_identity`: the local fibre dimension of the identity is zero.
- `rigRelDim_smooth`: a smooth formal morphism of relative dimension `n` has
  rig-dimension `n` at every rig-point; this includes the relative polydisc.
- `rigRelDim_empty`: the supremum of relative rig-dimensions for an empty source is `−∞`.

The global predicate `FormalScheme.IsRigFlatInDim` uses a finite type ideal sheaf
whose generic fibres have dimension less than `n`. On each affine chart, away from this
closed support and the pseudouniformizer, the localized coefficient module is flat over
the base chart ring. Thus the closed support, structural maps and scalar actions are
part of the condition.

- `IsRigFlatInDim_identity`: the structure sheaf over the identity satisfies every bound.

**Rig-flatness in top dimension is freeness at the generic point of the fibre.**
(*rig-flatness-generic-point-criterion*) Let `T = Spf A` be admissible and `h : Z = Spf B → T`
affine, smooth and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension `m`
(Bosch–Lütkebohmert say geometrically connected, equivalent for smooth fibres). Let `X → T` be
locally of tf presentation with a closed immersion `Y ⊆ X` of finite presentation, and `ℳ` a
coherent `O_X`-module that is an `O_Y`-module admitting a `T`-dévissage `(g : Y → Z, ℳ, α : ℒ → 𝒩,
𝒫)` in dimension `m` (*formal-devissage-step*), with `m = dim(Y/T) = dim(Z/T)`; `M = Γ(Y, ℳ)`, `N =
Γ(Z, 𝒩)`. Let `t` be a rig-point of `T` (a maximal ideal of `A_K`), viewed as a prime `t ⊆ A` with
`ϖ ∉ t`, and `η = tB`, the prime ideal that is the generic point of the fibre over `t`
(*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral*). Prove that the following are
equivalent: (a) `ℳ` is rig-flat over `T` in dimension `≥ m` above `t` (*rig-flat-in-dimension*); (b)
`𝒩` is rig-flat over `T` in dimension `≥ m` above `t`; (c) `N_η` is flat over `A_t`; (d) `N_η` is
free over `B_η` (BL II §3, before Prop. 3.12, p. 417, its purpose and the generic point `η = tB`;
proof of Prop. 3.12, p. 417, the step (c) ⇒ (d)). For `Z = D^m_T` and `ℳ = 𝒩 = O_Z^r` all four
conditions hold. For `Z = D¹_T` over `T = Spf O_K⟨s⟩`, `𝒩 = O_Z/(sζ)` with `ζ` the coordinate and `t
= (s)`: `N_η = k(η) ≠ 0` is killed by `s`, neither free nor `A_t`-flat, and `𝒩` is not rig-flat in
dimension `≥ 1` above `t` (its non-rig-flat locus is the whole rigid fibre). *Needs:*
*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral*; *formal-devissage-step*;
*rig-flat-in-dimension*; *rig-point*; *smooth-formal-scheme*; Mathlib
