**Fitting ideals of coherent modules on formal schemes.** (*formal-fitting-ideal*) Let `X` be a
formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf presentation and `ℳ` a coherent `O_X`-module, so that its sections
over formal affine opens are finitely presented modules over coherent rings
(*tfp-algebra-coherent*). For `r ∈ ℕ` the `r`-th Fitting ideal `F_r(ℳ) ⊆ O_X` is the coherent ideal
given on a formal affine open `U = Spf A` by Tau Ceti's ring-level Fitting ideal `fittingIdeal A M r
⊆ A` of the finitely presented `A`-module `M = Γ(U, ℳ)` (the ideal of `(n − r) × (n − r)` minors of
a presentation `A^m → A^n → M → 0`, with `F_r(M) = A` if `n − r ≤ 0`), whose independence of the
presentation, monotonicity `fittingIdeal_monotone`, base change `fittingIdeal_baseChange`
(`F_r(M ⊗_A A') = F_r(M)A'`), generation criterion (`fittingIdeal_eq_top_iff_finrank_le`,
`fittingIdeal_eq_bot_of_lt_finrank`, `fittingIdeal_le_iff_lt_finrank`) and value on cyclic modules
`fittingIdeal_quotient_zero` are library theorems and are not restated (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.4.1 is
their source). The scheme version, on any scheme and any finite-type quasi-coherent module, is Tau
Ceti's `Scheme.Modules.fittingIdeal` with `fittingIdeal_Spec`, `mem_support_fittingIdeal_iff` and
`fittingIdeal_pullback`. This target is the formal-scheme wrapper: the ring-level ideals glue to a
coherent ideal `F_r(ℳ)`, compatible with restriction and with pull-back along morphisms of formal
schemes, `F_0(ℳ) ⊆ F_1(ℳ) ⊆ …`, `F_r(ℳ)_x = O_{X,x}` iff `ℳ_x` is generated by `r` elements, and
`ℳ` locally free of rank `r` gives `F_r(ℳ) = O_X`, and also `F_{r−1}(ℳ) = 0` when
`r > 0`. Indices lie in `ℕ`: at rank zero `F_0(0) = O_X`, so truncated subtraction cannot
be used to claim `F_{0−1}(0) = 0`. In `FormalScheme`, define
`fittingIdeal` as `F_r(ℳ)`, a coherent ideal of `O_X`; prove `fittingIdeal_spf` (on `Spf A`,
`F_r(ℳ)` corresponds to `fittingIdeal A (Γ(Spf A, ℳ)) r`), `fittingIdeal_mono` (`F_r(ℳ) ⊆ F_{r+1}(ℳ)`, from `fittingIdeal_monotone`), `fittingIdeal_pullback` (`F_r(φ*ℳ) = F_r(ℳ)O_{X'}` for
`φ : X' → X`, from `fittingIdeal_baseChange`), `fittingIdeal_restrict` (compatibility with
restriction to open formal subschemes), `fittingIdeal_eq_top_iff` (`F_r(ℳ)_x = O_{X,x}` iff `ℳ_x` is
generated by `r` elements, from `fittingIdeal_le_iff_lt_finrank` and Nakayama),
`fittingIdeal_of_locallyFree` (`ℳ` locally free of rank `r` gives `F_r(ℳ) = O_X` and, for
`r > 0`, `F_{r−1}(ℳ) = 0`, from `fittingIdeal_eq_top_iff_finrank_le` and `fittingIdeal_eq_bot_of_lt_finrank`) and the
theorem `fittingIdeal_isCoherent` (`F_r(ℳ)` is a coherent ideal) (BL II §3, Def. 3.13, p. 418, the
definition, independence and base change; RG Première partie, §5.4, Rappels 5.4.1, p. 39, the
ring-level definition via exterior powers). *Needs:* *tfp-algebra-coherent*; *tfp-locality*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *formal-scheme-gluing* (layer F0); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.fittingIdeal`,
`TauCeti.fittingIdeal_monotone`, `TauCeti.fittingIdeal_baseChange`,
`TauCeti.fittingIdeal_eq_top_iff_finrank_le`, `TauCeti.fittingIdeal_eq_bot_of_lt_finrank`,
`TauCeti.fittingIdeal_le_iff_lt_finrank`, `TauCeti.fittingIdeal_quotient_zero`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.fittingIdeal`, `fittingIdeal_Spec`, `mem_support_fittingIdeal_iff`,
`fittingIdeal_pullback`.

The construction `FormalScheme.fittingIdeal` takes
`M : X.Modules` with `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation M` and a natural index.
Its sections are the functions whose germs lie in `TauCeti.fittingIdeal` of the
module stalk. `moduleStalk_finite` supplies finite generation of those stalks;
`fittingIdeal_stalk` identifies the resulting ideal stalk with the ring Fitting
ideal. These statements use local finite presentations (Fujiwara–Kato,
0.4.1.3–4, p. 107) and finite minors ([Stacks, §15.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07Z6)).
`fittingIdeal_eq_top_iff` expresses the unit-stalk condition as the existence of
a neighbourhood on which the ideal is the unit ideal; its right side is a family
of `n` elements spanning the module stalk. `fittingIdeal_of_locallyFree` assumes
an open trivialization of rank `r` around every point, including rank zero.
`fittingIdeal_pullback` and `fittingIdeal_restrict` use the existing
`modulePullback` and `IdealSheafData.extension`; their module arguments are
finitely presented, including the pulled-back module (finite presentation is
preserved by pullback: Fujiwara–Kato, 0.4.1.3, p. 107).

For `fittingIdeal_spf` and `fittingIdeal_isCoherent`, the base `O` is a complete
rank-one valuation domain with pseudouniformizer `ϖ`, and `s : X → Spf O`
satisfies `IsLocallyTFP ϖ s`. No noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The former
computes sections over every formal affine open `U`, using
`CoherentModule.affine_finitePresentation`; the latter asserts that the ideal
subsheaf is finitely presented, namely `IdealSheafData.IsCoherent`. Here finite
presentation agrees with coherence (Conrad AWS 2007, §3.3, p. 32;
Fujiwara–Kato, 0.4.1.7–8, p. 108). `fittingIdeal_mono` and the other local
identities apply to any formal scheme and finitely presented module sheaf;
they do not assert coherence of the ideal over arbitrary noncoherent rings.

`fittingIdeal_test_cyclic` states the two identities for the actual sheaf
cokernel of `𝒥 → O_X`. `fittingIdeal_test_baseChange` gives the extended ideal
for its pullback along any formal morphism. `fittingIdeal_test_notAnnihilator`
uses the direct sum of two such cokernels: its zeroth Fitting ideal is `𝒥²`,
and an ideal annihilates the sum exactly when it is contained in `𝒥`.
The inequality assumes `𝒥² ≠ 𝒥`; the zero and unit ideals are excluded from
that inequality. These three statements assume `𝒥` coherent and the displayed
cokernel or pullback finitely presented. Their algebra is
[Stacks, Lemma 15.8.4 and Example 15.8.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07Z6),
applied to local presentations.

- `fittingIdeal_test_zero` (degenerate) — `ℳ = 0`: `F_r(0) = O_X` for every `r ≥ 0`.
  The ring-level Check `fittingIdeal_test_zero_core` also checks truncated subtraction.
- `fittingIdeal_test_baseChange` (compatibility) — for `ℳ = O_X/ϖO_X` on `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` and the
  open immersion `Spf O_K⟨ζ, ζ⁻¹⟩ → X`: `F_0 = (ϖ)` restricts to `(ϖ)`.
- `fittingIdeal_test_notAnnihilator` (non-example) — for `ℳ = (O_X/ϖO_X)²`, `Ann(ℳ) = (ϖ)` but
  `F_0(ℳ) = (ϖ²)`: the Fitting ideal is not the annihilator.
- `fittingIdeal_padic` (computed non-example) — the completed associated sheaf of
  `(ℤ₂/2)²` on `Spf ℤ₂` has `F_0 = (4)` on global sections, whereas its
  module of global sections has annihilator `(2)`; these ideals are unequal.

- `fittingIdeal_test_zero_core` — `F_{0−1}(0) = F_0(0) = A`, since natural subtraction truncates.
- `fittingIdeal_test_twoTerm_core` — the diagonal presentation `diag(4,6)` over `ℤ` gives

**A principal Fitting ideal makes `M/Ann_M(F_r(M))` generated by `r` elements.**
(*rg-fitting-ideal-principal-generators*) Let `A` be a ring, `M` a finitely presented `A`-module and
`r ∈ ℕ`. Prove that if the `r`-th Fitting ideal `F_r(M)` is locally principal (locally generated by
one element), then `M/Ann_M(F_r(M))` is locally generated by `r` elements, where `Ann_M(I) = {m ∈ M
: Im = 0}` (RG Première partie, §5.4, Lemme 5.4.2 and its proof, p. 39: Cramer's rule). For `A` a
domain, `a ≠ 0`, `M = A/(a) ⊕ A` and `r = 1`: `F_1(M) = (a)`, `Ann_M((a)) = A/(a) ⊕ 0`, and
`M/Ann_M(F_1(M)) ≅ A` is generated by one element. *Needs:* *formal-fitting-ideal*; Mathlib
`Matrix.det`, `Matrix.mulVec_cramer`, `Submodule.annihilator`, `Module.FinitePresentation`.

(*fitting-ideal-invertible-locally-free*) Let `A` be a ring, `M` a finitely presented `A`-module and
`r ∈ ℕ`. Assume that `M` is free of rank `r` at every associated point of `A` — in the weakly associated sense of

(locally generated by one non-zero-divisor). Prove that `M/Ann_M(F_r(M))` is locally free of rank
`r` (BL II §3, Lem. 3.14, p. 418, the statement as quoted by Bosch–Lütkebohmert; RG Première partie,
§5.4, Lemme 5.4.3 and its proof, p. 40). For `A = O_K⟨ζ⟩` and `M = A/(ζ) ⊕ A`: `F_1(M) = (ζ)` is
invertible, `M` is free of rank `1` at the only associated point `(0)`, and `M/Ann_M(ζ) ≅ A`.

**An open and closed partition of the generic fibre extends to an admissible blow-up.**
(*partition-by-admissible-blow-up*) `FormalScheme.exists_admissibleBlowup_partition` states the
formal decomposition over `AdmissibleBlowup`; `exists_admissibleBlowUp_partition_affine` states

`ϖ`-torsion) and `e_1, …, e_k ∈ A_K = A ⊗_{O_K} K` pairwise orthogonal idempotents with `Σ e_i = 1`
(a partition of the generic fibre into open and closed parts). Choose `N` with `ϖ^N e_i ∈ A` for all
`i` and put `𝒥_i = {a ∈ A : a(1 − e_i) = 0 in A_K} = Ann_A(ϖ^N(1 − e_i))` and `𝒥 = 𝒥_1 + … + 𝒥_k`.
Prove that `𝒥` is a coherent open ideal, whose centre `V(𝒥)` lies in `T_0`, and that the admissible
blow-up `φ : T' → T` of `𝒥` is a disjoint union `T' = T'_1 ⊔ … ⊔ T'_k` of open formal subschemes,
`T'_i` being the locus where `𝒥_iO_{T'} = 𝒥O_{T'}`, with generic fibre the part `{e_i = 1}` of the
generic fibre of `T`; and that if `t ∈ T_0` and `a ∈ A` with `a ∉ t` satisfy `e_i = 1` in `A_K[a⁻¹]`
for some `i`, then `t ∉ V(𝒥)`, so `φ` is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of `t` (RG Première
partie, §5.1, Lemme 5.1.5 and its proof, p. 36, the scheme-theoretic statement, blowing up the sum
of the two ideals; BL II §4, proof of Special case 4.4, p. 421, Bosch–Lütkebohmert's use of 5.1.5 in
the formal setting). The formal chart argument uses FK II, Propositions 1.1.3–1.1.4,
pp. 434–436: on a chart generated by an element of `𝒥_i`, its products with the other
ideals vanish, and invertibility of the centre separates the pieces. In the statement,
`A` has its `ϖ`-adic topology, the structural ring map is continuous, and the type-(S)
instance for `Spf A` supplies `genericFibre` (it follows from admissibility).
The ideal sheaves are generated by the displayed coefficient ideals, and the strata are
characterized on every open by equality of the extended ideals. Under the generic-fibre
isomorphism, the `i`th stratum is `{x | ∃ a ∈ 𝒥_i, |a(x)| ≠ 0}`, which is exactly `{e_i = 1}`.
Whenever `e_i = 1` after inverting `a`, the projection is an isomorphism over all of `D(a)`.

### R2.8 formal completions of schemes and the good-reduction locus

This subsection compares the generic fibre of the formal completion of a scheme with the
analytification of its generic fibre: Huber's morphism `σ` and the comparison `φ` of his Proposition

`φ` is an isomorphism for proper models), and the converse for flat quasi-projective models.

completion `X̂` along a closed subscheme defined by an ideal of finite type — the formal scheme of

Layer 4 (§4.8); no noetherian hypothesis on `X` is made here — assumed of type (S),
prove that there is a natural
morphism of locally ringed spaces `σ_X : d(X̂) → X`, the unique one such that for every open `U ⊆

→ Y` be locally of finite type between schemes, `Y' ⊆ Y` closed and defined by a quasi-coherent

R1). Prove Proposition 1.9.6: (i) `φ` is a local isomorphism; (ii) if `f` is separated, `φ` is

for general separated `X` of finite type the compactification step needs Nagata's theorem over

**Unique Frobenius lift on a formal scheme étale over the formal torus.**
(*frobenius-lift-etale-over-torus*) Let `κ` be a perfect field of characteristic `p`, `W = W(κ)`
with Witt-vector Frobenius `σ` (Mathlib `WittVector.frobenius`), and `𝕋^d = Spf W⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩` the formal torus. Let `𝔛 = Spf R` be affine with an étale morphism `𝔛 → 𝕋^d`, `T_i ↦ T_i ∈ R`, so that `R` is `p`-adically complete and étale levelwise over `W⟨T^{±1}⟩`. Prove that there is
a unique ring endomorphism `φ : R → R` such that `φ` is `σ`-semilinear (`φ(a·r) = σ(a)φ(r)` for `a ∈
W`), `φ(T_i) = T_i^p` for all `i`, and `φ(r) ≡ r^p mod pR` for all `r ∈ R`; more generally, that if
`A → R` is a formally étale map of `p`-adically complete rings (étale modulo every `p^m`) and `φ_A`
is a Frobenius lift on `A`, there is a unique Frobenius lift `φ_R` on `R` extending `φ_A`, so that
Frobenius lifts are compatible with étale maps over `𝕋^d`; uniqueness uses `p`-adic completeness and
formal unramifiedness. In general a smooth formal scheme over `W` admits no global Frobenius lift;
lifts exist on each open étale over a torus (TT §2.3, Rem. 2.20, p. 19: no global lift in general,
and existence and uniqueness on opens étale over the torus). On the torus itself `φ(Σ a_ν T^ν) = Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}`; on `𝔛 = Spf W⟨T^{±1}, (T − 1)⁻¹⟩` (open in the torus), `φ((T − 1)⁻¹) = (T^p − 1)⁻¹`,
which lies in `R` because `T^p − 1 ≡ (T − 1)^p mod p` is invertible. For `d = 0`, `R ≅ ∏ᵢ W(κ'ᵢ)`
for finitely many finite separable `κ'ᵢ/κ` (a single `W(κ')` when `Spf R` is connected, `R = 0`
allowed), and `φ` is the product of the Witt-vector Frobenii. Equal characteristic
is degenerate: if `pR = 0` the `p`-adic topology is discrete, the only Frobenius lift is the
absolute Frobenius `r ↦ r^p`, and `R` cannot be étale over `(W(κ)/p²)[T^{±1}]` unless `R = 0` (an
étale algebra over `(W(κ)/p²)[T^{±1}]` is flat over `W(κ)/p²`, and `p = 0` on a flat
`W(κ)/p²`-module forces the module to vanish); the general form with `A → R` of characteristic `p`
(étale levelwise, each level being `A → R` itself) is the statement that the absolute Frobenius
of `R` is the unique lift of that of `A`. The scheme-level absolute and relative Frobenius
are supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.29.

### R2.10 fractional bounds, section domains and Hasse domains

This subsection defines the valuative loci `{|f| ≤ |g|^q}` and `{|f| ≥ |g|^q}` for rational
exponents `q` without adjoining a `q`-th root, the domains `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` cut out on the generic
fibre by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal model together with their formal models (open
charts of an admissible blow-up), the Hasse domains `X(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}` with their transition
maps, and Conrad's Hasse-invariant loci of a generalized elliptic curve; it closes with three
supporting results used across the layer: the adic flatness criterion behind Bosch–Lütkebohmert I
Lemma 1.6, the properties preserved by Conrad's generic-fibre functor, and coherent modules and
rings.

**Fractional valuation bounds `|f| ≤ |g|^q` and `|f| ≥ |g|^q` for `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`.**
(*fractional-valuation-bound*) Let `A` be a commutative ring, `f, g ∈ A` and `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`. For `v ∈ Spv A` write `q = a/b` with `a ∈ ℕ`, `b ∈ ℕ_{>0}`, and define `|f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q` to mean `v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)` (the valuative relation `f^b ≤_v g^a`), and `|f(v)| ≥ |g(v)|^q` to mean `v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a)`;
strict versions likewise. This does not depend on the representative `(a, b)` of `q`, because `x ↦
x^n` is strictly increasing on a totally ordered value monoid. No element `g^q` of `A` (or of the
base field) is used: when `K = ℚ_p`, `|p|^{1/2}` is not the absolute value of any element of `K`,
yet `{|f| ≤ |p|^{1/2}}` is defined; the threshold `|g|^q` is realised by an element only after an
explicit extension. Second convention, compatible with the first: if `φ : A → B` is a ring map
and `B` contains `c` and a unit `u` with `u, u⁻¹ ∈ B⁺` and `c^b = φ(g)^a u` (e.g. `c = ϖ^{a/b} ∈ L = K(ϖ^{1/b})`, or `c = p^ε ∈ ℤ_p^cycl` of `p`-adic valuation `ε`), then for `v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺)` one has
`|φ(f)(v)| ≤ |φ(g)(v)|^q ⟺ v(φ(f)) ≤ v(c)`, since `v(u) = 1`. Degenerate values: for `q = 0` the
sets are `{v(f) ≤ 1}` and `{v(f) ≥ 1}` whatever `g` is; for `g = 0` and `q > 0`, `fracPowLE f 0 q =
{v(f) = 0}` and `fracPowGE f 0 q = Spv A`, consistently for every representative of `q` because
`0^n = 0`; for `g` a unit and `q > 0`, `fracPowGE f g q` contains no `v` with `v(f) = 0`; the
prime `p` plays no role in the definition (`p = 2` changes nothing, there being no signs). When
`A` is Huber and `g` is a unit (e.g. `g = ϖ` in a Tate ring), `fracPowLE f g q ∩
Spa(A, A⁺)` is the rational subset `R({f^b, g^a}/g^a)` and `fracPowGE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺)` is
`R({g^a, f^b}/f^b)`. For `q = a/b` the set `fracPowLE f g q` differs from Tau Ceti's
`basicOpenFinset {f^b} (g^a)` only by the condition `v(g^a) ≠ 0`, which is automatic for a unit
`g`; Tau Ceti's `FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound`/`IsRadiusUpperBound` on `Spv` of a Witt vector
ring are the case `f = [ϖ]`, `g = p`; this target is the general pair `(f, g)`, and those predicates
must be its specialisation. In `ValuationSpectrum`, define `fracPowLE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≤ v(g^{q.num})}` and `fracPowGE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≥ v(g^{q.num})}`;
prove `mem_fracPowLE_iff` (for every `a ∈ ℕ`, `b ∈ ℕ_{>0}` with `q = a/b`: `v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔
v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)`); the simp lemma `fracPowLE f g n = {v : v(f) ≤ v(g^n)}` for `n ∈ ℕ`;
`fracPow_inter_spa` (if `g` is a unit: `fracPowLE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {f^b, g^a}
(g^a)` and `fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {g^a, f^b} (f^b)`); monotonicity (on
`{v(g) ≤ 1}`: `q ≤ q'` implies `fracPowLE f g q' ⊆ fracPowLE f g q` and
`fracPowGE f g q ⊆ fracPowGE f g q'`); compatibility with pullback (for `φ : A → B`:
`(Spv φ)⁻¹(fracPowLE f g q) = fracPowLE (φ f) (φ g) q`); the explicit-extension form (if
`c^b = g^a u` with `u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺` and `q = a/b`, then for `v ∈ spa A⁺`:
`v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔ v(f) ≤ v(c)`); invariance under units (if `u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺`:
`fracPowGE (u f) g q ∩ spa A⁺ = fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺`, and likewise for LE); the power rule
(`fracPowLE (f^n) g (n q) = fracPowLE f g q` for `n > 0`); and the product rule
(`fracPowLE f g q ∩ fracPowLE f' g q' ⊆ fracPowLE (f f') g (q + q')`) (BHW §2.1, p. 7 of the author version, fractional thresholds with the explicit condition that `|p|^ε` lies in the value group;
Scholze15 §III.2, Def. III.2.12, p. 38, the explicit-extension convention with `p^ε ∈ ℤ_p^cycl`;
Conrad-MR §4.1, Thm 4.1.1(1), p. 26, thresholds in the divisible hull of the value group of `k`).

**The domain `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` cut out by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal model.**
(*section-valuation-domain*) Let `𝔛` be an admissible formal `O_K`-scheme, `ℒ` an invertible `O_𝔛`-module, `s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ)` and `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`, interpreted by *fractional-valuation-bound*. Choose an open cover `𝔛 = ⋃ U_j`
by formal affines `U_j = Spf A_j` with generators `ℒ|_{U_j} = O e_j`, and write `s|_{U_j} = f_j e_j`. Define `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) := ⋃_j (fracPowGE f_j ϖ q ∩ d(U_j)) ⊆ d(𝔛)`, and likewise `𝔛_η(|s| ≤
|ϖ|^q)` with `fracPowLE`. These sets do not depend on the cover or the generators: on `U_j ∩ U_k`
one has `e_k = u e_j` with `u ∈ O(U_j ∩ U_k)^×`, so `f_j = u f_k`, and `|u(x)| = 1` on `d(U_j ∩

∈ ϖ^c ℒ` for some `c ∈ ℚ` with `c > q` (`ϖ^c ℒ` meaning sections whose local coordinates satisfy

The generic-fibre API assumes that `𝔛` has type (S), and that `O_K` is a
complete rank-one valuation ring with pseudouniformizer `ϖ`. The scalar
argument `a : Γ(𝔛, O)` is the image of `ϖ` under the structural map
`b : 𝔛 → Spf O_K`. `sectionDomainGE` and `sectionDomainLE` return
`Opens (genericFibre 𝔛).obj`. Their general scalar interface takes the interior of
the locus described by integral affine frames; for the admissible model and
pseudouniformizer above, `sectionDomainGE_of_trivialization` identifies that open
with the full local `fracPowGE` locus and also gives the `fracPowLE` identification.
Thus on these models the definitions glue the rational opens without changing
membership. This uses Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.1 and (1.9.3), pp. 96–98;
the rational-subset formulas are the two clauses of `fracPow_inter_spa`.
Invertibility is expressed by local isomorphisms with the structure module;
sections are morphisms from that module, using the existing `FormalScheme.Modules`.

`sectionDomainGE_indep_generator` is the integral-unit specialization of the unit-invariance
clause of *fractional-valuation-bound*. The separate `sectionDomainGE_congr_affine` supplies the
estimate for adding `ϖ^c t` with natural `c > q` and `t ∈ A⁺` on `Spa(A, A⁺)`.
`sectionDomainGE_congr` concerns sections of the invertible sheaf on the formal
model, with their difference locally bounded by `|ϖ|^c` for rational `c > q`; changing frames and
changing lifts are different operations. Under the same admissibility and
invertibility hypotheses, `isCompact_sectionDomainGE` adds quasi-compactness
when the formal scheme is quasi-compact. `sectionDomainGE_preimage` requires an
adic morphism between admissible models; any integral identification of its
pulled-back unit with the structure module gives the same domain. These assertions
follow by applying the affine formulas on the generic-fibre charts of Huber96
Prop. 1.9.1 and (1.9.3), pp. 96–98. The monotonicity, zero, power and tensor
identities above use those same charts and the ordered valuation laws; the
positive-power hypothesis excludes the zeroth-power counterexample below.

`sectionDomainGE_ofMod` uses the sheaf cokernel of a morphism `μ : ℒ → ℒ` and
local lifts of its section. In `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_eq`, `μ` acts on every
open by multiplication by `a^m`, and `q < m`; any global lift yields exactly
`sectionDomainGE`, and the same statement after restriction identifies local
lifts. Its definition requires no global lift. The strict estimate and gluing
are the general line-bundle form of Scholze15 Def. III.2.12, Lem. III.2.13 and
the following generic-fibre description, p. 38.

`SectionDomainModel.genericFibre_eq` identifies the image of the model's generic
fibre with `sectionDomainGE` and states that its projection is an open immersion.
It assumes an admissible model, an invertible `ℒ`, `c ≠ 0`, and
`c^(q.den) = ϖ^(q.num) · w` with `w ∈ O_Kˣ`; both formal schemes have type (S).
The unit factor has value one. The statement is the valuation-domain form of
`sectionDomainModel_genericFibre`, using the local equation in Scholze15
Lem. III.2.13, p. 38. For thresholds not realized in `O_K`, the existing model
of `(s^{⊗b}, ϖ^a)` and `sectionDomainGE_pow` give the same fractional domain.

**Checks for upper bounds and quotient sections.**

- `sectionDomainLE_zero` — the zero section lies below the unit threshold everywhere.
- `sectionDomainLE_unit` — the unit section at exponent zero gives the whole space.
- `sectionDomainLE_zeroThreshold` — a unit section cannot lie below the zero threshold at exponent `1/2`.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_zero` — for `q < m`, the zero class modulo `ϖ^m` has empty lower domain.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_generator` — the class of the unit section has the whole domain.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_lifts` — adding `μ(t)` to a lift preserves its domain when `μ` is multiplication by `ϖ^m` and `q < m`.

**Checks.**

- `sectionDomain_test_projectiveLine` (computation) — for `𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}`, `ℒ = O(1)`, `s = T_0` and
  `q = 1`: `sectionDomainGE s 1 = {x : |T_0(x)| ≥ |ϖ| · max(|T_0(x)|, |T_1(x)|)}`, the complement of
  the closed valuation subset `{|T_0/T_1| < |ϖ|}` (which need not be open at higher-rank points).
  The check states the local homogeneous-coordinate formula for a pair of
  sections generating the line: in an integral frame their coordinates generate
  the unit ideal, so their maximum value is one. It applies to `T_0,T_1` on both
  standard formal charts of `P̂¹`.
- `sectionDomain_test_generatorIndependence` (characterisation) — on `𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩` with `ℒ =
  O`, the generators `e` and `T·e` give the same domain for `s = T² e = T·(Te)`: `{|T²| ≥ |ϖ|^q} =
  {|T| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` because `|T| = 1` on `d(𝔛)`.
- `sectionDomain_test_liftIndependence` (characterisation) — on `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` with `ℒ = O` and `q =
  1/2`: `s = T` and `s' = T + ϖ` give the same domain `{|T²| ≥ |ϖ|}`; for `q = 1` they do not (the
  point `T = −ϖ` lies in the first but not the second). The check also
  evaluates these two sections after that constant specialization: at `q = 1`
  their domains are respectively the whole generic fibre and the empty open.
- `sectionDomain_test_integralStructure` (non-example) — replacing `ℒ` by the lattice `ϖ⁻¹ℒ ⊇ ℒ` in
  the same `ℒ_η` multiplies the local coordinates of `s` by `ϖ` and changes the domain from `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` to `{|s|_ℒ ≥ |ϖ|^{q−1}}`; a definition using only `ℒ_η` is ill-defined. The
  equality uses `q+1` on the rescaled side and `q` on the original side, and
  separately states emptiness for rescaled exponents below one.
- `sectionDomain_test_degenerate` (degenerate) — if `s̄` generates `ℒ/ϖℒ` everywhere then the domain
  is `d(𝔛)` for every `q ≥ 0`; if `s = 0` it is empty.

**Checks for powers and lift independence.**

- `sectionDomainGE_test_zeroPower` — the zeroth tensor power of the zero section is `1`:
  its threshold-zero domain is the whole space, whereas the original zero section's is empty.
  Thus the power identity requires `n > 0`.
- `sectionDomainGE_test_twoTerm` — `|1+p| = 1 ≥ |p|^{1/2}` and
  `|0+p| = |p| < |p|^{1/2}` at the `p`-adic valuation, including `p = 2`.
  Adding a term divisible by `p` preserves these two sides of the threshold.

`FormalScheme.SectionInverse` records a morphism from the pulled-back line bundle
to the pulled-back unit with composite multiplication by the threshold.
**Checks:** `SectionInverse_unit` has a unique solution for the unit section;
`SectionInverse_zeroThreshold` admits the zero solution; `SectionInverse_zeroSection`
has no solution for nonzero threshold on a nonempty admissible model.
`FormalScheme.SectionDomainModel` records the representing formal scheme and
`FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel` selects it.
**Checks:** `SectionDomainModel_unit` / `sectionDomainModel_unit` give the original
model for the unit section; `SectionDomainModel_zero` / `sectionDomainModel_zero`
give the empty model for the zero section and nonzero threshold;
`SectionDomainModel_associated` / `sectionDomainModel_associated` identify thresholds
differing by a unit.


**Checks for the selected model.** `sectionDomainModel_unitSection` makes its projection
an isomorphism for the unit section and any nonzero threshold;
`sectionDomainModel_zeroSection` makes its space empty for the zero section and nonzero
threshold; `sectionDomainModel_representing` gives a unique isomorphism over the original
formal scheme to any other model representing the same functor. These statements apply
to the selected `sectionDomainModel` itself, with the line-bundle and admissibility hypotheses.
At exponent `q = 0` the threshold is `c = 1`: the model is the open where the section
is invertible, and is the entire formal scheme when the section generates everywhere
(Scholze15, Lemma III.2.13, p. 38, the equation `u s = 1`).

invariant; for modular curves and Shimura varieties it is supplied by the moduli roadmaps. For `ε ∈
ℚ` with `0 ≤ ε < 1` the Hasse domain is `X(ε) := 𝔛_η(|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε) ⊆ d(𝔛)`, the section domain
(*section-valuation-domain*) of any local lift `H̃a` of `Ha` to `ω^{⊗(p−1)}`, with the fractional
convention of *fractional-valuation-bound*; it is well defined because two lifts differ by
`p·(section)` and `|p| < |p|^ε` for `ε < 1` (for `ε = 1` the domain depends on the lift). If `O_K`

domain on the generic fibre or passes to an explicit extension. `X(0) = {|Ha| = 1}` is the tube of
the ordinary locus `𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha)`. Formation of `X(ε)` commutes with pull-back along morphisms `𝔜 → 𝔛`

**Flatness from flatness modulo powers of an ideal.** (*adic-local-flatness-criterion*) Let `A` be a
commutative ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `M` an `A`-module, with no noetherian or completeness
hypothesis on `A`. Assume that for every finitely generated ideal `a ⊆ A` (1) the `I`-adic topology
of `A` induces the `I`-adic topology of `a`: for every `n` there is `m` with `a ∩ I^m ⊆ I^n a`, and
(2) `a ⊗_A M` is `I`-adically separated: `⋂_n I^n (a ⊗_A M) = 0`; the two conditions replace
Artin–Rees and Krull intersection. Prove that if `M/I^n M` is flat over `A/I^n` for every `n ≥ 1`,
then `M` is flat over `A`; and that in the same situation, if moreover `I ⊆ Jac(A)` and `M/IM` is
faithfully flat over `A/I`, then `M` is faithfully flat over `A` (BL I §1, proof of Lem. 1.6, p.
295: Bosch–Lütkebohmert reduce Lemma 1.6 to the proof of Bourbaki AC III §5 no. 2 Theorem 1 under
exactly the conditions (1) and (2), condition (2) reading '`a ⊗ M` is separated with respect to the
`𝔍`-adic topology'; p. 296, the faithful-flatness addendum via Nakayama). For `A` noetherian, `I ⊆
Jac(A)` and `M` finite over a noetherian `A`-algebra `B` with `IB ⊆ Jac(B)`, (1) is Artin–Rees and
(2) Krull's intersection theorem, giving the noetherian local flatness criterion used in the
noetherian case of Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6. *Needs:* Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_injective`.

**Conrad's Berthelot-type generic fibre preserves finiteness, smoothness, flatness, properness and
fibre dimension.** (*berthelot-rig-functor-preserves-properties*) Let `C` be an adic noetherian ring
with a continuous map `C → R` to the valuation ring of a complete nonarchimedean field `k` (no
discreteness assumption), and let `f : X → Y` be a morphism in `FS_C` that is locally topologically
of finite type. Prove: (a) if `f` is finite so is `f^rig`; (b) if `f` is formally smooth of pure
relative dimension `d` then `f^rig` is smooth of pure relative dimension `d` (formally étale implies
étale), in Part II's sense, on generic fibres that are locally noetherian and hence locally
Huber-standard; (c) if `f` is finite flat of constant rank `d` so is `f^rig`; (d) if `f` is proper so is
`f^rig`; (e) if `f` is flat (resp. faithfully flat) so is `f^rig`; (f) if all fibres of `f` have
dimension `≤ d` so do those of `f^rig`; (g) if `f` is flat with geometrically reduced fibres of pure
dimension `d`, so is `f^rig` (Conrad-MR §3.1, Thm 3.1.6, p. 17, statements (a)–(g); proof of Thm
3.1.6, p. 18, the reduction by base change along `Spf R → Spf C` and by the rescalings `Y_c` to
Raynaud's generic fibre of formal `R`-models). After that reduction the inputs for (d), (f) and
(g) are targets of this roadmap. In (d), `f^rig` is proper in the adic sense of
*universally-closed-and-proper-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0). This is the forward direction
of *formal-rigid-properness-comparison* (ii), applied to the `R`-flat quotients of the base-changed
models; `d` kills `ϖ`-torsion, so their generic fibres do not change. Conrad's rigid statement
asserts Kiehl-properness. For non-discrete `|k^×|` that needs Temkin's comparison through Berkovich
spaces [Te, Cor. 4.4 and 4.5, p. 18 of the
[author version](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Local_Properties_I.pdf)], which is not
asserted here. Clauses (f) and (g) are *formal-model-fibre-comparison* (v) for the base-changed
models, the statement Conrad uses on p. 18 as Thm A.2.1. For `C = ℤ` and the Tate curve over
`ℤ[[q^{1/n}]]`, (d) and (e) give a proper flat adic curve over the open unit disc (Conrad-MR §3.1,
after Thm 3.1.6). *Needs:* *berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*;

`FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_preservesProperties` has seven conjuncts in the order
(a)–(g) above. Its field presentation identifies the chart ring with the complete
nontrivially valued field `K`, continuously in both directions, and its plus ring
with `K`'s power-bounded subring. The coefficient map is continuous and lands in
that plus ring. The common hypothesis `Hom.LocallyOfFiniteType f` includes
adicness. Write `rₙ` for `Hom.adicReduction f hft.choose n`, formed using powers
of the target ideal of definition extended to the source. In (b), formal
smoothness of dimension `d` is expressed by `SmoothOfRelativeDimension d rₙ`
for every `n`; the conclusion uses Part II's `Smooth.relativeDimension` and
includes `Etale` when `d = 0`. In (c), formal stalk flatness, finiteness of `r₀`
and `r₀.finrank y = d` yield analytic finiteness, flatness and local bases indexed
by `Fin d` for the sections over inverse images of affinoid target neighbourhoods.
Clause (e) also preserves surjectivity under its flatness hypothesis.

In (f), the scheme fibres of `r₀` have topological Krull dimension at most `d`.
In (g), `r₀` is geometrically reduced with pure-dimensional fibres, and `f` is
flat on formal stalks. Both analytic conclusions quantify over maps from every
complete rank-one field spectrum and supply an actual cartesian fibre. Clause
(f) bounds the ring Krull dimension on each affinoid chart of that fibre;
(g) requires those chart rings to be reduced and their prime spectra to have
pure dimension `d`. Quantifying over field extensions is essential for geometric
reducedness. These formulations retain empty fibres. Sources: Conrad-MR,

**Coherent modules and coherent rings.** (*coherent-modules*) Let `A` be a commutative ring, with no
noetherian hypothesis: the point of the notion is the non-noetherian rings `O_K⟨ξ⟩/a`. A finitely
generated `A`-module `M` is coherent if every finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely
presented (coherent means finitely generated with all finitely generated submodules finitely
presented, not merely finitely presented); `A` is a coherent ring if it is coherent as an
`A`-module, i.e. every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented. This is the ring case of EGA
0 §5.3 as recalled in Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1. Neither predicate is in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Tau
Ceti's `FinitelyPresentedSheaf` is finite presentation only), and SchemeAndStackFoundations'
pseudo-coherence (Layer 0, §0.5) is a different notion — a module with a resolution by finite free
modules up to a given degree. Its finite syzygy conditions are distinct from requiring every
finite submodule to be finitely presented. Define `Module.IsCoherent` (`M` is finitely generated
and every finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely presented) and `IsCoherentRing` (`A` is
`Module.IsCoherent` over itself); prove `Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_left`,
`Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_right` and `Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_middle` (in a short exact
sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` any two coherent members make the third coherent),
`Module.IsCoherent.ker`, `Module.IsCoherent.coker`, `Module.IsCoherent.range`,
`Module.IsCoherent.sup` and `Module.IsCoherent.inf` (kernels, cokernels and images of linear maps
between coherent modules, and sums and intersections of coherent submodules of a coherent module,
are coherent; hence finite direct sums are), `IsCoherentRing.isCoherent_iff_finitePresentation`
(over a coherent ring, `Module.IsCoherent A M ↔ Module.FinitePresentation A M`),
`Module.IsCoherent.tensorProduct` and `Module.IsCoherent.linearMap` (over a coherent ring, `M ⊗_A N`
and `Hom_A(M, N)` are coherent for coherent `M`, `N`), `IsCoherentRing.quotient` (if `A` is coherent
and `a ⊆ A` is a finitely generated ideal then `A/a` is a coherent ring, and an `A/a`-module is
coherent over `A/a` iff it is coherent over `A`) and the instance `IsNoetherianRing.isCoherentRing`
(noetherian rings are coherent) (BL I §1, before Prop. 1.3, p. 294: the definition, and the
two-out-of-three and closure properties quoted from EGA I_new 0 5.3.2;
[Stacks, Definition 10.90.1 and Lemmas 10.90.3–10.90.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05CU),
for the general predicates, exact sequences and finite-presentation comparison). *Needs:* Mathlib
`Module.FinitePresentation`.

**Checks.**

- `coherent_test_noetherian` (compatibility) — a noetherian ring is `IsCoherentRing`, and over it
  `Module.IsCoherent` coincides with `Module.Finite`.
- `coherent_test_nonCoherentRing` (non-example) — for a field `k`, `A = k[x, y_1, y_2, …]/(x y_1, x
  y_2, …)` is not a coherent ring: the principal ideal `(x)` is finitely generated but not finitely
  presented, since its annihilator `(y_1, y_2, …)` is not finitely generated.
- `coherent_test_notJustFinitelyPresented` (non-example) — in the ring `A` of
  `coherent_test_nonCoherentRing`, the module `A` itself is finitely presented (free of rank one)
  but not coherent, since its finitely generated submodule `(x)` is not finitely presented; so over
  non-noetherian rings 'coherent' cannot be replaced by 'finitely presented' (or by 'finitely
  generated').
- `coherent_test_infinitePolynomial` (computation) — the polynomial ring `ℤ[x_1, x_2, …]` in
  countably many variables is a coherent ring that is not noetherian.
- `coherent_test_zero` (degenerate) — the zero module is coherent over every ring, and the zero ring
  is a coherent ring.

The finite-syzygy predicate `Module.IsPseudoCoherentTo R M n` uses a projective
resolution whose terms in degrees `0` through `n` are finite free. The augmentation is
part of Mathlib's `ProjectiveResolution`, so the finite terms resolve the specified module.
This is the module form of finite pseudo-coherence (Stacks, Tag 064N).

**Checks.** `IsPseudoCoherentTo_zeroModule` holds in every degree for the zero module;
`IsPseudoCoherentTo_finite` identifies degree zero with finite generation;
`IsPseudoCoherentTo_presentation` identifies degree one with finite presentation.

The moduli scheme below and its formal completion supply the algebraic family and formal
group used for Hasse invariants. Étale descent of admissible opens is also developed here.
The analytic local-algebraicity, classification and level-cover package
(*rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification*) and its application
*hasse-loci-admissible-opens* are R3.7a targets, after R3.6's proper coherent theory
and R3.7's GAGA. Formal Hasse-section domains and their models remain in R2.10.

**The compactified moduli of generalised elliptic curves with level structure, and the formal group
along the identity section.** (*compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*) Let `Γ` be
`Γ(N)` with `N ≥ 3`, or `Γ₁(N)` with `N` divisible by an integer `d ≥ 5`.
`GeneralisedEllipticCurve.Level` records `N`, an auxiliary factor `d ∣ N` and `full`
(`true` for full level, `false` for cyclic level); full level takes `d = N`. The base
of `L` is `ℤ[1/d]`. In cyclic level only the primes dividing `d` are inverted, so `N`
may be divisible by a prime `p` with `p ∤ d`. Over this base, the compactified fine
moduli scheme `moduli L` carries
`universalCurve L` and `universalLevel L`. Full level includes all values of the
Weil pairing; fixing a primitive root selects the corresponding component over
`ℤ[ζ_N,1/N]`. Smaller levels require stacks; level one has the affine coarse
j-line on the smooth locus and its projective completion on the compactification.

`EllipticModuli.GroupCurve S` has a proper flat locally finitely presented
structure map, its entire smooth open as a commutative group object, and an
action of that group on the whole curve extending multiplication. Properness
supplies the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness required for finite
presentation. `GroupCurve.Iso` preserves the inclusion, group and action;
`GroupCurve.baseChange` uses scheme pullbacks. `ofElliptic` uses the imported
Modular Curves carrier. `nGon S n` uses positive `n` and cyclically identifies
infinity on component `i` with zero on component `i+1`; `nGon_normalization`
states this gluing's universal property over a field, including the self-gluing
for `n = 1`. `nGon_smoothLocus` identifies the smooth scheme over any ring
with the disjoint union of `n` multiplicative groups. `nGon_smoothPoints`
identifies its group of points over any ring `A` with units times locally constant
component labels on `Spec A`, including disconnected and nonreduced rings. The points `[a:b]` in this statement are `projectivePoint K a b h`
in Mathlib's `Proj K[X₀,X₁]`. `GeneralisedEllipticCurve S` requires every
geometric fibre, with its smooth group and whole-curve action, to be isomorphic
to a smooth elliptic curve or a standard polygon. This imposes the rotation
condition on singular fibres. Explicitly, a generalised elliptic curve over `S` is a proper flat
finitely presented curve `E → S` whose geometric fibres are elliptic curves or standard `n`-gons,
with a morphism `+ : E^sm ×_S E → E` that is an action of the smooth locus `E^sm` on `E`,
restricts on `E^sm ×_S E^sm` to a commutative group law on `E^sm`, and on every singular geometric
fibre acts by rotations on the cyclic polygon of irreducible components; the identification of
such a fibre with a standard `n`-gon carries this group and action structure, not only the curve.
The definition and classification are those of
[Conrad-GEC](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/kmpaper.pdf), Definition 2.1.4
and the paragraph following it, p. 5; the polygon construction is on pp. 4–5.

In full level, over a `ℤ[1/N]`-scheme `S`, `LevelStructure L E` is an isomorphism
of commutative `S`-group schemes `α : ((ℤ/N)²)_S ≅ E^sm[N]` whose labelled
sections meet every irreducible component of every geometric fibre of `E`.
The label of `(i,j)` is `α(i,j) = iP + jQ`, where `P = α(1,0)` and `Q = α(0,1)`;
these sections are killed by `N` and give a basis of the `N`-torsion in every geometric fibre.
This extends ModularCurves §3N's naive full-level group-scheme definition to generalised
elliptic curves; for smooth `E` it agrees with `GammaFullStructure` via
ModularCurves §3D's naive–Drinfeld comparison. The generalised-curve extension and its
component condition belong to this target. Prove `LevelStructure_map_zero`, giving
`α(0,0) = 0`, and `LevelStructure_map_add`, giving `α(u + v) = α(u) + α(v)` for
full level over every `S`-scheme after base change. In cyclic level the
section `P` is an ample Drinfeld `ℤ/N`-structure: the relative effective Cartier
divisor `∑_{j ∈ ℤ/N} [jP]` in `E^sm` is a subgroup scheme and meets every
irreducible component of every geometric fibre. In residue characteristic `p ∣ N`
this divisor need not be étale; allowing such structures is what gives an integral
moduli problem over a `p`-adic base containing curves whose polygon fibres have a
multiple of `p` sides (Conrad-MR §3.2, p. 19). Where `N` is invertible the
divisor is étale, and the condition says that `P` has exact order `N` on every
geometric fibre and that its multiples meet every component. The component
condition is the curve-specific ampleness criterion, not an extra assumption on an
arbitrary moduli scheme (Conrad-GEC, Definitions 2.4.1–2.4.2, p. 14, and 2.4.7,
p. 16). `moduli_classifies` states existence and uniqueness of the classifying
map for every such family over a `ℤ[1/d]`-scheme, with an isomorphism preserving
the smooth-group law, the whole-curve action and the level structure.
`moduli_isProper` and `moduli_finitePresentation` apply
to this particular representing scheme over `ℤ[1/d]`. For the latter, the conclusion
is local finite presentation together with quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness. Sources: Conrad-GEC, Theorems 3.1.4, p. 19, 3.2.7 and
3.3.1, p. 26, and 4.2.1(2), pp. 35–36 (the stack is a scheme over `ℤ[1/d]` for
every factor `d ∣ N` with `d ≥ 5` in cyclic level); Deligne–Rapoport IV §3 gives the
historical construction.

For a prime `p ∤ d` and a complete field `k` over `ℚ_p` with valuation ring `R`,
the base change of `moduli L` to `R` is a proper flat finitely presented
`R`-scheme with generic fibre the moduli scheme over `k`; it is the integral model
whose formal completion *hasse-loci-admissible-opens* uses, with `formalGroup`
applied to the base change of `universalCurve L`
(Conrad-MR §4.1, proof of Thm 4.1.1, p. 26, the level `Γ₁(N)` with an
auxiliary factor `d ≥ 5` invertible in `R`). A level prime to `p` does not
reach curves with a `p`-gon fibre: the component group of a `p`-gon is `ℤ/p`, on
which multiplication by an `N` prime to `p` is invertible, so every `N`-torsion
point lies on the identity component and no level structure meets the other components,
over any extension of the base field (`LevelStructure_pGonPrimeToP`). With `p ∤ d` and
`N = dp` the mixed range applies (`LevelStructure_pGonMixed`).

`identitySection E` is the identity of the smooth group. `formalGroup E` is
its completion along the kernel ideal of that section, using
`FormalScheme.idealCompletion`; `formalGroup.structure` is the induced base
map. The instances `formalGroup.grp` and `formalGroup.comm` supply the
completed commutative group law. `formalGroup_points` identifies its points on
discrete test schemes with smooth-group points supported on the identity,
commutes with the map into the smooth group, and preserves multiplication. Completion uses the identity ideal, so it
retains nilpotents in the base. For a smooth augmented algebra `ε : B →ₐ[A] A`,
write `I = ker ε`. If `t ∈ I` is a basis of `I/I²`, then
`formalGroup.coordinate ε t` identifies `B̂_I` with `A[[X]]`;
`formalGroup_coordinate` sends the image of `t` to `X`.
`formalGroup_affineCoordinate` gives the formal-scheme isomorphism for an
actual affine neighbourhood of `identitySection E`, with compatibility of its
structure map and augmentation, and the `X`-adic topology on `A[[X]]`.
`formalGroup_localParameter` supplies these affine neighbourhoods and a
parameter locally around every base point, with a scalar-preserving completed-ring
equivalence. The basis condition is stated explicitly by generation and linear independence
modulo `I²`. Source: [Stacks, 10.139.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05D5);
the local choice of neighbourhoods is [29.35.20](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05D9).
Completion of multiplication uses EGA I, 10.9.1–3, pp. 198–199.
After completion of the base these give the same one-parameter formal group
over the affine formal opens where the invariant differential line is trivial.

`jMap L b` has the complex fibre of `moduli L` as source and `Proj ℂ[X₀,X₁]`
as target. `jMap_values` uses points over `ℂ` and identifies its value on a smooth Weierstrass fibre
with `[j(W):1]` and characterizes the inverse image of `[1:0]` by polygon
fibres (Conrad-GEC, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, p. 36).
`tateCurve n` is the algebraic `n`-gon Tate family over `ℤ[[Q]]`, with
`Q = q^(1/n)`; it specializes to `nGon` and becomes smooth after inverting `Q`.
Its identity completion is isomorphic as a formal group to the identity
completion of the standard 1-gon over the same base, hence to `𝔾̂_m`
(Conrad-GEC, §2.5, construction and (2.5.3), p. 17).
*Needs:* the imported Modular Curves elliptic scheme and group law;
*formal-completion*; `FormalScheme.idealCompletion`; Mathlib `Scheme`,
`IsProper`, `LocallyOfFinitePresentation` and `GrpObj`.

**Checks.**

- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_jLine` (computation) — the `j`-invariant of the universal curve
  is a finite surjective morphism `j : M_Γ ⊗ ℂ → P¹_ℂ` onto the compactified `j`-line (the coarse moduli space
  of the compactified level-`1` problem, which is not itself one of the `M_Γ`: the level-`1` problem is not representable,
  every curve having the automorphism `−1`); the cusps are `j⁻¹(∞)`.
- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_tateCurve` (computation) — the Tate curve over `ℤ[[q]]` (with level after adjoining the
  required roots of unity and a root of `q` over `ℤ[1/d]`) has formal
  group `𝔾̂_m` along its identity section: `[p](X) = (1 + X)^p − 1`, with coefficient `1` at `X^p`,
  so its Hasse invariant is `1` and its fibres lie in `S^{≥1}` of *hasse-loci-admissible-opens*.
  The Check uses the formal-group isomorphism of `tateCurve n` with the
  standard 1-gon's identity completion. The power-series coefficient calculation
  applies in the multiplicative coordinate supplied by that isomorphism.
- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_nGon` (characterisation) — the smooth locus of the standard
  `n`-gon (the fibre of `E` over a cusp, `n ∣ N`) is `𝔾_m × ℤ/n`, with identity component `𝔾_m`;
  for `n = 1` the fibre is the nodal cubic with smooth locus `𝔾_m`.

**Admissible opens, admissible coverings and quasi-compactness descend along étale coverings with
local quasi-sections.** (*rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*) Let `k` be a complete
nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value. A morphism `q : S' → S` of rigid spaces over
`k` is an étale covering, `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering q`, if it is étale (`RigidSpace.IsEtale`,
*rigid-adic-etale-comparison*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1), surjective on points, and admits local
étale quasi-sections: there are an admissible covering `{S_i}` of `S` and, for each `i`, a
quasi-compact étale surjection `U_i → S_i` with an `S_i`-morphism `U_i → q⁻¹(S_i)` (Conrad-RA
Def 4.2.1, p. 30). Prove:

(a) `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.baseChange`, `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.ofAdmissibleCover` and
`RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.analytification`: étale coverings are stable under base change; the
coproduct of the members of an admissible affinoid covering maps to the base by an étale
covering; and the analytification of an étale surjection of `k`-schemes locally of finite type is
an étale covering (Conrad-RA, p. 31, after Def 4.2.1, and Thm 4.2.2, p. 31).

(b) `RigidSpace.descendOpen`: if `q` is an étale covering and `U' ⊆ S'` an admissible open whose
inverse images under the two projections `S' ×_S S' ⇉ S'` coincide, then `q(U')` is an admissible
open `U` of `S` with `q⁻¹(U) = U'` (`descendOpen_preimage`), and `U` is the only admissible open of
`S` with this inverse image (`descendOpen_unique`) (Conrad-RA Lemma 4.2.4, pp. 32–33).

(c) `RigidSpace.descendOpen_isAdmissibleCover`: if `{U'_j}` is an admissible covering of `S'` by
admissible opens satisfying the hypothesis of (b), the descended opens form an admissible covering
of `S` (Conrad-RA Cor 4.2.6, p. 34).

(d) `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.isQuasiCompact_iff`: a morphism `f : X → S` is quasi-compact if and
only if its base change `X ×_S S' → S'` is (Conrad-RA Thm 4.2.7, pp. 34–36, for this property).

Conrad states (b)–(d) for faithfully flat maps with local fpqc quasi-sections, of which étale
coverings are a special case (Conrad-RA Def 4.2.1); the étale class is enough here because the
level covers of *rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification* are étale. On quasi-separated
rigid spaces these statements are read on adic spaces through `r_K`
(*rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1). Part II's admissible-cover
comparison transports a given covering and its finite-locally-free coequaliser descends morphisms
into a fixed target; neither constructs the descended open of (b).
*Needs:* *rigid-analytic-space*, *rigid-analytification*, *rigid-adic-etale-comparison*,
*analytification-etale-smooth*, *analytification-surjective* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
quasi-compact morphisms of rigid spaces (RigidAnalyticGeometry §6.3, transported through
Part II's *rigid-analytic-space* and *proper-separated-comparisons*).

**Checks.**

- `descendOpen_identity` (degenerate) — for `q = id_S` every admissible open satisfies the
  hypothesis of (b) and descends to itself.
- `descendOpen_fold` (non-example) — the fold map `Sp k ⊔ Sp k → Sp k` is an étale covering; the
  first summand has different inverse images under the two projections and is not `q⁻¹(U)` for
  any admissible open `U`.
- `descendOpen_needsQuasiSections` (boundary) — the map `{|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → Sp k⟨t⟩` is étale
  and surjective, and each summand satisfies the hypothesis of (b), but the images do not form an
  admissible covering of the closed disc; by (c) this map admits no local étale quasi-sections, and
  that hypothesis cannot be removed from (c).
- `isQuasiCompact_iff_openDisc` (characterisation) — the inclusion of `{|t| < 1}` into `Sp k⟨t⟩` is
  not quasi-compact, and neither is its base change along the étale covering
  `Sp k⟨t⟩ ⊔ Sp k⟨t⟩ → Sp k⟨t⟩`.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above and the instances recorded at the lemmas. On
the algebra side: `O_K⟨T⟩` is admissible with generic fibre `K⟨T⟩`, `O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)` is topologically
finitely presented but not admissible, the `m_K`-adic completion of `O_K[T]` over `ℂ_p` is `k[T]`
(so the `m_K`-adic topology is the wrong one), and `Spf O_K[[T]]` with the `(ϖ, T)`-adic topology is
neither locally of tf presentation nor, for non-discrete `K`, of type (S). On generic fibres and
specialisation: `t(Spf ℤ_p) = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p)` has two points, `d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩)` is
the closed unit disc; for discretely valued `K`, the full analytic locus
`d(Spf O_K[[T]])` is quasi-compact and also has points with `|ϖ| = 0`, whereas its fibre
over `Spa(K, O_K)` is the non-quasi-compact open unit disc; `ϖ`-torsion is invisible (`d(Spf O_K/ϖ) = ∅`), the Gauss point specialises to the generic
point of `A¹_k`, the tube of the origin is the open unit disc while `λ⁻¹(0)` also contains `η_{1⁻}`,
the rig-points of `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` correspond to closed points of `Spec K⟨T⟩`
(including points with finite residue-field extension; its `K`-rational points are `T ↦ c` for
`c ∈ O_K`), and the admissible blow-up of `(T, ϖ)`
has special fibre `P¹_k ∪ A¹_k` and an isomorphic generic fibre, whereas blowing up the non-open
`(S, T)` changes the generic fibre. The annulus model `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`
runs through the whole flattening argument: its étale-local structure is `Z' = D¹_T` without
localisation, the quotient map `O_{D¹_T} → O_X` is a complete one-step dévissage in dimension `1`
with `𝒫 = 0` and non-injective `α`, its flat locus is `X_0 ∖ V(ζ)` so `O_X` is `T`-flat in dimension
`≥ 2` but not `≥ 1`, it is rig-flat at every rig-point, `F_0 = (ζξ − ϖ)` has ideal of coefficients

flat with the pull-back modulo `ϖ`-torsion equal to the strict transform. Contents are computed on

presentations (`F_0((O_X/ϖ)²) = (ϖ²) ≠ Ann = (ϖ)`), and the partition blow-up on `O_K⟨ζ⟩/(ζ(ζ − ϖ))`

flat non-proper quasi-projective model whose `φ` misses a point. For Conrad's functor and

## Layer R3: coherent sheaves and finite traces

This layer builds on AdicSpacesPartII R0–R1 and F0 of this roadmap. It constructs the sheaf `M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X` of a finite module on a
noetherian affinoid and proves its acyclicity in both of Huber's noetherian cases (Huber's Theorem
2.5); R3.1a identifies sections of analytified modules on strongly noetherian affinoid charts
with scalar extension, using Part II R1.3–R1.4's general module pullback;
it proves Čech acyclicity of the structure sheaf on every sheafy Tate affinoid (Kedlaya–Liu)
through the reduction of rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings — Tau Ceti has this
reduction for the structure presheaf in degree 0 only, and the results here are for an arbitrary
presheaf in all degrees; it introduces glueing squares and proves Kiehl's theorem; it builds the
abelian tensor category of coherent sheaves, the correspondence between coherent ideals and closed
adic subspaces and between coherent algebras and finite morphisms; it applies Kiehl's Theorems A
and B on quasi-Stein spaces to the open polydisc; it identifies vector bundles on sheafy Tate
affinoids with finite projective modules and treats uniform rings (Tau Ceti's `Huber.IsUniform` is
uniformity as boundedness of `A°`; here its Banach-ring form through the square bound is proved
equivalent); it constructs the coherent sheaf of continuous differentials; it develops strict
complete continuity, relative compactness, Kiehl-properness and étale base change of proper
coherent cohomology around Kiehl's proper mapping theorem, and the GAGA comparison maps; and it
constructs traces of finite projective modules, of finite locally free algebras, of finite locally
free morphisms of schemes and of adic spaces, and the pull–identify–trace operators along
correspondences that the Hecke-operator consumers use. The last subsection states the Gel'fand
spectrum of a Banach ring and Berkovich's spectral-seminorm formula, which the uniform-ring results
of this layer need.

The binary-cover variant (stronger hypothesis) `AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction_of_binary` assumes
`P U {V,W}` for every pair of rational subdomains with `V ∪ W = U`, together with the same
locality and transitivity hypotheses, and concludes `P` for every finite nonempty rational
cover. Its base case includes all simple Laurent coverings. The simple-Laurent criterion

functions in the original ring `A` alone are not its hypothesis.

`AdicSpace.RationalChart S U B Q` records a rational presentation of `U`, the
completion algebra `B`, and a morphism `S → Q` whose ring map is `A → B` and whose
map on spectra embeds `Spa(Q)` with image exactly `U`. Its algebra identification is
`Huber.IsRationalCompletion` (Lean): a ring equivalence from Tau Ceti's completion for
`locUniformSpace`, continuous in both directions, intertwining `toCompletionLoc`
with `algebraMap A B`. Thus the function in the Laurent hypothesis has type `B`.
The spectral identification is supplied by `spaCompletedLocalizationHomeomorph`
(Wedhorn, Proposition 8.2(2)); its construction is already in Tau Ceti.

**Checks for rational completion models.**

- (zero denominator) — `A⟨1/0⟩` is the zero ring.
- (identity) — `A⟨1/1⟩` is the original complete
  Hausdorff ring as a topological `A`-algebra.
- (diagonal) — for nonzero complete Hausdorff `A`,
  the diagonal algebra `A × A` cannot be a model of `A⟨1/1⟩`, even when abstract
  ring isomorphisms fail to distinguish the two rings.

**Checks for rational charts.**

- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_whole`: the whole spectrum has an identity chart,
  with the identity morphism of Huber pairs.
- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_empty`: a chart over the empty rational domain has
  no points in its source spectrum.
- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_zero_function`: in every rational chart the Laurent
  cover for the localized function `0` pulls back to `(U, ∅)`.

Prove that Čech acyclicity is inherited from a refinement whose restrictions are acyclic
(*cech-acyclicity-refinement*): let `X` be a topological space, `ℬ` a family of open subsets of `X`
closed under finite intersections, and `F` a presheaf of abelian groups on `ℬ` (restriction maps
along inclusions in `ℬ`, functorial). For `U ∈ ℬ` and a finite covering `𝔘 = (U_i)_{i∈I}` of `U` by
members of `ℬ`, call `𝔘` `F`-acyclic if the augmented alternating Čech complex
`0 → F(U) → ∏_{i₀} F(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} F(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯` (for a chosen total order of `I`) is
exact. Let `𝔙 = (V_i)_{i∈I}` and `𝔚 = (W_j)_{j∈J}` be finite coverings of `U ∈ ℬ` by members of
`ℬ` such that `𝔚` refines `𝔙` (every `W_j` is contained in some `V_i`), and suppose that for every
`p ≥ 0` and every `i₀ < ⋯ < i_p` in `I` the covering `𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} = (W_j ∩ V_{i₀…i_p})_{j∈J}`
of `V_{i₀…i_p}` is `F`-acyclic. Then `Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔙) ≅ Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔚)` for every `n ≥ 0`, compatibly
with the maps from `F(U)` in degree 0; in particular `𝔙` is `F`-acyclic if and only if `𝔚` is.
Consequently (the locality used by Kedlaya–Liu) if `𝔚` refines `𝔙` and the restriction of `𝔚` to
every member of `ℬ` contained in `U` is `F`-acyclic (`𝔚` is universally `F`-acyclic), then so is
every restriction of `𝔙` (KL15 §2.4, proof of Prop. 2.4.21, p. 46, where the locality is referred
to BGR 8.1.4/3 and is supplied here through the Čech double complex; Stacks Tag 0G6S,
Lem. 20.9.3, a covering having the whole set as a member has contractible augmented Čech
complex, which gives exactness of the rows; Stacks Tag 01FM, Lem. 20.23.6, alternating and full
Čech complexes have the same cohomology). If `𝔙 = (U)` is the trivial covering the lemma is a
tautology, and if `𝔚 = 𝔙` the hypothesis is that `𝔙` is universally acyclic on its own
intersections. Use the double complex whose `(p,q)` term is the product of
`F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q})` over increasing tuples. Its column augmentations
are exact by the hypothesis. For each W-intersection, refinement makes the restricted
V-cover contain that whole intersection as a member, giving exact row augmentations.
Identify both augmented edges with the supplier's kernel complexes and use its canonical
comparisons; naturality gives the refinement map and compatibility with `F(U)`.
*Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows`
and `DoubleComplex.spectralSequence_map`, with transposition and the sign transport
specified in the supplier contract.

Prove Kedlaya–Liu's Proposition 2.4.21 (*cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction*): for a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber
pair `(A, A⁺)`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, and a presheaf `F` of abelian groups on the rational subsets of
`X`, with `F(∅) = 0`, such that for every rational `U ⊆ X` and every `f ∈ 𝒪_X(U)`, with `V₁ = {|f| ≤ 1}` and
`V₂ = {|f| ≥ 1}` in `U`, the sequence `0 → F(U) → F(V₁) ⊕ F(V₂) → F(V₁ ∩ V₂) → 0` is exact, the
augmented alternating Čech complex of `F` is exact on every finite rational covering of every
rational subset, including its empty cover. The assumption `F(∅) = 0` is necessary for
that last case: the constant presheaf `ℤ` has exact two-member Laurent complexes but its
empty-cover augmentation is `ℤ → 0` (KL15 §2.4, Prop. 2.4.21 and its proof, pp. 45–46). For `F = 𝒪_X` of a complete
strongly noetherian Tate pair the hypothesis is AdicSpaces layer 4.1's two-piece Laurent exactness
(Wedhorn Lem. 8.33) and the conclusion is its all-degree Čech exactness; for `F = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X` with
`M` finite projective over a sheafy Tate `A` the hypothesis follows from the case `F = 𝒪_X` by
taking direct summands (stated as *finite-projective-module-acyclicity* below). *Needs:*
*rational-covering-reduction*; *cech-acyclicity-refinement*;
DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and
`DoubleComplex.spectralSequence_map`; Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`.

`AdicSpace.isCechAcyclic_of_simpleLaurent` takes precisely the injectivity, middle
exactness and surjectivity of this three-term sequence in each `RationalChart`,
plus `Subsingleton (F.obj (op ⊥))`. It concludes `IsCechAcyclic` for every finite
rational cover, with no nonemptiness restriction on the indexing type. A presheaf
on the rational basis is used through its right Kan extension to all opens.

Apply *rational-covering-reduction* first to injectivity of
`F(U) → Ȟ⁰(U, F; (V_i))`. Locality and transitivity follow from restriction maps;
the Laurent hypothesis supplies the base case. Next apply it to bijectivity of
this map. For locality, a matching family descends along the refinement by its
sheaf condition, and separatedness on the original members identifies its
restrictions with the original family. Transitivity is gluing in two stages.
Together with `F(∅) = 0`, these steps give the sheaf condition on the rational basis.
For positive degrees use exactly
`P(U, (V_i)) := ∀ rational U' ⊆ U, the augmented Čech complex for (V_i ∩ U') is exact`.
Locality follows from *cech-acyclicity-refinement* on each `U'`, and transitivity
from the Čech double-complex comparison for composite coverings, using the
universal acyclicity hypotheses on rational intersections. These comparisons use
DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 with the same total differential and natural edge maps.
A rational pullback of a simple Laurent covering is the simple Laurent covering
for the restricted function, so the localized three-term hypothesis supplies this
base case. The empty cover is handled separately by `F(∅) = 0`.

**Checks for `IsCechAcyclic`.**

- `IsCechAcyclic.test_singleton`: the one-member cover `V₀ = U` is acyclic for every
  presheaf; its augmentation is the identity and its higher cohomology is zero.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_empty`: the empty family is acyclic exactly when `F(U) = 0`.
  In particular, the constant presheaf `ℤ` fails this test, even at `U = ∅`.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_empty_cover_obstruction`: the constant presheaf `ℤ` on a point
  has an exact two-member Čech complex over the empty open, but its empty-cover
  augmentation is not injective. Binary-cover exactness alone cannot force `F(∅) = 0`.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_zero`: the zero presheaf is acyclic for every family and every `U`.
- For `f = 1`, the Laurent covering is `(U, U)` and every rational pullback is
  `(U', U')`. Its augmented complex is the split exact sequence
  `0 → F(U') → F(U') ⊕ F(U') → F(U') → 0`, with diagonal and difference maps.
  Every finite rational cover refines `(U, U)`; exactness for those other covers
  is a conclusion of the reduction, while this base case only concerns the
  duplicated cover; the diagonal–difference sequence is split exact for any abelian group.
- For `f = 0`, the covering and its pullbacks are `(U, ∅)` and `(U', ∅)`.
  With `F(∅) = 0` the augmentation is the identity of `F(U')`.
- For a localized function `f ∈ 𝒪_X(U)` and rational `U' ⊆ U`, the pullback
  pieces are `{|f|_{U'} ≤ 1}` and `{|f|_{U'} ≥ 1}`; the base case uses the
  Laurent sequence on `U'` itself, including when `U'` is empty.

### R3.1a affinoid sections of analytified modules

**The affine section comparison for analytified modules.** Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete
Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate Huber pair, let `Spec C → Spec A` be locally of finite
type, put `X = Spec C`, and let `M` be any `C`-module. Use Part II R1.3–R1.4's relative
analytification `X^ad = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A,A⁺)`, its scheme projection `q_X`, and its module
pullback `(M̃)^ad = q_X^*M̃`, where `M̃` is the algebraic associated sheaf. For a strongly
noetherian affinoid open chart `c : Spa(B,B⁺) → X^ad`, require that the coefficient map
`φ : C → B` induce `q_X ∘ c`. In `AdicSpace`, prove `analytification.modules_chartSections`:
the canonical comparison
`B ⊗_C M → Γ(Spa(B,B⁺), c^*((M̃)^ad))` is a `B`-linear isomorphism, with the `B`-action
given by the chart's actual coefficient map `c.affinoid.coeff`. It sends `b ⊗ m` to `b`
times the pullback of the section corresponding to `m`. Commutativity identifies the source
with `M ⊗_C B`.

For finite `M`, pull back a finite presentation and use R3.1's `tilde_exact`,
`tilde_obj_top` and `tilde_obj_rational` to identify the restricted sheaf with the sheaf
associated to `B ⊗_C M` and its sections with that module (Zavyalov24 §4, Lemma 4.3(2) and
Theorem 4.2(1)–(2), applied to the mixed projection of §6). For arbitrary `M`, use its
filtered colimit of finite submodules and the quasi-compact rational basis of the affinoid:
sections on the whole chart commute with these colimits (Stacks, Tag 009F, Lemma 6.29.1).

### R3.2 glueing squares and Kiehl's theorem

**Glueing squares of complete Tate rings.** (*glueing-square*) A glueing square is a commutative
square of complete Hausdorff Tate rings with continuous homomorphisms `R → R₁`, `R → R₂`,
`R₁ → R₁₂`, `R₂ → R₁₂` such that (a) the sequence `0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ → 0`,
`(r₁, r₂) ↦ r₁ − r₂`, is exact and strict (`R` carries the subspace topology of `R₁ × R₂` and
`R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂` is open onto `R₁₂`); (b) `R₂ → R₁₂` has dense image; (c) every maximal ideal of
`R` is the contraction of a prime ideal of `R₁ × R₂`. A finite (resp. finite projective) glueing
datum on it is a triple of finite (resp. finite projective) modules `M₁, M₂, M₁₂` over
`R₁, R₂, R₁₂` with isomorphisms `ψ_i : M_i ⊗_{R_i} R₁₂ ≅ M₁₂`; its module of sections is
`M = ker(ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂)`. Condition (c) replaces the surjectivity of Gel'fand
spectra `M(R₁ ⊕ R₂) → M(R)` in KL15 Def. 2.7.3(c), p. 57, by its consequence from
Cor. 2.3.5, p. 34, used in the proof of Prop. 2.7.5, p. 57; every topological ring here is
metrised by the norm `|x| = inf{cⁿ : ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ R₀}` of a pseudouniformiser `ϖ` and ring of definition
`R₀` (KL15 Rem. 2.4.4). In `Huber`, define `GlueingSquare R R₁ R₂ R₁₂` as a proposition on the four complete Hausdorff Tate
rings and their algebra maps, with commutativity expressed by the scalar-tower instances
and continuity and (a)–(c) as fields, with projections
`GlueingSquare.exact_sub` (exactness of `0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ → 0`),
`GlueingSquare.isStrictMap_sub` (strictness of `R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂`, open onto `R₁₂`),
`GlueingSquare.denseRange` (`R₂ → R₁₂` has dense range) and `GlueingSquare.exists_prime_comap_eq`
(every maximal ideal of `R` is the contraction of a prime of `R₁ × R₂`); define `GlueingDatum` as a glueing
datum with module parameters `M₁, M₂, M₁₂` and fields `ψ₁, ψ₂`; finiteness and
projectivity are the existing `Module.Finite` and `Module.Projective` of each module. Define `GlueingDatum.sections` as the `R`-module `M = ker(ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂)`
with its maps `M → M_i`, and `GlueingDatum.ofModule` as the glueing datum
`(N ⊗ R₁, N ⊗ R₂, N ⊗ R₁₂)` of an `R`-module `N` with its canonical isomorphisms, for which the

**Checks.**

- (identity) — construct the identity glueing square and apply
  its `exact_sub` and `surjective_sub` fields to its difference map. The same map sends
  `(1,2)` to `−1` (KL15, Definition 2.7.3, pp. 56–57).
- (diagonal, not dense) — for a nonzero Hausdorff Tate ring, the
  diagonal in `R × R` misses `(1,0)` and is closed; the difference map also misses `(1,0)`.
- (computation, Laurent) — for `A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩` and `f = T/p` (the simple
  Laurent covering `{|T| ≤ |p|}`, `{|T| ≥ |p|}`): `R = ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, `R₁ = ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩`,
  `R₂ = ℚ_p⟨T, p/T⟩`, `R₁₂ = ℚ_p⟨T/p, p/T⟩` is a glueing square: every `Σ_{n∈ℤ} a_n (T/p)ⁿ` in
  `R₁₂` splits as `(Σ_{n≥0} a_n (T/p)ⁿ) − (−Σ_{n<0} a_n (p/T)^{−n})`, the kernel of the difference
  map is `ℚ_p⟨T⟩` (Tate acyclicity), and the truncations `Σ_{n≤N} a_n (T/p)ⁿ ∈ R₂` show that
  `R₂ → R₁₂` has dense image.
- (degenerate) — `R₁ = R`, `R₂ = R₁₂ = 0` is a glueing square
  (`R₂ → R₁₂` trivially dense); every glueing datum is `(M, 0, 0)` with `M = M₁`.
- (non-example, exactness) — `R = ℚ_p → R₁ = R₂ = R₁₂ = ℚ_p⟨T⟩` with
  identity maps `R_i → R₁₂` satisfies (b) (identity) and (c) (`R` is a field), but
  `ker(R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂)` is the diagonal `≅ ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ≠ ℚ_p`, so (a) fails; a definition omitting
  exactness of `0 → R → R₁ × R₂` would accept it, and then the section module of the datum
  `(R₁, R₂, R₁₂)` would be `ℚ_p⟨T⟩` rather than `R`.
- (compatibility with KL15) — for complete Tate rings, conditions
  (a)–(b) are exactly KL15 Def. 2.7.3(a)–(b) for the norms of KL15 Rem. 2.4.4, and Kedlaya–Liu's
  (c) implies condition (c) by KL15 Cor. 2.3.5, p. 34.
- (non-example, density) — for a nonzero Hausdorff ring `R`,
  the diagonal square `R → R, R → R × R` does not satisfy the density condition:
  the diagonal image is closed and misses `(1, 0)`. Its difference map
  `(a, b) ↦ (a − b, a − b)` also misses `(1, 0)`, so this example fails exactness as well.


**Checks for `GlueingDatum`, `GlueingDatum.sections` and `GlueingDatum.ofModule`.**

- (zero) — base-changing the zero module gives a zero section module.
- (sections of the trivial square) — for the identity square over a commutative
  ring `R`, `(1 ⊗ x, 1 ⊗ y)` is a section of the datum of `R` exactly when `x = y`.
- (rank two) — for the identity square over a nonzero commutative ring, the pair of vectors
  `((1,2),(1,2))` glues and `((1,2),(2,1))` does not. Thus the condition is equality of the
  two restrictions, with difference `ψ₁ − ψ₂`, not their sum or a coordinate permutation.

Prove the factorisation of matrices near the identity along a strict surjection
(*matrix-factorisation-strict-surjection*): let `R₁ → S` and `R₂ → S` be bounded homomorphisms of
nonarchimedean Banach rings such that `ψ : R₁ ⊕ R₂ → S`, `(x, y) ↦ x + y`, is a strict surjection of groups; then
there is `c > 0` such that for every `n ≥ 0` every `U ∈ GLₙ(S)` with `|U − 1| < c` factors as
`U = ψ(U₁)ψ(U₂)` with `U_i ∈ GLₙ(R_i)`, and if `d ≥ 1` and every `x ∈ S` lifts to `(y₁, y₂)` with
`|y_i| ≤ d|x|` one can take `c = d⁻²` when the norms are nonarchimedean and the maps
`R_i → S` are submetric (the explicit-constant form), as for the Tate-ring norms of AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (then `d ≥ 1` for `S ≠ 0`, since
`|x| ≤ max|y_i| ≤ d|x|`; one step of the iteration replaces `U = 1 + X` by
`(1 − φ₁(Y₁))U(1 − φ₂(Y₂)) = 1 + X'` with `|X'| ≤ d²|X|²`, a contraction when `|X| < d⁻²`) (KL15
§2.7, Lem. 2.7.2, p. 56; KL15 §2.7, proof of
Lem. 2.7.2, p. 56, the explicit constant; Kiehl-AB §1, proof of Hilfssatz 1.5, p. 261, the same
Cartan-type factorisation for Laurent coverings). For `R₁ = ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, `R₂ = ℚ_p⟨T⁻¹⟩`,
`S = ℚ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩` (`d = 1`) every `U ∈ GLₙ(S)` with `|U − 1| < 1` factors as a product of a matrix
over `ℚ_p⟨T⟩` and one over `ℚ_p⟨T⁻¹⟩` (Cartan's lemma for the annulus). The proof uses
Mathlib's Neumann series `Units.oneSub`; the factorisation across two rings is additional.
*Needs:* *glueing-square*; Mathlib `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`, `Units.isOpen`, `Units.oneSub`.

**Checks.**

- (negative control, archimedean norm) — for the real two-by-two
  matrix `M` whose entries are all `1`, each entry has norm `1` but `(M²)₀₀ = 2`.
  The maximum-entry norm is not submultiplicative without the nonarchimedean hypothesis.
- (degenerate, zero source) — a unital ring map
  from the zero ring to `S` forces `S = 0`; taking `R₂ = 0` does not give a nonzero

`M`; then (a) `M ⊗_R R_i → M_i` is surjective for `i = 1, 2`; (b) `ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂` is
surjective; (c) there is a finitely generated `R`-submodule `M₀ ⊆ M` with `M₀ ⊗_R R_i → M_i`
surjective for `i = 1, 2` (KL15 §2.7, Lem. 2.7.4(a), p. 57, part (a); KL15 §1.3, Lem. 1.3.8(c),

Prove that finite glueing data on a simple Laurent covering of a strongly noetherian Tate

which discusses the extension over `ℤ((z))` and its affinoid algebras). The general

`Huber.GlueingDatum.finite_sections_of_simpleLaurent` (Lean) states finiteness of the

any other finite module with compatible identifications on the two pieces has a

**Coherent sheaves on locally noetherian adic spaces.** (*coherent-sheaf*) Let `X` be a locally
noetherian adic space (*locally-noetherian-adic-space*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) with structure sheaf `𝒪_X`
(AdicSpaces layer 5; `𝒪_X` is a sheaf). A sheaf `F` of `𝒪_X`-modules on the topological space `X`
is coherent if there is an open covering of `X` by affinoid open subspaces `U_i ≅ Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)`
with `A_i` complete of noetherian type (noetherian ring of definition, or strongly noetherian
Tate) and finitely generated `A_i`-modules `M_i` with `F|_{U_i} ≅ M̃_i` (*associated-module-sheaf*).
`Coh(X)` is the full subcategory of `𝒪_X`-modules on coherent objects. On strongly noetherian Tate
affinoid opens `U` the condition then holds with `M = F(U)` (*tate-kiehl-affinoid*); on affinoid
opens with a noetherian ring of definition the definition is used only through such coverings.
In `AdicSpace`, define `IsCoherent` as the predicate (an open covering by noetherian affinoids on
which `F` is associated with finite modules) and `Coh` as the full subcategory of `𝒪_X`-modules
on coherent objects; prove `IsCoherent.of_iso` (coherence is invariant under isomorphism of
`𝒪_X`-modules), `isCoherent_tilde` (on a noetherian affinoid `Spa(A, A⁺)`, `M̃` is coherent for
every finite `A`-module `M`), `IsCoherent.restrict` (restriction along an open immersion preserves coherence)
and `IsCoherent.local` (coherence can be tested on a jointly surjective family
of open immersions), `isCoherent_structureSheaf` (`𝒪_X` is coherent when `X` has noetherian-type
affinoid charts), `IsCoherent.isFiniteType` (a coherent sheaf is of finite type, Mathlib
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`), `IsCoherent.test_finitePresentation` (on `X` covered by strongly
noetherian Tate affinoids, `IsCoherent F ↔ SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation F`),
`IsCoherent.obj_affinoid` (for a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid open `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X`,
`F(U)` is a finite `A`-module and `F|_U ≅ (F(U))~`, from *tate-kiehl-affinoid*) and
`IsCoherent.stalk_finite` (every stalk `F_x` is a finitely generated `𝒪_{X,x}`-module) (Kiehl-E
§0, Def. 0.5, p. 195, where coherent means locally, on an admissible affinoid covering,

*associated-module-sheaf*; *tate-acyclicity-finite-modules*;
*noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules*; Mathlib `SheafOfModules`,
`SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`, `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`.

**Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the `M̃`.**
(*tate-kiehl-affinoid*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a Huber pair with `A` a complete Hausdorff strongly
noetherian Tate ring and `A⁺` a ring of integral elements, and `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`. Prove that (i) a
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F` is coherent (*coherent-sheaf*) iff `F ≅ M̃` for a finite `A`-module `M`,
and then `M ≅ F(X)`; (ii) `M ↦ M̃` is an exact equivalence of categories from finite `A`-modules to
`Coh(X)`, with quasi-inverse `F ↦ F(X)`, compatible with `⊗` and internal Hom (a tensor
equivalence); (iii) equivalently, for every finite rational covering `{U_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺)}` of
`X`, `A → ∏ B_i` is an effective descent morphism for finite modules: every system of finite
`B_i`-modules with compatible isomorphisms on the `U_i ∩ U_j` (cocycle condition) comes from a
finite `A`-module. `AdicSpace.coherentEquivalence` states the equivalence with these two
functors. `AdicSpace.coherentEquivalence_tensor` supplies the tensor and unit
comparisons and a monoidal equivalence naturally identified with association on
objects and maps; both inclusions into the ambient module categories are monoidal.
`AdicSpace.Coh.internalHom_tilde` supplies internal Hom, with finite
presentation of the first module (automatic for finite modules over this noetherian
ring). `AdicSpace.coherentEquivalence_descent` states effective descent of coherent
sheaves along a surjective local open isomorphism. Apply it to the disjoint union
of a finite rational cover and compose with `coherentEquivalence` on its affinoid
pieces: its coalgebras encode the overlap isomorphisms, their cocycle equation,
and compatible morphisms. Thus it includes effectivity for finite modules in (iii).
For strongly noetherian Tate affinoids, use DLLZ-A Appendix A, Lemma A.3,
pp. 95–96, and Theorem A.8 with its proof, p. 97: the proof reduces to simple Laurent
coverings and applies finite-module gluing. In particular, for `A` an affinoid algebra over a
complete nonarchimedean field `K`, this is Kiehl's theorem in Kedlaya–Liu's adic form
(KL15 §2.5, Thm 2.5.20(b), p. 52; Kiehl-AB §1, Thm 1.2, p. 259, Kiehl's glueing
theorem: an `𝒪_X`-module is associated with a finite module iff it is `𝔘`-coherent; Kiehl-AB §2,
Satz 2.2, p. 270, coherent equals associated on an affinoid, the rigid form of (i)). For
`A = K⟨T⟩`, `U₁ = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `U₂ = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}` and the datum `𝒪_{U₁}`, `𝒪_{U₂}` glued by
`s₁ = (T/ϖ)·s₂` on `U₁ ∩ U₂`, the glued coherent sheaf is `Ã` (`T/ϖ` is already a unit on `U₂`, so
the datum is trivial), with global generator `(1, ϖ/T)`; the section `(T/ϖ, 1)` lies in it but
generates only `T·Ã`. Coherent sheaves on the non-reduced affinoid `Spa(K⟨T⟩/(T²))` correspond to
finite `K[T]/(T²)`-modules, including the non-free module `K`. *Needs:* *coherent-sheaf*;
*associated-module-sheaf*; *tate-acyclicity-finite-modules*; *strongly-noetherian-laurent-gluing*;
*rational-covering-reduction*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`.
