# Roadmap: finiteness and simplicity of the groups on the CFSG list

The [CFSGStatement roadmap](../CFSGStatement/README.md) constructs a group
`CFSGIndex.Group` for every entry on its list and states that every finite simple group is
isomorphic to one of them. This roadmap proves the complementary, concrete assertion: **every
group on that list is finite and simple**. The endpoint is the pair of theorems

```lean
theorem CFSGIndex.finite (i : CFSGIndex) : Finite i.Group
theorem CFSGIndex.isSimpleGroup (i : CFSGIndex) : IsSimpleGroup i.Group
```

Here `i.Group` is *exactly* the carrier defined by CFSGStatement: `Multiplicative (ZMod p)`,
Mathlib's alternating group, the derived central quotient of the Steinberg fixed points, or the
group of the recorded sporadic presentation. An isomorphic group constructed for a proof must be
connected back to that carrier by a proved `MulEquiv`. Neither the validity proof in a Lie index
nor the word “sporadic” supplies a finiteness or simplicity hypothesis.

The endpoint says every **listed** group has the two properties. It does not prove
`ClassificationStatement`, which says every finite simple group **occurs** on the list. It also
does not assert pairwise nonisomorphism or a unique index for each group.

The sporadic lane also develops the Monster's complete conjugacy structure in P2M:
actual representative words, centralizers, power and fusion data, and the count 194 for both
classes and irreducible complex characters. It reuses native conjugacy and character theory;
no proof of the classification proposition or prior verification of the full Monster character
table is a prerequisite. The companion prototype displays selected P0/P2M interfaces only;
the full programme below remains definitive.

The intended Tau Ceti home is `TauCeti/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/CFSG/BasicProperties/` for
family results, with reusable presentation, group-action, finite-field, and Tits-system theorems
in their existing mathematical homes. The final assembly imports the family theorems; it does not
recompute their proofs by unfolding the four-way index.

## Starting points and ownership

- CFSGStatement owns `CFSGIndex`, its validity ranges, its seventeen Lie-type constructors,
  `ValidLieTypeIndex.Group`, `SporadicName.presentation`, and `SporadicName.Group`. Every
  Lie-type branch is the derived central quotient of the fixed points of its actual Steinberg
  endomorphism `d.steinberg` on `d.AmbientGroup`. CFSGStatement L0 designates each family's
  carrier: classical matrix groups and explicit spin, weight-module or short-root carriers
  are admissible alongside the pinned construction. These carriers are not definitionally
  the pinned Chevalley--Demazure points. L5 owns their root-subgroup-preserving comparison
  with those points, intertwining the actual Steinberg maps. Consume that comparison when
  transporting a theorem proved on the pinned carrier; a direct proof on the designated
  explicit carrier does not wait for L5. CFSGStatement separately owns L4, identifying the
  Suzuki branch with Mathlib's `suzukiGroup`; it can transport results but is not a prerequisite
  for the basic-property theorems.
- The [Chevalley groups roadmap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/1d6918b25647df1f606ccae78241fc75527d50ee/TauCetiRoadmap/ChevalleyGroups/README.md) owns the theory of the ambient
  group: root subgroups for every root, the commutator formula, the Bruhat decomposition and Tits
  system of the group over a field, its centre, Steinberg's presentation, generation of the points
  over an algebraically closed field by root subgroups, and the Frobenius, graph, and exceptional
  endomorphisms with their action on root subgroups (C2 to C5 there). Apply these results to
  their actual carrier: on a different designated explicit carrier, either transport the
  needed root calculus through a proved compatible equivalence or establish it directly as
  part of F1/T1/T3 below. L0's numbered simple-root data alone do not supply this full theory. The
  [ReductiveGroups roadmap](../ReductiveGroups/README.md) owns abstract Borel, root-datum, and
  Bruhat theory. The present roadmap owns everything about **finite fixed points**: the
  finite-field descent of a Steinberg map, the twisted root groups, the BN-pair of the fixed-point
  group, and the resulting simplicity theorem. Existing `TauCeti.TitsSystem` and its Bruhat-cell
  API are the starting interface; extend them for the general group-theoretic theorems below. The
  [Mathlib BN-pair work](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40363) informs
  names and structure, while Tau Ceti supplies what the endpoint needs regardless of its timing.
- [Rank24LatticeConstructions, Layer 6][rank24] owns the canonical Construction-B-and-odd-shift
  Leech lattice, its rational form and coordinate/congruence API. Consume that lattice; this
  roadmap owns its sporadic automorphism groups and their representation comparisons, not a
  second Leech construction. [AlgebraicCodingTheory](../../Completed/AlgebraicCodingTheory/README.md)
  supplies the chosen Golay code and code theory, and excludes the Mathieu identification.
- [SporadicOrders, O0–O2][sporadic-orders] owns the ten canonical ATLAS permutation models
  listed in P1, their orders and presentation surjections, using the Hex permutation-group
  kernel checker. This roadmap owns their presentation upper bounds, recognition and
  simplicity, and the four additional P1 models. Consume that checker for finite permutation
  order/membership certificates; its certificates do not bound abstract presented groups.
- [CertifiedPermutationComputation, §§2.1–2.2][certified-perm] owns the shared signed-word,
  orbit-witness and primitivity interfaces. Reuse or prove adapters between those formats,
  Mathlib actions and Hex certificates. Its Jordan recognition or randomized-search results
  are not sporadic simplicity theorems and are not prerequisites for this programme.
- Mathlib supplies the prime-order cyclic group theory, the simplicity of alternating groups of
  degree at least five, and `MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup`. Reuse those results and
  prove the small transport lemmas needed by the exact CFSGStatement carriers.
- The existing finite-field and matrix-coordinate lemmas in the CFSG files, including the
  `fixedField` and Suzuki descent results, are inputs. Their existence alone does not make an
  algebraic-closure-valued point group finite.

Every proof of `IsSimpleGroup` must also establish the candidate is nontrivial. A proof that a
quotient is simple because an assumed target is simple, or that a presentation is finite because
the source calls it a finite group, does not discharge an item.

## E0: cyclic and alternating branches

For `.cyclic p hp`, prove finiteness of `Multiplicative (ZMod p)` and simplicity from `hp` using
Mathlib's prime-cardinality criterion. For `.alternating n hn`, prove finiteness of
`alternatingGroup (Fin n)` and use Mathlib's general `n ≥ 5` simplicity theorem. State the
results for those exact types, not for a separately named cyclic or alternating group.

## F0–F1: finiteness of the Lie-type candidates

Prove a general **finite-coordinate fixed-point criterion**. Let a group embed faithfully in a
finite matrix type over a field of characteristic `p`, and let `F` be an endomorphism. If some
positive iterate `F^r` acts on every matrix coordinate by `x ↦ x^(p^e)` with `e > 0`, then
`fixedSubgroup F` is finite: its entries lie among the roots of `X^(p^e) - X`. Package the
result for a faithful finite-dimensional representation, for subgroups of `GL`, and for transport
across an intertwining `MulEquiv`. Give the induced `Finite` instances for a subgroup's derived
subgroup and its quotient by its centre. The latter transport is general group theory, not a
Lie-specific calculation.

Apply this criterion to the actual pair `(d.AmbientGroup, d.steinberg)`. If using a
different matrix realization or pinned carrier, construct a `MulEquiv e` and prove
`e (d.steinberg g) = F' (e g)` for the independently specified target endomorphism `F'`.
Use native `TauCeti.fixedSubgroupCongr` and `TauCeti.FixedPointCandidate.congr` to transport
fixed points and the derived quotient by its own centre; an ambient group equivalence alone
does not identify fixed points. On the direct explicit-carrier route, prove a faithful
coordinate embedding and the iterate formula for that carrier itself. Neither route assumes
finiteness or simplicity of the candidate. L5 is required only when its pinned comparison
is actually used, not for a direct proof on the designated carrier.

For each of the nine ordinary families (`A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, `E6`, `E7`, `E8`, `F4`, `G2`), prove
the required coordinate formula for the CFSGStatement Steinberg map. For the four graph-twisted
families (`twistedA`, `twistedD`, `twistedE6`, `trialityD4`), prove that the finite-order graph
part commutes with Frobenius and that a positive iterate has the coordinate formula. For
`suzuki`, `reeG2`, `reeF4`, and `tits`, use the proved square of the half-Frobenius Steinberg
map, then verify the coordinate formula for the corresponding field Frobenius. Proving the
formula merely on the named simple root subgroups is insufficient: it must hold on the whole
faithfully represented carrier or follow from a proved generation theorem, such as generation by
root subgroups over an algebraically closed field (C4 of the Chevalley groups roadmap).

Apply F0 to each branch to obtain `Finite d.FixedPoints` and `Finite d.Group`, and assemble
`ValidLieTypeIndex.finite` by cases. This includes the Tits group and every small parameter
retained by `LieTypeIndex.Valid`. Record the field size and the positive iterate in branch lemmas
for use by the simplicity proofs without unfolding the entire dispatcher.

## T0: a reusable simplicity criterion

Consume native `TauCeti.TitsSystem.bruhatCell_injective`, `disjoint_bruhatCell_iff`, and
`existsUnique_mem_bruhatCell` from `TitsSystem/Bruhat/Uniqueness`; distinct generic Bruhat
cells are already supplied. Consume native `TauCeti.TitsSystem.standardParabolicOrderIso`
from [Parabolic/Classification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/a9d0ba7b634affde557687933f3cb3c9b266c29d/TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/Parabolic/Classification.lean)
for standard-parabolic classification. Extend the remaining Coxeter/split-structure
API needed here: specify `U ≤ B`, its normality and solvability, the complement `B ∩ N`, and
the product and intersection equations of a split BN-pair.
Prove the Tits normal-subgroup criterion in the following form. Put
`Z = ⋂_{h : H} hBh⁻¹` and let `H⁺` be the normal closure in `H` of `U`.
If the Coxeter graph is connected and nonempty, `Z ∩ U = 1`, and `H⁺` is
perfect, then `Z ∩ H⁺` is its centre and `H⁺ / (Z ∩ H⁺)` is simple whenever nontrivial.
Prove the normal-subgroup theorem behind this criterion, not merely its final typeclass
instance. Supply transport across an isomorphism and a bridge from this quotient to
`DerivedCentralQuotient H` whenever `H⁺ = [H,H]`. The application milestones must prove
the hypotheses and this equality (or a direct quotient equivalence) for their fixed-point
groups; a bare BN-pair on a larger group does not establish the desired type's simplicity.
This is the split-BN-pair criterion in
[Conrad's Tits-system notes](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/249BW16Page/handouts/titssystem.pdf),
Theorem 2.4.

Also provide the group-action route where it is shorter. Connect a faithful quasiprimitive
action and conjugate commuting root subgroups to Mathlib's
`MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup`, with lemmas for passing to derived subgroups and
central quotients. This is particularly useful for rank-one and small-field calculations.
Neither criterion should require a separate order formula for the whole group.

## T1–T2: ordinary and graph-twisted groups

for every root, Weyl representatives, the torus, the commutator formula, the Bruhat
decomposition with distinct cells, a Tits system, and generation by root subgroups, together

Build on that calculus the theory of the **Steinberg fixed points**: the finite-field root groups, the fact that the Steinberg map permutes the ambient root
subgroups and preserves the Bruhat decomposition, fixed-point Bruhat descent including the

For an ordinary group, take the finite-field root groups fixed by Frobenius. For a graph-twisted

The validity predicate handles the index range, not these proofs. The local calculations must

   Reidemeister–Schreier transformations beyond the native index-two interface, including

   systems. The soundness theorem must yield a finite index or a finite spanning set of words

   any nontrivial normal subgroup. Group-specific certificates must verify both coverage and

normalization factor; a different displayed norm requires its proved scaling dictionary. Classify **all** minimal vectors from this actual congruence model. In its raw integer
coordinates `x_i=a_i/2`, of norm `∑a_i²/8`, construct the three exhaustive families:
two coordinates `±4`; octad-supported eight coordinates `±2` with the sum congruence;
and one coordinate `±3` with the others `±1`, parametrized by a Golay word and a
distinguished coordinate. Prove their disjoint counts `1104`, `97152`, `98304`, hence
196560 minimal vectors. The code's weight/rank theorems supply the octad and codeword
counts; the vector classification and sign/congruence checks belong here, not to the
minimum-norm theorem alone. Prove the antipodal involution has no fixed point and its
pair set has cardinality 98280 before using that permutation degree or any orbit count.
Prove the minimal vectors span the rational ambient space, so that their faithful
permutation action proves the lattice isometry group `Co0 := Aut(Λ)` finite. Construct
`Co1 := Co0 / {±1}` and deduce its finiteness by quotient finiteness. The action on
minimal **vectors** is the Co0 action; `−1` negates those vectors, so it does not descend to
Co1. Construct the Co1 action on antipodal pairs and prove its kernel statement separately.
Give the Conway generators of Co0, prove they generate the full lattice-isometry group by
the lattice/minimal-vector reduction, and compute its order using that actual action.

For Co1 recognition, select the Praeger–Soicher/GPL `Co1.1` eight-involution presentation
used by native `co1Presentation`, retaining its nine additional relations and alphabetical
renaming. Construct its generator dictionary with the antipodal-pair action of degree 98280.
Build a word-defined subgroup of the abstract presentation mapping onto the specified Co2
point stabilizer, derive a surjection from the **exact** recognized Co2 presentation onto
that subgroup, and certify a complete right-coset/normal-form cover of index at most 98280.
This bounds its order by `|Co2|`; the independent lattice orbit/stabilizer calculation gives
the matching lower bound for Co1. Neither the finite-image stabilizer nor its order alone
proves those abstract subgroup relations or the coset cover. Construct the subgroup words,
relation deductions and all coset transitions as P0-checked certificates. Prove Co1
simplicity by P0's prime-order normal-generation criterion, using local Sylow normal forms
for primes `2,3,5,7,11,13,23`, complete prime-element coverage/fusion words, and witnesses
normally generating every canonical model generator. Then transport to the exact presentation. Define the induced action on `V := Λ/2Λ`; prove the required kernel,
faithfulness, and irreducibility statements for this action over `F₂`. For a specified short
vector class `λ ∈ V` of type 2 in the Höhn–Seysen conventions, identify
`Stab_Co1(λ)` with the P1 `Co2` model by an explicit
`MulEquiv`. Construct the equivariant bijection from antipodal pairs of minimal vectors
to type-2 classes in `Λ/2Λ`, sending `{v,−v}` to `v + 2Λ`. Prove independence of sign,
injectivity using the minimum-norm bound, and surjectivity from the definition of type 2.
Match the Co0 quotient action with the mod-two Co1 action under this bijection, and identify
its actual stabilizers. An unrelated permutation group of the same order does not provide
that interface.

**P2-G: construct the local representations used by the Monster.** Follow
[Höhn–Seysen, v1, §2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.01037v1#S2.SS1) and its Conway
construction to realize `G := Gx0` of shape `2^{1+24}_+.Co1` and `N := N0` of shape
`2^{2+11+22}.(M24 × S3)` on the same rational Griess algebra. Specify their embeddings,
their intersection `Nx0` of shape `2^{1+24+11}.M24`, and triality `τ`, with
`N = ⟨Nx0, τ⟩`. Prove the extraspecial structure of `Q := Qx0`, identify its central
involution `z`, and give an equivariant identification `Q/⟨z⟩ ≃ Λ/2Λ` for the actual
`Co1` action from P2-L. Connect the code action to the Parker-loop and `M24` actions used
in these representations, rather than importing a second, unidentified Mathieu model.

Assign the representation and character calculations consumed by §2.1 to this milestone.
In particular, prove the fixed-space statement in Lemma 2.1, including the restriction of
the 300-dimensional symmetric-square representation to the identified `Co2`, with
constituent dimensions `1, 1, 23, 275`. Höhn–Seysen assumes Conway/Leech theory and
character information for `Co1`, `Co2`, and `M24`; those are prerequisites to formalize for
these representations, not consequences of P1's order and simplicity theorems.

**P2-M: count the constructed Monster through its actual stabilizers.** Define
`M_alg := ⟨G, τ⟩`. Prove the axis–involution correspondence of §2.1 and
`C_M_alg(z) = G` (Theorem 2.9). Choose the paper's short involution `β⁺`, put
`β⁻ := β⁺ z`, and let `v⁺, v⁻` be their axes. The counting interface is

```text
X⁺ = orbit M_alg v⁺
K  = Stab_M_alg(v⁺) = C_M_alg(β⁺)
X⁻ = orbit K v⁻
S  = Stab_M_alg(v⁺, v⁻).
```

Prove `S = C_G(β⁺)` using `β⁺β⁻ = z` and `C_M_alg(z) = G`. Prove that its map to
`Stab_Co1(λ)` is surjective with kernel `C_Q(β⁺)` of order `2^24`. This identifies the
actual two-axis stabilizer of shape `2^{1+23}.Co2` and gives
`|S| = 2^24 · |Co2|` using the P2-L equivalence. The kernel here is not the extraspecial
group `Q` of order `2^25`.

Formalize the orbit certificates of §§3–4 and Appendix D: representative words, stabilizer
generators, complete subgroup-orbit decompositions, and the triality transitions in Tables
2 and 4. Prove the soundness of the action calculations and exhaustive coverage of both
`X⁺` and the full `K`-orbit `X⁻`. For the latter, justify the passage from the local
`H := K ∩ G` and triality calculations to the full stabilizer action; closure under a
subgroup's generators alone does not prove this coverage. Justify any modular arithmetic
used to certify equalities in the rational representation. Prove finiteness of `X⁺`, `X⁻`,
and `S` first. Use the actual orbit/fibre equivalences to deduce `Finite K` from finite
`X⁻` and `S`, then `Finite M_alg` from finite `X⁺` and `K`; neither application assumes
that the group being proved finite is already finite. Only afterwards take cardinalities
in these two equivalences to obtain

```text
|M_alg| = |X⁺| · |X⁻| · |S|.
```

Prove Monster simplicity through Lemmas 5.3–5.5 and Theorem 5.6. This includes the full
normal-subgroup list `1, ⟨z⟩, Q, G` for `G`, using its extraspecial subgroup and the
faithful irreducible `Co1` action on `Λ/2Λ`, and the explicit triality calculations that
exclude each proper possibility for a normal subgroup's intersection with `G`.

Define `B_alg := K/⟨β⁺⟩` and obtain its finiteness and order
`|B_alg| = |X⁻| · |S| / 2` as in Corollary 5.2. Use P0's prime-order normal-generation criterion separately for this quotient: construct
its Sylow normal forms for primes `2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23,31,41,47`, certify coverage of
their prime-order elements up to quotient conjugacy, and give normal-generation words for
each resulting representative and every quotient generator. Prove nontriviality and the
quotient word-evaluation/central-kernel comparisons before applying that criterion. The Monster simplicity
theorem and the Baby Monster order calculation do not discharge this target.

**P2-D: prove the central-extension prerequisite.** Select the recorded Ivanov
presentation route, with the no-proper-double-cover hypothesis attributed to Griess in
[Breuer–Magaard–Wilson, v2, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/1902.07758v2). Prove this
hypothesis for `M_alg` after P2-M and before Baby Monster presentation recognition.
An explicit sufficient target is that no perfect group admits a surjection onto `M_alg`
with central kernel of order two. This excludes a proper covering group, while allowing
the split extension `C2 × M_alg`. Formalize the required part of Griess's
*The Schur multipliers of the known finite simple groups, III* directly for this `M_alg`,
carrying its concrete local-subgroup and construction hypotheses. Any comparison with
Griess's construction must be proved from those earlier P2-L/G/M identifications,
independently of P2-R, the `Y₄₄₃` recognition theorem and `ClassificationStatement`.
Do not identify the two Monsters by the presentation theorem whose proof is being supplied.
Computing the entire Schur multiplier is not a separate endpoint. Order and simplicity of
`M_alg` alone do not imply this prerequisite.

**P2-R: identify the exact two presentations.** Formalize the recorded presentation
theorems, including their structural hypotheses and the maps to `M_alg` and `B_alg`.
Construct the intermediate group `BiM := (M_alg × M_alg) ⋊ C₂` from the already
constructed Monster, with the nontrivial `C₂` element swapping the two factors. Give the
two factor inclusions, the projection onto `C₂` with its kernel, the swap element and its
square/conjugation equations, and generation by those factors and the swap. This carrier
does not depend on presentation recognition.

For the Baby Monster select the `Y₅₅₅` presentation used in Ivanov's *Presenting the Baby
Monster*, as invoked by Breuer–Magaard–Wilson §2. Transcribe its exact numbered generators
and full source relator family, including the additional spider relation and any other
relations actually required in that chosen source. Do not infer a presentation from the
Coxeter diagram alone or add deflation relations from a different construction. Give the
source-to-Lean numbering and generator dictionaries, check all relations and generation,
and prove the resulting presented group is `MulEquiv` to this actual `BiM`. Then formalize
the precise deduction of the `Y₄₃₃` central extension/quotient used below, with its actual
subgroup maps and kernels and the independently proved P2-D hypothesis, before concluding
Baby Monster presentation recognition. Neither this intermediate carrier nor its
presentation theorem may be assumed through P2-R's final recognition conclusion.
For the Monster use
Ivanov's *Y-groups via Transitive Extension*, especially Lemma 3.2 and §3.9, carrying its
transitive-extension and subgroup-identification arguments as proof obligations.
These presentation-identification theorems must supply the upper bounds for the
presented groups; checking relators in the constructed models supplies only maps out of
them.

Account for the quotient conventions in the actual Lean definitions:

- `TauCeti.Sporadic.Monster.presentation` has the `Y₄₄₃` Coxeter relators followed by
  `spiderRelator = (a b₁ c₁ a b₂ c₂ a b₃ c₃)^10` and
  `centralInvolutionRelator = (a b₃ c₃ d₃ b₁ c₁ b₂)^9`, Ivanov's `f₃₁₂`.
  Identify the Coxeter-plus-spider group with `M_alg × C2`, prove that `f₃₁₂` kills its
  central factor, and identify the full 80-relator quotient with `M_alg`.
- `TauCeti.Sporadic.BabyMonster.presentation` has the `Y₄₃₃` Coxeter relators followed by
  `spiderRelator = (t₅ t₄ t₃ t₅ t₆ t₇ t₅ t₉ t₁₀)^10`,
  `extraRelatorOne = (t₅ t₄ t₃ t₆ t₇ t₈ t₉)^9`, and
  `extraRelatorTwo = (t₅ t₄ t₃ t₆ t₉ t₁₀ t₁₁)^9`.
  Identify the Coxeter-plus-spider group `2 × 2·B` with `C2 × K`, including the
  identification of the cover with this constructed centralizer. Prove that the normal
  closure of the two extra relators is exactly the kernel of the map to
  `K/⟨β⁺⟩ = B_alg`, so that the full 69-relator presentation gives `B_alg`.

Give the numbered-generator dictionaries, verify generation, and transport the resulting
`MulEquiv`s to the exact `SporadicName.Group` carriers. The existing
`mulEquivPresentedGroupCoxeterAppend` declarations only identify the presentations with
the corresponding Coxeter quotients; they do not recognize a finite simple group.
Group-specific constructions and certificates live in P2, while their reusable soundness
theorems and group-action criteria live in P0.

For the involution-class input to P2M, select the finite local route of Höhn–Seysen
Appendix E: prove the odd-index reduction from `M_alg` to `Gx0`, construct exhaustive local
involution families in `Gx0`, and certify their fusion to `β⁺` or `z` by actual conjugating
words. Prove those two representatives nonconjugate using their actual representation
invariants. Supply the required Co1/local character facts from P2-L/G. The published
computation is input to a soundness proof and checked certificate, not an imported theorem;
do not use its alternative Monster-character-table calculation or require identification
with the full Griess/VOA automorphism group. This places the two-involution proof after the
order/local-action constructions and before the complete 194-class analysis.

## P2M: the Monster's conjugacy classes and character count

Build the conjugacy structure of the concrete Monster from P2 and transport it across P2's
proved recognition `MulEquiv` to **exactly** `SporadicName.M.Group`. Construct an explicit finite
list of representative words in the recorded generators, evaluate those words in the actual
model and presented group, and prove pairwise nonconjugacy and completeness. Deliver native
`TauCeti.ClassData` with this very list, its label/representative round trips and the criterion
that two elements have the same label exactly when they are conjugate. Prove each
representative's element order, the order and stated structure of its actual centralizer, and
its inverse and power-class labels. Check the subgroup-fusion maps used to identify the rows.
The final class equivalence must send a label to the class of its specified representative;
a bare equivalence chosen from the desired cardinality is not the construction.

The group-specific proof must build all its inputs. In particular establish that there are
exactly two classes of involutions, with actual representatives and the two nonconjugacy and
coverage assertions. Identify their actual centralizers: the central extension of the Baby
Monster in the `2A` case, with the involution as its kernel, and the
`2^{1+24}_+.Co1` local group in the `2B` case, with proved maps, kernels and quotients rather
than an abstract group-shape label. These use the P2 Baby Monster quotient and Conway/Griess
constructions; prove the required local group and character-table facts for those actual
subgroups, or connect them by proved isomorphisms to their existing constructions. Construct
the degree-196883 complex representation from the Griess module, identifying its fixed line
and the complementary or quotient module in dimension 196884, and prove the resulting
representation is irreducible independently of the Monster's full character table. Record
which representation values, local centralizer calculations and fusion tests separate each
remaining pair of candidate classes. These are explicit construction and theorem targets,
not opaque hypothesis fields for a conditional Monster-count theorem.

Follow the class-verification argument of [Breuer, Magaard and Wilson, *Verification of the
conjugacy classes and ordinary character table of the Monster*, §2 and §4.9 Proposition1](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.12182v1).
Supply its individual local subgroup/table and representation prerequisites before the class
count. In particular distinguish classes meeting the involution centralizers from the
odd-order analysis and prove exhaustion over **all** element orders. Where the argument uses
a power map or fusion test, prove its value on the actual elements; matching names in a
printed table is not a fusion proof. P0's mass-exhaustion criterion is available when the
independently certified group and centralizer orders give the complete class-size sum.
Do not treat the finite axis-orbit certificate that gives the group order as a conjugacy
classification of its elements.

Prove that the resulting actual representative list has length 194 and deduce
`Nat.card (ConjClasses SporadicName.M.Group) = 194` using native `ClassData` soundness. Then
consume native `TauCeti.card_irreducibleCharacters` over `ℂ` to deduce that the Monster has
194 irreducible complex characters and that its ordinary character table has 194 rows and
columns. The generic theorem requires a finite group, an algebraically closed field and
invertible group order; P2 supplies finiteness and `ℂ` supplies the field conditions. Do not

verification precedes the final full-table verification. This milestone does not require
that full table's construction as a prerequisite and does not duplicate CharacterTheory's
generic irreducible/class-count theorem.

Prove the class-count and group-order statements separately. The exact ATLAS order belongs
to P2's recognized group; neither that order, simplicity, nor `ClassificationStatement` alone

## A0: assemble the list properties

Prove `CFSGIndex.finite` and `CFSGIndex.isSimpleGroup` by the four constructors, invoking E0,
the uniform F1/T2/T3 Lie-type results, and the P1/P2 sporadic results. Check a test theorem for
one cyclic, one alternating, one ordinary Lie, one graph-twisted, each of Suzuki/Ree/Tits, and
one P1 and one P2 sporadic entry; these are checks of the dispatcher, not replacements for
the uniform proofs. Audit the endpoint's axioms and confirm that no case uses
`ClassificationStatement` or assumes the corresponding basic property.

# Characteristic classes and Chern–Weil theory

Build integral Chern, Pontryagin and Euler classes, mod2 Stiefel–Whitney classes,
cohomological Thom and Gysin maps, universal cohomology calculations, and the
comparison with curvature. Construct the compact connected Lie-group CE/de Rham,
primitive/exterior and universal-transgression comparisons on these same
cohomology and universal-bundle carriers. Construct the rational Chern character and the
Todd, L and Â multiplicative classes, including their relative and supported
interfaces. Classes carry their coefficient ring, degree, orientation and
bundle; formal roots are a proved splitting device.

## Carriers, scope and suppliers

Use Mathlib `FiberBundle`, `VectorBundle`, `VectorBundleCore`, `Bundle.TotalSpace`,
pullbacks, Hom/dual constructions and `ContMDiffVectorBundle`. The continuous
finite-rank category, locally constant ranks, finite embeddings, metrics,
Grassmannians, Stiefel spaces and numerable BO/BU classification are
[TopologicalKTheory T1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/7575afad9ceed0ff19ecf5629ba196e54fdf7637/TauCetiRoadmap/TopologicalKTheory/README.md)
dependencies. Its T6.4 supplies continuous principal/associated bundles and
descent. Use TopK T1.5's actual finite real Grassmannians and tautological bundles.
C1.0 and C1.1a construct their positive-rank oriented double covers, lifted
finite cells and coordinate maps. TopK T1.6a owns the fixed-rank and stable
colimits, universal-bundle diagrams and classifier comparison on those
carriers. [HomotopySpheres §3A and §4A](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1287)
supplies the earlier compactly generated substrate and consumes these
classifiers for its later stable O/SO and ΩBSO comparison; §4A is not an
input to the finite oriented-cover construction. Write BO(n) and BU(n)
for T1.6's fixed-rank universal Grassmannians, and BSO(n) for the
ambient-dimension colimit in `CompactlyGenerated` of C1.1a's actual finite
oriented carriers. C1.1b compares these carriers and their universal bundles
with the SO join classifier. Stable classification is consumed only for
finite CW bases.
The oriented frame/classifier statements use n≥1. In rank0 retain the
orientation sign separately as a section of the trivial two-point cover;
BSO(0)=pt represents the canonically oriented zero bundle. Write
B_join(G) for the principal universal join model; BG means B_join(G) except
for the named classical Grassmannian carriers. The O/U/SO comparisons identify
its associated universal bundles with these named carriers; ring calculations
are transported through those maps, and no second Grassmannian carrier is defined.

The principal-group scope is compact Lie G, including finite discrete groups.
Numerable principal bundles are classified over paracompact Hausdorff bases.
Characteristic classes in singular cohomology are natural for their continuous
pullbacks. Classification of lines by singular H² assumes CW type; on a general
paracompact base distinguish Čech H² from singular H². Variable ranks are handled
on clopen strata, with the singular cohomology product comparison for disjoint
unions. Smooth statements use finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable
Mathlib manifolds; the de Rham comparison uses its precise σ-compact hypotheses.

- [AlgebraicTopology Stages2–6,8.1–8.7](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/0e8b058a97cc4f9401d2679313e0e937761c1024/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology/README.md) owns singular
  chains/cochains, local systems, cup/cap/cross products and pair
  sequences, excision, cellular comparison, Künneth and homotopy
  comparison. Consume actual Tau Ceti `TopCat.singularCohomology`,
  `singularCohomologyMap`, `singularCup`, `TopPair.singularCohomology`,
  `singularCohomologyδ` and the relative exactness/naturality lemmas. The
  cup module already proves associativity and units; its full graded
  and relative packaging is that supplier's target.
  C2's primary Euler obstruction additionally consumes AT8.9; ordinary line

## Conventions

Write H^k(X;R) for the existing singular cohomology object, with cochain degree k and zero groups in negative degrees.
Package H* as the graded direct sum and completed even classes as
`Hhat_even(X;R)=Π_(j≥0) H^(2j)(X;R)`, with finite convolution in each degree.
All universal identities are degreewise; truncation requires a displayed
cohomological dimension bound. Coefficient maps Z→Q→R commute with products,
relative maps and connecting morphisms. No de Rham class specifies torsion.

A real rank-n bundle E has orientation system o(E), the integral sign local
system of its orientation double cover. Its Thom class is
`U_E ∈ H^n(E,E\0;π*o(E))`. A chosen orientation trivializes that system and
fixes each positive-rank fibre generator by its ordered positive basis.
In rank0 the chosen orientation is a sign ±1, and that sign is its degree0
Thom/Euler generator; the canonical empty-basis orientation gives+1. The Thom map is
`a↦π*a ∪ U_E`, in that order. Direct-sum fibre orientation orders E before F.
The Euler class is zero-section pullback of the absolute image of U_E; it lives
in H^n(X;o(E)) without a chosen orientation. Complex fibres have their canonical
real orientation `(v₁,iv₁,…,v_r,iv_r)`.

For an invariant polynomial P on the real Lie algebra define the abstract
Chern–Weil map as `cw(P)=[P(F)]`, with no automatic 2π or i rescaling.
Polarization satisfies P(z)=B_P(z,…,z), and evaluation uses that B_P on F
with no additional factorial. For a unitary representation ρ use the actual
polynomials `coeff_(t^j) det(1+t(i/(2π))dρ(z))`; for ch use
`tr((i dρ(z)/(2π))^j)/j!`. Pontryagin/Pfaffian polynomials likewise include
the displayed 2π factor themselves; prove the prescribed Chern/character
polynomials real-valued on the compact unitary Lie algebra before taking real forms. In SBC's Lie(Circle)=R convention
θ↦exp(iθ), the standard character has dρ(a)=ia and its degree1 invariant
polynomial is −a/(2π). Thus cw sends it to −[F_real/(2π)], exactly the
standard-character line class, while the dual character gives the opposite.

Chern classes have degree2i and `c_r(E)=e(E_R)`. On CP^N let
`h=c₁(O(1))`, with ∫_(CP¹)h=1, so `c₁(O(−1))=−h`. For projectivization
P(E) of lines use its tautological sub-line H and `a=c₁(H)`; its monic relation
is `a^r−c₁(E)a^(r−1)+…+(-1)^r c_r(E)=0`. Real projectivization uses
`a=w₁(H)` and relation `a^n+w₁(E)a^(n−1)+…+w_n(E)=0` over F2.

Define `p_i(E)=(-1)^i c_(2i)(E⊗_R C)` integrally. Odd Chern classes of a
complexified real bundle are annihilated by2. Accordingly the exact integral
Whitney formula retains the odd-times-odd Chern terms; clean Pontryagin
multiplication is asserted after inverting2, not over arbitrary integral bases.

For a connection d+A on column coefficients use `F=dA+A∧A` and
`c(F)=det(1+(i/(2π))F)`, `ch(F)=tr exp((i/(2π))F)`. The exponential is
interpreted degreewise and terminates on a fixed-dimensional manifold. A metric
connection of rank2r>0 in an oriented orthonormal real frame has Euler form `Pf(F/(2π))`,
with `Pf([[0,a],[−a,0]])=a`, and Pontryagin
forms from `det(1+tF/(2π))`. The Euler form is0 in odd rank and the
chosen locally constant orientation sign in rank0. Check the block `[[0,−α],[α,0]]`: its complex
line curvature is i dα and its Euler form is −dα/(2π). This matches the
standard-character associated line, whose c₁ is the negative of SBC B6's
principal circle class defined using the dual-character line. CKG's O(1)
curvature is −2πiω_FS, so the Chern form is +ω_FS.

# Roadmap: Chevalley groups and the Chevalley–Demazure group schemes

This roadmap develops, for every valid Dynkin type `t`, the explicit realization and
point-group theory of **the simply connected Chevalley–Demazure group scheme
`G_sc(t)` over `ℤ`**. Its canonical constructor is the Chevalley–Demazure construction of
ReductiveGroups Layer 9 (9A and 9B) at `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum t`; `G_sc(t)` here is
that specialization. It develops the theory of its points that the finite groups of Lie type are
built from and studied with:

- its root subgroups `x_α` for every root, its split maximal torus, and the Chevalley commutator
  formula;
- over a field, the Bruhat decomposition, the Tits system, the centre, and Steinberg's presentation;
- the endomorphisms a Steinberg map is made of: field Frobenius, graph automorphisms, and the
  exceptional isogenies of `B₂` and `F₄` in characteristic two and `G₂` in characteristic three,
  together with their action on the character lattice;
- flatness of `G_sc(t)` over `ℤ`, its big cell, and the identification of its points over an
  algebraically closed field with the group generated by the root subgroups;
- Chevalley's comparison theorem, which identifies any two Chevalley group schemes of the same
  type and weight lattice by an isomorphism matching root subgroups.

The construction is the classical one: Chevalley's, via Kostant's `ℤ`-form of the enveloping
algebra acting on an admissible lattice in a faithful representation, taken as the closed subgroup
scheme of `GLₙ` over `ℤ` generated by the root subgroups and a weight torus. The simply connected
form uses the direct sum of the fundamental representations, whose weights span the full weight
lattice for every type at once. Suggested home: `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Chevalley/` for the
group schemes and their points, with the representation-theoretic inputs in the existing homes
`TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/` and `TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/UniversalEnveloping/Kostant/`.

## Scope and boundaries

In scope: everything about the explicitly constructed Chevalley group schemes and their points
that is proved from the construction, by the methods of Chevalley, Steinberg, and Demazure. The
general theory is not in scope, and the dividing line is one question: *is the statement about a
specified integral Chevalley model or its explicit realization, proved using the constructor/comparison interface?*

- The [reductive-groups roadmap](../ReductiveGroups/README.md) owns abstract affine group schemes:
  reductive and semisimple groups, maximal tori and Borel subgroups of an abstract group, the root
  datum of a reductive group, central isogenies and simple connectivity as properties, and the
  isomorphism and existence theorems. Its Layer 9 (9A and 9B) owns the canonical integral Lie/group constructor, proves split reductivity
  and the specified root datum, and supplies the native model used here. This roadmap constructs
  the realization adapters and transports that certification, including
  `TauCeti.simplyConnectedSemisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty`, to its displayed point API.
- The [root-systems roadmap](../RepresentationTheory/RootSystems/README.md) owns `DynkinType`, the
  Bourbaki numbering, `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum`, diagram automorphisms of root data,
  and root-datum isogenies.
- The [Lie highest-weight roadmap](../RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight/README.md) owns Verma
  modules, the irreducible quotients `L(λ)`, PBW, finite-dimensionality of `L(λ)` for dominant
  integral `λ` (its Layers 3 and 4), and Serre's theorem (its Layer 7). The split-field finite-dimensionality and rational descent adapter used here is
  constructed once in ReductiveGroups Layer 9A, item 5, beside that existing native highest-module API; C1
  consumes it and computes its fundamental-module and symmetry specializations.
- The [CFSG statement roadmap](../CFSGStatement/README.md) owns the classification list, the
  choice of Steinberg map for each index and the transport of its family-specific
  realizations to the common canonical carrier. Reusable represented models are retained. The [CFSG basic-properties roadmap](../CFSGBasicProperties/README.md) owns
  finite fixed-point groups: Steinberg descent, twisted root groups, and simplicity. Everything in
  this roadmap is about the ambient group and holds over an arbitrary field or ring, not only for
  fixed points of an endomorphism.

## Constructor ownership and comparison order

C0–C2 below retain every explicit Geck, fundamental-module, admissible-lattice,
root-index and torus calculation. Their generic producers live **once** in
ReductiveGroups Layer 9A (item 1, the integral Chevalley lattice; item 5, the admissible
lattices of the highest-weight modules) and Layer 9B (the Chevalley–Demazure construction and its
base change). C0 supplies the concrete normalization adapter; C1 computes the fundamental modules,
weight bases and numbered symmetries; C2 identifies `G_D`, the Chevalley–Demazure group of
ReductiveGroups 9B at the root datum with character lattice `Λ(D)`, with the displayed native
toral closure. Thus saying “construct” below includes these actual adapters and inverse/value
equations, not a second canonical group. `DynkinType.chevalleyGroupScheme` and
`DynkinType.ChevalleyGroup` name that group scheme and its points; no independent carrier is
introduced beside them.

C3 proves the presentation and point-group formulas on this model. C4 instantiates the native
generic flatness theorem and proves the integral big cell and its point consequences; it does not
repeat a generic flatness construction. C5's exceptional **point** map and character compatibility
come from the field presentation, independently of algebraicity. ReductiveGroups 9B ("Special
isogenies in characteristics two and three") owns the exceptional isogenies as morphisms of group
schemes; C7 compares that morphism with C5 on all roots, the torus and points. C6 owns the
Chevalley-datum comparisons and their extension from the big cell to the whole scheme. There is no
C5↔C7 or C3↔ReductiveGroups 9B existence cycle.

For a general reductive datum, including central tori or empty roots, the full construction is
ReductiveGroups 9B. C0–C7's single-type notation denotes the semisimple specialization and does not
narrow it. For every represented datum, its actual `Λ(D)` torus is used: the full-`P`
parametrization can have `μ₂` kernel already for adjoint `A₁`. No point-image saturation is
silently substituted.

## Standing conventions

- **Numbering.** Simple roots, fundamental weights, and simple coroots are indexed by `Fin t.rank`
  in the Bourbaki numbering fixed by `DynkinType.cartanMatrix`, and all roots by `Fin t.numRoots`
  as in `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum`. No second enumeration of the roots is introduced.
- **The Lie algebra.** The Lie algebra is `DynkinType.lieAlgebra t ht` over `ℚ`, with its numbered
  Chevalley generators `DynkinType.lieBasis`, Cartan subalgebra `DynkinType.cartanSubalgebra`, and
  the instances `DynkinType.instIsKillingLieAlgebra` and
  `DynkinType.instIsTriangularizableLieAlgebra`. A representation of the Serre algebra
  `Matrix.ToLieAlgebra ℚ t.cartanMatrixᵀ` is read as a representation of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra`
  through the inverse of `DynkinType.serreLift`, which is an isomorphism by Serre's theorem
  (LieHighestWeight Layer 7, specialized as the target `DynkinType.serreLift_injective` of C2).
- **Root subgroups.** `x_α(u) = Σₙ uⁿ ρ(e_α)⁽ⁿ⁾` for the root vector `e_α` of the Chevalley system
  of C0, as in `kostantRootSubgroupParam`. For a root `α` and a unit `s`,
  `n_α(s) = x_α(s) x_{-α}(-s⁻¹) x_α(s)` and `h_α(s) = n_α(s) n_α(1)⁻¹`, following Steinberg,
  *Lectures on Chevalley Groups*, Chapter 3, Lemma 19, who writes `w_α` for `n_α`. The Weyl
  representative `n_α(1)` agrees with `kostantWeylPoints`.
- **Characters.** The torus of a Chevalley datum `D` is the split torus whose character lattice is
  the lattice `Λ(D)` spanned by the weights of `D` (C2), and it acts on the weight-`μ` part of the
  module through the character `μ`. For `G_sc(t)`, `Λ = Fin t.rank → ℤ`, identified with the weight
  lattice of `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum t` through the fundamental weights. A character
  map of an endomorphism `F` preserving the torus is a pullback `χ ↦ χ ∘ F`, in the same direction
  as `RootPairingIsogeny.weightMap`. It is data attached to `F` together with a proof of the torus
  compatibility equation (C5). It is not extracted from an arbitrary abstract homomorphism.
- **Exceptional isogenies.** The exponent `e_i` is `1` on a long simple root and `p` on a short
  one, long and short as in `DynkinType.IsLongSimpleRoot`, and `σ` is the length-exchanging
  permutation of `DynkinType.IsSpecialNodePerm`, so that `τ (x_{±α_i}(u)) = x_{±α_{σ i}}(u ^ e_i)`
  up to the signs recorded in C5. This is the convention of the root-datum isogenies
  `DynkinType.b2SpecialIsogeny`, `DynkinType.f4SpecialIsogeny`, and `DynkinType.g2SpecialIsogeny`.
- **Generality.** The group schemes are over `ℤ` and their points are taken over every commutative
  ring. The group theory of C3 and C5 is over a field. Results that need an algebraically closed
  field, or a field of characteristic `p`, say so in their hypotheses.

## What already exists (consume)

Tau Ceti already contains most of the representation-independent machinery. The remaining work here is the explicit model/normalization comparison and point-group
consumer theory; the generic integral constructor is owned by ReductiveGroups Layer 9 (9A and 9B).

- **The Lie algebra and its root datum.** `DynkinType.lieAlgebra`, Geck's explicit matrix
  realization of the split Lie algebra of every valid type over `ℚ`; `DynkinType.serreLift`, the
  surjection from the Serre algebra; `DynkinType.exists_isChevalleySystem`, a Chevalley system over
  `ℚ` for the involution `DynkinType.chevalleyInvolution`, indexed by `Weight ℚ H L` and asserted
  to exist; `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum`, `DynkinType.diagramAut`, and
  `RootPairingIsogeny` with its powers and the special node permutations.
- **Kostant forms and lattices.** `UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantForm` and its Serre-presented
  version; `kostantWeightBasis`, which gives any finitely generated admissible lattice lying in the
  integral weight spaces a weight basis; the weight-component decomposition of an admissible
  lattice.
- **Generic Chevalley carriers.** For any Kostant-stable lattice with a weight basis:
  `kostantRootSubgroupParam`; the elementary subgroup `kostantElementarySubgroup` and its functor
  in the value ring; the split torus `kostantTorusPoints`; the Weyl elements `kostantWeylPoints` and
  their action on the torus; the class-two and multiply-laced commutator relations, including `G₂`;
  the generated and toral-closure group schemes `kostantGeneratedGroupScheme` and
  `kostantToralGroupScheme`, with base change, finite type, and rigidity (a homomorphism out of the
  generated scheme is determined by the root subgroups); numbered symmetries
  `kostantElementaryNumberedSymmetryAut` and their descent to the schemes; the Frobenius
  `kostantElementaryFrobenius` and the composite `kostantElementarySteinberg`.
- **Instances of the generic carrier.** The adjoint Geck carrier `DynkinType.geckGroupScheme` for
  every valid type, which becomes `DynkinType.adjointGroupScheme`, and the classical carriers
  `SlStd`, `SpStd`, `TypeBSpinCarrier`, `TypeDSpinCarrier`. The minuscule, doubled, tripled and short-root carriers remain represented models,
  including their independent representation/Spin consumers. Their full lattices, weight tables
  and polynomial maps feed C1, C6 and ReductiveGroups 9B; only redundant CFSG dispatch aliases may be
  retired after proved transport and an import audit.
- **Highest-weight theory.** `VermaModule` and `irreducibleQuotient` over any field of
  characteristic zero with a triangularizable Cartan subalgebra, and finite-dimensionality of
  `L(λ)` for dominant integral `λ` over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero
  (`TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/FiniteDimensional.lean`), whose supporting weight-space
  files also assume `IsAlgClosed`.
- **Tits systems.** `TauCeti.TitsSystem` and the Bruhat-cell API in
  `TauCeti/GroupTheory/TitsSystem/`.

## Milestones

| Item | Depends on | Deliverable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C0: the Chevalley basis | root systems Layer 6 | a named Chevalley system of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra` for every root, and its structure constants |
| C1: the simply connected module | C0, LieHighestWeight Layers 3 and 4 | the fundamental modules over `ℚ`, their admissible lattices, and the full-weight module `V_sc(t)` with its numbered symmetries |
| C2: Chevalley data and their group schemes | C0, C1, LieHighestWeight Layer 7 | `ChevalleyDatum`, its group scheme, root subgroups for every root, the torus, and the pinning equations; `G_sc(t)` as the full-weight instance |
| C3: the group over a field | C2 | commutator formula, Bruhat decomposition, Tits system, centre; Steinberg's presentation in the simply connected case |

C0 to C2 are one lane and C3 to C7 build on it. C4 needs C3; C5 and C6 can proceed in parallel
once C4 lands; C7 needs C4 and C5. C5 does not use C7: the character maps of the exceptional
isogenies are computed in C5 from their action on the root subgroups.

### C0: the Chevalley basis

Beside the existence statement `DynkinType.exists_isChevalleySystem`, construct a named Chevalley
system `DynkinType.chevalleySystem t ht` of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra t ht` for the involution
`DynkinType.chevalleyInvolution`, with root vectors `e_α` for every `α : Fin t.numRoots`, built from
Geck's basis rather than chosen from the existence theorem. `LieModule.Weight ℚ H L` contains the
zero weight of the Cartan action (for `A₁` its elements are `0, α, -α`), so the roots are the subtype
`{α : LieModule.Weight ℚ H L // α.IsNonZero}`. Transport the root enumeration `Fin t.numRoots` to
that subtype by a named equivalence, with `e_{α_i}` and `e_{-α_i}` the numbered generators of
`DynkinType.lieBasis`. `IsChevalleySystem` takes a family indexed by all of `Weight ℚ H L`, so
provide a separate adapter that extends the root-vector family by a chosen value at the zero
weight before calling that API. Prove that it is an
`IsChevalleySystem` for the signed Geck involution, that its roots are those of
`DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum` under the fixed enumeration, and the structure-constant
theorem: for roots `α, β` with `α + β` a root, `⁅e_α, e_β⁆ = N_{α,β} e_{α+β}` with
`N_{α,β} = ±(r + 1)`, where `r` is the largest integer with `β - rα` a root (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 1, Theorem 1).
Record `N_{α,β}` as an integer-valued function `DynkinType.structureConstant`, with the symmetries
`N_{β,α} = -N_{α,β}` and the Chevalley relation `N_{-α,-β} = -N_{α,β}` for the involution-compatible
choice.

### C1: the simply connected module

1. **Finite-dimensionality over a split field.** Prove that `irreducibleQuotient b λ` is finite
   dimensional for dominant integral `λ` over a field `K` of characteristic zero under
   `[IsTriangularizable K H L]`, with no `IsAlgClosed K` hypothesis. Either remove the algebraically
   closed hypothesis from the weight-space files the existing proof uses, replacing it by
   triangularizability, or prove that base change to an algebraic closure carries `L_K(λ)` to
   `L_{K̄}(λ)` and deduce finite-dimensionality from the closed case. Its home is beside
   `TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/HighestWeight/FiniteDimensional.lean`.
2. **The fundamental modules.** For `i : Fin t.rank`, let `ϖ_i` be the fundamental weight of
   `DynkinType.lieAlgebra` with respect to the pinned base. Define `DynkinType.fundamentalModule t ht
   i` as `irreducibleQuotient` at `ϖ_i` over `ℚ`, and `v⁺_i` its highest-weight generator. Prove it
   finite dimensional and nonzero; nonvanishing of the Verma module `M(ϖ_i)` is PBW, from
   LieHighestWeight Layer 3.
3. **Admissible lattices.** Define `DynkinType.fundamentalLattice t ht i` as the `U_ℤ`-orbit
   `U_ℤ · v⁺_i` of the highest-weight vector, for `U_ℤ` the simple-generator Kostant form. Prove it
   is stable under `U_ℤ`, finitely generated over `ℤ`, and spans the module over `ℚ`
   (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 2, Corollary 1 to Theorem 2, whose part (b) also gives the
   weight decomposition), and that it lies in the span of the integral
   weight spaces, so that `kostantWeightBasis` gives it a weight basis. Its weights are those of
   `L(ϖ_i)`, and its `ϖ_i`-weight space is `ℤ · v⁺_i`.
4. **The full-weight module.** Define `DynkinType.scModule t ht` as the direct sum of the
   fundamental modules and `DynkinType.scLattice t ht` as the direct sum of their lattices, with the
   product weight basis. Prove that its weights span the weight lattice
   `Fin t.rank → ℤ` (each `ϖ_i` is a weight) and that the representation of
   `DynkinType.lieAlgebra` on it is faithful. This is the analogue for every type of
   `span_range_basisWeight_eq_top` for the spin carriers; that the sum of the fundamental
   representations realizes the full weight lattice is Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 3, the remark
   after Lemma 27.
5. **Numbered symmetries.** For `σ` in `DynkinType.diagramSymmetry t`, construct the
   `ℚ`-linear automorphism `θ_σ` of `scModule` that maps `L(ϖ_i)` to `L(ϖ_{σ i})`, sends `v⁺_i` to
   `v⁺_{σ i}`, intertwines `e_{±α_i}` with `e_{±α_{σ i}}`, and preserves `scLattice`. Construct it
   from the universal property of `irreducibleQuotient` applied to the twist of `L(ϖ_i)` by the
   diagram automorphism of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra`, and prove `θ_σ ∘ θ_τ = θ_{στ}`. Package
   `(σ, θ_σ)` as a symmetry of the numbered Kostant data in the sense of the module
   `TauCeti.Algebra.Lie.UniversalEnveloping.Kostant.RootSubgroup.NumberedSymmetry`. The direct sum
   of all fundamental modules is stable under every diagram automorphism, so one module carries all
   of them.

   `θ_σ` maps the weight-`μ` component of `scLattice` onto the weight-`σ·μ` component, but it need
   not permute a weight basis: fundamental modules have weight spaces of dimension greater than one,
   and `θ_σ` can act on a `σ`-fixed weight space by a non-monomial matrix. The scheme-level descent
   `kostantToralNumberedSymmetryIso` asks for a monomial action. Generalize it to a lattice
   automorphism carrying each weight component `M_μ` onto `M_{σ·μ}`: such an automorphism
   conjugates the weight torus to itself, which is what the descent uses monomiality for.

### C2: Chevalley data, their group schemes, and root data

**Serre's theorem for the pinned algebra.** `DynkinType.serreLift_injective`: specialize Serre's
theorem from LieHighestWeight Layer 7 to `DynkinType.serreLift`, so that it is an isomorphism and a
representation of the Serre algebra is one of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra`.

A **Chevalley datum** of type `t`, `DynkinType.ChevalleyDatum t ht`, is a finite-dimensional
faithful representation of `DynkinType.lieAlgebra t ht` over `ℚ` together with a lattice spanning
it that is stable under the simple-generator Kostant form, and a weight basis of that lattice. Its
**weight lattice** `Λ(D)` is the sublattice of `Fin t.rank → ℤ` spanned by its weights; it contains
the root lattice and is free of rank `t.rank`. Fix a `ℤ`-basis `b_D : Basis (Fin t.rank) ℤ Λ(D)` and
write each weight of the weight basis in `b_D`-coordinates. These coordinate weights span
`Fin t.rank → ℤ` by the definition of `Λ(D)`. Its group scheme `ChevalleyDatum.groupScheme` is
`kostantToralGroupScheme` on the module, lattice, and weight basis, with the coordinate weights as
`wt`. Its points are `ChevalleyDatum.Points D A`. `scModule` with `scLattice` is a Chevalley datum
with `Λ = Fin t.rank → ℤ` and `b_D` the standard basis, so the coordinate weights are the weights
themselves. The Geck module is a datum with `Λ` the root lattice and `b_D` the simple roots.
Everything in C2 and C3, except the two items marked as simply connected, is stated for every
Chevalley datum.

Do not use the weights themselves, read in `Fin t.rank → ℤ`, as `wt` for a datum with
`Λ(D) ≠ Fin t.rank → ℤ`. That parametrizes the torus by `Hom(P, -)` for `P` the full weight lattice,
and the resulting map to `GLₙ` has kernel the diagonalizable group with character group `P / Λ(D)`.
For adjoint `A₁`, `Λ = 2ℤϖ`, the weights are `2ϖ, 0, -2ϖ`, and the map is
`s ↦ diag(s², 1, s⁻²)`, with kernel `μ₂`. That map is not a closed immersion, and in characteristic
two its kernel is nontrivial as a group scheme although its points over a field are trivial.

Define

```text
DynkinType.chevalleyGroupScheme t ht := kostantToralGroupScheme (scModule, scLattice, weight basis)
```

### C3: the group over a field

Let `k` be a field, `D` a Chevalley datum, and `E(k)` the subgroup of its points generated by the
root subgroups and the torus `T(k) = T_D(k) = Hom(Λ(D), kˣ)` of C2, not the smaller range of the
full-weight parametrization. For `G_sc(t)` the torus is already in the subgroup generated by root
subgroups, by C2. Following Steinberg's *Lectures on Chevalley Groups*, Chapters 3 and 6,
which treat every admissible lattice. Steinberg's Chevalley group is the subgroup generated by the
root subgroups alone; the torus normalizes it, and each statement below extends to `E(k)` by that
normalization:

- **The Chevalley commutator formula** for every pair of linearly independent roots `α, β`, in
  Steinberg's normalization, which is also Mathlib's `commutatorElement` and the one the existing
  Kostant commutator lemmas use:
  `⁅x_α(u), x_β(v)⁆ = x_α(u) x_β(v) x_α(u)⁻¹ x_β(v)⁻¹ = ∏ x_{iα+jβ}(c_{ijαβ} u^i v^j)`, the product
  over `i, j > 0` with `iα + jβ` a root, in increasing `i + j` (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 3,
  Lemma 15). Write `M_{α,β,i}` for the integer with `(ad e_α)^i e_β / i! = M_{α,β,i} e_{iα+β}`, so
  `M_{α,β,i} = (1/i!) N_{α,β} N_{α,α+β} ⋯ N_{α,(i-1)α+β}`. In this convention the coefficients are
  `c_{11} = N_{α,β}`, `c_{i1} = M_{α,β,i}` and `c_{1j} = -M_{β,α,j}`, and in type `G₂` the two
  remaining ones are `c_{32} = (2/3) M_{α+β,α,2}` (`α` short, `β` long) and
  `c_{23} = (1/3) M_{α+β,β,2}` (`α` long, `β` short). The sign of `c_{1j}` is constant: the part
  of the commutator linear in `u` is `X - exp(v ad e_β) X` for `X = e_α`, that is
  `-Σ_{j ≥ 1} v^j (ad e_β)^j e_α / j!`, and products of two nonconstant factors have degree at
  least two in `u`. Carter's convention `[x, y] = x⁻¹y⁻¹xy` with `(-t)^i` gives other signs; do not
  mix the two. The existing class-two (`x_α(t) x_β(u) x_α(t)⁻¹ = x_β(u) x_{α+β}(c t u)`),
  multiply-laced, and `G₂` relations are the cases, and the formula is proved for all pairs of the
  root system, not only for the simple ones.

  **Checks.**
  - `A₂`, `e_α = E₁₂`, `e_β = E₂₃`, `N_{α,β} = 1`: `⁅x_α(u), x_β(v)⁆ = x_{α+β}(uv)`. A formula
    with `c_{11} = -N_{α,β}` gives `x_{α+β}(-uv)`.
  - `C₂ = Sp₄` over `ℚ` in the standard symplectic basis, `α = 2e₂` long, `β = e₁ - e₂` short,
    `e_α = E₂₄`, `e_β = E₁₂ - E₄₃`, so `[e_β, e_α] = E₁₄ + E₂₃ = e_{α+β}` and
    `[e_β, e_{α+β}] = 2E₁₃`, hence `M_{β,α,2} = 1`: `⁅x_α(u), x_β(v)⁆ = x_{α+β}(-uv) x_{α+2β}(-uv²)`,
    whose `(1, 3)` entry at `u = v = 1` is `-1`. The sign `(-1)^j` in `c_{1j}` gives `+1` there, and
    agrees with the correct formula only for `j = 1`, so the `A₂` test cannot see it.
  - `G₂` in its seven-dimensional representation, weights `2α + β, α + β, α, 0, -α, -α - β,
    -2α - β` with `α` short, `e_α = E₁₂ + 2E₃₄ + E₄₅ + E₆₇`, `e_β = E₂₃ + E₅₆`: the commutator
    `⁅x_α(u), x_β(v)⁆` equals the ordered product with exponents `uv [e_α, e_β]`,
    `u²v (ad e_α)² e_β / 2`, `u³v (ad e_α)³ e_β / 6` and `u³v² (ad [e_α, e_β])² e_α / 3`, the last
    being `c_{32}` with `c_{32} = (2/3) M_{α+β,α,2}`; the same matrices with the roles exchanged
    confirm `c_{23} = (1/3) M_{α+β,β,2}`. Negating either coefficient makes the two sides differ,
    since the root vector it multiplies acts nontrivially on this module.
- **The unipotent radical and Borel subgroup.** `U(k)` generated by the positive root subgroups,
  with unique expression `∏_{α > 0} x_α(u_α)` in any fixed order of the positive roots;
  `B(k) = U(k) T(k)` with `U(k)` normal; the opposite `U⁻(k)`; `U(k) ∩ B⁻(k) = 1`.
- **The Weyl group.** `N(k)` generated by `T(k)` and the `n_α(1)`, with `N(k) / T(k)` isomorphic to
  the Weyl group of `DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum` by `n_α ↦ s_α`, and `N(k) ∩ B(k) = T(k)`.
- **Bruhat decomposition and the Tits system.** `E(k) = ⊔_w B(k) n_w B(k)`, with unique normal form
  `u n_w b` for `b ∈ B(k)` and `u` in `U(k) ∩ n_w U⁻(k) n_w⁻¹` (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 3,
  Theorem 4 and Theorem 4′), and a `TauCeti.TitsSystem` on `E(k)` with `B = B(k)`, `N = N(k)`, and
  the simple reflections `s_{α_i}`.
- **Centralizer and centre.** For `k` infinite, the centralizer of `T(k)` is `T(k)` and its
  normalizer is `N(k)`. For every field, the centre of `E(k)` is `{h ∈ T(k) : α(h) = 1 for every
  root α}` (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 3, Lemma 28(d), there for the subgroup generated by the
  root subgroups), which is `Hom(Λ(D)/Q, k^×)` for `Q` the root lattice, and `Hom(P/Q, k^×)` in the
  simply connected datum, `P` the weight lattice.
- **Steinberg's presentation (simply connected).** For `G_sc(t)`, `E(k)` is presented by the
  generators `x_α(u)`, `α` a root and `u ∈ k`, subject to additivity in `u`, the commutator formula
  for `α ≠ -β`, and, writing `h_α(s)` for the word above, `h_α(st) = h_α(s) h_α(t)` for
  `s, t ∈ k^×` (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 6, Theorem 8, for an irreducible root system). State
  it as
  a `MulEquiv` from `PresentedGroup` on that relator set, and prove the consequence used in C5: a map
  on the generators `x_α(u)` into any group that respects these relations extends uniquely to a
  homomorphism out of `E(k)`. In rank one the commutator formula is empty and the presentation uses
  Steinberg's relation `n_α(s) x_α(u) n_α(s)⁻¹ = x_{-α}(-s⁻² u)` instead; include it.

### C4: flatness, the big cell, and points over an algebraically closed field

The toral closure is defined over `ℤ`, and without further proof its base change to a field `k`
only contains the closed subgroup scheme that the root subgroups and torus generate over `k`. This
milestone proves equality and identifies the points.

Statements are for a Chevalley datum `D` with group scheme `G_D` and torus `T_D` of C2, and
`G_sc(t)` is the case `D = (scModule, scLattice)`.

- **Flatness.** Instantiate native
  `TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.isTorsionFree_kostantToralCoordinateHopfAlgebra` at D's actual
  e,h,ρ,M,hM,hnil,b,wt. The quotient coordinate Hopf algebra is torsion-free,
  hence flat over ℤ and the schematic closure of its generic fibre. Preserve the
  actual parameter equality through C2's realization isomorphism. This consumes
  the existing theorem; it supplies neither specialization nor smoothness by itself.
- **The big cell.** Order the weights of `D` linearly, refining the dominance order (`μ` before `ν`
  when `μ - ν` is a nonzero sum of positive roots), and order the weight basis compatibly, so the
  weight spaces are consecutive blocks. Then `U` acts by block upper unitriangular matrices, `U⁻`
  by block lower unitriangular ones, and `T_D` by diagonal ones. Let `GLₙ^{LDU}` be the open
  subscheme of `GLₙ` over `ℤ` where the leading principal minors at the block boundaries are
  invertible; block `LDU` factorization identifies it with (block lower unitriangular) ×
  (block diagonal) × (block upper unitriangular). The big cell is `Ω_D = G_D ∩ GLₙ^{LDU}`, and the
  multiplication morphism `U⁻ × T_D × U → Ω_D` is an isomorphism over `ℤ`, so `Ω_D` is open in
  `G_D`. On points over a field the content is
  `E(k) ∩ GLₙ^{LDU}(k) = U⁻(k) T_D(k) U(k)`: by the Bruhat decomposition of C3, conjugated by a
  representative of the longest element, `g ∈ U⁻(k) T_D(k) n_w U(k)`. For `l` block lower
  triangular and `u` block upper unitriangular, the leading block minors of `l n_w u` are invertible
  exactly when those of `n_w` are. `n_w` maps the weight-`μ` block onto the weight-`wμ` block, so
  its leading block minor at an initial segment `S` of weights is invertible
  only if `wS = S`. If that holds for every initial segment, `w` fixes every weight. The weights
  of a faithful representation span `Λ(D) ⊗ ℚ`, so `w = 1`. Over an algebraically closed field
  this is Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 5, Theorem 7. Over `ℤ`, prove that the multiplication
  morphism is an isomorphism by writing its inverse on coordinate rings: the block `LDU` factors
  are polynomials in the matrix entries and the inverses of the leading block minors, and the
  inverse identities, their compatibility with base change, and the covering of `G_D` by the Weyl
  translates of `Ω_D` with their overlaps are part of this item. A fibrewise isomorphism criterion
  may replace that proof only after its full finite-presentation, flatness and fibre hypotheses
  have been proved for the actual morphism; flatness of the source alone is not such a criterion
  (Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, Part II, Chapter 1, and SGA 3 guide this proof). `U` and `U⁻` are the closed subgroup
  schemes whose points are the unique products of C3, so they are isomorphic to affine space of
  dimension the number of positive roots.

  For `G_sc(t)` the same open set is cut out by the product of the highest-weight matrix
  coefficients `g ↦ ⟨v⁺_i*, g v⁺_i⟩` of the fundamental summands. That formula is specific to
  `G_sc(t)` and is not used for a general datum: on `SL₂` the coefficient is the entry `a`, and
  `g ↦ -g` changes its sign, so it does not descend to `PGL₂`. The block minors above are
  polynomials in the matrix entries of `GLₙ` for every datum, so no descent is needed.
- **Fibres.** `G_D` is covered by the translates of the big cell by the Weyl representatives,
  and is smooth over `ℤ` with geometrically connected fibres of dimension `t.rank + t.numRoots`.
- **Points.** For every field `k`, every point over `k` lies in some translate `n_w Ω_D(k)` of the
  big cell, and `Ω_D(k) = U⁻(k) T_D(k) U(k)`; hence the points over `k` are `E(k)`, generated by
  root subgroups and `T_D(k) = Hom(Λ(D), kˣ)`. For adjoint `A₁` over `ℚ` this is `PGL₂(ℚ)`. For
  `G_sc(t)` they are generated by root subgroups alone: `ChevalleyGroup t ht k = E(k)` for every
  field `k`. The base change of the group scheme to a field `k` equals the closed subgroup scheme
  of `GLₙ` over `k` generated by the reduced root subgroups and torus.
- **Points of the adjoint form over an algebraically closed field.** The pinned Geck carrier
  `TauCeti.DynkinType.geckPoints`, the points of `DynkinType.adjointGroupScheme`, has root
  subgroups `TauCeti.DynkinType.geckRootSubgroupPoints` only for the simple roots and their
  negatives. Prove `closure_geckRootSubgroupPoints_eq_top`: for every valid `t` and every
  algebraically closed field `k`, these subgroups generate all of `geckPoints t ht k`. Over an
  algebraically closed field the restriction `Hom(P, kˣ) → Hom(Q, kˣ)` is surjective because `kˣ`
  is divisible, so the full-weight parametrization `TauCeti.DynkinType.geckWeightTorusPoints`
  reaches every torus point; the torus is generated by the `h_{α_i}(s)`, the other root subgroups
  are conjugates of the simple ones by the Weyl representatives `n_{α_i}(1)`, and the previous item
  finishes. For `E₈`, `F₄` and `G₂` the Geck weights span the full weight lattice, so this is also
  the statement for `G_sc(t)`.

  **Checks.**
  - Adjoint `A₁` over `𝔽̄_p`: the points are `PGL₂(𝔽̄_p)`, and the images of the upper and lower
    unipotent matrices generate it, since `SL₂(𝔽̄_p) → PGL₂(𝔽̄_p)` is surjective (every determinant
    is a square). A statement without the algebraic closure fails over `ℚ`: the class of
    `diag(2, 1)` in `PGL₂(ℚ)` is not in the image of `SL₂(ℚ)`.
  - Over `𝔽₂` in type `B₂`, the torus and the simple positive root subgroups generate a group
    generated by two involutions modulo a trivial torus, hence dihedral, while the unipotent radical
    of `Sp₄(𝔽₂) ≅ S₆` has order 16 and is not dihedral. So the subgroup generated by the simple
    positive root subgroups is not the Borel subgroup over small fields, and the theorem uses
    positive and negative simple root subgroups together.

### C5: endomorphisms and their character maps

Work on `DynkinType.ChevalleyGroup t ht k` for a field `k`, which is `E(k)` by C4. Write
`torus s = ∏ h_{α_i}(s_i)` for `s : Fin t.rank → kˣ`, and `χ(s) = ∏ s_i ^ χ_i` for a character
`χ : Fin t.rank → ℤ` in fundamental-weight coordinates, so `χ(torus s) = χ(s)`; define `charEval χ s`
as this product, for `s` with values in any commutative group. The items below are about
`G_sc(t)`, except the three that name the adjoint form `TauCeti.DynkinType.geckPoints`: the
predicate `IsCharacterMap` with the torus parametrization
`TauCeti.DynkinType.geckWeightTorusPoints`, which is indexed the same way and is not injective in
general, its kernel being `Hom(P/Q, kˣ)`; `exists_specialIsogeny`; and
`exists_geckWeightTorusPoints_eq_mul_inv`, the last two over an algebraically closed field. They do
not extend to the adjoint points over an arbitrary field, where the torus `T_D(k) = Hom(Q, kˣ)` of C2
is larger than the image of that parametrization and is not generated by root subgroups.

**Character maps are data.** An abstract endomorphism of `ChevalleyGroup t ht k` that maps the torus
into itself need not act on it through characters, even over an algebraically closed field.
Complex conjugation, applied entrywise to `SL₂(ℂ)`, preserves the diagonal torus and every root
subgroup, and acts on the torus coordinate by `z ↦ z̄`. If that were `z ↦ z^m`, `z = 2` would force
`m = 1` and `z = i` would contradict it. The same happens for the ambient groups the CFSG roadmap
uses: `Gal(𝔽̄_p / 𝔽_p) ≅ Ẑ`, and an element of `Ẑ` outside `ℤ` gives an automorphism of
`𝔽̄_pˣ` that is not an integer power. The integer-matrix theorem is about morphisms of split tori as
group schemes (Conrad, *Reductive group schemes*, proof of Theorem 1.1.19), not about homomorphisms
of their groups of points. So a character map is supplied with `F` and checked.

Define, over every field `k`, for a group `G` with a torus parametrization
`T : (Fin r → kˣ) →* G`, an endomorphism `F` of `G` and `φ : AddMonoid.End (Fin r → ℤ)`, the
predicate

```text
IsCharacterMap T F φ  :↔  ∀ s, F (T s) = T (fun i => charEval (φ (Pi.single i 1)) s),
```

used with `T = torus` on `G_sc(t)` and `T = geckWeightTorusPoints` on the adjoint form. Equivalently
`χ(F (torus s)) = (φ χ)(s)` for every character `χ`, which is the pullback `χ ↦ χ ∘ F`. Prove:

- **Composition.** `IsCharacterMap T F φ → IsCharacterMap T G ψ → IsCharacterMap T (F ∘ G) (ψ ∘ φ)`.
- **Uniqueness over an infinite field.** If `k` is infinite, `IsCharacterMap torus F φ` and
  `IsCharacterMap torus F φ'` give `φ = φ'`, since distinct characters are distinct functions on
  `(kˣ)^{rank}`. Over a finite field `φ` is not determined by `F`, which is why it is data rather
  than a function of `F`.
- **Surjectivity on the torus.** If `k` is algebraically closed and `φ` is injective, `F` maps the
  torus onto itself. `kˣ` is divisible, hence an injective `ℤ`-module, so the dual of an injective
  `φ` is surjective on `Hom(Fin t.rank → ℤ, kˣ)`.

Each of the three families below comes with its character map and a proof of `IsCharacterMap`,
computed from its action on the root subgroups through `h_α(s) = n_α(s) n_α(1)⁻¹`. None of them
uses C7.

- **Field maps.** A field endomorphism `φ` of `k` induces an endomorphism of `ChevalleyGroup t ht k`
  by functoriality, with `φ (x_α(u)) = x_α(φ u)` for every root. Such a map has no character map
  in general, and none is asserted. The `q`-power Frobenius over a field of characteristic `p`
  satisfies `IsCharacterMap torus Frob_q (q • id)`, since `Frob_q (torus s) = torus (s ^ q)`.
- **Graph automorphisms.** For `σ` in `DynkinType.diagramSymmetry t`, the automorphism
  `DynkinType.chevalleyGraphAut σ` of `G_sc(t)` induced by the numbered symmetry `θ_σ` of C1,
  with `γ_σ (x_{±α_i}(u)) = x_{±α_{σ i}}(u)` on the positive and negative simple roots and
  `γ_σ (x_α(u)) = x_{σ α}(ε_{σ,α} u)` with signs `ε_{σ,α} = ±1` on every root, the signs computed
  from the structure constants of C0 (Steinberg, *Lectures*, Chapter 10, Theorem 29);
  `γ_σ γ_τ = γ_{στ}`; `γ_σ` commutes with every field map; and
  `IsCharacterMap torus γ_σ (DynkinType.diagramAut σ)⁻¹.weightMap`, from
  `γ_σ (h_{α_i}(s)) = h_{α_{σ i}}(s)`. The inverse is the orientation fixed in the standing
  conventions.
- **Exceptional isogenies.** For `(t, p)` one of `(B₂, 2)`, `(F₄, 2)`, `(G₂, 3)` and `k` of
  characteristic `p`, the endomorphism `DynkinType.chevalleySpecialIsogeny` of `E(k)` with
  `τ (x_α(u)) = x_{ᾱ}(ε_α u^{q(α)})`, where `ᾱ` is the image of `α` under the length-exchanging map
  of root systems, `q(α)` is `1` for `α` long and `p` for `α` short, and `ε_α = ±1`. Define it from

  simple root subgroups in the convention above, and `IsCharacterMap torus τ φ_X` for `φ_X` the weight

  `DynkinType.g2SpecialIsogeny` respectively. The proof is the computation
  `τ (h_{α_i}(s)) = h_{ᾱ_i}(s ^ {q(α_i)})`, read from the images of `n_{α_i}(s)`, and then the
  comparison of the resulting integer matrix with that weight map.

  On the adjoint form, prove `exists_specialIsogeny`: for `(t, p)` as above, `σ` with
  `TauCeti.DynkinType.IsSpecialNodePerm t σ`, and `k` algebraically closed of characteristic `p`,
  there is an endomorphism `τ` of `geckPoints t ht k` with `τ ∘ τ` equal to
  `TauCeti.DynkinType.geckFrobenius t ht p 1 k` and, for every `i`, signs `ε₊, ε₋ = ±1` with

  The exponents are forced and are not a free convention. Write `α` long and `β` short in `B₂`,
  so `⟨α, β^∨⟩ = -2` and `⟨β, α^∨⟩ = -1`. Applying `τ` to

- **Determination by simple root subgroups.** For a Chevalley datum `D` and a field `k`, two
  homomorphisms from `E(k)` to a group that agree on the positive and negative simple root
  subgroups and on `T_D(k)` are equal: the `n_{α_i}(1) = x_{α_i}(1) x_{-α_i}(-1) x_{α_i}(1)` lie in
  the subgroup generated by the simple root subgroups, every root is a Weyl conjugate of a simple
  one, and `x_α(u) = n_w x_{α_i}(± u) n_w⁻¹` by C2. Agreement on the simple root subgroups alone

  in the first case `T(k)` is generated by the `h_{α_i}(s)` (C2), in the second the restriction
  `Hom(P, kˣ) → Hom(Λ(D), kˣ)` is surjective because `kˣ` is divisible, and its image is generated
  by the `h_{α_i}(s)`. With the presentation, this gives the uniqueness that pins `γ_σ` and `τ` by
  their simple-root equations.

  **Checks.**
  - Adjoint `A₁` over `ℚ`, `E(ℚ) = PGL₂(ℚ)`: `δ([A]) = v₂(det A) mod 2` is a well-defined

    full-weight parametrization, and differ at `[diag(2, 1)] ∈ T_D(ℚ)`. So without the torus

    not repair it.

    consistent

  injective `φ` satisfying `IsCharacterMap torus F φ` is *standard* if it maps each root subgroup onto a

  to sign. It determines the sign too: if a second standard map with the same `φ` sent `x_α` into
  `x_{-β}`, its field endomorphism `g'` would satisfy `g g' = 1` on `kˣ`, and expanding

  most two values there, contradicting injectivity of `g` on the infinite field `k`. So the root
  permutation of a standard map, and the field endomorphisms on its root subgroups, are read from
  `φ`.

  `F² = Frob_{p²}` because `n²` is central. `IsCharacterMap torus F (-p • id)` holds, so `F` is standard

  scaling, and a normal form for such isogenies holds only for based ones, those preserving the
  positive system.

  for a torus point `s`. By the previous item, they send `x_{±α_i}(u)` to
  `x_{±β_i}(c_{±i} g_{±i}(u))` and `x_{±β_i}(c'_{±i} g_{±i}(u))`, with `β_i` and the field

  injective, and `kˣ` is divisible, so there is `s` with
  `β_i(s) = c_i / c'_i` for all `i`. `F` and `F'` map the torus onto itself (surjectivity above),

  algebraically closed and `IsCharacterMap torus F' φ` with `φ ^ n = p ^ r • id` for some `n, r > 0`,

  complex eigenvalue of `φ` has absolute value `p ^ (r / n) > 1` when `p > 0`, and `φ` is nilpotent

  adjoint form as `exists_geckWeightTorusPoints_eq_mul_inv`: for `k` algebraically closed of
