F8 specializes that scalar-valued functional to `tr_N`, including fixed points, instead of introducing another generic cycle-product API. |

For F8's expected empirical measures consume RandomMatrices Milestone 1's
`empiricalMeasure`/`spectralMeasure` and decreasing Hermitian eigenvalues.
Prove its trace-moment dictionary and measurability comparison with the
all-moments quotient. Moment-to-weak convergence uses Milestone 3's common
law interface; it does not imply an almost-sure or operator-norm conclusion.

## F1. Distributions, moments, and free independence

Develop normalized expectations, positivity, traces, restriction to
subalgebras, state-preserving homomorphisms and transport. For each
introduced distribution give extensionality by words, identity/composition
and relabeling maps, subfamilies, adjoints and substitutions of polynomials.
Prove joint distributions determine every polynomial moment, and equality
of *-distributions is preserved by *-polynomial evaluation. Construct the
GNS realization of a positive normalized *-distribution, distinguishing an
algebraic pre-Hilbert representation from a bounded C*-representation.
For bounded realization fix R_i≥0 and require
`φ(p*X_i*X_i p)≤R_i²φ(p*p)` for every *-polynomial p, with the
analogous adjoint-generator inequalities. Prove these give bounded left
multiplication and its adjoint, with norm at most R_i, and characterize
bounded GNS realizations by these inequalities. Prove a uniform exponential
bound `|φ(w)|≤R^length(w)` on all generator/adjoint words implies the
corresponding bounds through iterated Cauchy–Schwarz. Positivity alone is
not a boundedness theorem.

For a bounded selfadjoint a in a C*-probability space, construct its law μ_a
as the probability measure on ℝ supported in spectrum(a), characterized by
`φ(f(a))=∫ f dμ_a` for continuous f on that spectrum. Prove uniqueness,
`m_n(μ_a)=φ(a^n)`, positivity, compact support, affine pushforwards and
polynomial functional-calculus pushforwards. Compare the CFC construction
with integration of the scalar spectral measure in a GNS representation.
Show every compactly supported probability measure has a bounded
commutative realization. Consume Tau Ceti's
`Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_monomial_eq_of_support` from
`Probability.Moments.CompactDeterminacy` for moment determinacy, and prove
its compatibility with these CFC laws. Define convergence in distribution as convergence of every
word moment, with convergence in *-distribution testing adjoints too.
For scalar laws prove the moment-to-weak-convergence implications used in
F6, using tightness and uniform integrability from higher moments; the
approximating supports need not fit in one fixed compact set.

Unital subalgebras `(A_i)` are free with respect to φ when
`φ(a_1⋯a_n)=0` for every nonempty centered word with
`a_j∈A_(i_j)` and `i_j≠i_(j+1)`. Nonadjacent labels may coincide.
Variables are free when the unital algebras they generate are free;
*-freeness uses the unital *-algebras generated by variables and adjoints.
Develop subfamily, reindexing, restriction, generated-algebra, grouping of
disjoint index sets, and state-preserving image lemmas. Prove multilinear
expansion reduces general moments to centered alternating words, yielding
uniqueness of the joint distribution from factor distributions and freeness.
Include first mixed moment factorization, centered polynomial tests, and
compatibility with norm closure in C*-probability spaces and weak closure
in the tracial von Neumann setting.

Distinguish classical independence of commuting algebras from freeness.
For free variables compute mixed moments that demonstrate the distinction,
including fourth moments of two free centered variance-one semicirculars.
Prove constants form a free family with any other family, and handle empty
families and empty words explicitly. For positive states obtain the
covariance/orthogonality statements used in reduced Hilbert products.
Do not infer positivity of an arbitrary algebraic free-product functional
without the realization in F3.

## F2. Noncrossing partitions and free cumulants

Represent partitions of n ordered positions using
`Finpartition (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))`. A partition is noncrossing
when distinct blocks never contain four positions a<b<c<d with a,c in
one and b,d in the other. Develop decidability, finite enumeration,
restriction and increasing relabeling, intervals, block extraction,
singleton insertion/deletion, rotation and concatenation. Equip NC(n)
with refinement order: discrete is bottom, one block is top for n>0,
and NC(0) consists of the empty partition. Prove it is a lattice;
meet is ordinary common refinement, while join is least noncrossing
coarsening and need not equal join in the full partition lattice.
Construct joins and prove their universal property and interval APIs.

Prove `card NC(n)=catalan n`, the Catalan enumeration of noncrossing
pair partitions of 2n, and the recurrences by the block containing the
first position. Develop the correspondence with plane trees and the
permutation model: blocks are cycles in their increasing cyclic order.
Prove the transposition-length/geodesic characterization, cycle-count
formulas, and the noncrossing-pairing criterion used in F8's genus bound.
Construct Kreweras complement on the interlaced positions
`1,bar1,2,bar2,…`, as the largest complementary noncrossing partition.
Prove existence, uniqueness, order reversal, bijectivity, its square's
rotation formula, and `#blocks(π)+#blocks(Kπ)=n+1` for n≥1; both block counts are zero
at n=0. Permutations compose with the rightmost map acting first; for
γ=(1 … n) prove `p_(Kπ)=p_π⁻¹γ`, so K² relabels by γ⁻¹.
Prove the corresponding cycle formulas rather than identifying differently
oriented complements by notation alone.

Use `IncidenceAlgebra.zeta` and `.mu` on the finite NC posets. Prove
interval factorization into products of smaller NC lattices, Möbius
multiplicativity, and `μ(0_n,1_n)=(-1)^(n−1)catalan(n−1)` for n≥1.
Supply the corresponding blockwise formula and both inversion directions;
this Möbius function is distinct from number-theoretic Möbius inversion.
Prove the interval-partition embedding and partial-inversion identities
needed for grouped arguments.

For a word a_1,…,a_n define its block moment φ_π by multiplying scalar
moments of each block, keeping arguments within a block in increasing
order. Define `κ_π=Σ_(σ≤π) φ_σ μ(σ,π)` by Möbius inversion on NC(n),
put `κ_n=κ_(1_n)` for n≥1, and prove κ_π is the product of its block
cumulants. Establish both directions of

```
φ(a_1⋯a_n) = Σ_(π∈NC(n)) κ_π(a_1,…,a_n)
κ_n(a_1,…,a_n) = Σ_(π∈NC(n)) μ(π,1_n) φ_π(a_1,…,a_n).
```

Develop multilinearity, scalar/adjoint transport, vanishing when one input
is 1 for n≥2, centering invariance for n≥2, cyclic invariance for traces,
and complex conjugation with reversed adjoints for *-states. Compute the
first four cumulants and moments with repeated and distinct arguments.
Prove the grouped-product formula: cumulants of products of consecutive
arguments are sums over π with `π∨intervalPartition=liftedPartition`,
including the lift and its compatibility with block restrictions.

Prove subalgebras are free iff every mixed cumulant of order n≥2 vanishes
whenever its labels are not all equal. Give both proofs from the centered
word criterion and grouped-product formula, and expose the generated-
algebra tests. Deduce additivity of cumulants for sums of free families.
For two free families `(a_j)` and `(b_j)`, prove

```
κ_n(a_1b_1,…,a_nb_n) = Σ_(π∈NC(n)) κ_π(a_1,…,a_n) κ_(Kπ)(b_1,…,b_n)
φ(a_1b_1⋯a_nb_n) = Σ_(π∈NC(n)) κ_π(a_1,…,a_n) φ_(Kπ)(b_1,…,b_n).
```

These identities do not require a trace. Prove them by odd/even-position
partitions and the chosen Kreweras convention; include n=1 separately
from the empty-word identity.

## F3. Hilbert free products, Fock space, and operator algebras

Use Mathlib's `LinearAlgebra.FreeProduct ℂ A` and `lift` for the
algebraic unital free product of a set-indexed family of complex algebras;
construct its compatible star structure, its reduced-word linear decomposition after a chosen
splitting by normalized functionals, and its universal property. For
nontrivial unital C*-algebras construct the full unital C*-free product by
the universal C*-seminorm. Control its universe by cyclic representations
of density at most `κ=max(aleph0,Σ_i |A_i|,|I|)` and carrier cardinality
at most κ^aleph0, using a fixed universe/model family. Prove the supremum
agrees with representations in arbitrary larger universes, finiteness on
each word, completeness, and the universal property for unital
*-homomorphisms. For arbitrary pointed factor representations prove
`kerλ_i=kerπ_i`; use V0's faithful representation with a chosen unit vector
to prove factor embeddings. A faithful state is not needed on each A_i.
The empty product is ℂ. Supply relabeling, grouping and universal maps;
a reduced product is a different completion, specified by input states.

For pointed Hilbert spaces `(H_i,ξ_i)` with unit vectors, put
`H_i°=H_i⊖ℂξ_i` and construct

```
H = ℂΩ ⊕ ⊕_(n≥1, i_j≠i_(j+1)) H_(i_1)° ⊗⋯⊗ H_(i_n)°.
```

Give inclusions, word projections, dense finite tensors, and canonical
unitaries `H_i⊗H(i)≅H`, where H(i) has vacuum and words not starting in i.
Construct the left representations λ_i and right representations with
reversed-word convention, and prove their adjoint, norm, unit, multiplication
and commutation identities. For GNS inputs prove the vacuum state on the
full product is positive, restricts to each factor and makes them free.
The reduced C*-product is the norm-closed algebra generated by the λ_i.
Prove its GNS space is the constructed H, and its factor representations
have exactly the kernels of the input GNS representations. State
faithfulness of an input state separately from faithfulness of its GNS
representation. Characterize the latter kernel by
`a∈kerπ_φ ↔ ∀b, φ(b*a*ab)=0`.

Develop expectation-preserving identifications, regrouping of free
products, and the quotient map from full to reduced. Prove the reduced
vacuum state is faithful when the input states are faithful, proving
separation on the reduced C*-algebra by the shortest-word compression
argument. Remove factors equal to ℂ before applying the nontrivial-factor
form of that argument; if only their GNS representations are faithful, prove the factor maps
injective. The vacuum state need not be faithful, as a pure M₂ state
in the one-factor case shows. Prove tracial inputs
give a trace, and construct the conditional expectations onto factors
and subproducts, with their bimodule, positivity and norm properties.
Give the full-versus-reduced example from two copies of C(𝕋) with Haar
states: using `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`, their full and reduced products are
respectively C*(F₂) and C*_r(F₂). Prove the quotient is not injective:
on ℓ²(F₂) the adjacency sum of the four standard generators/inverses has
norm 2sqrt3, while the full trivial character sends it to 4. Consume
OperatorKTheory K7.FreeGroups' early shared reduced-word/path/acyclicity
interface on the native `SimpleGraph.mulCayley` carrier, identified at
n=2 with this four-regular word model. Construct the end-oriented shift
for the upper norm bound and finitely supported radial vectors for the
matching lower bound. This use is before K7's Julg–Valette, free-group PV,
and Toeplitz–Cuntz constructions; none of those analytic/K-theoretic results
is a prerequisite for the tree interface. Thus the trivial character cannot factor through the reduced
algebra, proving the full/reduced distinction directly.

For von Neumann algebras with faithful normal states construct the weak
closure of the left copies, prove their normality, and construct its
faithful normal free-product state. Prove the commutant theorem using the
right copies of the factor commutants and their cyclic vectors. Compute
Tomita conjugation on reduced words, reversing order and applying factor
conjugations, and the modular operator/action using the factor modular
data. For trace inputs prove Δ=1 and the free-product vector is cyclic,
separating and tracial. Identify group von Neumann free products with
`L(Monoid.CoprodI G)` and their canonical traces. Include the representation and
expectation compatibility between C*-reduced products and weak closures.

Construct full Fock space `𝓕(H)=ℂΩ⊕⊕_(n≥1) H^(⊗n)` from completed
Hilbert tensors and ℓ² sums. Define creation ℓ(h), annihilation ℓ(h)*,
and gauge Λ(T), with Λ(T)Ω=0 and T acting on the first tensor factor.
Prove boundedness, `‖ℓ(h)‖=‖h‖`, `‖Λ(T)‖=‖T‖` when H≠0,
linearity/adjoints and the vacuum formulas. For an orthonormal basis give
the creation isometries, orthogonal range projections and strong sum
`Σℓ(e_i)ℓ(e_i)*=1−P_Ω`. Compare finite-rank Fock representations with
K7's Toeplitz–Cuntz algebra, compact vacuum ideal and quotient O_n;
for countably infinite rank prove `O∞→C*(ℓ(e_i))` is an isomorphism,
using K7's faithful finite-stage representations and the nonzero vacuum
complement `1−Σ_(i≤n) ℓ(e_i)ℓ(e_i)*`. Keep vacuum
states on creation algebras distinct from their traces on Gaussian algebras.

For a real Hilbert space H construct its Hilbert complexification,
with its isometric real inclusion, complex inner product and completeness,
and put `s(h)=ℓ(h)+ℓ(h)*`. Prove the vacuum Wick formula over noncrossing pairings,
variance `‖h‖²` and freeness for orthogonal subspaces; F6 identifies
these moments with its explicit semicircle measure.
For `Γ(H)={s(h):h∈H}''` prove the vacuum state is faithful normal tracial.
Construct second quantization for real contractions as
normal unital completely positive trace-preserving maps, with identity,
composition, isometry-induced embeddings and projection-induced conditional
expectations. Prove the reduced-word/tensor implementation and agreement
with orthogonal direct sums and free products.

## F4. Amalgamated freeness and reduced products

For unital inclusions B⊆A_i and conditional expectations E_i:A_i→B,
define a C*-conditional expectation as a unital positive B-bimodule
projection onto B. Develop its norm-one/idempotence properties and prove
complete positivity from the positive matrix `[E(a_i*a_j)]`, testing its
B-valued quadratic form `E((Σa_i b_i)*(Σa_j b_j))`. Use the existing
`CompletelyPositiveMap` (`→CP`) for its CP view.
Construct the algebraic free product over B and its universal property,
without confusing its universal maps with those of a reduced product.
Define B-valued freeness by vanishing of E on centered alternating words.
Develop B-balanced moments, regrouping, restrictions, and uniqueness of
E on the algebraic product from its factor expectations. Prove positivity
and complete positivity through the represented construction below.

Construct `L²(A_i,E_i)` by its B-valued inner product `E_i(a*b)`, null
quotient and completion. Prove left multiplication bounded and adjointable
with adjoint multiplication by a*, and identify the orthogonal decomposition
`L²(A_i,E_i)=B⊕L²(A_i,E_i)°` given by E_i. The left GNS representation
is faithful iff every nonzero a∈A_i has b with `E_i(b*a*ab)≠0`.
Faithful expectation implies this condition; the converse need not hold.
Construct the right Hilbert B-module

```
𝓔 = B ⊕ ⊕_(n≥1, i_j≠i_(j+1))
           L²(A_(i_1),E_(i_1))° ⊗_B⋯⊗_B L²(A_(i_n),E_(i_n))°.
```

Use interior tensors, including the left B-actions. Construct the λ_i by
prefix/deletion formulas and canonical module unitaries, and prove their
boundedness, adjoints and agreement on B. The reduced amalgamated product
is their generated norm-closed algebra, with
`E(T)=⟨1_B,T1_B⟩_B`. Prove E is a unital completely positive conditional
expectation, its restrictions are E_i, and the copies are free over B.
Prove factor embeddings under the stated GNS-faithfulness hypothesis,
the reduced-word density and the module-GNS comparison. Establish uniqueness
by an expectation-preserving isomorphism of represented products, and
associativity/regrouping with all intermediate expectations specified.

Develop expectation-preserving factor embeddings into other systems with
the same B, assuming both source and target expectations have faithful
GNS representations, and prove the induced reduced-product embedding.
Give the obstruction without source GNS faithfulness: A=ℂ⊕ℂ with
E(z,w)=z embeds diagonally into M₂ with ψ(x)=x₁₁, preserving
expectation, but the reduced source kills (0,1) while the target GNS
representation retains its nonzero diagonal image. Retain a pure M₂
vector state as a positive control for faithful GNS representation
without a faithful state. Prove the
free product of B-bimodule unital completely positive maps that fix B and
preserve the expectations exists, assuming both source and target
expectations have faithful GNS representations. Give its word formula,
complete positivity,
composition and restriction properties. Consume the unital specialization
of [OperatorKTheory K4](../OperatorKTheory/README.md)'s Hilbert-module
Kasparov–Stinespring dilation for these CP maps; the strictness condition
is automatic for a unital domain. This early dilation layer precedes
extension invertibility. F4 supplies the free-product assembly and its
word identities. Construct conditional expectations onto factors/subproducts
as cases of this construction. State and prove
faithfulness of the product expectation when all E_i are faithful,
separately from faithful GNS representations. Remove factors equal to B
before the nontrivial-factor compression proof; the zero/one-factor cases
have their direct identifications: the zero-factor product is B;
the one-factor product is the image in the expectation-GNS representation,
equal to the original algebra when that representation is faithful.
For arbitrary inputs put `Ā_i=λ_i(A_i)` and prove that E_i descends to
a conditional expectation `Ē_i:Ā_i→B`, with `Ē_i(λ_i(a))=E_i(a)`.
Identify its expectation-GNS module and represented free product with
the ones already constructed. Prove that E is faithful iff every Ē_i
is faithful: restriction gives necessity on these actual subalgebras,
and the faithful-input theorem gives sufficiency. When each λ_i is
injective, in particular under the stated GNS-faithfulness hypothesis,
this is equivalent to faithfulness of every original E_i. Include the
one-factor example `A=ℂ⊕ℂ`, `B=ℂ1`, `E_i(z,w)=z`: its represented
product is ℂ with faithful identity expectation, although E_i is not
faithful. This demonstrates why restriction to the original A_i
requires injective factor maps.
Do not give the reduced product the unrestricted categorical universal
property of the full product.

For finite von Neumann algebras `(M_i,τ_i)` with faithful normal tracial
states and a common unital von Neumann subalgebra B on which their traces
agree, consume NoncommutativeIntegration I4's faithful normal
trace-preserving E_i. Prove the trivial modular-flow specialization,
uniqueness, and identification with the L² projection onto L²(B,τ).
This supplier applies to arbitrary finite algebras and subalgebras, not
only II₁ factors. Construct their tracial amalgamated
von Neumann product on the scalar Hilbert completion of 𝓔, using L²(B,τ).
Prove the factor embeddings normal, the vacuum trace faithful normal,
and the B-valued expectation faithful normal and trace preserving.
Prove the normal state/expectation-preserving uniqueness, regrouping,
commuting left/right representation formulas and density of reduced words
in L². Construct the orthogonal reduced-word decomposition of L²(M),
its B-bimodule actions and tensor associators. Normality must be proved
from the bounded and L² interfaces, not from algebraic freeness alone.

Include B=ℂ as the scalar product, one factor as its original algebra,
and products of group algebras amalgamated over a common subgroup, with
Fourier-coefficient expectations and the trace-preserving identification
with `Monoid.PushoutI`, using its reduced-word/group universal property. Supply the reduced group-word and
Hilbert tensor identifications. The finite-factor and rigidity properties
of these algebras have their separate owning roadmaps.

## F5. Free convolution, formal series, and scalar transforms

For compactly supported μ,ν on ℝ realize free bounded selfadjoint a,b
and define μ⊞ν as the law of a+b. Prove independence of realization
from F1's uniqueness, associativity, commutativity, δ₀ identity, affine
pushforward laws and support bounds. Develop finite convolution powers,
convolution of freely independent families and transport through their
C*- and von Neumann realizations. Prove cumulants add and expose the corresponding convolution-power APIs.

For a normalized algebraic expectation define moments M(z), cumulant
series C(z) and the shifted law R(z) by

```
M(z)=1+Σ_(n≥1)m_n z^n,
C(z)=1+Σ_(n≥1)κ_n z^n=1+zR(z),
M(z)=C(zM(z))=1+zM(z)R(zM(z)).
```

Use the existing formal `PowerSeries.subst`, `HasSubst` and
`substInvOfIsUnit` APIs for composition and compositional inversion.
Prove the moment/cumulant coefficient, zero-constant and unit-linear
coefficient hypotheses on these objects, and their transport interfaces;
reuse the existing inverse identities and uniqueness. Prove the displayed identities
coefficient by coefficient from the block containing the first position.
Prove exponential cumulant bounds for compactly supported measures and
convergence of their series on a disk. Use `G_μ=−MeasureTheory.resolventTransform μ`, since the native integrand
is `(t−z)⁻¹`. Consume its `analyticOn_resolventTransform` theorem and
prove the sign/conjugation,
sign of imaginary part, normalization at infinity and moment expansion.
Use the local inverse of `w↦G_μ(1/w)` near zero to construct
`K_μ(w)=1/w+R_μ(w)`. Prove the local inverse identities and equality
with the formal series; do not claim G is globally injective.
Establish `R_(μ⊞ν)=R_μ+R_ν` in both senses on their common domain.
Give a scalar Stieltjes-inversion API recovering measures from G, with
integrals over intervals and atom limits; expose density and atom recovery
for the law computations in F6. Distinguish endpoints with atoms
when taking interval limits.

Construct multivariable noncommutative formal series on words in
`FreeMonoid ι`: coefficients are functions on words, product sums over
word decompositions, and the constant coefficient is separated explicitly.
Give unit, associativity, degree filtration, and substitution for finite
index types by series with zero constant coefficient; prove coefficient
extensionality, and the one-variable `PowerSeries` comparison.
The joint degree-n R-coefficient is κ_n; prove that freeness is equivalent
to the absence of mixed coefficients between the specified free families.
A commutative `MvPowerSeries` cannot replace this word-indexed series.

Define boxed convolution by the NC/Kreweras coefficient sum. Prove its
associativity, its unit and inverse construction when the degree-one
coefficients are units, and its identification with joint cumulants of
products of two free families. The one-variable operation is commutative;
no such assertion is imposed in multiple variables. Expose moment/zeta,
cumulant/Möbius and grouped-argument formulas as compatible operations.

For an algebraic variable with m₁≠0 put Ψ(z)=M(z)−1 and define

```
S(z)=(1+z) Ψ^⟨−1⟩(z)/z.
```

Division by z removes a proven zero constant coefficient. Prove this
agrees with `C₀^⟨−1⟩(z)/z`, where `C₀(z)=zR(z)`, and prove the
one-variable boxed-convolution/S-series group isomorphism. Deduce
`S_(ab)=S_a S_b` for free a,b with nonzero means, with no trace hypothesis
for this algebraic moment identity. Compute constant laws, retaining the
nonzero-mean condition; F6 computes
the transforms of its Poisson and compound laws.
For compactly supported μ,ν supported in [0,∞), define μ⊠ν as the law of
`a^(1/2)b a^(1/2)` in a tracial free realization. Prove its independence,
associativity, commutativity, δ₁ identity and δ₀ absorbing law; prove
its moments equal those of ab and its S-transform is the product when
both means are nonzero. A positive compact law of mean zero is δ₀,
so handle that case through the absorbing law rather than defining an
inverse transform with zero linear coefficient.

## F6. Semicircular laws and free limit theorems

Construct the centered semicircle probability measure of variance σ²≥0:
for σ>0 its density is
`(2πσ²)⁻¹ sqrt(4σ²−t²)` on `[−2σ,2σ]`, and at σ=0 it is δ₀.
Prove normalization, symmetry, support, odd moments zero and
`m_(2n)=catalan(n) σ^(2n)`. Its only nonzero cumulant is κ₂=σ².
Prove equivalence of this law, its cumulants and the Fock realization,
including shifts and rescaling. Prove the one-dimensional Gaussian von
Neumann algebra is L(ℤ) by CDF transport from its atomless semicircle spectral measure to
Lebesgue probability on [0,1], then circle Haar probability and V8's
L(ℤ) Fourier model; prove the measure-algebra/L∞ and generator maps.
Using F3's free-product decomposition, identify Γ(H) with the group algebra
of the free group on an orthonormal basis, including zero rank ℂ, rank one
L(ℤ), and the II₁ factor for rank at least two. Define semicircular systems by joint
cumulants: only κ₂ survives, with the specified covariance matrix.
Prove realization for every positive semidefinite real covariance matrix,
change of real coordinates, and the equivalence of orthogonality and
freeness for the centered system. Semicircularity of each variable alone
does not specify a free semicircular system.

Prove the free central limit theorem for freely independent identically
distributed centered selfadjoint variables of variance σ²: the normalized
sum `N⁻¹ᐟ² Σ_(j=1)^N a_j` has moments converging to the semicircle law.
Give the noncrossing pairing proof and the cumulant proof, and their
agreement. Extend to freely independent centered variables satisfying
`sup_j |φ(a_j^k)|<∞` for every positive integer k and
`N⁻¹ Σ_(j=1)^N φ(a_j²)→σ²`. Prove the needed uniform cumulant bounds;
no identical-distribution hypothesis is imposed in this extension.
For C*-realizations deduce weak convergence of the scalar laws by F1's
moment/tightness interface. Also prove the free law of large numbers:
for freely independent identically distributed selfadjoint variables, their
averages converge in moments and the state's GNS L² norm to their mean. Prove the exact
squared L² error is κ₂(a)/N; no trace is needed for that assertion.
These conclusions do not assert operator-norm convergence.

Construct the free Poisson law with rate λ≥0 and jump α∈ℝ by
`κ_n=λα^n`. For jump 1 and λ>0 let
`a=(1−sqrt λ)²`, `b=(1+sqrt λ)²`; prove the measure is

```
max(1−λ,0) δ₀ + 1_[a,b](t) sqrt((b−t)(t−a))/(2πt) dt.
```

Define the density at t=0 by any fixed value and prove the formula as an
a.e. density, including its integrable endpoint singularity at λ=1.
For general jump use pushforward by t↦αt; negative jumps reverse interval
orientation, and λ=0 or α=0 gives δ₀. Prove positivity, total mass,
support, moments and cumulants. Prove the free Poisson limit theorem:
for N large enough that λ/N≤1, the N-fold free convolution of
`(1−λ/N)δ₀+(λ/N)δ_α` converges in moments and weakly to this law.
Give its first-order cumulant expansion and the moment bounds for the
measure conclusion. Identify s² for a semicircular s of variance σ²
as rate 1, jump σ² free Poisson.

For compactly supported ν and λ≥0 construct the compound free Poisson
law with `κ_n=λ∫t^n dν(t)`, by the analogous free rare-event limit.
Give its positivity, compact-support bound, uniqueness, λ-addition
semigroup, jump pushforwards and its transform formulas on F5's native
series, including
`R(z)=λ∫t/(1−tz)dν(t)` and, when the mean is nonzero, the S-series. Include
δ₀ and degenerate jumps rather than assuming a nonzero mean.

Within compactly supported laws define free infinite divisibility by
existence of compactly supported additive free convolution roots of every
positive integer order. Prove the free Lévy–Khintchine criterion: μ is
freely infinitely divisible iff its real cumulants are conditionally
positive, meaning
`Σ_(i,j=1)^r conjugate(c_i)c_j κ_(i+j)≥0` for every r and c∈ℂ^r.
The equivalent transform representation is
`R_μ(z)=κ₁+∫ z/(1−tz) dρ(t)` for a finite positive compactly supported
measure ρ. Supply uniqueness of κ₁ and ρ, the moment/GNS construction of
ρ, and the bounds ensuring bounded realizations. Conversely realize these
cumulants on full Fock space by a scalar, creation/annihilation, and gauge
operator; prove the word-moment recursion and positivity.
Construct the compactly supported convolution semigroup μ_t, t≥0,
with cumulants tκ_n, prove its weak continuity, μ₀=δ₀ and
`μ_s⊞μ_t=μ_(s+t)`, and identify its convolution roots. Prove the
corresponding characterization by moment limits of N-fold powers of
compact laws, with positivity and moment bounds stated in the limit argument.
The general unbounded-law Lévy theory is outside the stated scope.

## F7. Compression, circular and R-diagonal elements

For a projection p free from a specified family and t=φ(p)≠0,
construct the corner probability space `(pAp,φ/t)` with unit p and prove

```
κ_n^(pAp)(pa_(i1)p,…,pa_(in)p)=t^(n−1)κ_n(a_(i1),…,a_(in)).
```

This algebraic identity does not require a trace. For a positive state
have 0<t≤1, and for faithful states p≠0 suffices; prove the positivity
and normalization of the corner state. Derive the law R-transform
`R_compressed(z)=R_a(tz)`, the consequences for semicircular and free
Poisson laws, and preservation of freeness for compressed subfamilies.
Build the product/interval-partition and Kreweras block-count proof.

For matrix units e_ij with `φ(e_ij)=δ_ij/d`, free from `(a_r)`, put
p=e_11 and `a_(ij)^r=e_(1i)a_r e_(j1)` in pAp. Prove their compressed
joint cumulants vanish unless `j_k=i_(k+1)` cyclically, and when this
condition holds equal `d^(1−n)κ_n(a_(r1),…,a_(rn))`. Supply the matrix
reconstruction and normalized trace comparisons. This is a cyclic-index
formula, not independent freeness of all corner matrix entries.

Define a circular element `c=(s₁+i s₂)/sqrt 2` for free variance-one
semicirculars. Compute its full *-distribution: κ₂(c,c*) and κ₂(c*,c)
are 1, all other joint cumulants vanish. Prove coordinate change and
circular-system realization, and identify the laws of c*c and cc* as
rate-one jump-one free Poisson. Define a Haar unitary by
`φ(u^k)=0` for every nonzero integer k; prove its circle-valued spectral
law is Haar probability and compute its alternating cumulants as
`(-1)^(n−1)catalan(n−1)` in degree 2n.

An R-diagonal variable has zero joint cumulants except at even alternating
words in a,a*. Define its two determining sequences from the two starting
letters. Prove reconstruction of all *-moments, adjoint/scalar transport,
rotation invariance and the circular/Haar examples. Prove traciality on
the generated *-algebra is equivalent to equality of the determining
sequences. Give the cumulants of aa* and a*a by their noncrossing-block
formulas, and show their two distributions determine the R-diagonal
*-distribution; in the tracial case either one suffices.

Prove the free-Haar multiplication characterization and the realization
of a tracial R-diagonal *-distribution as uh with u a Haar unitary *-free from positive h having the law of
|a|=(a*a)^(1/2), in a C*-probability space. Distinguish a distribution model from a polar decomposition
inside the original algebra. In a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful
normal trace, if ker(a)=0, prove a is R-diagonal iff its polar decomposition
`a=u|a|` has u Haar and *-free from |a|; prove u is then a unitary.
With nonzero kernel the polar factor is only a partial isometry, so the
Haar-unitary assertion belongs to the distribution model and is not imposed
on that partial isometry.

## F8. Gaussian and Haar random-matrix asymptotic freeness

For each N≥1 use a probability space and measurable complex N×N matrix
entries with all finite moments. Construct the *-algebra of matrix-valued
random variables using `MeasureTheory.AEEqFun` for a.e. equality, with entries in
`⋂_(1≤p<∞) L^p`, and the normalized tracial expectation
`φ_N(X)=E[tr_N(X)]`. Prove integrability, closure under sums/products/star
by Hölder, positivity, normalization and trace identities. Gaussian entries
are unbounded, so this algebra is not M_N(L∞). Develop joint *-moment
convergence across possibly different probability spaces for different N,
and construct its limiting positive tracial polynomial functional by word
limits. A limiting deterministic distribution need not have a bounded
C*-realization; the algebraic limit remains meaningful in that case.

Construct GUE matrices by independent centered diagonal real Gaussians of
variance 1/N and upper-triangular complex Gaussians whose real and imaginary
parts are independent of each other and have variance 1/(2N), with lower
entries their conjugates. All these independent real coordinates are jointly
independent. Prove
`E[G_ij G_kl]=N⁻¹δ_ilδ_jk`. Construct the complex Ginibre ensemble with
independent centered entries satisfying
`E[Z_ij conjugate(Z_kl)]=N⁻¹δ_ikδ_jl` and `E[Z_ij Z_kl]=0`.
Use Mathlib's Gaussian laws and classical independence, and extend
Tau Ceti's `centralMoment_id_two_mul_gaussianReal` and
[StandardDistributions Layer5](../StandardDistributions/README.md) to the finite
real/complex Gaussian Wick formula needed for matrix words from Gaussian
moments and multilinearity. This is classical Wick pairings before any
noncrossing restriction is imposed.

For GUE prove the exact expected normalized-trace expansion, for m=2k≥2,

```
φ_N(G^m)=Σ_(π∈P₂(m)) N^(#cycles(γπ)−1−k),  γ=(1 … m),
```

with moment zero equal to 1 and odd moments zero. Prove the exponent is −2g with g≥0, and g=0
exactly for noncrossing pairings. Give the colored-pairing version for
independent GUE families, the adjoint-sensitive version for Ginibre,
and the leading-term/free Wick comparison. Deduce their joint expected
*-moment convergence to free semicircular or circular systems, respectively.
Include finite-N correction bounds for each fixed word by counting the
positive-genus terms; these are moment errors rather than norm bounds.

For a fixed finite deterministic matrix family D_N whose joint
*-moments under tr_N converge, prove independent GUE families are
asymptotically free from D_N, with the specified free semicircular limit.
No uniform operator-norm bound on D_N is required. Construct the
permutation-trace functional as the product of normalized traces of the
cycle words, prove the exact mixed Wick expansion, and show its subleading
terms vanish because each fixed deterministic trace-word is bounded by
its convergence hypothesis. Identify the leading color-respecting NC sums
with F2's mixed moments, keeping the permutation orientation compatible
with Kreweras complement. Extend the argument to nonselfadjoint Gaussian
families using adjoint colors. Specify bounded realizations only when
the deterministic limiting distribution has them.

Use the existing matrix unitary group and finite-dimensional topology.
Consume `TauCeti.Matrix.isCompact_unitaryGroup` and its `CompactSpace`
instance from `TauCeti.Topology.Algebra.UnitaryGroup`, comparing its
entrywise topology with this matrix realization. Construct normalized
Haar probability and develop invariance and matrix coefficient
measurability. Construct the Haar-averaging orthogonal
projection onto invariant tensors and the correspondence with tensor-power
intertwiners. Consume SchurWeyl Layer8's permutation centralizer for GL_N
and prove the unitary-group comparison by differentiating U(N)'s tensor
action on skew-Hermitian matrices, whose complex span is gl_N, then using
matrix exponentials/polar decomposition to obtain the GL_N centralizer.
Include the
small-dimension relations among permutation tensors. Compute their Gram
matrix `G_(σ,τ)=N^(#cycles(σ⁻¹τ))`. For all N build its inverse on its
range and the invariant projection; for N≥k prove G invertible and define
unitary Weingarten coefficients from G⁻¹. Prove phase invariance makes
unbalanced coefficient integrals zero, and, for N≥k, the balanced formula

```
E[Π_(r=1)^k U_(i_r j_r) conjugate(U_(i'_r j'_r))]
 = Σ_(α,β∈S_k) (Π_r δ_(i_r,i'_(β(r))))
                   (Π_r δ_(j_r,j'_(α(r)))) Wg(N,βα⁻¹).
```

Provide conjugation/inversion symmetries and the inverse-Gram identities.
Derive, for fixed σ∈S_k,
`Wg(N,σ)=N^(#cycles(σ)−2k)(Mob(σ)+O(N⁻²))`, where
`Mob(σ)=Π_(cycles C) (-1)^(|C|−1)catalan(|C|−1)`.
Make each error bound uniform over the finite permutations at fixed k,
and prove it through the finite Gram expansion and transposition-length
geodesics. The large-N formula does not use a matrix inverse at a
singular small dimension.

Prove independent Haar unitary matrices converge in joint *-moments to
free Haar unitaries, and are asymptotically free from any deterministic
finite family with convergent joint *-moments. Supply the full centered
mixed-word proof using Weingarten expansion, the geodesic fixed-point
lemma and vanishing centered cycle traces; a proof for only a single
unitary or single alternating word does not discharge the theorem.
Prove the conjugation version: for deterministic families A_N and B_N
whose separate joint *-distributions converge, and independent Haar U_N,
the families `U_N A_N U_N*` and B_N have free joint limiting
*-distribution. No joint limit of the original combined deterministic
family, and no uniform norm bound, is required.

For selfadjoint sums and the positive matrix products
`A_N^(1/2) U_N B_N U_N* A_N^(1/2)` with A_N,B_N≥0, deduce convergence
of expected empirical spectral measures to the additive/multiplicative
free convolution of the input laws when those limiting laws are compactly
supported. Construct empirical measures from the finite spectral theorem, prove
measurability using continuous ordered eigenvalues of selfadjoint matrices,
and compare every normalized trace moment, and prove tightness and the
higher-moment uniform integrability needed for weak convergence. Give the
semicircle example, sums of independent semicircular ensembles, and Haar
conjugation of deterministic positive matrices as concrete computations.
The scope is expected measures and expected *-moments, as fixed above.

TauCetiRoadmap/GeneralizedCohomology:
# Generalized cohomology, spectra and orientations

Build the stable algebraic topology needed to use cohomology theories rather than
only singular cohomology: integer gradings, relative and reduced theories,
representing spectra, products, infinite-CW comparisons, generalized bundle
orientations and Thom spectra. Brown representability, the Milnor sequence and
Spanier–Whitehead duality are parts of a usable library with explicit comparison
maps. The construction of a spectrum does not substitute for its homotopy theory.

The spectrum model is **symmetric spectra of pointed simplicial sets**. Its
pointed simplicial sets use Mathlib `SSet`, its sphere actions use the permutation
groups of `Fin n`, and its structure is a module over the symmetric sphere
sequence under Day convolution. Follow Hovey–Shipley–Smith's model, including the
stable model structure and its comparison with sequential spectra. In particular,
naïve colimits of homotopy groups do not define stable equivalences for arbitrary
symmetric spectra.

`README.md` is definitive. `Suggested.lean` checks selected carrier and interface
shapes; it is not an exhaustive checklist and its admitted constructions are targets.
Suggested implementation homes are `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Spectra/` and
`TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/GeneralizedCohomology/`.

## Scope and suppliers

All CW statements include arbitrary cell sets and unbounded dimension in the
chosen universe. Finite or countable hypotheses occur only on results that use
them. Spaces of CW type are included by comparison, and the spectrum-defined
extension to arbitrary spaces uses singular simplicial sets. No dimension axiom
is imposed on generalized theories.

## Conventions and complete basic APIs

- Work in explicitly fixed universes. The category of u-small CW objects has a
  set of cells in `Type u`, and theory values for Brown's theorem are u-small.
  Prove the solution-set bounds so the representing CW object is in that same
  universe, and prove universe-lift comparisons. Do not use a proper-class
  wedge in a construction. The pointed CW category has chosen cell structures,
  a 0-cell basepoint, all continuous based maps, and pointed homotopy classes.
  Its products are CW products in PR284's convenient category: prove the weak
  product CW structure agrees with k(X×Y). All products, wedges, smash and
  relative-product unions below use that topology and its comparison maps.
- Based spaces carry a point and maps preserve it. For CW models use a chosen
  0-cell as basepoint; for general models use the derived singular extension.
  `X₊` means a **disjoint** basepoint; it is distinct from one-point
  compactification. Form mapping cones for arbitrary pointed maps; identify
  them with subset quotients only for cofibration/NDR pairs.
- Write `ΣX = S¹ ∧ X`, with the suspension coordinate on the left, and orient
  `S¹` by the increasing interval parameter. `Σ` on spectra is the derived
  suspension, made invertible in the stable homotopy category. `Σⁿ` uses every
  integer n, with native `HasShift C ℤ`, inverse and composition isomorphisms.
  Use native `Pretriangulated`/`IsTriangulated` for the cofiber triangles.
  A reduced cone uses A×[0,1], with A attached at t=0 and its t=1 end
  collapsed. The increasing collapse c:C_f→ΣA sends (a,t) to [t,a].
  Suspension in cohomology is σ(a)=ι×a with the positively oriented interval

# Integral currents, geometric homology and minimizing hypersurfaces

Build a reusable theory of currents on finite-dimensional smooth real Riemannian
manifolds: test forms, mass, integer rectifiability, boundary, pushforward, products,
slicing, integral homology, deformation and compactness, Plateau and homological
minimization, and interior regularity of codimension-one minimizers. The same
integral carrier supports geometric-chain comparisons in Morse theory and the
minimizing-hypersurface input to nonspin positive mass in ambient dimensions 3–7.
Every construction includes its restriction, locality, naturality, change-of-chart
and normalization API. [Suggested.lean](Suggested.lean) gives selected interfaces;
this README is definitive.

The ambient manifold M is Hausdorff, second countable, smooth, boundaryless and
finite dimensional, with a chosen smooth positive-definite Riemannian metric.
Compact domains with boundary sit inside this ambient manifold. Integration sources
may be compact oriented smooth manifolds with boundary or corners. Relative
homology also includes the closed neighborhood-retract subsets specified in G3.
Use [HopfRinow L0](../HopfRinow/README.md)'s induced-distance and native
`IsRiemannianManifold` interfaces. No orientation, connectedness, completeness
or compactness of M is assumed unless
a theorem needs it. Use native `ModelWithCorners`, `ChartedSpace`, `IsManifold`,
`TangentSpace`, `RiemannianBundle` and `IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle`. Distances used
for Lipschitz statements are the induced Riemannian distance on connected components,
with the native induced extended distance for disconnected manifolds; build the
chart-local bi-Lipschitz comparisons. An unrelated pre-existing metric on the same
type is not silently identified with the Riemannian distance.

The regularity headline is **interior**, codimension one and locally mass minimizing:
an integral (n−1)-current with no boundary in an open set of a smooth Riemannian
n-manifold has smooth embedded minimal support there when 2≤n≤7. Multiplicity is
retained. This is not a theorem about every stable varifold, about higher codimension,
or about arbitrary behavior at a prescribed boundary. All-dimensional nonspin
positive mass, spacetime/Jang theory, and generic Morse/Bott trajectory compactification
are application theories, not consequences built into this headline.

## Carriers, conventions and suppliers

Use one intrinsic real-current carrier `Current k M`, acting continuously and
real-linearly on compactly supported smooth **k-forms**, and its integer-rectifiable,
locally integral, finite integral and compactly supported integral subgroups. These
are subobjects of the same current theory, not independent models. Put
`A_k = Λ^k T* M`, let `D = DensityBundle M`, and put `V_k = A_k* ⊗ D`.
Consume the early real finite-rank `BundleTest(V_k* ⊗ D)` foundation of
[ComplexKahlerGeometry K5a](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/17de96c131cb4bba925c11191595b59dd39cde98/TauCetiRoadmap/ComplexKahlerGeometry/README.md).
The canonical evaluation/bidual and density-dual cancellation give
`V_k* ⊗ D ≃ A_k`. G1 specializes this test space to forms and owns its
current-specific differential, boundary and mass. In a Euclidean chart the test
forms compare with native `TestFunction Ω (E [⋀^Fin k]→L[ℝ] ℝ) ⊤`.
No complex structure, orientation or compactness is required for this real
specialization. The real ambient vector space of currents does not make its
integral subgroup an ℝ-vector space.

Pin

`∂T(ω)=T(dω)`,

with no additional sign, and outward-first orientation on a smooth boundary.
For a degree-k current, `∂(T×S)=∂T×S+(−1)^k T×∂S`. Interval-first products give
`∂([0,1]×T)={1}×T−{0}×T−[0,1]×∂T`. Use nonnegative extended masses and the
normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure
[`MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.html#MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure),
written Hᵏ below: H⁰ is counting measure and Hᵏ agrees with Lebesgue volume in
real Euclidean dimension k. Prove all raw-Hausdorff conversion factors explicitly.
For rectifiable Jacobians use native `LinearMap.normDet`; pointwise form norms and
simple-vector volume agree through CalibratedGeometry C1's comass/Gram comparison.

For smooth geometry use RiemannianGeometry's conventions
`R(X,Y)Z=∇_X∇_Y Z−∇_Y∇_X Z−∇_[X,Y]Z`,
`B(X,Y)=(∇^N_X df(Y))^⊥`, `S_νX=−(∇^N_Xν)^⊤`,
`H=(tr B)/m` for m>0, and `Δ⁺=−div grad`.
The outward unit sphere has `B=−gν` and averaged `H=−ν`.
Scalar curvature is full trace, `Scal=2Σ_(i<j)K_ij`.

# Geometric measure theory: rectifiability, BV, and finite perimeter

Build a reusable Euclidean geometric measure theory library through the structure theorem for
sets of finite perimeter, area and coarea, approximation, compactness, traces, and Gauss–Green.
These results supply the measure-theoretic foundation for
[Euclidean isoperimetry](../Isoperimetry/README.md), including its sharp inequality and ball rigidity.
The objects must support further analysis independently of that application: restriction,
localization, a.e. equivalence, change of variables, and comparisons with classical calculus are
part of their basic theory.

The scope is finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces, with metric curve results in the greater
generality their statements permit. Currents, varifolds, and regularity theory for minimizing
hypersurfaces are outside this roadmap. All the milestones below are required.
[Suggested.lean](Suggested.lean) illustrates some interfaces; this README is definitive.

## Conventions and ownership

- Use `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` and intrinsic finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces,
  with `volume` for Lebesgue measure. Transfer results by linear isometry equivalences rather
  than developing coordinate-specific theories. In dimension two include the existing real
  inner-product space `ℂ`.
- For set theorems, Lebesgue measurability means `NullMeasurableSet E volume`; use
  `MeasurableSet` for a Borel representative and transfer by equality a.e. The full perimeter
  theory must accommodate all Lebesgue measurable representatives, including null
  modifications of Borel sets.
- **Hausdorff measure is the normalized Euclidean measure**
  [`MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.html#MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure),
  written `μHE[k]`. It agrees with `volume` on a `k`-dimensional Euclidean space. Write
  `Hᵏ` for this measure below. Retain explicit comparison lemmas with Mathlib's raw Hausdorff
  measure. Do not silently exchange the two normalizations.
- A rectifiable parameterized curve is a continuous map on a compact real interval with
  `BoundedVariationOn`; its length is the existing `eVariationOn`. No new path or length
  carrier replaces Mathlib's maps, `Path`, or total variation. Use extended nonnegative
  quantities first; conversion to real length requires a finiteness theorem.
- A countably `k`-rectifiable set is covered, up to an `Hᵏ`-null set, by countably many
  Lipschitz images of subsets of `ℝᵏ`. Distinguish this from finite `Hᵏ` measure and from
  parameterized rectifiability. State measurability separately where it is needed.
- For real-valued functions on Euclidean open sets, `BV_loc(Ω)` means a locally integrable
  function whose distributional
  derivative is a locally finite vector-valued Radon measure. `BV(Ω)` additionally requires
  integrability and finite total variation. Use the distributional identity
  `∫ u div φ = −∫ φ · dDu` for smooth compactly supported vector fields in `Ω`.
  Derivatives and variation are invariant under equality a.e. on `Ω`.
- Define extended perimeter for every measurable set by the supremum of
  `∫_E div φ` over smooth vector fields compactly supported in the open set `Ω`, with
  pointwise norm at most one. A set has locally finite perimeter when its indicator
  belongs to `BV_loc`. Its perimeter measure is `|Dχ_E|`, and the supremum agrees with
  `P(E; Ω) = |Dχ_E|(Ω)` whenever that measure exists. Finite perimeter on the
  whole space means `P(E; univ) < ∞`; it does **not** require finite volume. Global `BV`
  membership of the indicator additionally requires finite volume. Complements must have
  the same perimeter.
- The outward measure-theoretic unit normal has sign
  `Dχ_E = −ν_E Hⁿ⁻¹|∂*E`. Distinguish topological frontier, essential boundary, and reduced
  boundary. The last two are measure-theoretic notions, with statements independent of
  the chosen a.e. representative.

[PDE](../PDE/README.md), Lane A.1–A.3, owns weak-derivative Sobolev spaces and their smooth
density and Fourier comparisons. Extend the actual `TauCeti.HasWeakFDerivOn` and `W1p`
APIs to measure-valued derivatives; prove the comparison rather than inventing another weak
derivative. Its Lane A.5–A.6 owns Sobolev Poincaré, domain traces, extensions, and Rellich.
This roadmap owns BV versions and their agreement with those Sobolev results.

[ConformalMapping](../ConformalMapping/README.md), L5, owns Jordan separation and the
filled-hull topology. [DifferentialGeometry](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md), whose
[Green layer 5.6 targets](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/826) specify
the flat planar extension, owns
winding numbers, planar curve integrals, and Green's area identity. This roadmap owns metric
length, arclength, rectifiability, and Hausdorff measure comparisons. The sharp Euclidean
isoperimetric constants, Brunn–Minkowski, rearrangements, and ball rigidity belong to
[Isoperimetry](../Isoperimetry/README.md). The nonsharp local estimate in G4 below is a
foundation for perimeter structure, not a dependency on that sharp theorem.

## Existing floor and API design

Consume Mathlib's Hausdorff measures, Radon measures, signed and vector measures, total
variation, Radon–Nikodym and Lebesgue decomposition, Bochner integration, Rademacher and
change of variables, and the calculus of test functions. Tau Ceti supplies
`TauCeti.metricDerivative`, its a.e. existence and integrable distance bound for
absolutely continuous curves, the `C¹` variation–speed identity in
`TauCeti.Analysis.Calculus.MetricVariation`, weak derivatives, and `W1p`. G1 extends these
curve results; G2–G3 build the remaining measure and derivative bridges.

Use [`LinearMap.normDet`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NormDet.html#LinearMap.normDet)
and its continuous-linear-map version for geometric Jacobians. Mathlib already relates it
to Gram determinants and the volume of linear images; do not introduce another Jacobian
for rectangular linear maps. In particular, consume
`LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume` for linear images.
For the coarea Jacobian of a map from dimension `n` to `m ≤ n`,
use the norm determinant of its adjoint. Prove the chart and tangent-space comparison lemmas
needed for the nonlinear formulas.

Follow the API direction of these Mathlib proposals and discussions, implementing missing
results in Tau Ceti without waiting for them:

- [Arclength continuity, mathlib4#31766](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/31766):
  cumulative variation and continuity for continuous rectifiable curves.
- [Finite variation of finite-dimensional vector measures, #42103](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42103):
  vector-measure variation, used by G2–G3.
- [Connected sets of finite Hausdorff length, #41839](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41839):
  diameter and length comparisons, used by G1.
- [Uniformly distributed measures, #37310](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37310)
  and the [Hausdorff/coarea discussion](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/217875-Is%20there%20code%20for%20X%3F/topic/Finding%20n-dimensional%20polar%20coordinate%20formula%20for%20sobolev.):
  normalized Hausdorff measure, sphere measures, and polar integration. G2 requires the
  actual sphere-measure comparison, not merely a uniqueness theorem that could prove it.

## G1 — Rectifiable curves and arclength

Consume the existing variation API: `eVariationOn.mono`, `Icc_add_Icc`,
`comp_eq_of_antitoneOn`, `comp_eq_of_monotoneOn`, `lowerSemicontinuous_uniformOn`, and
`edist_le`, together with Tau Ceti's `eVariationOn_le_liminf_of_eventually_le`. Use the
`TauCeti.IsCurveJoining`/`Path` comparison in `Topology/MetricSpace/Length.lean` where a
joining curve is required. Build the curve-specific concatenation and restriction
comparisons not already expressed by those APIs. Build cumulative arclength,
prove its continuity and endpoint values, and factor a rectifiable curve through a
unit-speed Lipschitz curve on its length interval. Handle constant pieces by factorization;
an inverse of the cumulative arclength function is not available for a general curve.
For injective arcs, give the strictly increasing reparametrization and its homeomorphism.
For closed curves injective except at the endpoints, give an arclength parametrization
with that same simplicity property. Include zero-length cases explicitly.

For absolutely continuous curves prove length equals the integral of the metric derivative.
In finite-dimensional real normed spaces identify it a.e. with the norm of the vector derivative and
deduce `eVariationOn γ = ∫⁻ ‖γ'‖`. Supply the interval-integral real-valued form with its
integrability and finite-length hypotheses. Relate the factorization to the FTC and prove
that a nonconstant arclength parametrization has speed one a.e. Reconcile these statements
with existing `C¹` and `Path` APIs.

Prove `H¹(trace γ) ≤ length γ`, with equality for injective arcs and simple closed curves
(endpoints identified). Conversely, a continuous injective arc or simple closed curve
with finite `H¹` trace has finite variation. Prove this using partitions, the connected-set
diameter bound, and additivity of trace measure; it must not assume a Lipschitz input
parameter. Thus finite geometric length and parameterized rectifiability agree for these
curves. Include the multiplicity formula supplied by G2 for nonsimple
curves, so a twice-traversed circle has twice the variation length and the same trace
measure. Deduce that rectifiable planar traces have zero two-dimensional volume.
Make all length identities invariant under increasing continuous onto reparametrizations.
DifferentialGeometry's [rectifiable-curve interface](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md#rectifiable-curves-and-geometric-measure-theory)
consumes this arclength factorization to construct geometric
line integrals and their orientation/parametrization comparisons. G1 does not use those
integral comparisons as an input to the metric theory.

The variation, factorization, upper length bound, and exact comparisons for injective arcs
and simple closed curves are G1 targets independent of G2, using partitions and the
connected-set diameter bound for the lower comparison. The multiplicity formula for
nonsimple curves follows G2's one-dimensional area formula. G2 does not assume that
multiplicity formula in its proof.

## G2 — Rectifiability, area, and coarea

Build the closure and transport API for countably rectifiable sets: measurable restrictions,
countable unions, null modifications, Lipschitz images, and isometries. For countably
`k`-rectifiable sets with locally finite `Hᵏ` measure prove existence and a.e. uniqueness
of approximate tangent `k`-planes,
measurability of the tangent-plane field, and the density theorem. Build tangential
differentiation for Lipschitz maps on these sets and show independence of charts and null
modifications. Prove agreement with tangent spaces and surface Jacobians on `C¹` graphs.

Prove the **area formula** for Lipschitz maps `f : ℝᵐ → ℝⁿ`, `m ≤ n`, on measurable sets,
with nonnegative measurable weights:

```
∫_A g(x) J_m f(x) dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} Σ_{x ∈ A ∩ f⁻¹{y}} g(x) dHᵐ(y).
```

Multiplicity is an extended nonnegative count, with measurable weighted fiber sums; do
not use a finite-cardinality convention that returns zero for infinite fibers. Supply the
injective specialization and finite-dimensional isometric transport. Derive the tangential
area formula for maps on countably rectifiable sets.

Prove the **coarea formula** for Lipschitz `f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ`, `m ≤ n`, with the same weighted
generality, integrating `Hⁿ⁻ᵐ` over fibers and Lebesgue measure in the target. Include the
fiber measurability, a.e. rectifiability, and exceptional-set statements the formula needs.
Give real integrable versions after proving finiteness. The differentiability, covering,
measurability, and approximation lemmas needed for these formulas are themselves targets
of G2, using Mathlib's Rademacher theorem rather than presuming nonlinear area or coarea.

Derive graph surface measure, spherical surface measure, polar integration, and slicing by
linear projections. Prove `Hⁿ⁻¹(sphere c r) = n ω_n r^(n−1)` for `n ≥ 1`, `r > 0`, where
`ω_n = volume(ball 0 1)`, and the unit-sphere comparison with angular measure. Normalize
`H⁰` as counting measure. These identities must agree with existing ball volume and
linear-image formulas; they provide the actual constants used by isoperimetry.

## G3 — Distributional BV and variation measures

Construct the measure-valued derivative, its uniqueness, and its total variation from the
test-function identity. Prove equivalence with the local variational characterization
using compactly supported smooth vector fields with pointwise norm at most one. Establish
the Radon representation and its localization on arbitrary open subsets, using Mathlib's
Riesz representation and vector-measure infrastructure and building every missing bridge.
Handle locally finite derivatives on unbounded domains by compatible restrictions; do not
assume a globally finite vector measure at the definition of `BV_loc`.

Give the unbundled a.e.-invariant predicate and the normed a.e.-quotient `BV(Ω)` with norm
`‖u‖₁ + |Du|(Ω)`. Prove completeness, restriction, scalar multiplication, addition, lattice
operations, multiplication by smooth cutoffs, Lipschitz scalar composition and its variation
bound, affine isometric transport, and scaling by positive dilations. For global BV
composition require integrability of the composite, obtained for example from `φ(0)=0`;
local BV has no such whole-space integrability requirement. Supply the polar decomposition
`Du = σ_u |Du|`, with `‖σ_u‖ = 1` a.e., and the absolutely continuous/singular decomposition.
Do not apply the classical chain rule across jumps: composition results must give the
correct BV identity or a variation inequality.

Compare with `TauCeti.HasWeakFDerivOn` and `W1p`: a `W¹,¹` function is BV, its derivative
measure has weak gradient as density, and its variation is the integral of the gradient
norm. Conversely an integrable BV function with an absolutely continuous derivative is
`W¹,¹`. Include the local versions and the one-dimensional comparison with classical
variation and the derivative measure of a BV function. Prove measure-valued integration
by parts and agreement with smooth calculus.

## G4 — Approximation, compactness, and scalar coarea

Prove lower semicontinuity of variation under local `L¹` convergence, weak convergence of
the derivative measures under locally bounded variation, and compactness in `L¹_loc` for
families locally bounded in `L¹` and variation. For bounded Lipschitz domains derive global
`L¹` compactness under a global BV bound. Establish convolution estimates, local smooth
approximation on arbitrary open sets by a partition of unity, and **strict approximation**:
`u_j → u` in `L¹` and `|Du_j|(Ω) → |Du|(Ω)`.

Prove scalar BV coarea on open sets:

```
|Du|(Ω) = ∫_{ℝ} P({x | u(x) > t}; Ω) dt.
```

The superlevel sets have locally finite perimeter for a.e. `t`; provide their measurable
dependence on `t`, the local measure identity, layer-cake formulas, truncation formulas,
and the converse characterization. Derive approximation of finite-volume finite-perimeter
sets by bounded smooth sets with volume convergence and perimeter convergence on the whole
space. Build cutoff/truncation and regular-level arguments. Consume
`TauCeti.addHaar_image_criticalPoints_eq_zero` from
`TauCeti.Analysis.Calculus.Sard.OutermostStratum` in the smooth scalar regime: its finite
regularity threshold is automatically met by `C∞` functions. Build the regular-level and
level-set boundary comparisons needed for the approximation from that theorem. Do not strengthen
this to preservation of equality cases under approximation.

Supply BV Poincaré on balls and the nonsharp relative perimeter estimate

```
min(|E ∩ B_r|, |B_r \ E|)^((n−1)/n) ≤ C_n P(E; B_r),    n ≥ 2,
```

for locally finite-perimeter sets and `r > 0`, with a positive constant depending only on
`n`, plus scaling and localization. Consume Mathlib's compactly supported `C¹` estimate
`MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one`; build its BV and local-domain extensions,
and the covering estimates needed for this result here, without using the
sharp theorem in Isoperimetry. This is the analytic input for G5's boundary structure.

## G5 — Finite perimeter and boundary structure

Build the usable perimeter API: a.e. invariance, complements, locality, relative perimeter,
unions/intersections with the submodularity inequality, truncation by balls, scaling,
isometries, smooth approximation, compactness, and lower semicontinuity. Distinguish finite
perimeter from finite volume in every theorem.

Define measure-theoretic density, essential interior/exterior, essential boundary, reduced
boundary, and outward normal. Prove the Lebesgue density facts and **De Giorgi's structure
theorem**: the reduced boundary is countably `(n−1)`-rectifiable, its blow-up is an oriented
half-space at `Hⁿ⁻¹`-a.e. point, and

```
|Dχ_E| = Hⁿ⁻¹|∂*E,       Dχ_E = −ν_E Hⁿ⁻¹|∂*E.
```

Prove that the essential boundary differs from the reduced boundary by an `Hⁿ⁻¹`-null set
for locally finite-perimeter sets. Supply the converse finite-perimeter criterion for a
measurable set whose essential boundary has locally finite `Hⁿ⁻¹` measure. In particular,
establish `P(E) ≤ Hⁿ⁻¹(frontier E)` for measurable sets, as an extended-measure statement
with the appropriate local version. Its proof must include the boundary criterion; a
finite topological boundary measure is not an assumed smoothness hypothesis.

The proofs of blow-up, density estimates, covering, and rectifiability are G5 targets,
resting on G2–G4. Specifying a reduced-boundary predicate without proving the representation
theorem does not discharge this milestone.

## G6 — Traces, Gauss–Green, and classical domains

Construct the BV trace on bounded Lipschitz domains with the `Hⁿ⁻¹` boundary measure,
its boundedness estimate, interior approximate-limit characterization a.e., uniqueness,
locality, and agreement with PDE Lane A.6's Sobolev trace. Establish the extension operator,
zero-extension derivative formula including the boundary trace term, and gluing across
a Lipschitz interface. Use the boundary regularity and chart conventions of PDE A.6;
build missing surface-measure/chart comparisons using G2, rather than a second domain type.

Prove Gauss–Green for locally finite-perimeter sets and compactly supported `C¹` vector
fields, including localized forms and integrable noncompact-support extensions under
explicit hypotheses. For BV functions on Lipschitz domains give integration by parts
with the trace term. Compare outward normals and surface area for Lipschitz and `C¹`
domains with the classical graph formulas and DifferentialGeometry's Euclidean divergence
theorem. This comparison does not require manifold Stokes to construct the flat theory.

For the bounded region `Ω = TauCeti.filledHull C \ C` of a rectifiable Jordan curve,
prove finite perimeter and `P(Ω) = H¹(C)`. Explicitly prove the Jordan index theorem for
its closed simple AC arclength parametrization: for one sign `σ ∈ {−1,1}`, the existing
winding number equals `σ` on `Ω` and zero on the unbounded complementary component.
Identify that sign with orientation and prove its reversal and parametrization laws;
it is a conclusion, not a supplied hypothesis of Green's theorem.
The proof must establish the boundary normal and
measure comparison, using Jordan separation, G1–G5 and the AC boundary-integral identity
of DifferentialGeometry 5.6, with parametrization transport from G1. With `Jv = I*v`
and arclength unit tangent `τ`, identify the outward normal as `−σ Jτ` a.e. and the
corresponding signed boundary measure, so clockwise and counterclockwise curves both
give the same perimeter. This supplies
the genuine bridge from the measure-theoretic inequality to arbitrary rectifiable Jordan
curves; `frontier Ω = C` alone gives no equality of perimeter and curve length.

## Acceptance examples and completion

Compute derivative measures and perimeter for intervals, balls, boxes, and annuli; include
the endpoint atoms for a one-dimensional step function. Construct the Cantor–Lebesgue
function `C` on `[0,1]`, extended constantly outside that interval, from the ternary
Cantor-set/dyadic-value construction, using
Mathlib's Cantor set. Prove continuity, monotonicity, `C(0)=0`, `C(1)=1`, variation one,
and `C'=0` a.e.; its derivative measure is a singular continuous probability measure
supported on the Cantor set. This is the named singular BV example and the input to
Isoperimetry's non-AC homeomorphism example. Check complement invariance on the exterior of a ball, an infinite-volume
finite-perimeter set. Check null modification invariance on a punctured ball and on a
ball with a null dense subset added outside it; topological frontier and perimeter differ.
Compute the area formula for a graph and the multiplicity of a twice-traversed circle.
Give a rectifiable Jordan curve with a continuous non-AC parametrization and recover its
length, perimeter, and area through arclength. These exercise the APIs rather than replacing
the general theorems.

Completion requires all comparisons as well as all named theorems. Real-valued formulas
must establish integrability and finite measures before using `toReal` or a Bochner
integral. Null-set choices, chart choices, and parametrizations must disappear from the
final measures and geometric invariants.

## References and prior formalizations

- Francesco Maggi, [*Sets of Finite Perimeter and Geometric Variational Problems*](https://cvgmt.sns.it/paper/1880/):
  the perimeter, approximation, structure, and boundary framework.
- Leon Simon, [*Lectures on Geometric Measure Theory*](https://web.stanford.edu/class/math285/ts-gmt.pdf):
  rectifiability, tangential differentiation, and area/coarea.
- [MovingSofa](https://github.com/deancureton/MovingSofa) contains formalized Jordan-curve
  area and Hausdorff-length developments relevant to G1 and G6.
- The [Humanfia public source archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/humanfia-lab/lean-eval-source/tree/main/problems/isoperimetric_inequality),
  [Jonathan Ho's isoperimetric development](https://github.com/hojonathanho/isoperimetric)
  (also [in LeanPool](https://github.com/LeanPool/lean-pool/tree/main/LeanPool/Isoperimetric)),
  and [kim-em/isoperimetric](https://github.com/kim-em/isoperimetric) are related formalizations;
  Isoperimetry describes their mathematical relation to the target.

These are sources of mathematical and API evidence, not required dependencies or prescribed
proofs. The targets are independently specified on top of Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Any use of
existing code follows the repository's coordination and attribution rules; completion is
judged against the intrinsic statements and reusable APIs above.

# Geometric representation categories and coherent local transport

A family of representation categories needs more than a category at each
parameter and an equivalence for each pair of isomorphic parameters. Transport
must respect identities and composition, act on morphisms, and commute coherently
with the representation symmetries. This roadmap develops those interfaces for
smooth affine Lie-algebra modules at a fixed level and their critical central
characters. Its local Langlands endpoint is the precise categorical-lift
conjecture; the conjecture's existence is not an unconditional theorem target.

The reusable library consists of categorical group actions, full-subcategory
restriction, coherent actions on the supplied central-character categories,
equivariant groupoid transport, descent along equivalences of parameter
groupoids, and the outer-derivation/self-extension infinitesimal bridge.
These constructions use Mathlib's categories, monoidal actions and
pseudofunctors. They do not replace these carriers with private versions.

## Scope, conventions and prerequisites

The representation-side group is a connected simply connected simple complex
algebraic group `G`; its Lie algebra is `𝔤`. The Langlands-dual group `G∨` is
adjoint. The representation-side group of complex loop points is
`H=G(ℂ((t)))`. The critical form is `κc=-½ Killing`, and the distinguished central
generator acts as identity. Modules are algebraic vector spaces with discrete
topology, smooth in the vectorwise sense `∀v ∃N>0, t^N𝔤[[t]]·v=0`.
The categorical group actions here are coherent actions by complex loop points.
They do not assert that every smooth module has a single rational congruence
stabilizer. AffineLieAlgebras A3's uniform rational `K_N` integration theorem
requires finite generation; the unrestricted smooth category retains the
vectorwise condition. Mere objectwise isomorphisms are not coherent equivariance.
Formal coefficient rings and modules carry the discrete coefficient topology;
the completed algebra carries its inverse-limit topology. ALA Suggested installs
its discrete complex-coefficient instance locally. GRC's generic signatures
instead take the actual topological algebra and continuity hypotheses explicitly;
its affine application installs ALA's supplied completion topology. Ordinary
complex-point Lie groups in FCO retain their usual complex topology.

[AffineLieAlgebras A2–A5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/roadmap/affine-lie-algebras-20261018/TauCetiRoadmap/AffineLieAlgebras/README.md) supplies the actual
smooth level-one module category, the continuous completed-enveloping action,
the equivalence of these categories, kernels, cokernels, sums, continuous
coinduction, enough injectives and the native `HasExt` adapter. A2 exports
continuous completed loop/coordinate automorphisms and their order-shift bounds.
A5 owns generic strict central-character categories, closed central quotients
and their twist comparisons; A8 specializes these to critical oper characters
and the center-fixing representation-side loop action. A6 supplies the flat
formal deformation and its compatible higher-order truncations.
[FormalConnectionsOpers F3–F8](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1056)
supplies the original and dual loop groups and congruence subgroups, dual
opers, their function algebra, coordinates, evaluation, the gauge-isomorphism
groupoid and its cotangent Lie-algebroid comparison.
These are construction prerequisites and independent owners, not applications
of the conjecture below.

Use `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` for restrictions of `ModuleCat` or the
existing smooth-module category. The critical-character equation is an actual
predicate: for every central `z` and vector `v`, `z·v=χp(z)v`. AffineLieAlgebras A5
constructs
this category and A8 its critical specialization; consume these exact carriers.

The parameter groupoid `Γ` has oper objects `p`; arrows `p→q` are **all
isomorphisms of their underlying dual local systems**, including automorphisms.
An arrow may be written `(p,q,g)` with `g∈G∨(ℂ((t)))` after trivialization. It
need not preserve the oper Borel reduction. Composition of `g:p→q` followed by
`h:q→r` is `hg`. This is FormalConnectionsOpers F8's `IsomOp`, not the
Borel-preserving oper groupoid and not a global action of `G∨((t))` on a
Drinfeld–Sokolov slice. The separate group `H` acts within each character fiber.

For a left group action, `T_(gh)=T_g∘T_h`, written `T_h ⋙ T_g` in Lean. The
native category `SingleObj H` has `g ≫ h = h*g`. Mathlib's endofunctor tensor
is `F⊗G=F⋙G`; therefore left actions correspond to monoidal functors into its
**monoidal opposite**, as in `MonoidalLeftAction.curriedActionMop`. Pin this
convention in every comparison and transported action.

## R1. Categorical actions and invariant full subcategories

Consume `MonoidalLeftAction (Discrete H) C`, `SingleObj H`, `LocallyDiscrete`,
`Cat`, `Pseudofunctor`, `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans` and modifications. Construct
the comparison between a native monoidal left action and a pseudofunctor
`LocallyDiscrete (SingleObj H) ⥤ᵖ Cat` concentrated at `C`. Prove the formulas
for units, group products, inverse equivalences and action on morphisms. The
comparison must transport the unit/associator coherence, rather than merely
matching object functions. The TODO in the native action file is a construction
target here, using the existing carriers.

For an isomorphism-stable object predicate `P`, prove an action preserving `P`
restricts to `P.FullSubcategory`. Construct the fully faithful inclusion, its
equivariant comparison, and the canonical comparison when restricting in two
steps. An equivariant functor carries natural isomorphisms
`T_g^C ⋙ F ≅ F ⋙ T_g^D` satisfying the unit and product diagrams. Build identity,
composition, equivariant natural transformations and transport along equivalences.
Prove the comparison with strong transformations between the corresponding
classifying-group pseudofunctors. For linear categories, prove restriction and
transport retain scalar linearity. When the full subcategory inherits an abelian structure, prove that the
restricted exact actions preserve its inherited kernels and cokernels. Build
this inherited structure under the explicit hypotheses that P contains zero
and is closed under finite biproducts, kernels and cokernels. For strict
central-character fibers these closure properties follow from the scalar-action
equation; no closure under arbitrary ambient extensions is inferred.

Define the source's objectwise congruence-invariance predicate on an `H` action:
`∀ M ∃ N>0 ∀ g∈K_N, Nonempty (T_g M ≅ M)`.
Prove invariance under equivariant equivalence and restriction to stable full
subcategories. This predicate asks only for objectwise isomorphisms; coherent
rational integration with the prescribed Lie derivative is separate data.

These are complete interfaces: constructors, extensionality on components,
identity/product simplifications, inverse-action comparison, inclusion
naturality, equivalence invariance and the associated coherence lemmas.

## R2. Coherent twists on the supplied module categories

Consume AffineLieAlgebras A5's generic discrete continuous module object
property on `ModuleCat A`, its annihilator/open-ideal criterion, categorical
closure, central-character predicate, closed central-ideal quotient and category
comparison. For products use A5's smooth vectors in the ordinary product. These
constructions have one owner, A5. R2 builds the categorical coherence of twists
on those supplied categories.

For a group homomorphism `a:H→Aut_cont,ℂ(A)`, use the actual continuous algebra
equivalences and native `ModuleCat.restrictScalars` to construct `T_h` by
restricting through `a_h⁻¹`. Assemble the supplied A5 single-automorphism
comparisons into `MonoidalLeftAction (Discrete H) C` and its R1 classifying-group
pseudofunctor. Pin the underlying vector spaces and linear maps. The unit and product
comparisons are exactly the restrictions of native

## Grounding and validation

Mathlib's [monoidal action definitions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Action/Basic.lean),
[endofunctor comparison](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Action/End.lean),
[locally discrete bicategories](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Bicategory/LocallyDiscrete.lean),
and [pseudofunctor/strong-transformation API](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Bicategory/NaturalTransformation/Pseudo.lean)
are the native carriers. The
[composition-order discussion](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/near/523092176)
explains the left/right action distinction. Follow that design.
[Mathlib PR32410](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/32410)
develops pseudofunctor evaluation with `eval` and `evaluation`; use those
interfaces for the R5 family comparisons, constructing the needed forms here
against the available pin. It is not a timing dependency.

The mathematical source is the local-category discussion in
[Frenkel, Langlands Correspondence for Loop Groups](https://math.berkeley.edu/~frenkel/loop.pdf)
and the critical representation setting in
[Frenkel–Gaitsgory, Local geometric Langlands correspondence and affine Kac–Moody algebras](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508382).
[Johnson–Yau, 2-Dimensional Categories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06055)
supplies the general pseudofunctor/coherence reference. Formal/algebraic
gauge foundations and finite-dimensional smooth groupoid foundations have
different owners; this roadmap uses the former.

Acceptance requires consumption of the actual A5/A8 character categories and
comparisons, checked left-action composition order, semidirect covariance, mixed
coherence diagrams, isotropy preservation, conditional descent, the continuous
outer-derivation/self-extension bridge, and the specified relative lift types. The
conjecture must be represented by the complete type of lift data, never by an
empty `Prop` field or by an unconditional existence theorem. Suggested Lean
signatures are interface checks, not proofs of the mathematical targets.
