Follow the `MonomialOrder.IsRemainder`, `IsGroebnerBasis` and S-polynomial
design of [Mathlib PR29203](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/29203)
and [PR34873](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/34873).
Build needed targets in Tau Ceti on that design and adopt Mathlib declarations
when available. For generic minors follow
[PR40266](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40266)'s
`Matrix.mvPolynomialMinor`/`determinantalIdeal` interfaces. The
[Gröbner-basis discussion](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/217875-Is%20there%20code%20for%20X%3F/topic/Gr%C3%B6bner%20bases)
records the division/remainder direction; a tactic's internal Gröbner engine
does not replace the mathematical API.

This roadmap owns polynomial minor/flag-minor presentations, straightening
and flat families. Scheme identifications with Grassmannians or flags, section
comparisons, and geometric Schubert ideals are outside its scope; they consume
these polynomial results. No scheme identification with a homogeneous space is
an input to this roadmap. Rational highest-weight modules and crystals remain
with their representation suppliers; character identities here do not assert
semisimple decomposition in characteristic p.

## G1. Ideals, normal forms and elimination

Construct the ideal generated by leading terms of an ideal I. A Gröbner basis
G of I is a subset of I with the same leading-term ideal. Build subset/span,
monic rescaling, zero removal, transport, extension by redundant generators
and change-of-coefficients APIs. Separate ring statements with unit leading
coefficients from field statements. Define remainders using a bounded-degree
division representation and irreducibility of every remaining monomial;
the condition concerns divisibility, not merely comparison of total degrees.

Prove ideal membership iff a Gröbner remainder is zero, uniqueness of the
irreducible remainder, the quotient basis of standard monomials and its
linear normal-form map. Give additive/scalar/product-reduction equations,
idempotence, kernel I and compatibility with quotient multiplication.
For homogeneous ideals construct graded versions and their homogeneous bases.

Use native `m.sPolynomial`, its lcm formula and leading-coefficient cancellation
lemmas; construct the missing remainder/standard-representation API for it.
Prove Buchberger's criterion and certified completion: each nonzero reduced
S-polynomial strictly enlarges the monomial ideal, so Noetherianity gives
termination in finitely many variables. Supply the finite Gröbner existence
theorem, unique reduced monic basis and equivalence of generator sets by
normal forms. Executable operations on computable fields return mathematical
certificates; no complexity bound is presumed. Use native lexicographic and
graded lexicographic orders; construct graded reverse lexicographic order in
the same `MonomialOrder` API, with its comparison and well-foundedness lemmas.
Pin the usual antitone single-variable convention: X_i precedes X_j iff j≤i
in the ordered variable index. In G5 use `OrderDual` of the lexicographic
row-subset index, so P_I<P_J when I precedes J lexicographically.

Prove elimination/intersection, saturation by an element, colon ideals and
ideal equality computations, with the added-variable localization comparison.
Prove that any finite set of comparisons in the given monomial order is represented
by positive integral weights, including bounded-total-degree comparisons;
prove the finite linear-inequality separation lemma used for this. Do not
claim that one weight represents every comparison of an arbitrary term order.
Build weight initials, refinement by a term order and finite Gröbner-cone
inequalities, with the finite reduction certificates that certify an unchanged
initial ideal. Extend scalar fields without changing initial ideals/bases.

## G2. Semigroup presentations, normalization and degree

For finitely many exponents a_i, construct the exponent map from N^i, its
image S and the polynomial-to-monoid-algebra surjection X_i↦chi^(a_i).
Its kernel is generated by binomials X^u−X^v with equal exponent image.
Prove the presentation over arbitrary commutative coefficient rings,
finite binomial generation and elimination computation. First use Noetherianity
over Z to select finitely many of the defining binomials; base change their
ideal/presentation to arbitrary R using the freeness of Z[S], rather than
assuming R is Noetherian. For domain coefficients prove k[S] is a domain. Give unit groups, group completion, dimension
rank(L_S), localization to k[L_S], products and monoid-map functoriality.

Define saturation inside L_S by the existence of a positive multiple in S.
Identify it with the integral points of the rational cone, prove finite
generation/finite normalization and identify k[sat S] with the integral closure
of k[S] in its own fraction field. Prove normality iff S is saturated, with
the field/integrally-closed coefficient hypotheses explicit. Construct the
canonical comparison to `TauCeti.Toric.affineToricScheme` for dual semigroups
over C using `toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv`. Construct the integral model
`Spec (AddMonoidAlgebra Z S)` and consume native
`AddMonoidAlgebra.scalarTensorEquiv Z R` and `instIsPushout` for every
commutative coefficient ring R, together with `pullbackSpecIso`. Its C base change is the native
normal affine toric scheme when S is that cone's dual semigroup. A direct
k-to-C base change is asserted only with a chosen algebra structure k→C.
Do not normalize in a larger fraction field by enlarging the lattice.

For a monoid face F, construct its prime monomial ideal, closed face scheme
and the localized orbit Spec k[gp F]. Prove the orbit/face bijection on
geometric points, dimensions, closure order and stabilizer character group.
Retain lattice-index stabilizers, including finite nonreduced ones in positive
characteristic. Compare normalization on each orbit; it need not be a
one-to-one map on every boundary orbit. Supply the dense torus action as a
native coaction and compare cone faces and semigroup faces.

For a positive integral grading with a nonempty finite family of generators
of degree 1,
construct Proj k[S], its affine degree-zero charts and the homogeneous
monomial-map projective image. Define the Hilbert function by homogeneous
component rank and prove equality with the count of semigroup elements of
that degree. Build the rational Hilbert series and compare the eventual Hilbert polynomial
with Mathlib's `Polynomial.hilbertPoly p d` over Q when its rational Hilbert
series is `p/(1−T)^d`. Prove the graded-module/counting-series comparison
from the component ranks, using the native eventual coefficient theorem;
that polynomial API does not itself supply this module comparison. Counting
is over Q even when k has positive characteristic.
For the saturated monoid prove the Ehrhart count for the generator polytope;
construct the lattice-normalized measure and the leading-coefficient theorem.
For nonsaturated S use finite normalization/conductor estimates to prove
the same leading term. Degree is dimension factorial times the leading
coefficient, hence normalized polytope volume in the **difference lattice**
generated by a_i−a_j. Prove projective dimension rank(L_S)−1 and the primitive
simplex normalization, including the zero-dimensional projective case.
Treat the empty generator family separately: S={0}, k[S]=k in degree 0
and Proj k[S] is empty; the rank-minus-one dimension formula does not apply.

## G3. Subalgebras, SAGBI and subduction

For a subalgebra A of k[x], define its initial algebra as the subalgebra
generated by the leading terms of all its elements. The exponent set of its
nonzero elements is an additive submonoid; prove the monomial-algebra
isomorphism with the initial algebra. A SAGBI basis B is a subset of A whose
leading terms generate this algebra. Keep this definition for arbitrary B;
monicity is not part of the general SAGBI predicate. Build zero removal,
scalar-field extension, transport and inclusion APIs. Over a field, for an
indexed family first remove its zero members and put
`ell_i = m.leadingCoeff b_i`, `c_i = C(ell_i^(-1)) * b_i`.
Prove `ell_i != 0`, `m.Monic c_i`, `m.degree c_i = m.degree b_i`,
`b_i = C(ell_i) * c_i`, equality of the generated subalgebras, equality
of the algebras generated by their actual leading terms, and equivalence
of their SAGBI properties. These normalization comparisons also apply to
an infinite set; finite certificates below use finite indexed families.
Keep nonzero scalar generators as degree-zero generators, with their
relations to 1, or remove them by an explicit base-field comparison.
Neither zero polynomials nor scalar generators acquire fictitious
positive leading exponents.

Construct subduction: cancel a leading term using a product of basis elements
with that exponent, record the polynomial expression and recurse in the
well-founded monomial order. For a SAGBI basis every element subducts to zero,
so B generates A. For a general finite B, retain both the expression and the
nonzero remainder; it must not be called an element outside A merely because
the particular subduction procedure stopped.

For a finite nonzero monic family c, write a_i=m.degree c_i and
A(u)=sum_i u_i a_i for u in N^(i). Compare G2's coefficient-one semigroup
presentation with the actual homomorphisms
`psi_1(Y_i)=monomial a_i 1` and `phi_c(Y_i)=c_i` into k[x].
Prove that the semigroup-algebra embedding into k[x] is injective, so the
kernel computed by G2 is exactly ker(psi_1). Choose a finite family of
nonzero binomials `beta_j=Y^(u_j)-Y^(v_j)` generating that kernel, with
the displayed common exponent `alpha_j=A(u_j)=A(v_j)`; an empty relation
family is allowed. Prove the SAGBI criterion in this normalization:
c is SAGBI for k[c] iff each phi_c(beta_j) admits a bounded zero
subduction. The exact certificate is a polynomial Q_j in the Y variables
such that `phi_c(Q_j)=phi_c(beta_j)` and, for EVERY exponent w in the
support of Q_j, `A(w) <_m alpha_j`. Construct it by genuine leading-term
subduction. Monicity first gives
`phi_c(beta_j)=0 OR m.degree(phi_c(beta_j)) <_m alpha_j`;
when nonzero, the products in a zero-subduction expression have exponent
at most that of this substituted value. When it is exactly zero take
Q_j=0, whose support is empty. Do not assert a strict inequality for
Mathlib's totalized degree of zero; a degree-zero relation such as Y_i-1
must remain valid.

Set `F_j=beta_j-Q_j`. Prove phi_c(F_j)=0 and that its top
A-homogeneous part is exactly beta_j. Prove sufficiency and the complete
presentation `ker(phi_c)=(F_j)` by decreasing the maximal A-exponent of
a polynomial expression: its cancelling top block lies in ker(psi_1);
use that kernel's A-grading to express this block by monomial multiples
of the beta_j ALL at that same exponent, then replace them by the
strictly smaller Q_j expressions. This supplies a well-founded induction,
not merely a list of relations whose substitutions happen to vanish.
Export these standard representations, exact kernel maps and their
finite-support data. Necessity uses the SAGBI subduction theorem with
the same exponent bounds. Quotient normal forms use this presentation;
expressions in a redundant SAGBI generating family need not be unique.

Retain the coefficient change in every certificate for the original
nonmonic family. Define the polynomial algebra automorphism D_ell by
`D_ell(Y_i)=ell_i*Y_i`, with inverse D_(ell^(-1)), and prove
`phi_b=phi_c composed D_ell` and
`psi_b=psi_1 composed D_ell`, where psi_b sends Y_i to the ACTUAL
leading term of b_i. Thus `ker(psi_b)=D_ell^(-1)(ker(psi_1))` and the
same inverse transport carries F_j to generators of ker(phi_b).
Record the factor product_i ell_i^(w_i) on every monomial, and its
inverse on the transported relation and subduction coefficients;
clearing nonzero scalar denominators does not change the ideal or the
exponent bounds. This comparison preserves the original unnormalized
subalgebra and its presentation, rather than silently substituting b
into a coefficient-one relation.

Completion adjoins each nonzero subduction remainder together with its
expression in the previous generators, divides it by its nonzero leading
coefficient, and records that scalar in the same presentation maps.
Prove termination under finite generation of the full initial algebra
and fairness of relation processing; without that hypothesis completion
may be infinite even for a finitely generated A.

As a regression over Q[x,y] with lex x>y, take
`b=(x,x+y,2*x+y)`. All leading exponents are that of x. The raw
coefficient-one relations U-W,V-W evaluate to -(x+y),-x and have
one-step zero subductions, although y belongs to Q[b] and is absent
from the algebra of the actual leading terms. For the NORMALIZED family
`c=(x,x+y,x+y/2)`, those relations evaluate to -y/2,y/2; their leading
exponent is below that of x, but cannot be expressed by products of c
with exponent below that of x. The bounded criterion correctly rejects
this family. Also test a nonzero scalar generator, an empty generator
family, an exact-zero substituted relation, and redundant monic generators.

## G4. Rees algebras and flat initial families

Use native `IsFiltration` and `IsRingFiltration` for the increasing
multiplicative polynomial/subalgebra filtration by nonnegative integral
weight, with the lower stages as the native F_lt family. Construct its
Rees algebra inside A[t]. Give the graded
sum/subalgebra comparison, t action, associated graded, fibre at 0, fibre at 1,
generic localization and naturality under filtered homomorphisms. Compare
ideal-power Rees algebras through the extended Rees ring inside native
Laurent polynomials: `R[It,t^(-1)]` has nonnegative graded part equal to
Mathlib `reesAlgebra I`, and quotient by `t^(-1)` equal to `gr_I R`.
Construct `gr_I R = ⨁_{n≥0} I^n/I^(n+1)` and its graded multiplication,
unit, quotient maps and functoriality, using native direct sums and quotients.
The increasing Z-indexed I-adic filtration is F_j=R for j≥0 and
F_j=I^(−j) for j<0; its F_j/F_(j−1) pieces identify the nonpositive
indices with the displayed nonnegative associated-graded degrees.
Prove these comparisons and their generator/base-change maps; the ordinary
ideal Rees ring need not contain t as a scalar parameter. Build the homogenized polynomial presentation and prove its
t-saturation; multiplying an equation by a power of t can create an unwanted
component at 0.

For finitely generated ideals construct the flat weight-initial quotient
family. For a finite SAGBI basis use G3's nonzero monic family c, binomial
relations beta_j and strict certificates Q_j to construct the finite-type
subalgebra Rees family with fibres A and its initial algebra. Choose a
positive integral ambient weight w from the following FINITE comparisons:
every nonleading exponent gamma in each c_i satisfies
`w(gamma)<w(a_i)`, and every v in support(Q_j) satisfies
`w(A(v))<w(alpha_j)`. Equalities A(u_j)=A(v_j) are retained exactly,
not approximated by inequalities. G1's finite weight-realization theorem
supplies this w. The generator weights delta_i=w(a_i) are nonnegative;
constant generators have delta_i=0 and their degree-zero relations to1.
All comparisons are on explicit finite supports, with exact zero giving
no fabricated comparison.

Prove again by the certificate induction that these data imply
`in_w(A)=k[monomial a_i 1]` and that the delta-weight initial ideal
of ker(phi_c) is ker(psi_1). One cannot infer a whole initial-ideal
equality merely from the initial forms of chosen generators.
Construct the Rees presentation by `Y_i -> c_i*t^(delta_i)` and
`t -> t`, using the lifted relations
`Y^(u_j)-Y^(v_j)-sum_v q_(j,v)*t^(w(alpha_j)-w(A(v)))*Y^v`.
The correction exponents are strictly positive; at t=0 these are
precisely beta_j and at t=1 they are F_j. Prove that they generate the
whole Rees kernel and its t-saturation from the bounded standard
representations, then identify the algebra with the ambient increasing
weight filtration Rees algebra; homogenized equations alone are not the
identification. Transport the presentation back through D_ell^(-1),
retaining all scalar factors. These steps give the finite-type family
and its actual special-fibre maps without changing A.
Prove flatness over k[t] from the actual
torsion-free module/PID theorem and identify every fibre and base change.
For homogeneous data with a positive grading and degree-zero part `k`, construct
the projective flat family using relative Proj. The standard projective route
applies when the entire family has a fixed standard-graded presentation: use a
quotient of `k[t][Z_0, …, Z_N]` with each `Z_i` of degree one, and require the
presentation maps and fibre maps to preserve this grading. In this route prove
preservation of every graded-piece Hilbert function, Hilbert polynomial,
projective dimension and degree in the fixed `P^N_{k[t]}`.

Keep nonstandard positive gradings in scope. For a finitely generated graded
Rees-family algebra `B` over `k[t]`, construct a sufficiently divisible
Veronese algebra `B^(r) = ⨁_{n≥0} B_{rn}` that is generated in degree one, prove
that construction and its fibre maps commute with base change, and give the
canonical `Proj B ≃ Proj B^(r)` comparison with
`O_{Proj B^(r)}(1) ≃ O_{Proj B}(r)`. Construct the fixed projective embedding
from the degree-one generators of `B^(r)` and prove the standard-graded
Hilbert-polynomial and ambient `K₀` conclusions there. This is the general projective-polynomial conclusion for nonstandard grading:
define the polynomial from the ample Veronese polarization by
`P_r(n)=χ(X,F⊗O_B(r)^{⊗ n})`, and compare fibres in the new Veronese degree
`n`. Further Veronese refinement by `s≥1` gives
`B^(rs)=(B^(r))^(s)`. Prove this further Veronese is generated in degree
one by grouping degree-one generators into `s`-fold products, and construct
the same-`Proj` comparison and polarization
`O_B(rs) ≃ O_{B^(r)}(s) ≃ O_B(r)^{⊗ s}` from the degree-divisible
localizations and their transition maps. Its Hilbert
polynomial is `P_{rs}(n)=P_r(sn)`, and its degree is `s^d` times the degree
for `O_B(r)`. This handles all chosen Veronese polarizations without asserting
an eventual polynomial in the original component index.

A separate comparison with an ample invertible sheaf `L` is licensed only when
the roadmap constructs a family-level isomorphism
`O_B(r) ≃ L^{⊗ r}` compatible with base change. Define
`P_L(m)=χ(X,F⊗L^{⊗ m})`; after that isomorphism and the large-degree
section comparison, the Veronese polynomial is `P_L(rn)` and its degree in
dimension `d` is `r^d deg_L(X)`. For another refinement `s`, use the tensor
power of the same isomorphism to identify `O_B(rs) ≃ L^{⊗ rs}` and obtain
`P_L(rsn)` and `(rs)^d deg_L(X)`. Ample invertibility of `O_B(1)` alone does
not supply these twist identifications. Do not assert that the graded twists
`O_B(m)` are powers of `O_B(1)` without constructing the multiplication
isomorphisms; do not identify a nonstandard graded ring's component function
with an eventual polynomial unless that statement is separately proved. For every original degree
`m`, retain the Hilbert-function comparison at that graded piece: in a
finite-type positively graded flat family over `k[t]`, each graded piece is a
finite `k[t]`-module and a submodule of the flat total module, hence torsion-free
and therefore finite free; its rank is constant. These statements distinguish
preservation of all graded-piece ranks from existence of an eventual polynomial.

For every finitely generated `Z`-graded module over a standard polynomial ring (bounded below, allowing graded shifts), define its Hilbert function by the finite-dimensional rank of each graded piece, its formal Laurent Hilbert series and its eventual polynomial.
Prove rationality and the alternating graded-syzygy numerator formula; compare
with G2's monoid-counting functions. Here κ denotes the same field k, under PR779's fixed-field
notation. For the standard-graded family above embedded in a fixed `P^N_{κ[t]}`, prove
`[i_0* O_{X_0}]=[i_1* O_{X_1}]` in `Chow.K0(P^N_κ)`. For a nonstandard
family, use the fixed projective embedding obtained from the chosen Veronese
algebra and state the equality in that embedding's ambient `P^M_κ`. First form
the coherent pushforward classes in `Chow.G0`, then transport through PR779's
`K0.toG0_bijective` for the regular ambient projective space. This roadmap
owns the projective-space comparison. Consume O(d), coherent cohomology,
Serre vanishing and proper G0 pushforward from §§0.3,2.6,5.7. For
π:P^N_κ→Spec κ define the Hilbert-polynomial map by
`[F] ↦ (m ↦ rank π_!([F]·[O(m)]))`, proving additivity, polynomiality
and independence of representatives. Prove K0 is free on `[O(−i)]`,
0≤i≤N, and this map injective. For spanning, prove every coherent sheaf
on P^N_κ is the sheafification of a finitely generated graded module.
Use its graded free resolution to express its class through O(d), and
prove the exact projective coordinate Koszul complex gives
`(1−[O(−1)])^(N+1)=0`; reduce all twists to the stated basis.
For independence use the binomial Euler polynomials of O(m−i).
Construct the graded-module sheafification API on projective space: restriction
and localization charts, exactness, `S(−d)~ = O(−d)`,
`(S/I)~ = i_*O_X`, and the comparison of `(S/I)_m` with
`Γ(X,O_X(m))` for sufficiently large m. Prove graded Hilbert syzygy
over κ[x_0,...,x_N], giving finite graded free resolutions and their
sheafified locally free resolutions. Identify each fibre class's polynomial
with its preserved Hilbert polynomial; injectivity proves the equality.
For the standard-graded (including Veronese-regraded) flat initial families,
also prove the direct numerator formula
`[i_*O_X]=Σ_d k_d[O(−d)]` where
`Σ_d k_d T^d = HS_(S/I)(T)(1−T)^(N+1)`. Their preserved full Hilbert
function makes these numerators equal. For every closed subscheme X of P^N_A over a Noetherian ring A,
construct its saturated homogeneous-ideal presentation and prove the
closed-subscheme/presentation comparison, restriction and Proj base change.
For a flat X over A=κ[t], prove its saturated graded quotient is
torsion-free over κ[t], using the projective affine charts and saturation;
each graded piece is finite free. Identify fibre schemes with Proj of
the base-changed quotient, and deduce constant fibre Hilbert polynomials
using the large-degree section comparison. Small-degree functions of the
separately saturated fibre presentations need not be constant. This supplies
the general scheme-flat family used in the K0 equality above. The two classes are in that one ambient
group; no identification of the intrinsic K0 groups or cohomology rings of
the fibres is asserted.

## G5. Minor, flag-minor and invariant algebras

Construct generic rectangular matrix minors with sorted indices, alternating
signs and the repeated-index zero rule. Follow `Matrix.mvPolynomialMinor`
and `determinantalIdeal` on pair-indexed variables; construct the
`MvPolynomial.renameEquiv` comparison along `toLex`, including all minors
and determinantal ideals. The flag-minor formula below is the transported
first-column minor under that equivalence. Fix row-major lexicographic variable
order, with z_(0,0) largest, then z_(0,1), and so on; prove every minor with
sorted rows and columns has its main diagonal as leading term. Construct this
as a native `MonomialOrder` through the lexicographically ordered variable
index, not the product partial order. Prove determinant exchange/shuffle
identities with all indices/signs, polynomial identities over Z and their
base changes. For maximal minors, give the polynomial presentation by Plücker
relations, prime ideal, standard-monomial basis and a certified Gröbner order.
On Plücker variables P_I, use graded reverse lexicographic order with
P_I<P_J when sorted row subsets I precede J lexicographically. Prove
the quadratic straightening relations are a Gröbner basis and their initial
ideal is generated by P_I P_J for pairs incomparable in componentwise order.
Prove spanning by a well-founded straightening order and independence by
distinct diagonal leading monomials. Use native bounded semistandard tableaux,
with weak rows/strict columns, rather than a second tableau type. This is the
polynomial algebra theorem; scheme and section identifications are consumers.

For an n-by-n matrix fix flag minors using increasing row subset I and the
first card(I) columns. Prove diagonal SAGBI and standard-monomial bases of
the flag-minor subalgebra, with its fundamental multigrading. Identify its
initial exponent monoid with the nonnegative part of native `GTPattern n`,
constructing the complete pointwise `AddCommMonoid` API, its nonnegative
`AddSubmonoid`, and `shift m` as addition of the constant pattern. The map
from diagonal exponent e to a pattern is
`P.entry c j = if n < j then 0 else Σ_{r<j} e(r,c)`;
prove its inverse by successive differences, its interlacing/nonnegativity
and additive equivalence with the generated initial monoid. For row subset
`I={i_0<...<i_(d−1)}`, the diagonal exponent is that of `∏_{c<d}z_(i_c,c)`.
The row-subset generators number 2^n−1, including the determinant. Prove finite
generation, saturation, pattern/tableau/content comparisons and the Rees

# Hamiltonian Floer operations: geometric product and multiplicative PSS

Construct the geometric pair-of-pants product on capped Hamiltonian Floer complexes, its unit and sewing identities, and the multiplicative Piunikhin–Salamon–Schwarz comparison with GromovWittenTheory G7. The construction includes classical oriented counts on positive spherical-monotone and spherical-c1-zero targets, and the rational virtual punctured application on arbitrary closed symplectic targets. The definitive specification is this README; `Suggested.lean` gives nonexhaustive interface prototypes.

## H0. Scope and prerequisites

The main target is a closed connected boundaryless symplectic manifold (X^(2n),ω), n≥1, with its actual finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth structure. Work componentwise for disconnected targets; the zero-dimensional case has the separate point/count model. Hamiltonians are smooth period-one functions; the contractible one-periodic orbits used as generators are nondegenerate. Their finiteness is the actual clopen-contractible-sector argument of DGF7.C.1. Degenerate Hamiltonians have an invariant homology interpretation through specified nondegenerate perturbations and continuation, not unperturbed generator counts.

There are two geometric coefficient branches. **Classical**: positive spherical-monotone or spherical-c1-zero targets with DGF7.C's actual regular count-dimensional cylinder/PSS package, first mod2 and then oriented integral counts and scalar extensions. This owner proves the additional punctured product/family and sphere-incidence theorems; a cylinder exclusion theorem is not a product exclusion theorem. **Rational virtual**: arbitrary closed symplectic targets, with a coherent punctured Hamiltonian atlas/count package constructed here, including cylinder, plane and comparison families outside DGF's classical hypotheses. G7's rational coefficients are the common comparison coefficients. An integral product in the classical branch is retained; an arbitrary closed integral virtual theory is not inferred from a rational implicit-atlas trace.

Use the following exact prerequisite interfaces and keep their applications distinct.

- [DGFloer, capped classical branch7.C](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/71c960fc2d43fabd27cd77c770128a0271e39225/TauCetiRoadmap/DGFloer/README.md): the cap cover/period datum, cylinders, continuation, ordered orientation conventions and module PSS on its stated positive spherical-monotone and spherical-c1-zero branches. Consume the actual supported complexes and both module inverse homotopies, not a bare isomorphism type. H1–H3 construct the three-ended cap/domain/energy application, and H5 constructs the broader rational virtual extension and its classical overlap.
- [HeegaardFloer F0/F1/F2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957): the Banach/Sobolev, punctured linear Fredholm, CZ/relative-Chern/determinant and local curve interfaces at their actual hypotheses. H2–H5 construct the inhomogeneous product, matching, sphere-incidence and parameter-family applications.
- [AnalyticStableMaps M3](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/987): unforced marked genus-zero stable-map compactness, evaluation and class splitting. H3–H5 construct its attached inhomogeneous, fixed-asymptotic and varying frozen-J application; unforced compactness is not itself punctured Floer compactness.
- [MorseNovikov N1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/890): exact finite-sublevel Novikov completion, finite convolution, continuous coefficient/period pushforward and finite-orbit module laws. H3/H6 prove their geometric support hypotheses and H1/H7 their coefficient comparison.
- [GromovWittenTheory G0/G5–G7](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/990): closed stable-map support and invariants, the unit, ordered diagonal/left-dual conventions and quantum ring. H7 constructs the Morse-incidence chain application and geometric PSS comparison, without rebuilding this generic closed theory.
- [ImplicitAtlases V0–V7](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/974): the stated atlas, relative virtual complex, H-level trace, specified refinement/concordance, finite cell-like/product and transverse-diagonal machinery. H5 constructs the punctured atlas, thickened gluing and coherent trace diagrams before applying these interfaces.
- [HF Lane M](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957), [MorseTheory](../MorseTheory/README.md), [AlgebraicTopology](../AlgebraicTopology/README.md) and [DifferentialGeometry](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md): actual oriented Morse/singular comparison, continuation, fundamental class, Poincare duality, forms and parameter/flow calculus at the coefficients and manifold hypotheses used below. H7 constructs their incidence/PD comparison with G7.
- [DGAInfinity](../DGAInfinity/README.md): generic graded tensor, Hom, differential, shift and DG algebra vocabulary. H4/H6 construct the actual shifted Floer determinant-to-operator realization.

[SymplecticFieldTheory](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1054) owns contact/Reeb buildings and its contact/full-SFT levels; its count package is distinct from this Hamiltonian application. [FukayaTheory](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1045) owns the distinct Lagrangian m2 construction.

The primary closed quantum product does not assert a product on every arbitrary-symplectomorphism component, a full extended TFT, SH/Viterbo multiplicativity, or an unrestricted noncompact invariant. Existing DGF atoroidal, arbitrary-seam and Liouville targets remain intact on their hypotheses. An application to those settings requires its own relative cap/reference and no-escape/sewing contracts; it is not an implicit consequence of the closed theorem here.

## H1. Coefficients, caps and degree dictionary before counts

Use DGF's contractible convention: i_(X_H)ω=dH, u_s+J(u_t−X_H)=0, positive ends are inputs, negative ends outputs, A_H(x,D)=∫Dω+∫Hdt, μ=−CZ_HF, μ(constant)=ind(H)−n. For D'−D=B, A increases by ω(B) and μ by 2c1(B). Let S_sph be the spherical Hurewicz image and Γ=S_sph/(kerω∩kerc1). Caps are actual Γ-torsors. The joint kernel, not area alone, preserves equal-energy different-degree classes. Construct class addition, cap gluing and cap/reference changes before matrices.

The Floer ring uses e^B with degree +2c1(B) and valuation ν(B)=−ω(B). For a punctured pair of pants u with input reference caps D1,D2 and output cap D0, put A=D0+u−D1−D2 using the oriented compactification. Its coefficient in the reference-output basis is e^(−A). The raw Fredholm index is

    ind D_u = μ1+μ2−μ0−n+2c1(A).

Thus a rigid coefficient satisfies μ0−2c1(A)=μ1+μ2−n: the product CF_i⊗CF_j→CF_(i+j−n) has degree −n. Define the comparison cochain regrading C^k=CF_(n−k), with differential d_C=d_CF; its product has degree zero and d_C has degree +1. The cap-dependent orientation lines are regraded at the same time. The regrading is an actual construction with sign/shift identities, not a renaming of an unrelated complex.

Let Γ_G be G7's chosen class group with energy and Chern maps. First work over a common class group retaining the classes needed by both constructions. Prove descent to any joint-period quotient and the finite coefficient-summing map, rather than assuming GW invariants are individually cap-quotient classes. The comparison sends q^A to e^(−A): ν(−A)=ω(A). G7's degree +2c1(A) becomes cochain coefficient degree −deg_CF(e^(−A))=+2c1(A). Its energy completion therefore maps in the correct direction. The map is a continuous unital coefficient map only with the actual positive-rescaling period identity and finite-sublevel hypotheses of N1. No t↦1 map on the entire completed Novikov ring is asserted.

General Γ need not have injective valuation, and the resulting graded completed algebra need not be a field. Positive monotonicity has the finite Laurent model before completion; c1-zero has its separate completed integer grading. For arbitrary classes use homogeneous graded pieces and the energy-compatible completion (or the resulting residue grading), not an integer direct sum containing every inhomogeneous infinite series. The PD comparison is H^k(X;Q)→H_(2n−k)(X;Q)→FH_(n−k). Over other rings retain actual orientation, UCT, tensor/base-change and perfect-pairing hypotheses; G7's Q comparison does not prove them automatically.

## H2. Actual punctured domains and perturbation data

Take S=P1 minus three distinct ordered points, with positive strip-like cylindrical ends e1,e2 and negative e0, all period1 and oriented ds∧dt. Fix markers, end coordinates, collars and their changes. Its Euler characteristic is −1 and there is no translation quotient of the entire pair-of-pants domain. Use a fixed three-marked sphere model and explicit plumbing families for compositions; distinguish map-stable domains from stable pointed domains. The inserted Floer cylinders have their own translation quotient, with stationary cylinders treated by the actual invertible block.

Choose K in Ω1(S;C∞(X)) equal to H_i(t)dt on each tail and compatible J_z equal to the already selected J_i(t) there. Compact cores have independent localized δK variations; domain-dependent J variations have their actual compatible tangent condition, and their tame versions have the distinct allowed tangent condition. Construct nonempty extensions of all fixed end/corner data and the complete smooth coefficient carriers before any regularity selection. Extend prescribed product/continuation/cap faces with all corner jets and all-order flat interior variations. Genuine unary operations, nonconstant components, curvature data and marked/unit insertions are retained; only undecorated unstable metric/combinatorial subdivisions are suppressed.

For K=K_s ds+K_t dt define {F,G}=ω(X_F,X_G), R_K=∂sK_t−∂tK_s−{K_s,K_t}. The equation is (du−X_K)^(0,1)=0. Prove its covariant linearization with the K and ∇J terms, weighted end operator and evaluation constraints. In every compact parameter/energy/index window fix the full F0 differentiability list, including ALL moving-domain, neck, incidence and external parameters. There is no genericity assertion on a face merely from genericity of its pieces.

## H3. Energy, support and raw compactness before regular counts

With compatible J put E=∫ω(u_s−X_(K_s),u_t−X_(K_t))≥0. The exact identity is

    E = ∫u*ω + ∫∂ K(u) − ∫R_K(u)
      = A1(x1,D1)+A2(x2,D2)−A0(x0,D0)+ω(A)−∫R_K(u).

If B=−A is the output monomial, ν(B)=ω(A). A bound ∫sup_X|R_K|≤C implies ν(B)≥−A1−A2+A0−C. Conversely ν(B)<L bounds E above by A1+A2−A0+L+C. These are the exact lower-support and energy-cutoff implications. Include reference-cap constants, Hamiltonian normalization changes, all inhomogeneous terms and class splitting. On tame compact windows use the actual positive symmetric metric/coercivity and operator homotopy; do not call ω(·,J·) a symmetric metric for a merely tame J.

Prove uniform integrated curvature bounds over EVERY declared stretched/collapsed/relative family. Use long necks with cylindrical K=Hdt and R_K=0; transition collars have bounded fixed geometry, and synthesized perturbations have the integrated coefficient/target-derivative controls of DGF7.C.2b. A C0 bound times an infinite neck length is insufficient. At cutoff-zero comparison faces make K vanish in the specified domain coordinates with an explicit uniform curvature allowance. Moving reference and cap terms have their own bounds.

Construct raw Gromov–Floer convergence and compactness for bounded energy and compact parameter windows, including Floer breaking at each end, sphere trees attached at actual frozen J_(p,z), marked collisions, ghost components and all parameter faces. A bubble at an unstable attachment freezes J at that attachment; a domain-dependent J does not turn it into a sphere for an unrelated global J. Work with stable domain charts and their actual forgetful/attachment maps. Cap classes add under every degeneration.     d m2(a,b)=m2(da,b)+(-1)^a m2(a,db).

# Roadmap: heights, units and S-units of number fields

Dirichlet's unit theorem says that the units of a number field form a lattice of rank `r₁ + r₂ − 1`
modulo torsion, and Mathlib proves it. The height of an algebraic number says how large it is
arithmetically. This roadmap writes the dictionary between the two. A unit's height is the ℓ¹ norm
of its logarithmic embedding, up to the coordinate that embedding drops. The torsion units are
exactly the units of height one. The regulator is bounded above and below by products of heights
of a fundamental system, and the lower bound is sharp enough to choose a fundamental system of
controlled height. The roadmap then carries all of this to `S`-units. It proves the `S`-unit
theorem, builds the `S`-logarithmic lattice and defines the `S`-regulator.

Two pieces of geometry of numbers are needed on the way, and both are built here. The first is a
lattice **basis** controlled by the successive minima, not merely an independent family. The
second applies it to the kernel of an integer matrix. The result is a `ℤ`-**basis** of the integral
kernel of bounded sup norm, at the cost `k!/2^{k−1}` over the Bombieri–Vaaler bound for
independent vectors, with the gcd of the maximal minors. The roadmap also owns a small set of height
estimates that every consumer of heights needs and that no other roadmap supplies:
- the affine height of a tuple,
- bounds for values of linear forms and determinants,
- the `Northcott` instances for projective points and subspaces,
- the projective form of Kronecker's theorem,
- the lower bound for the height away from one at bounded degree.

"Done" means a contributor who needs a fundamental system of units of bounded height, an
`S`-unit group of known rank with an explicit fundamental system, a lattice basis inside dilates of
a convex body, or an integer kernel basis of bounded sup norm finds each one stated in its
natural generality, with its basic API, in Mathlib's vocabulary.

Suggested home: `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Height/` for Layers 0–1, beside the height foundation of
[DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence](../DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence/README.md);
`TauCeti/NumberTheory/GeometryOfNumbers/` for Layer 2; `TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/`
for Layer 3; and `TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SUnit.lean` with
`TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/SUnits/` for Layer 4.

## Standing hypotheses and pinned conventions

Work over a field with `[Height.AdmissibleAbsValues K]` wherever the mathematics allows. Layers 0
and 1 are stated at that generality, except where an absolute height forces characteristic zero
or a number field. Layers 3 and 4 are about a number field `K` of degree `d = [K : ℚ]`, with
`r = NumberField.Units.rank K`. Tuples are indexed by an arbitrary finite type, never by `Fin n`
alone.

| Question | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| multiplicative or logarithmic | **Both** for every owned object. The multiplicative one is primary and `logX := Real.log (mulX)`, as in Mathlib. |
| relative or absolute | **Both, distinguished by name.** Over a fixed `K`, `Height.mulHeight` is relative. The absolute height carries the `abs` prefix (`NumberField.absMulHeight₁`) or is DAT's `absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight`. Layer 3 states its regulator bounds in the **absolute logarithmic** height `h = absLogHeight₁`, as Bugeaud–Győry do, and its comparisons with `logEmbedding` in the **relative** `logHeight₁`, which is `d · h`. |
| local factor at a place | `⨆ i, v (x i)`, written out, never wrapped in a definition. |
| the affine height | `Height.mulHeightAff x := Height.mulHeight (fun o : Option ι ↦ o.elim 1 x)`, the projective height of `(1, x)`. It is **not** scaling-invariant, and that is its whole purpose. |
| `S` | `S : Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))`, **finite places only**, with the infinite places always present. These are the carriers of `S.integer K` and `S.unit K`. The rank of `S.unit K` is `r + #S`. Bombieri–Gubler 1.5.10 instead includes the archimedean places in `S` and so writes the rank as `\|S\| − 1`. A contributor reading the book translates, and every statement here is in Mathlib's convention. |
| fundamental system | A family `ε : Fin r → (𝓞 K)ˣ` with `Subgroup.closure (Set.range ε) ⊔ torsion K = ⊤`, which is what Mathlib's `closure_fundSystem_sup_torsion_eq_top` says of `fundSystem K`. |
| ℓ¹ norm on `logSpace K` | Mathlib's `‖·‖` on the `Pi` type `logSpace K` is the **supremum** norm. Every ℓ¹ norm is written as `∑ w, |x w|`, and the sup-norm forms are separate statements. |
| declaration names | Statement-named, as in Mathlib. Siegel, Bombieri–Vaaler, Kronecker, Northcott and Dirichlet appear in docstrings, never in identifiers. The exception is a name that is the standard name of an object, such as `Northcott` the typeclass. |

## The build, in layers

### Layer 0: affine heights and the value bounds

**0.1 The affine height of a tuple.** Define
`Height.mulHeightAff (x : ι → K) := Height.mulHeight fun o : Option ι ↦ o.elim 1 x`, with
`logHeightAff` alongside, over any `[Height.AdmissibleAbsValues K]` and `[Finite ι]`. Prove:
- `1 ≤ mulHeightAff x`.
- `mulHeight x ≤ mulHeightAff x` and `mulHeight₁ (x i) ≤ mulHeightAff x`. The second fails for
  `mulHeight`.
- `mulHeightAff (x ∘ f) ≤ mulHeightAff x` for any `f`, with equality for a bijection.
- `mulHeightAff 0 = 1`.
- `mulHeightAff ![x] = mulHeight₁ x`, which is the test that the appended coordinate is the right
  one.
- The non-invariance as a theorem, `exists_mulHeightAff_smul_ne`: over `ℚ`, `![1]` and `![2]` have
  affine heights `1` and `2` and the same projective height.
- The bridge to DAT: for a number field `K` and `f : K →+* AlgebraicClosure ℚ`,
  `absoluteLogHeightAff (f ∘ x) = logHeightAff x / [K : ℚ]` for `x : Fin n → K`. DAT prepends the
  `1` with `Fin.cons`, and this layer appends it with `Option.elim`; the bridge is a reindexing.
(Bombieri–Gubler 1.5.)

**0.2 Values of linear forms and determinants.** Prove:
- `mulHeight₁ (∑ i, a i * x i) ≤ #ι ^ totalWeight K · mulHeightAff a · mulHeightAff x` for
  nonempty `ι`, with its logarithmic form. No bound in the projective heights of `a` and `x`
  exists, because `a ↦ c • a` scales the value and fixes `mulHeight a`.
- `mulHeight₁ A.det ≤ (#n)! ^ totalWeight K · ∏ j, mulHeightAff (fun i ↦ A i j)`, columnwise,
  from the Leibniz expansion and DAT §1.3's signed tuple sum bound
  `Height.mulHeight_sum_sign_comp_le`. Also the corollary `mulHeight₁ A.det ≤ (#n)! ^ totalWeight K · mulHeightAff (entries A) ^ #n`.
- The rejection test `exists_not_mulHeight₁_det_le`: a `1 × 1` matrix has `matrixMulHeight A = 1`
  and determinant its entry.
- Sharpness: `a = x = ![1, 1]` attains the linear-form constant.

**0.3 Arakelov bounds with constant one.** Over a number field, with DAT's `arakelovMulHeight`
applied to the tuple of entries `fun p : m × n ↦ A p.1 p.2`, prove:
- `arakelovMulHeight (fun j ↦ ∑ i, A (j, i) * x i) ≤ arakelovMulHeight A · arakelovMulHeight x`.
- `arakelovMulHeight (entries (A * B)) ≤ arakelovMulHeight (entries A) · arakelovMulHeight (entries B)`.
- Their logarithmic forms.

These need no `Nonempty` hypothesis and carry no cardinality. That is the contrast with DAT's
`matrixMulHeight_mul_le`, whose constant is `(card n) ^ totalWeight K` and which needs a nonempty
inner index. At an infinite place the local factor is the Frobenius norm, and Cauchy–Schwarz makes
it submultiplicative; at a finite place the ultrametric inequality does the same. The
linear-map bound is the one-column case of the matrix bound. Test: over `ℚ`, `A = [1 1]`,
`B = [[1, 0], [1, 1]]` give `matrixMulHeight (A B) = 2` against `matrixMulHeight A = matrixMulHeight B = 1`,
so the sup-norm constant `2 ^ totalWeight K` is attained, while the Arakelov bound holds with
constant `1`.

### Layer 1: Northcott instances and Kronecker's theorem

**1.1 Northcott on projective space.** Over a field with
`[Northcott (Height.mulHeight₁ (K := K))]`, prove `Northcott (Projectivization.mulHeight (K := K) (ι := ι))`
and the `logHeight` instance. Mathlib's `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Northcott.lean` records both
as TODOs. The number-field instances then follow by instance resolution. Route:
- **Normalization.** `Projectivization.exists_rep_apply_eq_one_of_ne_zero` gives a representative
  with a chosen nonvanishing coordinate equal to `1`, and `exists_rep_apply_eq_one` is its
  corollary.
- **Coordinate bound.** `Height.mulHeight₁_div_le_mulHeight`, that
  `mulHeight₁ (x i / x j) ≤ mulHeight x`, is `Height.mulHeight_comp_le` along `![i, j]`.
- **Finiteness.** A bounded-height point is in the image of a finite set of normalized tuples.
  No ring of integers and no ideal norm enter.

There is **no** `Northcott` instance for `Height.mulHeight` on `ι → K`: the whole line `Kˣ • x` has
one height. (Hindry–Silverman B.2.3; Bombieri–Gubler 2.4.9 for `ℙⁿ`.)

**1.2 Northcott for subspaces.** Over a number field, `Northcott` instances for DAT's
`relativeSubspaceHeight`, `relativeSubspaceArakelovHeight` and `subspaceHeight`, and for their
logarithms, on `Submodule K (ι → K)` with **no rank condition**. Route:
- **Absolute height.** For `subspaceHeight` this is DAT's `finite_subspaceHeight_le`.
- **Relative Arakelov height.** `relativeSubspaceArakelovHeight = subspaceHeight ^ [K : ℚ]`, so
  its sublevel sets are those of `subspaceHeight`.
- **Relative sup height.** This needs the **reverse** comparison, because a bound on the smaller
  height must bound the larger one. Prove `relativeSubspaceArakelovHeight_le`: for
  `n = #ι` and `k = finrank K T`,
  `relativeSubspaceArakelovHeight T ≤ (n.choose k) ^ ([K : ℚ]/2) · relativeSubspaceHeight T`.
  It is the upper half of DAT's `arakelovMulHeight_sup_comparison` on the Plücker vector, whose
  index `Set.powersetCard ι k` has `n.choose k` elements and is nonempty because `k ≤ n`. Both
  heights are invariant under scaling, so the representative `relativePluckerPoint` picks does
  not matter. Bound `n.choose k ≤ 2 ^ n` uniformly. Then
  `{T | relativeSubspaceHeight T ≤ B}` lies inside
  `{T | relativeSubspaceArakelovHeight T ≤ 2 ^ (n [K : ℚ]/2) · B}`, which is finite by the
  previous item.
- **Logarithms.** These follow by `Northcott.comp_of_bddAbove` along `Real.log`, as Mathlib
  derives `Northcott (logHeight₁)`.

The rank-free statement is what the typeclass needs, because `Northcott h` quantifies over the
whole domain of `h`. The deliverable is the instance, through which `Northcott.exists_min_image`
produces a subspace of least height with a prescribed property.

**1.3 Kronecker's theorem and the height gap.** Over a field `F` of characteristic zero:
- **Kronecker.** For `x` integral over `ℚ`, `absMulHeight₁ x = 1 ↔ x = 0 ∨ ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ x ^ n = 1`,
  and `absLogHeight₁ x = 0 ↔ …`. The hard direction is DAT's `mahlerMeasure_eq_one_iff` through
  `mahlerMeasure_eq_absMulHeight₁_pow`. The easy direction is the power law
  `absMulHeight₁ (x ^ n) = absMulHeight₁ x ^ n` with `1 ≤ absMulHeight₁`.
- **Tuple power law.** `absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight (fun i ↦ x i ^ N) = absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight x ^ N`.
  It is local: `(⨆ i, v (x i))^N = ⨆ i, v (x i ^ N)`.
- **Projective Kronecker.** For a nonzero tuple `x` of algebraic coordinates,
  `absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight x = 1` if and only if every ratio `x i / x j` with `x j ≠ 0` is
  zero or a root of unity. The converse direction is a statement about tuples,
  `absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight_eq_one_of_forall_eq_zero_or_pow_eq_one`. Its proof: with `N` a
  common order of the nonzero coordinates, `x ^ N` has coordinates in `{0, 1}`, so it is its own
  square, and its height is an idempotent `≥ 1`. (Hindry–Silverman B.2.3.1.)
- **The gap.** `1 < absMulHeight₁ x` for `x` integral over `ℚ`, nonzero and not a root of unity.
  Also, for each `D`, `∃ c > 0` with `c ≤ absLogHeight₁ x` for every such `x` with
  `[ℚ⟮x⟯ : ℚ] ≤ D`. The proof is DAT's bounded-degree Northcott plus Kronecker, and the constant
  is **ineffective**: it is the minimum of a finite set. (Bombieri–Gubler 1.6.15.)
- **Refutation.** The dependence of `c` on `D` is essential: `2 ^ (1/N)` has
  `absLogHeight₁ = (log 2)/N`. State it as "for every `c > 0` there is such an `x` with height
  below `c`". The same family keeps `[ℚ(x):ℚ] · h(x) ≤ log 2`, so it does not bear on Lehmer's
  question.

### Layer 2: a basis from the minima, and Bombieri–Vaaler in the sup norm

**2.1 A basis from the minima** (Cassels, *An Introduction to the Geometry of Numbers*, Ch. V,
Lemma 8; Ch. I, Thm. I). Let `E` be a finite-dimensional real normed space, `L` a discrete
`Submodule ℤ E` and `B` a convex, symmetric set with nonempty interior.

*General form.* For any `ℝ`-independent `a : Fin n → E` with `a i ∈ L` and `n = finrank ℝ E`,
there is a `ℤ`-basis `b` of `L` with
`gauge B (b j) ≤ max (gauge B (a j)) ((∑ i ≤ j, gauge B (a i)) / 2)`. `IsZLattice ℝ L` is a
consequence, not a hypothesis. Route, by induction on `j`, with `V_j = span_ℝ {a i : i < j}`:
1. A basis of `L ∩ V_j` extends by one vector `y` to a basis of `L ∩ V_{j+1}`. This is GoN's
   §0.2.7 `saturated_adapted_basis_of_basis`, applied inside `V_{j+1}`.
2. Write `a j = c • y + w` with `c` a nonzero integer and `w ∈ L ∩ V_j`.
3. If `|c| = 1`, take `b j = c · a j`.
4. Otherwise replace `y` by `y − ∑ round(t_i) • a i`, where `y = c⁻¹ • a j + ∑ t_i • a i`. The
   result still extends the basis, and has gauge at most `½ gauge B (a j) + ½ ∑_{i<j} gauge B (a i)`.

The proof uses `gauge B (r • x) = |r| · gauge B x` for symmetric convex `B`, stated as
`gauge_smul_of_symmetric`. Over `ℝ` a convex symmetric set is balanced: for `x ∈ B` and
`|t| ≤ 1`, `t • x` lies on the segment from `-x` to `x`. Mathlib has no lemma saying so, so state
it as `balanced_of_convex_of_neg_mem`; then `gauge_smul_of_symmetric` is Mathlib's `gauge_smul`.

*Minima form.* In GoN's vocabulary: for `K : ConvexBody E` symmetric with `0 ∈ interior K` and `L`
a full lattice, there is a `ℤ`-basis `b` of `L` with
`b i ∈ (max 1 ((i + 1)/2) · successiveMin L K i) • K` for every `i : Fin (finrank ℝ E)`. Apply the
general form to GoN's `exists_successiveMin_witnesses`. This is strictly more than GoN's
`exists_integral_minimum_flag`, which bounds no vector of the basis.

Further requirements:
- The loss against Minkowski's second theorem is
  `∏_{i<n} max 1 ((i+1)/2) = n! / 2^{n−1}`. State it as `prod_max_one_add_one_div_two`.
- The `max` is forced at `i = 0`, where `λ_0` is attained.
- The general form needs no measure, no closedness and no boundedness. Those enter only in the
  minima form.

**2.2 Integral kernel bases and the minor gcd** (Bombieri–Vaaler 1983, Theorems 1 and 2;
Aliev–Henk 2023, §6; Cassels V Lemma 8). For an integer matrix `A : Matrix (Fin m) ι ℤ` whose rows
are linearly independent over `ℚ`, let `minorGcd A` be the gcd of its `m × m` minors, and let
`k = #ι − m` be the rank of the integral kernel `ker A = {x : ι → ℤ | A *ᵥ x = 0}`.

*Owned here.*
- **The arithmetic identity.**
  `minorGcd A · subspaceHeight (ker A) = √det(A Aᵀ)`, together with
  `linearIndependent_rows_rat_iff : rows independent over ℚ ↔ det(A Aᵀ) ≠ 0`, `0 < det(A Aᵀ)`
  and `1 ≤ minorGcd A`. This turns DAT §2.8's remark on the `K = ℚ` constant into a theorem.
- **Invariance.** `√det(A Aᵀ) / minorGcd A` is unchanged by `A ↦ U A` for `U ∈ GL_m(ℤ)`
  (`sqrt_det_div_minorGcd_unit_mul`, from `minorGcd_unit_mul` and the Gram determinant's
  `det U ^ 2 = 1`). Classical Siegel's bound `(#ι · max |A i j|)^{m/(#ι−m)}` moves under this
  substitution.
- **The geometric half.** For any lattice `L` in a subspace `V` of `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`, with
  `cubeSlice V` the slice of `[−1, 1]^ι`, `∏ i, successiveMin L (cubeSlice V) i ≤ covolume L`.
  The `2^k` of GoN's `minkowski_second_upper` cancels the `2^k` of DAT's `siegelProductBallSlice`.
- **An integral kernel basis.** A `Module.Basis (Fin k) ℤ (ker A)`, so a basis of the whole
  integral kernel and not only of a sublattice of finite index, with
  `∏ l, (⨆ i, |b l i|) ≤ k!/2^{k−1} · √det(A Aᵀ) / minorGcd A`. At `k = 0` both sides are `1`.
- **Sharpness of Siegel's exponent.** The `m × (m+1)` system `B x_i = x_{i+1}` has every nonzero
  integer solution of sup norm at least `B^m`, against Siegel's bound `((m+1)B)^m`.

Assembly of the basis:
1. The covolume of `ℤ^ι ∩ ker A` in its real span equals `subspaceHeight (ker A)`. This is the
   `K = ℚ` case of DAT's `kernelLattice_covolume`.
2. The arithmetic identity rewrites it as `√det(A Aᵀ) / minorGcd A`. Its proof is DAT's
   `subspaceHeight_orthogonal`, which passes to the row space, and `plucker_cauchyBinet`, which
   computes the rows' Plücker norm as `√det(A Aᵀ)`.
3. The geometric half bounds the product of the minima of the cube slice by that covolume.
4. The minima form of 2.1 converts the minima into a basis. The cube slice's gauge is the sup
   norm, and the loss is `prod_max_one_add_one_div_two k = k!/2^{k−1}`.

*Adapters of DAT's `siegelKernelBasis`, not owned.* At `K = ℚ` DAT's theorem gives a `ℚ`-basis of
the kernel in `ℤ^ι` with `∏ Habs(x_l) ≤ H₂(rowSpace A)`. Dividing each vector by its content keeps
it in the kernel, keeps the family independent, and makes its sup norm equal to its height
(Mathlib's `Rat.mulHeight_eq_max_abs_of_gcd_eq_one`). With the arithmetic identity this is the
sup-norm form of Bombieri–Vaaler's Theorem 2: `ℤ`-independent `x : Fin k → (ι → ℤ)`, each primitive, with
`A *ᵥ x l = 0` and `∏ l, (⨆ i, |x l i|) ≤ √det(A Aᵀ) / minorGcd A`. Theorem 1 is the smallest
vector of that family: for `m < #ι` a nonzero `x` with
`⨆ i, |x i| ≤ (√det(A Aᵀ) / minorGcd A)^{1/k}`. State both as corollaries.

The independent family need **not** span `ker A`. For `A = [0, 0, 1]`, the vectors
`(1, 1, 0)` and `(1, −1, 0)` meet the bound `1`, but they span a sublattice of index `2` that misses
`(1, 0, 0)`. The basis milestone is therefore a separate statement, and its factor `k!/2^{k−1}` is
not to be dropped.

### Layer 3: heights of units and the regulator

Throughout, `K` is a number field, `w₀` and `logEmbedding` are Mathlib's
(`NumberField.Units.dirichletUnitTheorem`), and `u : (𝓞 K)ˣ`. Sums over `{w // w ≠ w₀}` use
`open scoped Classical`, since `InfinitePlace K` has no `DecidableEq`.

**3.1 The logarithmic embedding as a height** (Bombieri–Gubler 1.5.12; Bugeaud–Győry 1996, (12)).
The finite local factors of a unit are `1`, so:
- `logHeight₁ u = ∑ w, (mult w · log (w u))⁺`, the sum over all infinite places, which by the
  product formula is
- `2 · logHeight₁ u = ∑ w, |mult w · log (w u)|`.

These are the `S = ∅` case of DAT §4.5's identity and are cited from there. What this milestone
owns is the translation to `logEmbedding`, which drops the coordinate at `w₀`:
- `2 · logHeight₁ u = ∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w| + |∑_{w ≠ w₀} logEmbedding u w|`.
- The two-sided bound `∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w| ≤ 2 · logHeight₁ u ≤ 2 ∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w|`.
- The sup-norm forms `‖logEmbedding u‖ ≤ 2 · logHeight₁ u` and
  `logHeight₁ u ≤ rank K · ‖logEmbedding u‖`.
- The absolute form `absLogHeight₁ u ≤ (∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w|) / d`.
- Both tempting identities, as criteria. `logHeight₁ u = ∑_{w ≠ w₀} (logEmbedding u w)⁺` holds
  **iff `w₀ u ≤ 1`**, and `2 · logHeight₁ u = ∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w|` holds **iff
  `w₀ u = 1`**.
- `finite_setOf_logHeight₁_le`: the units of bounded height are finite. This is Northcott along
  `(𝓞 K)ˣ → K`.

**3.2 Units of height one.**
- `absMulHeight₁ u = 1 ↔ u ∈ torsion K`, with the `mulHeight₁`, `logHeight₁` and `absLogHeight₁`
  forms. From 3.1, `2 · logHeight₁ u` is a sum of nonnegative terms and vanishes exactly when
  every `w u = 1`, which is Mathlib's `mem_torsion`.
- `logHeight₁ u = 0 ↔ logEmbedding u = 0`.
- Kronecker (1.3) removes the unit hypothesis: a nonzero `x : 𝓞 K` has `absMulHeight₁ x = 1` iff
  it has finite order. Such an `x` is a unit.
- Off the torsion the height is strictly above one, and no member of `fundSystem K` is torsion.
  Hence `0 < ∏ i, absLogHeight₁ (fundSystem K i)`.

**3.3 The regulator and the heights of a fundamental system** (Bugeaud–Győry 1996, Lemma 1, case
`S = S_∞`). Write `h = absLogHeight₁`.
- *Hadamard's bound, for every fundamental system* `ε`:
  `regulator K ≤ (2d)^r · ∏ i, h(ε i)`. Also `regOfFamily u ≤ (2d)^r · ∏ h(u i)` for any family,
  and the relative form `regulator K ≤ 2^r · ∏ logHeight₁ (ε i)`. Route: the rows of the
  `logEmbedding` matrix have ℓ¹ norm at most `2 · logHeight₁ = 2d · h` by 3.1, and
  `Matrix.abs_det_le_prod_sum_abs` bounds `|det M|` by the product of the ℓ¹ norms of the rows,
  over any linearly ordered field. For a fundamental system `regOfFamily ε = regulator K` is
  Mathlib's `regOfFamily_div_regulator` at index one. Also prove the positivity of `∏ h(ε i)` for
  every fundamental system.
- *A reduced fundamental system exists*: some fundamental system has
  `∏ i, h(ε i) ≤ (r!)² / (2^{r−1} d^r) · regulator K`, and it can be chosen to satisfy Hadamard's
  bound simultaneously. Route, which is Bugeaud–Győry's and produces exactly this constant:
  1. Let `logBall K = {x : logSpace K | ∑ w, |x w| ≤ 1}`. It is convex, symmetric, closed and
     bounded, and `volume (logBall K) = 2^r / r!` (`MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_le` at `p = 1`;
     by hand at `r = 0`).
  2. Minkowski's upper bound gives `∏ λ_i ≤ r! · regulator K`. `logSpace K` carries the sup norm
     and is not an inner-product space, so state the adapter: transport `unitLattice K` and
     `logBall K` to `EuclideanSpace ℝ {w // w ≠ w₀}` along `WithLp.linearEquiv`. That map preserves
     volume, so it preserves the covolume (`ZLattice.covolume_comap`), and the minima are preserved
     by GoN's `successiveMin_linearEquiv`. Then apply GoN's `minkowski_second_upper`.
  3. Take the basis `b` of 2.1, which costs `r!/2^{r−1}`.
  4. Take units `ε i` with `logEmbedding ε i = b i`. They form a fundamental system because `b`
     spans `unitLattice K`, the whole image of `logEmbedding`
     (`closure_sup_torsion_eq_top_of_span`).
  5. Bound `h(ε i) ≤ (∑ w, |b i w|)/d` by 3.1.
- *Rank zero, as a check.* Both products are empty, and the two bounds agree with Tau Ceti's
  `NumberField.Units.regulator_eq_one_of_rank_eq_zero`, which is consumed and not reproved.

The reduced statement is existential and cannot be made for `fundSystem K` or for every fundamental
system once `r ≥ 2`: a unimodular change of basis then makes the heights arbitrarily large at fixed
regulator. In rank one `GL₁(ℤ) = {±1}`: the fundamental systems are `ζ ε^{±1}` with `ζ` torsion, and they
all have the same height. The
statement `∃ c₁ c₂ > 0, c₁ R ≤ ∏ h(ε_i) ≤ c₂ R` for a fixed field says nothing, so the constants
are part of the target.

### Layer 4: S-integers, the S-unit theorem and the S-regulator

**4.1 The height of an S-integer** (Bombieri–Gubler 1.5.10).
- *Dictionary.* For `v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)` and `x : K`, `FinitePlace.mk v x ≤ 1 ↔
  v.valuation K x ≤ 1` and `FinitePlace.mk v x = 1 ↔ v.valuation K x = 1`. These are
  equivalences because the norm of a prime exceeds `1`. Consequently
  `Set.mem_integer_iff_finitePlace` and `Set.mem_unit_iff_finitePlace`.
- *Height identity.* For `x ∈ S.integer K`,
  `mulHeight₁ x = (∏ w : InfinitePlace K, max (w x) 1 ^ mult w) · ∏ᶠ v ∈ S, max (FinitePlace.mk v x) 1`.
  Also its logarithmic form, a `Finset` form, and the `S`-unit form derived in one line.
- *Characterization.* For `x ≠ 0`, the identity holds **iff** `x ∈ S.integer K`. A single finite
  place outside `S` where `|x|_v > 1` makes the full product strictly larger.
- *The case `S = ∅`.* `Set.mem_integer_empty_iff` (the algebraic integers) and
  `Set.mem_unit_empty_iff` (the units of `𝓞 K`), proved directly, so that the unit identity of
  3.1 is the `S = ∅` case of the display.
- *Tests.* The rational test is DAT §4.1's `mulHeight₁_sUnits_rat`. The rejection test is `1/2` at
  `S = ∅`: its infinite factor is `1` while its height is `2^d`.

**4.2 The S-unit theorem** (Bombieri–Gubler Theorem 1.5.13). Build it under the names and shapes
of mathlib4#40791, so that adopting that PR is a deletion plus an import:
- `Set.unitValuation : S.unit K →* (S → Multiplicative ℤ)`, `unitValuation_ker`, and
  `Set.unit_fg`.
- `Set.unit_finrank_numberField : finrank ℤ (Additive (S.unit K)) = Units.rank K + Nat.card S`
  for finite `S`.
- Beside it, the usable form in the shape of Mathlib's `exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`: a family
  `ε : Fin (rank K + #S) → S.unit K` such that every `S`-unit is uniquely `ζ · ∏ ε i ^ e i` with
  `ζ` torsion and `e` an integer vector.

Route:
1. The kernel of `unitValuation` is the image of `(𝓞 K)ˣ`, by 4.1's `S = ∅` statement. Its rank
   is Mathlib's `NumberField.Units.finrank_eq`.
2. The image has full rank `#S`. For each `v ∈ S`, the class of `v` has finite order in
   `ClassGroup (𝓞 K)`, and a generator of `v ^ orderOf [v]` is an `S`-unit with valuation nonzero
   at `v` and zero at the other places of `S` (`Set.exists_unitValuation_apply_ne_zero`). Only
   this torsion statement about the cokernel is needed. The class number is never computed and no
   map to the class group is built.
3. Rank–nullity over `ℤ`.

Build the fundamental system from the quotient of the `ℤ`-module `Additive (S.unit K)` by
`Submodule.torsion ℤ`, which is free, rather than from a quotient group.

**4.3 The S-logarithmic lattice and the S-regulator.** For a finite `S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))`:
- Define `SUnit.logSpace S := ({w : InfinitePlace K // w ≠ w₀} ⊕ S) → ℝ`, and
  `SUnit.logEmbedding S` sending `x` to `mult w · log (w x)` on the left and
  `log (FinitePlace.mk v x)` on the right.
- Prove the product formula for `S`-units,
  `∑ w, mult w · log (w x) + ∑ v ∈ S, log (FinitePlace.mk v x) = 0`.
- Prove the `S`-analogue of 3.1 in `logEmbedding` coordinates:
  `2 · logHeight₁ x = ∑ |logEmbedding S x| + |∑ logEmbedding S x|`, with the two-sided and
  sup-norm comparisons. The rejection test `x = 2` at `S = ∅` is an `∅`-integer but not an
  `∅`-unit, and its sum is `d · log 2`.
- `logEmbedding S (unitOfUnits u) = Sum.elim (logEmbedding u) 0`.
- Define `SUnit.unitLattice S`, the image. Prove it is a **full lattice**:
  - **Discreteness** is Northcott: a bounded embedding is a bounded height by 4.1, and Mathlib's
    `NumberField.finite_setOfPred_logHeight₁_le` finishes (`SUnit.unitLattice_inter_ball_finite`).
  - **Spanning** is Mathlib's `unitLattice_span_eq_top` for the infinite coordinates together with
    the generators of 4.2 at the places of `S` (`SUnit.unitLattice_span_eq_top`).
- **The kernel.** `SUnit.logEmbedding_ker`: the kernel of `SUnit.logEmbedding S` is the torsion
  of `S.unit K`, as `(CommGroup.torsion (S.unit K)).toAddSubgroup`, the `S`-analogue of Mathlib's
  `logEmbedding_ker`. Route: if the kept coordinates vanish, the product formula makes the
  coordinate at `w₀` vanish too, so `logHeight₁ x = 0` by the height identity above, and
  Kronecker (1.3) makes `x` a root of unity. Equivalently, the kernel is the set of `S`-units of
  height one.
- **The quotient.** By the first isomorphism theorem, `SUnit.logEmbedding S` induces a `ℤ`-linear
  equivalence from the torsion-free quotient
  `Additive (S.unit K) ⧸ Submodule.torsion ℤ (Additive (S.unit K))` onto
  `SUnit.unitLattice S` (`SUnit.exists_quotTorsionEquiv_unitLattice`, sending the class of `x`
  to `logEmbedding S x`). It is the bridge from 4.2's quotient to 4.3's lattice.
- **Fundamental systems are bases.** A family `ε : ι → S.unit K` is a fundamental system, meaning
  `Subgroup.closure (Set.range ε) ⊔ CommGroup.torsion (S.unit K) = ⊤` with
  `#ι = rank K + #S`, **iff** `fun i ↦ logEmbedding S (Additive.ofMul (ε i))` is a `ℤ`-basis of
  `SUnit.unitLattice S` (`SUnit.isFundSystem_iff_basis`). The forward direction transports
  generation along the quotient equivalence. The converse lifts a basis to `S`-units and uses
  the kernel statement. In particular 4.2's fundamental system gives a basis.
- Define `SUnit.regulator S := ZLattice.covolume (SUnit.unitLattice S)` and prove
  `SUnit.regulator_pos`.
- **The determinant formula.** For a fundamental system `ε : ι → S.unit K`, an omitted infinite
  place `w'` and any `e : ι ≃ ({w // w ≠ w'} ⊕ S)`, `SUnit.regulator S` is the absolute
  determinant of the matrix whose row `i` is the weighted logarithms of `ε i` at the places
  `e`-indexed by its columns: `mult w · log (w (ε i))` at an infinite place and
  `log (FinitePlace.mk v (ε i))` at `v ∈ S` (`SUnit.regulator_eq_abs_det`). The generic `ι` and
  `e` carry the compatibility with reindexing. Independence of the basis is the
  `GL(ℤ)` invariance of `|det|`. Independence of `w'` is the product formula, which makes the
  columns sum to zero, so deleting any one column gives the same `|det|`. This is the
  `S`-analogue of Mathlib's `regulator_eq_det`, and it is how `regulator_empty` and the worked
  example are computed.
- Prove `SUnit.regulator_empty : SUnit.regulator ∅ = NumberField.Units.regulator K`. This is a
  theorem, not a definitional unfolding: `α ⊕ Empty` is not `α`. Transport the covolume along the
  measure-preserving linear equivalence of the two log spaces.
- **Rank.** `finrank ℤ (SUnit.unitLattice S) = rank K + #S`, from `ZLattice.rank`. Through the
  quotient equivalence, and because quotienting by torsion keeps the `ℤ`-rank, this is 4.2's
  `Set.unit_finrank_numberField`. The two routes must agree. `ZLattice.rank` alone computes only
  the rank of the image. The quotient equivalence is what makes it a statement about `S.unit K`.

## Worked examples (acceptance criteria)

- **Affine height.** `mulHeightAff ![1] = 1` and `mulHeightAff ![2] = 2` over `ℚ`, while
  `mulHeight ![1] = mulHeight ![2] = 1`.
- **Value bound.** Over `ℚ`, `a = x = ![1, 1]` gives `mulHeight₁ 2 = 2 = 2 ^ totalWeight ℚ · 1 · 1`.
- **Kronecker.** `absMulHeight₁ (-1 : ℚ) = 1`, `absMulHeight₁ (2 : ℚ) = 2`; the tuple
  `![1, -1]` has `absoluteProjectiveTupleHeight = 1` and `![1, 2]` has `2`.
- **Gap.** For every `c > 0` some `2 ^ (1/N)` has `absLogHeight₁` below `c`.
- **Basis from the minima.** For `L = ℤ⁵ + ℤ·(½,…,½)` and `K` the Euclidean unit ball, every
  minimum is `1`, attained by `e_0, …, e_4`, which span `ℤ⁵`, a sublattice of index `2`. So the
  minima witnesses are not a basis. 2.1 still produces a basis inside the bounds
  `max 1 ((i+1)/2)`, using `(½,…,½)`, of norm `√5/2 ≤ 5/2`, as its last vector.
- **Minor gcd.** The row `[1, 1]` has `det(AAᵀ) = 2`, `minorGcd = 1`, kernel generator
  `(1, −1)` of sup norm `1 ≤ √2`. The row `[2, 2]` has `det = 8`, `minorGcd = 2` and the same bound
  `√2`. This tests rational rescaling of a row, not a unimodular change.
- **Unimodular shear.** `A = [[1, 0, −1], [0, 1, −1]]` has Gram determinant `3`, minors `1, −1, 1`
  and `minorGcd = 1`, so the bound is `√3`. The kernel is generated by `(1, 1, 1)`, of sup norm `1`.
  The shear `U = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]` gives `U A = [[1, 1, −2], [0, 1, −1]]`, again with Gram
  determinant `3` and minors `1, −1, 1`. Classical Siegel's bound moves from `3^2 = 9` to
  `6^2 = 36`.
- **Independent family against basis.** For `A = [0, 0, 1]`, `(1, 1, 0)` and `(1, −1, 0)` meet
  the bound `1` and span a sublattice of index `2` in `ker A = ℤ² × 0`. The basis milestone
  returns `(1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0)`, inside its bound `2!/2 · 1 = 1`.
- **Regulator, sharp at `ℚ(√2)`.** `r = 1`, `d = 2`, `ε = 1 + √2`, and
  `regulator = log(1+√2)` by Mathlib's `regulator_eq_det` at rank one,
  `h(ε) = log(1+√2)/2`. Hadamard: `log(1+√2) ≤ 4 · log(1+√2)/2`. Reduced:
  `log(1+√2)/2 ≤ (1/2) · log(1+√2)`, an **equality**, so the constant `(r!)²/(2^{r−1} d^r)` cannot
  be lowered at `r = 1, d = 2`.
- **Rank zero.** For `ℚ` and every imaginary quadratic field, both bounds of 3.3 have empty
  products and agree with Tau Ceti's `regulator_rat_eq_one` and
  `regulator_eq_one_of_isTotallyComplex_of_finrank_eq_two`.
- **S-units over `ℚ`.** `S = {2}`: rank `0 + 1 = 1`, fundamental system `{2}`, torsion `{±1}`,
  `SUnit.regulator S = log 2` by the determinant formula: the `1 × 1` matrix at the place `2`
  is `log |2|_2 = −log 2`. The element `1/2` is in `S.unit ℚ`, and its height `2` is carried at
  `2`.

## Ordering

Layer 0 first: 0.1 is used by 0.2, which also uses DAT §1.3's tuple sum bound. Layer 1 needs
only Layer 0's normalization lemmas and DAT §§0.2–0.3, 2.5. Layer 2 needs GoN §§0.2, 1.2, 1.5 and
DAT §§2.5, 2.8; its 2.1 is the input to 2.2's basis and to 3.3. Layer 3: 3.1, then 3.2 (which
also uses 1.3), then 3.3 (which uses 2.1). Layer 4: 4.1 needs nothing from Layer 3 except 3.1's
`S = ∅` identity as a check; 4.2 needs 4.1; 4.3 needs 4.1, 4.2, 3.1 and Kronecker (1.3). The
headline milestones are 3.3, 4.2 and 4.3.

```

d_rel(α,β)=(∂̄α, α|_(W\S)−∂̄β).
```

## HF2. Purity, flabbiness and compact duality

**HF2.AnalyticPreparation — Malgrange top vanishing.**

Own **MalgrangeTopVanishing**: for n≥1, every open Ω⊆ℂⁿ and 0≤p≤n,

onto. Use the following constructive real-Laplacian route on Ω⊆ℝ^(2n),
with `Δ=Σ_a∂_a²`.

Own the filled-compact exhaustion and harmonic Runge lemma. There are
compact K_j⊂int K_(j+1) exhausting Ω such that Ω\K_j has no relatively
compact connected component. If h is harmonic on a neighborhood of K_j,
then for every m and ε>0 there is H harmonic on all Ω with
`max_(|α|≤m,x∈K_j)|∂^α(H−h)(x)|<ε`. Prove this by Hahn–Banach and the
compact-distribution dual from K5a: a separating distribution T supported
in K_j annihilates every harmonic function on Ω. Its Newton potential
w=E*T satisfies Δw=T and is real analytic off K_j. Here in real dimension
d=2n, use `E=log‖x‖/(2π)` for d=2 and
`E=‖x‖^(2−d)/((2−d)area(S^(d−1)))` for d>2, proving ΔE=δ.
Annihilation of pole kernels and all their derivatives at points outside Ω
makes every jet of w zero there; harmonic-polynomial annihilation and the
convergent exterior multipole expansion make w zero near infinity.
Filledness implies every component of ℝ^(2n)\K_j is unbounded or meets
ℝ^(2n)\Ω: a bounded component contained in Ω would have compact closure
in Ω and would contradict the filled-exhaustion property. Apply analytic
unique continuation on each of these components of ℝ^(2n)\K_j, using
the zero exterior expansion in the unbounded case and the zero jets at
a point outside Ω in the other case. This gives supp w⊆K_j.
Integration by parts against the germ h gives ⟨T,h⟩=0, proving Runge density.
Own the exhaustion, Newton convolution, multipole expansion and harmonic
analyticity/unique-continuation steps with these exact support hypotheses.

For each bounded open O relatively compact in Ω solve Δv=f weakly using
the gradient completion of C_c∞(O), its Poincaré inequality and Hilbert
Riesz representation, with weak identity `∫∇v·∇η=−∫fη`; PDO's interior elliptic regularity gives a smooth
solution on O. On the exhaustion, subtract the global harmonic Runge
approximants to successive differences, with summable errors in the
successive C^j(K_j) seminorms. Prove convergence to a smooth solution of
Δv=f on all Ω, including disconnected Ω componentwise.

For scalar f solve Δv=4f and use
`∂̄(Σ_j(−1)^(j−1)∂_(z_j)v dbar(z)_[j])=f dbar(z₁)∧…∧dbar(z_n)`.
For the holomorphic-first (p,q)-form convention, multiply the corresponding
coefficientwise primitive with dz_I on the left by (−1)^p. This proves
surjectivity, hence closed range, of the stated top Dolbeault operator.
These Euclidean Poisson/Runge inputs form an independent construction
before purity and compact analytic duality.
Dimension0 is treated directly.
