### P0.15 the trace-form criterion

**Almost finite projective algebras are étale iff the trace form is perfect.**
(*trace-form-criterion*) Let `S` be a basic setup and `φ : A → B` a morphism of almost algebras with
`B` almost finite projective as an `A`-module. Then `φ` is étale iff the trace form
`t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A` is a perfect pairing, i.e. `τ_{B/A} : B → B* = alHom_A(B, A)` is an
isomorphism (`Almost.Algebra.isEtale_iff_isPerfectTraceForm`; [GR] §4.1, Theorem 4.1.14, p. 75;
[Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.16, p. 21; [KL15] §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132, where the criterion is the
definition). In that case
`(1_B ⊗ τ_{B/A})(e_{B/A}) = ζ_B`, where `e_{B/A}` is the diagonal idempotent and
`ζ_B = ω_{B/A}⁻¹(1_B)` ([GR] §4.1, Remark 4.1.17, p. 76). In particular, for `B` almost finitely
presented, `φ` is finite étale iff `B` is flat over `A` and `t_{B/A}` is perfect. For `L°a/K°a`
(`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, `p ≠ 2`, `L = K(√p)`) the trace form is perfect on the almost level (the discriminants `4p^{1/p^n}` of the
approximations `R_n` tend to a unit up to `m`); in the classical setup with `B` finite free this is
the criterion "finite free étale iff the discriminant is a unit". The trace uses P0.12's internal
realization of PivotalSpherical §Layer 2. *Needs:* P0.12; P0.14.

`Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_trace` states the identity on the relative module
`P = Almost.Algebra.relativeModule S φ`. The element `e : A → P ⊗_A P` is specified by
`μ(e) = 1` and `(b ⊗ 1)e = (1 ⊗ b)e`, expressed as equality of morphisms
`P → P ⊗_A P`; these conditions characterize the diagonal idempotent.
For `P` almost finite projective, the conclusion is
`e ≫ (1 ⊗ traceFormDual) = ζ_B`, with `ζ_B` explicitly the internal-Hom representative of
`1_P` followed by `dualTensorHomIso.inv` ([GR] Remark 4.1.17, p. 76).
`Almost.Algebra.isFiniteEtale_iff_flat_perfectTraceForm` assumes almost finite presentation of
`P` and states finite étaleness iff there is a flatness proof for which the trace pairing is
perfect. Flatness and presentation supply the almost finite projectivity needed to define that
trace ([GR] Proposition 2.4.18, p. 26, and Theorem 4.1.14, p. 75).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_product` (computation) — `B = A × A` over `A`: the diagonal
  idempotent is `e = (1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1)`, `μ(e) = 1`, and `t_{B/A}` has matrix `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`, so both sides of the criterion hold.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers` (non-example) — for a nonzero almost algebra `A`,
  `B = A[ε]/(ε²)` is finite free,
  `t_{B/A}` has matrix `[[2, 0], [0, 0]]` and is not perfect; correspondingly `I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}² = Ω_{B/A} = (B/(2ε))·dε ≠ 0`, so no idempotent `e` with `μ(e) = 1` and `I_{B/A}·e = 0` exists: both
  sides of the criterion fail. Over `ℚ`, `Ω` has dimension `1`; over `𝔽₂` it has dimension `2`.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_product_diagonal` — in the split product algebra, the displayed
  tensor is idempotent, its multiplication is one, and it annihilates the diagonal ideal.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers_quotient` — the differential module is
  `B/(2ε)`, with `dε` sent to one; the formula includes characteristic two.
- `Almost.Algebra.traceForm_test_dual_numbers_differentials` — after almostification,
  the module of differentials of `R[ε]/(ε²)` remains nonzero whenever `R^a` is nonzero.
- `Almost.Algebra.algebraTrace_test_zero` (degenerate) — `B = 0`: `t_{B/A}` is perfect on `0 ⊗ 0` and

Unramified morphisms are characterised by a diagonal idempotent
(*unramified-idempotent-characterisation*, `Almost.Algebra.isUnramified_iff_exists_idempotent`):
for a basic setup `S` and `φ : A → B`, `φ` is unramified (`B` almost projective over
`B ⊗_A B`) iff there is an almost element
`e_{B/A} ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_*` with `e² = e`, `μ_{B/A}(e) = 1` and `x·e = 0` for every `x ∈ (I_{B/A})_*`;
`e` is unique, and `B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B` as `B ⊗_A B`-algebras (`I_{B/A}` with unit `1 − e`). More
generally, for an ideal `I` of an almost algebra `A`, `A/I` is almost projective over `A` iff `I` is
generated by an idempotent of `A_*`, which is then unique ([GR] §3.1, Proposition 3.1.4, p. 40; [GR]
§3.1, Remark 3.1.8, p. 40; [Sch12] §4, Definition 4.12(i), p. 20; [Bhatt] §4.3, Definition 4.3.1(2),
p. 26). In the classical setup with `B` finite étale over `A`, `ker μ` is a finitely generated
idempotent ideal generated by `1 − e` (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`, `IsIdempotentElem`).

`Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_unique` equates any two almost elements satisfying the
three displayed conditions. `Almost.Algebra.diagonalIdempotent_split` gives the product
isomorphism on almost elements: with `D = B ⊗_A B`, it is the additive and multiplicative
bijection `D_* → (diagonalIdeal S φ) × B_*`, sending `x` to `((1 − e)x, μ(x))`.
Its first factor has inherited multiplication and unit `1 − e`; its `D_*`-action is multiplication,
and the action on `B_*` is through `μ`. Thus almostification gives the asserted isomorphism of
`D`-algebras ([GR] Proposition 3.1.4, Remark 3.1.8 and Corollary 3.1.9, p. 40).

### P0.16 inverting an element of `m`

**Inverting an element of `m`: almost modules become honest modules over `V[1/ϖ]`.**
(*almost-inversion-and-completion*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `ϖ ∈ m` (so `ϖ` kills
almost zero modules; `ϖ` need not be a nonzerodivisor). The localisation `M ↦ M[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] ⊗_V M`
is exact and kills almost zero modules (`ϖM = 0`), so it factors, uniquely up to unique
isomorphism, through an exact functor `Almost.invert ϖ : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]` with
`invert(M^a) ≅ M[1/ϖ]` and `invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ] ≅ M_![1/ϖ]` ([GR] §5.2, proof of Corollary 5.2.15,
p. 110; [Bhatt] §4.1, Exercise 4.1.9, p. 22). Consequences: almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms
and almost exact complexes become exact after inverting `ϖ`; the setup `S.baseChange V[1/ϖ]` is
classical (`m·V[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ]`), so `Almost.Module` over it is `ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]`; `invert` is
symmetric monoidal and sends almost algebras to `V[1/ϖ]`-algebras ([Berkeley] Lecture 8, proof of
Proposition 8.2.8, p. 60: almost vanishing of `H^i(X, O⁺)` gives vanishing of
`H^i(X, O) = H^i(X, O⁺)[1/ϖ]`). The `ϖ`-adic completion side of this passage — completeness of `M`
versus `M_*`, and exactness of complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo `ϖ`,
with the `lim¹` term kept — is *almost-completeness-via-almost-elements* and
*almost-exactness-passes-to-completion* (P0.28). Define `Almost.invert` (the exact functor
`Almost.Module S ⥤ ModuleCat (Localization.Away ϖ)` for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`); prove
`Almost.toAlmostCompInvertIso` (`toAlmost S ⋙ invert ϖ ≅` localisation at the powers of `ϖ`),
that `invert ϖ` preserves finite limits, `Almost.invertElementsIso`
(`(invert ϖ).obj M ≅ LocalizedModule (powers ϖ) M.elements`), that localising at the powers of `ϖ`
turns almost isomorphisms into isomorphisms and almost zero modules into zero modules,
`Almost.BasicSetup.baseChange_away_eq_classical`
(`S.baseChange (Localization.Away ϖ) = classical (Localization.Away ϖ)`), `Almost.invertMonoidal`
(with `Almost.Algebra.invert` on almost algebras) and that a complex of `V`-modules with almost
zero cohomology becomes exact after inverting `ϖ`. *Needs:* P0.5 for inversion;
P0.8's `Almost.Algebra`, `Almost.Algebra.ModuleCat` and algebra adjunction for
*change-of-basic-setup* (i); Mathlib
`SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft`, `LocalizedModule`, `Localization.Away`.

On algebras, `Almost.Algebra.invert` sends `A` to `A_*[1/ε]`; on canonical numerators its map is induced by `elements.map`.

### P0.17 comparison with Mathlib's finite étale algebras

**Comparison of finite étale almost algebras with Mathlib's finite étale algebras.**
(*finite-etale-localizes*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `R → R'` a map of commutative
`V`-algebras. (i) If `R'` is finite étale over `R` in Mathlib's sense (`Algebra.Etale R R'` and
`Module.Finite R R'`), then `R^a → R'^a` is finite étale in the almost sense ([Bhatt] §4.3,
Construction 4.3.3, p. 26: a finite étale algebra is a direct summand of a free module via the
diagonal idempotent and the trace). (ii) In the classical setup (`m = V`) the converse holds, so
`A_fet` for `A = R^a` is equivalent to Mathlib's category of finite étale `R`-algebras. (iii) For
`ϖ ∈ m`, if `R'^a` is finite étale over `R^a` then `R'[1/ϖ]` is finite étale over `R[1/ϖ]` in
Mathlib's sense (inverting `ϖ` turns almost statements into honest ones, P0.16). (iv) Gabber–Ramero's
étale morphisms in the classical setup are exactly the absolutely flat (weakly étale) maps whose
diagonal is almost projective; they need not be of finite presentation, and a classical étale map in
EGA's sense is étale in their sense ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.44), p. 64, which states the comparison in the
classical limit `m = V`; [GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39; for a general basic setup, (i) follows because a finite étale `R'` is finite projective
over `R` and carries the diagonal idempotent, so `R'^a` is almost finite projective over `R^a` by
[GR] (2.4.8) and unramified by *unramified-idempotent-characterisation*; (iii) because finite étale
morphisms are stable under the base change `R^a → R[1/ϖ]^a` (*etale-morphisms-stability*) and
`S.baseChange V[1/ϖ]` is classical, so by *change-of-basic-setup* the base-changed morphism is the
honest `R[1/ϖ] → R'[1/ϖ]` in the classical setup, where (ii) applies). For `K` a perfectoid field
and `L/K` finite separable,
`L°a` is finite étale over `K°a` while `L°` need not be finite étale over `K°` in Mathlib's sense (it
is not finitely presented in general; for instance the odd-`p` `L°` of P0.10 need not be finitely
presented over `K°`), so (i) is strictly weaker than the almost statement; for
`R → R' = R × R` the diagonal idempotent is `(1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1)`. *Needs:* P0.14; P0.11;
P0.16; Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`, `Module.Finite`, `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`,
`KaehlerDifferential`.

### P0.18 almost Kähler differentials

**Almost Kähler differentials `Ω_{B/A}` and almost derivations.** (*almost-differentials*) Let `S` be
a basic setup and `A → B` a morphism of almost algebras, `I_{B/A} = ker(μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B)`.
The module of almost differentials is the `B`-module `Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}²`, with the
`A`-derivation `δ : B → Ω_{B/A}`, `b ↦ 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1` on almost elements ([GR] §2.5, Definition
2.5.22(ii), p. 33). For a `B`-module `M`, an `A`-derivation `B → M` is an `A`-linear `∂` with
`∂(b₁b₂) = b₁∂(b₂) + b₂∂(b₁)` on almost elements; they form a `V`-module `Der_A(B, M)`, and
`f ↦ f ∘ δ` is an isomorphism `Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] §2.5, (2.5.23), p. 33).

### P0.19 the cotangent complex of a ring map, consumed

**The cotangent complex of a ring map and its deformation theory, consumed.**
(*cotangent-complex-of-ring-map*) Ownership: the ordinary cotangent complex (simplicial
resolutions, [Stacks] Tag 08PL) and its square-zero obstruction class belong to
DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.4 and 0.25, consistently with SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.6; Mathlib's
`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex` and `Algebra.H1Cotangent` cover only the two lowest degrees.
This roadmap consumes that carrier and owns only the almost construction of P0.20. What follows is
the contract that P0.20–P0.24 need of the consumed carrier, with its Checks; the names
`CotangentComplex` and its API below stand for the corresponding declarations of that roadmap. For a map of commutative rings `R → S`, the cotangent complex
`L_{S/R} ∈ D(S)` is the complex of Kähler differentials of a simplicial resolution of `S` by
polynomial `R`-algebras, tensored termwise with `S` along the augmentation
([Stacks] Tag [08PL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08PL), Definitions 92.3.1–92.3.2), together
with: (a) `H_0(L_{S/R}) ≅ Ω_{S/R}`, compatibly with Mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential`, and `H_1`
compatible with the truncation `Algebra.Extension.Cotangent` and with `Algebra.H1Cotangent`
(Mathlib has the degree `≤ 1` truncation only, no simplicial `L_{S/R}`); (b) the transitivity
triangle `S ⊗_T^L L_{T/R} → L_{S/R} → L_{S/T}` for `R → T → S` ([Stacks] Tag 08QX), whose
`H_1`/`H_0` part is Mathlib's Jacobi–Zariski sequence `Algebra.Generators.Cotangent.exact`; (c) base change
`L_{S'/R'} ≃ S' ⊗_S^L L_{S/R}` for a Tor-independent square ([Stacks] Tag 08QQ); (d) commutation
with filtered colimits of rings ([Stacks] Tag 08S9); (e) `Ext^0_S(L_{S/R}, M) ≅ Der_R(S, M)` and
`Ext^1_S(L_{S/R}, M) ≅ Exal_R(S, M)`, the group of square-zero `R`-extensions of `S` by `M`
([Stacks] Tag [08S3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08S3), Lemma 91.2.3,
and Tag [08RB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08RB) for the truncation comparison); (f) for a flat `R`-algebra `S` and a square-zero extension
`R' → R` with kernel `J`, the obstruction to a flat deformation of `S` over `R'` lies in
`Ext^2_S(L_{S/R}, S ⊗_R J)`, deformations form a torsor under `Ext^1` and automorphisms are `Ext^0`
([Stacks] Tag 08SP), and for a square-zero extension `T′ → T` of `R`-algebras with kernel `J`,
the obstruction to lifting an `R`-map `S → T` to `T′` lies in `Ext^1_S(L_{S/R}, J)`,
where `J` is an `S`-module through `S → T`, with lifts a torsor under `Ext^0`
([Stacks] Tag [08S3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08S3), Lemma 91.2.1); (g) for a map of simplicial rings `R_• → S_•`, the diagonal complex `L^Δ` with the
spectral sequence `H_j(L_{S_i/R_i}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ)`, and `L_{S/R} ≃ L^Δ` for simplicial resolutions
([Illusie] Chapter II, 1.2.6.2). For the free simplicial resolution `S_• → S`
and `R_• = S_• ×_S R` used to compare cotangent complexes of almost-isomorphic algebras,
[GR] Proposition 8.1.7, proof, printed pp. 220–221, gives precisely
`E¹_{i,j} = H_j(L_{S_i/R_i}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ)` in homological degrees.
The consumed carrier provides `CotangentComplex` with `CotangentComplex.homologyZeroIso`

`CotangentComplex.baseChange` under the Tor-independence in (c), `CotangentComplex.filteredColimit`
for (d), `CotangentComplex.extZero` and `CotangentComplex.extOne` for (e),

complex, never of a two-term truncation. Tensor products of complexes in the derived category

Mathlib
`KaehlerDifferential`, `Algebra.Extension.Cotangent`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`,
`Algebra.Generators.Cotangent.exact`, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject`.

### P0.20 the almost cotangent complex

**The almost cotangent complex `L_{B/A}`.** (*almost-cotangent-complex*) Let `S` be a basic setup
(`m̃` flat is used in [GR] Proposition 2.5.34 and Theorem 2.5.35) and `A → B` a morphism of almost
algebras. Put `Ã := V^a × A` and `B̃ := V^a × B` (exact almost algebras). The almost cotangent
complex is `L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗_{B̃_!!} L_{B̃_!!/Ã_!!}`, an object of the derived category of
`B_!!`-modules, where `L_{−/−}` is the cotangent complex of the ring map `Ã_!! → B̃_!!` (simplicial
polynomial resolution, the consumed carrier of P0.19, whose `Ext` groups are those of the full
complex); this almost construction is the one this roadmap owns. Its almostification `L^a_{B/A} ∈ D(B-Mod)` is the object used in
deformation theory ([GR] §2.5, Definition 2.5.20, p. 32; [Sch12] §5, before Remark 5.15, p. 25).
Properties: `H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`; `Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` ([GR]
(3.2.8)); `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] 2.5.29) and `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` (P0.21); the transitivity
triangle *cotangent-transitivity* (P0.22); Tor-independent base change
*cotangent-flat-base-change*; `L_{colim B_λ/colim A_λ} ≅ colim L_{B_λ/A_λ}` for filtered systems
([GR] §2.5, Proposition 2.5.33, p. 35); vanishing for weakly étale maps
*cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale* (P0.24); and for `V`-algebras `R → S`,
`L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a` by *almost-cotangent-comparison-classical*, so the almost cotangent
complex depends only on `R^a → S^a` ([Sch12] §5). Define `Almost.cotangentComplex` (`L_{B/A}` in
`DerivedCategory (ModuleCat B_!!)`) and `Almost.almostCotangentComplex` (`L^a_{B/A}` in
`DerivedCategory (B-Mod)`); prove the identification `H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`, the comparison
`Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)`, the identifications `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` and
`Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)`, the transitivity statement (the distinguished triangle
`C ⊗ L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} →`), Tor-independent base change, the colimit statement, the
comparison `L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a` with the almostified classical complex, and vanishing for
weakly étale maps (weakly étale, more generally Tor-trivial diagonal, `⇒ L_{B/A} ≃ 0`). *Needs:* P0.9; P0.18; P0.8; P0.19; Mathlib
`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`, `DerivedCategory`.

The named additive map `Almost.cotangentDerivationComparison` sends a degree-zero
class to its derivation. The identification `Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M)` above asserts bijectivity
of this map. For every basic setup, algebra map and coefficient module, its evaluation
formula applies `H⁰` to the class, transports along the identification
`H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}`, and evaluates on `Algebra.kaehlerDifferentialD`. It
commutes with every coefficient-module map, and a comparison statement
identifies its value with the underlying V-linear
`cotangentDerivation` of P0.22. These are the universal-derivation comparison of
[GR] (2.5.24), p. 33, and Proposition 2.5.29, p. 34.

`Almost.cotangentExtComparison` is the named additive map from ordinary Ext
with lower-shriek coefficients to almost Ext, in each integer degree.
The comparison `Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` above asserts its bijectivity.
Its formula is fixed as follows: apply Mathlib's
`mapDerivedCategory` to scalar extension from `B_!!` to `B_*` followed by
almostification, use the comparison with extension by zero in every
nonpositive degree, and use the scalar-extension counit and the inverse
lower-shriek unit at the coefficient module. The canonical shift and
single-object comparisons determine the degree convention.
It is compatible with coefficient maps. Sources: [GR] Proposition 2.5.42, p. 36, and (3.2.8), p. 41.

**Checks.** `cotangentDerivationComparison_zero` sends zero to zero;
`cotangentDerivationComparison_identity` vanishes for the identity algebra map;
`cotangentDerivationComparison_polynomial` realizes `d/dX` over `ℚ[X]` and
sends every polynomial `p` to `p′` on almost elements. Thus its values at
`1`, `X`, and `X²` are `0`, `1`, and `2X`, respectively.
`cotangentExtComparison_zero` sends zero to zero;
`cotangentExtComparison_identity` is zero in every degree for an identity
algebra map; `cotangentExtComparison_nonzero` preserves every nonzero class.

Two supporting results. The almost cotangent complex of `R^a → S^a` is the almostified classical one
(*almost-cotangent-comparison-classical*): for a basic setup `S` and a map `f : R → S` of
`V`-algebras, (i) if `f^a : R^a → S^a` is an isomorphism then `(L_{S/R})^a ≃ 0` in `D(S^a-Mod)`;
(ii) the natural map `L^a_{S^a/R^a} → (L_{S/R})^a` is an isomorphism in `D(S^a-Mod)`; hence the
almost cotangent complex of a morphism coming from `V`-algebras is computed by the cotangent complex
of P0.19 and depends only on `R^a → S^a` ([GR] §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7(i)-(ii), pp. 219–220; [Sch12]
§5, before Remark 5.15, p. 25). For `R = V` and `S = V × k` (`k = V/m`), `f^a` is an isomorphism and
`L_{S/V} ≅ 0 × L_{k/V}` has homology consisting of `k`-modules, hence almost zero, as (i) predicts.
Tor-independent base change (*cotangent-flat-base-change*): for `A → B` and `A → A'` morphisms of
almost algebras, `B' := B ⊗_A A'`, with `B ⊗^L_A A' → B'` an isomorphism (`Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0` for
`i > 0`; e.g. `B` or `A'` flat over `A`), the maps `B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'}` and
`(B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A}) ⊕ (B'_!! ⊗_{A'!!} L_{A'/A}) → L_{B'/A}` are quasi-isomorphisms ([GR] §2.5,
Theorem 2.5.35, p. 35, and Proposition 2.5.34, p. 35; cited by [Sch12] §5, proof of Theorem 5.10,
p. 26, as Theorem 2.5.36 in the book numbering). In that proof, for `A_n` flat over `(K°/ϖ^n)^a`
the square `(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`, `A_n → A_{n−1}` is Tor-independent, so
`L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ≅ A_{n−1} ⊗ L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}`.

### P0.21 square-zero extensions and `Ext¹`

**Square-zero extensions of almost algebras are classified by `Ext¹` of the almost cotangent
complex.** (*almost-exal-ext-comparison*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A → B` a morphism of almost
algebras and `M` a `B`-module; `A`-extensions of `B` by `M` are short exact sequences
`0 → M → E → B → 0` in `A-Mod` with `E` an `A`-algebra and `M` a square-zero ideal with its given
`B`-module structure ([GR] 2.5.2–2.5.7). (i) Almostification from ordinary `A_!!`-extensions
of `B_!!` by `M_*` to almost `A`-extensions of `B` by `M` is an equivalence of categories,
inducing the group isomorphism `Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` on
isomorphism classes, functorial in all arguments ([GR] §2.5, Lemma 2.5.17(i)–(ii), p. 32). (ii) There are
natural isomorphisms `Ext⁰_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M)` ([GR] §2.5, Proposition 2.5.29, p. 34)
and `Exal_A(B, M) ≅ Ext¹_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext¹_B(L^a_{B/A}, M)` ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.30,
p. 34; [GR] §3.2, (3.2.8), p. 41). (iii) For an epimorphism `A → B` with kernel `I`,
`Hom_B(I/I², M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` via pushout along `u : I/I² → M` of `0 → I/I² → A/I² → B → 0`. For
the trivial extension `B ⊕ M` the class is `0`; for `A → B = A/I` with `I² = 0` the extension `A`
itself corresponds to `1_I`; in [Sch12] Theorem 5.11 these groups classify deformations of
perfectoid `K°a/ϖ`-algebras.
*Needs:* P0.20; P0.18; P0.9.

`Almost.SquareZeroExtension` records the short exact sequence of underlying
almost modules, the algebra map from the base, and the quotient-compatible kernel
action. `Almost.extensionSetoid` fixes these maps under algebra isomorphisms,
and `Almost.Exal` is its quotient.

`CotangentComplex.extensionCategory` and `Almost.extensionCategory` give these
existing extension carriers their categories: an arrow is an algebra homomorphism
that fixes the base, quotient and specified kernel. In each namespace,
`extensionSetoid_iff_iso` identifies the existing relation with categorical
isomorphism ([GR] 2.5.4–2.5.7, p. 30). For every basic setup `S`, almost algebra
map `f : A → B` and `B`-module `M`, `Almost.ordinaryExtensions S f M` is the ordinary
extension category over `A_!!`, with quotient `B_!!` and kernel `M_*`, whose
`B_!!`-action is restricted along `B_!! → B_*`.
`Almost.extensionToAlmost` applies algebra and module almostification to each
term and each arrow, using `shriekShriekUnitIso` at the base and quotient and
`moduleEquiv_functor_forget` at the kernel. That `Almost.extensionToAlmost` is an
equivalence is the category-level assertion of [GR] 2.5.17(i), p. 32, for this specific functor;
in particular it preserves and recovers automorphisms.

In both namespaces `exalAddCommGroup` equips the existing quotient with Baer
addition. The theorem `CotangentComplex.exal_add_representative` characterizes
its sum by the fibre product modulo `(i_E(m), −i_F(m))`, with
`(i_E(m), i_F(n))` mapping to `i_G(m+n)`.
The almost representative statement gives the same construction on almost modules:
the two kernel inclusions `l,r` into the algebra fibre product have equal images
in the sum, and `0 → M →[l−r] E ×_B F → G → 0` is exact.
Both constructions fix the base and quotient maps ([GR] 2.5.5–2.5.7, p. 30).
An additive equivalence is derived from this equivalence of categories, with the image of every
representative equal to the class of its termwise almostification ([GR] 2.5.17(ii), p. 32); its
underlying class bijection is the isomorphism `Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of (i).

**Checks.** `CotangentComplex.extensionCategory_zero` and
`CotangentComplex.exalAddCommGroup_zero` give a unique arrow and zero sum when the
kernel is zero. Their `_classical` checks give only the identity automorphism
and the zero class for extensions of `ℚ` over itself.
`CotangentComplex.extensionCategory_polynomial` uses
`E = ℚ[X] ⊕ εℚ[X]`: the nonidentity automorphism sends `a+εb` to
`a+ε(b+a′)`, hence `X` to `X+ε`, while fixing the kernel and quotient.
`CotangentComplex.exalAddCommGroup_nonsplit` exhibits the nonzero order-two
class for `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2`.
For each of `Almost.ordinaryExtensions`, `Almost.extensionCategory`,
`Almost.extensionToAlmost`, and `Almost.exalAddCommGroup`, `_zero` checks the
zero kernel and `_classical` checks the rational base over itself. The first
three also have `_polynomial`: a nonidentity automorphism remains nonidentity
after almostification, although all extension classes of `ℚ[X]` by itself agree.
The `_nonsplit` Check of `Almost.exalAddCommGroup` gives the nonzero order-two class over `ℤ/2`.

**Checks.** Each carrier has `_zero` (zero kernel forces an invertible projection),
`_classical` (extensions of the rational base over itself split), and `_nonsplit`
(the classical `ℤ/4 → ℤ/2` class) examples. The zero-class characterization in
the identification `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of P0.20 uses an algebra section over the specified base,

The identification `Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M)` of P0.20 uses the named additive equivalence

It identifies addition with the Baer sum and kernel pushout with
postcomposition, and its almostification compatibility identifies the
class of each termwise almostified ordinary extension with the image of
`CotangentComplex.extensionClass` (the consumed ordinary classifier of P0.19). Its source map is induced by the projection
from exactified rings, with `t ⊗ x ↦ t·image(x)` in every degree; its target
map is the scalar-extension counit followed by the almost-elements counit.
This fixes the class itself, including its sign ([GR] Theorem 2.5.30,
p. 34, Lemma 2.5.17, p. 32, and (3.2.8), p. 41).

For a surjection of ordinary commutative rings `R → T`,
`CotangentComplex.conormalComparison` identifies `Ext¹(L_{T/R}, M)` with
`Hom_T(I/I², M)`, using Mathlib's conormal module.
`CotangentComplex.conormalComparison_extensionClass` specifies its value:
the image of `r mod I²` under the class of `E` is the unique `m` whose
kernel inclusion equals the base image of `r` in `E`.
For every commutative algebra map, `CotangentComplex.extensionClass_add`
asserts compatibility with Baer addition ([GR] Theorem 2.5.30, p. 34).
Together with this almostification compatibility, this is the conormal

**Checks.** `conormalComparison_zero` is the zero map;
`conormalComparison_identity` vanishes for `R → R`;
`conormalComparison_zmodNine` uses `ℤ/9 → ℤ/3`, with kernel generator sent

`cotangentExtensionClass_zmodNine` carries this extension to the classical

### P0.22 flat square-zero deformations

Nilpotent deformations of almost algebras come next: flat deformations, lifting of morphisms,
lifting of étale algebras, faithfully flat descent, tight ideals and henselian pairs, and modules
over complete almost algebras.

**Flat square-zero deformations of almost algebras: obstruction, torsor, automorphisms.**
(*almost-deformation-theory*) Let `S` be a basic setup (`m̃` flat), `A` an almost algebra,
`B̃ = (0 → I → B → B₀ → 0)` an `A`-extension (`I² = 0`) and `f₀ : B₀ → C₀` a flat morphism of almost
algebras. Let `ω(B̃, f₀) := ∂(I → C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ∈ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)`, `∂` the
boundary of the transitivity sequence for `B → B₀ → C₀`. Then (i) `ω(B̃, f₀) = 0` iff there is a
flat deformation of `C₀` over `B`, i.e. a `B`-extension `C̃ = (0 → C₀ ⊗ I → C → C₀ → 0)` with `C`
flat over `B` and `C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀`; (ii) if `ω = 0`, the isomorphism classes of flat deformations
form a torsor under `Exal_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext¹_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)`; (iii) the
automorphism group of a flat deformation (acting trivially on `C₀` and on `C₀ ⊗ I`) is
`Der_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I)` ([GR] §3.2, Corollary
3.2.11(i)-(iii), p. 42). More generally, for a `C₀`-module `J` and `B₀`-linear `u : I → J`, let
`u_C : C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J` be `c ⊗ i ↦ c·u(i)`. The obstruction
`ω(B̃, f₀, u) = (u_C)_* ω(B̃, f₀)` governs extensions `C̃` with kernel `J` ([GR] §3.2, Proposition
3.2.9, p. 41; [Sch12] §5, Theorem 5.11, p. 24, cites this proposition under the same number). If
`L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ 0` (e.g. `C₀` étale over `B₀`, or a perfectoid `(K°/ϖ)^a`-algebra) a flat deformation
exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism, which [Sch12] Theorem 5.10 applies over
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`; in the classical setup, for `A = B = B₀ ⊕ I` trivial and `C₀ = B₀[X]`, the trivial
deformation `C₀ ⊕ C₀ ⊗ I` exists and deformations form a torsor under `Ext¹(L^a, −) = 0`. *Needs:*
P0.21; P0.20; P0.18; P0.19; DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.25.

**Checks.**

- Degenerate: for `I = 0` (`B = B₀`): `ω = 0`, the only
  flat deformation is `C₀` itself, the torsor `Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗ 0) = 0` is a point and the
  automorphism group `Der_{B₀}(C₀, 0) = 0` is trivial, as it must be.
- Computation: in the classical setup, `C₀ = B₀[X]`: `L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ C₀·dX` in
  degree `0`, so `Ext² = Ext¹ = 0`: every square-zero `B` admits a flat deformation, unique up to
  isomorphism, with automorphisms `Der_{B₀}(B₀[X], B₀[X] ⊗ I) ≅ B₀[X] ⊗ I` (the value on `X`).
  In a general basic setup, `B₀[X]` is only almost projective as a module over itself:
  this does not imply vanishing of ordinary `Ext¹` or `Ext²`.
- Non-example: flatness of the deformation `C` over `B` is not
  decorative: for `B₀ = k`, `B = k[t]/(t²)`, `C₀ = k`, the `B`-algebra `C = k` (`t ↦ 0`) has
  `C ⊗_B k = k` but is not flat over `B` (`(t) ⊗_B k = k → (t)·k = 0` is the zero map, see
  *almost-local-flatness-criterion*) and its kernel `0` is not `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I = k`; the flat
  deformation of `C₀ = k` over `B` is `B` itself.

**Check `CotangentComplex.transitivityTriangle_cone_sign`.** Use Mathlib's
`CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle`: for the zero map `ℚ[0] → ℚ[0]`,
the cone has one copy of `ℚ` in degree `−1` and one in degree `0`.
Its connecting map sends the degree `−1` generator to `−1` in `ℚ[1]`.
Thus the cone triangle uses minus projection onto the shifted source;
this is the convention for interpreting the transitivity boundary in the
obstruction formula above. The supplier is
`CochainComplex.mappingCone.inl_v_triangle_mor₃_f` in
`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/Pretriangulated.lean`.

Two supporting results. The transitivity triangle for almost cotangent complexes
(*cotangent-transitivity*): for `A → B → C` morphisms of almost algebras there is a natural
distinguished triangle `C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A}[1]` in
`D(C_!!-Mod)`, hence `C ⊗_B L^a_{B/A} → L^a_{C/A} → L^a_{C/B} →` in `D(C-Mod)`; on `H_0` it extends
the exact sequence `C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0` ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35). For
`A → A[X] → A` (`X ↦ 0`) it gives `L^a_{A/A[X]} ≃ (X)/(X²)[1] ≅ A[1]`, the conormal module in
homological degree `1`. [Sch12]'s proof of Theorem 5.10 instead tensors `0 → A → A_n → A_{n−1} → 0`
with `L^a_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}` and uses base change ([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.35, pp. 35–36, which [Sch12]
cites as Theorem 2.5.36) to get
`L^a_{A/(K°/ϖ)^a} → L^a_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a} → L^a_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} →`. The local flatness criterion for square-zero thickenings
(*almost-local-flatness-criterion*): (i) for a ring `R`, an ideal `J ⊆ R` with `J² = 0`, `R' = R/J`
and an `R`-module `M` with `M' = M/JM`, `M` is `R`-flat iff `M'` is `R'`-flat and
`u(M) : J ⊗_{R'} M' → JM`, `x ⊗ m' ↦ xm`, is an isomorphism ([GR] §3.2, (3.2.19), p. 44); (ii) for
a basic setup `S` and a morphism `f̃ : B̃ → C̃` of `A`-extensions `0 → I → B → B₀ → 0` and
`0 → J → C → C₀ → 0` (`I² = J² = 0`) whose square is cofibred (`C₀ ≅ C ⊗_B B₀`), `B → C` is flat iff
`B₀ → C₀` is flat and `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J` is an isomorphism ([GR] §3.2, Lemma 3.2.6 with proof,
p. 41); the general nilpotent case follows by induction. For `R = k[ε]/(ε²)` and `M = R`, `M' = k`
is flat and `u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → εR` is bijective, while for `M = k`, `u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → 0` is not
injective and `k` is not flat over `R` (Mathlib `Module.Flat`, `TensorProduct`).

The square-zero flatness criterion uses the canonical `R/J` actions on `J`,
`N = JM`, and `M/N`: a residue class `[r]` acts by the original `r` action.
The first two actions use `Module.IsTorsionBySet.module`, with annihilation
following from `J² = 0`; the third is Mathlib's quotient-module instance.
Thus the multiplication map is linear for these specified actions in both
the ordinary and almost flatness criteria ([GR] (3.2.19), p. 44, and
Lemma 3.2.6, p. 41).

**Checks.** `flat_squareZero_ideal_action` computes `[r] • a = ra`,
`flat_squareZero_image_action` computes `[r] • n = r • n`, and
`flat_squareZero_quotient_action` computes `[r] • [m] = [r • m]`.
`flat_squareZero_regular` and `flat_squareZero_residue` distinguish the
regular module over rational dual numbers from its nonflat residue module.

`Almost.FlatDeformation` is the upper algebra of the specified pushout square,
with a flat map from the thickened base. `flatDeformationSetoid` identifies exactly
isomorphisms commuting with the base and reduction maps. The obstruction and torsor
are stated by `Almost.flatDeformation`; `flatDeformation_unique` includes unique
lifting of isomorphisms when the cotangent complex vanishes ([GR] Corollary 3.2.11).

**Checks.** For both carriers, `_zero` forces an invertible reduction, `_polynomial`
gives one isomorphism class with the expected polynomial kernel automorphisms in
the classical setup, and `_nonflat` excludes the residue algebra of dual numbers.

The normalization in `Almost.flatDeformation` uses a specified universal
`B₀`-linear map `u : I → J`: for each `C₀`-module `M`, composition with `u`
identifies `Hom_{C₀}(J,M)` with `Hom_{B₀}(I,M)`. Thus `J` is the tensor
kernel `C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I`, with its generator map retained.
Its kernel statement supplies this universal map and identifies its
coefficient module with `Module.baseChange f I` ([GR] (3.2.5), p. 41). For every deformation,
the theorem supplies an extension by this kernel and an isomorphism to the
given upper algebra, commuting with the base, reduction, and kernel maps.
These hypotheses include flatness of `B₀ → C₀`; no flatness of `I` is required.

`Almost.cotangentConnecting` is the connecting arrow for the functorial
polynomial-resolution transitivity triangle, after extension to `C₀_*` and
almostification. Its triangle statement specifies its first
two arrows as the images of `cotangentTransitivityFirst` and
`cotangentTransitivitySecond`. The cone convention is the minus projection
described above ([GR] Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35). Regard the given extension
`E = (I → B → B₀)` as an extension over `B`, with base map `id_B`.
`Almost.kernelExtensionClass E f J u` is the scalar-adjoint class of its
pushout by `u`. Its degree-one conormal map is `u`, using the given
inclusion of `I`, as in [GR] (3.2.2), (3.2.7), p. 41. Define
`Almost.deformationBoundary E f J u` by composing the connecting arrow
with this class shifted by one, followed by the canonical identification
`J[1][1] ≅ J[2]`. `Almost.flatDeformation` tests this specific element for
vanishing ([GR] (3.2.10), Corollary 3.2.11, p. 42).

`Almost.cotangentExtensionClass` is the additive extension classifier:
its polynomial-resolution cocycle uses the given kernel inclusion and the
order `d₀ − d₁`, with the exactification and almostification comparisons
([GR] (2.5.31), p. 34, and (3.2.8), p. 41). `Almost.exalRestriction`
forgets part of the base without changing the upper algebra, reduction,
or kernel. Its injectivity requires the square-zero
extension of the base and identifies the injection in [GR] (3.2.15), p. 43.
The torsor in `Almost.flatDeformation` is specified by
`restriction(class([D] −ᵥ [F])) = [D] − [F]` in `Exal_B(C₀,J)`.
Consequently translation by an `Ext¹` class is Baer addition with that class;
reversing the difference changes its sign.

The automorphisms fixing the base and reduction form a subgroup of
`CategoryTheory.Aut`. Their comparison is a multiplicative equivalence to
`Multiplicative Ext⁰`, so composition corresponds to addition. Its value
is determined by
`h − id = reduction ≫ derivation ≫ kernel inclusion`, using the specified
identification of the deformation with its extension. The additive map
`Almost.cotangentDerivation` evaluates a degree-zero derived morphism on
`H⁰(L) = Ω`. Its value on the universal differential is specified, and its range
statement gives injectivity and the exact Leibniz and base-vanishing conditions on its image
([GR] Proposition 2.5.25, p. 33, (2.5.29), p. 34, and Corollary
3.2.11(iii), p. 42). In particular identity maps to zero and inverses map
to negative derivations.

DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.25 supplies the following normalized ordinary deformation laws,
on the consumed carrier of P0.19. The target `CotangentComplex.flatDeformation` retains the same
flatness and square-zero hypotheses. Its
`CotangentComplex.deformationObstruction` is the composite of
`CotangentComplex.transitivityConnecting` with the shifted
`CotangentComplex.kernelExtensionClass`. The latter sends the conormal
class of `i` to `1 ⊗ i`; it does not discard the given kernel inclusion.

specifies ordinary extension representatives of each classical almost
flat lift. Restriction of the torsor difference is the difference of their

again a group isomorphism with value `h − id` under
`CotangentComplex.derivationEvaluation`;
`CotangentComplex.derivationEvaluation_differential` evaluates the map on
`H⁰` at `d x` ([GR] (3.2.7)–(3.2.11), pp. 41–42, in the classical setup).

`CotangentComplex.polynomialLift_sign` computes the automorphism convention
on the flat lift `ℚ[ε]/(ε²)[X]` of `ℚ[X]`. For each `a : ℚ`, translation
`hₐ(X) = X + aε` has a unique `Ext⁰` class satisfying the difference formula;
its derivation takes `X` to `a` and `X²` to `2aX`. For a polynomial `P`
over the dual numbers, the kernel inclusion of that derivation at `P mod ε`
is exactly `hₐ(P) − P`. **Checks** `CotangentComplex.polynomialLift_positive`,
`_inverse`, and `_composition` compute the values `ε`, `−ε`, and the law
`hₐ ∘ h_b = h_{a+b}`. Since `1 ≠ −1` in `ℚ[X]`, the positive translation
cannot be assigned the negative derivation under this comparison. This is
the polynomial computation of [GR] Corollary 3.2.11(iii), p. 42.

### P0.23 lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions

**Lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions of almost algebras.** (*almost-morphism-lifting*)
Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra, `B̃` an `A`-extension `0 → I → B → B₀ → 0`
(`I² = 0`), and `C̃ⁱ = (0 → Jⁱ → Cⁱ → C₀ⁱ → 0)`, `i = 1, 2`, `A`-extensions with morphisms
`f̃ⁱ : B̃ → C̃ⁱ` (kernel maps `uⁱ : I → Jⁱ` and reductions `f₀ⁱ : B₀ → C₀ⁱ`), together with a `B₀`-algebra map `g₀ : C₀¹ → C₀²` and a
`C₀¹`-linear map `v : J¹ → J²` (the target action is through `g₀`) such that `u² = v ∘ u¹` and
`f₀² = g₀ ∘ f₀¹`. Regard `C̃¹` and `C̃²` as extensions over `B`, via `f̃¹` and `f̃²`.
Their class difference `v_* e(C̃¹) − e(C̃²) ∗ g₀` belongs to
`Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B}, J²)`. Compatibility on `I` makes its restriction to
`Hom_{B₀}(I, J²)` zero. Its unique preimage under the transitivity injection
`Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) → Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B}, J²)` is the
obstruction to a morphism of `A`-extensions `g̃ : C̃¹ → C̃²` over `v` and `g₀` with
`f̃² = g̃ ∘ f̃¹`; when it vanishes, such `g̃` form a torsor under
`Der_{B₀}(C₀¹, J²) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀²}(C₀² ⊗ L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²)` ([GR] §3.2, Proposition 3.2.16, p. 43). In
particular, if `C` and `C'` are flat over `B` with reductions `C₀`, `C₀'` and `f₀ : C₀ → C₀'`, the
obstruction to lifting `f₀` lies in `Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I)` and lifts form a torsor under
`Hom(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I)` ([Sch12] §5, Theorem 5.12, p. 25, the almost version); with `L^a ≃ 0`
this gives unique lifting of morphisms, the full faithfulness in [Sch12] Theorem 5.10, and for `C₀`
étale over `B₀` morphisms lift uniquely (P0.24(i)). *Needs:* P0.21; P0.20.

`Almost.exalPush` pushes an extension along a linear map of its identified
kernel, and `Almost.exalPull` pulls it back along a map of quotient algebras.
Their representative statements specify
the resulting classes through maps of extensions that commute with the base,
quotient, and kernel inclusions ([GR] (2.5.5)–(2.5.7), p. 30, and (3.2.12)–(3.2.15),
pp. 42–43). `Almost.morphismObstruction` is the `Ext¹` class of the unique
preimage of `v_*[D₁] − g₀^*[D₂]` under `exalRestriction`.
Its existence statement supplies the unique preimage,
and its difference statement states its equality, with the
source-first order of subtraction. Its signature retains the two specified
kernel maps, their compatibility with the base extension, and `u₂ = v ∘ u₁`.

`Almost.liftMorphism` tests that particular obstruction for zero. Its torsor
is specified by the equality
`h − k = projection₁ ≫ cotangentDerivation(h −ᵥ k) ≫ inclusion₂`.
Thus a derivation acts by adding its composite through the quotient and
kernel; the negative action does not satisfy the contract. This also fixes
the identity-based automorphism comparison used in P0.22. If the relative
cotangent complex vanishes, a lift exists and is unique ([GR] Proposition
3.2.16, p. 43).

**Checks.** For `Almost.exalPush`, `_identity`, `_zero`, and `_negation` test identity,
zero, and negative identity on the kernel. For `Almost.exalPull`, `_identity`,
`_zero`, and `_section` test identity pullback, the zero extension class,
and a pullback with a specified section. For `Almost.morphismObstruction`, `_lift`,
`_zero_coefficient`, and `_unequal_classes` give zero for a supplied compatible
lift, zero for a zero target kernel, and a nonzero obstruction when the two
specified extension classes differ. These Checks are specified in this README only.

### P0.24 étale algebras lift along nilpotent ideals

**Étale almost algebras lift uniquely along nilpotent ideals.**
(*nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra and
`I ⊆ A` a nilpotent ideal (induction reduces to `I² = 0`), `A' := A/I`. (i) For `B` weakly étale
over `A`, `C` any `A`-algebra and `J ⊆ C` nilpotent, `Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C) → Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C/J)` is
bijective ([GR] §3.2, Theorem 3.2.18(i), p. 43). (ii) `B ↦ A' ⊗_A B` is an equivalence from weakly
étale `A`-algebras to weakly étale `A'`-algebras; (iii) it restricts to an equivalence of étale
algebras `A-Ét ≃ A'-Ét` ([GR] §3.2, Theorem 3.2.18(iii), p. 43) and (iv) to an equivalence of finite
étale algebras `A_fet ≃ A'_fet` (étale and almost finitely presented; [GR] §3.2, Theorem
3.2.28(ii), p. 46; almost finite presentation lifts by [GR] §3.2, Lemma 3.2.25(iii), p. 45). For
`A = (K°/ϖ^n)^a`, `n ≥ 2`, and `I = ϖ^{n−1}A`, finite étale `(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`-algebras lift uniquely to
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a`, the finite-level step of [GR] Theorem 5.3.27; in the classical setup the restriction of (iii) to finitely presented étale algebras
is [SGA1] Exposé I, Corollaries 5.5 and 8.3, printed pp. 6 and 12
([public edition](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0206203)); [GR] Theorem 3.2.18 supplies the larger category used here.
*Needs:* P0.22; P0.23; P0.14; P0.10.

Supporting result: vanishing of the almost cotangent complex when the diagonal is Tor-trivial
(*cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale*). For a basic setup `S` and a morphism `R → S'` of almost
algebras with `Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0` and `Tor^{S'⊗_R S'}_i(S', S') = 0` for all `i > 0` (the
`S' ⊗_R S'`-module structure via `μ`), `L_{S'/R} ≃ 0` in `D(S'_!!-Mod)`; in particular
`L_{S'/R} ≃ 0` for every weakly étale (hence every étale, every finite étale) morphism `R → S'`
([GR] §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36; used for weakly étale lifting in [GR] §3.2, proof of Theorem
3.2.18, p. 43). Every idempotent quotient `A → A/eA` is weakly étale, so `L_{(A/eA)/A} ≃ 0`; for a
perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra the vanishing `L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0` is of a different nature (Frobenius; [Sch12]
Proposition 5.13, layer P1).

### P0.25 faithfully flat descent

**Faithfully flat descent for almost modules and almost algebras.**
(*almost-faithfully-flat-descent*) Let `S` be a basic setup and `φ : A → B` a faithfully flat
morphism of almost algebras (P0.11). (i) `φ` is of effective descent for modules:
`M ↦ (B ⊗_A M, can)` is an equivalence from `A-Mod` to the category `Desc(B/A)` of `B`-modules `N`
with a `B ⊗_A B`-linear isomorphism `β : p₂*N ≅ p₁*N` satisfying the cocycle condition
`p₁₂*(β) ∘ p₂₃*(β) = p₁₃*(β)`; (ii) the same holds for `A`-algebras; (iii) both statements are
stable under base change `A → A'` (universal effective descent) ([GR] §3.4, introduction and
(3.4.1), p. 55); (iv) under (i) the full subcategories of flat, almost finitely generated, almost
finitely presented and almost finite projective modules correspond, and under (ii) those of weakly
étale, étale and finite étale algebras correspond (finite étale: combine étale with almost finitely
generated projective) ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1), pp. 55–56); (v) almost
projectivity descends when `B` is almost finitely presented over `A` (then `B` is almost finite
projective over `A`, so `B ⊗_A alHom_A(M, N) ≅ alHom_A(M, B ⊗_A N)` by
*tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective*, `B ⊗_A I` is `alHom_A(M, −)`-acyclic for `I`
injective, and `B ⊗_A alExt^i_A(M, N) ≅ alExt^i_B(B ⊗_A M, B ⊗_A N) = 0` for `i > 0`, whence
`alExt^i_A(M, N) = 0` by faithful flatness); for a general faithfully flat `φ` it is not asserted
([GR] §3.2, Remark 3.2.26(iii)–(iv), p. 45). For `M` almost finitely generated no hypothesis on `B` is
needed, since almost finite projective = flat + almost finitely presented descends by (iv). The
honest case is part of this target: for `V`-algebras `R → R'` with `R'` faithfully flat, (i) and
(ii) for the classical setup `S = classical V` are Grothendieck's effective descent of modules and
algebras ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1)). Mathlib supplies the comonadicity of `R' ⊗_R −` (`comonadicExtendScalars`)
and the degree `≤ 1` Amitsur statement for the ring itself (`CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`),
and descends injectivity, surjectivity and bijectivity of linear maps
(`Module.FaithfullyFlat.bijective_of_tensorProduct`); the identification of comodules with descent
data, hence the equivalence `R-Mod ≃ Desc(R'/R)`, is proved here, and for a general setup the
almostification of that descent is (i) for `R^a → R'^a`.
DiamondsAndVStacks layer D3 applies (ii) with `(S⁺/ϖ)^a` faithfully flat over `(R⁺/ϖ)^a` to descend
the datum on `(S̃⁺/ϖ)^a` to an almost `(R⁺/ϖ)^a`-algebra. *Needs:* P0.7; P0.10; Mathlib
`comonadicExtendScalars`, `ModuleCat.extendScalars`, `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`,
`CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`.

Three supporting results. Stability of flat, unramified and
étale morphisms (*etale-morphisms-stability*): for `φ : A → B`, `ψ : B → C`, (i) flatness, almost
projectivity, faithful flatness, almost finiteness, weak unramifiedness, unramifiedness, weak
étaleness and étaleness are stable under base change and (ii) under composition; (iii) if `φ` is
flat and `ψ ∘ φ` faithfully flat then `φ` is faithfully flat; (iv) if `φ` is weakly unramified and
`ψ ∘ φ` flat (weakly étale) then `ψ` is flat (weakly étale); (v) if `φ` is unramified and `ψ ∘ φ`
étale then `ψ` is étale; (vi) `φ` is faithfully flat iff it is a monomorphism and `B/A` is a flat
`A`-module; (vii) if `φ` is almost finite and weakly unramified then `φ` is unramified; (viii) if `ψ`
is faithfully flat and `ψ ∘ φ` flat (weakly unramified) then `φ` is flat (weakly unramified); finite
étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition ([GR] §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(i) and
(v)-(vii), p. 39). Classically (vi) is "faithfully flat iff injective with flat cokernel"; base change
of `L°a/K°a` along `K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a` gives a finite étale `(L°/ϖ)^a` over `(K°/ϖ)^a`. `B ↦ B_!!`
preserves and reflects faithful flatness, but not flatness (*lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness*):
(i) `φ` is faithfully flat iff `φ` is a monomorphism and `B/A` is a flat `A`-module ([GR] §3.1,
Lemma 3.1.2(vi), p. 39); (ii) `φ` is a monomorphism iff `φ_!! : A_!! → B_!!` is injective, and
`B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_!` is flat over `A_!!` iff `B/A` is flat over `A` (`m̃` flat is used here through
[GR] Proposition 2.4.35); (iii) hence `φ` is faithfully flat iff `φ_!!` is a faithfully flat ring map
([GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 40); (iv) flatness is not preserved: for `S = ofValuationRing V`
with residue field `k`, the flat projection `V^a × V^a → V^a` becomes `V ×_k V → V` under `(−)_!!`,
which is not flat ([GR] §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 39; [Bhatt] §4.2, Remark 4.2.8, p. 25; Mathlib
`Module.FaithfullyFlat`). The Amitsur complex of an almost faithfully flat map is exact
(*almost-amitsur-complex-exact*): for `φ : A → B` faithfully flat and `M` an `A`-module, the
augmented Amitsur complex `0 → M → M ⊗_A B → M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B → ⋯` (differentials the alternating sums
of the coface maps) is exact in `A-Mod`; in honest terms, for `V`-algebras `R → R'` such that `R'^a`
is faithfully flat over `R^a` (e.g. `Tor_i^R(X, R')` almost zero for `i > 0` and `X ⊗_R R'` almost
zero only if `X` is) and any `R`-module `N`, the cohomology of
`0 → N → N ⊗_R R' → N ⊗_R R' ⊗_R R' → ⋯` is almost zero, so `N^a` is the equalizer of
`(N ⊗ R')^a ⇉ (N ⊗ R' ⊗ R')^a` ([GR] §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 55; [ECD] §8, proof of Proposition 8.8,
p. 43; Mathlib `CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`). For `A → A × A` the Amitsur
complex is split exact; DiamondsAndVStacks layer D2 uses the almost exactness of
`R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ ⇉ S⁺/ϖ ⊗ S⁺/ϖ`.

`Module.baseChange` takes almost elements, extends scalars along the map of
almost-element rings, and almostifies. `Module.descentPseudofunctor` uses these
functors; `Algebra.descentPseudofunctor` uses pushouts of almost algebras. Their
descent data are Mathlib's `Pseudofunctor.DescentData`, including the cocycle equation.
The canonical comparison is an equivalence, also after any base change, by [GR] (3.4.1).

The coherence isomorphisms are fixed as follows. `Module.baseChangeUnit`
sends an almost element through the ordinary scalar-extension unit and the
almost-elements adjunction unit. `Module.baseChangeIdIso_exists` and
`Module.baseChangeCompIso_exists` give unique natural isomorphisms with the
prescribed generator equations; `Module.baseChangeIdIso` and
`Module.baseChangeCompIso` select them. `Module.baseChangeIdIso_unit` sends
the identity-extension generator back to the original element.
`Module.baseChangeCompIso_unit` sends an iterated generator back to its
direct-extension generator. These are the almost versions of Mathlib's

`mapId` and `mapComp` of `Module.descentPseudofunctor`. For
`Algebra.descentPseudofunctor` those fields are exactly `Under.pushoutId`
and `Under.pushoutComp`. Both use `pseudofunctorOfIsLocallyDiscrete` for
2-morphisms; associativity and the two unit equations concern these fixed

([GR] (3.4.1), p. 55).

### P0.26 tight ideals and henselian pairs

**Tight ideals, the Jacobson radical and henselian pairs of almost algebras.** (*tight-ideal*) Let
`S = (V, m)` be a basic setup and `A` an almost `V`-algebra; ideals of `A` are subobjects `I ↪ A`
stable under multiplication, with powers `Iⁿ` the images of `I^{⊗n}`. An ideal `I ⊆ A` is tight if
there are a finitely generated ideal `m₀ ⊆ m` and `n ∈ ℕ` with `Iⁿ ⊆ m₀·A` ([GR] §5.1, Definition
5.1.5, p. 103); for `ϖ ∈ m` the ideal `ϖA` is tight. The Jacobson radical of `A` is
`rad(A) := rad(A_*)^a` ([GR] §5.1, Definition 5.1.1, p. 103); for a `V`-algebra `R` and an ideal
`J ⊆ R`, `J^a ⊆ rad(R^a)` iff `mJ ⊆ rad(R)` ([GR] §5.1, Lemma 5.1.2, p. 103). A pair `(A, I)` with
`I ⊆ rad(A)` is henselian if `(A_*, m·I_*)` is a henselian pair (Mathlib
`HenselianRing A_* (m·I_*)`), and tight henselian if moreover `I` is tight ([GR] §5.1, Definition
5.1.8, p. 104); `(R^a, J^a)` is henselian iff `(R, mJ)` is ([GR] Lemma 5.1.10). If `A` is
`I`-adically complete (`A → lim A/Iⁿ` an isomorphism), `(A, I)` is henselian ([GR] §5.3, Remark
5.3.7, p. 112). Define `Almost.Algebra.IsTight` (`∃ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG ∧ ∃ n, Iⁿ ≤ m₀ • A`),
`Almost.Algebra.jacobson` (`rad(A) := (Ideal.jacobson ⊥ of A_*)^a`) and
`Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair` (`I ≤ rad A ∧ HenselianRing A_* (S.ideal • I_*)`); prove
`Almost.Algebra.isTight_span` (`ϖ • A` is tight for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`), `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.mono`
(subideals and powers of tight ideals are tight), `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.map` (tightness is
preserved by base change), `Almost.Algebra.le_jacobson_toAlmost_iff`
(`J^a ≤ rad(R^a) ↔ S.ideal • J ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥`),
`Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_toAlmost_iff` (`IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R (S.ideal • J)`), `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_of_isAdicComplete` and
`Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.elements_le_jacobson` (for `I` tight in `rad(A)`: `I_* ≤ rad(A_*)`, and
`(A_*, I_*)` is henselian if `(A, I)` is, [GR] Corollary 5.1.16). *Needs:* P0.8; P0.10; P0.11;
Mathlib `HenselianRing`, `Ideal.jacobson`, `IsAdicComplete`, `Submodule.FG`.

Two supporting results. The almost Nakayama lemma for tight ideals (*almost-nakayama*): for an
almost algebra `A` and `I ⊆ rad(A)` a tight ideal, (i) if `M` is an almost finitely generated
`A`-module with `IM = M`, then `M = 0` ([GR] §5.1, Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103); (ii) if `φ : N → M` is a
morphism of almost finite projective `A`-modules such that `φ ⊗_A A/I` is an isomorphism, then `φ`
is an isomorphism ([GR] §5.1, Corollary 5.1.7, p. 104); (iii) if `M` is almost finitely generated
and `M ⊗_A A/I = 0` then `M = 0` (Mathlib `Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`). For
`A = K°a` and `I = ϖA`, an almost finitely generated `M` with `M = ϖM` is zero; the finiteness
hypothesis is needed, since `K = K°[1/ϖ]` satisfies `K = ϖK`. Idempotents lift uniquely along tight
henselian pairs (*tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting*): for `(A, I)` a tight henselian pair (e.g.
`A` `I`-adically complete with `I` tight), `A → A/I` induces a bijection from the idempotents of
`A_*` to the idempotents of `(A/I)_*` ([GR] §5.1, Proposition 5.1.17, p. 105; [GR] §2.5, Proposition
2.5.13(i), p. 31, for square-zero extensions; Mathlib `HenselianRing`, `IsIdempotentElem`). The
honest case (`S = classical V`, a henselian pair `(A, J)` or an `J`-adically complete `A`) is Tau
Ceti's `TauCeti.HenselianRing.exists_isIdempotentElem_sub_mem` and
`TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.exists_isIdempotentElem_eq`; the tight almost version is what is new. In the classical setup, for
`A = (V⟦X⟧)^a` and `I = XA` the idempotents of `A_*` and of `(A/I)_* = (V^a)_*` agree; with the rank
decomposition it lifts the decomposition `A/ϖ = ∏ Ā_i` to `A`
in *uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi* (P0.28).

**Checks.**

- `Almost.Algebra.tight_test_principal` (computation) — for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`, the ideal `ϖA` is tight

### P0.27 almost finite projective modules over complete algebras

**Almost finite projective modules over I-adically complete almost algebras.**
(*adic-almost-projective-modules*) Let `S` be a basic setup, `A` an almost algebra and `I ⊆ A` a
tight ideal with `A → lim_n A/I^{n+1}` an isomorphism, `A_n := A/I^{n+1}` (Gabber–Ramero's
conditions (a), (b) of [GR] Lemma 5.3.5 for the system `(A_n)`; [GR] §5.3, Lemma 5.3.5(ii), p. 112).
Then `M ↦ (M ⊗_A A_n)_n` is an equivalence from almost finite projective `A`-modules to compatible
systems `(M_n)` of almost finite projective `A_n`-modules (`M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n`), with
quasi-inverse `(M_n) ↦ lim_n M_n` ([GR] §5.3, Theorem 5.3.24, p. 115; [GR] §5.3, (5.3.21), p. 115);
in particular `P ≅ lim_n P ⊗_A A_n` for every almost finite projective `P` ([GR] §5.3, Claim
5.3.25, p. 115). Moreover, if `M = lim_n M_n` for a compatible system of `A_n`-modules with
`M_{n+1} ⊗_{A_{n+1}} A_n ≅ M_n` (an `I`-c-adic module), and `M_0` is almost finitely generated,
then `M` is almost finitely generated and `M ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n` for every `n`. For `A = K°a` and `I = ϖA`, almost finite
projective `K°a`-modules are the limits of compatible almost finite projective `(K°/ϖ^n)^a`-modules;
P0.28 uses this for the underlying modules of finite étale algebras. *Needs:* P0.26; P0.10; P0.11;
P0.6.

scalar-extension isomorphisms. Morphisms are compatible families of module maps.
`adicReduction` is quotient scalar extension on objects and morphisms;
`adicReduction_evaluation` fixes each evaluation functor. The equivalence on
almost finite projectives is `adic_almost_projective_equivalence`.
`adic_almost_finitely_generated` gives effectivity from almost finite generation

almost zero (*almost-zero-limits-and-colimits*): for a basic setup `S` and any family `(M_i)_{i∈I}`
of almost zero `V`-modules, `∏_i M_i` and `⊕_i M_i` are almost zero; the colimit of any diagram of
almost zero modules is almost zero; for an inverse system `(N_n)_{n∈ℕ}` of almost zero modules,
`lim_n N_n` and `lim¹_n N_n = coker(∏ N_n → ∏ N_n, (x_n) ↦ (x_n − φ_n(x_{n+1})))` are almost zero;

all `i` and `N`; no finiteness or Mittag-Leffler hypothesis enters, the product being killed

### P0.28 finite étale lifting modulo a tight ideal

**Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely modulo a tight ideal of a complete almost algebra.**
(*finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras*) Let `S = (V, m)` be a basic setup
(`m̃` flat, needed for the cotangent complex behind the nilpotent lifting), `A` an almost
`V`-algebra and `I ⊆ A` a tight ideal (e.g. `I = ϖA` with `ϖ ∈ m`) such that `A` is `I`-adically
complete (`A → lim_n A/I^{n+1}` an isomorphism); flatness of `A` over `V^a` is not needed for the
equivalence itself. Then `B ↦ B ⊗_A A/I` is an equivalence of categories `A_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet`, with
quasi-inverse `B₀ ↦ lim_n B_n`, where `B_n` is the unique finite étale `A/I^{n+1}`-algebra lifting
`B₀` ([GR] §5.3, Theorem 5.3.27 with proof, p. 116). In particular, for `ϖ ∈ m` and `A`
`ϖ`-adically complete, `A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet`; this is [Sch12] Theorem 4.17 over an arbitrary basic
setup ([Sch12] §4, Theorem 4.17 with proof, p. 21, states it for `S = (K°, K°°)` and `A` flat over
`K°a`, citing [GR] Theorem 5.3.27 under the same number). Complements: in the case `I = ϖA`, if `A` is flat over `V^a`
then every `B ∈ A_fet` is flat over `V^a` and `ϖ`-adically complete,
by *finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete*; for root setups `B` is uniformly finite projective over
`A` iff `B/ϖB` is over `A/ϖ` by *uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi*. For `A = K°a` and
`ϖ ∈ K°°`, `K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet` is the middle link in
`K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet` ([Sch12] §4); for a finite étale
`(A/ϖ)`-algebra `B₀`, pairs `(B, ι : B/ϖB ≅ B₀)` with `B` finite étale over `A` exist and
are unique up to the unique isomorphism compatible with `ι`. The classical
case `m = V` with `A` `I`-adically complete (so `(A, I)` henselian) is included in
`Almost.Algebra.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence`: take `BasicSetup.classical V`
and use `Almost.Algebra.classicalEquiv` to identify ordinary algebras. The theorem
over a general basic setup and tight ideal is owned by P0.28 ([GR] Theorem 5.3.27,
p. 116). *Needs:* P0.14; P0.26; P0.24; P0.27; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

### P0.29 almost sheaves and almost cohomology

**Almost sheaves, almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech complexes on a site.**
(*almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology*) Let `(C, J)` be a site whose category of sheaves of
`V`-modules is abelian with enough injectives (Mathlib `sheafIsAbelian`, `HasSheafify`) and
`S = (V, m)` a basic setup. For a sheaf `F` of `V`-modules on `(C, J)` (Mathlib
`Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)`): `F` is almost zero if `m·F(U) = 0` for all `U`; almost zero sheaves form
a Serre class of the abelian category of sheaves, and the Serre localization `Almost.Sheaf J S` is
the category of sheaves of almost `V`-modules (a basic setup relative to the topos of `(C, J)`,
[GR] §3.3, (3.3.1)-(3.3.2) and the introduction, p. 47), with exact localization `F ↦ F^a`. For
`X ∈ C` and `n ≥ 0` the cohomology `H^n(X, F)` of the underlying abelian sheaf (Mathlib
`Sheaf.H'`) is a `V`-module through the action of `V` on `F`, and its almostification
`H^n(X, F)^a ∈ Almost.Module S` depends only on `F^a` (almost zero sheaves have almost zero
cohomology); `F` is almost acyclic on `X` if `H^n(X, F)^a = 0` for `n > 0`. For a family
`𝔘 = (U_i → X)` the Čech complex `Č(𝔘, F)` (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` on the underlying presheaf)
is a complex of `V`-modules with almostification `Č(𝔘, F)^a`, and the augmented complex
`F(X) → Č(𝔘, F)` is almost exact if its cohomology is almost zero ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, proof of
Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53). The Čech-to-derived comparison for almost acyclic bases is
*almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion*. Define `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostZero` (`∀ U, S.IsAlmostZero (F.val.obj U)`), `Almost.Sheaf` (the Serre localization of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)` at almost
isomorphisms of sheaves), `Almost.Sheaf.toAlmost` (the exact localization `F ↦ F^a`),
`Almost.Sheaf.cohomologyModule` (the `V`-module structure on `H^n(X, F)`), `Almost.Sheaf.almostH`
(`H^n(X, F)^a := (toAlmost S).obj (H^n(X, F))`), `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostAcyclic` (`∀ n > 0, IsZero (almostH F n X)`) and `Almost.Sheaf.almostCech` (`(toAlmost S).mapHomologicalComplex` of the Čech
complex); prove that almost zero sheaves form a Serre class, `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_eq_zero_of_isAlmostZero`
(almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology in all degrees; `almostH` factors through
`toAlmost`) and `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_localization` (for `ϖ ∈ S.ideal`: `almostH F n X ≅ 0 ⇒ H^n(X, F) ⊗ V[1/ϖ] = 0`, P0.16). *Needs:* P0.5; P0.16; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H'`,
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.map`, `CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor`, `CategoryTheory.sheafIsAbelian`,
`SerreClassLocalization.abelian`.

Supporting result: almost Čech acyclicity on a basis implies almost acyclicity
(*almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion*). Let `F` be a sheaf of `V`-modules and `𝔅` a full subcategory
of `C` stable under fibre products such that every covering of an object of `𝔅` is refined by a
covering by objects of `𝔅` (e.g. rational subsets of an affinoid adic space with finite rational
covers, or affinoid perfectoid objects of a pro-étale or v-site). If for every `U ∈ 𝔅` and every
covering `𝔘` of `U` by objects of `𝔅` the augmented Čech complex `F(U) → Č(𝔘, F)` is almost exact,
then `H^n(U, F)` is almost zero for all `U ∈ 𝔅` and `n > 0` (and `H^0(U, F) = F(U)`) ([ECD] §8,
proof of Proposition 8.8, printed p. 43 in
[v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.07343v4), for the affinoid perfectoid v-site; [Berkeley]
Lecture 7, proof of Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53). [Berkeley] Theorem 7.4.4 and [Sch12] Proposition 6.14
obtain `H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0` for `i > 0` on a perfectoid affinoid this way.
`Almost.Sheaf.almostCech_acyclicity_criterion` states the general basis criterion.
Induct on the cohomological degree: a class vanishes on a covering, the basis hypothesis
refines that covering, and the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence reduces to lower

### P1.3 pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge

**Pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge.**
(*pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*) Let `R` be a Tate ring. A pseudo-uniformizer
with compatible `p`-power roots is an element `ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_{n≥0}` of the multiplicative monoid
`lim_{x↦x^p} R` (Mathlib `Perfection R p`) such that `ϖ := ϖ^{1/p^0}` is a pseudo-uniformizer of
`R` lying in `R°` with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`. Then every `ϖ^{1/p^n}` is a pseudo-uniformizer in `R°`,
`ϖ^q := (ϖ^{1/p^n})^m` is well defined for `q = m/p^n ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}` (and for `q ∈ ℤ[1/p]` as a
unit of `R`), and, when `R` is perfectoid, `ϖ♭` is a pseudo-uniformizer of the tilt `R♭` with `(ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ`
(*tilt-integral-subrings*, P1.5). The gauge formula is defined for any such Tate ring; its norm properties require
`R` to be complete, Hausdorff and uniform. Attached to `ϖ♭` is the spectral gauge
`|x|_ϖ := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°}`, a power-multiplicative, submultiplicative,
ultrametric norm defining the topology of a nonzero `R`, with `|ϖ^qx|_ϖ = 2^{-q}|x|_ϖ`,
`R° = {x : |x|_ϖ ≤ 1}` and `R°° = {x : |x|_ϖ < 1}`; the normalisation `|ϖ|_ϖ = 1/2` is a
convention for nonzero `R`. On the zero ring the same infimum is zero; power-multiplicativity holds
there for positive exponents, and its exponent-zero form requires `R ≠ 0`. Changing `ϖ` gives an equivalent norm; it need not give a single real power of the old norm on a ring with several factors. The gauge is the spectral seminorm of
AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (`Huber.spectralSeminorm`, Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm`) applied to
its Tate norm datum `(R°, ϖ, 1/2)` (`Huber.TateNormDatum`). The compatible roots give the
`ℤ[1/p]`-exponent formula above; this formula and its `R°`-level identities are the added assertions. Existence is
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots* (P1.4) ([ECD] §3, Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [Sch12]
Remark 3.5, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44). Define `PseudoUniformizerRoots` (structure
on `R`: `roots : Perfection R p` with `coeff 0 roots ∈ R°`, `IsPseudoUniformizer (coeff 0 roots)`
and `(coeff 0 roots)^p ∣ p` in `R°`), `PseudoUniformizerRoots.root`

### P1.5 the sharp map

**The sharp map `♯: R♭ → R` (continuous, multiplicative, not additive).** (*sharp-map*) For a
perfectoid Tate ring `R`, the sharp map `♯ : R♭ → R`, `x ↦ x♯ := x^{(0)}` (Mathlib

multiplicative with `0♯ = 0`, and is not additive in general. It satisfies `(x^{1/p^n})♯ = x^{(n)}`;
`x ∈ R♭°` iff `x♯ ∈ R°`; `x♯ = 0` iff `x = 0`; for `x, y ∈ R♭°`, `(x + y)♯ ≡ x♯ + y♯ mod pR°`;

modulo `ϖ` is the ring isomorphism `R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ` of *tilt-integral-subrings*; and `(ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ`.

§6.2, p. 45; [AWS] Definition 2.3.14, p. 56 (`♯ = θ ∘ [·]`); [Sch12] Lemma 3.4(i), proof, p. 16).

statement about any ring `A` that is `π`-adically complete with `π^p | p`: surjectivity of the

### P1.10 perfectoid fields

Perfectoid fields follow: the definition, its characterisation, the Gelfand-spectrum and uniform
Banach-field inputs behind Kedlaya's theorem that a perfectoid Tate ring which is a field is a
perfectoid field, the tilt of a perfectoid field against Mathlib's `Tilt`, primitive elements of
`W(R⁺)`, and the identification of Fontaine's `θ` with Mathlib's.

**Perfectoid fields.** (*perfectoid-field-definition*) A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring
`K` (P1.1) whose underlying topological ring is a nonarchimedean field: `K` is a field, complete
with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value `|·|` defining its topology (in Lean,
`NontriviallyNormedField K` with `IsUltrametricDist K` and `CompleteSpace K`; the Tate structure has
ring of definition `K°`, the closed unit ball, and any `0 < |ϖ| < 1` as pseudo-uniformizer; `K` is
nonzero, so `p` is not a unit of `K°`; residue characteristic `p` is forced by `|p| < 1`) ([ECD] §3,
Definition 3.6, p. 15). Equivalently (P1.11; [Sch12] Definition 3.1, p. 15; [Bhatt] Definition 3.1.1,
p. 9): `K` is a nonarchimedean field which is not discretely valued, `|p| < 1`, and Frobenius is
surjective on `K°/p`. Its value group is `p`-divisible (*perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible*,
P1.15). In characteristic `p` a perfectoid field is the same as a complete perfect nonarchimedean
field ([Sch12] §3, after Lemma 3.2, p. 15). A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field
is automatically a perfectoid field (P1.14); `ℚ_p` and all discretely valued fields are not
perfectoid. Define `IsPerfectoidField` (`class IsPerfectoidField (K) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] : Prop`, extending `IsPerfectoidTateRing p K`) and

and the topologically nilpotent ideal is the open unit ball, using
`TauCeti.Huber.IsUniform.of_normedDivisionRing`, `isPowerBounded_iff_norm_le_one` and
`isBounded_closedBall_zero`. The compatibility signature at pin `a91d3aaf` and its canonical
supplier are specified in the internal-dependency note above;

### P1.11 characterisation of perfectoid fields

**Characterisation of perfectoid fields.** (*perfectoid-field-characterisation*) Let `K` be a
nonarchimedean field (complete with a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value). Then `K`
is a perfectoid field iff (i) `K` is not discretely valued, (ii) `|p| < 1`, and (iii) Frobenius
`Φ : K°/p → K°/p` is surjective ([ECD] §3, Proposition 3.8 with (i)–(iii), p. 15; [Berkeley]
Proposition 6.1.9, proof, p. 43). Condition (i) cannot be dropped: `ℚ_p` and its unramified
extensions satisfy (ii) and (iii) ([ECD] Remark 3.3, p. 14; [Sch12] §3, after Definition 3.1,
p. 15). Hence [Sch12] Definition 3.1 agrees with [ECD] Definition 3.6, and a nonarchimedean field is
a perfectoid ring in Kedlaya's sense iff it is a perfectoid field ([AWS] Corollary 2.3.11, p. 55).
`ℂ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl` and the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})` satisfy (i)–(iii) (P1.32a). *Needs:* P1.10;
Mathlib `NontriviallyNormedField`, `IsUltrametricDist`.

Lean: `IsPerfectoidField.iff`, with (i) stated as the accumulation of the norms at `1`.

### P1.12 Gelfand spectrum of a Banach ring

**The unit criterion on the Gelfand spectrum of a Banach ring.**
(*gelfand-spectrum-units-and-maximum-formula*) The Gelfand spectrum `M(A)` of a commutative
nonarchimedean Banach ring `A` (complete for a submultiplicative norm `|·|` with
`|a + b| ≤ max(|a|, |b|)`; not assumed to be over a field) — the bounded multiplicative seminorms
`α : A → ℝ_{≥0}` with the topology of pointwise convergence — together with its compactness, its
nonemptiness for `A ≠ 0` and Berkovich's maximum formula `|f|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(f)` for the
spectral seminorm, is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9 (*gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*, API
`GelfandSpectrum`, `GelfandSpectrum.compactSpace_nonempty`, `GelfandSpectrum.smoothingFun_eq_sSup`);
it is used
here for arbitrary nonarchimedean Banach rings, with the hypotheses stated there. The one clause
absent there is this target's content: `f ∈ A` is a unit iff `α(f) ≠ 0` for every `α ∈ M(A)`
([KBF] Lemma 2.4, proof, p. 4). For a complete Tate ring the carrier `M(A)` is the Berkovich
spectrum that DiamondsAndVStacks D5 uses downstream. The unit criterion and the maximum formula are the form
used by Kedlaya's Banach-field theorem (P1.13) and by the pointwise sharp-approximation lemma
(*sharp-approximation-lemma*, P1.23). *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9
(*gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*); Mathlib `MulRingSeminorm`, `RingSeminorm`,
`NonarchimedeanAddGroup`.

The proposed Lean form of the unit criterion, with no declaration in `Suggested.lean` yet, is
`gelfandSpectrum_isUnit_iff`, for a complete ultrametric
normed commutative ring. Its spectrum argument is written as the subtype of multiplicative
seminorms bounded by `C‖·‖` for some `C > 0`, the defining subtype of the spectrum owned by
AdicSpacesPartIII R3. No second spectrum definition is introduced.

### P1.13 uniform Banach fields over a nondiscretely valued field

**A uniform Banach field over a nondiscretely valued field is a nonarchimedean field.**
(*uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field*) Let `F` be a nonarchimedean field whose value group
`|F^×|` is dense in `ℝ_{>0}` (the discretely valued case is not covered by the proof, [KBF] Remark
3.9), and let `A` be a uniform Banach `F`-algebra (complete, with topology defined by a
power-multiplicative norm; equivalently the spectral seminorm `|·|_sp` is a norm defining the
topology) whose underlying ring is a field. Then `|·|_sp` is multiplicative, so `A` is a
nonarchimedean field ([KBF] Theorem 3.7 and its proof, pp. 10–11). The criterion used: a uniform
Banach field `A` is a nonarchimedean field iff `|t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1` for all `t ∈ A^×` ([KBF]
Remark 3.3, p. 8), because then `|x|_sp = |xy·y^{-1}|_sp ≤ |xy|_sp/|y|_sp`; the proof uses the
Berkovich spectrum (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.9 through P1.12: `M(A) ≠ ∅`, the unit criterion and
`|x|_sp = max_α α(x)`; [KBF] Lemma 2.4, proof, p. 4). Uniformity is essential: [KBF] Example 2.15, pp. 6–7, completes
`F(T_1,T_2,…)` for the norm
`β(x) = inf_{x=Σ_i x_i} max_i 2^{f(x_i)} α(x_i)`, where `α` is the multiplicative Gauss norm
and `f(x)` is the least number of initial variables needed to express `x`. This completion is
a nonuniform Banach field. The completion for `α` itself is a nonarchimedean field. The new
unit-criterion target of P1.12 is `GelfandSpectrum.isUnit_iff`; the norm target here is
`UniformBanachField.spectralNorm_mul` under the hypotheses of this paragraph. *Needs:* P1.12; Mathlib `NontriviallyNormedField`, `IsUltrametricDist`,
`CompleteSpace`.

### P1.14 a perfectoid Tate ring that is a field is a perfectoid field

**A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is a perfectoid field.**
(*perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field*) Let `A` be a perfectoid Tate ring (in the sense of
P1.1, with no perfectoid base field: such `A` need not be an algebra over any perfectoid field,
[KBF] Remark 4.3, p. 13) whose underlying ring is a field. Then the topology of `A` is defined by a
multiplicative absolute value, so `A` is a perfectoid field ([KBF] Theorem 4.2 and its proof (the
characteristic-`p` case via the base field `𝔽_p((z))^{perf}`, then the tilt), p. 13; answers [ECD]
§3, Remark 3.7, p. 15; [Berkeley] Remark 6.1.8, p. 43; [AWS] Theorem 2.9.1, p. 73). The theorem is
needed when the topology is given only by a ring of definition, e.g. for the field quotients
`ℚ_p^cycl` and `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` of Kedlaya's perfectoid ring over `ℚ_p` that lies over no
perfectoid field. *Needs:* P1.13; *tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*; *perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*;
P1.5.

Two supporting results. The tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p` (*tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring*): for `R` perfectoid, `R♭` is a complete
Hausdorff uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic `p`, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; `ϖ♭` is a
pseudo-uniformizer, `(R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°)` is a pair of definition (`TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`), and
`R♭ ≠ 0` iff `R ≠ 0` ([ECD] Lemma 3.10, p. 16; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44; [AWS] Lemma 2.7.1(b),
p. 66). A perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid field iff its tilt is (*perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*): for
`R` perfectoid with `ϖ♭` with compatible roots, `R` is a perfectoid field (a nonarchimedean field)
iff `R♭` is, and then the absolute values satisfy `|x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R` when normalised by
`|ϖ♭|_{R♭} = |ϖ|_R`, the spectral gauges being those of P1.3 ([Sch12] Lemma 5.21 and its proof,
pp. 27–28; [KL15] Lemma 3.5.2(a), p. 82, and Example 3.3.8, p. 78; [AWS] Corollary 2.3.11). For a
perfectoid field `K`, `K × K♭` is perfectoid but not a field, and its tilt `K♭ × K♭` is not a field.

### P1.16 primitive elements and ideals of degree one

**Primitive (distinguished) elements and ideals of degree 1 in `W(R⁺)`.**
(*primitive-degree-one-ideals*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`. An
element `ξ = Σ_{n≥0} p^n[ξ_n] ∈ W(R⁺)` is primitive of degree `1` (distinguished) if `ξ_0` is
topologically nilpotent and `ξ_1` is a unit of `R⁺`; equivalently `ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u` with
`u ∈ W(R⁺)^×` ([AWS] Definition 2.3.4, p. 54; [KL16] Definition 3.2.3, p. 57). An ideal `J ⊆ W(R⁺)`
is primitive of degree `1` if it is principal with a primitive generator. Equivalently ([ECD] §3,
Definition 3.15, p. 17), `J` is generated by an element `p + [ϖ♭]α` with `ϖ♭ ∈ R⁺` a
pseudo-uniformizer and `α ∈ W(R⁺)`: every such element is primitive, and every primitive element is
a unit multiple of one of this form, because a topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺` is divisible
by a pseudo-uniformizer ([KL16] Lemma 3.2.2, p. 56; [AWS] Exercise 2.3.6, p. 54). `ξ_0 = 0` is
allowed ([KL16] Remark 3.2.5, p. 57): `ξ = p` is primitive and corresponds to the untilt `R`
itself; `p²` and `[ϖ♭]` are not primitive when `R ≠ 0`; over the zero ring every Witt vector is primitive. In the notation of an untilt `S`, `R = S♭` and
`R⁺ = S♭⁺`. The coordinate predicates themselves are defined for any commutative topological ring `S`;
the equivalences and regularity results below concern nonzero characteristic-`p` perfectoid
pairs (`CharP R p` in Lean) with perfect plus rings as above. The zero coordinate predicates
are tested separately.
Define `IsPrimitive` (for `ξ : WittVector p R⁺`: `IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0 : R) ∧ IsUnit (ξ.coeff 1)`) and `IsPrimitiveIdeal` (`J : Ideal (WittVector p R⁺)` with `∃ ξ, IsPrimitive ξ ∧ J = Ideal.span {ξ}`), together with `IsDistinguished` (a Witt vector whose first
Witt coordinate is a unit, the notion of [BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23, used for `ker θ` in P1.18);
prove the Teichmüller form (`IsPrimitive ξ ↔ ∃ u : (W R⁺)ˣ, ξ = teichmuller p (ξ.coeff 0) + p * u ∧ IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0)`), that
`IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ → IsPrimitive (p + teichmuller p ϖ * α)` for every `α`, that every primitive
`ξ` is associated to such an element (`IsPrimitive ξ → ∃` unit `u`, pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ`, `α`,
`ξ = u * (p + [ϖ♭] α)`), that associates of primitive elements are primitive, the unit criterion
(`IsPrimitive ξ → IsPrimitive ξ' → ξ' = y * ξ → IsUnit y`,
*distinguished-element-criterion*, P1.18), that primitive elements are
nonzerodivisors ([Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.10, p. 46; [ECD] Lemma 3.16, p. 17),
`IsPrimitive.map` (for a morphism of perfectoid pairs of characteristic `p`,
`WittVector.map f` carries primitive elements to primitive elements, hence `J` to generators of
`J·W(R'⁺)`), that `p : W R⁺` is primitive (coefficients `(0, 1, 0, …)`),
`IsPrimitive.frobenius` (`φ(ξ)` and `φ^{-1}(ξ)` are primitive) and that a generator of `ker θ` is
primitive iff it is distinguished in the sense of [BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23 (`IsDistinguished`). *Needs:* P1.2;
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`; Mathlib
`WittVector`, `WittVector.teichmuller`.

### P1.17 ECD's `θ` is Mathlib's `fontaineTheta`

**ECD's `θ` is Mathlib's `WittVector.fontaineTheta`; surjectivity from `surjective_fontaineTheta`.**

ECD's `θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺`, `Σ_n p^n[r_n] ↦ Σ_n p^n r_n♯`. In particular `θ([x]) = x♯`

(`WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta`). Mathlib's `surjective_fontaineTheta` applies because Frobenius on

2.7.3, p. 67; [ECD] §3, Lemma 3.14(i) and its proof (the ring-map check through the ghost map modulo
`ϖ^m`), p. 17; [KL16] Definition 3.3.6, p. 59; [BMS] Definition 3.5, p. 21). Mathlib's
`fontaineThetaInvertP` and `BDeRhamPlus R⁺ p` are built on this `θ`. For `R = ℂ_p`,
`fontaineTheta` sends `[p♭]` to `p` and `[ε]` to `1`; for `R` of characteristic `p`, `θ` is

### P1.18 Fontaine's `θ`: the primitive kernel

Fontaine's map `θ` is treated next: its primitive kernel for any perfectoid Tate
pair, the untilt along a primitive ideal, and the proof that the untilt is a perfectoid Tate pair
whose tilt is the pair one started from.

**Fontaine's `θ: W(S♭⁺) → S⁺` has kernel generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor.**
(*fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel*) Let `(S, S⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (any
characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt `(S♭, S♭⁺)`, and `θ : W(S♭⁺) → S⁺`,
`Σ[r_n]p^n ↦ Σ r_n♯p^n`, Fontaine's ring homomorphism. (a) `θ` is surjective, by Mathlib's
`surjective_fontaineTheta` through the identification of P1.17. (b) `ker θ` is generated by a
primitive element of degree `1`, which can be taken of the form `ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α` with `ϖ♭ ∈ S♭⁺` a
pseudo-uniformizer such that `(ϖ♭♯)^p | p` in `S⁺`, and `α ∈ W(S♭⁺)`; `ξ` is a nonzerodivisor.
(c) An element of `ker θ` generates `ker θ` iff it is primitive ([BMS] Remark 3.11, p. 23). (d) `θ`
extends to a surjection `W(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]] → S` with kernel `ξW(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]`, and
`W(S♭⁺)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ♭♯`. If `pS = 0` then `ker θ = (p)` ([ECD] §3, Lemma 3.14(ii) and
its proof (the auxiliary `f` with `f♯ ≡ p mod pϖR⁺`, reduction to an isomorphism modulo `[ϖ♭]`),
pp. 17–18; [Berkeley] Lemma 6.2.8, proof, p. 46; [AWS]
Lemma 2.7.5, p. 67; [KL15] Lemma 3.6.3, p. 88, for `ℚ_p`-algebras; [Bhatt] Proposition 6.1.8,
p. 43, the field case). For `S = ℂ_p`: `ker θ = (p − [p♭])`, and `Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}` is another
generator. *Needs:* P1.17; P1.16; *tilt-integral-subrings* (P1.5); P1.5;
*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*; *distinguished-element-criterion*;
*quotient-by-primitive-element*.
