(*rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting*): let `R` be perfectoid with tilt `R♭`, `ϖ♭` with

in `R°`. (a) `R⁺ ↦ R♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺ = {x ∈ R♭ : x♯ ∈ R⁺}` is an inclusion-preserving bijection

(c) On both sides, rings of integral elements correspond to integrally closed subrings of the

### P1.19 the untilt along a primitive ideal

**The untilt of `(R, R⁺)` along a primitive ideal `J`: `(W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R⁺)/J)`.**
(*untilt-construction*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p`, `J ⊆ W(R⁺)`
a primitive ideal of degree `1` and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudo-uniformizer. The untilt of `(R, R⁺)` along
`J` is the pair `(A, A⁺)` with `A⁺ := W(R⁺)/J` and `A := A⁺[1/π]`, `π` the image of `[ϖ]`,
topologised so that `A⁺` is open with its `π`-adic (equivalently `(p,[ϖ])`-adic) topology;
equivalently `A = W^b(R)/J·W^b(R)` with `W^b(R) = W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]`. `A` is a complete Hausdorff Tate
ring with pseudo-uniformizer `π` and ring of definition `A⁺`, independent of the choice of `ϖ`; the
construction is functorial for morphisms of pairs `f` with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'` (then
`J' = W(f)(J)·W(R'⁺)`), and comes with the multiplicative map `♯_J : R → A`, given on
`x ∈ R⁺` by `θ_J([x])` (`θ_J` the quotient map followed by localization), and extended by
inverting a pseudo-uniformizer, with `♯_J(ϖ) = π`. That `(A, A⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R, R⁺)`
is P1.20 ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.17, p. 18; [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.11, p. 47; [AWS] Theorem 2.3.9,
p. 55, and Remark 2.3.3, p. 54; [Sch12] Remark 5.19, p. 27). Define `untilt` (`untilt (P : Pair R) J : Type`, the ring `W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] ⧸ J·W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]`, with the choice-free description
`W^b(R)/JW^b(R)`), `untiltPlus` (the subring `A⁺`, the image of `W(R⁺) ⧸ J` in `A`),
`untilt.instIsTateRing` (`IsTateRing`, `CompleteSpace`, `T2Space` and `NonarchimedeanRing`
instances, with pair of definition `(A⁺, πA⁺)`), the canonical `θ_J : W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]] →+* untilt P J` from Mathlib’s
`IsLocalization.map` applied to `Ideal.Quotient.mk J`; its surjectivity and kernel are
`IsLocalization.map_surjective_of_surjective` and `IsLocalization.ker_map`, `untilt.sharp` (`sharp_J : R →* untilt P J`,
`x ↦ θ_J([x])`, continuous and multiplicative; `sharp_J ϖ` is a pseudo-uniformizer) and
`untilt.map` (for arbitrary ideals `J,J'`, a pair morphism with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'`
induces a ring homomorphism; when both ideals are primitive this map is continuous;
`untilt.map_id`, `untilt.map_comp`, `untilt.continuous_map`); prove `untilt.quotEquiv` (`untiltPlus ⧸ (sharp_J ϖ) ≃+* R⁺ ⧸ (ϖ)`, for a
choice of `ϖ` for which `J` has a generator `p + [ϖ]α` as in *quotient-by-primitive-element*),
`untilt.congr_pseudoUniformizer` (canonical isomorphism between the constructions for two choices
of `ϖ`), `untilt.isPerfectoidTateRing` (the untilt is perfectoid with ring of integral elements
`untiltPlus`, P1.20), `untilt.tiltEquiv` (`tilt (untilt P J) ≃+* R`, identifying the plus rings and
`ker θ` with `J`, P1.20) and `untilt_p_recovery` (`untilt P (span {p}) ≃+* R`). *Needs:* P1.16;
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; *quotient-by-primitive-element*; Mathlib `Localization.Away`,
`WittVector`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`.

For every characteristic-`p` perfectoid Tate pair `P` and primitive ideal `J`,

### P1.21 untilts are classified by primitive ideals

The classification of untilts follows, with marked untilts, the behaviour of strict inclusions
under tilting, integral perfectoid rings and the integral/Tate dictionary, and the flat deformation
of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ`.

**Untilts are classified by primitive ideals of degree 1.**
(*untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals*) The functors `(S, S⁺) ↦ (S♭, S♭⁺, ker θ_S)` and
`(R, R⁺, J) ↦ (W(R⁺)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R⁺)/J)` are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between
(i) perfectoid Tate pairs `(S, S⁺)` with morphisms of Huber pairs and (ii) triples `(R, R⁺, J)`
with `(R, R⁺)` a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` and `J ⊆ W(R⁺)` primitive of degree
`1`, a morphism being a morphism `f` of pairs with `W(f)(J) ⊆ J'` (then `J' = W(f)(J)W(R'⁺)`). No
perfectoid base field is fixed and both characteristics are allowed. The unit is induced by
`θ_S : W(S♭⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ker θ ≅ S`, the counit is the identification of P1.20, and both are natural.
Characteristic-`p` pairs correspond to `J = (p)` ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.17 with (ii), p. 18; [KL16]
Theorem 3.3.8, p. 60; [AWS] Theorem 2.3.9, p. 55, and Remark 2.3.18, p. 57; [KL15] Theorem 3.6.5,
p. 89, the characteristic-`0` case; [Berkeley] Definition 6.2.9, Lemma 6.2.10 and Theorem 6.2.11,
pp. 46–47). For `(K♭, K♭°)` with `K` a perfectoid field and `J = ker θ`, the construction returns
`(K, K°)`; over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, `J = (p)` gives the field itself, `J = (p − [t])` the
completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`, `J = (Σ_{i<p}[1+t]^{i/p})` the field `ℚ_p^cycl`, and `φ(J)` gives
Frobenius-twisted markings. *Needs:* P1.20; *untilt-tilt-identification*; P1.18; P1.19; P1.6;
*theta-kernel-base-change*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

Supporting result: `ker θ` is compatible with base change (*theta-kernel-base-change*). Let
`f : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` be a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (`f` continuous with `f(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺`)
with tilt `f♭`. Then `θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R` and `ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭⁺)`; every generator

The categorical carriers are `PairCat p` and `PrimitiveTriple p`. `PairCat` stores

### P1.23 strict inclusions under tilting

**Strict inclusions correspond under tilting.** (*strict-inclusions-under-tilting*) A continuous
ring homomorphism `f : A → B` of complete Hausdorff Tate rings is a strict inclusion if it is
injective and a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology (equivalently, as `A` is
complete, a topological ring isomorphism onto a closed subring); strictness is a topological
condition and injectivity alone does not suffice. Let `A` be a perfectoid Tate ring, `ϖ♭ ∈ A♭` with
compatible roots, `ϖ = ϖ♭♯`, and `f : A → B` continuous. (a) If `B` is a perfectoid Tate ring, `f`
is a strict inclusion if and only if `f♭ : A♭ → B♭` (P1.6) is ([AWS] Theorem 2.4.3 and its proof
(completed by Lemma 2.8.1), p. 57). (b) More generally, let `B` be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring (`p` is topologically
nilpotent in `B` because it is in `A`) and `B♭` its tilt (P1.7; `f(ϖ) = (f♭ϖ♭)♯` has compatible
roots and `f(ϖ)^p | p` in `B°`). For the spectral gauges `|·|_ϖ`, `|·|_{f(ϖ)}`, `|·|_{ϖ♭}`,
`|·|_{f♭ϖ♭}`: `f` is a strict inclusion iff `|f(a)| = |a|` for all `a ∈ A`; `f♭` is a strict
inclusion iff it is isometric; and `f` is a strict inclusion iff `f♭` is ([AWS] Lemma 2.8.1, p. 69,
whose second right-hand side should read `zW^b(A♭)`; [AWS] Lemma 2.8.4, proof, p. 70; [KL16] Lemma
3.3.23, p. 66). The analogous statement for injections that are not strict is [AWS] Corollary
2.9.13 and is not stated here. A finite extension `K ⊆ L` of perfectoid fields is a strict
inclusion, and so is `K♭ ⊆ L♭`; the continuous injection `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,

its tilt `T ↦ ϖ♭T`. *Needs:* P1.6; P1.7; P1.1; P1.3; *metric-perfectoid-criterion*;

`W^b(A♭) := W(A♭°)[1/[ϖ♭]] → A`, and give `W^b(A♭)` the Gauss norm `|Σ_n p^n[x_n]| := sup_n |x_n|`;
an element `x = Σ_n p^n[x_n]` is prepared if `|x_0| ≥ |x_n|` for all `n ≥ 1`. Then: (a) (Euclidean
division) for `x ∈ W^b(A♭)` put `x′ := p^{-1}(x − [x_0])` and
`r(x) := x − z_1^{-1}x′z = [x_0] − [z̄_0]z_1^{-1}x′`; if `x ∉ zW^b(A♭)`, the terms of the sequence
`x, r(x), r(r(x)), …` are congruent to `x` modulo `z` and are prepared from some term on; no nonzero
element of `zW^b(A♭)` is prepared; (b) (norms) `|θ(x)| ≤ |x|` for every `x`, with equality when `x`
is prepared; hence the quotient norm of the Gauss norm on `W^b(A♭)/(z) ≅ A` is the spectral gauge,
and `|z̄_0| = |p|` (`|p| < 1`, and `|p| = 0` iff `pA = 0`); (c) (sharp approximation) for every
`a ∈ A` there is `y ∈ A♭` with `|a − y♯| ≤ |p|·|a|`, so `|y| = |a|`; for `a ∈ A°` one can take
`y ∈ A♭°`; (d) (pointwise form) `α ↦ α ∘ ♯` maps the Gelfand spectrum `M(A)` of bounded
multiplicative seminorms on `(A, |·|)` into `M(A♭)`, and for every `a ∈ A` and `ε > 0` there is
`y ∈ A♭` with `α(a − y♯) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a), ε}` for all `α ∈ M(A)` simultaneously; with
`|·| = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α` (P1.12; [AWS] Lemma 1.5.21, p. 25) this refines (c) up to `ε`; (e)
(quasi-additivity of `♯`) `|(x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯| ≤ |p|·max{|x|, |y|}` for `x, y ∈ A♭`. Part (d) uses
the Gelfand spectrum and the maximum formula of P1.12; parts (a)–(c) and (e) do not ([AWS]
Definition 2.6.5, Lemma 2.6.7 and Lemma 2.6.9, p. 64; [AWS] Lemma 2.8.3, proof, and Lemma 2.8.5,
proof, p. 70; [KL16] Lemma 3.2.7(a) with proof, p. 57, and Theorem 3.3.18, proof of case (ii),

characteristic `p`, `z = p`, `z̄_0 = 0`, `|p| = 0`, `r(x) = [x_0]` is prepared after one step and

### P1.24 integral perfectoid rings

**Integral perfectoid rings.** (*integral-perfectoid-rings*) A commutative ring `R` is integral
perfectoid if there is `π ∈ R` with `π^p | p` such that `R` is `π`-adically complete and separated,
the Frobenius `R/p → R/p` is surjective, and the kernel of Fontaine's map `θ : W(R♭) → R` is
principal, where `R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R/p` is the tilt (Mathlib's `PreTilt`) ([BMS] §3.2, Definition
3.5, p. 21). Equivalent forms: for a nonzerodivisor `π` with `π^p | p` and `R` `π`-adically
complete, `R` is integral perfectoid iff Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p` is an isomorphism; every integral
perfectoid `R` admits a unit multiple of `π` with a compatible system of `p`-power roots ([BMS]
Lemma 3.9 and Lemma 3.10, p. 22). Integral perfectoid rings may have `p`-torsion and need not be
domains. Define `IsIntegralPerfectoid` with an admissible adic element, surjective Frobenius,
and principal kernel of the supplied Fontaine map. In Lean the last condition quantifies over
proofs that `p` is a nonunit and that the ring is `p`-adically complete. The latter follows from
the adic presentation by [Stacks] Tag 090T; if `p` is a unit, that presentation forces the zero
ring, and the unique map has principal kernel. Thus the condition includes the zero ring without
an impossible `Fact ¬IsUnit p` instance. Prove that
for every `π` with `π^p | p` and `R` `π`-adically complete, Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p`
is bijective, with no nonzerodivisor hypothesis ([BMS] Lemma 3.10(i), p. 22), and that
for `π^p ∣ p` with `R` `π`-adically
complete, a unit multiple of `π` has compatible `p`-power roots. The zero ring satisfies the
definition using the unique Fontaine map; for nonzero rings use Mathlib’s `PreTilt` and `θ`. *Needs:* Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `PreTilt`, `WittVector.fontaineTheta`.

**Checks.**

- Non-example: `ℤ_p` is not integral perfectoid: Frobenius
  on `ℤ_p/p = 𝔽_p` is bijective and `ker θ = 0` is principal, but no admissible `π` exists: `π^p | p`
  forces `p·v_p(π) ≤ 1`, so `π` is a unit (`π = p` fails, `p^p ∤ p`), and `ℤ_p` is not `π`-adically
  complete for a unit `π` (`lim ℤ_p/π^n = 0 ≠ ℤ_p`).
- Computation: the `p`-adic completion of
  `ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]` is integral perfectoid with `π = p^{1/p}`.
- `integral_perfect_charP` (degenerate) — a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra that is `π`-adically
  complete for some `π` is integral perfectoid (`π^p | p = 0` trivially).

The proposed Mathlib [integral-perfectoid interface](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/26385)

is the complete separated `π`-adic topology and the chosen element satisfies `π^p ∣ p`; the
comparison must include the principal Fontaine-kernel condition.

`IntegralAdicPresentation p A π` records the divisibility, completeness, Frobenius and

relates it to the algebraic predicate under `π^p ∣ p` and completeness for that same `π`.
It uses the pinned Fontaine map, including its nonunit hypothesis. This specifies the algebraic

### P1.25 perfectoid Tate rings and integral perfectoid rings

**`R perfectoid Tate ⇔ R⁺ integral perfectoid and bounded`.** (*integral-perfectoid-comparison*) Let
`R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring and `R⁺` a ring of integral elements. If `R` is a perfectoid
Tate ring, then `R⁺` (and `R°`) is an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of P1.24: `π`-adically
complete for some `π ∈ R⁺` with `π^p | p` in `R⁺` (exact divisibility, as in P1.24; such a `π`
exists by *frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring* (b), and may be taken a pseudo-uniformizer of `R`),
Frobenius surjective on `R⁺/p`, and the kernel of `θ : A_inf(R⁺) → R⁺` principal. Conversely, if
`R⁺` is integral perfectoid and bounded in `R`, then `R` is a perfectoid Tate ring; boundedness of
`R⁺` is necessary for the converse (a non-bounded `R⁺` cannot occur inside a uniform `R`; conversely
`ϖR° ⊆ R⁺` for a bounded open integrally closed `R⁺`, so `R` is uniform), and the point of the
converse is to produce a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ'` of `R` with `ϖ'^p | p`: the given `π` is one when
`p` is a unit of `R`, but need not be a unit of `R` in general (`K × K♭` with `R⁺ = K° × K♭°` is
integral perfectoid for `π = (π_K, 0)`, and a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra for `π = 0`) ([BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.20 with its proof and the text before it, pp. 26–27; [BMS]
Definition 3.5, p. 21; [BMS] Lemma 3.10(ii), p. 22). The forward
direction is *frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring* (P1.17) together with the primitive-kernel theorem
(P1.18); what is proved here is the converse. Together with
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* ([BMS] Lemma 3.21, P1.20) this compares the integral
notion with the Tate-ring notion of this layer.
`ℤ_p^cycl`, `𝒪_{ℂ_p}` and the `p`-adic completion of `ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]` are integral perfectoid
([BMS] Example 3.6) and `ℚ_p^cycl`, `ℂ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` are perfectoid Tate rings; perfect
`𝔽_p`-algebras are integral perfectoid with `π = 0`, but with the discrete topology they are not
Tate, so the comparison needs `R` Tate. *Needs:* P1.1; P1.24; *perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid*;
*frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring*; *integral-elements-adically-complete*.

The reverse criterion of P1.24 holds
with a nonzerodivisor `π`, `π^p ∣ p`, and completeness for that same `π` ([BMS] Lemma 3.10(ii)):
bijectivity of Frobenius `R/π → R/π^p` then gives integral perfectoidness.
`isPerfectoidTateRing_iff_integral P` states the comparison for a complete Hausdorff Tate ring
and its actual ring of integral elements, with boundedness retained on the integral side.

### P1.26 flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ`

**Unique flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo `ϖ` over a perfectoid field.**
(*deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras*) Let `K` be a complete nontrivially
normed ultrametric perfectoid field, and choose a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` with compatible
roots and `ϖ^p ∣ p` in `K°`. The element `ϖ` is a nonzerodivisor on `K°`, and
`ϖ^{n−1}K°/ϖ^nK° ≅ K°/ϖ` is square-zero in `K°/ϖ^n` for `n ≥ 2`. Reduction modulo `ϖ`,
`A ↦ A/ϖ`, is an equivalence between (i) `ϖ`-adically complete `K°a`-algebras `A` that are
(almost) flat over `K°a` with `Φ : A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ`, and (ii) (almost) flat
`(K°/ϖ)^a`-algebras `B` with `Φ : B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B`. Concretely `B` lifts uniquely, through the
square-zero extensions `(K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a`, to a compatible system of flat
`(K°/ϖ^n)^a`-algebras `B_n` with `B_n/ϖ^{n−1} ≅ B_{n−1}`, and `A = lim B_n`; two flat
deformations with the same reduction are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the reduction.
The limit has no `ϖ`-torsion on almost elements, which implies flatness over the valuation
ring `K°` and almost flatness over `K°a` ([Sch12] Lemma 5.3(i), p. 22).
The almost deformation theory used (obstructions in `Ext²`, torsors under `Ext¹`, automorphisms
`Hom`, lifting of morphisms) is P0.22. This is [Sch12] Theorem 5.10, p. 24, with proof on p. 26,
the step `K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf` of Theorem 5.2, p. 22. Base flatness is retained in the
categories; the equivalence has field scope, as in P1.28. P1.27 supplies the arbitrary-base
tilting equivalence via primitive ideals.
This is Scholze's deformation-theoretic route: the tilting equivalence (P1.27) and the mod-`ϖ`
equivalence (P1.28) are derived from P1.21 and do not depend on it. `K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and
`K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` have the same reduction `(K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}]` and are therefore tilts of each other
([Sch12] Proposition 5.20). *Needs:* P0.22; P0.20; P0.16; P0.19; *cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi*; Mathlib
`IsAdicComplete`, `Module.Flat`.

Supporting result: the Frobenius criterion for vanishing of the (almost) cotangent complex
(*cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi*). (a) Let `A_0 → B` be a map of `𝔽_p`-algebras such that
the relative Frobenius `A_0(Φ) ⊗^L_{A_0} B → B(Φ)` is an isomorphism in `D(A_0)` (a hypothesis on
the derived relative Frobenius, not on `Ω¹` alone). Then `L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0`; in particular
`L_{B/𝔽_p} ≃ 0` for `B` perfect, and `L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0` whenever `A_0 → B` is flat and relatively
perfect. (b) The almost version holds over any basic setup `(V, m)` with `V` an `𝔽_p`-algebra: if
the relative Frobenius of a map of almost algebras is an isomorphism in the almost derived
category, then the almost cotangent complex `L^a` (P0.20) vanishes. (c) For `R` a perfectoid Tate
ring, `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` with compatible roots, and `A` a `(R°/ϖ)^a`-algebra which is (almost) flat over
`(R°/ϖ)^a` with `Φ : A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A`, `L^a_{A/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0`; for `R = K` a perfectoid field this is
[Sch12] Corollary 5.16 ([GR] arXiv v3, Lemma 6.5.9(i) with proof, pp. 176–177 (LNM 1800 Lemma
6.5.13(i)); [Sch12] §5, Proposition 5.13(i)–(ii) with proof, p. 25, and Corollary 5.16, proof,
p. 26; [Bhatt] Proposition 6.1.4, p. 42). `Ω¹_{R/𝔽_p} = 0` for perfect `R`, since
`dx = d(y^p) = py^{p−1}dy = 0` ([Sch12] Remark 5.14); the degree `0` and `1` parts are Mathlib's
`KaehlerDifferential` and `Algebra.H1Cotangent`. The classical cotangent complex with its
simplicial description, transitivity and Tor-independent base change is P0.19.

The categories `IntegralAlmostPerfectoid p R ϖ` and `ModAlmostPerfectoid p R ϖ` are full

### P1.27 the tilting equivalence

The layer closes with the tilting equivalence over an arbitrary perfectoid base, the mod-`ϖ`
equivalence over a perfectoid field, completed filtered colimits, perfected Tate algebras, the
cyclotomic field, the standard examples and the compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F`.

**Tilting equivalence `Perf_R ≃ Perf_{R♭}` over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring, with the explicit
tilt.** (*tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
and `J_R := ker(θ_R : W(R♭°) → R°)`, a primitive ideal (P1.18). No perfectoid base field is fixed;
continuous homomorphisms between Tate rings preserve power-bounded elements into uniform targets
(`map_mem_powerBoundedSubring`, P1.1), so `R`-algebras are pairs over `(R, R°)`. The tilting
functor `S ↦ S♭` (`R♭ → S♭` the tilt of `R → S`, P1.6) is an equivalence from perfectoid
`R`-algebras to perfectoid `R♭`-algebras, with quasi-inverse
`T ↦ T♯ := W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]/J_R·W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]`, the untilt along `J_R·W(T°)` (P1.19); the unit
`S ≅ (S♭)♯` is induced by `θ_S` and the counit `(T♯)♭ ≅ T` by P1.20, both natural. Explicitly
`S♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} S`, `S♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} S° ≅ lim_Φ S°/ϖ` and `S♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ S°/ϖ`; the functor is
independent of choices, extends to pairs `(S, S⁺) ↦ (S♭, S♭⁺)`, and `S` is a perfectoid field iff
`S♭` is, by *perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field*. For `R = K` a perfectoid field,
`T♯ = W(T°) ⊗_{W(K♭°)} K°[1/ϖ]` ([Sch12] Remark 5.19, p. 27; [Bhatt] Remark 6.2.8), and the functor
agrees with Scholze's chain `K-Perf ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf ≃ K♭°a-Perf ≃ K♭-Perf` ([ECD] §3, Theorem 3.13 with its proof ("the proof works in general", here supplied by the
untilt classification) and the text after it, p. 17; [Berkeley] Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45; [AWS] Remark
2.3.17, p. 56; [Sch12] Theorem 5.2, p. 22, and Proposition 5.17, p. 26, over a perfectoid field).
The tilt of `R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` is `R♭⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` with `T_i♯ = T_i`
(P1.30; [Sch12] Proposition 5.20; [AWS] Example 2.3.15). *Needs:* P1.21; *theta-kernel-base-change*;

### P1.28 the equivalence through the mod-`ϖ` category

**`Perf_K ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf` over a perfectoid field.**
(*perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence*) Let `K` be a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric
perfectoid field, and choose compatible roots of a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ` with `ϖ^p ∣ p` in
`K°`. Use the almost setup `(K°, K°°)`. A perfectoid `K°a`-algebra is a flat, `ϖ`-adically
complete almost algebra `A` with Frobenius `A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ` an isomorphism. A perfectoid
`(K°a/ϖ)`-algebra is a flat algebra over that almost base with Frobenius
`B/ϖ^{1/p} → B` an isomorphism. The functors `S ↦ S°a` and `A ↦ A/ϖ` are equivalences between
these categories and perfectoid `K`-algebras ([Sch12] Definition 5.1(ii)–(iii), Theorem 5.2,
pp. 21–22, and Theorem 5.10, p. 24, with proof on p. 26). Identifying the base reductions gives the chain of
equivalences with the corresponding categories over `K♭`.

The source scope here is a field. An unrestricted version over a perfectoid Tate ring `R`,
with almost flatness over `Λ = 𝔽_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x)` replacing base flatness, requires a reference
proving that exact category equivalence, including the inverse-limit lifting and almost-elements
claims. [ECD] Proposition 9.3, p. 44, supplies the totally disconnected application, with the
base-flatness input of Proposition 7.23; it does not supply the unrestricted statement. P1.27
retains the arbitrary-base tilting equivalence via primitive ideals.

Two supporting results have the same field scope. The *almost-integral-dictionary* sends
`S` to `S°a` and sends `A` to `A_*[1/ϖ]`, with `A_*` open and `ϖ`-adic. For a torsion-free
`K°`-module `N`, its almost elements are the elements `x ∈ N[1/ϖ]` such that
`ϖ^{1/pⁿ}x ∈ N` for every `n`. Reduction of almost elements gives an inclusion
`A_*/ϖ^qA_* ⊆ (A/ϖ^qA)_*`, not an equality in general; its cokernel is almost zero
([Sch12] Lemma 5.3, Remark 5.4, and Lemmas 5.6–5.7, pp. 22–23).

For *frobenius-inverse-limit-lifting-in-characteristic-p*, assume `K` has characteristic `p`.

### P1.29 completed filtered colimits

**Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with
them.** (*completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings*) Let `J` be a small filtered category (hence
nonempty) and `j ↦ R_j` a functor from `J` to perfectoid Tate rings (each in the sense of P1.1)
with continuous ring homomorphisms `φ_a : R_i → R_j` (no injectivity, flatness or density assumed;
characteristic `0`, `p` or neither; no perfectoid base field). Fix `j₀ ∈ J` and a
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ♭ ∈ R_{j₀}♭` with compatible roots, `ϖ = ϖ♭♯`, which exists by
*exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots*; on the tail `J_{j₀} = Under j₀` (final in `J`,
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`) the images of `ϖ` and of its roots are
pseudo-uniformizers with compatible roots and `ϖ^p | p` in every `R_j°` (a compatible
pseudo-uniformizer). The ring `R` with its maps `ι_j : R_j → R` is formed here by

### P1.31 the completed cyclotomic field

**The completed cyclotomic field `ℚ_p^cycl` is a perfectoid field; its tilt and primitive ideal.**
(*cyclotomic-perfectoid-field*) For any prime `p` and `ζ_{p^n}` a compatible system of primitive
`p^n`-th roots of unity, the completion `ℚ_p^cycl` of `ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})` is a perfectoid field: its
valuation ring is the `p`-adic completion `ℤ_p^cycl` of `ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}]`, its value group
`|p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)}` is nondiscrete and Frobenius on `ℤ_p^cycl/p` is surjective; the
pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1` has `ϖ^p | p` (`v_p(ϖ^p) = 1/(p−1) ≤ 1`), whereas `ζ_p − 1`
does not (`v_p((ζ_p − 1)^p) = p/(p−1) > 1`); for `p = 2`, `ϖ = ζ_4 − 1` has `ϖ² = −2ζ_4`, so
`ϖ² | 2`, while `(ζ_2 − 1)² = 4 ∤ 2` ([ECD] §3, Example
3.4(i), p. 14; [KL15] Example 3.3.8, p. 78, and Remark 3.5.12, p. 86; [BMS] Example 3.6, p. 21).
Its tilt is the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))` with `t = ε − 1`, `ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …)`, with
`|t♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)}` ([Berkeley] Example 6.2.4, p. 44), and it is the untilt of
`(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^)` along the primitive ideal generated by
`Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[1 + t]^{i/p}` ([AWS] Example 2.3.8, p. 54; [KL15] Example 3.3.8, p. 78). `ℤ_p^×`
acts compatibly, by `γ(t) = (1 + t)^γ − 1` on the tilt. For a finite extension `K` of `ℚ_p`, the
completion of `K(μ_{p^∞})` is the finite extension `K·ℚ_p^cycl` of `ℚ_p^cycl`, perfectoid by the
stability of perfectoid fields under finite extension of layer P3 ([Sch12] Theorem 3.7(i); [KL15]
Theorem 3.5.6). *Needs:* P1.11; P1.15; P1.19; Mathlib `Padic`, `PadicInt`.

### P1.32 perfectoidness

[ECD] §15, Lem. 15.3, p. 90 (stated for every Tate `ℤ_p`-algebra) and [Berkeley] Lecture 10,
Lem. 10.1.6, p. 75 (stated for every Tate ring in which `p` is topologically nilpotent) give the
perfectoidness of the completed tower; here its base ring is complete, because the henselian
comparison that transfers finite étale splittings to the completion needs that hypothesis, and
the polynomial example over `ℚ_p[T]` of [*uniform-completion-etale-comparison*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A4.4) prevents its
removal. Throughout, `p` is a prime (`[Fact p.Prime]`, or the field `p.Prime` of the presentation
record), the case `p = 2` included; the prime enters the arithmetic only through the exponent
bound `p^{n−1} > n` of [*pseudouniformizer-dividing-p*](#p1-32-split-tate-rings) (P1.32). In the Frobenius argument
the choice of exponent also makes `p/ϖ^p` topologically nilpotent: divisibility `ϖ^p | p` alone
does not make the root algebra étale, since at `ϖ = p^{1/p}` and `f = 1 − p` the polynomial
`X^p − pX + p − 1` has a double root at `1`.

**Roots of monic polynomials with invertible derivative.** (*root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring*)
Let `R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no nonsplit finite étale covers
(*finite-etale-split-ring*), `P ∈ R°[X]` monic of degree `d ≥ 1`, and `B := R[X]/(P)` with its
natural topology as a free `R`-module with basis `1, x, …, x^{d−1}`, `x` the class of `X`. Then
`x` is power-bounded in `B`. If moreover `P′(x) = u·(1 − τ)` in `B` with `u ∈ R^×` and `τ ∈ B`
topologically nilpotent, then `B` is complete and free, `1 − τ` is a unit (Tau Ceti
`IsTopologicallyNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub`), so `(P, 1)` is a standard étale pair (Mathlib
`StandardEtalePair`) and `B` is a faithfully flat finite étale `R`-algebra of rank `≥ 1`, which
has a section: `P` has a root in `R`, and every root of `P` in `R` lies in `R°` (a root is

### P1.33 compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F` and `A_inf`

**Compatibility with AdicSpaces' perfect field `F` and `A_inf = W(𝒪_F)`.**
(*adicspaces-layer-6-compatibility*) Let `F` be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of
characteristic `p` with a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ`, as in the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap
(AdicSpaces), layer 6.1 (no algebraic closedness). Tau Ceti's Fargues–Fontaine input is more
general than a field: a perfect ring `R` (`[CharP R p] [PerfectRing R p]`) with an element `ϖ`
and the `(p, [ϖ])`-adic topology on `W(R)` (`TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY`, `frobeniusHomeomorph`,
`windowU`, `windowV`, `spaX`); the statements below are for `R = 𝒪_F`. Then (a) `F` is a perfectoid
field of characteristic `p` (P1.2, P1.11), its tilt is `F` itself with `♯` the identity (P1.4), and
`(F, 𝒪_F)` is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` ([ECD] §3, Proposition 3.5, p. 15;
[Sch12] Lemma 3.4(iv), p. 16, and §3, p. 15); (b) AdicSpaces' `A_inf = W(𝒪_F)`, with pair of
definition `(A_inf, (p, [ϖ]))`, is the ring `W(F♭⁺) = W(𝒪_F)` of this layer, its `(p, [ϖ])`-adic
completeness, separatedness and Huber-ring structure being the library's
`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`, `isHausdorff_span_p_teichmuller` and
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller` (for the integers of a
normed field, `Complete.lean` has the instance directly), cited in
*witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring* ([Bhatt] Example 6.1.6, p. 43); (c) the untilts of `F` are the
pairs `(W(𝒪_F)[1/[ϖ]]/(ξ), W(𝒪_F)/(ξ))` for primitive `ξ ∈ A_inf` (P1.21). AdicSpaces' curve
`𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf)` and its Frobenius windows stay with AdicSpaces and the library; this layer
only identifies the input objects. For `F` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t))`, the untilts include
`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^` (`ξ = p − [t]`) and `ℚ_p^cycl` (`ξ = Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}`). *Needs:* P1.2; P1.11;
P1.4; *witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring*; P1.21; the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap
(AdicSpaces), layer 6.1; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY`,
`WittVector.isAdicComplete_span_p_teichmuller`,
`TauCeti.Huber.WittVector.isHuberRing_adicTopology_span_p_teichmuller`.

For a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field `F` with `CharP F p` and
`IsPerfectoidField p F`, `tilt.ainfEquiv` identifies
`WittVector p (Pair.tilt p (Pair.powerBounded F)).plus` with
`WittVector p (NormedField.valuation (K := F)).integer`. Here the latter integer
subring is `𝒪_F = {x : F | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}`. The perfect-field hypothesis above supplies
`IsPerfectoidField p F` by `IsPerfectoidField.iff_perfectRing`.
`tilt.ainfEquiv_coeff` specifies the map on every Witt coordinate as
`tilt.equivOfCharP`, so it is the Witt functor applied to the integral tilt
identification ([ECD] Lemmas 3.10–3.11, pp. 16–17).
For integral parameters `t ∈ F♭⁺` and `ϖ ∈ 𝒪_F` with
`tilt.equivOfCharP t = ϖ`, `tilt.ainfEquiv_map_ideal` identifies
`(p,[t])^n` with `(p,[ϖ])^n` for every `n : ℕ`, and
`tilt.ainfEquiv_continuous` states continuity in both directions for these
adic topologies. These are consequences of Witt functoriality and the
power-ideal neighbourhood bases; for a pseudouniformizer `ϖ` they identify
precisely the inputs to `TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY` and `windowU`.
The two statements also apply to zero and unit parameters; they do not
assert that those parameters are pseudouniformizers.

## Layer P2: rational localisation, the sheaf theorem and perfectoid spaces

The layer passes from perfectoid Tate pairs to perfectoid spaces. It constructs the tilting map
`x ↦ x♭` on adic spectra and proves that it is a homeomorphism `Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`
identifying rational subsets; shows that rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are
perfectoid with tilt the rational localisation of the tilt, that completed residue fields are
perfectoid, and that perfectoid Tate pairs are stably uniform and sheafy, with `O_X` acyclic and
`O_X⁺` almost acyclic on rational subsets (the sheaf theorem); defines affinoid perfectoid spaces
and the full subcategory `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces inside the adic spaces of AdicSpaces, with
`Perf` in characteristic `p`; glues the tilt `X ↦ X♭` and proves the tilting equivalence
`Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭`; and builds completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs, fibre products of
perfectoid spaces (over perfectoid and over analytic bases), absolute products in `Perf`, and the
comparison with Scholze's perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field. Throughout, `(R, R⁺)` is a
perfectoid Tate pair in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, of characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, with no
perfectoid base field; `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` is a pseudouniformiser with `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and compatible
`p`-power roots, as in the standing conventions of this roadmap; "almost zero" refers to the
ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of `R⁺` (layer P1); and `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` abbreviates
the completed perfection `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` of `𝔽_p((t))` (the tilt of `ℚ_p^cycl` and of
`ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`, layer P1), the uncompleted union `⋃_n 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^n}))` not being complete.

Global objects are Tau Ceti's pre-adic spaces (`TauCeti.PreAdicSpace`): the perfectoid
subcategory `Perfd` (P2.10) is cut out by sheafiness together with open covers by affinoid
perfectoid opens, the adic spectra `presentationLimitPreAdicSpace` of perfectoid Tate pairs (the
spectra of `Perfectoid.PairCat p` objects). Its charts are sheafy, so this is the usual category of
perfectoid adic spaces. AdicEtaleGeometry's analytic Yoneda carrier `YonedaAdicSpace` (rational
sheaves locally represented by complete Huber pairs, with its supplied underlying valuation-space
functor) receives perfectoid spaces, as adic spaces, through its fully faithful
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`; the statements below that are phrased on that carrier, notably the
comparisons with AdicEtaleGeometry's predicates and sites, apply to a perfectoid space through this
embedding, and the comparison of the two presentations belongs to AdicEtaleGeometry. Rings and pairs
remain the pinned Tau Ceti rings and pairs. Characteristic `p` means `p = 0` on every affinoid
chart, including the zero chart; in Lean, `InCharP` asks for `p = 0` in every ring of sections. The bundled global category here uses small affinoid rings
and spaces covered by a set of such charts.

### P2.1 the tilting map on adic spectra

**The tilting map `x ↦ x♭` from `Spa(R, R⁺)` to `Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`.** (*tilting-map-of-spectra*) Let
`(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and sharp map `♯ : R♭ → R` (continuous
and multiplicative, not additive), `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`; no base field. For
`x ∈ X` with valuation `v_x : R → Γ_x ∪ {0}`, the composite `v_x ∘ ♯ : R♭ → Γ_x ∪ {0}` is a
continuous valuation of `R♭` with `v_x(f♯) ≤ 1` for all `f ∈ R♭⁺`; its class is a point `x♭ ∈ X♭`,
characterised by `|f(x♭)| ≤ |g(x♭)| ⟺ |f♯(x)| ≤ |g♯(x)|` for all `f, g ∈ R♭` (written
`|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|`). The tilting map `τ_R : X → X♭`, `x ↦ x♭`, satisfies: (a)
`supp(x♭) = {f ∈ R♭ : f♯ ∈ supp(x)}`; (b) `τ_R` is continuous: if `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭` and some
`f_i` is a unit of `R♭` (for instance `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`; the unit makes `f_i♯` a unit of `R` because
`♯` is multiplicative with `1♯ = 1`, and without such a normalisation the unit-ideal condition on
the `f♯` is not automatic before the homeomorphism is known), then `f₁♯, …, f_n♯` generate the unit
ideal of `R` and `τ_R⁻¹(U(f₁, …, f_n / g)) = U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)`; every rational subset of `X♭`
has a presentation with `f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺` and `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N` for some `N`; (c) naturality: for a
morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs `φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` (continuous, `φ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺`) with tilt
`φ♭` (layer P1, P1.6), so that `φ ∘ ♯_R = ♯_S ∘ φ♭`, one has `τ_R ∘ Spa(φ) = Spa(φ♭) ∘ τ_S`; (d)
if `pR = 0` then `(R♭, R♭⁺) = (R, R⁺)` with `♯ = id` and `τ_R = id`. That `τ_R` is a homeomorphism
identifying rational subsets is P2.2; here only the map and its first properties are built

### P2.2 the tilting homeomorphism

The tilting map of P2.1 is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets; its two inputs are the
characteristic-`p` rational localisations and the approximation lemma, proved here.

**The tilting homeomorphism `Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` identifies rational subsets.**
(*tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1; characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, as in ECD Example 3.4(iv); no perfectoid base
field) with tilt `(R♭, R♭⁺)`. Then the tilting map `τ_R : X = Spa(R, R⁺) → X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`,
`|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|` (see *tilting-map-of-spectra*), is a homeomorphism, natural in morphisms of
perfectoid Tate pairs. A subset `U ⊆ X` is rational if and only if `τ_R(U) ⊆ X♭` is rational;
explicitly, for `f₁, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭⁺` with `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`,
`τ_R(U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)) = U(f₁, …, f_n / g)`, and every rational subset of `X` can be written
as `U(f₁♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯)` for such `f_i, g`. Consequently `τ_R` preserves the specialisation
order (Mathlib `Topology.IsInducing.specializes_iff` applied to the homeomorphism),
quasi-compact opens and rank-one (maximal) points, and restricts, for every rational
`U ⊆ X`, to the homeomorphism `Homeomorph.image τ_R U`, identifying rational subsets of `U` and of `τ_R(U)`
([ECD] §3, Thm 3.12, p. 17, and proof of Thms 3.12–3.13, p. 17, the route followed; [Sch12] §6,
Cor. 6.7(ii)–(iii) with proof, p. 35, injectivity from the approximation lemma and surjectivity by
untilting the residue field over `R`; [KL15] Thm 3.6.14(b) and [KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.16, p. 63, the
explicit form of the rational subsets and an independent proof for Fontaine perfectoid Tate rings,
including those in which `p` is neither `0` nor invertible; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.5, Thm 2.5.1,
pp. 59–60, the analytic-ring generalisation). Sch12 Theorem 6.3(i) (perfectoid affinoid
`K`-algebras over a perfectoid field) is a special case. For `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`τ({|T| ≤ |ϖ|}) = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}`, the Gauss point goes to the Gauss point and the classical point
`T ↦ ϖ` to `T ↦ ϖ♭`. The theorem applies to ECD Example 3.4(iv),
`R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]` with `ϖ = T^{1/p}`, which lives over no field: its
spectrum has points with `|p(x)| = 0` and points with `|p(x)| ≠ 0`, both matched with points of the

### P2.3 rational localisation of perfectoid affinoids

Rational localisation: the rational localisations of a perfectoid Tate pair are perfectoid, their
tilts are the rational localisations of the tilt, they form a functor on rational subsets with
tilting as a natural isomorphism, completed residue fields are perfectoid, and the structure
presheaf is a sheaf with `O⁺` almost Čech-acyclic.

### P2.5 completed residue fields

**Completed residue fields of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid and tilt to those of the tilt.**
(*completed-residue-fields*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (no base field),
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)`, `x ∈ X`, and `(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)` the completed residue affinoid field of `x` (the
completion of the residue field of the stalk `O_{X,x}` for the topology of `v_x`, with the
completion of the valuation ring of `v_x`; the uncompleted residue field with its valuation and
`Valued` structure and the stalk material are library, Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.residueFieldValuation`, `valued_algebraMap_residueFieldValuation`,
`continuous_algebraMap_residueFieldValuation`,
`isLocalRing_stalk_presentationLimitPresheafInCommRingCat`, `supp_presentationLimitStalkValuation`,
`presentationLimitStalkResidueValuation`, and AdicSpaces layer 3.3 supplies the completed residue
affinoid field; the completion and the perfectoidness are what this target adds; `k(x)^` is a complete nonarchimedean field whose
topology is that of the rank-one generisation of `x`, `x` being analytic because `R` is Tate), with
its canonical morphism `(R, R⁺) → (k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)`. Then `k(x)^` is a perfectoid field and
`(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate pair. Its tilt is canonically `(k(x♭)^, k(x♭)^⁺)`,
compatibly with the canonical morphisms from `(R, R⁺)` and `(R♭, R♭⁺)` and with `♯`; in particular
the value groups `Γ_x` and `Γ_{x♭}` coincide and `x` has rank one iff `x♭` has. Explicitly,

rational neighbourhoods of `x` (an element `h` of the stalk with `|h(x)| ≤ 1` lies in `O_X⁺` of the

### P2.7 almost acyclicity of `O⁺` on rational coverings

**Almost exactness of the integral Čech complex of `O⁺` on rational coverings of a perfectoid
affinoid.** (*integral-almost-acyclicity*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1; no base field), `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`. For every rational `U ⊆ X` and every finite
covering `𝔘 = (U₁, …, U_m)` of `U` by rational subsets (all finite intersections are then rational),
the augmented alternating Čech complex, with `(d⁰s)_{ij} = s_j|_{U_i∩U_j} − s_i|_{U_i∩U_j}` for `i < j`,
`C⁺(𝔘): 0 → O_X⁺(U) → ∏_i O_X⁺(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} O_X⁺(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯` is almost exact: each of its
cohomology modules is killed by every topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺` (equivalently by
`ϖ^{1/p^n}` for all `n`; the ideal is idempotent, layer P1). It is exact at its first two terms. The
same holds for the complex of the `O_X(V)°`, which is almost equal to `C⁺(𝔘)` termwise; in the
almost category `C⁺(𝔘)ᵃ` is exact. Consequently `H^i(U, O_X⁺)ᵃ = 0`, i.e. `H^i(U, O_X⁺)` is almost
zero, for every rational `U ⊆ X` and every `i > 0` (see *cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis*)
([Berkeley] Lecture 7, proof of Thm 7.4.4, p. 53, bounded torsion plus the Frobenius step in
characteristic `p`; [Sch12] §6, proof of Prop. 6.14, p. 38, the tilting reduction of the general

perfectoid rings through almost optimal exactness). Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12
Proposition 6.14, proved there through `p`-finite algebras and Tate's acyclicity theorem
(see *p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate*), a route this layer keeps. For `R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and the
Laurent covering `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}`, `C⁺` is exact: the Laurent decomposition of
`Σ_{k ∈ ℤ[1/p]} d_k (T/ϖ)^k` splits exactly. The conclusion is about `O⁺` up to almost zero
modules: after inverting `ϖ` it recovers the exactness of the `O`-Čech complex, but `C⁺` itself need
not be exact when `R⁺ ≠ R°`. *Needs:* *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*;

### P2.8 the sheaf theorem

The sheaf theorem collects the sheaf property, the perfectoidness of the rational localisations
and the (almost) vanishing of cohomology; the `p`-finite route of Scholze is kept alongside it.

**The sheaf theorem: `O_X` is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology and `H^i(X, O_X⁺)` is almost
zero.** (*sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a perfectoid Tate pair (ECD
Definition 3.1: any perfectoid Tate ring, of characteristic `0`, `p` or mixed, with no perfectoid
base field) and `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`. Then: (i) `O_X` and `O_X⁺` are sheaves on `X`; (ii) for every
rational `U ⊆ X`, `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt
`(O_{X♭}(U♭), O_{X♭}⁺(U♭))`, `U♭` the image of `U` in `X♭`; (iii) `H⁰(X, O_X) = R` and
`H^i(X, O_X) = 0` for `i > 0` (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.1 (*sheafy-cech-acyclicity*), for the pair
made
sheafy by *perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy*); (iv) `H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺` and, for `i > 0`, the `R⁺`-module
`H^i(X, O_X⁺)` is almost zero, i.e. killed by every topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺`
(equivalently `H^i(X, O_X⁺ᵃ) = H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0` in the almost category, [Sch12] §6, Rem. 6.12,
p. 36); (v) (i)–(iv) hold for every rational `U` in place of `X`. Sheaf cohomology is that of
sheaves of abelian groups on the topological space `X`. This is ECD Theorems 3.18 and 3.24 in their
stated generality; ECD's citations [Sch12], [KL15] cover perfectoid algebras over a perfectoid field
and over `ℚ_p` (with characteristic `p`), and the case where `p` is neither zero nor invertible is
Kedlaya–Liu II §3.3 ([ECD] §3, Thm 3.18, p. 18, for (i)–(ii), and Thm 3.24, p. 19, for (iv);
[Sch12] §6, Thm 6.3(iii)–(iv), p. 30, and Prop. 6.14, p. 37, over a perfectoid field; [KL15] §3.6,
Thm 3.6.15, p. 94, for the vanishing of `H^i(X, O)` and the almost vanishing of `H^i(X, O⁺)`;

p. 19, (iv) without a base field; [AWS] Lecture 2, §2.9, Thm 2.9.5, p. 73, (iv) for analytic
perfectoid pairs). Sch12 Theorem 6.3(iii)–(iv) and Proposition 6.14, Kedlaya–Liu II
Corollary 3.3.20, Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4, Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 6.14 and Kedlaya AWS

**Affinoid perfectoid spaces: adic spectra of perfectoid Huber pairs.** (*affinoid-perfectoid-space*)
A space `X` here is an object of Tau Ceti's `PreAdicSpace`; the adic spaces among them are the
sheafy ones (`PreAdicSpace.isAdic`). AdicEtaleGeometry's analytic carrier `YonedaAdicSpace`, the full
subcategory of `J_rat`-sheaves on `CAffᵒᵖ` covered by open affinoid Yoneda spectra
([Berkeley] §3.4, Def. 3.4.1, printed p. 22), receives adic spaces through

embedding. `X` is
*affinoid perfectoid* if there are a complete Hausdorff Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`:
`R⁺ ⊆ R°` open and integrally closed) with `R` a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD
Definition 3.1 (layer P1, P1.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ` such that `ϖ^p | p`
in `R°` and Frobenius `R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` bijective) and an isomorphism of adic spaces

(for a pair of definition contained in `R⁺`), for `R : Perfectoid.PairCat p`; it is an adic space,
and its image under `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` is the Yoneda spectrum

### P2.10 perfectoid spaces

Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory `Perfd` of adic spaces, its characteristic-`p` part
`Perf`, and the glued tilt.

**Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory Perfd of adic spaces, and Perf in characteristic p.**
(*perfectoid-space*) Fix a prime `p`. A *perfectoid space* is an adic space, that is, a sheafy
object `X` of Tau Ceti's `PreAdicSpace`, covered by open subspaces that are affinoid perfectoid
(see *affinoid-perfectoid-space*): every `x ∈ X` has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the open
subspace `X|_U` (`PreAdicSpace.restrict`) is isomorphic to `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfectoid Tate
ring and `R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring of integral elements ([ECD] §3, Def. 3.19, p. 18; [Berkeley] Lecture 7,
§7.1, Def. 7.1.2, printed p. 49). Sheafiness is part of the definition: without it the empty
pre-adic space with nonzero sections over `∅` would qualify, the chart condition being vacuous for
it. The category `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces is the full subcategory
of `PreAdicSpace` on these objects (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`):
morphisms are those of pre-adic spaces. Open immersions are `PreAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion`; the
point carrier is the underlying space. Through AdicEtaleGeometry's `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`
these agree with the analytic carrier's open immersions `YonedaAdicSpace.IsOpenImmersion` and
points `YonedaAdicSpace.space` (`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace_space`, and
*adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces* for open immersions). `Perf ⊆ Perfd` is the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces of characteristic
`p`, those with `p = 0` in `O_X(X)` (in Lean, `InCharP` asks for `p = 0` in `O_X(U)` for every open
`U`, equivalent by `mem_perf_iff` below); equivalently, `X` admits a (necessarily unique) morphism to the
discrete adic space `Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)`, which is an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII R0.2
(*discrete-huber-pair-sheafy*)) but
not a perfectoid space, and which `Perf` does not contain ([ECD] §1, p. 3). With the
definition: every point of a perfectoid space is analytic, so every morphism of adic spaces into a
perfectoid space is adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6 (*adic-morphism*)); an adic space with `p = 0`
in its structure sheaf
is perfectoid iff it is covered by open subspaces `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfect complete Tate
ring ([ECD] §3, Prop. 3.5, p. 15). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `isPerfectoidSpace` (the object
property of `PreAdicSpace`: sheafy, and every point has an open neighbourhood `U` with `X|_U` affinoid

**The glued tilt `X ↦ X♭` of a perfectoid space.** (*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*) For every
perfectoid space `X` (*perfectoid-space*; any characteristic, no base field) there is a perfectoid
space `X♭` of characteristic `p`, the *tilt* of `X`, with a homeomorphism `|X| ≅ |X♭|`, `x ↦ x♭`,
constructed by gluing ([ECD] §3, the sentence after Def. 3.19, p. 18; [Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.1,
after Rem. 7.1.3, printed p. 49, the target `Perf`; [Sch12] §6, Def. 6.16 and Prop. 6.17 with
proof, p. 38, over a perfectoid field, where property (a) is "a formal consequence" of tilting of
algebras, of rational localisations and of maps into affinoid adic spaces; [Bhatt] §9.3,
Thm 9.3.10(1), printed p. 111). Affinoid case: for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` perfectoid,
`X♭ := Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`, where `(R♭, R♭⁺)` is the tilt of the pair (layer P1: `R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R`,
`R♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R⁺`), and `x ↦ x♭` is the tilting homeomorphism `|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|`
(*tilting-map-of-spectra*, *tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets*), which matches rational
subsets `U ↔ U♭` and satisfies `(O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭` compatibly with
restrictions (see *rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids*). General case: `X♭` is glued
(AdicSpaces layer 5.3) from the tilts `V♭` of all affinoid perfectoid open subspaces `V ⊆ X`, along
the tilts of their common rational refinements (*affinoid-perfectoid-basis* (iii)); the family being
canonical, `X♭` is defined up to unique isomorphism, and `|X♭| = |X|` as sets with the same open
subsets. A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces gives `f♭ : Y♭ → X♭`, affinoid-locally `Spa` of
the tilt of the corresponding morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (layer P1, P1.6), glued because
morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf; so `X ↦ X♭` is a functor `Perfd ⥤ Perf` with `|f♭| = |f|`
under the homeomorphisms. Properties: (a) for `U ⊆ X` open, `(X|_U)♭ = X♭|_{U♭}`, `U♭` being `U`
viewed in `|X♭|`; `U` is affinoid perfectoid iff `U♭` is, and then

### P2.12 the tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces

The tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: the slice equivalence over a perfectoid base, its
affinoid form, and the completed tensor products and affinoid fibre products that it is compatible
with.

**Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: `Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭`.** (*tilting-slice-equivalence*) Let
`X` be a perfectoid space with tilt `X♭` (*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*; any characteristic,
no perfectoid base field). (a) The functor `Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ = Perfd/X♭` on slice categories
(Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over`), `(f : Y → X) ↦ (f♭ : Y♭ → X♭)`, is an equivalence of categories (a
Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`). (b) It commutes with restriction to open subspaces of `X`, and
a perfectoid space `Y` over `X` is affinoid perfectoid iff `Y♭` is; for `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` it restricts
on affinoid perfectoid spaces to the equivalence of
*affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*. (c) Untilts over `X`: for every perfectoid space
`T` of characteristic `p` and every morphism `g : T → X♭` there are a perfectoid space `T♯` with a
morphism `T♯ → X` and an isomorphism `ι : (T♯)♭ ≅ T` over `X♭`, and the pair `(T♯ → X, ι)` is unique
up to unique isomorphism; so `Hom_Perf(T, X♭)` is in natural bijection with isomorphism classes of
such pairs, functorially in `T`. (d) Under the homeomorphisms `|Y| ≅ |Y♭|` the structure maps
correspond. Unit and counit are isomorphisms compatible with restriction to open subspaces of `X`.
The quasi-inverse depends on `X`: there is no quasi-inverse to tilting that recovers every untilt without a chosen
base (`tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes`) ([ECD] §3, Cor. 3.20, p. 19, statement (a) over an
arbitrary perfectoid base; [Berkeley] Lecture 7, §7.1, Thm 7.1.4, printed pp. 49–50; [Sch12] §6,
Prop. 6.17, p. 38, the field case; [Bhatt] §9.3, Thm 9.3.10(2), printed p. 111). Sch12
Proposition 6.17 is the case `X = Spa(K, K⁺₀)` for a perfectoid field `K`,
where `K⁺₀` is the smallest ring of integral elements (P2.19)
(see *perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison*). For `X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)`, the
perfectoid disc over `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))` untilts to `Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`,
and `Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})))` itself (with the identity to `X♭`) untilts to `X`. *Needs:*
*perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting*; *affinoid-perfectoid-basis*;
*open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Over`, `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

**Tilting is an equivalence between perfectoid Tate pairs over `(A, A⁺)` and over `(A♭, A♭⁺)`,
compatible with rational localisation.** (*affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence*) Let
`(A, A⁺)` be a complete perfectoid Tate pair (`A` perfectoid Tate ring, `A⁺ ⊆ A°` a ring of integral
elements; no perfectoid base field) with tilt `(A♭, A♭⁺)`. Let `Perfd_{(A,A⁺)}` be the category of
complete perfectoid Tate pairs `(B, B⁺)` with a morphism of Huber pairs `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)`,
morphisms being morphisms of Huber pairs under `(A, A⁺)`, and define `Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)}` likewise.
The tilting equivalence of perfectoid `A`-algebras, with quasi-inverse the untilt along a
generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(A♭°) → A°)`, is P1.27 (*tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt*); what

generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺)`, `ϖ♭ ∈ A♭` a pseudouniformiser (ECD Lemma 3.14 and Theorem

### P2.13 completed tensor products of perfectoid pairs

**Completed tensor products of perfectoid Tate pairs are perfectoid, uniform, and commute with
tilting.** (*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*) Let `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)` and

`A, B, C` perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1; any characteristic; no perfectoid base field).
Both maps are adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1 (*adic-ring-homomorphism*)), so the completed tensor
product

### P2.14 the uniform completed tensor product over an arbitrary Tate ring

**The uniform completed tensor product of perfectoid rings over an arbitrary Tate ring is
perfectoid.** (*uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete
Hausdorff Huber pair with `A` a Tate ring (not necessarily perfectoid, uniform or of characteristic
`p`), and let `(A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺)`, `(A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺)` be morphisms of Huber pairs with `B, C`
perfectoid Tate rings. Then the uniform completed tensor product `B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C` (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0 (*uniform-completed-tensor-product*)) is a perfectoid Tate ring ([KL16] §3.3, Cor. 3.3.21, p. 66;
[KL15] §3.6, Cor. 3.6.18,
p. 96, over `ℚ_p`, where Kedlaya–Liu's `D` is the uniform completion of `B ⊗_A C` in the present notation). If `A` is perfectoid it equals
`B ⊗̂_A C` (*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid* (i)); otherwise `B ⊗̂_A C` need not be
uniform (`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not), and the uniformisation cannot be omitted ([KL15] §3.1,
Rem. 3.1.6(c), p. 67). For `B = C = ℚ_p^cycl` over `ℚ_p`, `ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl` is a
perfectoid Tate ring over the non-perfectoid base `ℚ_p`; `ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is perfectoid although
`ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p` is not uniform. *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII R0.4 (*uniformization*,
*uniform-completed-tensor-product*: the spectral
seminorm, uniformisation and the uniform completed tensor product);
*completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid*; *perfectoid-dense-image-criterion*; layer P1 (P1.5,
P1.30); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**A uniform Tate ring receiving a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid.**
(*perfectoid-dense-image-criterion*) Let `f : A → B` be a continuous ring homomorphism with dense
image from a perfectoid Tate ring `A` to a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring `B` (`B°` bounded).
Prove that `B` is a perfectoid Tate ring and that `f♭ : A♭ → B♭` has dense image ([AWS] §2.8,
Lem. 2.8.4, p. 70, and §2.4, Thm 2.4.3(a), p. 58; [KL16] §3.3, Thm 3.3.18(ii), p. 64, the class of
morphisms along which the perfectoid property transfers; [KL15] §3.6, Thm 3.6.17(b), p. 95, over

## Layer P3: almost purity and the étale site

Layer P3 proves the almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings and builds the étale site of a
perfectoid space. It opens with the algebraic prefix — henselian pairs, Elkik's approximation theorem
and its non-noetherian form, and the invariance of finite étale algebras under henselian completion
and under completed colimits — then proves almost purity in characteristic `p`, constructs the
untilting functor on finite étale algebras, treats finite extensions of perfectoid fields and the
Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem, and assembles the almost purity theorem with its three conclusions:
finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid, tilting is an equivalence of finite
étale algebras, and the integral closure is almost finite étale. On the geometric side it defines
finite étale and étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces, compares them with the adic notions of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2–A1.3 (finite étale Huber pairs, finite étale and étale morphisms) and A1.6
(the sites), and builds the étale site with its tilting equivalence and the almost
acyclicity of `O⁺`. AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.4–A1.0.5 supplies classical henselian approximation
and finite étale completion. The perfectoid-ring results require no perfectoid base field;
the field results explicitly assume a perfectoid field.

### P3.2 perfectoid-field specialization of henselian completion

The perfectoid-field application of henselian completion is supplied by
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (*henselian-finite-etale-approximation*): for a perfectoid
field `K`, a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ K°` and a flat `K°`-algebra `A` henselian
along `(ϖ)`, apply its part (a) with `R = A`, `t = ϖ` and `I = A` to obtain
`FÉt(A[ϖ⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(Â[ϖ⁻¹])`, where `Â` is the `ϖ`-adic completion
([Sch12] §7, Proposition 7.4). *Needs:* P1.10; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5.

### P3.3 almost purity in characteristic p

Almost purity in characteristic `p` is the case in which perfectness does the work: a finite étale
algebra over a perfect complete Tate ring is again perfectoid, and its integral closure is almost
finite étale.

**Almost purity in characteristic `p`: finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p`.** (*finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p` (equivalently a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic `p`, layer P1; no base
field), `ϖ ∈ R` a pseudouniformiser (it has all `p`-power roots `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}` in `R°`), `R⁺ ⊆ R°` a ring
of integral elements, and `S ∈ FÉt(R)` with its natural topology and plus ring `S⁺` = the integral
closure of `R⁺` in `S`. Then: (i) `S` is perfect, complete and uniform, hence a perfectoid Tate ring of
characteristic `p`, and `(S, S⁺)` is a perfectoid Huber pair; (ii) `S°` is the integral closure of `R°`
in `S` and `S°/S⁺`, viewed as an `R⁺`-module, is killed by `R°°`;
thus `S°a` and `S⁺a` agree after transport between the basic setups
`(R⁺, R°°)` and `(R°, R°°)`; (iii) `S°a` is an almost finite étale `R°a`-algebra
(almost finitely presented projective and unramified: the diagonal idempotent `e ∈ S ⊗_R S` lies in
`(S°a ⊗_{R°a} S°a)_*`); (iv) `S°a` is uniformly almost finite projective: there is `n ≥ 0` such that
for every `ε ∈ R°°` there are `R°`-linear maps `S° → (R°)ⁿ → S°` whose composite is multiplication by
`ε`; (v) if `S` is faithfully flat over `R`, then `Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°°` and `R°a → S°a` is almost
faithfully flat and almost split. Almost mathematics is that of the basic setup `(R°, R°°)`
(layer P1), equivalently of the ideal `(ϖ^{1/p^∞})`, and almost finite étale is the notion of
layer P0. Not claimed: `S°` finite, flat or étale over `R°`, or `S` free over `R`. The statement
specialises to the case of a perfectoid `K`-algebra over a perfectoid field `K` of characteristic `p`,
and to the finite separable extensions of such a field ([Sch12] §5, Prop. 5.23, pp. 28–29, over a field; [GR] §3.5,
Thm 3.5.28, pp. 69–71, applied to `R°`, gives the base-field-free argument). *Needs:*
layer P1 (perfectoid Tate rings, the characteristic-`p` criterion, the basic setup `(R°, R°°)`).

`finiteEtale_charP_perfectoid` proves perfectness and supplies the Tate structure,
completeness and Hausdorffness for the finite-module topology in (i).
Its characteristic hypothesis is `pR = 0`, allowing the zero base and zero algebra;
it requires no `CharP S p` instance for the zero algebra.
For the resulting finite étale pair, `Pair.integralClosure_powerBounded`
states (ii), including the annihilation formula `εs ∈ S⁺` for every
`ε ∈ R°°` and `s ∈ S°`. `Pair.integralClosure_almostFiniteEtale` states (iii),
`Pair.integralClosure_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective` states the fixed-rank
factorizations in (iv), and `Pair.integralClosure_faithfullyFlat` states (v),
including exact trace lifts of topologically nilpotent elements and linear
splittings after multiplication by each almost scalar. These pair theorems
also give the characteristic-independent conclusions of P3.12. The trace
and splitting clauses follow from the almost purity assertion and
[GR] Cor. 4.1.11 and Thm 4.1.14, pp. 74–75.

Two lemmas feed the proof. Relative Frobenius of a weakly étale map is an isomorphism, and étale
algebras over perfect rings are perfect (*etale-over-perfect-is-perfect*): for a weakly étale map
`A → B` of `𝔽_p`-algebras (flat with flat multiplication `B ⊗_A B → B`) the square of `A → B` with the
absolute Frobenii (Mathlib `frobenius`) is a pushout, so `B ⊗_{A, Frob} A → B` is an isomorphism and `B`
is perfect (Mathlib `PerfectRing`) when `A` is; the same holds for weakly étale morphisms of almost
algebras over a basic setup of characteristic `p`, so for a finite étale `(R°a/ϖ)`-algebra `B`, relative Frobenius identifies
`B/ϖ^{1/p}` with `B`, with the base rings identified by `x ↦ x^p` ([Bhatt] Ch. 4, §4.3, Lem. 4.3.8).
Uniformity and the power-bounded integral-closure comparison for finite étale algebras
are supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2a (*finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform*).

### P3.4 characteristic p: inverting `ϖ` is an equivalence

**Characteristic `p`: inverting `ϖ` is an equivalence between almost finite étale `R°a`-algebras and
finite étale `R`-algebras.** (*characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence*) Let `R` be a perfectoid
Tate ring of characteristic `p` with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, and `(R°a)_afet` the category of almost
finite étale `R°a`-algebras (layer P0). Then the functor `(R°a)_afet → FÉt(R)`, `A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹]`
(`A_*` the ring of almost elements, layer P0), with its natural topology, is an equivalence of
categories, compatible with tensor products; a quasi-inverse is `S ↦ S°a`. Moreover every
`A ∈ (R°a)_afet` is uniformly almost finite projective, `A_*` is perfect, `ϖ`-torsion free and
`ϖ`-adically complete, and `A_*` is the integral closure of `R°` in `A_*[ϖ⁻¹]`; almost faithful
flatness of `A` corresponds to faithful flatness of `A_*[ϖ⁻¹]` ([GR] §3.5, 3.5.26 and Thm 3.5.28,
p. 69). *Needs:* P3.3.

The construction `AlmostFiniteEtale p R` uses P0's category under the almost
base algebra. `almostInversion p R ϖ` sends `A` to the localization of its
actual algebra of almost elements. `almostInversionMap_scalars` identifies
`R° → A_* → A_*[1/ϖ]` with the structural map through `R`;
`almostInversion_isLocalization` specifies its universal property and
`almostInversionMap_natural` its action on arrows. The equivalence instance is
`almostInversion_isEquivalence`; the same construction applies in all
characteristics by P3.11. Parameter comparison `almostInversionParameterIso`
fixes every almost element and satisfies the cocycle equation.

`almostInversion_charP_perfect` states bijectivity of Frobenius on the ring
of almost elements when `pR = 0`, including the zero ring ([GR] proof of Thm 3.5.28,
Claim 3.5.35, pp. 70–71). For every almost finite étale algebra,
`almostInversion_elements_complete` states injectivity of multiplication
by `ϖ` and `ϖ`-adic completeness of its almost elements;
`almostInversion_elements_integralClosure` states that the localization map
is injective and its image consists exactly of elements integral over `R°`.
`almostInversion_uniformlyAlmostFiniteProjective` gives a single finite bound,
and `almostInversion_faithfullyFlat_iff` identifies almost faithful flatness
with faithful flatness after inversion. These four assertions hold in all
characteristics by P3.11 ([Sch12] Lem. 5.3(iv), p. 22, Prop. 5.23 and
Thm 5.25, pp. 28–29, Thm 7.9, p. 42; [GR] Claims 3.5.31–35, pp. 70–71).

**Checks.** `inversion_rank_zero`, `inversion_rank_one`, `inversion_rank_two`
apply this actual functor to the almostifications of `(R°)⁰`, `R°`, `(R°)²`,
with outputs `0`, `R`, `R²`. `inversion_characteristic_p_wrong_parameter`
asserts that the image of `almostSplit p R 1` under `almostInversion p R ϖ`
is nontrivial for a nonzero characteristic-`p` perfectoid pair and admits no
ring equivalence to `Localization.Away (p : R)`. Thus replacing `ϖ` by `p=0`
changes the functor's actual output.

### P3.5 the untilting functor on finite étale algebras

**The untilting functor on finite étale algebras, `T ↦ T♯`, via almost finite étale integral
structures.** (*finite-etale-untilting-functor*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
(layer P1) and choose a pseudouniformiser `ϖ♭ ∈ R♭` with `ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯` satisfying `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`
(layer P1), so that `R♭°/ϖ♭ = R°/ϖ` (layer P1). In `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale`, define `untilt` as the
untilting functor `(−)♯ : FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` (`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R♭ ⥤ CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R`),
the composite

`FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), T ↦ T°a ↦ T°a/ϖ♭ ↦ A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] =: T♯,`

where the first equivalence is *characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence*, the middle equivalence
is the unique flat deformation of almost finite étale algebras along the `ϖ`-adically complete flat
`R°a` (layer P0), and the last functor inverts `ϖ` (natural module topology on `T♯`).
Prove `untilt_isPerfectoid` directly for the constructed `T♯`, from layer P1's primitive-ideal
untilting: `T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ` is the untilt of the perfectoid ring `T` (of characteristic
`p`, `T` being finite étale over the perfectoid `R♭`, hence perfectoid as a uniform complete Tate
ring that is perfect) along the primitive element `ξ`, and untilts of perfectoid rings are
perfectoid (layer P1); no statement about arbitrary finite étale `R`-algebras is used. The
general theorem `FiniteEtale.naturalPerfectoid` — for every finite étale algebra `S` over a
complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring `R`, the supplied `Huber.FiniteEtale R S` with its natural
module topology is perfectoid ([ECD] Theorem 6.1(i), p. 26) — is NOT a target of this subsection:
it is the essential-surjectivity milestone of *finite-etale-tilting-equivalence* (P3.9) and is
exposed, and registered as an instance, only there and in P3.10, after that milestone; nothing in
P3.5–P3.8 depends on it. Prove `tiltUntiltIso`
(a canonical isomorphism `(T♯)♭ ≅ T` of `R♭`-algebras, natural in `T`, so that `(−)♯` is inverse to
tilting on its image and compatible with the untilting of perfectoid algebras of layer P1). Further,
`T♯` is finite étale over `R`; `(T♯)°a = A` is almost finite étale over `R°a`; the functor is
independent of `ϖ♭` up to canonical isomorphism, preserves tensor products, finite products, ranks
(the rank of `T♯` at `x ∈ Spa R` equals the rank of `T` at `x♭`) and faithful flatness; and it
commutes with base change along every map of perfectoid Tate rings `R → R'` (for example a rational
localisation or the completed residue field at a point): `(T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'`. Equivalently
`T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ`, with `T⁺` the integral closure of `R♭⁺` in `T`, for a generator `ξ` of `ker(θ : W(R♭⁺) → R⁺)` (layer P1), which shows finite
étaleness without almost mathematics ([KL15] Lem. 3.6.20; [AWS] Lem. 2.8.10) ([Sch12] §5, Prop. 5.22
and the diagram following it, p. 28). *Needs:* P3.4; layer P0 (flat deformation of almost finite
étale algebras along a complete flat almost algebra); layer P1 (tilts, untilts, `θ`).

### P3.6 untilting is fully faithful and inverse to tilting on its image

**The untilting functor `FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` is fully faithful, inverse to tilting on its image, with
image the `S` having almost finite étale integral structure.**
(*tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful*) Let `R` be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt `R♭`
(any characteristic, no perfectoid base field). The untilting functor `(−)♯ : FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R)` of
*finite-etale-untilting-functor* is fully faithful and, on its essential image, inverse to tilting:
for `S = T♯`, `S` is perfectoid and `S♭ ≅ T`. Its essential image consists exactly of the finite
étale `R`-algebras `S` such that `S` (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and `S°a` is almost
finite étale over `R°a`; for such `S`, `S°a` is uniformly almost finite projective over `R°a`. The
functor preserves degrees (rank functions), tensor products and faithful flatness. For `R = K` a
perfectoid field this is the input of [Sch12] Thm 3.7; for `R` of characteristic `p` (`R♭ = R`) it is
the identity ([Sch12] §5, Thm 5.25, p. 29). *Needs:* P3.5.

### P3.7 finite extensions of perfectoid fields

**Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid, and tilting is a degree-preserving
equivalence of finite extensions.** (*finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields*) Let `K` be a perfectoid
field (characteristic `0` or `p`) with tilt `K♭`. (i) Every finite extension `L/K`, with its natural
topology (the unique extension of the absolute value, Mathlib `spectralNorm`), is a perfectoid field.
(ii) The untilting functor `(−)♯` of P3.5 is an equivalence `FÉt(K♭) ≃ FÉt(K)` with quasi-inverse
`L ↦ L♭`; it restricts to an equivalence between finite field extensions of `K♭` and of `K`,
preserving degrees, automorphism groups and Galois extensions. (iii) `K` is algebraically closed if
and only if `K♭` is: `isAlgClosed_tilt [IsAlgClosed K]` gives
`IsAlgClosed (tiltField p K)`, since the degree-preserving equivalence in (ii) forces every
finite extension of `K♭` to have degree one ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(ii), p. 17).
Here `p` is prime and `K` is complete, nontrivially normed, ultrametric and perfectoid at `p`;
`isAlgClosed_of_tilt` gives the reverse implication ([Sch12] §3, Prop. 3.8, pp. 17–18).
(iv) For every finite extension `L/K`, `L°a` is almost finite étale over `K°a`
(Tate; [GR] §6.6 for deeply ramified fields), uniformly almost finite projective ([Sch12] §3,
Thm 3.7(i), p. 17). *Needs:* P3.6.

Three lemmas accompany the theorem. If the tilt of a perfectoid field is algebraically closed, so is
the field (*untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field*): for `K` a perfectoid field with tilt `K♭`
(layer P1), `IsAlgClosed K♭` implies `IsAlgClosed K` (Mathlib `IsAlgClosed`); in characteristic `p`,
`K♭ = K` and the statement is trivial ([Sch12] §3, Prop. 3.8). The completed cyclotomic extension of
a finite extension of `ℚ_p` is perfectoid (*cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension*): for `K` a
finite extension of `ℚ_p` inside a fixed algebraic closure, with completion `C`, the closure `L` of
`K(μ_{p^∞})` in `C` is a perfectoid field, namely the compositum `L = K·ℚ_p^cycl` with the completed
cyclotomic field `ℚ_p^cycl` (layer P1), a finite extension of `ℚ_p^cycl` of degree at most
`[K : ℚ_p]` in which `K(μ_{p^∞})` is dense, and its tilt `L♭` is a finite extension of
`(ℚ_p^cycl)♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` of degree `[L : ℚ_p^cycl]`, with
`Gal(L/ℚ_p^cycl) ≅ Gal(L♭/(ℚ_p^cycl)♭)` by (ii) ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(i)). The completed tensor
product of plus rings
need not be integrally closed (*completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed*): for `K` the
completion of `ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞})`, with algebraically closed residue field and
`|K×| = |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)}`,  `ℓ` a prime with `ℓ ∤ p(p − 1)` and `L = K(p^{1/ℓ})` — a cyclic Galois extension of
degree `ℓ`, perfectoid by (i), with trivial residue extension — one has `L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ` with plus ring
`(L°)^ℓ`, while `L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ` is injective and not surjective; so the map from the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺` to `D⁺` in layer P2 is an almost isomorphism that is not an isomorphism,
and the completed tensor product of plus rings is not integrally closed in `D`, hence not a ring of
integral elements. Indeed every tensor has the same residue in all `ℓ` factors,
and this condition persists on completion; the integral idempotent `(1,0,…,0)`
fails it. This calculation uses the Galois product decomposition and P3.12
for the almost comparison.

`completed_tensor_plus_not_integrally_closed` gives the same obstruction for any
nontrivial finite Galois extension of perfectoid fields whose automorphisms act
trivially on the residue field. It specifies the completed-tensor map on pure
tensors and exhibits the integral idempotent of the identity factor outside its
image. `tame_cubic_perfectoid_extension` supplies the residue-characteristic-two,
degree-three instance inside `ℂ₂`. The finite-field theorem and Galois product
decomposition above supply the hypotheses; equal residues exclude that idempotent.

perfectoid) and `isPerfectoidField_of_isAlgClosed` (a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
field with `‖p‖ < 1` is a perfectoid field).

### P3.8 the Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem

The Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem is the field case of the tilting equivalence, passed to the
limit over all finite extensions.

**Fontaine–Wintenberger: the absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and of its tilt are
isomorphic.** (*fontaine-wintenberger*) Let `K` be a perfectoid field with tilt `K♭`. Fix an algebraic
closure `K̄` of `K` with completion `C`, so that `C♭` is an algebraically closed perfectoid field
containing `K♭` (P3.7(iii), `isAlgClosed_tilt`), and let `K♭^sep` be the separable
closure of `K♭` in `C♭`. Then `L ↦ L♭` (for finite Galois `L/K` inside `K̄`, with `L♭ ⊆ C♭` by
functoriality of tilting) defines an isomorphism of profinite groups
`Gal(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K♭^sep/K♭)` (Mathlib `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` up to the choice of closures),
compatible with the Galois correspondences (Mathlib
`InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`): finite subextensions of `K̄/K` correspond to
finite subextensions of `K♭^sep/K♭` with the same degrees ([Sch12] §3, Thm 3.7(ii), p. 17, the
degree-preserving equivalence of finite extensions; §1, Thm 1.1, p. 2, is the case
`K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`). The
direction of the comparison is fixed by the functor: `L ↦ L♭` goes from finite extensions of `K`
to finite extensions of `K♭`, and its quasi-inverse is the untilt `M ↦ M♯` of P3.5; on Galois groups
the isomorphism `Gal(K̄/K) → Gal(K♭^sep/K♭)` sends `σ` to the automorphism of `K♭^sep` induced on
the inverse limit `lim_{x ↦ x^p}` of `C` by the continuous extension of `σ` to `C`. *Needs:* P3.7;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (henselian completion); layer P1 (the tilt of a perfectoid field).

**Checks.**

- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_kummer_tower` (computation) — `K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^`: `K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^` with `t = (p, p^{1/p}, p^{1/p²}, …)`, `t♯ = p`; `K♭^sep` is the separable closure
  of `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^`, and `Gal(K♭^sep/K♭) = Gal(𝔽_p((t))^sep/𝔽_p((t)))` since
  `𝔽_p((t)) ⊂ K♭` is a purely inseparable, then completed, extension, neither of which changes
  finite étale algebras (*finite-etale-under-completed-perfection*, *henselian-finite-etale-approximation*);
  so `G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}` (the uncompleted `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})` has the same Galois group
  as its completion by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5(b)). For `p` odd the quadratic extensions correspond: `K(√p) ↔ K♭(√t)`
  (P3.5, `untilt_test_quadratic`).
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_p_two_cyclotomic` (degenerate, `p = 2`) — `K = ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})^`:
  `K♭ = 𝔽_2((t^{1/2^∞}))^` with `t = ε − 1`, `ε = (1, −1, ζ_4, ζ_8, …)` (for `p = 2` the first
  nontrivial root of unity is `ζ_2 = −1`, and `ε` is a compatible system of `2^n`-th roots of `1`),
  and `G_{ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_2((t))}`; in characteristic `2` no polynomial `u² − a` is separable
  (`t^{1/2}` already lies in `K♭`), so the separable quadratic extensions of `𝔽_2((t))` are the
  Artin–Schreier ones `u² − u = f`, and they match the quadratic extensions of `ℚ_2(ζ_{2^∞})`: the
  unramified one `K(ζ_3) = K(√−3)` corresponds to `u² − u = 1`, i.e. `𝔽_4((t))`, and all others are
  wildly ramified (`√−1 = ζ_4` and `√2 = ζ_8 + ζ_8^{-1}` already lie in `K`). The
  Kummer-type check `untilt_test_quadratic` of P3.5 needs `p` odd for this reason.
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_char_p` (degenerate) — `K` of characteristic `p`: `K♭ = K`, the
  isomorphism is the identity of `Gal(K^sep/K)`.
- `fontaine_wintenberger_test_algebraically_closed` (degenerate) — `K = C` algebraically closed:
  `C♭` is algebraically closed by `isAlgClosed_tilt` (P3.7(iii)) and both groups are trivial;
  conversely a nontrivial `Gal(K̄/K)` forces `K♭` not separably closed.

In characteristic `p`, finite étale algebras are insensitive to completed perfection
(*finite-etale-under-completed-perfection*): for `S` a complete Tate ring of characteristic `p` with
ring of definition `S₀ ∋ ϖ` and `R = (S^{perf})^` the completion of `S^{perf} = colim(S → S → ⋯)`
along Frobenius, for the Tate topology with ring of definition `colim S₀^{1/pⁿ}` — a perfect complete
Tate ring, hence perfectoid (layer P1, P1.2) — base change is an equivalence
`FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(R)`; in particular, for a `p`-finite perfectoid affinoid `(R, R⁺)`, the completed
perfection of a reduced affinoid `(S, S⁺)` of topologically finite type over a characteristic-`p`
perfectoid field, `R_fét ≃ S_fét`, and the base field is not needed ([Sch12] §7, Lem. 7.5(ii)).

The continuous group isomorphism is `Perfectoid.fontaineWintenberger` on
Mathlib's absolute Galois groups. Its marking by the action on the completed
algebraic closure is the coordinatewise convention above.
`fontaine_wintenberger_test_p_two_unramified` computes the actual untilt over
`ℚ₂^cycl`: the Artin–Schreier algebra `u²−u−1` over its tilt becomes the
algebra `v²+v+1`, adjoining a primitive third root of unity. This is the
unramified quadratic check, not a characteristic-two Kummer polynomial.

`fontaineWintenbergerFiberIso` identifies the geometric fibre of the actual
untilt with the tilted geometric fibre. `fontaineWintenberger_fiber_action`
fixes the action convention by postcomposition on algebra maps into the
