At pair level, `pair_finite_identity`, `pair_finite_zero`, and
`pair_finite_strict_plus` test the identity, the zero algebra, and a bijective
ring map whose target plus ring is strictly larger than the image of the
source plus ring. The last map is not finite étale.

### P3.15 étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces

Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are the local composites of open immersions and finite étale
maps; the strong variants carry the almost finite étale condition explicitly, and the comparison with
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 identifies étale with strongly étale, and finite étale with strongly finite étale.

**Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces*) A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is étale if it is étale in the local sense of AdicEtaleGeometry
A1.3 (`AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`, stated in Lean on `TauCeti.AdicSpace`; its Yoneda form
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` is an A1.9 target specified in AdicEtaleGeometry's README
only): every `y ∈ Y` has an open neighbourhood `V ⊆ Y` such
that `f|_V` factors as `V ↪ W → U ↪ X` with `V → W` an open immersion, `W → U` finite étale (P3.14)
and `U ⊆ X` open. `W` is then automatically perfectoid. This is [ECD] Def. 6.2(ii) (whose printed
condition `y ∈ Y` is read as `y ∈ V`), [Sch12] Def. 7.1(iii) and [Berkeley] Def. 7.5.1(2). Equivalent
local form: `U` may be taken a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid open of `X`, `W = Spa(S, S⁺)`
with `S ∈ FÉt(O(U))`, and `V` a rational subset of `W` — here `R = O(U)` is a perfectoid Tate ring,
`S` is finite étale over it, and almost mathematics on the chart is that of `(R°, R°°)` (layer P1) —
so étale morphisms are locally composites "rational embedding, finite étale, rational embedding" of
affinoid perfectoid spaces; they need not be separated or quasi-compact. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`IsEtale f` as `YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` applied to the image of `f` under
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` (A1.16); `IsEtale.iff_adic` records this identity. Prove `IsEtale.of_isOpenImmersion`
(open immersions are étale) and `IsEtale.id` (the identity of any perfectoid space is étale)
([ECD] §6, Def. 6.2(ii), p. 26; [Sch12] Definition 7.1(iii), p. 39). *Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3
(étale morphisms by the local description) and A1.9 (its Yoneda form); P3.14; layer P2.

**Checks.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_openImmersion` (degenerate) — open immersions of perfectoid spaces
  are étale; the identity is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_rational_in_cover` (computation) — for `R` perfectoid, `S ∈ FÉt(R)`
  and a rational subset `V ⊆ Spa(S, S⁺)`, the composite `V → Spa(R, R⁺)` is étale (standard affinoid
  étale map).
- Non-example: the inclusion of the open unit disc (a
  non-quasi-compact open) into the closed perfectoid disc is étale but not finite étale; so is the
  quasi-compact open immersion `{|T| ≤ |p|} ↪ {|T| ≤ 1}` (P3.14, `test_rational`), whose image is
  not closed, while finite maps are closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_frobenius` (degenerate) — for `X` of characteristic `p` the
  absolute Frobenius `φ : X → X` is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces (every `R` is perfect), hence
  finite étale of degree `1` and étale; nothing in this layer calls it inseparable, which it is only
  on the non-perfect `𝔽_p((t))` of P3.8.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_separatedness_not_required` (characterisation) — the doubled disc
  `X ⊔_U X → X` for a nonclosed rational `U ⊊ X` is étale and not separated: the diagonal
  pulls back on the cross chart `X ×_X X` to the nonclosed inclusion `U ↪ X`.
  Étale morphisms need be neither separated nor quasi-compact, and the étale site of P3.18
  contains such objects.
- Empty-overlap boundary: for nonempty `X` and `U = ∅`, the fold `X ⊔ X → X` is split finite
  étale and separated. Properness of the overlap alone does not imply nonseparatedness.

The proposed `IsEtale` uses open factorizations in `Perfd p` and their equality
with the given map; A1’s `YonedaAdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` uses the
corresponding factorizations on the analytic Yoneda carrier. `IsEtale.iff_adic` compares these, and
`perfectoid_of_analyticEtale` supplies perfectoidness of an analytic étale
source over a perfectoid base.

**Checks.** `etale_identity`, `etale_empty`, `etale_open_not_finite` test
identity, empty inclusion, and a nonclosed open inclusion which is étale but
not finite. `analytic_etale_identity`, `analytic_etale_empty`,
`analytic_etale_nonclosed` make the same distinctions on the analytic carrier.

### P3.16 strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms

**Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces; tilting invariance and
base change.** (*strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change*) Over an arbitrary perfectoid base
([Sch12] Def. 7.2 over a perfectoid field): a morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` of perfectoid Huber pairs
is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale (`S ∈ FÉt(R)` with its natural topology, `S⁺` the
integral closure of `R⁺`) and `S°a` is almost finite étale over `R°a` (layer P0). A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale if `X` has a cover by open affinoid
perfectoid `V` with `f⁻¹(V)` affinoid perfectoid and `(O_X(V), O⁺_X(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O⁺_Y(f⁻¹V))`
strongly finite étale; strongly étale if locally on `Y` it factors as an open immersion, a strongly
finite étale map and an open immersion. Define `Perfectoid.Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (the affinoid
condition on a map of perfectoid pairs), `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` and
`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale` (the two Prop-valued classes on morphisms). Properties: (a) `f` is
strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt `f♭` is (the almost finite étale condition is transported by
*almost-finite-etale-equivalence* (b)); (b) base change along arbitrary maps `Z → X` of perfectoid
spaces preserves both classes, with finite-étale affinoid formula `D = A ⊗_B C` (already complete, being finite
projective over `C`), `D⁺` the integral closure of `C⁺` in `D`, and `|Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z|`
surjective ([Sch12] Lem. 7.3(i)–(ii), with the printed `|X ×_Z Y|` read as the fibre product of the
base change); (c) composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale ([Sch12]
Cor. 7.8); (d) in characteristic `p` every (finite) étale map is strongly (finite) étale, and by
almost purity this holds in general, by *etale-is-strongly-etale*, so the strong classes coincide with
*finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces* and *etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces* ([Sch12] §7,
Def. 7.2(i), p. 39). *Needs:* P3.14; P3.15; P3.11; P3.12; layer P0
(almost finite étale algebras).

**Checks.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_charp` (computation) — for a characteristic-`p`
  perfectoid pair `R`, the diagonal `R → R × R` gives a strongly finite étale cover;
  `(a+b)^p = a^p+b^p` and componentwise Frobenius on `R × R` is bijective.
  The characteristic hypothesis is needed for these Frobenius assertions
  ([Berkeley] Proposition 6.1.6, pp. 42–43; [ECD] Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2, p. 26).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.test_open` (degenerate) — open immersions are strongly étale;
  they are strongly finite étale only when also closed.
- Compatibility: `IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsStronglyFiniteEtale f♭`.

`Pair.almostMap` is almostification of the actual restriction `R° → S°` of
the continuous pair map, over the source basic setup. `Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale`
requires it to be almost finite étale, in addition to the finite étale pair
condition. The global strong finite condition uses a covering by such
cartesian affinoid squares; the strong étale condition uses local open
factorizations. `Pair.finiteEtale_iff_strong`, `finiteEtale_iff_strong` and
`etale_iff_strong` are the three comparison theorems.

**Checks.**

- `pair_strong_identity`, `pair_strong_zero`, `pair_strong_tilt` test the
  identity, zero algebra, and preservation and reflection by actual pair tilting.
- `strong_finite_identity`, `strong_finite_clopen`, `strong_finite_tilt` test
  identity, a clopen inclusion, and geometric tilting.
- `strong_etale_identity`, `strong_etale_empty`, `strong_etale_open_not_finite`
  test identity, the empty open, and a nonclosed open which is strongly étale
  but not strongly finite étale.

### P3.17 comparison with AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 and with finite étale algebras

**Comparison of perfectoid finite étale and étale morphisms with AdicEtaleGeometry layer A1 and with
finite étale algebras.** (*perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space.
(a) (Perfectoidness) If `g : Y → X` is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of analytic adic spaces
in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3, then `Y` is a perfectoid space. (b) (Morphism classes) For
morphisms of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: finite étale in the sense of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 (= *finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces*); [ECD] Def. 6.2(i) (for
every open affinoid perfectoid `U` the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with
integral-closure plus ring); [Sch12] Def. 7.1(ii) (for one open affinoid perfectoid cover); [Berkeley]
Def. 7.5.1(1); strongly finite étale. Likewise étale in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3 ⇔
[ECD] 6.2(ii) ⇔ [Sch12] 7.1(iii) ⇔ [Berkeley] 7.5.1(2) ⇔ strongly étale. (c) (Algebraic comparison)
For `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid, the functors `X_fét → FÉt(R)^op` (global sections),
`FÉt(R) → {finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)}` (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`, plus
ring forced to be the integral closure) and the latter `→` Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` (forget
topology and plus ring) are equivalences; every finite étale `R`-algebra is perfectoid for its
natural topology. (d) (Sites) The category of perfectoid spaces étale (resp. finite étale) over `X` is
the small étale (resp. finite étale) site of the underlying adic space in the sense of
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6, with the same coverings; that layer's structure sheaves `O`, `O⁺` on it,
its Galois category of finite étale objects and its basis of affinoid objects apply. (e) (Base change
from adic spaces) If `Y' → X'` is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of locally strongly sheafy
analytic adic spaces (e.g. locally noetherian ones) and `Z → X'` is a morphism from a perfectoid
space, then `Y' ×_{X'} Z` exists and is finite étale (resp. étale) over `Z`, with ring on a finite-étale affinoid chart
`D = A ⊗_B C` and `D⁺` the integral closure of `C⁺` — this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.5
(*etale-base-change*, pullback along finite étale and étale maps), used with its hypotheses; the
clause proved here is that `Y' ×_{X'} Z` is perfectoid ([Sch12] Lem. 7.3(iii)–(iv) and Prop. 7.10)
([ECD] §6, paragraph after Def. 6.2, p. 26). *Needs:* P3.10; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.1 (strongly
sheafy rings), A1.3 (finite étale and étale morphisms), A1.5 (*etale-base-change*) and A1.6 (the
sites).

`perfectoid_of_analyticFiniteEtale` and `perfectoid_of_analyticEtale` take
A1’s `YonedaAdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` and `.IsEtaleLocalDescription`, respectively,
and a perfectoid target; their conclusion is `isPerfectoidSpace p Y` for the adic space underlying `Y`.
For (e), `perfectoid_finiteEtale_baseChange` and `perfectoid_etale_baseChange`
take locally strongly sheafy adic spaces `Y, X`, a finite étale or étale map
`f : Y → X`, a perfectoid `Z`, and a map
`Z.obj → YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj X`. They produce a perfectoid `W`,
a projection `W → Z` in the corresponding perfectoid morphism class, and
a cartesian square in `YonedaAdicSpace` over `ofAdicSpace.map f`.
Thus the universal property includes all Yoneda-adic test spaces
([Sch12] Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv), p. 40, Proposition 7.10, p. 43; [ECD]
Theorem 6.1 and Definition 6.2, p. 26, give the perfectoid Tate-ring form).

For (d), `globalSections_adicComparison` gives ring equivalences from
`globalSections p X = Γ(X, O_X)` (P2, the structure-sheaf sections of the underlying
`PreAdicSpace`) to the global sections of every adic representative
`A` with `ofAdicSpace.obj A ≅ X.obj`. They carry `globalPlus p X` exactly to
`AdicSpace.Oplus A ⊤` and commute with every pair of corresponding morphisms.
`etaleSheaves_adicComparison` gives an equivalence with the small étale
site of a locally strongly sheafy adic representative, preserving and reflecting
covering sieves, and natural isomorphisms identifying `etaleO` and `etaleOPlus`
with A1’s `structureSheafEtale` and `structureSheafPlusEtale` after forgetting
to additive groups and changing universes. The site comparison also transports
A1’s affinoid basis and Galois-category results.
`smallEtale.affinoidCover` gives every étale object an open covering by
affinoid perfectoid étale objects, and `smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory`
concludes `GaloisCategory (smallFiniteEtale p X)` when
`ConnectedSpace (YonedaAdicSpace.space.obj X.obj)` holds ([Sch12]
7.11–7.13, p. 43; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6
`AdicSpace.smallEtaleBasis_openCover` and `AdicSpace.smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory`).

The following results support the comparison. Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy, and perfectoid
spaces are locally strongly sheafy (*perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy*): for `R` perfectoid
Tate and every `n ≥ 0`, the Tate algebra `R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩` (Tau Ceti
`Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R`) is stably uniform, hence sheafy for every ring of
integral elements, so `R` is strongly sheafy in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.1;
`PerfectoidSpace.stronglySheafy p R` concludes A1’s `Huber.IsStronglySheafy R`
for every complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring `R`.
`PerfectoidSpace.locallyStronglySheafy p X` gives an adic space `A` with
`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy A` and an isomorphism
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace.obj A ≅ X.obj`. Every rational localisation and every finite étale algebra of a
perfectoid Tate ring is strongly sheafy, and the local-to-global description of finite étale maps,
fibre products of étale maps and the étale sites of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.3–A1.6 apply to perfectoid
spaces ([Berkeley] Lecture 6, §6.3, Example 6.3.2(1),
Propositions 6.3.3(3) and 6.3.4, pp. 47–48). Preimages of
affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with strongly finite
étale ring map (*strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids*): for `f : Y → X` finite
étale (a morphism of perfectoid spaces, or of analytic adic spaces with `X` perfectoid) and
`V = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` open affinoid perfectoid, `f⁻¹(V) = Spa(S, S⁺)` with `S = O_Y(f⁻¹V) ∈ FÉt(R)`
perfectoid and `S⁺` the integral closure of `R⁺`, `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` is strongly finite étale,
global sections give `V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op`, and strongly finite étale covers of `V` correspond to finite
étale `R`-algebras; in particular every finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces satisfies [ECD]
Def. 6.2(i) ([Sch12] §7, Prop. 7.6). Every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is
strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) (*etale-is-strongly-etale*): for `f : Y → X` a morphism
of perfectoid spaces, `f` is finite étale iff strongly finite étale and étale iff strongly étale — in
characteristic `p` by *finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p*, in general by
*integral-closure-almost-finite-etale* — so the tilting invariance and base-change properties of the
strong classes hold for all (finite) étale morphisms ([Sch12] §7, after Thm 7.9).

### P3.17a.1 sousperfectoid rings

**Sousperfectoid Tate rings and perfectoid frames.** (*sousperfectoid-ring*) Fix a prime `p`
(the Lean declarations `PerfectoidFrame` and `IsSousperfectoid` take any `p : ℕ`). Let
`R` be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`) in which `p` is topologically
nilpotent — equivalently, a Tate ring with a continuous ring map `ℤ_p → R`, that is, a complete Tate
`ℤ_p`-algebra. A perfectoid frame for `R` is a triple `(R̃, ι, σ)` consisting of a perfectoid Tate
ring `R̃` satisfying P1.1's `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing p R̃`,
a continuous ring homomorphism `ι : R → R̃`, and a continuous `R`-linear map
`σ : R̃ → R` (`R̃` an `R`-module through `ι`) with `σ ∘ ι = id_R`.
The ring predicate, as P1.1 defines it, is a condition on a complete Hausdorff Tate ring:
`R̃°` is bounded and some pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ R̃°` has `ϖ^p ∣ p` with Frobenius
`R̃°/ϖ → R̃°/ϖ^p` bijective; equivalently it includes completeness, Hausdorffness, uniformity,
an explicit prime, a pseudouniformizer with the required divisibility, and surjective
Frobenius modulo `p` (`TauCetiRoadmap.PerfectoidSpaces.Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP`;
Berkeley Definition 6.1.1).
`R` is sousperfectoid if it admits a perfectoid frame; a Huber pair `(R, R⁺)` is
sousperfectoid if `R` is. Conventions: `ι` is then injective and a homeomorphism onto the closed
subring `ι(R) = ker(id − ι∘σ)`; `σ` need not be multiplicative and need not map any ring of integral
elements into `R⁺`; no perfectoid base field is fixed, and `R̃` is not required to contain one;
characteristic `p` is allowed, and then `R̃` is a perfect complete Tate ring. In `Huber`, define the
structure `PerfectoidFrame` (a perfectoid frame `(R̃, ι, σ)` for `R`) and the class
`IsSousperfectoid` (`R` is a Tate ring admitting a perfectoid frame); prove that a perfectoid
frame makes `R` sousperfectoid, `IsSousperfectoid.of_isPerfectoidTateRing` (perfectoid Tate rings
are sousperfectoid, with the identity frame `PerfectoidFrame.refl`),
`PerfectoidFrame.powerBoundedSubring_eq_comap` (`a ∈ R°` iff `ι(a) ∈ R̃°`: power-boundedness is detected in the
frame, Tau Ceti `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`), `IsSousperfectoid.isUniform` (sousperfectoid rings are
uniform, [*sousperfectoid-uniform*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `IsSousperfectoid.isReduced` (sousperfectoid rings are reduced,
uniform rings being reduced), invariance under isomorphisms of
topological rings, base change of a frame along a map `R → S` of
complete Tate rings whose completed tensor product `R̃ ⊗̂_R S` is perfectoid (P3.17a.2, through
AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5's [*split-injection-completed-base-change*](../AdicSpacesPartIII/README.md) (AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5)), `isSousperfectoid_ratLoc` (rational
localisations of sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid, [*sousperfectoid-rational-localisation*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)),
`IsSousperfectoid.finiteEtale` (finite étale algebras over sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid,
[*sousperfectoid-finite-etale*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `IsSousperfectoid.restrictedMvPowerSeries` (Tate algebras over
sousperfectoid rings are sousperfectoid, [*sousperfectoid-rings*](#p3-17a-2) (P3.17a.2)), `isUniform_ratLoc`
(sousperfectoid pairs are stably uniform, [*sousperfectoid-stably-uniform*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3)) and
`IsSousperfectoid.isSheafyRing` (sousperfectoid pairs are sheafy and strongly sheafy, [*sousperfectoid-sheafy*](#p3-17a-3) (P3.17a.3)).
The closed-embedding assertion is Mathlib `Function.LeftInverse.isClosedEmbedding` applied to
`σ ∘ ι = id_R` and the continuity of `σ` and of `ι`, using the Hausdorff property of `R̃`
(Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Def. 6.3.1, p. 47; HK §7, Def. 7.1, p. 25 (perfectoid frames); BHW §3.1,
Def. 3.2(1), p. 1724; Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(1), p. 47 (perfectoid rings are
sousperfectoid with the frame `(R, id, id)`); Berkeley Lecture 6, §6.3, Ex. 6.3.2(2), p. 47

### P3.19 étale descent

**Étale descent for finite étale morphisms and finite projective modules on perfectoid spaces.**
(*etale-descent-perfectoid*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with étale site `X_ét`
of *etale-site-of-perfectoid-space*. (a) (Locality) A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is
finite étale if, for some covering `{X_i → X}` in `X_ét`, every base change `Y ×_X X_i → X_i` is
finite étale; étaleness of `f` is local on `Y` and on `X` for open coverings — for rational
coverings this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2 (*finite-etale-rational-descent*, KL 2.6.9), and the
étale-covering case is proved here. (b) (Stack) The prestack `U ↦ U_fét` (finite étale perfectoid
spaces over `U`, with isomorphisms) on `X_ét` is a stack for the étale topology (Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`): finite étale spaces with descent data along an étale
covering descend uniquely (the sheaf property of `U ↦ O(U)` on `X_ét` that it rests on is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6, *etale-structure-sheaf*). (c) (Vector bundles) For `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`
affinoid perfectoid, the equivalence `M ↦ M ⊗_R O_{X_ét}` between finitely generated projective
`R`-modules and finite locally free `O_{X_ét}`-modules, with `M ⊗ O` a sheaf on `X_ét` and
`M ⊗ O(Y) = M ⊗_R O(Y)` on affinoid perfectoid `Y ∈ X_ét` ([KL15] Thm 8.2.22(c), (d)), is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a (*stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles*, for pairs with the stable étale basis supplied by strong sheafiness;
the rational-site form is AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5 (*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*)),
used here with `(R, R⁺)` perfectoid and strongly sheafy by P3.17. The ordinary
finite-étale descent is [KL15] Theorems 1.3.4–1.3.5, and the étale vector-bundle
comparison is Theorem 8.2.22(c)–(d), p. 165. Descent along
v-covers belongs to the downstream consumer DiamondsAndVStacks layer D3.
*Needs:* P3.18;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.2, A1.6 (*finite-etale-rational-descent*, *etale-structure-sheaf*);
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.6a (*stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles*); AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5
(*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*).

### P3.20 tilting identifies the étale sites

**Tilting identifies the étale sites: `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét`, compatibly with affinoids, fibre products,
coverings and `O⁺/ϖ`.** (*etale-site-tilting-equivalence*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with tilt
`X♭` (layer P2). The tilting functor `Y ↦ Y♭` of the slice equivalence (layer P2: perfectoid spaces
over `X` `≃` perfectoid spaces over `X♭`) restricts to equivalences of categories `X_ét ≃ X♭_ét` and
`X_fét ≃ X♭_fét` of *etale-site-of-perfectoid-space*. These equivalences preserve and reflect affinoid
perfectoid objects (with `Spa(S, S⁺)♭ = Spa(S♭, S♭⁺)`), fibre products, and covering families
(`|Y| ≅ |Y♭|` compatibly with the maps to `|X| ≅ |X♭|`); hence they are equivalences of sites and
induce equivalences of topoi `Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X♭_ét)` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`).
They are functorial in `X`: compatible with the morphisms of sites induced by maps `X' → X` and their
tilts. Locally choose a pseudouniformiser `ϖ♭` with `ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯` and
`ϖ^p | p` in the integral ring (as in P3.5); they identify the sheaves `O⁺_X/ϖ` and
`O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭`, and the almost sheaves `O⁺a/ϖ` and `O⁺a_{X♭}/ϖ♭`, on the identified sites. For affinoid
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)` the restriction to `X_fét` is the tilting equivalence `FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭)` of
*finite-etale-tilting-equivalence* ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.3, p. 26). *Needs:* P3.18.

### P3.21 almost acyclicity on the étale site

**Almost acyclicity of `O⁺` and acyclicity of `O` on the étale site of an affinoid perfectoid
space.** (*etale-almost-acyclicity*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space (`R`
perfectoid Tate, no base field) with étale site `X_ét`, and write `H^i(X_ét, −)` for sheaf cohomology
of abelian sheaves on `X_ét` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). Then: (a) `H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺` and
`H^i(X_ét, O⁺)` is almost zero (killed by `R°°`) for `i > 0`; (b) `H⁰(X_ét, O) = R` and
`H^i(X_ét, O) = 0` for `i > 0`; (c) for every finite covering `{U_j → U}` in `X_ét` of an affinoid
perfectoid object `U` by affinoid perfectoid objects, the augmented Čech complex of `O⁺` is almost
exact and that of `O` is exact; (d) `H⁰(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)^a = (R⁺/ϖ)^a` and `H^i(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)` is almost zero
for `i > 0`; (e) for every finitely generated projective `R`-module `M`, `H^i(X_ét, M ⊗_R O) = 0` for
`i > 0`. The same holds on the analytic site (layer P2) and for every affinoid perfectoid object of
`X_ét` ([ECD] §6, Thm 6.3, second paragraph, p. 26 (`O⁺`); [Sch12] Prop. 7.13, p. 43 (`O^{°a}` and
hence `O` on `X_ét`, over a perfectoid field)). *Needs:* P3.18; P3.19 (finite projective coefficients).

presheaf. `finite_basechange_split_two` computes the two copies of the new

## Layer P4: injections, immersions and separatedness

The layer builds the points of a perfectoid space with values in affinoid perfectoid fields,
injections together with the qcqs isomorphism criterion, immersions, Zariski closed immersions and
the universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset, the theorem that Zariski closed
immersions are strongly Zariski closed, diagonals, separatedness with its valuative criterion, and
the behaviour of all of these under tilting.

### P4.1 affinoid perfectoid fields and their points

**Affinoid perfectoid fields and `(K, K⁺)`-valued points of perfectoid spaces.**
(*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*) An affinoid perfectoid field is a pair `(K, K⁺)` of a
perfectoid field `K` (a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field, [ECD] §3,
Definition 3.6; P1.10) and an open and bounded valuation subring `K⁺ ⊂ K`; equivalently `K⁺` is a
valuation subring with `K°° ⊂ K⁺ ⊂ K° = O_K`, so `(K, K⁺)` is a Huber pair and `Spa(K, K⁺)` is an
affinoid perfectoid space; it is algebraically closed if `K` is. A morphism `(K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺)` is a
morphism of Huber pairs, also called an extension of affinoid perfectoid fields. The points of
`Spa(K, K⁺)` are the valuation subrings `V` with `K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°`; they form a chain, `K⁺` is the
unique closed point, `K°` the unique rank-one point, and the nonempty quasicompact open subsets
are the rational subsets `{|h| ≤ 1} = Spa(K, K'⁺)`, `h ∈ K`, where `K'⁺` is the smallest valuation
subring containing `K⁺[h]`, with `h ∈ K°` for a nonempty subset (a finite union of such sets is again one, the chain being totally
ordered); when `K⁺` has finite rank every valuation subring `K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K°` is of this form, but
in general `Spa(K, K'⁺)` need not be open, and in particular the rank-one point `K°` need not be
open (see the Checks). For a perfectoid space `X` (P2.10) the set of
`(K, K⁺)`-valued points is `X(K, K⁺) := Hom(Spa(K, K⁺), X)`, covariant in `X` and in extensions of Huber pairs
`(K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺)` (precomposition with `Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺)`), with the closed-point map `X(K, K⁺) → |X|`; for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid it
is the set of morphisms of Huber pairs `(R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺)`, and the closed-point map sends `φ` to
`spaComap φ` of the closed point. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `AffinoidField` (a perfectoid field
with an open and bounded valuation subring), `AffinoidField.toPair` (the underlying Huber pair),
`AffinoidField.ofRankOne` (the pair `(K, K°)`), `AffinoidField.closedPoint` and `fieldPoints`
(`X(K, K⁺)`, with `fieldPoints.map`, `fieldPoints.restrict`, `fieldPoints.closedPointImage`); prove
`AffinoidField.valuationEquiv`, `AffinoidField.isOpen_iff` and `fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv`
(`X(K, K⁺) ≃ Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺)` for `X` affinoid) ([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.3 (ii),
p. 21; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (2)–(3), p. 61). *Needs:* P1.10; P2.10;
Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`; Mathlib `ValuationSubring`.

**Checks.**

- `AffinoidField.subsingleton_spa_ofRankOne` (computation) — for every perfectoid field `K`,
  `|Spa(K, K°)|` has exactly one point.
- `AffinoidField.card_spa_eq_two` (computation) — if `K⁺ ⊊ K°` is the preimage of a rank-one
  valuation ring `k⁺ ⊊ k` of the residue field `k = K°/K°°`, then `|Spa(K, K⁺)|` has exactly two
  points and only `K⁺` is closed.
- `AffinoidField.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv_closedPoint` (compatibility) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`
  affinoid perfectoid and `φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) = Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺)`, the closed-point image of
  `φ` is Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap φ` applied to the closed point of `Spa(K, K⁺)`.
- `AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint` (non-example) — let `K⁺` be the preimage of a valuation
  ring `k⁺` of the residue field `k = K°/K°°` with value group `⋃_n ℚⁿ` ordered lexicographically
  with the last coordinate dominant, whose convex subgroups are `0 ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℚ² ⊂ ⋯` with union the
  whole group. Then `|Spa(K, K⁺)|` is the chain `K⁺ = W_0 ⊂ W_1 ⊂ W_2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ K°` with
  `K° = ⋃_n W_n`; each `{V ⊇ W_n} = {|h_n| ≤ 1}` (`h_n` of value `−e_n`, for `n ≥ 1`) is open, but every open
  set containing `K°` contains some `{V ⊇ W_n}`, so `Spa(K, K°) = {K°}` is a quasicompact subset
  that is not open: not every `Spa(K, K'⁺)` is an open subset. The divisible group is essential:
  the residue field of a perfectoid field is perfect, so any valuation on it has
  `p`-divisible value group. The negative control `rank_group_not_integer` takes
  `K : AffinoidField 2` and an actual residue presentation `ρ : K° → k`,
  surjective with kernel the elements of norm less than one. It asserts that no
  valuation `k → WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)` is surjective, excluding an integer
  residual value group for this carrier.

The structure `AffinoidField` stores a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field,
its perfectoid-field instance, and a valuation subring satisfying `IsRingOfIntegralElements`.
`AffinoidField.valuationEquiv` gives the valuation-subring classification above;
`AffinoidField.closedPoint_spec` identifies the unique closed point. The two-point test uses
strict inclusion and the absence of intermediate valuation subrings, the equivalent
valuation-ring formulation of the rank-one residual hypothesis.

| `AffinoidField.toPair_proper` | A strict smaller plus ring gives a different pair on the same field. |
| `AffinoidField.closedPoint_rankOne` | Every point of the maximal-plus spectrum equals its closed point. |
| `AffinoidField.closedPoint_two` | For strict smaller plus, a second point exists and is not closed. |

| `fieldPoints_quadratic` | A separable degree-two extension has two distinct geometric field points with the same image. |
| `fieldPoints_map_identity`, `fieldPoints_map_composition` | The identity field point sends each scalar `t` to `t`; postcomposition along `R → S` sends `t` to `a(f(t))` under the affinoid comparison. |
| `fieldPoints_restrict_identity`, `fieldPoints_restrict_composition` | The identity field point extended along `e : K → L` sends `t` to `e(t)`; a further extension `d : L → M` sends it to `d(e(t))`. |

`AffinoidField.exists_infiniteRank` supplies this realization for every prime `p`:
a characteristic-`p` affinoid perfectoid field `K`, a surjective residue map
`ρ : K° → k` with kernel `{a | ‖a‖ < 1}`, and a surjective valuation of the perfect

It identifies `K⁺` with the inverse image of its valuation ring, and supplies
all the proper coarsenings `W_n`, strictly increasing from `K⁺` and exhausting `K°`.
One construction takes the Hahn field `k = 𝔽_p((⊕ₙ ℚ))` and

Thus `K` is perfectoid by [ECD] Proposition 3.5, p. 15. The convex subgroups
supported on the first `n` coordinates give the asserted coarsenings; the
valuation-ring description of points is [Berkeley] Example 2.3.8, p. 16.
The example `AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint_realization` applies
`AffinoidField.not_isOpen_rankOnePoint` to this existence theorem and exhibits
an actual non-open rank-one singleton.

### P4.2 quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms

**Quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms of perfectoid spaces.**
(*quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*) A perfectoid space `X` is quasicompact (resp.
quasiseparated) if `|X|` is quasicompact (resp. a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`). A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is quasicompact if `f⁻¹(U)` is quasicompact for every quasicompact
open `U ⊆ |X|`, equivalently for every open affinoid `U ⊆ X`; it is quasiseparated if the diagonal
`Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal` in the category of perfectoid
spaces, whose fibre products are P2.16) is quasicompact; qcqs means both. Equivalently, `f` is
quasiseparated if and only if for every open affinoid `U ⊆ X` and all open affinoids
`V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U)` the intersection `V ∩ W` is quasicompact; if `X` is affinoid (or quasiseparated),
`f` is quasiseparated if and only if `|Y|` is quasiseparated. The comparison with the topos-theoretic notions for represented sheaves is owned by
AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.10 ([ECD] §8, Proposition 8.3, p. 41). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `QuasiCompact` and `QuasiSeparated`; prove
`quasiCompact_iff_affinoid` (the test on open affinoids), `quasiSeparated_iff_affinoid_inter`,
`quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace`, `QuasiCompact.comp`, `QuasiSeparated.comp`,
`QuasiCompact.baseChange` and `QuasiSeparated.baseChange` ([ECD] §5, remark after Proposition 5.11,
p. 25). *Needs:* Mathlib `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`; P2.16.

`QuasiCompact` lives on `Perfd`; `quasiCompact_iff_adicCompactOpens` identifies it with
AdicSpacesPartII R0.6's `AdicSpace.QuasiCompact` through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`. Since a
perfectoid space is itself an adic space on the pre-adic carrier of P2.10, the representatives below
may be taken to be `Y.obj` and `X.obj` themselves, with `eY`, `eX` the identities.
Precisely, for `f : Y → X`, adic representatives `A, B`, isomorphisms
`eY : ofAdicSpace(A) ≅ Y.obj`, `eX : ofAdicSpace(B) ≅ X.obj`, and `g : A → B`
with `ofAdicSpace(g) ≫ eX.hom = eY.hom ≫ f.hom`, it equates `QuasiCompact p f`
with compactness of `g⁻¹(U)` for every compact open `U` of `B`. These are the
compact-open tests in R0 and [ECD] §5, p. 25; the comparison uses
`YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace_space`, which is natural in the adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16).

### P4.3 injections of perfectoid spaces

Injections are the monomorphisms of the category of perfectoid spaces; this subsection and the six
after it define them, build the residue-field points on which they are tested, and characterise
them by points, by residue fields and by base change.

**Injections of perfectoid spaces.** (*injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*) Throughout, `p` is a fixed
prime; perfectoid fields are those of [ECD] Definition 3.6, of either characteristic, with no base
field; `K⁺` is a valuation subring, and open integrally closed subrings that are not valuation
subrings (they occur in [ECD] Lemma 9.9) do not give affinoid perfectoid fields. A morphism
`f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for every perfectoid space `Z` the map
`f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X)` is injective ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.1, p. 21). It suffices to test
affinoid perfectoid `Z`, because two morphisms `Z → Y` that agree on an open affinoid cover of `Z`
agree ([ECD] §5, sentence after Definition 5.1, p. 21). In the category `Perfd` of perfectoid spaces
this says exactly that `f` is a monomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`), and, fibre products
existing in `Perfd` (P2.16), it is equivalent to the diagonal `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` being an
isomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`). In `PerfectoidSpace`,
use `CategoryTheory.Mono` directly for injections. The comparison
`isInjection_iff_affinoid_tests` identifies it with injectivity on affinoid test objects.
Use Mathlib’s `pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`, monomorphism composition and cancellation, and
split-monomorphism instances for the categorical consequences; sections and diagonals are injections.
The affinoid form `IsInjection_affinoid` is stated for a morphism `φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` of
arbitrary complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pairs (not assumed perfectoid or sheafy) as the
epimorphism condition towards perfectoid Huber pairs `(W, W⁺)`: `a ∘ φ = b ∘ φ` forces `a = b`;
for `R`, `S` perfectoid this is the notion above for `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)`, since
`Hom(Spa(W, W⁺), Spa(S, S⁺)) = Hom((S, S⁺), (W, W⁺))` for affinoid perfectoid pairs (P2.9).
*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`, `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`,
`CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`; P2.10; P2.16.

**Checks.**

- `injection_id` (degenerate) — the identity pair map cancels against every perfectoid test
  pair, including when the source ring is zero.
- `injection_rational` (computation) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid and `U ⊆ X`
  rational, the open immersion `U → X` is an injection.
- `isInjection_diagonal` (computation) — for the split double cover `X ⊔ X → X`
  with `X` nonempty, the diagonal is an injection but is not surjective on points.
  In general, for every morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces,
  `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` is an injection, being a split monomorphism.
- `injection_quadratic` and `injection_quadratic_pair` (non-example) — for a perfectoid field `K` and a separable
  quadratic extension `L/K` with continuous structure map (`L` carries the extended valuation and is perfectoid by P3.7), `Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K)` is bijective
  on underlying spaces but not an injection: the two `K`-embeddings of `L` into a completed
  algebraic closure `C` give distinct `(C, O_C)`-points with the same image.

Integral perfectoid rings give perfectoid Tate rings
(*integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli*): that `R := R₀[1/π]`, for `R₀` `π`-adically complete
and integral perfectoid with `π` a non-zero-divisor and `π^p | p`, with chosen compatible roots of `π`, is a perfectoid Tate ring with
`R₀ ⊆ R°`, `πR° ⊆ R₀` and `R°/R₀` killed by every `π^{1/pⁿ}` is
*perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid* (P1.20, [BMS] §3.2, Lemma 3.21, p. 27); it is
applied here to the compatible-root annulus rings `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^a/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩`, which are
therefore perfectoid. For a nonzero perfectoid field `R = K` and a nondegenerate annulus
(`a` a positive integer), the ordinary annulus `K⟨T, ϖ^a/T⟩` is not perfectoid; the zero-ring case
does not give a non-example.

The carrier `ordinaryAnnulus` is the quotient of the supplier's two-variable restricted
series ring by `TU − ϖᵃ`, with the quotient topology and its additive uniformity.
`ordinaryAnnulus_not_perfectoid` requires `a > 0` and an affinoid perfectoid field.
`rootAnnulus` instead rationally localizes the P1 root disc at `|ϖᵃ| ≤ |T|`.

exclude the zero ring, and give bijective Frobenius in characteristic p.

### P4.4 filtered intersections of rational subsets

### P4.5 the completed residue field point

**The completed residue field point `i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X`.** (*residue-field-point-injection*)
For a perfectoid space `X` and a point `x ∈ X` (of any rank), the completed residue field `K(x)`
with its open and bounded valuation subring `K(x)⁺` is an affinoid perfectoid field (P2.5), and
there is a canonical morphism `i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X` sending the closed point to `x`: on an
affinoid perfectoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(R, R⁺)` of `x` it is given by `(R, R⁺) → (K(x), K(x)⁺)`,
independently of `U`. Moreover ([ECD] §5, Example 5.2, p. 21): (a) `i_x` is isomorphic over `U` to
the pro-rational subspace `ι_𝒰` for `𝒰` the rational neighbourhoods of `x` in `U`
(P4.4), so `K(x)⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
`colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)` and `K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ`; (b) `i_x` is an injection and `|i_x|`
is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of `x`; (c) every `(K, K⁺)`-valued point `φ` of
`X` whose closed point maps to `x` factors uniquely as `φ = i_x ∘ φ'` with
`φ' : Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)` given by a morphism of affinoid perfectoid fields; (d) for
`f : Y → X` and `y ∈ Y` with `f(y) = x`, `f ∘ i_y = i_x ∘ Spa(K(x) → K(y))`. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `residueFieldPoint` (the morphism `i_x`); prove `residueFieldPoint_closed` (simp: `i_x`
maps the closed point to `x`), `residueFieldPoint_injection`, `residueFieldPoint_range`,
`residueFieldPoint_factor` ((c)), `residueFieldPoint_naturality` ((d)) and
`residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` ((a)). *Needs:* *intersection-of-rational-subsets*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*; *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; P2.5.

**Checks.**

- `residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (degenerate) — for `X = Spa(K, K⁺)` and `x` the closed point,
  `i_x` is the identity of `X`.
- `residueFieldPoint_gauss` (computation) — for the Gauss point `η` of
  `Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, `K(η)` is the completion of `C(T^{1/p^∞})` for the Gauss
  norm, `K(η)⁺ = K(η)°`, and `|i_η|` has image `{η}`.
- `residueFieldPoint_not_isImmersion` (non-example) — `i_η` is an injection whose image `{η}`
  is not open (and not locally closed), so `i_η` is not an immersion.

### P4.6 the isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps

**Isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps: bijectivity on points and on `(C, C⁺)`-points.**
(*qcqs-isomorphism-criterion*) Let `f : Y → X` be a quasicompact and quasiseparated morphism of
perfectoid spaces (P4.2). The following are equivalent: (i) `f` is
an isomorphism; (ii) `|f| : |Y| → |X|` is bijective and for every rank-one point `y ∈ Y` with image
`x` the map `K(x) → K(y)` is an isomorphism; (iii) for every affinoid perfectoid field `(K, K⁺)` the
map `Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is a bijection; (iv) for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid
field `(C, C⁺)` the map `Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺)` is a bijection. The qcqs hypothesis makes `|f|` a
spectral map of spectral spaces over an affinoid in (ii)+(iii) ⇒ (i) ([ECD] §5, Lemma 5.4, p. 23).
*Needs:* *quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*; *affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*;
*residue-field-point-injection*; P2.16.

**Checks.**

- `isIso_of_bijective_qcqs_id` (computation) — the identity of `Spa(K,K⁺)` with
  `K⁺ ⊊ K°` and exactly two valuation overrings has two underlying points,
  satisfies the residue-field bijectivity clause (ii), and is bijective on both
  field-valued and algebraically closed field-valued points, (iii)–(iv).
  Its isomorphism assertion is obtained through `isIso_iff_residueFields`.
  `isIso_of_bijective_qcqs_empty` gives the empty-space case, whose sets of
  field-valued points are empty ([ECD] Lemma 5.4, p. 23).
- `not_isIso_openDisc_sum` (non-example, the qcqs hypothesis) — for
  `X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, `D ⊆ X` the open unit disc and `Z_𝒰 → X` the closed
  immersion onto its complement `T = ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}` (P4.17), the map `D ⊔ Z_𝒰 → X` is
  bijective on points with isomorphic completed residue fields at every point, so (ii) holds, but it
  is not quasicompact (the preimage of `X` is not quasicompact) and not an isomorphism: `D` is open
  and closed in `D ⊔ Z_𝒰` and not closed in `X` (the point `y` with `|T(y)| = 1⁻` lies in its
  closure).

The proof rests on five results. A qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point `x` is
`Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)` (*qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point*): `i_x` is an isomorphism, so
`X` is affinoid with `O_X(X) = K(x)` and `O⁺_X(X) = K(x)⁺` ([ECD] §5, Example 5.2, last paragraph,
p. 21). Points of fibre products surject onto compatible pairs (*fibre-product-points-surjective*):
for `W = Y₁ ×_X Y₂` (P2.16), `|W| → |Y₁| ×_{|X|} |Y₂|` is surjective and spectral on spectral opens,
so points `y₁, y₂` over the same `x` lift to `(K(w), K(w)⁺)`-points `pr_i ∘ i_w` with the same
image ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 22). Every affinoid perfectoid field embeds into an
algebraically closed one, and `(K, K⁺)`-points are detected there
(*algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field*): for `C` the completion of an algebraic
closure of `K` and `C⁺ ⊆ C°` the preimage of a valuation subring of the residue field of `C°`
dominating the image of `K⁺`, `(C, C⁺)` is an algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field with
`C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺`, and `Y(K, K⁺) → Y(C, C⁺)` is injective for every perfectoid `Y` ([ECD] §5, proof of
Lemma 5.4, p. 23). A map of perfectoid fields that is injective on geometric points is an
isomorphism (*rank-one-residue-field-rigidity*): a continuous homomorphism `K → L` of perfectoid
fields such that any two continuous homomorphisms `L → C` agreeing on `K` are equal, for every
algebraically closed perfectoid field `C`, is an isomorphism ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3,
p. 22). A homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue pairs is an isomorphism
(*isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs*): if `|f|` is a homeomorphism and
`(K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K(y), K(y)⁺)` is an isomorphism for every `y` over `x`, then `f` is an
isomorphism ([ECD] §5, proof of Lemma 5.4, p. 23; *stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer*
for the sheaf half).

The declarations are `isIso_iff_fieldPoints`, `isIso_iff_geometricPoints` and
`isIso_iff_residueFields`, each with explicit quasicompactness and quasiseparatedness.
`isIso_residueFieldPoint_of_uniqueClosed`, `AffinoidField.exists_algebraicallyClosed`,
`AffinoidField.rigidity` and `isIso_of_homeomorphism_residuePairs` state the supporting
interfaces. Fibre-product point surjectivity is already `pullback_points`
in P2.16; the spectral assertion on affinoids follows from `QuasiCompact_affinoid`.
`not_isIso_openDisc_sum` uses the genuine coproduct of the open disc and its pro-rational
complement, and states bijectivity, residue-pair isomorphisms and failure of quasicompactness
and of being an isomorphism together.

### P4.7 characterisations of injections

**Characterisations of injections of perfectoid spaces.** (*injection-criteria*) Let `f : Y → X` be
a morphism of perfectoid spaces, with no quasicompactness hypothesis. The following are equivalent:
(i) `f` is an injection (P4.3); (ii) for every affinoid perfectoid
field `(K, K⁺)`, `Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is injective; (ii') the same for every algebraically closed
affinoid perfectoid field `(C, C⁺)`; (iii) `|f|` is injective and `K(x) → K(y)` is an isomorphism
for every rank-one point `y ∈ Y` with image `x`; (iv) `|f|` is injective and, for every perfectoid
space `Z`, `Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) ×_{C⁰(|Z|, |X|)} C⁰(|Z|, |Y|)` is a bijection, i.e. `f` is final
among morphisms `g : Z → X` for which `|g|` factors through a continuous map `|Z| → |Y|`. This is
the continuous-factorisation contract of [ECD] Proposition 5.3(iv): continuity of `|Z| → |Y|` is for
the topology of `|Y|`, which need not be the subspace topology of the image. In
particular injections `Y → X` are determined, up to unique isomorphism over `X`, by the continuous
injection `|Y| → |X|`, not by its image set; `|Y|` need not carry the subspace topology of `|X|`.
Only when `|f|` is in addition a topological embedding does the factorisation condition reduce to
`|g|(|Z|) ⊆ |f|(|Y|)`, so that the injection is determined by its image subset with the subspace
topology ([ECD] §5,
Proposition 5.3 (iii)–(iv) and the paragraph after it, p. 21; [Berkeley] Lecture 8,
Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3), p. 61 for (ii')). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*;
*affinoid-perfectoid-field-points*; *residue-field-point-injection*; *qcqs-isomorphism-criterion*;
P2.16.

The step (iii) ⇒ (iv) uses the `(K, K⁺)`-points of a map that is injective on points with
isomorphic rank-one residue fields (*field-points-of-residually-injective-maps*): under (iii), for
every affinoid perfectoid field `(K, K⁺)` the map `f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺)` is injective with image
the `φ` whose closed point maps into `f(|Y|)` ([ECD] §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, (iii) ⇒ (iv),
p. 22).

The four criteria are `injection_iff_fieldPoints`, `injection_iff_geometricPoints`,
`injection_iff_residueFields` and `injection_iff_continuous_lift`; the affinoid comparisons
are `isInjection_iff_affinoid_tests` and `isInjection_affinoid_iff`.
`fieldPoints_image` specifies the image as precisely the points whose closed point lands in
that of the injection.

  injection is not determined by its image set.
- Embedding case: a rational open immersion is an injection whose `|f|` is an open embedding, so it is

### P4.8 base change of injections

**Base change of injections, and the underlying space of a pulled-back injection.**
(*injections-base-change-composition*) Let `f : Y → X` be an injection of perfectoid spaces and
`X' → X` any morphism, with base change `f' : Y' = X' ×_X Y → X'`. Then `f'` is an injection, and
the natural map `|Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|` is a homeomorphism (the target with the fibre product
topology). Moreover composites of injections are injections, and if `g ∘ f` is an injection then so
is `f` (use the supplier monomorphism instances for these categorical assertions) ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *injection-criteria*;
*maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing*; P2.16.

`injectionPullbackHomeomorph` identifies the actual categorical pullback with the
subspace of pairs `(y,z)` having the same image, and `injectionPullbackHomeomorph_apply`
fixes both projections in the order `(pullback.fst, pullback.snd)`.

### P4.9 universally injective maps

**Injections are exactly the universally injective maps.** (*injection-iff-universally-injective*)
A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an injection if and only if it is universally
injective: for every morphism `X' → X` the base change `f' : X' ×_X Y → X'` is injective on
underlying spaces; nothing beyond the existence of fibre products is assumed ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (ii), p. 24). *Needs:* *injections-base-change-composition*; *injection-criteria*.

### P4.10 immersions, open immersions and closed immersions

Immersions are injections that are topological embeddings with locally closed image; this
subsection and the next define them and match the open ones with the open immersions of AdicSpaces.

**Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces.** (*perfectoid-immersion*)
A morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if `f` is an injection
(P4.3) and `|f| : |Y| → |X|` is a locally closed immersion, i.e. a
topological embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`; `|Y|` carries its own spectral topology, and
the embedding condition says it is the subspace topology) with locally closed image (Mathlib
`IsLocallyClosed`). It is an open immersion (resp. closed immersion) if moreover `|f|` is an open
(resp. closed) embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`). No
quasicompactness is assumed. The definition is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent
structure: an injection is determined by its continuous injection `|Y| → |X|`
(*injection-criteria* (iv)), and when `|f|` is an embedding by its image with the subspace topology,
so an immersion is determined up to unique isomorphism over `X` by the locally closed subset
`f(|Y|)`. Neither condition on `|f|` follows from P4.7, so the definition is not redundant: the
injection of P4.6 from the open disc and its pro-rational complement is a bijection onto the closed
set `|X|` but not an embedding, and `i_η` at the Gauss point (P4.5) is an injection that is not an
immersion.
Closed immersions are strictly more general than Zariski closed immersions (P4.17). In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsImmersion`, `IsOpenImmersion` and `IsClosedImmersion`.
`IsImmersion.isInjection` projects the `Mono f` conjunct of `IsImmersion`. Prove `IsImmersion.ext` (two immersions into `X` with the same image are
uniquely isomorphic over `X`), `IsImmersion.stableUnderGeneralization_range`,
`IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` and `IsOpenImmersion.of_isOpen` (for `U ⊆ |X|` open, the open
perfectoid subspace `U → X` is an open immersion) ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.6 and the sentence after
it, p. 24). *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`,
`IsLocallyClosed`, `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`; P2.10.

**Checks.**

- `isOpenImmersion_rationalSubset` (computation) — for `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` affinoid perfectoid and
  `U ⊆ X` rational, `U → X` is an open immersion.

### P4.12 Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions

Zariski closed subsets of an affinoid perfectoid space are the zero loci of ideals; this subsection
and the next define the two notions of closed immersion attached to them, which P4.15 shows agree.

**Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions into affinoid perfectoid spaces.**
(*zariski-closed-immersion*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space. For an ideal
`I ⊆ R` put `V(I) := {x ∈ |X| : |g(x)| = 0 for all g ∈ I}`; a subset `Z ⊆ |X|` is Zariski closed if
`Z = V(I)` for some ideal `I` ([Torsion] §II.2, Definition II.2.1, p. 13). A morphism `f : Z → X` of
perfectoid spaces is a Zariski closed immersion (defined by `I`) if `f` is a closed immersion
(P4.10) and `f(|Z|) = V(I)` ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.7 (i), p. 24). Conventions:
`V(I)` depends only on the closure of `I` and on its radical; `V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F` with
`U_F := {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}` rational, because `I` is an ideal and `|ϖ(x)|ⁿ → 0` cofinally at
every continuous valuation; `V(I)` is closed, pro-constructible and stable under generalization;
`V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J)` and `V(IJ) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J)`; for a closed ideal `J`, `V(J)` is
the range of the closed embedding `spaComap` of the quotient pair (Tau Ceti
`Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`, `ValuationSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientMk`),
which gives `isClosed_zeroLocus`. Every Zariski closed subset is the
image of exactly one Zariski closed immersion up to unique isomorphism (P4.14). A Zariski closed immersion defined by `I` need not be
`Spa(R/I, ·)`: the perfectoid structure on `V(I)` kills all compatible `p`-power roots. The global
notion over non-affinoid `X` (locally Zariski closed) is layer [P8](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p8-finite-quotients-and-closed-perfectoid-loci-in-towers). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`zeroLocus` (`V(I)`), `IsZariskiClosed` and `IsZariskiClosedImmersion`; prove
`zeroLocus_eq_iInter_rational` (`V(I) = ⋂_F U_F`), `isClosed_zeroLocus`,
`stableUnderGeneralization_zeroLocus`, `zeroLocus_sup`, `zeroLocus_mul`, `zeroLocus_closure`
(simp: `V(closure I) = V(I)` and `V(√I) = V(I)`).
`IsZariskiClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` projects the closed-immersion conjunct
of [ECD] Definition 5.7(i), p. 24. *Needs:* *perfectoid-immersion*; Tau Ceti

### P4.13 strongly Zariski closed immersions

**Strongly Zariski closed immersions: surjective perfectoid quotients.**
(*strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space. A
morphism `f : Z → X` is strongly Zariski closed if `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)` is affinoid perfectoid, `f` is
induced by a morphism `(R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)` with `R → S` surjective, and `S⁺` is the integral closure
of the image of `R⁺` in `S` ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.7 (ii), p. 24); `S` perfectoid is part of the
data. Equivalently (by the open mapping theorem, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), with
`I := ker(R → S)` closed, `(S, S⁺)` is isomorphic to the library's quotient pair
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`, whose plus ring is the integral closure of the image of
`R⁺` (`Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`), and `R/I` is perfectoid. The plus-ring clause is part of the
definition: it is what makes a strongly Zariski closed map a closed immersion (P4.21).
The algebraic predicate `IsStronglyZariskiClosed_affinoid` is defined for arbitrary Huber pairs
by these two clauses, without completeness or perfectoidness; its geometric interpretation and
the base-change theorem here require perfectoid Tate rings. For base change along `(A,A⁺) → (C,C⁺)`,
the resulting ring map is `C → B ⊗̂_A C`, the supplier’s `completedTensor.inr` (in `Huber.Pair`). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsStronglyZariskiClosed`;
prove `stronglyZariskiClosed_affinoid_iff` (the affine predicate supplies both surjectivity
and the plus-ring equality through its fields), `stronglyZariskiClosed_isClosed_ker`,
`stronglyZariskiClosed_quotient_comparison` and `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`
(the quotient immersion is defined by `ker(R → S)`). *Needs:* Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`.

### P4.14 the universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset

The universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace is the pro-rational subspace of the rational
neighbourhoods `U_F` of `V(I)`; this subsection builds it and the next two show it is a surjective
perfectoid quotient and match it with the closed immersions of AdicSpaces.

**The universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset.**
(*universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space with a
pseudouniformizer `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with `ϖ^p | p` admitting compatible `p`-power roots, and `I ⊆ R` an ideal (not necessarily
closed or finitely generated). Let `𝒰_I := {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}`,
`U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}`, and use `zariskiClosedSubspace.presentation_affinoid D F` for the presentation
`({1} ∪ F)/1`. This definition only needs a commutative topological ring and a pair of
definition `D`, without a perfectoid hypothesis. Let `ι_I : Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) → X` be the pro-rational
subspace of `𝒰_I` (P4.4): `S_I⁺` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of
`colim_F O⁺_X(U_F)` and `S_I = S_I⁺[1/ϖ]`. Then: (a) `Z_I` is affinoid perfectoid and `R → S_I`
has dense image; (b) `|ι_I|` is a homeomorphism onto `V(I)`; (c) a morphism `g : W → X` from a
perfectoid space factors through `ι_I` if and only if `g^*(h) = 0` in `O_W(W)` for all `h ∈ I`, if
and only if `|g|` lands in `V(I)`, and then uniquely; (d) `ι_I` is a Zariski closed immersion
defined by `I` (P4.12); (e) `I^perf := ker(R → S_I)` is a closed ideal
containing `I`, equal to `{h ∈ R : |h| = 0 on V(I)}`, and `Z_{I^perf} = Z_I`; (f) `Z_I` depends
only on `V(I)`. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `zariskiClosedSubspace` (`Z_I`) and
`zariskiClosedSubspace.ι` (`ι_I`); prove `zariskiClosedSubspace.range_ι` (homeomorphism onto
`V(I)`), `zariskiClosedSubspace.lift` (with factorization and uniqueness in the `∃!` statement),
`zariskiClosedSubspace.isZariskiClosedImmersion`, `zariskiClosedSubspace.denseRange`,
`zariskiClosedSubspace.ker_eq` ((e)), `zariskiClosedSubspace.congr` ((f)) and
`zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (simp: `Z_0 = X`, `Z_R = ∅`) ([Torsion] §II.2, Lemma II.2.2, p. 13, and
Remark II.2.3, p. 14; [Bhatt] §9.4, Proposition 9.4.1 (1), p. 112). *Needs:*
*intersection-of-rational-subsets*; *zariski-closed-immersion*; *perfectoid-immersion*.

Convention: `M` is J-completely flat precisely when `M ⊗_B^L B/J` is a flat
`B/J`-module in degree zero; complete faithful flatness additionally means that this
reduction is faithfully flat. Neither predicate includes completeness. The equivalent
J-power-torsion-module criterion is the supplier's §1.7. A completed tensor is
`Λ_J(M ⊗_B^L N)`. Realizations use direct-sum totalization of simplicial module models,
while Čech descent uses product totalization of cosimplicial complexes; completion is
applied to the resulting derived objects. Retain simplicial algebra models and their
multiplication through `simplicialRingCompletion`, rather than treating normalization as
a strictly commutative differential graded algebra. For discrete modules, ordinary
completion agrees with derived completion when the higher Koszul homology towers are
pro-zero; in particular a principal ideal and bounded power torsion on the module suffice
([BS22] §1.2, pp. 10–12, footnotes 5–7;
[Stacks, tag 0920](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0920)).

The additional targets below use these same carriers and units.

- `semiperfectoidFiniteIdealDescent`: for a commutative ring `B`, finite
  `J = (f₁, …, f_r)` and a J-completely faithfully flat map `E• → F•` of simplicial
  commutative B-algebras, prove effective descent for derived J-complete modules along
  its derived J-completed Čech nerve. Thus the complete module category over `E•` is
  equivalent to the limit of those over that nerve, and a complete module is recovered
  by product totalization of its completed base changes. Complete flatness is measured
  after reduction to `π₀(E•)/Jπ₀(E•)`. This is strictly more general than the supplier's
  §1.9: it permits arbitrary finite ideals and simplicial bases without a bounded-torsion
  hypothesis. Supply the derived module models over simplicial bases and their coherent
  descent data, using simplicial resolutions and quasi-isomorphisms on underlying module
  complexes. Build the adapter to compatible systems over the simplicial Koszul quotients
  on `(f₁^n, …, f_r^n)` with the supplier's module-limit models. Prove simplicial
  faithfully flat descent at each Koszul level, then take the inverse limit. On §1.9's domain,
  identify this equivalence and its augmentation with `DerivedDeRham.completeFlatDescent`
  ([BS22] §1.2, footnote 7, p. 12). Composition, completed base change and completed
  filtered colimits preserve complete flatness; complete faithful flatness is preserved
  for diagrams of covers over a fixed base, as detected by faithfully flat reduction.
- `semiperfectoidCompletionSurjectivity`: for a p-completely faithfully flat map of
  ordinary rings `B → C`, and a map `M → N` of discrete derived p-complete B-modules,
  surjectivity on `H⁰` after derived p-completed base change implies surjectivity of
  `M → N`. Use the supplier's derived Nakayama and complete-flat reduction on the
  cokernel. Degree-zero completion is right exact on connective complexes for every
  finite ideal: completing a triangle of connective complexes gives the right exact
  sequence on `H⁰` ([BS22] §1.2 and proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 62;
  [Stacks, tag 0G1U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G1U) and
  [tag 0AAJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AAJ)).
- `semiperfectoidCompletionTransfinite`: for a fixed finite ideal of `B`, derived
  completion commutes with `ω₁`-filtered colimits in `D(B)` and in simplicial B-algebras,
  compatibly with `completionUnit` and `ringCompletionUnit`. The finite-generator Koszul
  tower has countably many levels; `ω₁`-filtered colimits commute with the countable
  products in its derived-limit model. Apply this to `(p,d)` in P4.15.2 and `(p)` in
  P4.15.4 ([BS22] proof of Proposition 7.2, p. 55).

*Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §§0.1–0.4, 0.14 and 1.1–1.9 as listed above;
Mathlib `DerivedCategory`, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject` and `TensorProduct`.

The simplicial module and faithfully flat descent adapters are included in
`semiperfectoidFiniteIdealDescent` here, as in [BS22] §1.2, footnote 7.
P4.15.2–P4.15.5 consume this subsection; the transfinite constructions use P1's

**Checks.**

- For `J = (p)` and `B = ℤ_p`, completion fixes `B` in degree zero.
- The derived p-completion of `ℚ` is zero; `ℚ` is not itself derived p-complete.
- Over `ℤ_p`, the derived tensor of `𝔽_p` with `𝔽_p` has nonzero first Tor,
  so `ℤ_p → 𝔽_p` is not p-completely flat despite its flat ordinary reduction.
- Finite-ideal descent along the identity of the simplicial algebra
  `𝔽_p ⊗^L_ℤ 𝔽_p`, with `J = (p)`, retains its nonzero `H^−1`; descent does not
  replace a simplicial base by its degree-zero ring.
- For `J = (p,d)` and `B = ℤ_p[[d]]`, descent along `B → B × B` recovers every
  complete B-module with its canonical augmentation, using both ideal generators.
- For nonzero derived p-complete `M`, derived p-completed base change to `B[1/p]`
  kills `M`, so it cannot reflect surjectivity of `0 → M`; its zero reduction is not
  faithfully flat when `B/p ≠ 0`.
- Degree-zero completion sends the surjection `ℤ → ℤ/p` to `ℤ_p → ℤ/p`.
- A constant `ω₁`-filtered diagram has the identity comparison with completion.
- In the `ω₁`-filtered union of countable subsets `S` of `ω₁`, the union of the
  p-completions of `⨁_{s∈S} ℤ` is the p-completion of `⨁_{s<ω₁} ℤ`: every completed
  element has countable support.
- Countable filtered colimits alone fail: the union of `ℤ_p^n` under zero-extension
  is not p-complete; the compatible reductions of `(1,p,p²,…)` are missing.

#### P4.15.2 universal prisms and perfection

**Prisms for semiperfectoid rings.** (*semiperfectoid-universal-prism*) Develop `δ`-rings,
free `δ`-algebras, distinguished elements, and their divided-power comparison as in
[BS22] §2, restricted to the constructions below. A prism `(B, J)` has `B` a `δ`-ring,
`J` a Cartier-divisor ideal, derived `(p, J)`-complete `B`, and `p ∈ J + φ(J)B`;
bounded means `B/J` has bounded p-power torsion, and perfect means `φ` is invertible.
Prove rigidity `JB' = J'` for maps of prisms. For a bounded prism `(B,J)` and a
`(p,J)`-completely flat `δ`-`B`-algebra `D`, construct the prismatic envelope of an ideal
`K ⊇ JD` locally generated by `J` and a `(p,J)`-completely regular sequence relative
to `B`; prove its complete flatness over `B`, completed base change in bounded prisms
and compatibility with flat localization in `D`. Prove the equivalence between
perfect prisms and P1.24's integral perfectoid rings.
For any prism construct its initial perfect prism by Frobenius colimit and
`(p, J)`-completion; this construction includes the bounded-torsion comparison that
makes the completed perfection an ordinary ring ([BS22] §3, Definition 3.2,
Lemmas 3.5, 3.8–3.9, Theorem 3.10 and Proposition 3.13, pp. 28–35).

For an integral perfectoid `R`, prove that `(A_inf(R), ker θ)` is initial among prisms
with a map from `R` to their quotient ([BS22] Lemma 4.8, pp. 38–39). For a derived
p-complete quotient `A = R/K`, construct the initial prism `(Δ_init(A), (d))` with
`A → Δ_init(A)/d`: freely `δ`-adjoin `k/d` for lifts of generators of `K`, kill the
`δ`-ideal generated by d-power torsion, and iterate degree-zero derived `(p,d)`-completion
and torsion removal transfinitely until d is regular. Prove independence of the
presentation by initiality. Perfect this prism and take its quotient to construct
`semiperfectoidPerfectoidization` and its universal map ([BS22] Proposition 7.2 and
Corollary 7.3, pp. 55–56). This construction proves initiality without surjectivity.
*Needs:* P1.16–P1.18 and P1.24; P4.15.1; P0.19's cotangent and lifting API for Lemma 4.8.

**Checks.**

- For a perfect `𝔽_p`-algebra `k`, the corresponding perfect prism is `(W(k), (p))`.
- For integral perfectoid `A`, the initial prism is `(A_inf(A), ker θ)`, and its
  perfect-prism quotient recovers `A` with the identity structural map.
- For `A = 0`, the initial prism, its perfection and its quotient are zero;
  regularity is interpreted in the zero ring as well.

#### P4.15.4 André's root-adjoining cover

**Completely faithfully flat perfectoid root cover.** (*semiperfectoid-andre-cover*)
For every integral perfectoid `R`, construct a p-completely faithfully flat map
`R → R'` with `R'` integral perfectoid and every monic polynomial of positive degree
over `R'` having a root in `R'`: for `P : R'[X]`, assume `P.Monic` and `0 < P.natDegree`.
In particular every element of `R'` admits compatible p-power roots.

quasisyntomic `B/d`-algebra `C`, construct a prism `(D,dD)` with a p-completely
faithfully flat map `C → D/dD`. The prism map is completely flat, and is completely
faithfully flat if `B/d → C` is p-completely faithfully flat; these properties persist
on perfection when `B` is perfect. Build it using the root-adjoining quasisyntomic cover and the discrete
Hodge–Tate comparison of P4.15.3. Apply this to adjoining roots of all positive-degree
monic polynomials, and iterate with completed transfinite colimits to obtain `R'`

**Checks.**

- For an algebraically closed characteristic-p field, the identity is a cover with
  the asserted positive-degree monic-root property.
- The zero ring admits the identity cover, and its unique element has zero roots.
- The monic polynomial `1` has degree zero and no root over any nonzero ring. In particular,

#### P4.15.6 the Zariski-closed application

**Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed.** (*zariski-closed-is-strongly-zariski-closed*)
Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` be an affinoid perfectoid space and `I ⊆ R` an ideal. The universal perfectoid
space `Z` over the Zariski closed subset `V(I)` (P4.14) is affinoid
perfectoid, `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)`, with `R → S` surjective, `S⁺` the integral closure of the image of

Zariski closed immersion is strongly Zariski closed, and the two notions coincide.

### P4.16 comparison with the closed immersions of AdicSpaces

For a morphism `f : Y ⟶ ofPair p R` of perfectoid spaces, the reverse implication
(*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*) goes from `IsStronglyZariskiClosed p R f`

**Comparison with AdicSpaces' closed immersions.** (*adicspaces-closed-immersion-comparison*)

strongly Zariski closed if and only if it is isomorphic over `X` to the library's closed immersion
