`W` inside a chart `Spa(A, A⁺)` with ideal `J` being `V(J·O(W))`. This is the only global
identification made here. It is not PerfectoidTowers P8.14's notion of Zariski-closed embedding,
which asks for strong Zariski closedness over every open affinoid perfectoid of `X`; the two global
notions are not identified in this roadmap. (c) AdicSpaces' closed
immersion defined by a closed ideal `J` of a perfectoid `R` need not have perfectoid source: for
`R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and `J = (T)`, `R/J` is not reduced, whereas the Zariski closed subspace `V(T)` is
`Spa(C, O_C)` ([AWS] Lecture 2, Example 2.4.9). (d) That every Zariski closed immersion into an
affinoid is of the form (a) is [ECD] Theorem 5.8 (P4.15). *Needs:*
*strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*; P4.15; P4.12; AdicSpacesPartII R0.8
`AdicSpace.IsClosedImmersion`; AdicSpaces 0.6 (the open mapping theorem); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient_plus`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`,
`TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`.

Immersions are stable under base change and composition, and closed immersions are quasicompact
(*immersions-base-change-and-composition*): immersions, open immersions and closed immersions are
stable under composition and under base change along arbitrary morphisms, the image of the base
change of `f` being the preimage of `f(|Y|)`; closed immersions are quasicompact ([ECD] §5,
Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24). A surjective perfectoid quotient is a Zariski closed immersion
(*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*): for `ψ : R → S` a surjective continuous
homomorphism onto a perfectoid Tate ring, `I := ker ψ` and `S⁺` the integral closure of `ψ(R⁺)`,
the ideal `I` is closed, `(S, S⁺) ≅ Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`, and `Spa(S, S⁺) → X` is a
Zariski closed immersion defined by `I`, isomorphic to `Z_I` over `X`; thus every strongly Zariski
closed map is Zariski closed, the direction that needs the plus-ring clause ([ECD] §5, after
Definition 5.7, p. 24; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`).

`stronglyZariskiClosed_quotient_comparison` identifies a strong quotient with
`Huber.Pair.quotient` by its kernel, including the topology, plus ring and the quotient map.
The global geometric equivalence is `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`.
The composition and base-change declarations are `IsImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`,
`IsOpenImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`, `IsClosedImmersion.comp`, `.baseChange`;
`IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` gives quasicompactness.

`IsAdicClosedImmersion` expresses the adic cover-local condition of (b) on the actual `Perfd`
morphism, with the same quantifier everywhere: there exists an affinoid cover of the target such
that over each chart of that cover the source is an affinoid quotient, with the quotient topology
and the integral closure of the image as plus ring. The equivalence
`isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_locally_strong` identifies this with the existence of an affinoid
perfectoid cover on whose charts the map is strongly Zariski closed (the statement of (b)); there
is no `isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_strong`: for an affinoid target the direct comparison is (a),
whose source is supplied as an affinoid quotient, and no upgrade from a cover-local immersion into
an affinoid target to a quotient presentation over the whole target is asserted or used (see the
note after the chart condition below).
`IsAdicClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` compares the cover-local quotient condition with
P4's topological closed immersion. Checks `adicClosed_identity`, `adicClosed_empty`,
`adicClosed_principal` and `adicClosed_annulus_negative` give the identity, empty source,
a principal perfectoid quotient, and the annulus boundary that fails the quotient
condition. `isAdicClosedImmersion_iff_adicCharts` uses the complete sheafy charts
`AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.Chart` and `AdicSpace.Affinoid.map` to express R0's quotient-chart
condition on adic representatives, again as the existence of a cover by quotient charts; all
representative isomorphisms commute with the morphism being tested.

**No local-to-global upgrade is asserted.** No implication from the cover-local predicate to a global
quotient presentation over an arbitrary affinoid target is used in this roadmap. If a global closed
ideal `J ⊆ R` with image `V(J)` is supplied, P4.15 identifies the immersion with the universal
perfectoid quotient, whose kernel is `J^perf` (equal to `J` only when `J` is already perfectoid-saturated,
as the root-disc example `R/(T)` shows). PerfectoidTowers P8.14 retains its separate every-affinoid
condition (Hansen–Johansson, Definition 5.4 and the caution following it). Any further upgrade of a
cover-local immersion into an affinoid target to a global quotient would need an independent
descent theorem for arbitrary closed ideals — the restricted kernels must be identified with the
extended ideals after closure and perfectoid saturation, the locally given ideals must descend (the
obstruction lives in `H^1(X, J)`, not in the acyclicity of `O` or `O⁺`), and `J = J^perf` must be
shown — and such kernels need not be finitely generated (`ker(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K)` is a nonzero
idempotent ideal of a domain), so AdicSpacesPartIII R3.5's finite-projective glueing does not
apply; this is not deduced here from acyclicity, is not a target, and is not used to satisfy any
downstream contract. [ECD] Definitions 5.6–5.7 and Theorem 5.8, pp. 24–25,
distinguish this condition from P4's broader `IsClosedImmersion`, as does the remark
after [Berkeley] Definition 17.4.2, p. 155. The affine construction uses the pinned
quotient-pair suppliers above.

### P4.17 closed immersions versus Zariski closed immersions

**Closed immersions and Zariski closed immersions are different notions.**
(*closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed*) (a) Every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed, and
every Zariski closed immersion is a closed immersion (*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*,
*zariski-closed-immersion*). (b) The image of an immersion is stable under generalization, so a
closed subset of `|X|` that is not (the closed point of `Spa(K, K⁺)` for `K⁺` of rank two) is not
the image of any immersion: the Zariski statements do not extend to arbitrary closed subsets. (c) A
closed immersion need not be Zariski closed: for `X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` with `C` a
perfectoid field and `ϖ ∈ C` a pseudouniformizer with compatible roots, the subset
`T := ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}` (the closed annulus `{|T| = 1}` together with the rank-two point `y`
with `|T(y)| = 1⁻`) is the complement of the open unit disc, hence closed, and `ι : Z_𝒰 → X` for
`𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}}` (P4.4) is a closed immersion with image
`T`; but `T` is not Zariski closed, since every `g ∈ C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` vanishing on `T` vanishes at the
Gauss point, hence is `0` (the Gauss norm is the spectral norm), while `T ≠ X`. (d) Equivalently, a
closed immersion `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid perfectoid spaces does not force `R → S` to
be surjective ([Berkeley] Lecture 17, remark after Definition 17.4.2, p. 155). *Needs:*
*intersection-of-rational-subsets*; *perfectoid-immersion*; *zariski-closed-immersion*.

**Checks.**

- `not_isZariskiClosed_annulusClosure` (non-example) — the closed immersion `Z_𝒰 → X` of (c):
  `T = {|T| = 1} ∪ {y}` is closed, `S_𝒰 = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` (P4.4), `R → S_𝒰` is the
  (non-surjective) inclusion `C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩`, and the only `g ∈ R` with
  `|g| = 0` on `T` is `g = 0`, so `V(I) = T` has no solution `I`.
- `not_range_isImmersion_closedPoint` (non-example) — for `K⁺ ⊊ K°` the closed point `K⁺` of
  `Spa(K, K⁺)` is a closed subset that is not stable under generalization (`K°` generalizes it),
  so no immersion has image `{K⁺}`; the closed immersions into `Spa(K, K⁺)` are `∅` and the
  identity.

The Check `zariskiImmersion_annulus_negative` also tests the morphism predicate
`IsZariskiClosedImmersion` itself on this closed boundary inclusion.

### P4.18 the diagonal is an immersion

**The diagonal of a morphism of perfectoid spaces is an immersion.** (*diagonal-of-perfectoid-map*)
Let `f : Y → X` be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y` is an immersion
(P4.10). More precisely: (a) `Δ_f` is a split monomorphism, hence an injection;
(b) for open affinoids `V ⊆ Y` and `U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U`, the restriction `V → V ×_U V` is strongly
Zariski closed: the multiplication map from the affinoid ring of `V ×_U V` onto `O_Y(V)` is
surjective and `O⁺_Y(V)` is the integral closure of the image of the plus ring; (c) the open subsets
`V ×_U V` cover an open `W ⊆ |Y ×_X Y|` containing `Δ_f(|Y|)`, and `Δ_f(|Y|)` is closed in `W`, with
`|Δ_f|` a homeomorphism onto its image ([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.9, p. 25). *Needs:*
*injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *perfectoid-immersion*; *strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*;
P2.16; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`.

`diagonalMultiplication` is the map from the actual P2 tensor pair, fixed by its two
identity composites in `diagonalMultiplication_inclusions`.
`diagonalMultiplication_strong` includes both ring surjectivity and the plus-ring clause.
Checks `diagonalMultiplication_zero`, `diagonalMultiplication_identity` and
`diagonalMultiplication_two_terms` compute a zero target, the tensor over the identity,
and the sum of a left and a right scalar.

### P4.19 separated morphisms

Separatedness is the closedness of the diagonal; this subsection defines it and the next gives its
valuative criterion.

**Separated morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*separated-perfectoid-map*) With fibre products as
in P2, a morphism `f : Y → X` of perfectoid spaces is separated if its diagonal `Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y`
is a closed immersion (P4.10) ([ECD] §5, Definition 5.10, p. 25); it is
quasiseparated if `Δ_f` is quasicompact (P4.2). In Mathlib's
vocabulary, `IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion` on `Perfd`, the pattern of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`. Since `Δ_f` is always an immersion (P4.18),
`f` is separated if and only if `Δ_f(|Y|)` is closed. This is the notion that DiamondsAndVStacks
layer D3 (*immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness*) restricts to on perfectoid spaces downstream.
The adic supplier is AdicSpacesPartII R0.10's `AdicSpace.IsSeparated`, and the comparison is made
only for `f` locally of weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6), the fibre product being that of
P2.16. P4's notion lives on `Perfd` and agrees with R0.10 through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace` when the
adic representative is locally of weakly finite type and its source has stably sheafy
charts. More precisely, `isSeparated_iff_adicDiagonal` identifies `IsSeparated p f`
with closedness of the diagonal of any compatible adic representative `g : A → B`
with a self-pullback, using the representative isomorphisms and commutative square
of P4.2. R0 includes the two additional hypotheses in its predicate; P4 imposes
neither on an arbitrary perfectoid morphism ([ECD] Definition 5.10 and Proposition
5.11, pp. 25–26). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsSeparated`;
prove `isSeparated_iff_isClosed_range_diagonal`, `IsSeparated.quasiSeparated`,
`IsSeparated.of_affinoid`, `IsSeparated.of_isInjection`, `IsSeparated.comp`,
`IsSeparated.baseChange`. The identity `isSeparated_eq_diagonal` unfolds the
definition into Mathlib’s diagonal operation ([ECD] Definition 5.10, p. 25). *Needs:* *perfectoid-immersion*;
*quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps*; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`,
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.diagonal`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`; P2.16.

Analytic separatedness, a diagonal that is a Zariski-closed embedding, is a different condition,
owned by [PerfectoidTowers P8.15](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#p815-analytically-separated-perfectoid-spaces);
it and its comparison with this subsection's notion belong to P8.15 and are not used here. That
comparison has two distinct conclusions there. `PerfectoidSpace.IsAnalyticallySeparated.isSeparated`
takes a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` with both `X` and `Y` in `Perfd p` and concludes
this subsection's `IsSeparated p f`; in particular it applies over a perfectoid
field. `PerfectoidSpace.IsAnalyticallySeparated.closed_diagonal` takes
`f : X.obj ⟶ B`, analytic separation of `f`, and any chosen
`AnalyticSelfProduct p X B f`, and concludes that its diagonal is a closed
immersion. This is the representable closed-diagonal clause for v-sheaf
separatedness over an analytic base, including a nonperfectoid field
([ECD] Definition 10.7(ii)–(iii), p. 51). Its interpretation as separation of
`X^◇ → Spd(K, K⁺)` uses PerfectoidTowers' diamond comparison; the
perfectoid-base conclusion uses [ECD] Definition 5.10, p. 25.

**Checks.**

- `IsSeparated_affinoid` (computation) — every morphism `Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` of affinoid
  perfectoid spaces is separated: its diagonal is strongly Zariski closed (P4.18 (b)), hence a
  Zariski closed immersion ([ECD] §7, after Lemma 7.19, p. 37).
- `IsSeparated.of_isInjection` (degenerate) — injections, in particular identities and open
  immersions, are separated: their diagonal is an isomorphism; so is the map from the empty space
  (`Δ : ∅ → ∅`).
- `isSeparated_sum_iff` (computation) — for `Y = Y₁ ⊔ Y₂` over `X`,
  `Y ×_X Y = ⊔_{i,j} Y_i ×_X Y_j` and `Δ_Y(|Y|) = Δ_{Y₁}(|Y₁|) ⊔ Δ_{Y₂}(|Y₂|)` lies in the two
  components `Y_i ×_X Y_i`, so `Y → X` is separated if and only if both `Y_i → X` are; two
  copies of `Spa(C, O_C)` over `Spa(C, O_C)` are separated although `Y → X` is not an injection.
- `not_isSeparated_gluedDisc` (non-example) — glue two copies of the perfectoid closed disc over a
  perfectoid field `C` along the rational subset `{|ϖ| ≤ |T|}`; the result `Y` is quasiseparated
  over `Spa(C, O_C)` but not separated: for the rank-two point `y` of the disc with
  `|T(y)| = |ϖ|⁻` (in the closure of the overlap, not in it), the point `Δ_D(y)` of the chart
  `D₁ ×_C D₂ = D ×_C D` lies in the closure of `Δ_Y(|Y|)` but not in `Δ_Y(|Y|)`.

Checks `IsSeparated_identity`, `IsSeparated_empty` and `IsSeparated_affinoid` test the
three basic cases. `sumSpaceEquiv` identifies the topological coproduct through its two
inclusions; `sumPullbackEquiv` orders the four pullback components as
`(1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2)`. `sum_diagonal_four_components` places the diagonal in exactly
`(1,1)` and `(2,2)`, with the separate diagonals inside those components.
`sum_empty_left` computes the coproduct with the empty space;
`sum_disjoint_components` gives disjoint images of the two inclusions;
`sum_two_fields` gives a separated map which is not an injection.
The theorem `isSeparated_sum_iff` applies to arbitrary two maps over the same base.

`sumPullbackEquiv_coordinates` fixes both projections on each of the four components,
so the order is part of the comparison. `glueSelf X U` is the categorical pushout of
the two inclusions of the open subspace `U` in `X`; `glueSelf.fold` is induced by the
two identity maps. `glueSelf.openCharts` and `glueSelf.overlap` specify the two open
charts, their cover, and their intersection. Checks `glueSelf_whole`, `glueSelf_empty`
and `glueSelf_two_copies` compute gluing along the whole space, along the empty
space, and the two distinct copies of a point outside the overlap.
`discAnnulusOpen` is the rational overlap above, with Checks `discAnnulusOpen_gauss`,
`discAnnulusOpen_not_closed` and `discAnnulusOpen_compact`. The Check
`not_isSeparated_gluedDisc` applies quasiseparatedness and failure of separatedness to
the actual glued space and its structure map to the base field.

### P4.20 the valuative criterion for separatedness

Separatedness is detected on rank-one points of affinoid perfectoid fields.

**Valuative criterion for separatedness of perfectoid spaces.**
(*valuative-criterion-separatedness*) Let `f : Y → X` be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The
following are equivalent: (i) `f` is separated; (ii) `|Δ_f| : |Y| → |Y ×_X Y|` is a closed
immersion of topological spaces; (iii) `f` is quasiseparated and for every affinoid perfectoid
field `(K, K⁺)` and every commutative square formed by `a : Spa(K, O_K) → Y` and
`b : Spa(K, K⁺) → X` with `f ∘ a = b ∘ j` (`j : Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺)` the inclusion of the
rank-one point) there is at most one `c : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y` with `c ∘ j = a` and `f ∘ c = b`
([ECD] §5, Proposition 5.11 (i)–(iii), p. 25). *Needs:* *separated-perfectoid-map*;
*diagonal-of-perfectoid-map*; *immersions-base-change-and-composition*.

Maps from `Spa(R, R⁺)` into a separated space are determined on `Spa(R, R°)`
(*separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus*): for `f : Y → X` separated, `(R, R⁺)` any
perfectoid Tate ring with a ring of integral elements, and `a, b : Spa(R, R⁺) → Y` with
`f ∘ a = f ∘ b` and `a ∘ j = b ∘ j` for `j : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)`, one has `a = b`; for
`(R, R⁺) = (K, K⁺)` this is the uniqueness in (iii) ([ECD] §10, Proposition 10.10, p. 52).

The declarations `valuativeCriterion_separated` and `separated_unique_extension` use the
actual rank-one inclusion and the identity-ring map from the smaller to the maximal plus
ring. The first retains quasiseparatedness; the second quantifies arbitrary perfectoid
Tate pairs. `valuativeCriterion_adicDiagonal` transports the first equivalence to
closedness of the actual diagonal of a compatible adic representative `g : A → B`
with a self-pullback; its right side is P4 quasiseparatedness and uniqueness for all
`AffinoidField p` tests. AdicSpacesPartII R0.10's `AdicSpace.IsSeparated.iff_valuativeCriterion`
is the corresponding uniqueness-of-centres criterion on adic spaces (Huber 1.3.7):
it assumes analytic source and target, stably sheafy source charts, local weak finite
type, and a quasicompact diagonal. On perfectoid representatives under those hypotheses,
`isSeparated_iff_adicDiagonal` and `valuativeCriterion_adicDiagonal` identify the two
criteria with the same closed diagonal (Huber 1996, Proposition 1.3.7, pp. 52–53).
The P4 field criterion itself retains the
generality of [ECD] Proposition 5.11, pp. 25–26.

### P4.21 tilting

**Tilting of injections, immersions, separatedness and strongly Zariski closed immersions.**
(*zariski-closed-tilting*) Let `X` be a perfectoid space with tilt `X♭` and `f : Y → X` a morphism
with tilt `f♭ : Y♭ → X♭` (P2.11; `|Y| = |Y♭|`, `|X| = |X♭|`). (a) `f` is an injection, an
immersion, an open or closed immersion, quasiseparated or separated if and only if `f♭` is. (b) For
`X = Spa(R, R⁺)` and `Z = Spa(S, S⁺)` affinoid: `f : Z → X` is strongly Zariski closed if and only
if `f♭` is ([Torsion] §II.2, Lemma II.2.7, p. 15). (c) Formulas for a strongly Zariski closed `f`
with `I := ker(R → S)`, choose `ϖ♭` with sharp `ϖ`, compatible roots,
and `ϖ^p | p` in `R⁺` (and use their images in `S`): `I♭ := ker(R♭ → S♭)` is a closed perfect ideal and `I` is the closure of the
ideal generated by `♯(I♭)`; `S♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} S⁺` and `S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ` compatibly with
`R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ`; `S⁺ = {s ∈ S : |s(z)| ≤ 1 for z ∈ |Z|}`; and `|Z| = V(I) = V(I♭)` inside
`|X| = |X♭|`. *Needs:* *injection-of-perfectoid-spaces*; *perfectoid-immersion*;
*separated-perfectoid-map*; *strongly-zariski-closed-immersion*; P2.11.

Surjectivity and closed ideals with perfectoid quotient are detected on tilts
(*surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting*): for a continuous homomorphism `f : A → B` of complete Hausdorff Tate
rings with `A` perfectoid, if `B` is uniform and `f` surjective then `B` is perfectoid; if `B` is
perfectoid then `f` is surjective iff `f♭` is; and `I ↦ I♭ := ker(A♭ → (A/I)♭)` is a bijection
between closed ideals with `A/I` perfectoid and closed perfect ideals of `A♭`, with inverse `J ↦`
the closure of the ideal generated by `♯(J)` ([AWS] Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.4 and Corollaries 2.4.5–2.4.6, p. 58). Strong Zariski
closedness is characterised by almost surjectivity on plus rings
(*strongly-zariski-closed-criterion*): for `f : Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺)` a morphism of affinoid
perfectoid spaces and `T⁺` the integral closure of the image of `R⁺` in `S`, `f` is strongly Zariski
closed iff `R⁺ → S⁺` (equivalently `R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ`) is almost surjective and `S⁺ = T⁺` (almost
surjectivity of `R⁺ → S⁺` already forces `R → S` surjective, `S = S⁺[1/ϖ]`, and the converse
is *surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings*). Almost surjectivity without the
clause `S⁺ = T⁺` is strictly weaker: `Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R⁺ ⊊ R°` has `R → R` the
identity and `R⁺ → R°` almost surjective but `R° ≠ T⁺ = R⁺`, and it is not a closed immersion
(P4.13). If, however, `|Spa(S, S⁺)|` is in addition closed in `|X|`, the clause is automatic:
`Spa(S, S⁺) ⊆ Spa(S, T⁺) = V(I)` is closed, contains every rank-one point (`S⁺ ⊆ S°`), and the
rank-one points are dense in `Spa(S, T⁺)`, so `Spa(S, S⁺) = Spa(S, T⁺)` and
`S⁺ = {s : |s| ≤ 1 on Spa(S, S⁺)} = T⁺`. This is why [ECD] (after Definition 5.7) records, via
[KL15] Proposition 3.6.9 (c), that its definition agrees with [Torsion] Definition II.2.6, where
almost surjectivity is asked for a closed subset of `|X|` presented as `Spa(S, S⁺)`
([Torsion] §II.2, Definition II.2.6, p. 15; [ECD] §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24).

The ideal correspondence is `tiltIdealEquiv`. `PerfectoidQuotientIdeal` consists of
closed ideals presented as kernels of continuous surjections onto perfectoid pairs;
the Tate open-mapping theorem gives the quotient topology. `ClosedPerfectTiltIdeal`
consists of closed ideals stable under taking pth roots in the perfect tilt.
`tiltIdealEquiv_kernel` fixes the forward map on a quotient presentation, and
`tiltIdealEquiv_symm` fixes the inverse as the closed ideal generated by sharp images.
`surjective_iff_tilt` and `stronglyZariskiClosed_tilt_iff` give the map predicates.
The complete uniform-target assertion is P2's `isPerfectoid_of_denseRange` (P2.14),
applied to a surjection. The integral quotient isomorphism is P1's
`Perfectoid.tilt.sharpQuotEquiv`, with its `_apply` characteristic equation;
its `sharp_quotient_two_terms` Check supplies both addition and multiplication conventions.

Checks `perfectoidIdeal_zero`, `perfectoidIdeal_unit`, `perfectoidIdeal_reduced_quotient`
test the zero and unit ideals and exclude a nonreduced quotient.
`tiltIdeal_zero`, `tiltIdeal_unit`, `tiltIdeal_characteristic_p` compute the correspondence
at the endpoints and under the characteristic-p untilt identification.
`tilt_surjection_identity`, `tilt_kernel_zero_target`, `tilt_kernel_two_roots` compute the
identity kernel, the whole kernel for a zero target, and the sharp-generated ideal's
closure under a two-term sum, together with sharp's multiplication equation.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above: `Spa(K, K°)` as a single point and the
two-point space `Spa(K, K⁺)` for `K⁺` of rank two; the open unit disc, quasiseparated but not
quasicompact over the perfectoid closed disc; the quadratic extension `Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K)`,
bijective on points but not an injection; the closure of the annulus `{|T| = 1}` as a filtered
intersection of rational subsets and as the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski
closed; the Gauss point `η` with `K(η)⁺ = K(η)°` and `i_η` an injection that is not an immersion;
the origin `Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` as a closed, Zariski closed and
strongly Zariski closed immersion with kernel the closure of `(T^{1/pⁿ})` and not `(T)`;
`V((T − 1)) ≅ ℤ_p` with `S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)`; `Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺)` as almost surjective on
plus rings but not strongly Zariski closed; and the glued disc, quasiseparated but not separated.

## Layer P5: cofiltered limits and finite-stage étale descent

The layer builds the completed direct limit `(R, R⁺)` of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate
pairs — the `ϖ`-adic completion of the colimit of the plus rings, with `R = R⁺[1/ϖ]` — proves that
it is again a perfectoid Tate pair, and shows that `Spa(R, R⁺)` is the limit of the affinoid
perfectoid spaces `Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` in the category of perfectoid spaces, with underlying space the
inverse limit of the `|X_i|` and with every rational subset, quasicompact open and finite cover by quasicompact opens
coming from a finite stage. It then shows that no completion is needed when the index category is
`ω₁`-cofiltered, that every affinoid perfectoid space is an `ω₁`-cofiltered limit of topologically
countably generated ones, and that cofiltered limits respect cutoff cardinals. Finally it constructs
the filtered 2-colimit of a pseudofunctor of categories and proves finite-stage descent: finite
étale, quasicompact quasiseparated étale, and quasicompact separated étale objects over the limit
form the 2-colimit of those over the stages, with surjectivity, isomorphism and separatedness
recognised at a finite stage. No perfectoid base field is assumed anywhere.

### P5.1 the completed direct limit of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate pairs

The ring construction in P5.1–P5.3 depends on P1 and P2. The uses of P4 below concern
examples and the étale descent arguments in P5.10–P5.12.

`φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺` (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). No injectivity, flatness or density of the

has a pseudouniformiser in its plus ring with compatible roots and `ϖ^p | p` in that plus ring.

perfectoid ring ([BMS] Def. 3.5; [BMS] §3, Lem. 3.20, p. 26; [BMS] §3, Lem. 3.10(ii), p. 22);

morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs; its tilt `R♭` is the completed direct limit of the `R_i♭`

### P5.3 cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces

The second group passes to spaces: the limit in perfectoid spaces, its underlying space, and the

**Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces.** (*cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*)
In the standing setting let `(R, R⁺)` be the completed direct limit for a compatible
pseudouniformiser (P5.1), a perfectoid Tate pair
(P5.2), and put `X := Spa(R, R⁺)`, an affinoid perfectoid space (P2.9),

`X` is the limit in the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces, `O_X(X) = R` and
`O⁺_X(X) = R⁺`, and `X` is independent of the choices up to unique isomorphism
(see *limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice*). Morphisms into affinoid perfectoid spaces are described

### P5.8 the 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories

**The 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories.** (*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*) Let
`J` be a small filtered category and `F` a pseudofunctor from `J` (as a locally discrete
bicategory) to categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`; base change is only defined up to
canonical isomorphism, hence a pseudofunctor): categories `C_j`, functors `F_a : C_i → C_j` for
`a : i → j`, and coherent natural isomorphisms `F_{ba} ≅ F_b ∘ F_a` and `F_{id} ≅ id`. The filtered
2-colimit `2-colim_j C_j` is the category whose objects are pairs `(i, x)` with `x` an object of
`C_i`, whose morphisms are

`Hom((i, x), (j, y)) := colim_{(k, a: i → k, b: j → k)} Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y)`

(a filtered colimit of sets over the category of cospans under `i` and `j`), with composition and
identities induced from the `C_k`. It carries functors `ι_i : C_i → 2-colim C_j` and isomorphisms
`ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i`, and is the pseudo-colimit of `F`: pseudo-cocones (`G_i : C_i → D`,
`G_j ∘ F_a ≅ G_i` coherently) correspond, up to unique isomorphism, to functors
`G : 2-colim C_j → D`, together with specified comparison isomorphisms; uniqueness is
among natural isomorphisms respecting those comparisons. For a pseudo-cocone the induced `G` is faithful iff morphisms in some `C_k`
with equal images in `D` become equal in some further `C_{k'}`; full iff every morphism
`G_i x → G_j y` of `D` comes from a morphism in some `C_k`; essentially surjective iff every object
of `D` is isomorphic to some `G_i x`. In this layer `J = Iᵒᵖ`, `C_i` is a category of objects over
`X_i` and `F_a` is base change; "the base change functors induce an equivalence
`2-colim (X_i)_? → X_?`" means that the induced `G` is an equivalence. In `CategoryTheory`, define
`FilteredTwoColimit` (the category `2-colim F` with objects `Σ j, F.obj j`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ι`
(the canonical functor `ι_j : F.obj j ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompIso` (for
`a : i → j`, the isomorphism `F_a ⋙ ι_j ≅ ι_i`, compatible with the coherence isomorphisms of `F`)
and `FilteredTwoColimit.desc` (the functor `FilteredTwoColimit F ⥤ D` induced by a pseudo-cocone);
prove `FilteredTwoColimit.homEquiv` (`Hom((i, x), (j, y)) ≃` the colimit over cospans `(k, a, b)` of
`Hom_{F k}(F_a x, F_b y)`), `FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompDescIso` (`ι_i ⋙ desc G ≅ G_i`),
`FilteredTwoColimit.descUniqueIso` (any `H` with isomorphisms `ι_i ⋙ H ≅ G_i` compatible with the
cocone has a unique isomorphism to `desc G` respecting those specified comparisons), `FilteredTwoColimit.isEquivalence_desc_iff` (`desc G`
is an equivalence iff (a) `colim_k Hom(F_a x, F_b y) → Hom_D(G_i x, G_j y)` is bijective for all
`(i, x)`, `(j, y)` and (b) every object of `D` is isomorphic to some `G_i x`),
`FilteredTwoColimit.equivOfFinal` (for a final functor `u : J' ⥤ J` between small filtered categories,
`FilteredTwoColimit (F ∘ u) ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F` is an equivalence: restriction to a tail),
`FilteredTwoColimit.fullSubcategory` (if `C'_j ⊆ C_j` are full subcategories stable under the `F_a`,
then `2-colim C'_j` is equivalent to the full subcategory of `2-colim C_j` on the `(i, x)` with
`x ∈ C'_i`) and `FilteredTwoColimit.equivConst` (for the constant pseudofunctor at a category `C`,
with identity transition functors, `FilteredTwoColimit ≌ C`). Use Mathlib
`((Functor.const J).obj (Cat.of C)).toPseudofunctor'` for that constant pseudofunctor. For the filtered system of categories
of finite étale algebras over complete Tate rings `A_i`, `Hom` in the 2-colimit is the colimit of
`Hom` over common targets, and the comparison functor to finite étale algebras over the completed
colimit is an equivalence (layer P3, read through `isEquivalence_desc_iff`) ([Berkeley] Lecture 7,
Rem. 7.4.7, printed p. 54; [KL15] §1.2, Rem. 1.2.9, p. 15). *Needs:* Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`, `CategoryTheory.IsFiltered`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence`,
`CategoryTheory.Grothendieck`.

### P5.9 finite étale objects come from a finite stage

Throughout P5.9–P5.12, for a perfectoid space `Z`, `Z_ét` is the category of perfectoid spaces
étale over `Z` ([ECD] Def. 6.2; P3.18), and `Z_fét`, `Z_ét,qcqs` and `Z_ét,qc,sep` are its full
subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (P4.2), and of quasicompact
separated étale spaces; base change along `X_j → X_i` or `X → X_i` is the fibre product of
perfectoid spaces (P2.16), which preserves these classes (layer P3; P3.18).

**Finite étale objects over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces come from a finite
stage.** (*finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation*) Let `X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim_i X_i` be a
cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)`
(P5.3), with `(i₀, ϖ)` a compatible pseudouniformiser.
Then the base change functors `(X_i)_fét → X_fét` induce an equivalence of categories
`2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét` (P5.8). Ring form: base change
`S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R` (no completion; the tensor product is finite projective over `R`) induces an
equivalence `2-colim_i FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R)`, compatible with tensor products and ranks — for the
uncompleted colimit `colim_i R_i` this is AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3
(*finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit*: `2-colim FÉt(A_i) ≃ FÉt(colim A_i)` for any filtered
colimit of rings), and invariance under completion `FÉt(colim R_i) ≃ FÉt(R)` is
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5, `finiteEtale_completedColimit` (*finite-etale-completed-direct-limit*). AdicEtaleGeometry A4.5's
*finite-etale-invariance-along-tower* is its specialization to finite étale torsor towers, downstream
of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; it does not supply the arbitrary-transition case here and is not an input. What is
proved here is the perfectoid cofiltered index with its compatible pseudouniformiser and the plus
rings: the plus rings of the corresponding perfectoid spaces are the integral closures of `R_i⁺`,
`R⁺`. Explicitly, the cited equivalences say: (lifting) every finite étale `R`-algebra is
`S_i ⊗_{R_i} R` for some `i` and some finite étale `R_i`-algebra `S_i`; (uniqueness) for finite
étale `R_i`-algebras `S_i`, `S_i'`, every `R`-algebra map `S_i ⊗ R → S_i' ⊗ R` is the base change
of an `R_j`-algebra map for some `j → i`, and two `R_j`-algebra maps with the same base change to
`R` agree over some `R_k`. The theorem concerns
finite étale algebras; finitely presented algebras over `R` do not in general come from a finite
stage: for `S = {0,1}^ℕ`, `0 < |ϖ| < 1` and `f(s) = Σ_k s_k ϖ^k`, the algebra
`B = C^0(S, K)/(f)` is finitely presented but not flat. Indeed `f` vanishes precisely at the
all-zero sequence; this singleton is not open, so `(f)` is not generated by an idempotent.
A flat quotient by a finitely generated ideal would have an idempotent kernel. Every algebra
over the finite product of fields `K^{S_n}` is flat as a module, and base change preserves
flatness, so `B` cannot descend. The two-term calculation `f(0) = 0`, `f(e_n) = ϖ^n ≠ 0`, where
`e_n` has just its `n`-th digit equal to one, also shows that `f` lies in no finite stage. The algebraic input — finite étale algebras over a completed direct
limit of complete Tate rings, through the henselian approximation theorem ([Berkeley] Lecture 7, Thm 7.4.8, printed p. 54)
— is supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5 (the invariance of finite étale algebras under completed colimits); here the
completion is identified with the limit's ring and the statement is carried to spaces. Over `C^0(S, K)`
finite étale algebras are locally on `S` constant: each is an `S_n`-indexed family of finite étale
`K`-algebras tensored with `C^0(S, K)` for some `n`; and a finite étale cover of the limit is the
pullback of one at a finite stage. A specified isomorphism between two pullbacks descends,
and two lifts of that specified isomorphism agree after enlarging the stage (used
in [ECD] proof of Prop. 7.16: a splitting over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood)
([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4(i), p. 27; [ECD] §6, proof of Prop. 6.4(i), p. 27; [Sch12] §7, proof of
Lem. 7.5(i), p. 41). *Needs:* *completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs*;
*completed-colimit-is-perfectoid*; *cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces*;
*filtered-two-colimit-of-categories*; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5, P3.17, P3.14, P3.10, P2.16; layer P3;
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3 (*finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit*); Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

### P5.13.2 the Fargues–Scholze specialisations by analytic algebra

The étale specialisations of [FS] §IV.4.1, pp. 135–141, are reconstructed by analytic algebra.
The order is: tube clauses (a)–(b) give regular sequences and finite projective dimension,
which then give tube clause (c); the characteristic-`p` Jacobian criterion supplies the étale parts of IV.4.15 and IV.4.17;
pseudocoherent gluing and the integral cut-off then give the closed-image and conormal statements
used in IV.4.19. The arguments of IV.4.14, IV.4.16 and IV.4.18 involving diamonds are not inputs.
The specialisations are exactly those [ECD] 6.4(iv) uses: étale (relative dimension `0`) loci and
closed immersions of affinoid étale perfectoid spaces into rational subsets of relative balls over
affinoid perfectoid bases; the smooth cases over general sousperfectoid bases are outside this
construction.

**A perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic `p` is an algebra over a perfectoid field and a
completed colimit of `p`-finite algebras.** (*char-p-perfectoid-base-field*) Let `(R, R⁺)` be a
perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic `p` (layer P1: `R` a perfect complete
Tate ring) and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` a pseudouniformiser (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`); no base
field is assumed, it is constructed. The compatible roots `ϖ^{1/pⁿ}` of the given `ϖ`, each again
a pseudouniformiser, are `exists_pow_roots_pseudoUniformizer_charP`. Let `K := F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧` be the `t`-adic completion of
the perfection of `F_p((t))`, a perfectoid field (layer P1). Prove: (a) there is
a unique continuous ring homomorphism `K → R` with `t^{1/pⁿ} ↦ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}`, the unique `pⁿ`-th
roots in the perfect ring `R`; it is injective when `R ≠ 0` and maps `K° = F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^∧`

consequently `(R, R⁺)` is the completion of a filtered colimit of `p`-finite perfectoid affinoid

**Comparison of a graph neighbourhood with the original target and its quotient modules.**
(*graph-neighbourhood-target-comparison*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete sousperfectoid Tate pair
with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, `R ⊆ B^N_X` rational, `B = O(R)`,

étale presentation `(n, H, k, π_c)` with **exact** lifts `w ∈ (B⁺)^n`,
`π_c(v_l) = q(w_l)`. Write `Y = Spa(C, C⁺)`, `g : Y → R`,
`E = B ⊗̂_A C`, and `p : Spa(E, E⁺) = R ×_X Y → R`; `E⁺` is the completed tensor pair's
plus ring. The scalar map is `B → E`, `b ↦ b ⊗ 1`, and the graph map on rings is
`E → C`, `b ⊗ c ↦ q(b)c`. Its equations are
`h_i = T_i ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ q(T_i)` for `1 ≤ i ≤ N`. Prove:

(a) There is a finite rational cover `{U_j}` of `R` such that each member is either disjoint
from `g(Y)`, or admits a rational `W_j ⊆ Spa(E, E⁺)` containing the graph over
`Y_j := g⁻¹U_j`, for which `p|_{W_j} : W_j → U_j` is an isomorphism of adic spaces,
inducing an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs. In particular the induced scalar map
`B_j := O(U_j) → D_j := O(W_j)` is an isomorphism; this is the scalar map used to transfer
the graph resolution.
The neighbourhood `W_j` lies in a graph tube over `C` for the integral equations `h_i`,
whose Jacobian in the `T` coordinates is the identity. Choose its radius small enough that
the rational inequalities defining `R ×_X Y` are preserved by translation from the graph.

Construct these comparisons by quantitative Newton iteration, not by restriction of scalars
along `B → E`. On sufficiently small rational neighbourhoods of `g(Y)`, impose
`H(w) ∈ ϖ^m O⁺(U_j)^n` and
`ϖ^k/det J_H(w) ∈ O⁺(U_j)`, with `m ≥ 2k + 1`; take `m` larger as needed for the finitely
many rational inequalities. These conditions hold on `Y` since `H(qw) = 0` and the standard
presentation bounds the inverse Jacobian. Newton supplies `r ∈ O⁺(U_j)^n` with `H(r) = 0`
and `r − w ∈ ϖ^{m−k}O⁺(U_j)^n`, hence a pair map `C → B_j`, `π_c(v) ↦ r`.
In `p⁻¹U_j`, the rational inequalities
`|v_l − w_l| ≤ |ϖ^{k+1}|` select this branch: both `v` and the image of `r` solve `H = 0`
in that congruence class, so [*restricted-power-series-newton*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2) identifies them. Thus this
branch projects isomorphically to `U_j`. Shrink it inside a graph tube, carrying the
shrinking across this isomorphism to `U_j`. The graph is retained because Newton
functoriality along the ambient pair map to `O(Y_j)` gives `q(r) = q(w)`.
The quotient-pair hypothesis identifies `g(Y)` with the closed vanishing set of `ker q`,
so rational subsets disjoint from it complete the cover. Compactness gives a finite cover.

(b) On every rational `V ⊆ U_j`, transfer the Koszul resolution of the graph equations
through `O(V) ≅ O((p|_{W_j})⁻¹V)`. Its quotient is
`C_V := O(g⁻¹V)`, with plus ring the integral closure of the image of `O⁺(V)`.
The equation ideal is closed, the quotient has its natural Hausdorff complete topology,
and the transferred resolution and its kernel give stably pseudocoherent modules over
`B_j`. These identifications commute with rational restriction: restrict `W_j` by the
inverse image under its isomorphism with `U_j`, use [*fs-iv-4-13-regular-sequence*](#p5-13-1) (P5.13.1) on that
rational subchart, and identify both quotient maps with the given map to `C_V`.
For members disjoint from `g(Y)`, the quotient module is zero and the kernel is `B_j`.

(c) Glue these quotient modules and their kernels as sheaves on `R`. Their identifications
with `g_*O_Y` and `ker(O_R → g_*O_Y)` fix the overlap maps. Apply
[*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1) to these locally stably pseudocoherent modules, rather than
assuming that an algebraic tensor product of `C` is already complete. Global sections
are `C` and `I := ker q`, so both are stably pseudocoherent **B-modules**. For every rational
`V ⊆ R`, `B' = O(V)`, prove the algebraic comparisons

`0 → I ⊗_B B' → B' → C ⊗_B B' → 0, C ⊗_B B' ≅ C_V = B'/I B' ≅ C ⊗̂_B B'.`

The maps are multiplication and restriction, `I ⊗_B B'` identifies with the closed ideal
`ker(B' → C_V)`, and both algebraic tensor modules are Hausdorff complete for their natural

integral closure of the image of `O⁺(V)`. These assertions follow from gluing and rational
pseudoflatness after stable pseudocoherence has been obtained, and include the empty preimage.

  subset `V(t^{1/pⁿ}T^{1/pⁿ} − s^{1/pⁿ} : n)` of the perfectoid ball, which is strongly Zariski
  closed.


#### Examples for analytic approximation

The worked examples of the layer run along its build. A rational subset `Y = X(s/t)` descends to
`X_i(s_i/t_i)` for approximations `s_i, t_i` of `s, t` (Tau Ceti's perturbation of rational
subsets, `exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`), and its closed embedding is
`Tᵢ ↦ sᵢ/t` with ideal the closure of `(tTᵢ − sᵢ)` ([*affinoid-etale-zariski-closed-embedding*](#p5-13-3) (P5.13.3),
[*finite-stage-approximation-char-p*](#p5-13-4) (P5.13.4)). For a finite étale `Y`, the model from an approximated
monic presentation agrees with [ECD] 6.4(i) of layer P5. The tube of
`e = T − a` on `B¹_X` is the translation `{|T − a| ≤ |ϖ|} ≅ B¹(|ϖ|)` (*tubular-neighbourhood*),
and the perturbation of `(T − a)` to `(T − a')` with `a ≡ a' mod ϖ²` gives the identity of `A`
(*standard-presentation-perturbation*). `F = T^p − a` in characteristic `p` is rejected by the
Jacobian condition, `J_F = 0`, and a nonempty such locus is not étale ([*standard-etale-presentation*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.2),
[*jacobian-criterion-char-p*](#p5-13-2) (P5.13.2)). Over `ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, strongly noetherian, the pseudocoherent theory
reduces to Kiehl's coherent theory (AdicSpacesPartIII layer R3, Kiehl's theorem on Tate affinoids;
[*pseudocoherent-kiehl-gluing*](../AdicEtaleGeometry/README.md) (AdicEtaleGeometry A3.1)) and pseudoflatness to flatness
(*rational-localisation-pseudoflat*). The applications in [ECD] are those recorded under
[*affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv*](#p5-13-4) (P5.13.4): in the proof of Lemma 7.18, affinoid étale covers descend
to a finite level of a tower; in the proof of Lemma 7.11(i), composites of affinoid pro-étale
maps are formed via Proposition 7.10 and 6.4(iv). Alongside these sit the non-examples that fix
the definitions: the finitely presented but not 2-pseudocoherent `R/xR` over
`k[x, y₁, y₂, …]/(x·yᵢ)`, the strictly but not stably pseudocoherent quotient `A/fA` of [KL16]
Ex. 2.4.2, the non-pseudoflat `ℚ_p⟨T⟩/(T)`, the pushforward `j_*O_U` that is not pseudocoherent,
the dilation `X ↦ ϖX` that is no automorphism of `A⟨X⟩`, and the non-integral equation `(T/p)²`
for which the tube theorem fails.

### Characteristic maps and computations

The ring used for P5.1 is P1's `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit p D j₀ ϖ`;
`completedColimit` denotes that ring here and does not introduce another completion type.
`Perfectoid.plusDiagram` remembers the **chosen** plus rings. Inside the P1 ring,
`completedColimitPlus` is the topological closure of their images and
`completedColimitPair` equips the ring with that plus ring. The ring's Tate, completeness,
Hausdorff and perfectoid instances are those of P1. The comparison
`completedColimit.plusCompletionEquiv`, characterized by `plusCompletionEquiv_ι`, identifies
this subring with the adic completion of the chosen integral colimit.
`completedColimit.integralPerfectoid` states regularity and the Frobenius quotient
isomorphism, assuming `ϖ^p ∣ p` in the chosen stage plus ring. Its topology is specified
by `completedColimit.hasBasis_nhds_zero`. The construction uses the chosen `R_i⁺`
at every stage. These identifications use [ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29.
`compatible_pseudouniformizer_map` carries the plus-ring root system, its divisibility
condition and its topologically nilpotent unit along each transition; on the category
over the chosen stage these images form the compatible system.

On a tail, choose actual compatible elements `t_j ∈ R_j⁺`, with
`φ_a(t_i) = t_j` and `t_j₀ = ϖ`. `completedColimit.quotientDiagram` is the functor
`j ↦ R_j⁺/(t_j^n)`. `plusQuotientEquiv` identifies its ring colimit with `R⁺/(ϖ^n)` for
`n > 0`; `plusQuotientEquiv_ι` sends the class of a stage element to the class of its canonical
image. This is the finite-quotient statement, with the distinguished element fixed before
passing to the colimit ([Bhatt] Lemmas 5.1.1–5.1.2, pp. 33–34; [Stacks] Tag 05GG).
`adicCompletion_kernel_divisible`, `adicCompletion_separatedQuotient` and
`adicCompletion_rootClosed` state the nonseparated completion arguments; the last assumes
`q > 1`, regularity of `t`, and root closure in `A[1/t]`.
`adicCompletion_localized_density` specifies the principal neighbourhood basis after
inverting `t` and proves density of the canonical map from `A[1/t]`.
`NormedAffinoidSystem` specifies complete nonarchimedean norms defining the stage
 topologies, with the chosen plus rings as unit balls and submetric transition maps.
`ringDiagram` retains the structural ring maps. `colimitSeminorm_apply` specifies the
infimum over all representatives, and `NormedColimit` is its Hausdorff completion.
`completedColimit_test_compatibility_sch12` identifies this completion with the adic
completed colimit when the common pseudouniformizer multiplies every norm by the
same number in `(0,1)` ([Sch12] Lemma 6.13, p. 37; [KL15] Definition 2.6.1 and
Remark 2.6.3, p. 53). The comparison agrees with every stage map.

**Checks.** For each of `ringDiagram`, `NormedAffinoidSystem`, `colimitSeminorm`,
and `NormedColimit`, `_zero` gives the zero ring and zero seminorm; `_terminal`
computes the seminorm at a terminal stage and recovers that complete stage;
`_killed` makes an element killed by a transition have zero class and seminorm.

The global declarations use P2's `PerfectoidSpace.Perfd`, `IsAffinoidPerfectoid`,
`globalSections` and `globalPlus`. In `PerfectoidSpace.cofilteredLimit`, `cone` and `isLimit`
specify the limit in that category; `homeomorph_apply` specifies the compatible tuple of
points, and `pairIso_π` identifies the projections with the maps induced by
`completedColimit.ι`. `baseChangeDiagram` uses the actual pullbacks over `Over i`;
`baseChangeHomeomorph_apply` fixes every coordinate of its homeomorphism.
`sectionsDiagram` and `plusSectionsDiagram` use actual pullback homomorphisms.
`globalSections_of_isCardinalFiltered` and `globalPlus_of_isCardinalFiltered`, together with
their `_ι` equations, identify the uncompleted ring colimits when `Iᵒᵖ` is `ℵ₁`-filtered
([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29).
`globalPlusQuotientDiagram` uses compatible global integral sections `t_i`; on every
stage chart their values must be pseudouniformizers. `cofilteredLimit.plusQuotient_ι`
fixes the quotient comparison on every stage section. `cofilteredLimit.globalPlusCompletion`
gives the integral completion comparison, again fixed on every stage section. Applying it
to the rational base-change diagram supplies the completed plus-ring formula in P5.4.
`integral_sections_completion_extension` fixes the image of the adic element;
`integral_sections_localization_extension` gives the unique extension after inverting it;
`integral_sections_chart_continuous` and `integral_sections_localized_continuous` give
continuity on every affinoid chart, with the principal topology explicitly specified.

For a cofiltered diagram `S` of finite profinite sets, `profiniteFunctionDiagram` uses
precomposition on continuous functions. `cofilteredLimit_prodProfinite` identifies its
space limit with the affinoid of continuous functions on `limit S`, and its `_π` equation
identifies each projection with `profiniteProjectionMap`. The underlying topology is fixed
by `continuousFunctionSpaceHomeomorph`; its `_eval` equation sends the point obtained by
evaluation at `s` and a point `x` of the coefficient affinoid to `(s,x)` ([Sch13] end of the
proof of Lemma 4.6, p. 25; [ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29).

`tateColimit_spectrum` states the general Tate-pair result without perfectoidness,
completeness or injectivity of the stages. Its input includes compatible open rings of
definition `A_{j,0} ⊆ A_j⁺`, a compatible pseudouniformizer, and the principal-adic topology
on each `A_{j,0}`. `TateColimitModel` carries a Tate pair and a specified ring equivalence to Mathlib's algebraic ring colimit. The theorem fixes
the plus ring, the neighbourhood basis, the canonical ring maps, the homeomorphism and
finite-stage rational descent. Completion of this spectrum uses the existing Tau Ceti
completion homeomorphism ([KL15] Remark 2.6.3, p. 53; [Wedhorn] Proposition 7.48, p. 68).
`cofilteredLimit.rational_descent` states rational descent for the completed perfectoid pair.
`cofilteredLimit.finite_qcOpen_cover` descends a finite cover by compact opens as a cover
at one common stage, including the empty-cover case when the limit is empty.
The independent spectral statements are `spectralLimit_qcOpen`,
`spectralLimit_constructible`, `spectralLimit_eventual_inclusion` and
`spectralLimit_eventual_clopen`, with a specified limit cone and spectral transition maps
([Stacks] Tags 0A30 and 0A2Y).

`Perfectoid.countablePerfectoidSubrings p R ϖ` is precisely the poset `𝒮(R)` of P5.6:
closed subrings containing `ϖ` and its inverse, perfectoid for their subspace topology,
with a countable dense subset. `countableSubring_powerBounded` identifies its power-bounded
subring with the inverse image of `R°`. `countablePerfectoidHull` additionally contains the specified
countable subset and every chosen root. The directedness, covering and cardinal assertions
are `countablePerfectoidSubrings_directed`, `_cover`, `_card` and
`_isCardinalFiltered`. `countableSubringPair` takes the inverse image of the ambient plus
ring; `countableSubringDiagram`, `countableSubringCocone` and `countableSubringIsColimit`
specify the pair presentation. The projection identity of the countable-subring limit isomorphism
fixes the global comparison on all projections. `cofilteredLimit.card_colimit_lt` bounds the uncompleted integral colimit.
`cofilteredLimit.card_lt` retains one common strong-limit
stage bound `κ' < κ`; it does not infer such a bound from separate inequalities `|R_i| < κ`
([ECD] Proposition 6.5, p. 29, for the countable-subring presentation; Proposition 6.4, last clause
and first paragraph of the proof, p. 27, and Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, for the cardinal bounds).

`CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit` uses Mathlib's localization of
`Pseudofunctor.Grothendieck F` at arrows whose fibre component is invertible.
`HomRepresentative` carries a stage, two legs and a morphism between the transported
objects. Its relation compares two representatives after a common refinement, including
the pseudofunctor's composition isomorphisms. `homEquiv_symm_mk` identifies the representative
with the composite of the two transport isomorphisms and the stage morphism.
`ι_obj`, `ι_map`, `ιCompIso_id`, `ιCompIso_comp` and `ιCompDescIso_coherence` fix the
inclusions and their coherence. A cocone is Mathlib's `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans` to the
constant diagram. `descUniqueIso` fixes its comparison isomorphisms before asserting
uniqueness. `equivOfFinal_ι` specifies reindexing, and `fullSubcategory` restricts to a family
of full subcategories stable under transitions ([KL15] Remark 1.2.9, p. 15;
[Berkeley] Remark 7.4.7, p. 54). `fpModuleDiagram` uses
`Module.FinitePresentation` and Mathlib's extension of scalars, with comparison
`fpModuleColimitEquiv_ι` ([Stacks] Tag 05N7).

The geometric pseudofunctors are `finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram`, `finiteStageQcqsDiagram`
and `finiteStageSeparatedDiagram`. For every small category `I`,
diagram `X : I ⥤ Perfd p`, stage `i` and object in the indicated slice,
`finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_mapId_hom_app`,
`finiteStageQcqsDiagram_mapId_hom_app` and
`finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_mapId_hom_app` identify the unit component
with `Over.pullbackId`, after transport by `X.map_id`. For arrows
`a : j → i` and `b : k → j`,
`finiteStageFiniteEtaleDiagram_mapComp_hom_app`,
`finiteStageQcqsDiagram_mapComp_hom_app` and
`finiteStageSeparatedDiagram_mapComp_hom_app` identify the composition
component with `Over.pullbackComp (X.map b) (X.map a)`, after transport by
`X.map_comp b a`. Thus the component goes from direct pullback to successive
pullbacks and preserves the projection to the original object. The
2-morphism action is equality transport. The equivalences to the limit
categories additionally require a cofiltered index and affinoid perfectoid
stages ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(i)–(iii), pp. 27–28). Their three equivalences,
ending in `Equiv`, have `_ι`
isomorphisms identifying each stage functor with geometric base change.
`finiteStage_faithfulness`, `_fullness`, `_essentialSurjectivity`, `_separatedness`,
`_surjectivity` and `_isomorphism` state recognition with qcqs hypotheses on the actual
étale slice objects. `finiteStagePullbackIso_fst` fixes the iterated pullback used in the
fullness formula ([ECD] Proposition 6.4(i)–(iii), pp. 27–28).

### Examples

## Layer P6: `κ`-small perfectoid spaces and pro-étale morphisms

The layer builds the size and the pro-étale notions on which the pro-étale and v-sites of
DiamondsAndVStacks rest. It defines `κ`-small and uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces for an
uncountable strong limit cardinal `κ`, proves the cover criterion with its uniform bound for
singular `κ`, and proves closure under open subspaces, finite disjoint unions and tilting,
and closure of uniformly `κ`-small spaces under fibre products. It also
records the finite-stage form of ECD Proposition 6.4(iv). It then defines affinoid pro-étale
morphisms as cofiltered limits of affinoid étale ones, pro-étale morphisms as their local form,
and the product `X × S` of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set; proves that
`X_proét^aff` is the pro-category of the affinoid étale site, with its `κ`-bounded refinement; and
proves the stability of (affinoid) pro-étale morphisms under composition, base change,
cancellation, sections and small limits, that Zariski closed immersions and diagonals are
pro-étale, and the comparison with Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects. Throughout, a
perfectoid space is one of layer P2 (P2.10), locally `Spa(R, R⁺)` for a perfectoid Tate pair in
the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field; étale morphisms are those of layer
P3 (P3.15, ECD Definition 6.2); cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces are those of layer
P5 (P5.3).

### P6.1 `κ`-small perfectoid spaces

The first five subsections concern `κ`-small perfectoid spaces: the definition, its uniform variant,
the cover criterion, the closure properties and the finite-stage descent of affinoid étale objects.

**`κ`-small perfectoid spaces.** (*kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) Fix a cardinal `κ` with `ℵ₀ < κ`
that is a strong limit (`2^λ < κ` for every cardinal `λ < κ`); every cutoff cardinal of
[ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, is one, and since Mathlib's
`Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts `ℵ₀` as a strong limit, `ℵ₀ < κ` is a separate hypothesis. A
perfectoid space `X` (layer P2 (P2.10): an adic space locally isomorphic to `Spa(R, R⁺)` for a
perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)` in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field)
is `κ`-small if (i) its underlying set `|X|` has cardinality `#|X| < κ`, and (ii) for every open
affinoid perfectoid subspace `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` (so `A = O_X(U)`) the ring `A` has cardinality
`#A < κ`. Cardinalities are those of underlying sets; the plus rings carry no condition; clause
(ii) quantifies over all open affinoid subspaces, of which there are at most `2^{#|X|} < κ`, so no
separate count of charts is imposed; neither clause implies the other (a one-point space with a
large field; a disjoint union of `κ` points). The predicate is invariant under isomorphism and
monotone in `κ`; the bound in (ii) is not uniform over the charts, the stronger notion with a
single bound `λ < κ` being P6.2, and for quasicompact `X` the two agree. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `IsKappaSmall` as the structure `IsKappaSmall κ X` with the two clauses, with projections
`IsKappaSmall.card_lt` (`#|X| < κ`) and `IsKappaSmall.card_sections_lt` (`#O_X(U) < κ` for every
open affinoid perfectoid `U ⊆ X`); prove transport along `X ≅ Y`,
`IsKappaSmall.mono` (`κ ≤ κ'` carries `κ`-small to `κ'`-small), `IsKappaSmall.restrict` (open subspaces
of `κ`-small spaces are `κ`-small) and `IsKappaSmall.empty`
(for `1 < κ`); define
`KappaSmall`, the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces on the `κ`-small objects, with
the instance `KappaSmall.essentiallySmall`; the affinoid form `IsKappaSmall_affinoid κ (R, R⁺)`
is stated for an arbitrary Huber ring `R` by the three clauses `#Spa(R, R⁺) < κ`, `#R < κ` and
`#R⟨T/s⟩ < κ` for every presentation with `T` generating the unit ideal. For general Huber
rings this is a cardinal predicate, with no assertion that `R` is the ring of global sections.
For perfectoid `R`, such presentations give a rational basis, and for uncountable strong limit `κ`
these clauses are equivalent to the two clauses above and to `#R < κ` alone (P6.3 (d)). The predicate
and its monotonicity are meaningful for all cardinals; uncountability and the strong-limit
condition are hypotheses of the comparison and closure theorems. For `κ`-small `X`,
`X_proét,κ` is the category of `κ`-small perfectoid spaces pro-étale over `X` (ECD Definition 8.1),

### P6.2 uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces

**Uniformly `κ`-small perfectoid spaces.** (*uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) Let `κ` be an
uncountable strong limit cardinal. A perfectoid space `X` is uniformly `κ`-small if there is a
cardinal `λ < κ` such that `#|X| ≤ λ` and `#O_X(U) ≤ λ` for every open affinoid perfectoid
subspace `U ⊆ X`; equivalently, `X` is `κ'`-small (see *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*) for some cardinal
`κ' < κ` (take `κ' = λ⁺`, which is `< κ` because `κ` is a limit cardinal). Properties: (a)
uniformly `κ`-small implies `κ`-small; (b) a quasicompact `κ`-small perfectoid space is uniformly
`κ`-small, so the two notions have the same affinoid and the same qcqs objects; (c) if `κ` is regular
(a strongly inaccessible cardinal) the two notions agree; (d) they differ for every singular `κ`
(take `cf κ` summands), in particular for every `κ` of cofinality `ω₁` such as the cutoff
cardinals `κ(µ)` with `cf µ = ω₁` constructed in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1:
`⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°)`, with perfectoid fields `K_α` whose cardinalities are `< κ` and
cofinal in `κ` (for infinite `λ < κ` the completed perfection of `𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ)` has
cardinality between `λ` and `2^λ < κ`), is `κ`-small (`ℵ₁ ≤ 2^{ℵ₀} < κ` points, finite products of
the `K_α` as affinoid rings) and not uniformly `κ`-small. The uniformly `κ`-small spaces
satisfy the cover criterion and the stability under fibre products that ECD Proposition 4.4 states
for `κ`-small spaces (P6.3, P6.4); ECD's own set-theoretic statements (Proposition 6.4, Lemma 11.22)
are formulated with such a uniform bound `κ' < κ`, and the class is intended for the cutoff
cardinals of [ECD] Lemma 4.1, pp. 19–20, which are in general singular. In
`PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsUniformlyKappaSmall` as the predicate
`∃ λ < κ, #|X| ≤ λ ∧ ∀ U, #O_X(U) ≤ λ`, `U` ranging over the affinoid perfectoid opens; prove the
reformulation `IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ X ↔ ∃ κ' < κ, IsKappaSmall κ' X`,
`IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isKappaSmall` (a), and the statements for (b) (quasicompact `κ`-small spaces
are uniformly `κ`-small) and (c) (the two notions agree for regular `κ`), the affinoid criterion
`IsUniformlyKappaSmall κ (Spa(A, A⁺)) ↔ #A < κ`, `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.isOpen` (open subspaces,
with the same `λ`) and `IsUniformlyKappaSmall.fibreProduct` (P6.4) ([ECD] §6, Prop. 6.4, final
sentence, p. 27; [ECD] §4, proof of Lem. 4.1, p. 20, for `cf κ(ω₁) = ω₁ < κ(ω₁)`, the singular
cutoff of the separating example). *Needs:* *kappa-small-perfectoid-space*;
*complete-tate-ring-cardinality*; layer P2 (P2.8, P2.3); layer P1; Mathlib `Cardinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof_ord`, `Cardinal.IsRegular`, `Cardinal.mk_iUnion_le`.

### P6.3 the cover criterion for `κ`-smallness

**Cover criterion for `κ`-smallness.** (*kappa-small-cover-criterion*) Let `κ` be an uncountable
strong limit cardinal and `X` a perfectoid space. Prove: (a) if `X` is `κ`-small, then `X` is
covered by fewer than `κ` open affinoid subspaces `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `#A < κ` (namely by all of
them: there are at most `2^{#|X|} < κ`); (b) if `X` has a cover `{U_j = Spa(A_j, A_j⁺)}_{j∈J}` by
open affinoid subspaces with `#A_j < κ` for all `j`, then every open affinoid subspace
`U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` has `#A < κ` (the sheaf condition embeds `A` into a finite product
of rings of rational subspaces of the cover charts), so such an `X` is `κ`-small as soon as `#|X| < κ`; (c) if moreover
`#J < κ` and `sup_j #A_j < κ` — automatic when `J` is finite, or when `#J < cf κ` — then
`#|X| < κ`, and `X` is `κ`-small, indeed uniformly `κ`-small (see *uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space*);
(d) in particular an affinoid perfectoid space `Spa(A, A⁺)` is `κ`-small iff `#A < κ`, and a
quasicompact perfectoid space is `κ`-small iff it has a finite cover by open affinoid subspaces whose
rings have cardinality `< κ`; (e) the converse of (a) as printed in ECD Proposition 4.4 — a cover by
fewer than `κ` open affinoids with rings of cardinality `< κ`, without a uniform bound, implies
`κ`-small — holds for regular `κ` and can fail as soon as `cf κ ≤ #J < κ`: for `κ` of cofinality `ω₁` (such
as the cutoff cardinal `κ(ω₁)` of the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and perfectoid fields `K_α`,
`α < ω₁`, with `#K_α < κ` cofinal in `κ`, the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs
`Spa(K_α⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K_α°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is covered by `ω₁ < κ` open affinoids with rings of
cardinality `< κ` and has at least `κ` points. Part (c) needs the uniform bound, and (e) records
exactly where the printed statement needs it. These are the affinoid criterion (in Lean
`isKappaSmall_presentationLimit_iff`: for uncountable strong limit `κ`, `Spa(A, A⁺)` of a perfectoid
pair is `κ`-small iff `#A < κ`) and the cover statement (a cover by open affinoids with `#A_j < κ` and

### P6.6 affinoid pro-étale morphisms

Affinoid pro-étale morphisms are the cofiltered limits of affinoid étale ones.

**Affinoid pro-étale morphisms and pro-étale presentations.** (*affinoid-pro-etale-map*) Let
`f : Y → X` be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (layer P2 (P2.10)). `f` is affinoid pro-étale if
`Y = Spa(S, S⁺)` and `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` are affinoid perfectoid and there are a small cofiltered
category `I`, a functor `i ↦ (Y_i → X)` from `I` to `X_ét^aff` (affinoid perfectoid spaces

pseudouniformiser `ϖ` of `R`, and `S = S⁺[1/ϖ]`). The data `(I, (Y_i), the isomorphism)` is a
pro-étale presentation of `f`. The transition maps are `X`-morphisms between étale `X`-spaces and
hence étale (layer P3, P3.18); they are not required to be surjective or finite étale, which
distinguishes these presentations from those of Scholze 2013 used in AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12;

### P6.7 pro-étale morphisms

Pro-étale morphisms are the morphisms that are affinoid pro-étale locally on source and target.

**Pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.** (*pro-etale-map*) A morphism `f : Y → X` of
perfectoid spaces, over no base field, is pro-étale if for every `y ∈ Y` there are an open
neighbourhood `V ⊆ Y` of `y` and an open subset `U ⊆ X` with `f(V) ⊆ U` such that `V` and `U` are
affinoid perfectoid and `f|_V : V → U` is affinoid pro-étale (see *affinoid-pro-etale-map*); ECD's
'open subset `U`' is taken affinoid, as the restriction `f|_V` must be affinoid pro-étale. `V` and
`U` can be chosen rational inside any given neighbourhoods of `y` and `f(y)`
(see *pro-etale-local-shrinking*); `X_proét` denotes the category of perfectoid spaces pro-étale over
`X` with all `X`-morphisms, which are automatically pro-étale (see *pro-etale-stability-and-limits*),
and for `κ`-small `X`, `X_proét,κ` is its full subcategory of `κ`-small objects. Pro-étale morphisms
need not be open nor locally of finite type; being pro-étale is local on the source and, for open
covers, on the target, but not local on the target for the pro-étale topology. This is neither
Mathlib's pro-étale site of a scheme (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`, defined by weakly étale
maps) nor Scholze 2013's `X_proét` of a locally noetherian adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry
A1.12). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `IsProEtale` as the structure above and `ProEtaleOver` as
`X_proét`, with the instance `ProEtaleOver.hasPullbacks` (fibre products, computed in perfectoid
spaces); prove `IsProEtale.of_isAffinoidProEtale`, `IsProEtale.of_isEtale` (étale maps are
pro-étale, *pro-etale-local-shrinking*), `IsProEtale.of_openCover` (if `X = ⋃ U_α` and every
`f⁻¹(U_α) → U_α` is pro-étale then `f` is), `IsProEtale.restrict` (`f|_V : V → U` for open `U ⊆ X`,
`V ⊆ f⁻¹(U)`), `isProEtale_iff_exists_rational` (rational `V ∋ y`, `U ∋ f(y)` with `f(V) ⊆ U` and
`V → U` affinoid pro-étale), `IsProEtale.comp`, `IsProEtale.baseChange`, `IsProEtale.of_comp`
(see *pro-etale-stability-and-limits*) and `IsProEtale.diagonal` (see *diagonals-are-pro-etale*) ([ECD] §7,
Def. 7.8(ii), p. 32; [Berkeley] Lecture 8, Def. 8.2.1, p. 57, the same definition; [Berkeley]
Lecture 8, after Prop. 8.2.5, p. 59, the failure of locality for the pro-étale topology). *Needs:*

### P6.8 the product with a profinite set

Products with infinite profinite sets supply affinoid pro-étale maps that are not étale.

**The product `X × S` of an affinoid perfectoid space with a profinite set, and its relative form
`X ×_{S₀} S`.** (*product-with-profinite-set*) Let `X` be an affinoid perfectoid space,
`φ : |X| → S₀` a continuous map to a profinite set and `S → S₀` a continuous map of profinite sets.
Write `S → S₀` as a cofiltered limit of maps of finite discrete sets `S_k → S₀,k` (`k ∈ K`)
compatible with `S → S₀` (Mathlib `Profinite.asLimit`, `DiscreteQuotient`). Each
`φ_k : |X| → S₀,k` is locally constant, so `X = ⊔_{t∈S₀,k} X_{k,t}` with `X_{k,t} := φ_k⁻¹(t)` open
and closed, hence a rational subset cut out by an idempotent of `O(X)` (`O_X` is a sheaf, layer P2
(P2.8)); `X ×_{S₀,k} S_k := ⊔_{s∈S_k} X_{k,image(s)}` is affinoid perfectoid and affinoid étale over
`X`. Define `X ×_{S₀} S := lim_k X ×_{S₀,k} S_k` (limit in perfectoid spaces, layer P5 (P5.3)), and
`X × S := X ×_∗ S = lim_k X × S_k`. Prove: (a) for every perfectoid space `T` over `X`,
`X`-morphisms `T → X ×_{S₀} S` correspond to continuous maps `|T| → S` over `S₀`, so the
construction is independent of the presentation and functorial in `S → S₀`; (b)
`X ×_{S₀} S → X` is affinoid pro-étale with the above pro-étale presentation; (c)
`|X ×_{S₀} S| = |X| ×_{S₀} S`; (d) `O⁺(X × S) = C⁰(S, O⁺(X))` and `O(X × S) = C⁰(S, O(X))`,
continuous maps for the `ϖ`-adic topology on `O⁺(X)` (for `X = Spa(K, O_K)` this is ECD's
`Spa(C⁰(S, K), C⁰(S, O_K))`); (e) for a morphism `T → X`, `T ×_X (X ×_{S₀} S) = T ×_{S₀} S`; (f)
`(X × S)♭ = X♭ × S`; (g) for `S` locally profinite, `X × S` is glued from the `X × S_c` over the
compact open subsets `S_c ⊆ S` and is pro-étale, not affinoid unless `S` is compact, over `X` when `X` is nonempty; for `X = ∅` the product is empty for every `S`.
For nonempty `X` and infinite profinite `S`, `X × S` is not the disjoint union of `#S` copies of `X`. The same construction
`S × X := lim ⊔_{s ∈ S_j} X`, with `|U × S| = |U| × S` and `Hom(V, U × S) = Hom(V, U) × C(|V|, S)`,

noetherian adic space; here the carrier is the category of perfectoid spaces over an affinoid
perfectoid `X` with ECD's limit, and the relative form `X ×_{S₀} S` is added. In `PerfectoidSpace`,
define `prodProfinite` (`X × S`) and `fibreProdProfinite` (`X ×_{S₀} S`) with the projection

`prodProfinite.homeomorph` (`|X × S| ≃ₜ |X| × S`),
`fibreProdProfinite.homEquiv` (`Hom_X(T, X ×_{S₀} S) ≃ {continuous |T| → S over S₀}`),

affinoid pro-étale `Y = lim Y_i` and `Z = lim Z_j` over `X`,
`Hom_X(Y, Z) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j)` ([ECD] §7, Prop. 7.10, p. 33; [ECD] §7, proof of

### P6.11 Zariski closed equals strongly Zariski closed

**Zariski closed equals strongly Zariski closed.** (*zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed*)
For an affinoid perfectoid space `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` and a morphism `f : Z → X` of perfectoid spaces,
`f` is a Zariski closed immersion if and only if `f` is strongly Zariski closed: the direction
strongly Zariski closed ⇒ Zariski closed, the case of an already given surjective perfectoid
quotient `R → S`, is P4.16 (*strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed*), and the direction
Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed is ECD Theorem 5.8, proved in P4.15 through the
perfectoidisation of semiperfectoid rings ([BS22] Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, via surjectivity of
perfectoidisation). Apply `stronglyZariskiClosed_iff_zariskiClosed`
from P4.15 to obtain the consequences for the pro-étale calculus below. Their completed
character-algebra application is given by `CharacterCompletion.fourier_surjective` and
`fourier_kernel_nontrivial`, with the coefficient conventions below. For every ideal `I ⊆ R`
the map `R → S_I` (layer P4 (P4.14)) is surjective with
kernel `I^perf = {h : |h| = 0 on V(I)}`, `S_I⁺` is the integral closure of the image of `R⁺`, and
`R⁺ → S_I⁺` is almost surjective. For `R = ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` and `I = (T − 1)` this gives
`R ↠ C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)` (Fresnel–de Mathan), contradicting Scholze's Remark II.2.4 and Bhatt's
Warning 9.4.2. The kernel is strictly larger than `(T − 1)`: writing `f = Σ_a c_a T^a`
(`a ∈ ℤ[1/p]`, `c_a → 0`), `(T − 1)R` is the set of `f` with `Σ_{k∈ℤ} c_{a+k} = 0` for every
`a`, the inverse being `d_a := Σ_{k≥1} c_{a+k}` with `‖d‖ ≤ ‖c‖`, so `(T − 1)` is closed and
`R/(T − 1) = ℂ_p⟨μ_{p^∞}⟩` (the `c_0`-completed group algebra, `T^{k/pⁿ} ↦ [ζ_{pⁿ}^k]`); the
element `Σ_{ζ∈μ_{pⁿ}} [ζ]` of norm `1` maps to the function `pⁿ·1_{pⁿℤ_p}` of norm `|p|ⁿ`, so
the surjection `ℂ_p⟨μ_{p^∞}⟩ → C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)` is not bounded below and, by the open mapping
theorem, has a nonzero kernel `I^perf/(T − 1)`, consisting of elements of spectral norm `0`.
**Checks for the coefficient and character conventions.**

- `division_by_T_sub_one` — in the rational unit-annulus pair of `discPair`, take
  `T = rationalMap (rootX 0)`. The coefficients `c₀ = −1`, `c₂ = 1`, zero elsewhere,
  give `d₀ = d₁ = 1` by the positive-index tail formula, and their images satisfy
  `(T − 1)(d₀ + d₁T) = c₀ + c₂T²` in this pair's ring.
- `two_character_sum` — `finiteFourier 2 1 (-1)` sends `[0]+[1]` to the values `2,0`.
  The image has norm `1/2` and the group-algebra coefficient norm is `1`.
  These are computations from the coordinate and character formulas in this subsection.

The finite group-algebra restriction of the character map is `finiteFourier`: for a primitive
`pⁿ`-th root `ζ`, it sends `[a]` in `C_p[Z/pⁿ]` to `b ↦ ζ^{ab}` and coefficients to constant
functions. Its coefficient norm is the maximum of the coefficient norms; its target uses the
supremum norm on functions on the finite group. This is the finite-level part of the completed
map above; `fourier_surjective` states surjectivity of the completed map.

**Checks for the Fourier map.**

- `fourier_two_character_norm` — for `p=2`, `n=1`, `ζ=-1`, the group-algebra element
  `[0]+[1]` has coefficient norm `1`; its image takes values `2,0` and has norm `1/2`.
- `fourier_constant` — `c[0]` maps to the constant function `c` at every level.
- `fourier_level_zero` — at level `0`, the group is trivial and the map returns the sole
  coefficient. These are direct computations from the displayed character formula.

The completed carrier `CharacterCompletion` is a complete normed `C_p`-algebra with a dense
algebra map from `C_p[μ_{p^∞}]` whose norm is exactly the coefficient maximum. Here
`pPowerRoots` uses the union of Mathlib's `rootsOfUnity` subgroups. The continuous character
`pPowerCharacter` is fixed by `ζ ↦ (x ↦ ζ^(x mod pⁿ))` whenever `ζ^(pⁿ)=1`.
`CharacterCompletion.fourier_single` fixes the completed transform on the dense group algebra;
`fourier_surjective` and `fourier_kernel_nontrivial` state the completed comparison above.

**Checks for the completion and its characters.**

- `completedFourier_zero` and `completedFourier_constant` — zero maps to zero and `c[1]`
  maps to the constant function `c`.
- `completedFourier_two_characters` — in the completed algebra at `p=2`, `[1]+[-1]`
  has norm `1`, while its Fourier transform takes values `2,0` at `0,1` and has norm `1/2`.
- `completion_distinct_coefficients` — `[ζ]-[η]` has coefficient norm `1` for distinct roots.
- `pPowerRoots_one`, `pPowerRoots_minus_one_two`, `pPowerRoots_two_not_root` — the identity
  is a root, `-1` is a two-power root, and `2` is never a root of unity in `C_p`.
- `pPowerCharacter_at_zero`, `pPowerCharacter_one`, `pPowerCharacter_minus_one` — every
  character is `1` at zero, the identity root gives the constant character, and at `p=2`
  the character of `-1` takes values `1,-1` at `0,1`.

#### Presentation examples

For `(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, the tower of finite Galois extensions has uniform completion `ℂ_p`.
Its profinite limit group `G` gives `ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p ≅ C^0(G, ℂ_p)` and
`|Spa ℂ_p|/G = |Spa ℚ_p|`. For `(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)`, the completed tower is
perfectoid although the original ring is not: approximate p-power roots of `T`
modulo `ϖ^p` exist in its power-bounded subring. The incomplete ring `ℚ_p[T]`
illustrates the completeness hypothesis. A perfectoid pair has the trivial
presentation with `G = 1`.

## Layer P7: tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers

The layer builds tilde-limits `X ~ lim_i X_i` of analytic adic spaces and their perfectoid form,
the residue-field variant of Scholze's perfectoid paper, and the good affinoid perfectoid subsets
through which a tilde-limit is computed at a finite level; Frobenius-controlled integral towers
with their completion, the uniformity bound and the perfectoid Frobenius criterion that makes their
completed generic fibre a perfectoid tilde-limit; preperfectoid spaces and the strong completion;
cofinality witnesses for towers indexed by compact open subgroups; the uniqueness and
representability of perfectoid tilde-limits, their comparison with inverse limits of represented
functors (the comparison with diamonds belongs to DiamondsAndVStacks), their restriction to opens
and rational subsets, étale and finite étale base change and gluing; the limit of a tower of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps; the
comparison of étale topoi along a tilde-limit of noetherian adic spaces; and the regular finite flat
towers of Česnavičius whose completion is perfectoid. AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 owns the intrinsic
tilde-limit relation; this layer adds the perfectoid specialisations.

### P7.1 tilde-limits of analytic adic spaces

**Tilde-limits of analytic adic spaces.** (*tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*) Let `I` be a
small cofiltered category, `(X_i)_{i ∈ I}` a diagram of analytic adic spaces (the Foundations of
adic spaces roadmap (AdicSpaces), layer 5) whose transition maps are quasicompact and
quasiseparated, and `X` an analytic adic space with compatible morphisms `φ_i : X → X_i`. Two
separate conditions: (T) the continuous map `|X| → lim_i |X_i|` is a homeomorphism; (D) every
`x ∈ X` has an open affinoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` such that, writing the morphisms
`U → X_i` through open affinoid subspaces `Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ⊆ X_i`, the union over `i` of the images
of `A_i → A` is dense in `A`. `X ~ lim_i X_i` (`X` is a tilde-limit of the `X_i`) means (T) and (D).
Neither `X` nor the `X_i` is required to be quasicompact or locally noetherian; the perfectoid
tilde-limits of P7.2 are the tilde-limits whose `X` is perfectoid. AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1 owns the
intrinsic relation `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` with its affinoid criterion
(*tilde-limits-affinoid-criterion*: `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.affinoid` and the completed-direct-limit
criterion, the latter specified in AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's README only); P7.1 uses only this sub-target. The base change
`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.baseChange` (*tilde-limit-base-change*, AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.2) is used in P7.12.
P7 specializes the intrinsic relation to analytic Yoneda carriers.
Here `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` expresses its analytic Yoneda form (the
predicate (T) and (D) on `X`, the system and the cone); prove `IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (the
homeomorphism `|X| ≃ lim_i |X_i|`) and `IsTildeLimit.dense_image` (the density clause (D) at every
point) ([SW13] §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20, which does not require the spaces to be analytic).
The comparison with the arbitrary-open density condition of [Huber96] §2.4,
Definition 2.4.2, p. 125 is `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.toHuber` in P7.2. *Needs:* AdicSpaces
layer 5; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `TopCat.limitCone`, `Dense`.

**Comparison with the intrinsic supplier.** `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofAdicSpace_iff`
states, for a small cofiltered diagram `D : I ⥤ TauCeti.AdicSpace` and cone `c`,

`AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit (D ⋙ ofAdicSpace) (ofAdicSpace.mapCone c)   ↔ AdicSpacesPartII.AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit D c.`

Its hypotheses are analyticity of `ofAdicSpace.obj c.pt` and of every
`ofAdicSpace.obj (D.obj i)`, and `AdicSpace.Qcqs (ofAdicSpace.map (D.map a))`
for every transition `a`. Honesty follows from the `TauCeti.AdicSpace` carriers.
Neither compactness of the levels nor a perfectoid apex is assumed. These
extra analytic and transition hypotheses belong to P7's Yoneda form; the
PartIV relation itself imposes only topology and density. Transport identifies
the point maps with the same cone projections and identifies sheafy affinoid
charts and their ring maps ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20; AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1).

- `IsTildeLimit_ofAdicSpace_nonanalytic` — the intrinsic relation holds for the

  fails. Thus the analytic hypothesis in the equivalence is essential.
