The affinoid predicate is evaluated on the ring maps `B.map` and `b.ι.app`.
Its conclusion is `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit (B.op ⋙ S) (S.mapCone b.op)`, where `S`
is the lift of `spaYFunctor` to `YonedaAdicSpace`: the apex is `ofSpaY b.pt`, and the
projection to `ofSpaY (B.obj j)` is induced by `b.ι.app j`. Thus (T) uses these precise
maps and (D) is witnessed by the whole affinoid chart. Maps between these affinoids
are qcqs; no separate transition hypothesis is needed. This is the analytic Yoneda
comparison with AdicSpacesPartII R0.20.1's `IsTildeLimit.affinoid`, not another intrinsic
criterion ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

The global carrier of this analytic tilde-limit is the Yoneda-adic category supplied by
AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16, into which perfectoid spaces embed through `YonedaAdicSpace.ofAdicSpace`.
`YonedaAdicSpace.IsAnalytic` means a cover by Tate affinoids ([Berkeley] Definition 4.3.2,
printed p. 33). Affinoid sheafiness is AdicEtaleGeometry's `R.Sheafy` for an object `R` of `CAff`, namely Tau
Ceti's `IsSheafyForEveryPresentation` on the plus ring. `AdicSpace.IsHonest` means that every point
lies in an open affinoid chart satisfying this predicate; the same predicate supplies the
finite-level hypothesis of `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.isTildeLimit` and the sheafiness
hypotheses of `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` and `IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace`.
**Checks.** `IsHonest_empty` holds for an empty point space; `IsHonest_sheafy_affinoid`
holds for `ofSpaY R` given `R.Sheafy`; `IsHonest_perfectoid` holds for every
`PerfectoidSpace.Perfd p`, using its sheafy perfectoid charts (P2.6).
Both the source and the levels of `IsTildeLimit` are analytic and honest. `Qcqs` tests inverse
images of affinoid open charts for quasicompactness and quasiseparatedness. `chartImage` includes
all finite-level affinoid factorizations, with their ring maps. `HasDenseCharts` imposes
density on an open cover. The homeomorphism is fixed by
`IsTildeLimit.homeomorph_apply`: its coordinates are the cone maps. For initial reindexing,
analyticity, honesty and qcqs transitions of the original diagram remain hypotheses ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

### P7.2 perfectoid tilde-limits

The next three subsections fix the perfectoid form of the tilde-limit, the residue-field variant of
Scholze's perfectoid paper, and the good affinoid perfectoid subsets through which a tilde-limit is
computed at a finite level.

**Perfectoid tilde-limits `X ~ lim X_i` of analytic adic spaces.** (*perfectoid-tilde-limit*) Fix a
prime `p`. Let `I` be a small cofiltered category, `i ↦ X_i` a functor from `I` to analytic adic
spaces (AdicSpaces layer 5: every point analytic, sheafy) whose transition morphisms
`f_a : X_j → X_i` (`a : j → i`) are quasicompact and quasiseparated, `X` a perfectoid space in the
sense of P2.10 ([ECD] Definition 3.19: locally `Spa(R, R⁺)` with `R` a perfectoid Tate ring in the
sense of [ECD] Definition 3.1, of characteristic `0` or `p`, no base field; sheafy by P2.6), and
`φ = (φ_i : X → X_i)_i` a compatible family of morphisms of adic spaces (`f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i`). The
pair `(X, φ)` is a perfectoid tilde-limit of `(X_i)`, written `X ~ lim_i X_i`, if it is a
tilde-limit in the sense of *tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*, i.e. (a) the continuous map
`|X| → lim_i |X_i|` into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`)
is a homeomorphism, and (b) every `x ∈ X` has an open affinoid neighbourhood `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X`
such that the union, over `i ∈ I` and over open subsets `V ⊆ X_i` with `φ_i(U) ⊆ V`, of the images
of the restriction maps `O_{X_i}(V) → A` is dense in `A`. Conventions: (i) the index category is
cofiltered and only the transition maps, not the `X_i`, are required to be quasicompact and
quasiseparated; (ii) no perfectoid base field is fixed: the `X_i` may be of characteristic `0` or
`p`, and `X` may lie over a different base than the `X_i` ([CHJ] Theorem 2.8: the `X_i` over `Q_p`,
`X` perfectoid; Scholze's universal cover of an affinoid over `Q_p` with limit over `C_p`); (iii)
the two conditions (a) and (b) are independent and both are required (the checks
`isTildeLimit_test_density_needed` and `isTildeLimit_test_topology_needed`); (iv) a tilde-limit is
not a categorical limit in adic spaces: `X ~ X_0` may hold with `X ≇ X_0` ([SW13] §2.4, after
Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20). Equivalent forms of (b), used throughout the layer: (b′) there is an
open cover of `X` by affinoids `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` for which `colim_{(i, V)} O_{X_i}(V) → A` has dense
image, `V` running over open affinoids of `X_i` through which `U → X_i` factors ([SW13] §2.4,
Definition 2.4.1, p. 19); (b″) the same with `U` affinoid perfectoid and `V` a quasicompact open at
one level (the good affinoid perfectoids of P7.4; [Survey] §2, Definition 2.20 and Remark 2.21,
p. 11). The equivalences (b) ⇔ (b′) ⇔ (b″) given (a) are *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*. Only the
density clause is formulated with sections; the weaker residue-field variant of [Sch12] Definition
7.14 is P7.3. In `PerfectoidSpace`, abbreviate `IsTildeLimit` by `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` on the underlying
adic spaces, `IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (`|X| ≃ lim_i |X_i|` induced by `φ`) and
`IsTildeLimit.dense` (every `x ∈ X` has an affinoid open neighbourhood `U` with
`⋃_{i, V ⊇ φ_i(U)} im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U))` dense in `O_X(U)`, with `U` sheafy);
prove `IsTildeLimit.toHuber`: for a perfectoid apex `X`, honest analytic levels `X_i`,
qcqs transition maps, and qcqs point spaces of `X` and every `X_i`, the perfectoid
predicate is equivalent to Huber's two conditions. The first is a homeomorphism
induced by the cone projections; the second uses sections on arbitrary opens, as
specified by `PerfectoidSpace.openChartImage` below. Huber's setting is qcqs
pseudo-adic spaces and adic morphisms ([Huber96] §2.4.1 and Definition 2.4.2, p. 125);
this comparison concerns honest analytic adic spaces, regarded as pseudo-adic
spaces with their full point spaces. Morphisms between these analytic spaces are
adic (AdicSpacesPartII R0.1, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing`). Prove also `IsTildeLimit.iff_goodCover` (`X ~ lim X_i`
iff (a) holds and `X` is covered by good affinoid perfectoids; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*),
`IsTildeLimit.lift` (for a perfectoid space `Y`, compatible maps `ψ_i : Y → X_i` factor uniquely as
`φ_i ∘ g`; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*), `IsTildeLimit.uniqueIso` (two perfectoid
tilde-limits of the same system are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the cones),
`IsTildeLimit.ofIso` (transport along an isomorphism `X ≅ X'` commuting with the cones),
`IsTildeLimit.open_baseChange` (restriction to the preimage of an open subset at a finite level;
*tilde-limit-rational-restriction*), `IsTildeLimit.reindex` (invariance under an initial change of
index category; *tilde-limit-cofinal-change*), `IsTildeLimit.const` (the constant system on a
perfectoid space with the identity cone is a tilde-limit) and `IsTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (if all
`X_i` are qcqs, `|X|` is a spectral space and each `φ_i` is a spectral map; [Sch12] §7, Remark 7.15,
p. 44; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons) ([SW13] §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20). *Needs:*
*tilde-limit-of-analytic-adic-spaces*; P2.10; P2.6; Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `TopCat.limitCone`.

**Checks.**

- `isTildeLimit_test_perfectoidDisc` (computation) — for an integral perfectoid ring `S`,
  a regular parameter `π`, `π`-adic completeness and `π^p ∣ p`, the generic cone of
  `FrobeniusTower.disc S π hπ hp` satisfies the global `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
  Its stages are the completed disc algebras with transition `T ↦ T^p`.
- `isTildeLimit_test_perfectoidTorus` (computation) — for a complete nonarchimedean
  perfectoid normed field `K` of characteristic zero, topologically nilpotent `p`,
  `PseudoUniformizerRoots p K`, and compatible primitive `p^n`-th roots of unity,
  the torus tilde-limit is `K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` with transitions `T ↦ T^p`.
  The example uses `FrobeniusTower`: each integral stage is the completion of
  `K°[T, T⁻¹]` along `ϖ`, the transitions fix coefficients and raise `T` to its
  `p`-th power, and the completed generic cone satisfies `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit`.
  The projection pulls the level-`n` coordinate back to `T^{1/p^n}`.
  This existence statement holds without choosing roots of unity; with compatible
  primitive roots, [`PerfectoidTowers.Perfectoid.TorsorDescent.rootTorusTower_exists`](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p9-continuous-torsor-descent-with-coefficients)
  equips it with the Galois action downstream (not an input here) ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23,
  and Lemma 4.10(iii–iv), pp. 26–27).
- `isTildeLimit_test_empty` (degenerate) — the identity cone on a zero perfectoid
  pair is a perfectoid tilde-limit. Together with `isTildeLimit_test_const` and the global
  `isTildeLimit_test_density_needed`, this tests the global predicate itself.
- `isTildeLimit_test_const` (degenerate) — for a perfectoid space `X` and the constant system
  `X_i = X` (`I` the one-object category) with `φ = id`, `X ~ lim X_i`; more generally any
  isomorphism `X ≅ X_0` of adic spaces with `X` perfectoid exhibits `X ~ X_0`.
- `isTildeLimit_test_not_categorical` (non-example) — set `K = C_p`. The quotient
  `φ : K[ε]/(ε²) → K` satisfies the single-affinoid predicate `IsTildeLimit_affinoid`
  for the one-object diagram, while `φ` is not injective. Thus this affinoid
  tilde-limit condition does not force the cone map to be an isomorphism.
  The pair on `DualNumber C_p` has plus ring `O_{C_p} + C_p ε`, and `φ(a + bε) = a`.
  Its product topology has ring of definition `O_{C_p} ⊕ O_{C_p} ε`.
  Every valuation kills `ε`, so the map on spectra is a homeomorphism of one-point
  spaces; the coefficient map is surjective and kills the nonzero element `ε`.
  This concretely illustrates the distinction following [SW13] Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20.
- `isTildeLimit_test_density_needed` (non-example) — the point `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})` with its map to
  the constant system `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` satisfies (a) (both spaces are one point) but not (b) (`Q_p`
  is not dense in `C_p`); (a) alone does not define tilde-limits.
- `isTildeLimit_test_topology_needed` (non-example) — for a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring `R` and
  `X = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)`, mapping `X` into the first summand of `X_n := D_n ⊔ D_n`
  (`D_n = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)`) satisfies (b) but not (a) (`|X| → lim |X_n|` misses the second
  summand); (b) alone does not define tilde-limits. The example uses `FrobeniusTower.disc`
  for an integral perfectoid ring `S`, a regular nonunit `ϖ`, `ϖ`-adic completeness and
  `ϖ^p ∣ p`. Natural first and second inclusions, with a binary coproduct at every level,
  specify the doubled diagram. The first-summand cone has `AdicSpace.HasDenseCharts` and
  an embedding on points, but misses a compatible family in the second summands; it
  therefore fails the global `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit` predicate. The nonunit
  hypothesis excludes the empty generic fibre ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).
- `isTildeLimit_test_huber_compat` (compatibility) — for a perfectoid `X`, honest analytic
  `X_i`, qcqs transitions, and qcqs `X` and `X_i`, `IsTildeLimit.toHuber` identifies the
  perfectoid predicate with the projection-compatible homeomorphism and arbitrary-open
  section density of [Huber96] Definition 2.4.2, p. 125.

`PerfectoidSpace.openChartImage D c R u` is the subset of `R.A` obtained from
sections on all finite-level opens: choose `i`, an open immersion `v : V → D_i`,
and a factorization `f : Spa^Y(R) → V` with `f ≫ v = u ≫ φ_i`. A coefficient `r`
belongs to the image exactly when some `s : globalFunctions V` pulls back to
`toGlobalFunctions R r`. For sheafy `R`, this is the image in `O_X(U) = R.A`;
`V` need not be affinoid or quasicompact. These are the sections in [Huber96]
Definition 2.4.2(b), p. 125, using AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16's `globalFunctions`,
`globalFunctions.map`, `toGlobalFunctions`, and `IsOpenImmersion`.
`IsTildeLimit.dense` gives this density without requiring qcqs total spaces.

**Checks for `openChartImage`.**

- `openChartImage_constant` — the identity cone on `Spa^Y(R)` has image all of `R.A`,
  since the whole finite-level open and its identity restriction supply every coefficient.
- `openChartImage_zero` — for a zero coordinate ring and any chart map into a cone
  over a cofiltered category, the image is `{0}`; the index category is nonempty.
- `openChartImage_nondense` — for the constant `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` system with apex
  `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p})`, even sections on arbitrary opens have nondense image in `C_p`.
  The only nonempty open of the finite-level point is the whole point.

The predicate `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit p D c` records that `c.pt` is perfectoid and
that `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit D c` holds. Thus its topology and density are exactly those of P7.1.
`IsTildeLimit.lift` quantifies over every perfectoid source and every compatible cone, and
`uniqueIso` requires compatibility with every projection ([SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21).

### P7.3 residue-field tilde-limits

**Residue-field tilde-limits `X ~′ lim X_i` over locally noetherian adic spaces.**
(*residue-field-tilde-limit*) Let `I` be a small cofiltered category, `(X_i)` an `I`-indexed system
of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII R0.6:
covered by `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `A` a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring; the transition maps are
then automatically qcqs), `X` a perfectoid space and `φ = (φ_i : X → X_i)` a compatible family.
Then `X ~′ lim X_i` (Scholze's notation `X ~ lim X_i` of Definition 7.14, written `~′` in [SW13]
after Theorem 2.4.7) means: (a) `|X| → lim_i |X_i|` is a homeomorphism, and (c) for every `x ∈ X`
with images `x_i = φ_i(x)`, the map of completed residue fields `colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^` has dense
image, where `k(y)^` is the completion of the residue field of `O_{Y,y}` for the valuation of `y`
(equivalently, `colim_i k(x_i) → k(x)` has dense image for the valuation topologies). No perfectoid
base field is fixed ([Sch12] works over a perfectoid field `K`; the definition and the results of
P7.15 use only that `X` is perfectoid and the `X_i` are qcqs locally noetherian); by Remark 7.15,
(a) forces `|X|` to be spectral, in particular `X` quasicompact and quasiseparated. The density
condition is pointwise on residue fields; the sectionwise condition of P7.2 implies it
(see *tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit*). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit` (the structure with fields `homeomorph` and `residueField_dense`),
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.homeomorph` (`|X| ≃ lim |X_i|`) and
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.residueField_dense` (for every `x`, `colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^` has dense
image); prove `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (`|X|` is spectral and `X` is qcqs; Remark
7.15), `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_isTildeLimit` (every tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian
`X_i` is a residue-field tilde-limit), `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_bijective` (for `X`
quasicompact and quasiseparated, bijectivity of `|X| → lim |X_i|` together with (c) already gives
(a); *residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change*). The map into the compatible families
is defined by the cone legs, with compatibility given by cone naturality. Also prove
`IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.etale_baseChange` (for `Y → X_i` étale,
`Y ×_{X_i} X ~′ lim_j Y ×_{X_i} X_j`; Proposition 7.16) and `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.reindex`
(invariance under an initial change of index category) ([Sch12] §7, Definition 7.14, pp. 43–44;
[Sch12] §7, Remark 7.15, p. 44; [SW13] §2.4, after Theorem 2.4.7, p. 21). *Needs:* AdicSpacesPartII
R0.6; P2.10; P2.5; AdicSpacesPartII R0.19.5–R0.19.8 and P5.4’s perfectoid limit comparisons; Mathlib `SpectralSpace`, `IsSpectralMap`.

**Checks.**

- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_disc` (computation) — for a perfectoid field `K`,
  `Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~′ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)`: the underlying
  spaces agree by the tilde-limit of the disc tower, and at every point the colimit of the residue
  fields is dense.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_point` (degenerate) — for a perfectoid field `K`, the constant
  system `Spa(K, K°)` (noetherian, as `K` is a field) with the identity satisfies
  `Spa(K, K°) ~′ lim Spa(K, K°)`.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_not_dense` (non-example) — `Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) → Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`
  (constant system) satisfies (a) but not (c): `Q_p` is not dense in `C_p`.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_of_tildeLimit` (compatibility) — if `X ~ lim X_i` in the sense of
  P7.2 and all `X_i` are qcqs locally noetherian, then `X ~′ lim X_i`.

- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_empty` (degenerate): the zero affinoid's constant
  system has no residue-field conditions. The point, empty, closed-field-extension non-example
  and section-density implication are examples of `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit`.

An affinoid description of the pointwise condition uses
`AdicSpace.CompletedResidue R x = Completion (WithVal (residueFieldValuation x))`.
`residueMap` is the canonical evaluation from `R`; `residueImage` consists of fractions of
functions from a common finite-level affinoid chart, with nonzero denominator at the point and a
commuting square into the cone. The source chart may shrink around the point for each fraction.
`residueRestriction` is the continuous residue-field isomorphism for that open immersion,
fixed on evaluated functions by `residueRestriction_map`. It transports the fraction into the
fixed completed residue field. `affinoidPoints_naturality` requires the affinoid point
identifications to commute with the pinned maps of valuation spectra. Around each point of the source, `IsResidueFieldTildeLimit`
requires such fractions to be dense. The chart point is identified with the given global point
through the supplied spectrum homeomorphism. This expresses the residue condition through
valuation fields ([Sch12] Definition 7.14, pp. 43–44).

### P7.4 good affinoid perfectoid subsets

**Good affinoid perfectoid subsets of a tilde-limit.** (*good-affinoid-perfectoid*) Let
`(X_i)_{i∈I}` be as in P7.2, `X` a perfectoid space with a compatible cone `φ`. A good affinoid
perfectoid of `(X, φ)` is a triple `(W, i_0, V)` where `W = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X` is an affinoid
perfectoid open subset (P2.9), `i_0 ∈ I` and `V ⊆ X_{i_0}` is a quasicompact open subset such that
(i) `W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)`, and (ii) writing `V_a := f_a^{-1}(V) ⊆ X_j` for `a : j → i_0` (the slice
category `I/i_0`, cofiltered), the ring map `colim_{a ∈ (I/i_0)^op} O_{X_j}(V_a) → R` has dense
image, for the topology of `R` (no topology is placed on the colimit). When moreover the `V_a` are
affinoid, `V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺)`, the pair `(R, R⁺)` is determined by the system
(see *good-affinoid-uniform-completion*). This is the form of Scholze's survey (the paragraph before
Proposition 2.22: dense image and homeomorphism with the limit of the finite-level affinoids), of
[Torsion] Theorem III.1.2(iii) and Definition III.3.5(i) (`V` the preimage of an affinoid `V_m` at
finite level, `lim H⁰(V_m, O) → H⁰(V, O)` with dense image), and of [CHJ] Theorem 2.8 (standard
affinoids pulled back from level `K(p^N)`). Under `X ~ lim X_i` the homeomorphism
`|W| ≅ lim_a |V_a|` is automatic, since `W` is the preimage of `V`. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define
`GoodAffinoid` (the data `(W, i_0, V)` with `W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)` and dense image of
`colim_a O(V_a)` in `O(W)`) and `GoodAffinoid.level` (the level `i_0` and the finite-level
quasicompact open `V ⊆ X_{i_0}`); prove `GoodAffinoid.preimage_eq` (`W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V)`),
`GoodAffinoid.denseRange` (`colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a) → O_X(W)` has dense range),
`GoodAffinoid.homeomorph` (under `X ~ lim X_i`, `|W| ≃ lim_a |V_a|`), `GoodAffinoid.rationalSubset`
(a rational subset of `W` is good at a possibly larger level; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*),
`GoodAffinoid.raise` (`(W, i_0, V)` is good at every level `j → i_0` with the preimage `V_a`),
`GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` (if all `V_a` are affinoid, `O_X(W)` is the uniform completion
of `colim_a O(V_a)`; *good-affinoid-uniform-completion*) and `GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` (if
all `V_a` are affinoid, `FÉt(O_X(W)) ≃ 2-colim_a FÉt(O(V_a))`) ([Survey] §2, after Remark 2.21,
p. 11; [Survey] §2, Definition 2.20, p. 11; [Torsion] §III.1, Theorem III.1.2 (i)–(iii), p. 28;
[CHJ] §2, Theorem 2.8, p. 11). *Needs:* P2.9; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`.

**Checks.**

- `goodAffinoid_test_disc` (computation) — in the perfectoid disc tower over a perfectoid Tate
  ring `R`, `W = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` is good at level `0` with `V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`: its
  coordinate ring is the rational localisation `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨T/ϖ⟩`, and the image of

- `goodAffinoid_test_not_dense` (non-example) — for `Spa(C_p)` over the constant system

- `goodAffinoid_test_ecd_limit` (compatibility) — if all `X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺)` are affinoid

- `goodAffinoid_test_const` (computation): the whole constant perfectoid affinoid

The affinoid pieces of a tilde-limit are computed by their finite-level coordinate rings

also one of `R`). Then (i) the canonical map `(C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺)` identifies `(R, R⁺)` with the
uniformization of `(C, C⁺)` ([KL15] §2.8, Definition 2.8.13, p. 63; AdicSpacesPartII R0.4),
`R⁺` being the integral closure of the closure of the image of `C⁺`, `Spa` being unchanged by
uniformization; in particular `R` (perfectoid, hence uniform, P1.1) is determined by the system
`(V_a)`; (ii) `GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` composes algebraic finite-stage descent
(AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3), AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5's `finiteEtale_completedColimit` for `L = colim_a A_a → C = L̂`, and
AdicEtaleGeometry A4.4's
`Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence` for `C → Cᵘ`,
then uses (i) to identify `Cᵘ` with `R`. This gives the scalar-extension equivalence
`2-colim_a FÉt(A_a) → FÉt(R)`, also for every rational localisation of `W`
pulled back from a finite level ([KL15] §2.8, Proposition 2.8.16(a), p. 64;
[Berkeley] Lecture 7, Theorem 7.4.8 and its following corollary, printed p. 54;
[SW13] §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.5, p. 21 (the form of (i) inside the uniqueness proof)).
*Needs:* *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; *tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; AdicSpacesPartII R0.4;
P1.1; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.5; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16 (the Yoneda carrier), A1.0.3 and A4.4; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`.

`GoodAffinoid` records the perfectoid pair of the chart, its open immersion, the finite level,
the quasicompact open immersion there, the equality of inverse images and density. Sections on
later inverse images are morphisms to the supplied affine line; equality after restriction to
an affinoid chart is equality of these morphisms. Consequently the density field also covers
nonaffinoid finite-level opens. `IsTildeLimit.iff_goodCover` assumes the topology of the limit,
analytic honest levels and qcqs transitions, and characterizes density by coverage with this
data ([Survey] Proposition 2.22, p. 11).

`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram` uses the finite étale categories of the specified
finite-level affinoids and algebraic scalar extension on arrows. Its Checks
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_identity`, `affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_zero` and
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram_two` compute the identity transition, the zero algebra
and the split rank-two algebra. `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` gives the
universal mapping property against complete uniform Tate pairs;
`GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` identifies its inverse functor on every finite-stage
object with this scalar extension.

**Topology of a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-homeomorph*)
`GoodAffinoid.homeomorph` restricts the tilde-limit homeomorphism to the inverse
image of its finite-level open. Its coordinate formula is the given chart followed
by each cone projection ([SW13] Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19–20).

**Raising a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-raise*) `GoodAffinoid.raise` takes a
good chart and a qcqs transition `j → W.level`. `GoodAffinoid.raise_spec` fixes
the new level as `j`, preserves the chart image, and identifies the new finite-level
open with the inverse image of the old one ([Survey] proof of Proposition 2.22, p. 11).

**Finite étale algebras on a good chart.** (*good-affinoid-finite-etale-equivalence*)
`GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` uses a perfectoid tilde-limit, a good chart, and
a compatible sheafy Tate affinoid presentation of the finite-level inverse images.
Its inverse is scalar extension along the specified maps into the good chart’s ring;
`affinoidFiniteEtaleDiagram` supplies the diagram. It composes the
algebraic colimit equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.0.3, A1.0.5's
`finiteEtale_completedColimit`, the imported
`Huber.Pair.uniformization.baseChange_finiteEtale_equivalence`, and the ring
identification from `GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion`. The two completion steps
use [Berkeley] Theorem 7.4.8 and its corollary, printed p. 54, and [KL15]
Proposition 2.8.16(a), p. 64, respectively. The colimit may be nonseparated;
no injectivity or finite étaleness of the transition maps is required.

### P7.5 Frobenius-controlled integral towers

The next two subsections define the integral towers whose transition maps are eventually Frobenius
modulo `ϖ^p` and compute their completed generic fibre; that this generic fibre is a perfectoid
tilde-limit is P7.13.

**Frobenius-controlled integral towers.** (*frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*) Fix a prime `p`.
A Frobenius-controlled integral tower `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` consists of: (1) a sequence of rings
`A_0⁺ → A_1⁺ → A_2⁺ → ⋯` with transition maps `t_m : A_m⁺ → A_{m+1}⁺`; (2) an element `ϖ ∈ A_0⁺`
(its images again written `ϖ`), the compatible pseudouniformiser, such that every `A_m⁺` is
`ϖ`-torsion-free and `ϖ`-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A_m⁺`) and
`p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺` (the condition `ϖ^p | p` of [ECD] Definition 3.1, placed on the integral model);
then every `A_m⁺/ϖ^p` is an `F_p`-algebra and absolute Frobenius induces a ring homomorphism
`Φ_m : A_m⁺/ϖ → A_m⁺/ϖ^p`, `x ↦ x^p` (well defined because
`(x + ϖy)^p ≡ x^p mod pϖA_m⁺ + ϖ^pA_m⁺ = ϖ^pA_m⁺`); (3) the eventual Frobenius lifting condition
modulo `ϖ^p`: an index `m_0` and, for every `m ≥ m_0`, a ring isomorphism
`w_m : A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p` such that (i) `t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1}` as maps
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` (`t_m` reduced modulo `ϖ^p`), and (ii) the `w_m` are compatible with
the transition maps: `w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m` as maps `A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` (`t`
reduced modulo `ϖ` on the left and modulo `ϖ^p` on the right). The `w_m` are data, exist only from
`m_0` on, and characteristic `p` is allowed (`p = 0 ∈ A_m⁺`, as for relative Frobenius towers over
a perfect base). The generic fibres are the complete Tate rings `A_m := A_m⁺[1/ϖ]` with ring of
definition `A_m⁺` (`ϖ`-adic topology) and the Huber pairs `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` with `A_m⁺⁺` the integral
closure of `A_m⁺` in `A_m`; `X_m := Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)`. The finite levels `A_m` are not assumed
perfectoid (in the sources they are strongly noetherian). Source form: if all `A_m⁺` are flat
algebras over an integral perfectoid ring `O` with `ϖ ∈ O` (`O = Z_p^cycl` or `O_K` for a
perfectoid field `K`) and `t_m` modulo `ϖ^p` is identified, `O`-linearly, with the relative
Frobenius of `A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p` over `O/ϖ^p`, then `w_m` is the composite of the canonical isomorphism
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p ≅ (A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p)^{(p)} ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p` with
`A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p` (`ϖ` is required to be a non-zero-divisor, `ϖ^p | p`, and `O` is
`ϖ`-adically complete; then `Φ_O : O/ϖ ≅ O/ϖ^p` is bijective by [BMS] Lemma 3.10(i)); in [Torsion] `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}` and `ϖ^p = p^{1−ε}`.
Every construction below takes a chosen regular parameter as an explicit input. Regularity is not a
consequence of integral perfectoidness (`𝔽_p` is integral perfectoid with `π = 0`), and the
regularity required at every stage is not weakened: P7.6 uses it for the `ϖ`-torsion-freeness of
the completion. In `Perfectoid`, define
`IntegralTower` (the rings `A_m⁺`, the transition maps `t_m` and a parameter `ϖ` marked at every
stage and preserved by the transitions, regular (`ϖ`-torsion-freeness), `ϖ`-adically complete and
with `ϖ^p ∣ p` at every stage, which gives `p ∈ ϖ^pA_0⁺`), with `IntegralTower.quotient` (the stage
`A_m⁺/ϖ^k`), `IntegralTower.quotientMap` (the transition modulo `ϖ^k`) and `IntegralTower.diagram`
(the direct system, built with Mathlib's `Functor.ofSequence`); `FrobeniusTower` (an
`IntegralTower` with the index `m_0` and the isomorphisms `w_m` satisfying the lifting conditions
(i), (ii)), `FrobeniusTower.frobMod`
(`Φ_m : A_m⁺/ϖ →+* A_m⁺/ϖ^p`, built from Mathlib `frobenius` on the `F_p`-algebra `A_m⁺/ϖ^p`),
`FrobeniusTower.genericFibre` (the Huber pairs `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` and `X_m`), `FrobeniusTower.Hom`
(compatible ring maps `A_m⁺ → B_m⁺` sending `ϖ` to `ϖ` and intertwining the `w_m`; identity and
composition, with a common eventual starting index), `FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius` (the tower from flat `ϖ`-adically complete
algebras over an integral perfectoid `O` with a non-zero-divisor `ϖ`, `ϖ^p | p`,
`O` `ϖ`-adically complete, whose transition maps reduce modulo `ϖ^p` to relative
Frobenius over `O/ϖ^p`), `IntegralTower.const` (the constant tower on a ring `A` with a chosen
regular parameter `π` as explicit input, `A` being `π`-adically complete with `π^p ∣ p`) and
`FrobeniusTower.constPerfectoid` (its Frobenius control with `w = Φ`, which exists exactly when
`A/π → A/π^p` is bijective, for instance when `A` is integral perfectoid for this `π` (P1.24), as
for `R°` with a pseudouniformiser of a perfectoid Tate ring) and `FrobeniusTower.perfection` (the relative
Frobenius tower of a flat `t`-adic algebra over a perfect base of characteristic `p`;
*perfection-tilde-limit*); the lifting conditions are the fields `FrobeniusTower.transition_comp_lift`
(`t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1}` for `m ≥ m_0`) and `FrobeniusTower.lift_comp_transition`
(`w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m` for `m ≥ m_0`); prove `FrobeniusTower.shift` (dropping the first `k` terms, lowering `m_0`, gives a Frobenius-controlled
tower with the same completion) and that
`Φ : colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p` is bijective (*frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*)
([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 42 (transition maps equal to relative
Frobenius modulo `p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43 (the
colimit Frobenius isomorphism `R_∞/ϖ ≅ R_∞/ϖ^p`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19,
p. 43 (a tower of flat formal schemes over `Z_p^cycl`); [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript
(relative Frobenius modulo `p^{1−δ}`)). *Needs:* Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `Ideal.span`,
`frobenius`, `integralClosure`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`,
`TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`; P1.1; P1.3.

**Checks.**

- Computation: for a perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)` and `ϖ ∈ R⁺` with

`IntegralTower` records the complete integral models before imposing Frobenius control.
Its parameter is marked at every stage and preserved by the transition maps; regularity and
`ϖ^p | p` are stagewise requirements. Its `diagram` iterates the consecutive ring maps.
`FrobeniusTower` adds the eventual quotient isomorphisms and both commuting squares above.
`Hom` preserves the parameter and transitions at every level, and the quotient lifts from
a recorded common index onward. Composition raises this index past the start of the intermediate
tower as well as those of the two morphisms. `discIntegral S ϖ` is
`AdicCompletion (ϖ) S[T]`; `discPower` is fixed on polynomial images by substitution `T ↦ T^p`.
`disc S ϖ` has these stages, transition maps and coefficient-Frobenius lifts. The hypotheses are
that `S` is integral perfectoid, `ϖ` is regular, `ϖ^p | p`, and `S` is `ϖ`-adically complete.
The constant-disc non-example assumes `ϖ` is not a unit, so that its residue polynomial ring
is nonzero.

`FrobeniusTower.discPowerHom S ϖ k` is the endomorphism of `disc S ϖ` given
at every stage by `T ↦ T^k`, with coefficients fixed and starting index zero.
It has the same integral-perfectoid, regularity, divisibility and completeness
hypotheses as `disc`. The lift calculation raises coefficients to their `p`th
powers while leaving the coordinate exponent unchanged; this is the affine
relative-Frobenius calculation in [Torsion] Definition III.2.18 and the proof
of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43.

- `discPowerHom_constant` evaluates `k = 0` on `a+bT`, obtaining `a+b`.
- `discPowerHom_quadratic` evaluates `k = 2` at every stage, obtaining `a+bT²`.
- `discPowerHom_lift_coefficients` computes both sides of `Hom.lift_comm` for
  the quadratic map on `[a+bT]`: both are `[a^p+b^pT²]` modulo `ϖ^p`.
  These three Checks test `Hom` as well as `discPowerHom`.
- `Hom_disc_lift_forced` tests a family of disc ring maps preserving the
  parameter and transitions, without assuming quotient-lift compatibility:
  compatibility follows because substitution `T ↦ T^p` is injective modulo
  `ϖ^p`. Thus such a family on this disc cannot violate `lift_comm`.

`relativeTwist` is the tensor product
`(A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ) ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} (O/ϖ^p)`; the scalar map into the next stage sends the base parameter
to its marked parameter. This equation also proves containment of the principal ideals
needed for the quotient scalar map; for the constant base tower it is the identity equation.
`relativeTwistLeft` sends `x` to `x ⊗ 1`. The base Frobenius is
bijective, hence this map is bijective. `ofRelativeFrobenius` takes flat models, scalar-linear
transitions and scalar-linear identifications of these twists with `A_m⁺/ϖ^p`; the characteristic
equations specify relative Frobenius and the right scalar inclusion. Compatibility of the
quotient lifts with transitions is a conclusion. These are the
relative-Frobenius presentations in [Torsion], proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43.

The constructor `FrobeniusTower.perfection` uses a perfect characteristic-`p` base `O`, a flat
`O`-algebra `B`, a regular `t ∈ O`, and `t`-adic completeness of `B`. Its stage `n` is
`B ⊗_{O,F^{-n}} O`; `perfectionTensor n b c` is `b ⊗ c`. The parameter is `1 ⊗ t`, and
`perfectionTransition_tensor` sends `b ⊗ c` to `b^p ⊗ c`. This keeps the right scalar fixed
([Torsion] §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18, p. 42). With these hypotheses, the lift specification of
`FrobeniusTower.perfection` gives the chosen base-change isomorphism
`w_n : B_{n+1}/(1 ⊗ t) → B_n/(1 ⊗ t)^p` by
`w_n([b ⊗ c]) = [b ⊗ c^p]`. The tensor balancing follows from
`F^{-(n+1)}(a)^p = F^{-n}(a)`; perfectness of `O` gives the inverse on coefficients.
The Frobenius square alone does not specify this lift: for the flat algebra
`B = O[ε]/(ε²)`, the transition kills `ε`, while the lift retains its class whenever
`O/(t^p)` is nonzero. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed on `B`.

Checks of the relative constructor itself use its scalar-linear presentations:
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_scalar` computes the transition on `1+ϖ` from the base;
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_zero` gives zero completed generic fibre for zero models;
`ofRelativeFrobenius_test_parameter_not` excludes a zero marked parameter in a nonzero stage.

The following Checks evaluate the constructor's quotient lift, under exactly its
flatness, completeness, marked-parameter and relative-presentation hypotheses
([Torsion], proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42–43):

- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_scalar` sends `[c]` from the scalar ring to `[c^p]`.
- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_tensor` writes `j(x)=x⊗1` and computes the lift on
  `j⁻¹(x⊗c)` as `e(x⊗1)·c`, for `c ∈ O/ϖ^p`. The right tensor scalar is
  retained; a scalar entering through the left factor is Frobenius-powered.
- `ofRelativeFrobenius_lift_two_terms` specifies `e(x⊗1)=[a]` and
  `e(y⊗1)=[b]`, then computes the constructed lift of `[cx+dy]` as
  `[c^p a+d^p b]`. This tests the presentation on two independent terms and
  fixes which coefficients are powered.

For the constant constructor, `constPerfectoid_test_zero` gives zero generic completion and
`constPerfectoid_test_lift_twoTerms` sends `a+b` modulo `ϖ` to `a^p+b^p` modulo `ϖ^p`.

**Relative Frobenius constructor.** (*relative-frobenius-tower*)
`FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius` is the scalar-linear constructor of P7.5,
with flat integral models, a marked non-zero-divisor, completeness, and the specified
relative Frobenius presentations. Its Checks are the scalar, zero-model and
nonzero-parameter examples above. The characteristic-`p` perfection construction
has the separate label *perfection-tilde-limit* ([Torsion] Definition III.2.18, p. 42).

### P7.6 completion and inversion of a Frobenius-controlled tower

### P7.7 preperfectoid adic spaces

**Preperfectoid adic spaces.** (*preperfectoid-space*) Let `X` be an analytic adic space in the
generality of [SW13] §2.1 (an analytic Yoneda-adic space, AdicEtaleGeometry A1.16; the sheafy
adic spaces of AdicSpaces layer 5 form a full subcategory). For an open affinoid `U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X`
with a pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A⁺`, the strong completion `(Â, Â⁺)` of `(A, A⁺)` is the completion
of `(A, A⁺)` for the topology on `A` that gives `A⁺` the `ϖ`-adic topology (`Â⁺` the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `A⁺`, `Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]`; independent of `ϖ`); it is taken for the `ϖ`-adic topology on
the plus ring, not the natural topology of `A`. `X` is preperfectoid if `X` has a cover by open
affinoids `U_α = Spa(A_α, A_α⁺)` whose strong completions `(Â_α, Â_α⁺)` are perfectoid Tate pairs
([ECD] Definition 3.1). Over a perfectoid field `K` this is [SW13] Definition 2.3.4 (they complete
for the `p`-adic topology on `A⁺`); [SW13] Definition 2.3.9 defines `X` over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` to be

Proposition 2.3.10 compares the two when `X` lies over a perfectoid `K`. The natural topology of
`A` and the `ϖ`-adic topology of `A⁺` can differ, and then `A` itself need not be perfectoid: the
nonreduced point `Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` is preperfectoid with strong completion `(K, O_K)`.

2.3.11). In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `strongCompletionPair` (for a Huber pair `(A, A⁺)` with
pseudouniformiser `ϖ ∈ A⁺`: `(Â, Â⁺)` with `Â⁺` the `ϖ`-adic completion of `A⁺` and
`Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]`) and `IsPreperfectoid` (`X` is covered by open affinoids with perfectoid strong
completion); prove `strongCompletionPair_indep` (the strong completion does not depend on the
choice of `ϖ`), `IsPreperfectoid.of_isPerfectoid` (instance: perfectoid spaces are preperfectoid),
`IsPreperfectoid.openSubspace` (open subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid),
`IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace` (closed, hence locally closed, subspaces are preperfectoid; [SW13]

### P7.9 cofinality witnesses for level families

**Cofinality witnesses for families of compact open subgroups.** (*level-cofinality-witness*) Let
`G` be a Hausdorff topological group in which the compact open subgroups form a basis of
neighbourhoods of `1` (a locally profinite group: a profinite group, or `G(Q_p)` for a linear
algebraic group `G` over `Q_p`). Write `CO(G)` for the set of compact open subgroups, a cofiltered
category under inclusion (`K′ → K` when `K′ ⊆ K`; `K ∩ K′` is compact open). A level family is a
cofiltered category `J` with a functor `j ↦ K_j` to `CO(G)`. A cofinality witness for `(K_j)` is a
function `U ↦ j(U)` from the open subgroups `U` of `G` (equivalently from open neighbourhoods of
`1`) to `J` with `K_{j(U)} ⊆ U`; the witness is data. By Mathlib's criterion
`CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` (morphisms in `CO(G)` are unique, so the
second condition is automatic), a witness makes `j ↦ K_j` an initial functor `J → CO(G)`; hence,
for every tower `(X_K)_{K ∈ CO(G)}` of analytic honest adic spaces with qcqs transition maps (a Shimura
tower at `p`) and every perfectoid `X` with compatible maps, `X ~ lim_{K ∈ CO(G)} X_K` iff
`X ~ lim_{j ∈ J} X_{K_j}` (see *tilde-limit-cofinal-change*). A level family without a witness only
computes the tilde-limit of the subtower it indexes: no infinite-level statement for the full tower
follows from it. The existence of a witness for decreasing sequences inside a compact open subgroup is
characterised by the library: a directed family of closed subgroups of a compact group whose
intersection lies in an open subgroup has a member inside it (Tau Ceti
`Subgroup.exists_le_of_iInf_le_of_directed`), and conversely the open normal subgroups of a
profinite group are a neighbourhood basis of `1` (Mathlib
`ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`); so a decreasing family of open
subgroups of a profinite group is cofinal iff its intersection is trivial, compactness being
essential. Hence the principal congruence subgroups `H ∩ (1 + p^n M_N(ℤ_p))` (`n ≥ 1`) of a closed
`H ⊆ GL_N(ℤ_p)` are cofinal (their intersection is trivial), `Γ_0(p^n)` and `Γ_1(p^n)` are not
(both contain the unipotent upper triangular subgroup; the `Γ_0`-, `Γ_1`- and `Γ`-level towers
are distinct towers, [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript), and a family below a cofinal
family is cofinal. In `PerfectoidSpace`, define `LevelFamily`
(a cofiltered `J` with a functor to the compact open subgroups of a locally profinite `G`),
`CofinalityWitness` (a choice `j(U)` with `K_{j(U)} ⊆ U` for every open subgroup `U`),
`CofinalityWitness.ofDecreasing` (a decreasing sequence of open subgroups of a compact open `K_0`

`CofinalityWitness.principalCongruence_closed` (for a closed subgroup `H ⊆ GL_N(Z_p)`,

the entrywise bound is `|g_ij − δ_ij| ≤ p^(-(n+1))`),
`CofinalityWitness.conj` (if `(K_j)` is witnessed, so is `(gK_jg^{-1})` for `g ∈ G`),

### P7.10 uniqueness and representability of perfectoid tilde-limits

A perfectoid tilde-limit is determined by the system: this subsection and the next prove that it
represents the inverse limit of the represented functors on perfectoid spaces, hence is unique up
to unique isomorphism, and compare it with inverse limits of represented functors; the further
comparison with inverse limits of diamonds is DiamondsAndVStacks', downstream.

**A perfectoid tilde-limit represents `lim_i Hom(−, X_i)` on perfectoid spaces and is unique.**
(*tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a cofiltered system of analytic adic
spaces with quasicompact quasiseparated transition maps and `X ~ lim X_i` a perfectoid tilde-limit
(see *perfectoid-tilde-limit*). Then for every perfectoid space `Y` (of any characteristic, over no
fixed base field), and more generally every analytic adic space `Y` with a basis of open affinoids
`Spa(B, B⁺)` with `B` uniform (for instance `Y` stably uniform; only uniformity of these coordinate
rings is used, not perfectoidness; [SW13] state it for perfectoid affinoid `(K, O_K)`-algebras),
the map
`Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i)`, `g ↦ (φ_i ∘ g)_i`, is bijective. Consequently: (i) `X` represents
the functor `Y ↦ lim_i Hom(Y, X_i)` on perfectoid spaces; (ii) if `(X′, φ′)` is another perfectoid
tilde-limit of the same system, there is a unique isomorphism `X ≅ X′` compatible with the cones;
(iii) a morphism of systems `(X_i) → (X′_i)` (over a common index category) induces a unique
morphism between perfectoid tilde-limits commuting with the cones; (iv) over a base `S` (all `X_i`
over `S` compatibly), the same holds for `S`-morphisms. Injectivity is by density and existence
starts from the good affinoid perfectoids ([SW13] §2.4, Proposition 2.4.5, p. 20; [SW13] §2.4,
proof of Proposition 2.4.5, p. 21; [Survey] §2, Proposition 2.23, p. 12 (representability)).
`IsTildeLimit.lift` states the perfectoid-source case with `Y : Perfd p`.
`IsTildeLimit.lift_uniform` states the extension to an honest analytic Yoneda adic space:
its point space has a basis consisting of images of open immersions `Spa^Y(B) → Y`,
where `B : CAff` is sheafy, Tate and uniform. For every compatible cone with vertex `Y`,
there is a unique morphism to `X` commuting with all projections. The uniform-source
extension uses the completion argument in [SW13] Proposition 2.4.5, pp. 20–21;
uniformity bounds the power-bounded elements of each source chart.
*Needs:* *perfectoid-tilde-limit*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid*; *good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis*;

### P7.12 locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits

Perfectoid tilde-limits are local on a finite level and glue; the restriction, finite étale and
étale base-change results used in the gluing are stated with it.

**Locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits.** (*tilde-limit-gluing*) Let `(X_i)_{i∈I}` be a
cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, `i_0 ∈ I`, and `(V^α)_α` an
open cover of `X_{i_0}` (a cover by opens of one finite level), with preimages
`V^α_a := f_a^{-1}(V^α) ⊆ X_j` (`a : j → i_0`). (i) Locality: a perfectoid space `X` with a
compatible cone satisfies `X ~ lim X_i` iff for every `α` the open subspace
`U^α := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V^α)` satisfies `U^α ~ lim_a V^α_a`. (ii) Gluing: if for every `α` the system
`(V^α_a)_a` has a perfectoid tilde-limit `U^α`, then there is a perfectoid space `X` with a
compatible cone and `X ~ lim X_i`; `X` is glued from the `U^α` along the open subspaces
`U^{αβ} ⊆ U^α` that are the restrictions of `U^α` to `V^α ∩ V^β` (see *tilde-limit-rational-restriction*),
identified by the unique isomorphisms of *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness* (which also give the
cocycle condition). (iii) Torsion-paper form: suppose that for all large `m` the `X_m` are the
generic fibres of a tower and that `|lim_m X_m|` is covered by subsets `W` that are preimages of
affinoid opens `V_m = Spa(R_m, R_m⁺) ⊆ X_m` for all sufficiently large `m` (the level at which the
affinoid description starts may depend on `W`; compatible with the transition maps) such that,

perfectoid (`R_∞⁺⁺` the integral closure of `R_∞⁺`); then there is a unique perfectoid space `X_∞`

### P7.13 the perfectoid Frobenius criterion

The criterion makes the completed generic fibre of a Frobenius-controlled tower a perfectoid
tilde-limit; its three ingredients are the Frobenius bijection with the uniformity bound, the tilt
of the limit, and the perfection of a characteristic-`p` space as the tilde-limit along relative
Frobenius.

**The perfectoid Frobenius criterion: Frobenius-controlled towers have perfectoid tilde-limits.**
(*perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers*) Let `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a Frobenius-controlled
integral tower (*frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*; the eventual Frobenius lifting modulo `ϖ^p`
is the only input beyond `ϖ`-torsion-freeness and `ϖ`-adic completeness) with generic fibres `(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)` and
completion `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` (see *frobenius-tower-completion*). Then: (i) `A_∞` is a perfectoid Tate ring
in the sense of [ECD] Definition 3.1 (complete, uniform, with the pseudouniformiser `ϖ` satisfying
`ϖ^p | p` in `A_∞°` and `Φ : A_∞°/ϖ ≅ A_∞°/ϖ^p`), when `A_∞ ≠ 0`, of characteristic `p` exactly when `p = 0` in
`A_∞` (so whenever some `A_m⁺` has characteristic `p`; a non-injective `t_m` may kill `p` at a
finite level even if `A_0⁺` has characteristic `0`), and `(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate
pair; (ii) the restriction map identifies
`|Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)|` with `lim_m |Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)|`, and, when the `A_m` are sheafy (for instance
strongly noetherian, as for affinoids of rigid spaces), `X_∞ := Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m X_m` in the
sense of *perfectoid-tilde-limit*, `X_∞` is unique up to unique isomorphism, and it represents
`lim_m Hom(−, X_m)` on perfectoid spaces; (iii) global form: let `(𝔛_m)` be a tower of flat
`ϖ`-adic formal schemes (over a `ϖ`-adically complete base) with generic fibres `X_m` analytic adic
spaces, and suppose `𝔛_{m_0}` has an affine open cover by `Spf A_{m_0}⁺` whose preimages `Spf A_m⁺`
(`m ≥ m_0`) form Frobenius-controlled towers compatibly with restriction; then the generic fibres
have a perfectoid tilde-limit `X_∞ ~ lim X_m`, glued from the `Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`
(see *tilde-limit-gluing*), which is the generic fibre of the formal scheme `lim 𝔛_m` (limit in formal
schemes, affine-locally `Spf A_∞⁺`). This theorem concerns towers whose finite levels are not
perfectoid; the case of perfectoid finite levels is P7.14 ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary
III.2.19, p. 42 (the eventual Frobenius lifting condition: transition maps equal to relative
Frobenius modulo `p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p` with `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}`); [Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary
III.2.19, p. 43 (the tilde-limit and its uniqueness from the completed limit; the completed limit is
a perfectoid integral algebra in the sense of [Sch12] Definition 5.1(ii), reached here over no base
field via [BMS] Lemmas 3.10 and 3.21); [BHW] §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 22 of the arXiv manuscript (the
Hilbert-modular instance: relative Frobenius modulo `p^{1−δ}`); [Sch13] §4, Example 4.4, p. 23 (the
torus tower over a perfectoid field)). *Needs:* *frobenius-controlled-integral-tower*;
*frobenius-tower-completion*; *frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*;
*tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit*; *tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness*; *tilde-limit-gluing*;

Frobenius on the completed tower is bijective modulo `ϖ`, and the uniformity bound
`ϖA_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺` holds (*frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound*): let `(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a
Frobenius-controlled integral tower with completion `(A_∞⁺, A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`

The tilt of the limit of a Frobenius-controlled tower (*frobenius-tower-tilt*): let
`(A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w)` be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower and `(S_•⁺, t, m_0, w′)` a
Frobenius-controlled integral tower of characteristic `p` (`p = 0` in `S_0⁺`), together with ring
isomorphisms `α_m : A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ S_m⁺/t^p` for `m ≥ m_0` compatible with the transition maps (and
with the `w`, `w′`), and quotient isomorphisms `β_m : A_m⁺/ϖ ≅ S_m⁺/t`
induced by the `α_m`. The quotient map uses `(t^p) ⊆ (t)`, from `1 ≤ p`;
parameter-preserving tower morphisms likewise carry `(ϖ^p)` into `(t^p)`. Require `α_m ∘ w_m = w′_m ∘ β_{m+1}`; the comparisons need not lift
to the integral rings. The completed tilt theorem `completed_tilt` states that the perfectoid
Tate ring `S_∞ = S_∞⁺[1/t]` of *perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers* is perfect and that
there is a unique topological ring isomorphism `e : A_∞♭ ≅ S_∞` preserving the Huber-pair
plus rings and satisfying the following characteristic equation. Write
`c : A_∞⁺/ϖ ≅ S_∞⁺/t` for the colimit of the `β_m`: for finite-level representatives with
`β_m([a]) = [b]`, require `c([ι_m(a)]) = [ι_m(b)]`. For every compatible integral root sequence
`x ∈ lim_{z ↦ z^p} A_∞⁺`, its image under `e` lies in `S_∞⁺`, and
`c([x⁽⁰⁾]) = [e(x)]`. Thus the square with sharp on the source and reduction modulo `t`
on the target commutes on the completed integral models, before taking integral closures.
The inverse Frobenius limits of these quotients determine the integral comparison uniquely
([BMS] Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19).
For every such `ϖ♭` with `(ϖ♭)⁽⁰⁾ = ϖu`, `u ∈ (A_∞⁺)ˣ`, also require
`e(ϖ♭) = tv` for some `v ∈ (S_∞⁺)ˣ`; such a choice of `ϖ♭` exists by [BMS] Lemma 3.9,
p. 22, and the sharp quotient has kernel `(ϖ♭)` by Lemma 3.10, pp. 22–23.
Under this isomorphism, `Spa(S_∞, S_∞⁺⁺)` is the tilt of
`Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)`, and in the global form of the criterion the tilt of `X_∞` is the limit of the
characteristic-`p` tower ([Torsion] §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43 (the tilt
identification from the congruence of the two towers); [Torsion] §III.2.3, before Definition
III.2.18, p. 42 (the characteristic-`p` side is a perfection)). *Needs:*

Checks for the completed tilt theorem `completed_tilt`:

- `completed_tilt_identity_reduction`: for a characteristic-`p` tower compared with itself,
  the canonical tilt isomorphism sends an integral root sequence to its zeroth coordinate,
  so the quotient comparison is the identity.
- `completed_tilt_zero_reduction`: when both completed integral models are zero, their quotient
  rings admit exactly one isomorphism and every representative equation holds.
- `completed_tilt_swap_reduction`: on the split characteristic-two quotient `𝔽₂ × 𝔽₂`,
  swapping the factors sends `(1,0)` to `(0,1)`. It cannot satisfy the identity comparison;
  preservation of integral elements alone would not detect this change.

The perfection of a characteristic-`p` adic space is a tilde-limit along relative Frobenius
(*perfection-tilde-limit*): let `k` be a perfect complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic `p`
with pseudouniformiser `t` (more generally a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic `p` with
`t ∈ k°` admitting all `p`-power roots), `(S, S⁺)` a complete Tate pair over `(k, k°)` with `S⁺`
flat over `k°` and `t`-adically complete. Put `S_m⁺ := S⁺ ⊗_{k°, F^{-m}} k°`, with the `k°`-algebra
structure from the right factor, and use the transitions `s ⊗ c ↦ s^p ⊗ c`. These are well defined:
`(as)^p ⊗ c = s^p ⊗ F^{-(m+1)}(a^p)c = s^p ⊗ F^{-m}(a)c`.
No identification of a Frobenius twist with `S` as a `k`-algebra is required. (i) This tower is
Frobenius-controlled with `ϖ = 1 ⊗ t` and `w_m` the base-change isomorphisms
of `FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius`, specified for `FrobeniusTower.perfection` by its lift
specification (P7.5): `w_m([s ⊗ c]) = [s ⊗ c^p]`;
(ii) its completion is `S^{perf⁺} :=` the `t`-adic
completion of `colim_m S_m⁺` with
`S^{perf} = S^{perf⁺}[1/t]`, a perfect, hence perfectoid, Tate ring; (iii) if `S` is sheafy,
`Y^{perf} := Spa(S^{perf}, S^{perf⁺⁺}) ~ lim_m Y_m`, where
`Y_m = Spa(S_m⁺[1/t], S_m⁺)` and `Y = Y_0 = Spa(S, S⁺)`, the maps `|Y^{perf}| → |Y|`
are homeomorphisms, and `Y^{perf}` is the unique perfectoid space over `k` with this property; (iv)
for an analytic adic space `Y` over `k` covered by such affinoids, the `Y^{perf}` glue to a
perfectoid space `Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y` (see *tilde-limit-gluing*). Here `lim_Φ Y` denotes this tower of base twists. The corresponding statement for flat

with the completed perfectoid pair specified above ([Sch13] Definition 4.3(i), p. 23).

*Needs:* P5.1; P6.14; P7.1–P7.2; AdicEtaleGeometry A1.12's site carrier
and affinoid presentations ([Sch13] Definition 4.3(i), p. 23, Remark 4.11, p. 26).

**Checks.**

- `proEtale_torus_tower` (computation) — over `ℂ_p`, with compatible primitive
  `p`-power roots of unity and pseudouniformizer roots, the root-torus site object
  has an `AffinoidPresentation` whose stages are the relative torus, whose
  transitions raise its coordinate to the `p`th power, and whose pair is
  `ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` with its power-bounded subring. The Check explicitly concludes
  `ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid`. The general perfectoid-base and discrete-base
  cases are `proEtale_torus_tower_general` and `proEtale_torus_tower_discrete` below
  ([Sch13] Example 4.4, p. 23).
- `prodProfinite_Zp_sections` (computation) — supplied by [P6.8](README.md)
  on its perfectoid-space carrier: `O(Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) × ℤ_p) = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p)`, with integral
  sections `C⁰(ℤ_p, O_{ℂ_p})`.
- `proEtale_not_affinoid_perfectoid` (non-example) — a constant object `Spa k⟨T⟩`, with `k`
  complete discretely valued of mixed characteristic `(0,p)`, is not affinoid perfectoid:
  `k⟨T⟩` is not perfectoid.

`ProEtaleSite.proEtale_rootTorus_exists` constructs this site object over a
complete nonarchimedean perfectoid field `K` of characteristic zero with
`p` topologically nilpotent and a chosen system of pseudouniformizer roots.
It requires no roots of unity in `K`. Its stages are AdicEtaleGeometry’s
`relativeTorus`, with structural maps the iterates of the coordinate p-power
endomorphism; its `AffinoidPresentation.pair` is the [P1](README.md) completed Laurent pair.
The Check `proEtale_torus_tower_general` uses this statement ([Sch13] Example 4.4,
p. 23). The `proEtale_torus_tower_discrete` Check excludes the same coordinate-root
presentation over a complete mixed-characteristic field with discrete valuation:
its coefficient values remain discrete, so adjoining only variable roots cannot
supply the pseudouniformizer required for perfectoidness. The constant-disc negative Check applies
`ProEtaleSite.IsAffinoidPerfectoid` to the constant object of this site.

`ProEtaleSite.AffinoidPresentation.baseMap` is the structure map
`X → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`, obtained by composing the map to `Spa(k, k°)` with the
base-field map. `AffinoidPresentation` also carries an affinoid presentation in the actual
pro-étale site, an isomorphism from the `p`-adic completion of its integral section
colimit to the plus ring of a perfectoid pair, and the localization property after
inverting `p`. `IsAffinoidPerfectoid` means existence of all this data, including
`baseMap`. The presentation and predicate follow [Sch13] Definition 4.3, p. 23,
with the base-field scope of Remark 4.11, p. 26.
`AffinoidPresentation.points` identifies the spectrum of the completed pair, with its
specified plus ring, homeomorphically with the pro-object's space ([Sch13] Lemma 4.10,
final clause, p. 26; Lemma 4.5(i), p. 23, supplies the étale base-change compatibility).

**Checks.** Both carriers have `_empty` (the empty object), `_nonperfect` (the
constant rational `2`-adic point is excluded), and `_profinite` (products with a
profinite set preserve the condition) examples.
The `_padic_base` Checks extract the map to `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` from the predicate.
The `_char_p` Checks exclude every site object over the spectrum of a complete
nontrivially valued characteristic-`p` field, including the empty site object:
that nonempty base admits no map to `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)`. This predicate is scoped
to a `p`-adic base; characteristic-`p` perfectoid spaces use the supplied P6 predicate.

### P7.16a finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field

**Finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field.**
(*regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*) Let `(R, m)` be a complete regular local ring (Mathlib
`IsRegularLocalRing`, of any characteristic) with residue field `k`. There is a filtered direct
system of finite flat `R`-algebras `R_i` such that each `(R_i, mR_i)` is a regular local ring and
`(lim→ R_i, m·lim→ R_i)` is a regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field. If `k` is
separably closed of characteristic `p > 0`, the `R_i` may be chosen of `p`-power rank over `R`
(then `k̄/k` is purely inseparable and its finite subextensions have `p`-power degree). The colimit
is Noetherian (a filtered colimit of noetherian local rings along flat local homomorphisms
`R_i → R_j` with `m_iR_j = m_j` is a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal `m_i` extended); it
is not claimed to be complete (`𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧ ⊋ colim 𝔽_{pⁿ}⟦x⟧`). The proof uses the three Cohen
presentations:
`R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` (equal characteristic); `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` with `W` a complete discrete
valuation ring with uniformizer `p` (`p ∈ m∖m²`); `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f)` with
`f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)²` (`p ∈ m²`), together with the regularity, normality, power-series,
quotient and filtered-colimit comparison theorems these presentations need ([Čes] §5, Lemma 5.1,
p. 11; [Čes] §5, proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12 (the ramified case of the construction)). *Needs:*
Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`, `Module.Flat`, `IsRegularLocalRing`.

**Cohen coefficient rings and regular presentations.** (*regular-cohen-presentations*)
`RegularTower.CohenDVR p k` is a characteristic-zero complete DVR with maximal ideal `(p)` and
specified residue isomorphism with `k`. This subsection owns the shared labelled carrier
and `RegularTower.exists_cohenDVR`: for every prime `p` and every field `k` with `CharP k p`,
there exists a `RegularTower.CohenDVR p k`, with no perfectness assumption on `k`
([Stacks, Lemma 10.160.6, Tag 0328](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0328)).
Coefficient-ring adapters use this carrier and existence theorem; truncated formal smoothness
and compatible coefficient lifts are additional properties of the chosen carrier.
`cohen_equalCharacteristic` assumes completeness and
regularity of `R` and equality of its characteristic with that of its residue field.
`cohen_unramified` and `cohen_ramified` assume characteristic zero and residue characteristic
`p`, splitting according to whether `p ∉ m²` or `p ∈ m²`. Their conclusions are precisely the
three displayed presentations. The forms used here are stated in [Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1,
pp. 11–12. The coefficient-ring existence theorem is also
[Stacks, Theorem 10.160.8, Tag 032A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A).

`powerSeries_regular_field` and `powerSeries_regular_cohen` assert regularity for finitely many
variables over a field and over a Cohen DVR, respectively
([Stacks, Remark 10.160.9, Tag 032C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032C)).
`ramified_quotient_regular` assumes `f ∈ (p,x_1,…,x_n)²`: then `p-f` is part of a regular system
of parameters, and its quotient is regular
([Stacks, Lemma 10.106.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NN)).
`regular_normal` asserts integral closedness of a regular local domain
([Stacks, Lemma 10.157.5, Tag 0567](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0567)).
`powerSeries_finite_flat` extends a finite flat local map of Cohen coefficient rings to their
finite-variable power-series rings ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12).
`exists_residueTower` names the finite flat regular system and the algebraically closed residue
field of its regular colimit. In the equal-characteristic construction its maximal-adic
completion is `k̄⟦x_1,…,x_n⟧`; the mixed-characteristic construction uses the completed coefficient
DVR and then the indicated quotient. Noetherianity in this construction follows by faithful-flat
descent from these completions ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12;
[Stacks, Tag 033E](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033E),
[Tag 05UU](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05UU),
[Tag 00MK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00MK)).

Checks:

- `cohen_test_equalChar_zeroVariables` (degenerate) — applying
  `cohen_equalCharacteristic` to a field `k` chooses `n=0`; its resulting presentation is
  `k ≃ (ResidueField k)⟦Fin 0⟧`. The Check retains the theorem's regularity, completeness
  and equal-characteristic hypotheses and tests its chosen number of variables.
- `cohen_test_ramified_two` (computation) — `W⟦X⟧/(p-X²)` is regular, including at `p=2`.
- Coefficient existence gives `ℤ_p` with its labelled `𝔽_p` residue in the prime-field case;
  for imperfect `k = 𝔽_p(t)` it still gives a Cohen DVR with residue `k`.
- `cohen_test_parameter_nonunit` (non-example) — the marked `p` in a Cohen DVR is not a unit.

- `cohen_test_parameter_not_square` (non-example) — the coefficient parameter of
  `CohenDVR` satisfies `p ∉ m²`.
- `cohen_test_wrong_characteristic` (non-example) — the characteristic-zero ring of
  `CohenDVR` cannot be isomorphic to a characteristic-`p` residue field.
  Together with `cohen_test_parameter_nonunit`, these test the coefficient-ring carrier.

The coefficient-extension interface `coefficient_extension` supplies an integral DVR extension
of a Cohen DVR with uniformizer `p`, algebraically closed residue field, and a finite flat DVR
subextension containing each element. It does not assert that this integral extension is
complete. `powerSeriesDiagram` applies finite-variable power series coefficientwise.
`powerSeries_colimit_field` completes the union of finite coefficient-field extensions at the
ideal generated by the variables. `powerSeries_colimit_cohen` completes at `(p,x_1,…,x_n)` and
uses the `p`-adic completion of the coefficient colimit on the right. The latter assumes
complete DVR stages with uniformizer `p`, finite flat over a fixed Cohen DVR. These are the
completion comparisons in [Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12.
`exists_residueTower_primePower` states the rank refinement with separably closed residue
field of characteristic `p`; its stages have rank `p^e` for some `e≥0`.

`powerSeries_colimit_regular` asserts regularity of the same finite-flat coefficient-extension
colimit before completion. `ramified_colimit_completion` starts with `f` in the square of the
maximal ideal at a fixed stage: quotienting the colimit by `p-f` gives a regular local ring,
and its maximal-adic completion is the quotient by the coefficientwise image of `p-f` over the
completed coefficient DVR ([Čes], proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12).

### P7.17 finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion

**Finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion.** (*regular-finite-flat-perfectoid-tower*)
Let `(R, m)` be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic `(0, p)` with perfect residue
field `k` (so `W ≅ W(k)` in the Cohen presentations of *regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*), and
`W := W(k)`. There is a tower `{R_m}_{m≥0}` of finite flat `R`-algebras `R_m` of `p`-power rank
over `R`, each a regular local ring, such that the `p`-adic completion `R̂_∞` of
`R_∞ := lim→_m R_m` is perfectoid (integral perfectoid in the sense of [BMS] Definition 3.5, so
`R̂_∞[1/p]` is a perfectoid Tate ring). Explicitly: if `p ∈ m∖m²`, then `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧` and
`R_m := W[p^{1/p^m}]⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧`; if `p ∈ m²`, then `R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f)`
with `f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)²` and `R_m := W⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧/(p − f)`. The finite levels
are not perfectoid, and `R_∞` is not complete. The criterion used is [Čes] Lemma 4.7, in the
instance proved here: for a `p`-torsion-free ring `S` with `(ϖ^p) = (p)` for some `ϖ ∈ S`, if `S`
is integrally closed in `S[1/p]` then `x ↦ x^p : S/ϖ → S/p` is injective, and if moreover every
element of `S/p` is a `p`-th power then the `p`-adic completion of `S` is perfectoid ([Čes] §5,
Lemma 5.2, p. 12; [Čes] §5, proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 12 (the reduction of the ramified case to a unit
multiple of `p`); [Čes] §4, Lemma 4.7, p. 8 (the criterion)). *Needs:*
*regular-finite-flat-residue-tower*; P1; Mathlib `WittVector`, `IsIntegrallyClosedIn`,
`IsAdicComplete`, `IsRegularLocalRing`.

`RegularTower.exists_perfectoidTower` names the sequence of finite flat regular algebras,
the `p`-power rank condition, and integral perfectoidness of the `p`-adic completion of
its ring colimit. The perfect residue-field hypothesis is an explicit `PerfectRing` assumption;
completeness of the initial regular local ring is maximal-adic ([Čes] Lemma 5.2, p. 12).

### Examples

The compatible-root disc and torus run through the whole layer: for a perfectoid Tate ring `R`
whose pseudouniformiser `ϖ` has compatible `p`-power roots,
`Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim_n Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)` along
`T^{1/p^n} ↦ T^{1/p^n}`, and likewise for `R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩` ([Sch13] Example 4.4 for the torus over a
perfectoid field); the whole disc is good at level `0` with `V = X_0`, and so is its rational subset
`{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}`, every rational subset of the perfectoid disc being the preimage of a rational subset
at a finite level; the Huber pairs `(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)` with `A_{n,0} = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`,
`I_n = ϖA_{n,0}` have completed direct limit `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, already uniform, and every finite étale
`R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`-algebra is defined over some `R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`; the integral tower `R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩`
with `w_m(r T^{a/p^{m+1}}) = Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}` is Frobenius-controlled with `A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`,
`A_∞° = R°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and the bound `ϖR°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` (because
`ϖR° ⊆ R°° ⊆ R⁺`); the characteristic-`p` tower `R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩` with `α_m` induced by
`R⁺/ϖ^p ≅ R♭⁺/(ϖ♭)^p` gives the tilt `R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`; two perfectoid tilde-limits of the tower (for
instance `R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩` and its presentation through `T ↦ T^p` transition maps) are uniquely
isomorphic; the preimage of the torus `{|T| ≥ 1}` is `~ lim` of the tori `{|T^{1/p^n}| ≥ 1}`; over a
perfectoid field `K` the Gauss point `x` has `k(x_n)^` the completion of `K(T^{1/p^n})` for the Gauss
norm, whose union is dense in `k(x)^`, so the tower is a residue-field tilde-limit; every finite
étale cover of the perfectoid disc is pulled back from some `K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩`; and for `p ≠ 2` the
Kummer cover `S ↦ S² = T` of the perfectoid torus pulls back to
`Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^n}⟩)`.

The Shimura towers are the geometric instances. [Torsion] Theorem III.1.2 and Corollary III.2.19:
the Siegel anticanonical tower `X(p^{-m}ε)` (`ε < 1/2`) has, over an affine `Spf R_{m_0}`,
preimages `Spf R_m` forming a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with `ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}`, `R_∞` the
`p`-adic completion of `colim_m R_m`, absolute Frobenius inducing `R_∞/p^{(1−ε)/p} ≅ R_∞/p^{1−ε}`,
whence unique perfectoid spaces `X_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_m X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a` (and similarly `X*`,
`A`) over `Q_p^cycl` whose tilt is the open subset of the perfection `X′*perf` where `|Ha| ≥ |t|^ε`
(using `X′*(p^{-m}ε)/t^{1−ε} = X*(p^{-m}ε)/p^{1−ε}`, Theorem III.2.15(i)), `X′*perf` over
`F_p((t^{1/(p−1)p^∞}))` being the tilde-limit of the Siegel space along relative Frobenius

The pro-finite-étale and formal examples: the universal pro-finite-étale cover
`X_∞ = Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)` of a connected affinoid noetherian `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` over `Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`
satisfies `X_∞ ~ lim X_i` for the finite étale `X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) → X` in both the sectionwise
and the residue-field sense, has no nonsplit finite étale covers, and
`H^j(X_{∞,ét}, L) = colim_i H^j(X_{i,ét}, L)` for all `j ≥ 0` ([Sch13] Theorem 4.9, the form used downstream in
`p`-adic Hodge theory); for the universal finite étale `G_i`-torsor tower `A → A_i` of a Tate
`Z_p`-algebra, the uniform completion of `colim A_i` is perfectoid,
`Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim Spd(A_i, A_i⁺)` and `Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) ~ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)` ([ECD] Lemma 15.3,
Proposition 15.4); `T(G)^{ad} ~ lim G[p^n]^{ad}` ([SW13] §3, proof of Proposition 3.3.2); the
generic fibre of `Spf Z_p⟦X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟧` is preperfectoid relative to
`Spa(Q_p, Z_p)` in [SW13] Definition 2.3.9: after each base change to a characteristic-zero
perfectoid field it has perfectoid strong completions locally ([SW13] Example 2.3.12,
Proposition 2.3.13 and the paragraph following it, p. 19). This relative condition does not
imply P7.7's `IsPreperfectoid` before base change; the zero-variable case is
`Spa(Q_p, Z_p)`, which fails that absolute condition. For a perfectoid field `K` the strong
completion of
`Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` is `Spa(K, O_K)`, with `Spa(K, O_K) ~ Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε)` although
the two spaces differ, while for `X` perfectoid `X̂ = X`; the perfected projective space
`((P^n)^{ad})^{perf} ~′ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad}` over a perfectoid field of characteristic `p` ([Sch12] Theorem 8.5)
has equal étale topoi at every level, whereas the Frobenius tower `T ↦ T^p` of `P^n` in
characteristic `0` has non-inseparable residue extensions and only the limit statement of P7.15
applies; for `Y = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩)`, `Y^{perf} = Spa(k⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, k°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)` with
`Y^{perf}_ét ≃ Y_ét`; and a pro-étale `G`-tower of perfectoid spaces `X_j → X` has
`X_∞ = lim X_j` ([P9.4](../PerfectoidTowers/README.md#layer-p9-continuous-torsor-descent-with-coefficients) in the perfectoid case).

The regular towers: for `R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧` the colimit `lim→ 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧` is not complete, its completion
`𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧` being strictly larger, and for `k = 𝔽_p` the levels `𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧` have rank `n`, not a
`p`-power; for `R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = ℤ_p[√p]`, `p ∈ m²`, `R_i = W(𝔽_{p^i})[√p]` with `i` ordered by
divisibility, and the colimit is regular with parameter `x = √p`; for `R = ℤ_p` (`n = 0`),
`R_m = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}]` and `R̂_∞` is the `p`-adic completion of `ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]`, a perfectoid ring,
while every finite level fails the perfectoid criterion: for `m ≥ 1`, `R_m/p ≅ 𝔽_p[T]/(T^{p^m})` and
`T` is not a `p`-th power, and at `m = 0` Frobenius on `𝔽_p` is surjective but no `ϖ ∈ ℤ_p` has
`(ϖ^p) = (p)`; for these displayed towers the residue field stays `k`, so perfectoidness of their completion
  forces `k` perfect, since Frobenius surjectivity descends to `k`; and the
completion is `p`-adic, not `m_∞`-adic.

The proved Lean example for this layer shows that integral-tower stages cannot be fields,
so `𝔽_p` has no constant tower with a regular adic parameter.

TauCetiRoadmap/PeripheralActions:
# Roadmap: peripheral actions on free pro-`p` groups

A free pro-`p` group `F` of finite rank `r` with a basis `x_1, …, x_r` carries one more
distinguished element, the *cusp* `z := (x_1 ⋯ x_r)⁻¹`, and the `r + 1` conjugacy classes of
`x_1, …, x_r, z` are its *peripheral classes*. For `r = 2` this is the pro-`p` fundamental group
of the thrice-punctured line, with the three classes of loops around `0`, `1` and `∞`. The
roadmap builds the theory of the automorphisms of `F` that preserve this structure up to a
common exponent: a continuous automorphism `φ` is *peripheral of exponent* `u ∈ ℤ_pˣ` when it
carries each of `x_1, …, x_r, z` to a conjugate of its `u`-th power. The headline theorem is that
such an automorphism exists for **every** unit `u`, by a self-contained group-theoretic argument
that lifts a solution of one equation through the closed lower central series of `F` and passes
to the limit by compactness.

The classical route to that theorem is arithmetic: `Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` acts on the profinite fundamental
group of `ℙ¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}`, cuspidal inertia is acted on through the cyclotomic character, and the
cyclotomic character is surjective. That route produces a *homomorphism* from the Galois group
into the peripheral automorphisms, together with much finer information; it is the subject of
the arithmetic successor of **BelyiMaps** (its Layers 12 and 13), and it is not built here. What
is built here is exactly the existence statement those layers reach in their peripheral-power
theorem, without the fundamental group, together with the group of all peripheral automorphisms,
its exponent character, its closedness, its explicit elements of exponent `-1`, its permutation
symmetries, and its continuous section over the principal units. The dyadic instance, for
`p = 2` and `r = 2`, is stated in the exact shape a consumer needs: an automorphism and three
conjugators, one for each of `P`, `T` and `C = (PT)⁻¹`.

## Scope and ownership

The roadmap owns:

- the peripheral system of a free pro-`p` group of finite rank: the cusp element, the peripheral
  tuple, and the predicate `IsPeripheralAut` for a continuous automorphism and an exponent;
- the **peripheral product identity**: for every unit `u` there are conjugators `c_1, …, c_r, d`
  with `∏_i c_i⁻¹ (x_i ^[p] u) c_i · d⁻¹ (z ^[p] u) d = 1`, with `c_1 = 1`, proved by
  central-series lifting and compactness;
- the **peripheral-power theorem**: for every unit `u` a continuous automorphism `φ_u` with
  `φ_u x_1 = x_1 ^[p] u`, `φ_u x_i = c_i⁻¹ (x_i ^[p] u) c_i` and `φ_u z = d⁻¹ (z ^[p] u) d`;
- the group `peripheralAut` of all peripheral automorphisms, its exponent character to `ℤ_pˣ`,
  closedness in the congruence topology, continuity and surjectivity of the exponent, the inner
  automorphisms as its exponent-one elements, the reflection of exponent `-1`, the permutation
  symmetries of the peripheral tuple, and the continuous homomorphic section of the exponent over
  the group of principal units;
- the dyadic instance on the free pro-`2` group of rank two, in both conventions for the third
  peripheral element, and the identity form that the `G_{ℚ_2}` formalization consumes.

It does not own, and consumes by name:

- free pro-`p` groups with their universal property, pro-`p` groups, topological finite
  generation, the Frattini quotient, the Burnside surjectivity criterion and the Hopf property:
  **ProfiniteProPGroups** specifies them and Tau Ceti implements them (`TauCeti.freeProP`,
  `TauCeti.IsProP`, `TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated`, `TauCeti.proPFrattini` and the
  theorems in the contract below). This roadmap uses the Tau Ceti declarations directly, and
  nothing from that roadmap's `Suggested.lean`;
- the `ℤ_p`-power `padicPow`, which is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.IsProP.padicPow`, and the closed lower
  central series with its graded pieces and bracket, which are Tau Ceti's lower `p`-series at
  `p = 0` (`TauCeti.pLowerCentralSeries 0`, `TauCeti.gradedPiece`, `TauCeti.gradedBracket`), both
  under the names **ProfiniteArithmetic** gives them;
- from **ProfiniteArithmetic** itself: the groups `TauCeti.ContinuousAut` and `TauCeti.ContinuousOut` with the
  congruence topology, the unit-exponent lemmas for `padicPow`, the `ℤ_p`-linearity of the
  bracket, the spanning theorem, and the exterior-square description of `gr_1` of a free pro-`p`
  group;
- from **BelyiMaps**, the conjugation-transfer lemma `conjugation_transfer`, which moves a
  conjugator across a change of convention, and the word identity `opposite_third_peripheral`.
  Both are generic group lemmas in its §Pinned conventions, which precedes its Layer 13 and does
  not depend on it or on this roadmap. BelyiMaps' Layer 13 cites the existence theorems here, so
  there is no cycle;
- every arithmetic object. There is no Galois group, no fundamental group, no cyclotomic
  character and no branch-cycle theorem in this roadmap, and no milestone asserts that the
  automorphisms constructed here are the ones the Galois action produces.

## Conventions

- `p : ℕ` is prime, carried as `[Fact p.Prime]`, and `r : ℕ` is the rank.
- **The carrier is abstract.** Statements are about a profinite group `F` with the unbundled
  profinite stack, a proof `hF : TauCeti.IsProP p F`, and a marked isomorphism
  `e : F ≃ₜ* TauCeti.freeProP p (Fin r)` to Tau Ceti's standard model. The basis is
  `x i := e.symm (TauCeti.freeProP.of i)`. This keeps every theorem applicable to any group
  presented as free pro-`p` on `r` generators, including the maximal pro-`2` quotient of Tau
  Ceti's free profinite group on two generators, which is definitionally
  `TauCeti.freeProP 2 (Fin 2)`.
- **The cusp** is `cusp x := ((List.ofFn x).prod)⁻¹`, the inverse of the product of the basis
  **in order**, so that `x_1 ⋯ x_r · cusp x = 1`. The product is `List.prod`, not a `Finset`
  product, because the group is not commutative.
- **Conjugation and conjugacy.** A conjugator is written on the right, `c⁻¹ * y * c`, matching the
  peripheral-power theorem of BelyiMaps and the `G_{ℚ_2}` formalization; conjugacy without a
  named conjugator is Mathlib's `IsConj`. `IsConj a b` is `∃ c, c * a * c⁻¹ = b`, so a conjugate
  `c⁻¹ * y * c` witnesses `IsConj y (c⁻¹ * y * c)` with `c⁻¹`.
- **Powers** are ProfiniteArithmetic's `padicPow p hF x u`, written `x ^[p] u` in prose; this is
  Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.IsProP.padicPow`. For a unit `u : ℤ_pˣ` the exponent is the coercion
  `(u : ℤ_[p])`.
- **The peripheral tuple** is the map `Fin (r + 1) → F` that lists `x_0, …, x_{r-1}, cusp x`
  (Lean indexes from `0`; prose indexes from `1`).
- **Automorphisms** are `ContinuousAut F` from ProfiniteArithmetic, multiplying by composition,
  with the congruence topology.
- **Exactness at the first generator.** The constructed automorphism satisfies
  `φ_u x_1 = x_1 ^[p] u` on the nose. Nothing forces a consumer to use it; the conjugator `c_1 = 1`
  is recorded so that the identity form has `r + 1` conjugators of which one is trivial.
