TauCetiRoadmap/SuccessiveMinima:
# Roadmap: successive minima and Minkowski's theorems

**Summary.** This roadmap develops the successive minima of a convex body with respect to a lattice
and the lower half of Minkowski's second theorem, in a finite-dimensional real normed space with an
arbitrary additive Haar measure, together with the sharpness of both halves. It also covers the
hermitian Gram–Hadamard bound, integral bases with a prescribed flag, and Minkowski's linear forms
theorem. We want it because these are the basic quantitative tools of the geometry of numbers:
Siegel's lemma and its Bombieri–Vaaler form, bases of unit lattices of controlled height, the
Subspace Theorem, lattice-point counting and reduction theory all start from them.

The roadmap builds on Mathlib's `ZLattice`, `ConvexBody`, `gauge` and Minkowski's first theorem,
and on Tau Ceti's real-valued body minima `ZLattice.successiveMin`, with their attainment, threshold
calculus and the upper half of Minkowski's second theorem. It adopts the foundational successive
minima of
[Mathlib's successive-minima proposal](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/35812),
identifies them with Tau Ceti's body minima, and proves on the body minima:
- the rank forms of the threshold calculus, and one real basis attaining all minima with the
  strict-sublevel flags, for bodies that need not be symmetric;
- monotonicity in the body and the lattice, and transport along linear equivalences;
- an integral basis whose flag contains the strict sublevels;
- the lower half of Minkowski's second theorem, with equality on weighted cross-polytopes, and
  equality in the upper half on weighted boxes;
- Minkowski's first theorem on successive minima.

The end theorem is `minkowski_second_lower` (2.1.4).

| Layer | Construction |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Gram determinants and integral bases with a prescribed flag |
| 1 | Successive minima |
| 2 | Minkowski's lower inequality and the linear forms theorem |
| 3 | Translate volumes and consequences of the upper inequality |

Layer 1 needs Layer 0.2 only for the integral minimum flag (1.11). Layer 2 needs Layer 1. Layer 3
needs Tau Ceti's upper inequality and the body-minimum API. Layer 0.1 is independent of the rest.

Suggested home: `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers/` for `MeasureTheory.successiveMin`
and its lemmas (1.1b), beside Mathlib's `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean`;
`TauCeti/Algebra/Module/ZLattice/SuccessiveMinima.lean` for the rest of Layer 1;
`TauCeti/NumberTheory/GeometryOfNumbers/` for Layers 2 and 3;
`TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/` for Layer 0.1; and `TauCeti/Algebra/Module/ZLattice/` for
Layer 0.2.

## Scope and boundaries

### Owned here

- The hermitian Gram–Hadamard inequality and its coordinate form (0.1).
- The integral basis with the flags of a prescribed real basis of lattice vectors (0.2).
- The foundational `MeasureTheory.successiveMin` of Mathlib's successive-minima proposal, its
  identification with Tau Ceti's `ZLattice.successiveMin`, and the natural-index extension
  `successiveMinNat`, with:
  - the proposal's lemmas on the foundational definition (1.1b);
  - the rank forms of the threshold calculus;
  - attainment by one real basis with the strict-sublevel flags;
  - monotonicity in the body and the lattice;
  - scaling and transport along linear equivalences;
  - the integral minimum flag (Layer 1).
- The lower half of Minkowski's second theorem, with an explicit additive Haar measure, and the box
  and cross-polytope minima that show both halves are sharp (2.1).
- Minkowski's linear forms theorem with its boundary convention (2.2).
- Two volume lemmas for translates of convex sets, the coordinate form of the upper inequality, and
  Minkowski's first theorem on successive minima, `λ_0^d·μ(K) ≤ 2^d·covolume(L,μ)` (Layer 3).

## Conventions

**Lattices and volumes.** A lattice is a `Submodule ℤ E` with `DiscreteTopology` and
`IsZLattice ℝ`. A lattice of lower rank is moved into its real span before any volume is taken.
Minkowski's second theorem takes any explicit additive Haar measure `μ` on a finite-dimensional real
normed space and uses `μ` for both the body measure and `ZLattice.covolume L μ`. Euclidean volume
targets use the canonical volume of the space in question, with volume `1` in dimension zero. Gram
matrices use Mathlib's convention that the inner product is conjugate-linear in the first argument.
An oriented determinant is never used as a covolume.

**Convex bodies and minima.** A body is a `ConvexBody E` with `0` in its interior. Central symmetry
is a separate hypothesis, assumed only where stated. The gauge is Mathlib's `gauge`. The successive
minima of a body are Tau Ceti's `ZLattice.successiveMin`, real numbers indexed by `i : Fin d`,
`d = finrank ℝ E`, with `i` meaning the `(i+1)`-st minimum; no second body-minimum function is
introduced. There is no minimum in dimension zero. The polar of a box is a weighted cross-polytope.

**Mathlib's successive-minima proposal.** Build `MeasureTheory.successiveMin` here, with the name,
signature and definition of
[revision `8423d1c`, lines 63–304](https://github.com/khwilson/mathlib4/blob/8423d1c878e50d8504a230ffd9b6ec76ce6a08eb/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean#L63-L304),
so that adopting the proposal if it lands is a deletion plus an import. The
[Zulip design discussion](https://leanprover-community.github.io/archive/stream/217875-Is-there-code-for-X%3F/topic/Minkowski.20Lattice.20Theorem.html)

## Layer 0: Gram determinants and integral bases with a prescribed flag

### 0.1 Gram determinants and the Hadamard inequality

Prove `orthonormal_coordinate_hadamard` (0.1.1): for an orthonormal basis `b : Fin n → E` over an
`RCLike` field and any `v : Fin n → E`, `‖det_b(v)‖ ≤ ∏ i, ‖v_i‖`.
`b` is a full orthonormal basis; `n = 0` and dependent families are allowed.
For every family, dependent or not, Mathlib's Gram–Schmidt orthonormal basis `e` of `v` has
`det_e(v) = ∏ i, ⟪e_i, v_i⟫`, and each factor has norm at most `‖v_i‖`. The determinants `det_b`
and `det_e` differ by the determinant of an orthonormal change of basis, which has norm one.
(Source: Couveignes2020, §3, printed p.494 (physical PDF p.8), Gram/covolume calculation.)
*Needs:* Mathlib `InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis`,
`InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det`, `norm_inner_le_norm`.
**Checks.**

- Orthogonal real columns (2,0),(0,3) attain determinant norm 6 and product norm 6.
- Columns (1,0),(1,1) have determinant norm 1 and product norm √2; equality fails.
- Duplicate nonzero columns have determinant 0 and positive product norms.

Prove `hermitian_gram_hadamard` (0.1.2): for any `v : Fin n → E` in a normed `RCLike`
inner-product space, `det Gram(v)` is the scalar image of its real part, and
`0 ≤ Re(det Gram(v)) ≤ ∏ i, ‖v_i‖²`. The ambient space need not be finite-dimensional.
`E` is normed, not merely seminormed; `n` may be zero. There is no linear independence or
nonsingularity assumption.
Reality and nonnegativity are positive semidefiniteness of the Gram matrix. For the bound, a
dependent family has Gram determinant zero. An independent one is a basis of its `n`-dimensional
span, where the Gram entries are unchanged. For an orthonormal basis `b` of that span
`det Gram(v) = ‖det_b(v)‖²`, which 0.1.1 bounds.
(Source: Couveignes2020, §3, printed p.494 (physical PDF p.8), Gram/covolume calculation.)
*Needs:* Mathlib `Matrix.det_gram_ne_zero_iff_linearIndependent`, `Matrix.posSemidef_gram`,
`finrank_span_eq_card`, `LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram`, 0.1.1
`orthonormal_coordinate_hadamard`.
**Checks.**

- The empty Gram determinant and diagonal product both equal 1.
- Family (1,i) in ℂ has Gram [[1,i],[−i,1]], determinant 0 and diagonal product 1. The
  unconjugated matrix [[1,i],[i,−1]] also has determinant 0, so this family does not test
  conjugation.
- The single vector i in ℂ has Gram determinant 1, whereas its unconjugated bilinear Gram
  determinant i·i = −1 is negative: conjugation is what makes the determinant nonnegative.
- Real vectors (1,0),(1,1) have Gram [[1,1],[1,2]], determinant 1 and diagonal product 2.
- A single vector has Gram determinant `‖v₀‖²`, the equality case of the bound. In `ℂ²` the vectors
  `(1,0),(0,i)` have Gram determinant 1 and coordinate determinant of squared norm 1.

Prove `gram_uniform_bound` (0.1.3): if `D ≥ 0` and every `v_i` in `v : Fin n → E` satisfies
`‖v_i‖² ≤ D`, then `Re(det Gram(v)) ≤ D^n`.
The bound is on squared norms, not individual coefficients; `n = 0` is allowed.
(Source: Couveignes2020, §3, printed p.494 (physical PDF p.8), Gram/covolume calculation.)
*Needs:* 0.1.2 `hermitian_gram_hadamard`.
**Checks.**

- `n = 0`, `D = 0` gives `1 ≤ 0^0 = 1`.
- A nonempty zero family with `D = 0` has determinant 0.
- Two orthogonal vectors of squared norm 5 attain determinant 25, so replacing `D^n` by `D` fails.

### 0.2 Integral bases with a prescribed flag

`E` is a finite-dimensional real normed space, `L` a discrete `ℤ`-submodule, and
`d = finrank ℝ E`. Reuse `Basis` and `Basis.flag`. Flag indices are zero-based. Prefix spans
of an integral basis `b` are written `span ℝ {b j | j < k}`, because its real extension
`Basis.ofZLatticeBasis` needs the fullness instance that 0.2.1 derives. After 0.2.1 they are
`(Basis.ofZLatticeBasis ℝ L b).flag k`.

Prove `exists_integral_basis_same_flag` (0.2.1): for a real basis `w : Fin d → E` with `w_i ∈ L`,
there is an integral basis `b : Fin d → L` whose real extension has exactly the same basis flags as
`w` at every `k = 0, …, d`.
Equality concerns real prefix spans, not equality of the vectors or of their integral spans. The
`w_i` need not be an integral basis. `L` is full as a consequence, not a hypothesis.
Tau Ceti's `ZLattice.exists_basis_triangular` gives an integral basis `b` with `b_j` in the real
span of `w_0, …, w_j`. So the `k`-th flag of `b` lies in that of `w`. Both have dimension `k`,
because `b` is real-linearly independent: its real span contains every `w_i`, so it is all of `E`.
(Source: Cassels, Ch. I, Theorem I B, pp.11–13; Henk2002, p.3, prefix-span equality and (2.1).)
*Needs:* Tau Ceti `ZLattice.exists_basis_triangular`; Mathlib `Module.Basis.flag`,
`Module.Basis.span`, `linearIndependent_of_top_le_span_of_card_eq_finrank`,
`Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq`, `finrank_span_eq_card`.
**Checks.**

- The columns (1,1),(1,−1) have determinant −2: an independent integral-valued real basis is not
  necessarily an integral basis.
- For the standard real basis of ℝ³, x lies in flag 2 exactly when `x_2 = 0`.
- For `w = ((2,0),(0,1))` in ℤ², every admissible `b` has `b_0 = ±(1,0)`: the first vector is the
  primitive generator of `L ∩ ℝ·w_0`, not `w_0` itself.
- In dimension zero the empty basis is the only one, and its single flag is the zero space.

### Examples

The basis `(2,0),(0,3)` spans a lattice of covolume `6` and Gram determinant `36 = 6²`, as
`ZLattice.covolume_sq_eq_det_gram` predicts, and 0.1.2 is an equality for it. The unimodular shear
`(1,0),(1,1)` of the standard basis has Gram determinant `1 < 2 = ‖(1,0)‖²‖(1,1)‖²`. The empty
family in the zero space has Gram determinant `1`.

### Dependencies

Mathlib `Matrix.gram`, `InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis`,
`LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram` and `Module.Basis.flag`; Tau Ceti
`ZLattice.exists_basis_triangular`.

## Layer 1: Successive minima

The successive minima `λ_i(L, K)` of a convex body `K` with `0` in its interior with respect to a
discrete full lattice `L` are Tau Ceti's `ZLattice.successiveMin L K i`, real numbers indexed by
`Fin d` with `d = dim E`. Tau Ceti proves their attainment, positivity, monotonicity in the index
and threshold calculus in terms of independent families, for bodies that need not be symmetric.
This layer builds the foundational definition of Mathlib's proposal on arbitrary sets and proves
that it agrees with `ZLattice.successiveMin` (1.1). It then proves the rank forms of the threshold
calculus and one real basis attaining all minima with the strict-sublevel flags, as corollaries of
the Tau Ceti API. It proves their monotonicity in the body and the lattice and their transport
along linear equivalences, and ends with the integral minimum flag (1.11). The minima live on the
carriers `IsZLattice` and `ConvexBody`, and the symmetry hypothesis is imposed only where a
statement needs it.

Write `λ_i` for `ZLattice.successiveMin L K i` below. The Tau Ceti inputs are used as follows.

| Role | Tau Ceti declaration |
| --- | --- |
| threshold with independent families | `ZLattice.successiveMin_le_iff`, `ZLattice.successiveMin_le` |
| attainment of the threshold | `ZLattice.successiveMin_isLeast` |
| positivity, monotonicity in the index | `ZLattice.successiveMin_pos`, `ZLattice.monotone_successiveMin` |
| one independent family attaining all minima | `ZLattice.exists_linearIndependent_gauge_eq_successiveMin` |
| strict-sublevel flags of that family | `ZLattice.mem_span_image_Iio_of_gauge_lt_successiveMin` |
| least gauge outside a proper subspace | `ZLattice.exists_mem_notMem_forall_gauge_le` |
| gauge sublevels as dilates | `ConvexBody.gauge_le_iff_mem_smul`, `ConvexBody.gauge_pos_iff` |

The symmetric-body source for the definition and gauge calculus of 1.1–1.5 and the scaling law of
1.8 is Evertse2023, §2.3, Lemma 2.8, printed pp.23–24 (physical pp.13–14). The proofs below also
give the stated nonsymmetric extension. 1.5 is Cassels, Ch. VIII, Lemma 1, p.204, which is stated
for any bounded star body and so needs no symmetry.

*Standing hypotheses.* `E` is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space; `L` is a discrete full
`ℤ`-submodule (the `IsZLattice` carrier). `K` is a `ConvexBody E` with `0` in its interior. No
replacement gauge or lattice carrier is introduced. Write `d = finrank ℝ E`. An index `i : Fin d`
means the source's `(i.val+1)`-st minimum. There is no minimum to evaluate when `d = 0`. Symmetry is
assumed only in statements that need it.

For the coordinate checks in ℤ², write `K₂₃ = [−1/2,1/2]×[−1/3,1/3]` and
`K₃₂ = [−1/3,1/3]×[−1/2,1/2]`. Their gauges are respectively `max(2|x₀|,3|x₁|)` and
`max(3|x₀|,2|x₁|)`; both have ordered minima (2,3).

**Definition** (1.1). Define `MeasureTheory.successiveMin L s i`, for a `ℤ`-submodule `L` of a real
normed space `E`, an arbitrary set `s` and `i : ℕ`, as
`sInf {r : ℝ≥0 | i < Set.finrank ℝ (r • s ∩ L)}`, following the Mathlib proposal. The body minimum
is Tau Ceti's `ZLattice.successiveMin L K i`, for `K : ConvexBody E` and `i : Fin d`: the real
infimum of the `t ≥ 0` such that the dilate `t·K` contains `i.val+1` real-linearly independent
vectors of `L`.

In finite dimension prove `MeasureTheory.coe_successiveMin`: for every `ℤ`-submodule `L`, every
`K : ConvexBody E` and every `i : Fin d`,
`(MeasureTheory.successiveMin L (K : Set E) i.val : ℝ) = ZLattice.successiveMin L K i`.
This comparison needs no discreteness, fullness, interior or symmetry. The `Fin d` index excludes
every index `≥ d`, at which no such `t` exists and both infima are the junk value `sInf ∅ = 0`. The
geometric laws of the minima require `L` discrete and full and `0 ∈ interior K`; central symmetry is
needed for Minkowski's product inequalities.

In finite dimension a set `S` has `i.val < Set.finrank ℝ S` exactly when it contains `i.val+1`
real-linearly independent vectors: extract an independent family spanning `span ℝ S`, or bound the
rank below by the family. So the two threshold sets correspond under `ℝ≥0 → ℝ`, and the real
infimum of the image of a set of `ℝ≥0` is the coercion of its infimum, also when the set is empty.
The threshold calculus, attainment, monotonicity and transport targets are 1.2–1.10; the integral
minimum flag is 1.11. The prescribed box and cross-polytope minima are `successiveMin_box` (2.1.5)
and `successiveMin_crosspolytope` (2.1.6).

For a closed body with zero in its interior and `t > 0`, `x ∈ t·K` exactly when `gauge K x ≤ t`

(`ConvexBody.gauge_pos_iff`). This identifies the dilation infimum with the least gauge threshold of
`successiveMin_isLeast_gauge` (1.3), which is how the gauge calculus below is read off the
definition.

`ofReal(2^n·(∏ a_i)/|det A|)`.
The matrix is square and `det A ≠ 0`; all `a_i > 0`. Lebesgue measure is the product volume on

`n ≥ 1`, `A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ`, `det A ≠ 0`, all `a_i > 0`, and `∏ a_i ≥ |det A|`. No

(Source: Evertse2023, §2.2, Corollary 2.6 and complete proof, printed p.20 (physical p.10).)

### Examples

The cross-polytope attains the lower bound `2^d/d!`. For Dirichlet approximation apply the linear
forms theorem to `x − αy` and `y` with bounds `(1/T, T)`, `T > 1`: the determinant is `1`, so there
is a nonzero integer pair with `|x − αy| ≤ 1/T` and `|y| ≤ T`. Since `1/T < 1`, `y = 0` would also

`i`, so `λ_0^d ≤ ∏_i λ_i`, and the upper inequality gives the bound.
(Source: Henk2002, p.2, Theorem 1.2.)
*Needs:* Mathlib `Finset.prod_le_prod`, `Finset.prod_const`; Tau Ceti `ZLattice.successiveMin_pos`,
`ZLattice.monotone_successiveMin`,
`ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measureReal_le_two_pow_mul_covolume`.
**Checks.**

- For `L = ℤ` and `K = [−1,1]`, `1·2 ≤ 2·1`, with equality.
- For `L = 2ℤ` and `K = [−3,3]`, `(2/3)·6 = 4 = 2·2`.
- For `L = 2ℤ×3ℤ` and `K = [−2,2]×[−1,1]`, `1²·8 = 8 < 24 = 4·6`, while the upper inequality is an
  equality for the same pair: the first theorem is weaker than the second.
- `d = 0` is excluded because there is no first minimum to evaluate.

### Examples

For `L = ℤ^d` and the cube `K = [−1,1]^d` every minimum is `1`, and the product
`λ_1⋯λ_d · vol K = 2^d` attains the upper bound. The box `∏[−a_i,a_i]` attains it for all positive
half-widths (2.1.5).

### Dependencies

Tau Ceti `ZLattice.prod_mul_measure_le_two_pow_mul_covolume`,
`ZLattice.prod_successiveMin_mul_measureReal_le_two_pow_mul_covolume` and the body-minimum API;
Mathlib `Convex.addHaar_frontier`, `ZLattice.covolume_eq_det` and the Haar-measure translation
lemmas.

# Symplectic geometry and Hamiltonian mechanics

Build the geometry of cotangent phase spaces, Lagrangian submanifolds, symmetry and reduction,
moment-map convexity, completely integrable systems and contact geometry. The result is a reusable geometric library:
canonical transformations, reduced spaces and torus fibrations carry smooth structures and symplectic
forms, with transport, uniqueness, examples and computational formulas as well as existence theorems.

## The roadmaps

- [Cotangent bundles and Lagrangian geometry](CotangentLagrangian/README.md): Liouville forms,
  cotangent lifts, conormals, generating functions, correspondences, relative neighborhood theorems.
- [Hamiltonian actions and symplectic reduction](HamiltonianReduction/README.md): group-level moment
  maps, global flux and Hamiltonian kernels, coadjoint orbits, free and locally free reduction, cotangent reduction and gauge geometry.
- [Convexity, Duistermaat–Heckman and symplectic toric manifolds](ConvexityToric/README.md): fixed-point
  normal forms, Morse–Bott theory, convexity, measure/class variation, Delzant classification and orbifold examples.
- [Integrable systems and classical mechanics](IntegrableSystems/README.md): involutive integrals,
  regular Lagrangian fibers, Liouville–Arnold, action-angle variables, Legendre transform and central forces.
- [Contact geometry and contact dynamics](ContactGeometry/README.md): contact lines and forms,
  Reeb dynamics, Darboux and Gray stability, symplectization and Legendrian neighborhoods.

Each subroadmap is independently definitive. Every milestone is wanted. The root file supplies common
conventions and ownership; each subdirectory's `Suggested.lean` illustrates genuine interfaces but is
neither exhaustive nor prescriptive about implementation.

## Shared floor and conventions

Work with real finite-dimensional smooth Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary,
unless a result explicitly treats a local model, an orbifold or the smooth connection space of gauge
theory. Use Mathlib's `ModelWithCorners`, `IsManifold`, `TangentSpace`, `mfderiv`, `Diffeomorph`,
`Bundle.TotalSpace`, and the continuous dual for cotangent fibers. A form is the existing
`TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm I M`, symplectic when `SmoothTwoForm.IsSymplectic` holds. Follow
[DifferentialGeometry](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md)'s generic-form migration: every evaluation,
pullback and closedness theorem is an adapter of that single differential-form calculus.

The linear compatibility layer [C2.1](CotangentLagrangian/README.md#c21-compact-intersections-and-group-applications) owns the displayed matrix-compatibility identities and the direct GL(n,ℂ) and Sp(2n,ℝ) maximal-compact theorems by trace growth. Identify the three pairwise intersections of the real symplectic, complex-linear and orthogonal groups with realified U(n). [C2.0](CotangentLagrangian/README.md#c20-elementary-matrix-polar-package) owns the ambient real and complex polar-coordinate floor. C2.1 proves connectedness of these two groups and Sp-specific polar preservation; its required semisimple/finite-center/Killing and adjoint-model comparison is separate from those primary direct proofs. Finally instantiate LieGroups Layer9's matrix-model theorem with H=C_R or Sp_R and π=id. The consuming LieGroups layers own the generic subgroup theorems; these final comparisons are not premises of C2.1's direct maximality proofs.

The canonical cotangent form is **ω = −dλ**, with λ_(q,p)(v)=p(dπ(v)) and ω=Σ dqᵢ∧dpᵢ.
The Hamiltonian convention is **ι_(X_f)ω=df**, the bracket is **{f,g}=df(X_g)**, and
X_{ {f,g} }=−[X_f,X_g]. Fundamental vector fields for a left group action satisfy
([ξ,η])_M=−[ξ_M,η_M]. Moment maps satisfy d⟨μ,ξ⟩=ι_(ξ_M)ω and coadjoint equivariance
μ(gx)=Ad*_(g)μ(x), where (Ad*_(g)ν)(ξ)=ν(Ad_(g⁻¹)ξ).
The default circle period is 2π, so integral weights pair integrally with Λ_Z=(2π)⁻¹ker(exp), and into 2πZ with the period lattice. S0 uses two period-1 time circles; R1a.3 also uses period-1 torus coordinates; [IntegrableSystems I2.0](IntegrableSystems/README.md#i20-positive-period-circles-and-families) supplies the single positive-period AddCircle atlas, oriented time form and normalization conversions. Its varying-period total form is specified separately from the closed fixed-period forms consumed by S0. Normalize Lebesgue measure on t* so the weight lattice Λ* dual to Λ_Z=(2π)⁻¹ker(exp) has covolume 1. Every measure comparison must retain these factors.

## Dependencies and single ownership

- [MorseTheory](../MorseTheory/README.md), M1–M5, owns ordinary Morse and abstract
  Morse–Bott normal forms, compact-band deformation and negative-disc attachment.
  ConvexityToric T2 owns the Hamiltonian specialization and equivariant perfection.
- [HamiltonianSystems](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/480) owns
  `SmoothTwoForm.IsHamiltonianVectorField`, `IsHamiltonian`, `hamiltonianVectorField`,
  `poissonBracket`, `IsSymplecticMap`, infinitesimal actions and moment maps, conservation and
  symplectic flows. Consume that API and build missing specializations in Tau Ceti
  in that shape. HF F2.1 supplies the shared contraction inverse and generic-form
  transport prerequisite; consume that construction here.
- [HeegaardFloer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957), Lane F2.1, owns ordinary Darboux/Moser and the
  symplectic/almost-complex base. This family owns relative/equivariant refinements and applications,
  with precise compactness and complete-flow hypotheses. It does not duplicate linear symplectic
  groups, symplectic orthogonals or compatible structures already in Tau Ceti.
- [DifferentialGeometry](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md) owns forms, Cartan and homotopy formulas,
  de Rham theory, integration, smooth flows and Frobenius. Generic tubular neighborhoods belong to
  [GeometricTopology](../GeometricTopology/README.md). HF F2.1 builds smooth-family primitive selection and time-dependent pullback; C4
  builds their relative Poincaré refinements on DifferentialGeometry’s homotopy floor.
- [SmoothBundlesConnections](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/887) owns bundle operations,
  principal and associated bundles, connections, curvature, Chern classes, holonomy and smooth affine gauge

- [RepresentationTheory/LieGroups](../RepresentationTheory/LieGroups/README.md) owns Lie groups, exponentials, Ad, compact maximal-torus existence/conjugacy/exhaustion, the geometric Weyl group and its compact REAL root/character/coroot/rank-one comparison with RootSystems. RootSystems owns the abstract signed inversion/dual positivity and closed-wall chamber theorem. HamiltonianReduction R2 applies these to compact connected coadjoint chambers/centralizers, separately from its arbitrary-group homogeneous coadjoint manifolds. ConvexityToric T1 adds only integral period/character/isogeny normalization, using those real data; T3 consumes the R2 chamber quotient. Use current Mathlib `GroupLieAlgebra` and Tau Ceti `Lie.adjointContinuousLinearMap`; transport to the derivation model through `leftInvariantDerivationLieEquivGroupLieAlgebra` of `TauCeti.Geometry.Lie.Tangent.LieEquiv` when the identity is interior, rather than identify these carriers definitionally.

Proper finite-isotropy action slices come from SmoothBundlesConnections B1. HamiltonianReduction R3 constructs its actual possibly ineffective Hamiltonian level presentation and symplectic form, together with singular reduction. [Orbifolds O1–O5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/969) owns the generic proper étale, invariant-form/Morita, represented-bundle, classifying/coarse/de Rham, character-class and weighted-integration interfaces, including O4-T's thin/torus comparison. ConvexityToric T4 consumes them on R3's actual model and owns the full effective/ineffective reduced-class, volume and DH applications. Generic O1–O5 does not consume CT integration; O7 comparisons are later. R5 owns surface Sobolev/elliptic gauge theory, consuming [PDE](../PDE/README.md) scalar estimates, [ComplexKahlerGeometry K5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/953) smooth BundleSobolev/localization and global bundle Laplace estimates, and SBC smooth gauge/holonomy. R5 owns the rough Sobolev-coefficient/slice extension and its surface quotient/stratum applications.

[ContactGeometry CG1](ContactGeometry/README.md#cg1--contact-distributions-contact-line-and-cooriented-forms)
owns the contact predicate and line-valued Levi form independently of cotangent applications.
[C2.2](CotangentLagrangian/README.md#c22-exact-lagrangians-and-basic-examples) consumes that predicate
for its two signed cosphere forms; [CG4](ContactGeometry/README.md#cg4--symplectization-and-contactization)
and [CG5](ContactGeometry/README.md#cg5--isotropic-and-legendrian-neighborhoods) consume the cosphere
application. Contact-specific Darboux, Gray and neighborhood refinements remain in CG3–CG5.
[CG6](ContactGeometry/README.md#cg6--contactjacobi-interface-floer-boundary) offers the geometric
boundary and sign adapters to HeegaardFloer and DGFloer; their analytic and invariant endpoints
remain with those owners.

The dependency order is cotangent/Lagrangian and Hamiltonian foundations, then reduction; ConvexityToric T1 consumes LG6’s compact REAL data for its integral refinement, while T3/T4 consume RootSystems and HamiltonianReduction R2/R3. IntegrableSystems I2.0 constructs positive-period circle quotients before I2 uses period2π angle charts. S0–S2 consumes the generic TauCeti smooth free/proper quotient theorem and I2.0's period1 circle, then HeegaardFloer F2.1's compatible-structure family, LieGroupoidsPoisson G0.1's kernel distribution, AlgebraicTopology5–6 and DifferentialGeometry8–9; it precedes TaubesGromov's mapping-torus application. Quantization consumes these developments without defining another moment map or Liouville measure. The explicit suspension quotient/translation flow does not require a flux theorem; HamiltonianSystems/DG time-dependent complete flows enter the Hamiltonian and common-support applications at their actual uses.

This S0–S2 family is the definitive general smooth suspension API: it constructs the mapping torus, its seam-compatible block almost-complex structure, periodic-orbit images and the compact horizontal-image theorem. It is general symplectic geometry, not a four-dimensional gauge/counting result; TaubesGromov consumes it for its separate application.

## S0. Smooth symplectic suspensions

Let (M,ω) be any Hausdorff second-countable finite-dimensional smooth symplectic manifold and let φ:M→M be a global symplectomorphism. Construct the smooth mapping torus

`Y_φ=(ℝ×M)/((t,x)∼(t+1,φ⁻¹x))`.

Put the product on a type synonym E_φ of ℝ×M, transporting its topology and smooth structure so no existing additive `zsmul` instance is changed. Define the smooth TOTAL carrier `Y_φ := MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient (Multiplicative ℤ) E_φ` for the action n·(t,x)=(t+n,φ^(−n)x). Prove its `MulAction`, `ContMDiffConstSMul`, `ContinuousConstSMul`, freeness/`IsCancelSMul` and proper-discontinuity instances from the integer translation coordinate and smooth iterates. Supply the product source’s `IsManifold`, T2 and local compactness to native `TauCeti.instIsManifoldQuotient` and `isLocalDiffeomorph_quotientMk`. Give Multiplicative ℤ the discrete topology; first countability supplies `CompactlyCoherentSpace (E_φ×E_φ)`, so `properlyDiscontinuousSMul_iff_properSMul` and the native ProperSMul quotient-T2 instance give Hausdorffness. Prove the open quotient is second countable from a countable source basis. Construct interval charts of width<1 and maximal-atlas compatibility, with integer-shift fiber transition φ^(−n). These are the particular action/atlas checks, not another generic quotient theorem; no compactness of M or properness of φ-orbits is needed. If the additive-action orbit quotient is used, prove its explicit homeomorphism with this defined multiplicative quotient and transport the structure through it. Identify the BASE translation quotient and the independent s-circle with [I2.0](IntegrableSystems/README.md#i20-positive-period-circles-and-families)’s actual smooth `AddCircle 1`, using its local-diffeomorphic covering and oriented form with integral1; each angular conversion is `dt=(1/(2π))dθ`. Keep both base circles distinct from the total mapping-torus carrier. Define p([t,x])=[t], prove the period-form normalization and identify a chosen-lift fiber by x↦[t,x] with change of lift φ^(−n).

Descend dt to a closed one-form on Y_φ and the fibre form to a smooth closed two-form ω_v with kernel the descended field T=∂_t. Translation in t gives its complete smooth flow, and time1 on a chosen fibre is φ. Prove the tangent/seam identifications and the splitting `TY_φ=ℝT⊕V`, where V is the vertical tangent bundle. On `X_φ=(ℝ/ℤ)_s×Y_φ` construct

`Ω=ds∧dt+ω_v`.

Prove closedness, nondegeneracy and the induced orientation ds∧dt followed by the fibre symplectic orientation. Both time circles use period1; their angular coordinates are 2πs and2πt. This convention fixes the area statements below.

## S1. Seam-compatible block structures and periodic images

Build the block structure upstairs on `R_s×R_t×M` before descent. Consume [HeegaardFloer F2.1](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957)'s smooth family of compatible structures, choose J₀ and a collar-constant path from J₀ to φ*J₀, and extend it with the seam rule `J_(t+1,x)=dφ_x⁻¹ J_(t,φx) dφ_x`. On the product set `J̃∂_s=∂_t`, `J̃∂_t=−∂_s`, and let J̃ restrict to J_(t,x) on the vertical tangent. For `Ω̃=ds∧dt+ω`, verify J̃²=−1 and `Ω̃((a∂_s+b∂_t+v),J̃(a∂_s+b∂_t+v))=a²+b²+ω(v,J_(t,x)v)>0` for every nonzero vector. Check invariance under the s-translation generator and under `(t,x)↦(t+1,φ⁻¹x)` using the seam identity, including all seam jets. Only then descend to the quotient to obtain J on X_φ; prove smoothness and compatibility there by the quotient atlas. This gives the strict vertical inequality used in S2. For fixed φ and a compact finite-dimensional parameter space P, allow a prescribed jointly smooth family J₀,p with endpoint family φ*J₀,p and carry the path construction through these compatible data. Include relative prescriptions both on closed parameter faces and on closed spatial regions of the vertical symplectic bundle over Y_φ. Require the prescribed data on an open neighborhood, agreement on all overlaps and face intersections, compatibility with the fixed time-end collars, and the seam identities to every order. Pulling those spatial data to ℝ×M must give the corresponding deck-compatible neighborhoods and tensors. Instantiate HeegaardFloer F2.1's actual pointwise homotopies and smooth bundlewise assembly on this vertical bundle, retaining its finite-C^k estimates and compact-source C∞ continuity hypotheses. If φ varies, require a separately supplied smooth family of endpoint pullbacks and compatible face data before applying this construction. Verify all t-seam jets from the seam identity for each parameter; arbitrary face data are not assumed extendable. No φ-invariant J₀ is required.

For a periodic point x of least positive return period d, construct γ:R/(dℤ)→Y_φ by γ(t)=[t,x]. Prove it is a primitive embedded closed T-orbit and that its d intersections with one mapping-torus fibre are exactly the d points x,φx,…,φ^(d−1)x. Their starting-point choices determine the same oriented image. Construct the embedded block-holomorphic torus `(s,t)↦(s,[t,x])`, with Ω-area d and ω_v-area0. A degree-k parametrized cover has the same image, Ω-area kd and the corresponding multiplied integral class; prove this for the actual oriented covering map and distinguish it from a different primitive orbit. The construction and its change-of-fibre, conjugacy and integer-iterate laws are part of this API. Surface/four-dimensional SW/Gr counts, signs and zeta functions remain with TaubesGromov.

## S2. Compact horizontal-image theorem

Let C be a closed connected Riemann surface and u:C→X_φ a smooth embedding satisfying du∘j=J∘du, using the block structure of S1 or a supplied seam-compatible block structure preserving H=span(∂_s,T) and V_X, with J∂_s=T, JT=−∂_s and ω_v-tamed vertical restriction J_V. For p:Y_φ→AddCircle 1 define V_Y=ker(dp), consuming LieGroupoidsPoisson G0.1’s actual constant-rank kernel distribution, and put V_X=pr_Y*V_Y under the product tangent identification. All vertical projections and J_V below are on this pulled-back bundle. Suppose [u(C)] lies in the image of `[S¹_s]×H₁(Y_φ;ℤ)`. Prove ω_v has zero pairing with this cross summand, using its pullback from Y_φ, [AlgebraicTopology5–6](../AlgebraicTopology/README.md)'s integral cross product and [DifferentialGeometry8–9](../DifferentialGeometry/README.md)'s de Rham integration comparison. On a positive source frame e,je compute

`u*ω_v(e,je)=ω_v((du e)_V,J_V(du e)_V)≥0`,

with equality exactly when (du e)_V=0. Integration and continuity make this density identically zero. Thus the tangent image is the horizontal plane span(∂_s,T).

Prove the embedded image is exactly S¹_s×γ for one primitive closed T-orbit γ. The ambient s-circle action is tangent and preserves the compact image. Its projection to the s-circle is a submersion; construct the compact embedded one-dimensional fibre at s=0 using the generic regular-fibre theorem of [LieGroupoidsPoisson G0.1](../LieGroupoidsPoisson/README.md), and use s-translation to identify the image with its product with S¹. Connectedness makes that fibre a circle; T is nowhere zero and tangent there, so its flow has a least positive period d. Projection to the mapping-torus time circle makes d a positive integer, and S1 identifies γ with a primitive φ-orbit. Construct the actual image parametrization and orientation comparison. Its Ω-area is d, whereas its ω_v-area is0; a zero Ω-area conclusion is not part of this theorem.

The argument uses compactness of this individual closed source/image, including completeness of the restricted tangent flows. It assumes no compactness of M and proves no uniform compact-image or no-escape statement for a family of different curves. Constant maps, nonembedded maps, parametrized multiple covers and their counting weights have their explicitly different carriers; this theorem classifies embedded images. Generic factorization of arbitrary holomorphic maps remains with its curve-analysis owner.


## Design evidence and existing interfaces

Tau Ceti supplies linear cotangent `strongDualCotangentSymplecticForm`, `cotangentLiouvilleForm`
and `neg_extDeriv_cotangentLiouvilleForm`; `SymplecticForm.IsLagrangian`, orthogonals and products;
`SmoothTwoForm.IsSymplectic`; manifold maximal flows; and tangent-space Ad. These are consumed,
not recast as new definitions. The [cotangent-bundle Zulip discussion](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/217875-Is.20there.20code.20for.20X.3F/topic/Cotangent.20Bundle.20as.20a.20Manifold/with/560999506)
shows that continuous-linear-map bundle operations infer the cotangent total-space manifold structure;
follow that construction. Use its product model rather than a private sigma space without charts.

TauCetiRoadmap/SymplecticGeometry/Contac:
# Contact geometry and contact dynamics

Develop the intrinsic geometry of contact hyperplane fields, Reeb and contact Hamiltonian
dynamics, contact Darboux and Gray stability, symplectization, and isotropic/Legendrian
neighborhoods. Include noncoorientable contact lines and their Jacobi bracket; a globally chosen
contact form is additional data, not the definition of a contact structure.

Use [DifferentialGeometry](../../DifferentialGeometry/README.md)'s generic forms, exterior
derivative, distributions, Lie brackets and smooth flows. [SmoothBundlesConnections
B2–B5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/887) supplies the finite-rank bundle, dual/tensor,
connection and bundle-transport operations; CG1 constructs the contact line as the quotient by the hyperplane subbundle
using adapted local frames. [GeometricTopology Layer1](../../GeometricTopology/README.md) supplies
tubular neighborhoods. [CotangentLagrangian C1 and C2.2](../CotangentLagrangian/README.md) owns the
cotangent Liouville form and unit-cosphere application; CG1 itself is independent of those
applications. HeegaardFloer and DGFloer retain their
Floer complexes, holomorphic-curve analysis and invariants; this roadmap offers the adjacent
contact-geometry interface for those developments.

## Conventions and carriers

Work over finite-dimensional real smooth Hausdorff second-countable manifolds, boundaryless unless
a local/contact-type-boundary result says otherwise. Let `dim M = 2n+1` be explicit. Reuse
`SmoothForm I M ℝ 1`, `mextDeriv`, manifold pullback, `TangentSpace`, and the canonical
distribution family `D x : Submodule ℝ (TangentSpace I x)`.
The standard model is `α_std=dz−Σ p_i dq_i` on coordinates `(q,p,z)`.
For n=1 it is the existing `dz−x dy` convention under `(q,p,z)=(y,x,z)`;
DG4's displayed `dz−y dx` model uses `(q,p,z)=(x,y,z)` and its already-owned
coordinate-swap adapter. These identify the same standard model by explicit
linear coordinate changes.

The primary invariant object is a smooth hyperplane distribution `ξ ⊂ TM` of rank `2n` with
nondegenerate Levi form

`Lξ : Λ² ξ → TM/ξ`, `Lξ(u,v) = −[U,V] mod ξ`.

Nondegeneracy means for each x the induced map `ξₓ → Hom(ξₓ, (TM/ξ)ₓ)`, `v ↦ (w ↦ Lξ(v,w))`, is an
isomorphism. This formulation is intrinsic and does not require coorientation. Its quotient `L =
TM/ξ` is the **contact line**. This minus sign is fixed so that when `ξ=ker α`, the isomorphism `α
: TM/ξ ≃ ℝ` sends the Levi form to `dα|ξ` (Cartan’s formula). Distinguish: (a) contact
distribution ξ, (b) its contact line L, (c) a coorientation (orientation/positive ray of L), and
(d) a global contact form α, a nowhere-zero trivialization of the annihilator line `ξ⁰ ⊂ T*M`. A
global form exists iff that line is trivial; do not use a global α as the definition in the
noncoorientable case.

For a chosen α, contactness is the pointwise nonvanishing of `α ∧ (dα)^n`. Replacing α by `f α`
for nowhere-zero f preserves ξ; f>0 preserves the chosen coorientation, f<0 reverses it. Prove the
equivalence between this volume condition and Levi nondegeneracy, including the line-valued
formulation. The nonvanishing condition is pointwise, not a chosen orientation or a normalized
volume form.

Use the SymplecticGeometry convention `ω = −dλ` and `ι_(X_f)ω=df`. Contact convention: `α(Rα)=1`,
`ι_(Rα)dα=0`; for contact Hamiltonian H, `α(X_H)=H`, `ι_(X_H)dα=(Rα H)α−dH`, whence `L_(X_H)α=(Rα
H)α`. This makes the local flow preserve ξ and its positive coorientation. State explicitly which
convention changes if adopting α_H=−H or alternate signs.


## Milestones

### CG1 — Contact distributions, contact line and cooriented forms

Build predicates on the existing distribution family and rank/frame APIs, not a new distribution
record. Provide the Levi form as the bracket modulo ξ; prove it is C∞-bilinear in fiber arguments
(the derivative terms cancel modulo ξ), tensorial and independent of extensions. Prove the contact
criterion from nondegeneracy and, in a cooriented chart, from α∧(dα)^n ≠ 0. Build local contact
forms as nonzero sections of `ξ⁰`, with transition functions, and prove the α↦fα laws. Include the
standard R³ structure ker(dz−x dy): explicit local frame, dα, contact volume, Reeb vector and the
existing non-involutivity witness. Consume DG4's stronger pointwise
no-integral-surface acceptance target through its coordinate adapter.

Acceptance models: standard R^(2n+1), the sphere S^(2n+1) with the restriction of `Σ_j (x_j
dy_j−y_j dx_j)` (check nonvanishing on the sphere by the radial Liouville field), and local
coorientation-reversing changes. Keep the 3D model linked to `TauCeti.standardContactDistribution
ℝ`; prove the coordinate adapter only, never duplicate that distribution implementation.

### CG2 — Reeb dynamics, contact vector fields and local flow

For a cooriented contact form α, use the isomorphism dα|ξ to prove existence and uniqueness of Rα.
For nowhere-zero f prove the exact rescaling law `R_(fα)=Rα/f+Y`, where `Y∈ξ` is uniquely
determined by `ι_Y dα|ξ=df|ξ/f²`; equivalently `R_(fα)=(Rα+Z)/f`, where `Z=fY` satisfies
`ι_Zdα|ξ=df|ξ/f`. The factor f² follows from `α(R_(fα))=1/f`; verify both equations directly. For
α=dz−xdy and f=eˣ, the result is `e^(−x)(∂y+(x+1)∂z)`. Also compute Rα=∂z for the standard form.
Define contact Hamiltonian fields by the displayed equations, prove uniqueness, Cartan formula and
infinitesimal preservation of ξ. State local flow intervals from the existing smooth ODE theorem;
assert global flow only with completeness/compactness hypotheses. A contactomorphism preserves ξ;
a strict contactomorphism preserves α; a coorientation-preserving contactomorphism pulls α back to
a positive multiple. Prove these are distinct notions and relate them to the contact Hamiltonian
local flow.

### CG3 — Darboux and Gray stability

Contact Darboux: each point in a (2n+1)-dimensional smooth contact manifold has a
contact chart, preserving a chosen local coorientation, to `(ℝ^(2n+1), ker α_std)`; for forms, pullback is
a nowhere-zero factor times the standard form, positive when coorientation is fixed. Proof route:
choose a contact-frame basis at p; use the linear contact normal form for the Levi form; apply a
local contact-Moser path, solve the ξ-linear equation using nondegeneracy of dα|ξ, and shrink the
chart so the time-dependent field has flow for the full compact parameter interval. This is
distinct from symplectic Darboux. Also prove the form-level Darboux theorem for a
chosen contact form, with exact pullback of `α_std`: use the Reeb flow to write
`α=dz+β` on a transverse slice, apply HF F2.1's symplectic Darboux to `dβ`,
and absorb the resulting exact difference of primitives into z. Generic
form/flow/Moser primitives come from DG and HF F2.1; all contact-specific
algebra and equations remain here.

Relative Gray: let M be any boundaryless manifold, K a closed subset, and
U an open neighborhood of K. Let ξ_t be contact distributions on U, jointly
smooth on an open time interval containing [0,1], whose hyperplanes agree on
`TM|K` for every t. Coorientation is not assumed. Prove a neighborhood-germ
isotopy φ_t fixing K with `(φ_t)_*ξ_0=ξ_t`. Locally its form identity is
`φ_t^*α_t=g_t α_0`, with nowhere-zero g_t, positive for compatible chosen
coorientations. Solve `Y_t∈ξ_t` and
`(ι_(Y_t)dα_t+∂t α_t)|ξ_t=0`. Prove independence under
`α_t↦f_t α_t` for every nowhere-zero local multiplier, so the field glues
without a global contact form or an oriented contact line.
The Moser field vanishes on K at every parameter. Each stationary trajectory
exists through [0,1]; openness of the time-dependent flow domain gives open
source and target neighborhoods containing K for its time1 map and inverse.
This needs no compactness of K and no globally uniform tube width. When U=M is compact and
boundaryless, this gives a global isotopy. Here a closed embedded submanifold is
without boundary and closed as a subset; it need not be compact.

### CG4 — Symplectization and contactization

For a contact line `L=TM/ξ`, let `π:L*\setminus 0→M` be the complement of the zero section in its
dual line bundle. Define the homogeneous tautological **one-form** `θ` at `(x,ℓ)` by
`θ_(x,ℓ)(v)=ℓ([Tπ(v)]∈T_xM/ξ_x)`. Prove that `ω=dθ` is symplectic by the Levi nondegeneracy
calculation. Set `λ=−θ`, so `ω=dθ=−dλ`; this convention agrees with the symplectic owner. A
contactomorphism `F` induces the unique lift to the punctured dual contact line by its dual
quotient-line map; it preserves `θ`, including when it reverses coorientation. For cooriented data
`F*α'=fα`, `f>0`, this is the unique homogeneous symplectic lift `(t,x)↦(t−log f(x),F(x))` under
`θ=e^tα` (equivalently `λ=−e^tα`). It is not an arbitrary `t`-translation: a fixed strict
symplectic lift has no free additive constant. The usual `ℝ×M` symplectization is the trivialized
cooriented case; the full `L*\setminus 0` construction also covers sign-reversing contact maps.

For an exact symplectic manifold with `ω=−dλ`, define its Liouville field by
`ι_Zω=−λ`. If an embedded hypersurface Y is transverse to Z, prove that
`α=ι_Zω|Y=−λ|Y` is contact. On a neighborhood of `{0}×Y` in `ℝ×Y`, the local
flow map `Φ(s,y)=φ_Z^s(y)` is a diffeomorphism onto a neighborhood of Y and
satisfies `Φ*(−λ)=e^s α` and `Φ*ω=d(e^s α)`. Prove `L_Zλ=λ` and use its
flow identity to pin both signs. For noncompact Y, use an open domain with
variable collar width; a uniform width requires a separate compactness or
flow-domain hypothesis. This collar is offered to Floer boundary
constructions. Under DGFloer's `ω=dλ_D` convention the primitive is
`λ_D=−λ`; its boundary form `α=λ_D|Y` agrees with the one here.

For exact symplectic `(W,ω=−dλ)`, contactization on `W×ℝ_z` uses `α=dz−λ`; then `dα=ω`, and the
contact volume is nowhere zero. For `W=T*Q` use its canonical cotangent Liouville form `λ_Q`,
giving the standard jet form `α=dz−λ_Q` on `J¹Q=T*Q×ℝ`. State how changing λ by an exact form
changes the z-coordinate.

### CG5 — Isotropic and Legendrian neighborhoods

An immersed submanifold N is isotropic when TN lies in ξ. Prove that the Levi
form then vanishes on TN by pulling back a local defining form and its exterior
derivative. Prove the dimension bound dim N≤n and define its L-valued conformal symplectic normal bundle
`(TN)^⊥_L/TN`, using local defining forms and their transition laws. Prove the isotropic
neighborhood theorem: a diffeomorphism between closed embedded isotropic submanifolds, together
with an identification of their contact lines and a compatible conformal-symplectic normal-bundle
isomorphism, extends to a contactomorphism of neighborhood germs realizing these data. Build the
full first-order tangent identification and realize it by a tubular embedding.
Extend the prescribed contact-line isomorphism from N to tubular neighborhoods
using bundle transport along the normal fibers (SmoothBundlesConnections B5),
so the two quotient forms can be compared in one line bundle. Choose complements
so their full values and line-valued Levi forms agree along N. Their affine
interpolation is contact on a neighborhood of N for all t∈[0,1]. Apply CG3's
relative Gray theorem there. This first germ fixes N and its contact line, but
its induced normal map need only be homotopic to the prescribed one.

Realize the prescribed normal map exactly by an additional contact flow. On the
source conformal-symplectic normal bundle S, write A_t for the normal-bundle
map induced by the Gray isotopy after the initial tangent identification.
The preceding full-value/Levi agreement makes A_t symplectic in the fixed
contact-line identification, with A_0=id. Set `B_t=A_t⁻¹` and
`K_t=(∂t B_t)B_t⁻¹`. Prove K_t is infinitesimally symplectic. The line-valued
quadratic Hamiltonian `H_t(s)=−½ Lξ(K_t s,s)` has Hessian
`−Lξ(K_t v,w)`. Extend it to a tubular neighborhood using a bundle complement;
its value and first derivative vanish on N. CG2's contact Hamiltonian field
therefore vanishes on N and induces K_t on S, by differentiating
`ι_(X_H)dα=(Rα H)α−dH` along N. Its flow fixes the contact line and has normal
map B_t. The line-valued construction glues in noncooriented charts. Stationary
trajectories along N and the open flow domain give a full-parameter germ
without compactness of N. Compose this correcting flow on the source with the
first germ to obtain exactly the specified normal map. Prove independence of
auxiliary complements at the level of the stated germ existence theorem.
Its Legendrian specialization has zero conformal symplectic normal bundle.

Define a Legendrian immersion/submanifold Λ^n⊂(M^(2n+1),ξ) by `TΛ⊂ξ` (equivalently pullback of a
local defining contact form is zero); distinguish embeddings from immersions. In J¹Q, 1-jets
`j¹f=(q,df_q,f(q))` are Legendrian; prove the graph criterion and contact lift.

For a closed embedded cooriented Legendrian `Λ` and a chosen contact form `α` near it, prove the
form-level neighborhood theorem: there are neighborhoods of `Λ` and the zero section of
`J¹Λ=T*Λ×ℝ`, and a diffeomorphism fixing `Λ` whose pullback sends the model contact form `dz−λ_Λ`
exactly to `α`. In particular, this is a **strict** contactomorphism for the chosen forms, not
merely preservation of their kernels. Follow the finite-dimensional construction in Kriegl–Michor,
Proposition 43.18: after identifying the full first-order contact data along `Λ`, arrange the two
forms to have the same value and exterior derivative on the full ambient tangent bundle along the
zero section; interpolate the contact forms on a sufficiently small neighborhood; solve
`i_(X_t)dα_t+d(α_t(X_t))=α_0−α_1`; solve the scalar Reeb-direction equation `d
h_t(R_t)=(α_0−α_1)(R_t)` for `h_t=α_t(X_t)` on a transverse slice with zero initial values; invert
`X↦i_Xdα_t+α_t(X)α_t`; and integrate the strict Moser field, which vanishes on `Λ`. This exact
form identity is required: the contact-structure Gray argument alone gives only a conformal
relation and does not discharge this target. A distribution-level statement may instead record
`F*α'=gα` for a nowhere-zero multiplier (positive when coorientation is preserved); that weaker
conclusion is not described as equivalent to strict form preservation. Kriegl–Michor's model
`θ_Λ−dt` is carried to `dz−λ_Λ` by reversing both the cotangent-fiber and real coordinates.
Compact `Λ` is a sufficient special case. For a possibly nontrivial contact line `L` along `Λ`,
consume [PseudodifferentialOperators
P1.0](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/952)'s
vector-bundle first jets `J¹L` and their transition/projection laws. A connection identifies that
existing carrier with `L ⊕ (T*Λ ⊗ L)`: consume PDO P1.0's connection splitting
and difference-of-connections law specialized to L. Choose a connection `∇` on
`L` and let `z` and `p` be the
tautological fiber sections. The `L`-valued one-form `θ=∇z−p` (with `p` evaluated on the base
projection) defines the hyperplane field near the zero section; its Levi pairing there is the
tautological pairing between `TΛ` and `T*Λ⊗L`. Prove this is contact near the zero section, give
transition maps, and prove that changing `∇` yields contactomorphic germs, explicitly by the fiber
shift in p induced by the difference of the two connections. In a trivialization with flat
connection this is `dz−Σ p_i dq_i`. Then prove the corresponding neighborhood theorem for a closed
embedded Legendrian with contact line `L|Λ`: its conclusion is a contact-hyperplane
germ equivalence inducing the specified identification of contact lines along Λ.
The canonical line-valued quotient forms intertwine under the induced line-bundle
map. The chosen-form strict theorem above additionally fixes a contact-form
trivialization; its untwisted jet model is the trivial-line case. A local/noncompact theorem must state the proper tubular germ and flow-domain hypotheses.
Keep generic tubular neighborhoods with GeometricTopology, while this milestone consumes them.

Cosphere application: consume CotangentLagrangian C1’s cotangent Liouville form and C2.2’s
unit-cosphere metric-rescaling result; prove the contact-line/coorientation invariance under
positive radial identification. For an embedded submanifold S⊂Q of positive
codimension, its unit conormal `N*S∩S*Q` is an embedded Legendrian for both
`α_b` and `α_g`; prove this from `λ_can|N*S=0` and the dimension formula.
For embeddedness, the radial field is tangent to the conic N*S and
transverse to S*Q, so their intersection is transverse. It is closed in S*Q
when S is closed in Q. Arbitrary nonclosed embedded S
need not give a closed unit conormal. For the canonical symplectic convention use C2.2's boundary form
`α_b=−λ_can|S*Q`: the chosen positive-annihilator component has
`θ=r α_b` and `dθ` pulls back `ω_can`. For the alternative cogeodesic form
`α_g=+λ_can|S*Q=−α_b`, the same radial map pulls back `ω_can` to
`−d(r α_g)`; it is anti-symplectic for `d(r α_g)`. The full punctured contact
line retains both sign components; the radial symplectomorphism just stated
uses the chosen positive component. Do not duplicate C2.2's construction.

### CG6 — Contact/Jacobi interface; Floer boundary

For cooriented α, define `{f,g}_α = dα(X_f,X_g)+f Rα(g)−g Rα(f)` only after fixing the CG2
Hamiltonian convention; prove it is a Jacobi bracket (skew, first-order Leibniz, Jacobi) from the
contact equations. In the noncooriented case, functions must be replaced by sections of the
contact line, with local trivializations and transition-law proof. Prove the contact-induced
bracket directly from contact vector fields. In a contact-form trivialization of the
symplectization with positive fiber coordinate r, pin the comparison `{r f,r g}_ω=r{f,g}_α` for
`ω=d(rα)` and SymplecticGeometry's `ι_(X_F)ω=dF` and `{F,G}_ω=ω(X_F,X_G)` conventions; prove
independence of trivialization on the punctured dual contact line. Explicitly derive
`X_(rf)=r(Rα f)∂r−X_f`, so `X_r=−Rα`, in the same conventions.
Generic Jacobi manifolds and
Jacobi algebroid/groupoid integration are outside this contact floor;
[LieGroupoidsPoisson](../../LieGroupoidsPoisson/README.md) owns the distinct generic Poisson and
symplectic-groupoid theory.

HeegaardFloer remains owner of contact/Floer invariants and holomorphic-curve constructions that
its roadmap specifies. CG1/CG4 own the contact-geometry and symplectization
interfaces for Liouville/contact-type-boundary geometry. On cotangent examples
the boundary form is `−λ_can`, as C2.2 specifies. DGFloer owns contact-type and
restricted-contact-type conditions with the primitive explicit, Hamiltonian and
holomorphic-curve analysis and Floer complexes. CG1's contact form and CG4's
Liouville collar offer a primitive-restriction interface for those boundary
constructions, with the explicit `λ_D=−λ` sign adapter above.
Contact homology and other Floer invariants require the corresponding Floer
roadmap's explicit analytic and chain-level targets.


## Order

CG1's line-valued Levi form, nondegeneracy and local forms precede CG2. Its adapted frames and
CG2's linear inversion precede the contact-Moser equations in CG3. CG4 uses CG1's contact line and
CG2's vector fields; CG6 follows CG2 and CG4. CG5's normal-bundle comparison follows CG1, CG3 and
GeometricTopology's tubular theorem. Its first-jet carrier and connection splitting consume only
PDO P1.0's first-jet subtarget and SBC B2–B4. Its smooth line-bundle
transport additionally consumes SBC B5. These dependencies are independent
of density adjoints, Sobolev or pseudodifferential analysis. CG1–CG4 do not depend on that jet construction. All constructions
include restrictions, changes of local form, pullback by diffeomorphisms, functoriality and
inverse/uniqueness comparisons before their use in the neighborhood theorems.

## References

- Gray, *Some global properties of contact structures*, Annals of Mathematics69 (1959),421–450, [primary article](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970192).
- Geiges, *An Introduction to Contact Topology*, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics109 (2008), for contact Darboux, Gray and isotropic neighborhood theorems.
- Kriegl–Michor, *The Convenient Setting of Global Analysis*, AMS (1997), §43, Proposition43.18, for the strict Legendrian neighborhood construction; [author-hosted text](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~michor/apbook.pdf).
- [Grenoble contact-geometry course notes](https://www-fourier.ujf-grenoble.fr/~courtes/cours.pdf), §§3.2–3.3, for intrinsic contact lines, contact vector fields and local/relative Gray stability.

# Hamiltonian convexity, Duistermaat–Heckman and symplectic toric geometry

Develop the geometry and topology of compact Hamiltonian actions, from local weight normal forms to
moment polytopes, reduced symplectic classes and measures, and Delzant classification. Both the
symplectic geometry and the lattice geometry should have full usable APIs; a polytope without its
stabilizers, measure normalization or reconstruction theorem is not the intended result.

## Setting, conventions and prerequisites

Use the [family conventions](../README.md). A torus is a compact connected abelian Lie group with
Lie algebra t and period lattice ker(exp); coordinates use R^m/(2πZ)^m. Define the integral cocharacter lattice Λ_Z=(2π)⁻¹ker(exp)⊂t and its dual weight
lattice; χ maps to (1/i)dχ. Weights pair integrally with Λ_Z and into 2πZ with ker(exp).
Normalize Lebesgue measure on t* so the weight lattice Λ* dual to Λ_Z=(2π)⁻¹ker(exp) has covolume 1;
use Mathlib `IsZLattice`/`Basis.addHaar` and Tau Ceti `Toric.IsIntegralLattice` for scalar-extension data. A Hamiltonian action means the smooth symplectic action and
equivariant moment map of [HamiltonianReduction](../HamiltonianReduction/README.md). Convexity below
assumes compact **connected** M unless explicitly stated otherwise. No assertion of connected fibers
or a bounded polytope is made for arbitrary noncompact M.

Consume Tau Ceti's compatible symplectic linear algebra and smooth forms, ordinary Darboux/Moser from
[HeegaardFloer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957), forms/integration from
[DifferentialGeometry](../../DifferentialGeometry/README.md), compact group actions/tori/roots from
[LieGroups](../../RepresentationTheory/LieGroups/README.md), quotient structures and integral Chern classes
from [SmoothBundlesConnections](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/887), and (co)homological
cellular and duality machinery from [AlgebraicTopology](../../AlgebraicTopology/README.md). For generic proper étale presentation, classifying/coarse, invariant-form, represented-bundle and weighted-integration interfaces, consume [Orbifolds O1–O5](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/969), including O4-T's thin/CW torus comparison. That owner consumes the ordinary CC/AT/DG and compactly generated interfaces and constructs their groupoid-specific adapters. T4 owns the application to R3's actual Hamiltonian data, reduced-class variation and DH/reduced-volume normalization, retaining ineffective isotropy and isotropy-sensitive bundles.
Consume [MorseTheory M1–M5](../../MorseTheory/README.md)'s ordinary and abstract
Morse–Bott normal-form, deformation and attachment theory. T2 owns its moment-map
specialization and equivariant perfection.
Symplectic toric manifolds are distinct from algebraic/analytic toric varieties of
[AnalyticToricGeometry](../../AnalyticToricGeometry/README.md); lattice comparisons are shared,
while quotient symplectic forms and Hamiltonian classification live here.

## T1. Compact symplectic actions and local models

Consume [LieGroups Layer6](../../RepresentationTheory/LieGroups/README.md)'s compact REAL adapter:
maximal-torus existence/conjugacy/exhaustion, the normalizer/Weyl comparison, actual adjoint root
characters χ_α with dχ_α=iα, the real root/coroot pairing and compact rank-one reflection
representatives. Consume [RootSystems Layer4](../../RepresentationTheory/RootSystems/README.md)'s abstract closed-wall
theory through that comparison. These are the real inputs to the integral refinement here.

Build the full 2π-normalized period/weight dictionary: compare a compact torus with its Lie
algebra modulo ker(exp), construct Λ_Z=(2π)⁻¹ker(exp), identify characters by (1/i)dχ, and
prove the dual lattice, restriction, quotient and integral basis-change formulas. For λ∈ker(exp),
prove α_χ(λ)/(2π)∈ℤ. For each adjoint root, prove 2πα∨∈ker(exp) through its realized compact
rank-one subgroup, and identify the resulting integer character/coroot pairing with the Cartan
integer. For the chosen compact rank-one map φ_α:SU(2)→G, consume Layer6's
normalization `dφ_α(diag(i,−i))=α∨` and check that the selected character convention
`dχ_α=iα` with α(α∨)=2 gives the same Cartan integer; the homomorphism identity gives
`exp_G(2πα∨)=1`. Use this as the consumer-side normalization check against the supplied Layer6 calibration; it
does not split the full torus period lattice integrally. Prove the finite-index lattice comparison under a central isogeny, retaining the full
torus lattice: the real center/semisimple splitting need not split the period lattice integrally.
Verify the index-two central/semisimple coupling for U(2).

LieGroups Layer6 owns maximal tori and the compact real root/Weyl adapter;
[HamiltonianReduction R2](../HamiltonianReduction/README.md#r2-coadjoint-orbits-and-kks) owns the
compact coadjoint chamber/centralizer application. T3 consumes that quotient and owns the
symplectic cross-section and convexity theorem. R2 is independent of this integral refinement.

Construct an invariant compatible almost complex structure and metric by averaging and polar
normalization; averaging an arbitrary compatible J does not preserve J²=−1. Prove a compact group's
fixed locus is a union of embedded symplectic submanifolds, tangent equal to invariant vectors, with
symplectic normal representation. Construct an equivariant tubular neighborhood; prove equivariant
Darboux near a fixed point and relative normal form along a fixed component using equivariant Moser, with
GeometricTopology Layer1’s generic tubular neighborhood as the nonequivariant floor.

For a torus-fixed p choose a unitary weight decomposition of its tangent space. In local coordinates
ω=Σdqᵢ∧dpᵢ and
**μ=μ(p)−½Σαᵢ(qᵢ²+pᵢ²)** for true complex weights αᵢ of
`zᵢ↦exp(i⟨αᵢ,ξ⟩)zᵢ` in compatible complex coordinates. Thus the local image is
μ(p)−cone{αᵢ}, and index of μ^ξ is twice the number of positive αᵢ(ξ). Relate integer αᵢ to the lattice, not just a chosen list of real vectors. Zero weights give fixed
tangent directions. Prove the quadratic identity, stabilizers, orbit rank and local moment cone.
For nonfixed orbits of general proper Hamiltonian actions of arbitrary finite-dimensional Lie groups consume HamiltonianReduction R3.1's full proper-orbit symplectic slice/Marle–Guillemin–Sternberg model, including its m*, coadjoint and slice directions, compact stabilizer and moment normalization. Construct its coordinate-compatible compact-torus specialization here and use it for global convexity and singularity descriptions. Its equivariant tube and relative Moser flow-germ theorem apply along the actual proper orbit; the compact-orbit averaging argument is a specialization.

## T2. Morse–Bott and moment-map topology

Consume MorseTheory M5's critical-submanifold/normal-Hessian carriers,
normal form and negative-disc-bundle attachment theorem. Identify these carriers
and indices for each moment component below. Consume
[CharacteristicClasses C2–C3](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/896)'s ordinary
cohomological Thom/Euler and Leray–Hirsch interfaces for the resulting relative
(co)homology; use twisted coefficients or F₂ for general negative bundles.
Moment-action negative bundles are complex, giving their integral orientations. Noncompact flow conclusions require an explicit properness or completeness hypothesis;
the application here uses compact M. Prove generic moment components have critical set M^T and
Morse–Bott Hessian determined by nonzero weights, with even index and coindex. For every ξ the critical set is M^(T_ξ), where T_ξ is the closure of exp(Rξ);
use this closure for irrational as well as rational directions.

Prove connectedness of scalar moment levels, including critical levels, by the even-index/coindex
handle argument. Prove perfection of moment-map Morse–Bott functions over rational coefficients using
the equivariant Euler-class/Thom argument. Consume
CharacteristicClasses C1's torus universal-bundle models, including the finite
models `ET_N=(S^(2N+1))^m`, `BT_N=(CP^N)^m`, their standard inclusions/colimits,
contractibility/free action and integral cohomology. Use its generator sign:
the standard coordinate-character class is `u_i=−h_i`, where h_i is the positive
dual-character hyperplane class; hence `H*(BT;ℤ)=ℤ[u₁,…,u_m]` and a weight
`Σ a_iχ_i` has first Chern class `Σ a_i u_i=−Σ a_i h_i`. Keep this sign in
equivariant Euler classes. Compare Borel constructions to those existing models.
Build the Borel fibration M_T→BT, equivariant Thom classes, Euler classes, localization by
nonzero weights, Leray–Hirsch and integral equivariant formality when ordinary cohomology is
free/even. These constructions are explicit targets here over AT’s ordinary cohomology.
Build equivariant Morse exact sequences and prove rational perfection.
Integral conclusions require their own proof and torsion hypotheses: when fixed points are isolated,
even cells give free integral homology/cohomology, vanishing odd groups, rank H^(2k) equal to the number of critical points of index 2k, unique maximum/minimum and simple connectedness. Do not assert these conclusions for arbitrary
positive-dimensional fixed components. For compact coadjoint orbits prove existence of a generic height
with isolated fixed points via root tangent planes and torus-centralizer structure, rather than a generic
Sard argument that never proves the fixed set is discrete.

## T3. Convexity and matrix examples

For compact connected Hamiltonian T-space prove: μ(M) is the convex hull of images of **fixed
components**, hence a compact polytope; every μ-fiber is connected. Build the torus local-to-global argument from proper moment map, local convexity cones and local
fiber connectedness (Condevaux–Dazord–Molino/Hilgert–Neeb–Plank), prove these hypotheses from
the symplectic slice normal form, then obtain convexity and connectedness at critical as well as
regular values. Finiteness of components is proved
from compact fixed-set manifold and local models; fixed points themselves need not be finite.
Prove restriction to subtori, translation/naturality and product polytopes. If the action is effective,
show μ(M) has full affine dimension dim T; otherwise identify its effective quotient and affine support.
Torus orbits are isotropic, hence dim T≤½dim M for effective actions. A regular level for a torus
is coisotropic; quotient dimension is dim M−2dim T, with an orbifold if only locally free.

For compact connected K prove **Kirwan convexity**: μ(M)∩t*_+ is a compact convex rational polytope
in a chosen closed positive Weyl chamber (rational facet directions in the weight lattice,
with real support constants), and the fibers of the orbit-projected map to t*_+ are
connected. The full K-moment image in k* need not be convex. Consume
[HamiltonianReduction R2](../HamiltonianReduction/README.md#r2-coadjoint-orbits-and-kks)'s compact
coadjoint-orbit, closed-chamber and centralizer theorems, including
`k*/K≅z(k)*×t*_(ss,+)`, on LieGroups Layer6 and RootSystems Layer4. Maximal-torus
conjugacy, Weyl uniqueness and this quotient are inputs from those owners. Construct the symplectic cross-section
and prove its moment-map and stabilizer comparisons. Prove Kirwan by cross-sections
and the local-to-global theorem. Also build the norm-square moment stratification,
including minimal degeneracy and strata. Before its convergence theorem, prove the
specialized degenerate gradient inequality for the transverse MGS polynomial
`p(η,v)=‖ν+η+μ_V(v)‖²`: near a critical point of value b there are

# Cotangent bundles and Lagrangian geometry

Develop the smooth geometry of canonical phase spaces and Lagrangian submanifolds. The cotangent
bundle should be usable intrinsically, in charts, under diffeomorphisms and products; generating
functions should produce actual local canonical transformations with domains and inverse formulas.
Neighborhood theorems identify precisely what data determine a symplectic germ along a submanifold.

## Conventions and prerequisites

Use the [family conventions](../README.md). Base manifolds are real finite-dimensional smooth,
boundaryless, Hausdorff and second countable. A submanifold is given by a smooth embedding with an
induced manifold structure, not just a subset. Compactness of the embedded submanifold is required
for the uniform neighborhood conclusions below. Symplectic germs/local transformations are maps
between specified open neighborhoods; no theorem asserts a globally defined map from a local implicit
function. The conormal of Q⊂M uses covectors in T*_qM annihilating the image of T_qQ.

Consume Tau Ceti's `SymplecticForm.IsIsotropic`, `IsCoisotropic`, `IsLagrangian`, linear cotangent
form and Liouville identity. Consume ordinary Darboux and compact-manifold Moser with a given smooth symplectic path from
[HeegaardFloer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/957), F2.1. Generic differential-form calculus belong to
[DifferentialGeometry](../../DifferentialGeometry/README.md); generic tubular neighborhoods belong to
[GeometricTopology](../../GeometricTopology/README.md); bundle duals and smooth operations belong
to [SmoothBundlesConnections](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/887). The missing instances or
lemmas needed to connect these interfaces are explicit work here or there, not assumptions.

§§22–25. Marsden–Ratiu, *Introduction to Mechanics and Symmetry*, momentum-map and cotangent-reduction
